title: Item 1: bd epic close-eligible in the coordinator loop
description: Plan: docs/plans/beads-coordination-rollout.md item 1. An epic does NOT close when its children close (measured). With ceremony epics (item 7) that means: ceremony beads all close, the ceremony epic stays open, the target stays blocked forever, bd ready returns empty, and an is-the-front-empty termination check reads that as SUCCESS. The run reports done having done nothing. HARD PREREQUISITE for item 7.
design:
The coordinator loop becomes two commands, in this order: 'bd epic close-eligible' then the ready query. Also add --exclude-type=epic to the ready query: epics appear in bd ready themselves (measured), so without it the coordinator tries to dispatch a phase container as work. Molecules do NOT appear, so they need no exclusion. The loop statement in bead-bonanza/SKILL.md and references/supervision.md must agree — today only one describes the loop.

Files: plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md, plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/supervision.md.

BYTE BUDGET. scripts/check-skills.sh caps a SKILL.md BODY at 20,000 bytes and the `skills-strict` check exits 1 on the warning. bead-bonanza/SKILL.md's body is ~18,480 bytes, so there is roughly 1,500 bytes of headroom — enough for this change, but measure rather than assume:

  python3 -c "t=open('plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md').read(); print(len(t.split('---',2)[2].encode()))"

Put the long-form explanation of why omitting close-eligible is a silent deadlock in references/supervision.md (uncapped) and keep the SKILL.md body's share to the loop itself plus a one-line pointer.

Do not re-measure bd's epic-close behaviour; it is recorded in docs/plans/beads-coordination-design.md.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] bead-bonanza/SKILL.md's loop calls bd epic close-eligible before every ready query.
- [ ] references/supervision.md states the same loop; the two do not disagree.
- [ ] The ready query uses --exclude-type=epic.
- [ ] A comment or line states why omitting close-eligible is a silent deadlock, not a slowdown.
- [ ] plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md's body measures <= 20,000 bytes after this bead.
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh --strict exits 0.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: Two prose edits, but they must make SKILL.md and supervision.md agree on one loop and state a non-obvious silent-deadlock failure mode; low ambiguity, no code.

title: The coordinator creates the sprint branch before the first worktree
description:
Implements step 5, `The sprint branch — created once, before the first worktree`, in `docs/plans/sprint-skill-design.md`.

Three steps consume the sprint branch today and none of them creates it: step 6 reviews `base_sha` → sprint head, D1 verifies its worktree branched from sprint HEAD rather than the default branch, and step 7 opens the PR against it.

**The coordinator creates it, immediately before dispatching wave 1.** Not at scope resolution: a run that bounces every bead at 3+4 has nothing to branch for, and a branch cut before grooming records a `base_sha` from before the grooming commits land.

**Reuse, do not recreate.** If the manifest already carries `branch` and `base_sha`, the coordinator uses them and creates nothing. That is the whole of what makes a resumed run land on the same branch, so it is not an optimisation.
design: `base_sha` is recorded at creation because that is the only moment it is unambiguous. Deriving it later from the branch's merge-base assumes the base branch has not moved, and on a long run it will have.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The coordinator creates the branch immediately before wave 1 and writes `branch` and `base_sha` into the run epic's manifest.
- [ ] A run whose manifest already carries both reuses them and creates nothing.
- [ ] A collision with an unrelated existing branch stops the run before any worktree exists.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/plan-sprint/references/run-record.md` documents both keys.
- [ ] Nothing downstream derives the branch name independently — one producer, three consumers.
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace mid-run escalation with recorded incidents
description:
Implements `The rule: no new questions after the gate` and `The four decisions that get recorded, not asked` in `docs/plans/sprint-skill-design.md`.

The design previously let four kinds of decision interrupt the run. It no longer does — **nothing escalates to a human between the authorization gate and the PR.** The posture is iterative: a recorded decision can be reviewed at the PR and revised in the next run, which is cheaper than a night blocked on a question nobody is awake to answer.

The four kinds survive as **incidents**, not escalations:

- an acceptance criterion needs amending
- a standard, requirement and AC are in tension
- a contract or interface change
- a spec is silent where the bead requires it to speak

**Recording one has three parts and all three are required:** a `retro:` comment on the bead carrying the decision and its reasoning; an `amend:` comment on the run epic so the run's record is independent of the bead; and a line in the report's incident section.

The incident count is a quality metric for the specs, not for the agent. A run with zero means the corpus answered every question; a run with twelve means the corpus has twelve holes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No skill instructs an agent to stop and ask a human between the gate and the PR.
- [ ] `run-bead` records an incident the three required ways when a bead forces one of the four decisions.
- [ ] The coordinator does the same for decisions it makes itself.
- [ ] The four kinds are named where a worker meets them, not only where the coordinator does.
- [ ] The retro treats each incident as a candidate finding against a spec rather than a complaint about the run.
notes: Touches `run-bead`, the coordinator, and whatever specifies the report. The report's incident section itself is `sprint-report`'s bead; this one makes sure the material exists to put in it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Re-test session-start hook premises on bd 1.2.2; fix fresh-clone bootstrap
description:
## Problem

The hook's guards were justified by measurements taken on bd 1.2.1. Re-tested each on 1.2.2 against fresh clones of this repository.

Two were stale (already removed with the sync.remote change). Three hold. One guard was ordered so it could never fire. And the hook could not bootstrap a fresh clone at all.

## Findings

| Premise | Verdict on 1.2.2 |
|---|---|
| bootstrap's "already exists" probe matches the tracked .beads DIR, exits 0 silently | STALE — clones correctly; errors exit 1 when a real DB is in the way |
| a stale empty embeddeddolt blocks bootstrap | HOLDS for a real DB (empty dir does not); move-aside rescue verified |
| metadata dolt_database mismatch -> silent empty tracker | HOLDS — 318 issues invisible, bd stats and bd ready both exit 0 |
| prefix travels with the DB, config.yaml ignored | HOLDS — issue-prefix ignored, id minted agent-plugins-4731 |
| proxy substitutes the credential; refs/dolt 403s through it | HOLDS — proxy+garbage token pushed to refs/heads successfully |
| both credential key URL forms needed | HOLDS — only the form matching origin's URL answers |

## Bugs found and fixed

1. **The hook could not bootstrap a fresh clone.** `bd stats` exits non-zero with no database; under `set -euo pipefail` `_n="$(_count)"` killed the script silently (exit 1, two lines of output) before bootstrap ran. Present in the predecessor revision too, so long-standing.
2. **The metadata-name guard was unreachable.** Ordered after the issue count, the measured sequence was: count reads 0 -> hook moves the REAL database aside as stale -> re-clones under the wrong name -> guard sees the directory and stays silent. Moved before any tracker read and made fatal.
3. **The fatal handler mislabelled every cause** as "no write access".

## Success Criteria

- [x] Fresh clone bootstraps through the hook (318 issues, exit 0, clean tree)
- [x] Name mismatch is fatal, exit 1, database untouched
- [x] Stale foreign DB moved aside and bootstrapped
- [x] Live healthy repo pulls and exits 0

title: [bug] spec check reports 'passed' for a document it could not parse
description:
A document whose frontmatter parses as YAML but does not decode into the document envelope is indexed with a parse_error and no frontmatter (AC-SPEC-002.4, working as specified). corpus.Corpus.check then skips it — 'if entry.Frontmatter == nil { continue }', cli/core/corpus/check.go — and the run reports every rule as outcome 'passed' with zero findings.

Reproduced 2026-08-05 on this branch. A probe at specs/adrs/ADR-999-probe.md declaring 'status: totally-made-up' AND 'slug: adr-001' (already held by ADR-001):

  $ spec check specs/adrs/ADR-999-probe.md
  no findings
  checks:
    frontmatter/missing-property  passed
    frontmatter/schema            passed
    slug/duplicate                passed
    slug/pattern-mismatch         passed
  $ echo $?
  0

Two separate error-severity defects, reported as four passes. Not a stale-index artifact: it reproduces with specs/specs.json deleted first. 'spec index --out -' records the entry correctly, with the message and span — so the CLI HAS the fact and the checker declines to report it.

This inverts the FRD's own division of labour. REQ-SPEC-002's rationale is that the indexer exits zero on parse failures because 'a build failure is the checker's job, not the indexer's'. The checker does not do that job, so nothing does: the worst-formed document in a corpus is the one document 'spec check --strict' is guaranteed to be silent about, and it reports that silence as a pass.

The check.go doc comment states the current behaviour deliberately ('has already been reported through ... the member's own parse_error and is not revisited here'). That reasoning holds for an EXCLUSION — a file with no frontmatter is not a spec document. It does not hold for a parse error: that document declared itself a spec document and got the declaration wrong. And 'already reported' means reported in the index, an artifact 'spec check' never shows the caller.

SPEC GAP, not just a code bug. No AC covers it: AC-SPEC-002.4/002.5 govern the indexer, and REQ-SPEC-003's ACs all presuppose parsed frontmatter. Adding an AC to REQ-SPEC-003 is part of this work — approximately: 'WHEN a corpus member is indexed with a parse error, the CLI SHALL report a finding carrying that error's message and span, and SHALL NOT report any check as passed for that document.'

Design (worked out, not guessed):
  1. schemas/finding.strata — add a FindingFrontmatterParse variant to the
     FindingDetail union, carrying the parse error's message. The union's
     own doc comment already sanctions this: 'a later check adds a variant
     without changing the envelope that carries it'. Regenerate via
     scripts/generate-schemas.sh (needs strata).
  2. cli/core/finding — add RuleFrontmatterParse = 'frontmatter/parse' and
     a FrontmatterParse(path, at, message) constructor, matching the
     existing four.
  3. cli/core/corpus/check.go — in the entry.Frontmatter == nil branch,
     emit that finding when entry.ParseError != nil rather than
     'continue'. Correct the doc comment, which currently records the
     wrong behaviour as intended.
  4. cli/cmd/check.go — add the rule to checkRules so it is accounted for
     in the report and reachable via --only.
  5. Tests: a corpus fixture with an undecodable document asserting one
     finding rather than zero; a cmd-level snapshot case. Note that
     cli/profile/self_application_test.go would NOT have caught this — it
     asserts exclusions == 1 and findings == 0, and a parse-error entry is
     neither an exclusion nor a finding.

INTERIM MITIGATION IN PLACE: .github/workflows/checks.yml's corpus job
has a 'No document failed to parse' step that greps the emitted index for
parse_error entries. Delete that step when this lands — it exists only
because the check is silent.
acceptance_criteria: spec check reports an error-severity finding for a document indexed with a parse_error, and does not report any rule as passed for that document; exit status is non-zero; REQ-SPEC-003 carries an AC covering it; the interim workflow step in checks.yml is removed
notes:
REAL-WORLD TRIGGER (2026-08-05): the framework's own templates, via the authoring workflow the spec skill prescribes.

SKILL.md step 1 says copy a template from references/ as the starting point. Every template ships 'updated_at: <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ>' as a placeholder. SKILL.md step 7 says run 'spec check <path>'. Between those two steps — i.e. for the entire authoring session, which is exactly when an agent checks its work — the document carries a placeholder that fails RFC 3339 parsing, so the envelope decode fails and every check reports passed.

Reproduced by copying adr-template.md, filling in title/description/slug, and leaving updated_at as the template left it:

  $ spec check specs/adrs/ADR-018-caching-layer.md
  no findings
  checks:
    frontmatter/missing-property  passed
    frontmatter/schema            passed
    slug/duplicate                passed
    slug/pattern-mismatch         passed
  $ echo $?
  0

Note that updated_at is a REQUIRED property and frontmatter/missing-property also reports passed. The check that exists for this property is silent about it.

Also confirmed on a real committed file: plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md (bead 6n4, 'mapping value is not allowed in this context') indexes with a parse_error, and 'spec check --strict' over a corpus containing it exits 0.

SEVERITY IS INVERTED. Three realistic defects, same corpus:
  version: 1.2 (unquoted, YAML float)  -> REPORTED (frontmatter/schema)
  status: proposed (Nygard's classic)  -> SILENT
  updated_at: 2026-07-29 (date only)   -> SILENT
A typo in a value that still decodes is caught; a value that breaks the envelope is not. The worse the defect, the quieter the tool.

The third case is AC-SPEC-003.2's OWN worked example, verbatim: 'updated_at: 2026-07-29 fails an RFC 3339 date-time check, even though a YAML parser would coerce it to a valid timestamp before any check could see it.' Strictly the AC's WHEN-trigger arguably never fires, since the CLI never reaches validation — but the example the FRD chose to demonstrate the requirement with produces no finding at all. Whatever the lawyering, REQ-SPEC-003 illustrates itself with a case the implementation does not handle, which is strong evidence the intent is unmet rather than merely unspecified.

Scanned all 66 commits of history: zero instances of an envelope-breaking status or updated_at in committed docs/ or specs/ documents. The corpus has been careful, not protected — every document that would have triggered this was authored correctly by hand.
close_reason: spec check now reports frontmatter/parse at severity error for any member indexed with a parse error; AC-SPEC-003.6 added to REQ-SPEC-003; corpus regression tests plus the check-frontmatter-parse snapshot case; interim workflow step removed

title: specs.toml points [workspace].root at docs/, so the CLI indexes an empty corpus
description:
Found by orchestrator smoke-test of the binary built from bge.12, run from
the repository root:

    $ spec index --out -
    { "workspace": "agent-plugins", "entries": [], "exclusions": [
        { "path": "docs/session-bootstrap.md", "reason": "no-frontmatter" } ] }

    $ spec check
    no findings
    checks: frontmatter/schema passed, slug/duplicate passed, ...
    exit=0

`specs.toml` declares `[workspace].root = "docs"`. `docs/` holds exactly one
markdown file and no specification documents; the corpus is the 27 documents
under `specs/`. So every command answers over an EMPTY corpus:

- `check` reports "no findings" and exits 0 — a clean bill of health on
  nothing. This is the vacuous-pass failure mode, reproduced in the shipped
  product: identical in kind to `scripts/validate-corpus.py` searching
  `docs/` (`rfcs/inbox/feature-blueprint/rfc-0010` P1) and to the Definition
  of Done's `docs/` anchor, both already corrected.
- `slug-exists frd-spec-validation-cli` answers "not found" for a slug that
  exists.
- `next-id adr` answers 1 with sixteen ADRs in the corpus.

This is NOT a new decision: the corpus root was confirmed as `specs/` by the
author on 2026-08-04, recorded on agent-plugins-bge.14. `specs.toml` is the
one place that was never updated — it predates the reorg (last touched in
bb8ef2a).

Implemented in the orchestrator's own loop rather than delegated: it is a
one-line configuration correction applying an already-recorded decision.

## Retro

**Approach.** One line: `specs.toml` `[workspace].root` from `docs` to
`specs`. Implemented in the orchestrator loop rather than delegated — it
applies a decision the author already recorded on bge.14 (the corpus root
is `specs/`), so there was nothing to decide, and dispatching an agent for
one TOML line would cost more than it saves.

**How it was found — not by a test.** By smoke-testing the binary built
from bge.12 against the real repository. Every gate in this run was green
while the shipped CLI answered over an empty corpus. The unit and
integration suites each construct their own fixture roots, and bge.14's
self-application gate resolves `specs/` from the test file's own path, so
nothing in the suite ever reads the committed `[workspace].root`. That is
the real gap: no test asserts that the shipped configuration points at the
actual corpus.

**Verified after the change**, from the repository root:

- `index --out -` gives 26 entries, 1 exclusion (was 0 entries)
- `slug-exists frd-spec-validation-cli` resolves to
  `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md` (was "not found")
- `next-id adr` gives 17 (was 1)
- `check` reports one finding — the known `/plan` additionalProperties
  violation at `spec-index-blueprint.md:12:7` — and exits 1 (was "no
  findings", exit 0)

That last line is the point: exit status now reflects a real defect instead
of an empty corpus, which is AC-SPEC-006.6 and AC-SPEC-006.9 doing their
job against real data for the first time.

**Implicit decision.** `docs/session-bootstrap.md` is left out of the
corpus; it is not a specification document and correctly falls outside the
new root.

**Fourth instance of one root cause.** The `specs/` reorg left `docs/`
references behind in `scripts/validate-corpus.py` (rfc-0010 P1), the
blueprint's Definition of Done, the blueprint's Tracker Reconciliation
(agent-plugins-mvx), and now `specs.toml`. Each was found by a different
mechanism and none by the others — a sweep for any remaining is warranted.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `specs.toml` declares `[workspace].root = "specs"`.
- [ ] `spec index --out -` emits entries for the corpus (27 documents), not an empty list.
- [ ] `spec slug-exists frd-spec-validation-cli` reports found, with its path.
- [ ] `spec next-id adr` returns one greater than the highest ADR in use.
- [ ] `cd cli && go test ./...` still passes, including the bge.14 self-application gate.
- [ ] `spec check` exit status reflects real findings rather than an empty corpus.

metadata.tier_reason: Implemented in the orchestrator loop; one-line config fix applying a recorded decision, but it changes what every command sees so the gates must be re-run.

title: The slug-less anchor form is omitted by spec refs and not rewritten by spec links
description:
agent-plugins-clau made the slug-less anchor form `[[#Heading]]` legal:
reference/unresolved now skips a reference whose slug half is empty and
whose anchor resolved against the containing document (AC-SPECREF-002.12).

Two consumers of the same reference still treat it as broken, because both
key off the SLUG half resolving and an empty slug never resolves.

Measured on a throwaway corpus (one document, slug adr-098, body `See
[[#Overview]] below.`, its own `## Overview` heading), with a binary built
from cli/ at the commit that closed agent-plugins-clau:

1. `spec refs 'adr-098#Overview'` -> exit 0, `references: []`. Same for
   `spec refs adr-098`. The document holds a reference whose anchor
   resolves to exactly that heading and the blast-radius query returns an
   empty list. Cause: corpus.indexReferences adds only RESOLVED references
   to the inbound index.

2. `spec links docs/adrs/adr-098-good.md` -> exit 0, and the emitted
   document still carries `See [[#Overview]] below.` verbatim rather than a
   rewritten markdown link. Cause: mdlinks.resolveOne takes its
   !isCorpusDocument branch for the same empty slug.

A wrong answer to a blast-radius query is not visible to any gate, which is
what makes (1) worse than the check defect that was fixed.

The decision recorded on agent-plugins-clau (owner, review of PR #38 on
rfc-0025 P6) is that the form is valid. Deciding what these two commands
should do with it is the work: refs plausibly treats a resolved self-anchor
as an inbound reference to its own document; links plausibly rewrites it to
the heading's fragment identifier, which markdown.Identifier already
derives. Both need a criterion in the owning FRD before the code changes.

comments.author: dev-59ic-g
comments.text:
retro: The bead named both consumers' causes exactly — corpus.indexReferences admits only resolved references, mdlinks.resolveOne takes its !isCorpusDocument branch — and both were true where I found them. That is the difference from agent-plugins-clau's retro, where an anchor pointed at a file that needed nothing: an anchor naming the LINE OF LOGIC rather than the file is what made this dispatchable cold.

The one thing the bead could not settle, and the dispatch had to: which FRD owns which behaviour. Working it out cost a read of four requirement blocks across two FRDs. What settled it was that the fix is one change to the inbound graph, so the criterion belongs beside AC-SPECREF-001.3 (the graph) rather than in either query feature (FEAT-SPECREF-003, FEAT-SPECANCH-003) that reads it. A bead that says 'this needs a criterion' could say which artifact holds the CAUSE, since that is where the criterion lands.

comments.author: dev-59ic-g
comments.text: retro: "$SCRIPTS"/bb-checks.py exits 1 in this container while agent-plugins-sqh6 is open. Measured this run: === strata-docs FAILED (exit 2), 'error: source not found: /root/.cache/strata-src/docs/public/strata.llm.md'; every other check green (format, vet, build, test-go, skills, shared-refs, schemas, corpus, ref-links, template-drift, skills-strict). Identical to what dev-59ic-f recorded on agent-plugins-clau, so this is now the second consecutive bead whose gate cannot go green for a reason outside its scope, and the second dispatch prompt that had to name it in advance for the failure to be readable. The prompt naming it is the only thing distinguishing 'broken elsewhere, already filed' from 'yours' — nothing in bb-checks.py's output does.

comments.author: dev-59ic-g
comments.text: retro: AC-SPECREF-001.3 reads 'inbound references ... derived from the outbound references of all other corpus members'. Read strictly, 'all other' makes the defect conformant — the one reference whose target is the document holding it is excluded by the criterion's own words. It is not a prohibition (the Then clause states what must be included, not what must not be), so AC-SPECREF-001.8 extends rather than contradicts it, and the new criterion's rationale says so explicitly. Flagging because 'all other' is the kind of incidental phrasing that reads as deliberate scoping two years later, and because the append-only rule means the wording cannot be repaired in place.

comments.author: dev-59ic-g
comments.text:
retro: Two consequences of the same empty slug survive this bead and are filed rather than fixed, both measured with a binary built from cli/ after the change:

- agent-plugins-jbx3 (P3): the refs answer now carries the self-anchor with resolution: {state: unresolved} beside rows reading resolved. A --json consumer filtering on resolution.state == 'resolved' drops it again — the same wrong answer AC-SPECREF-001.8 removes, one layer out. This bead deliberately took the do-nothing option, per the dispatch's 'do not invent a new top-level shape if an existing field already carries it'; Reference.Path does carry the origin. Filed so the owner can revisit rather than inherit it.
- agent-plugins-vvzj (P3): links/unresolved on an anchor-only citation reaching no heading reports '[[]] matches no corpus document' — finding.UnresolvedCitation is given ref.Slug, which is empty. The check half of the same reference reads '[[#Nowhere]] matches no document's slug', because finding.UnresolvedReference is given ref.Text too. Negative-case only, and unchanged by this bead.

title: sync-strata-docs.sh breaks: upstream renamed docs/ to site/
description:
scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh line 54 hardcodes 'docs/public/strata.llm.md'. Upstream strata-lang/strata renamed that directory: 'c0df36a Rename docs/ to site/ to match the @strata-lang/site package (#305)'.

Measured in this container:
  git -C /root/.cache/strata-src log --oneline -1  -> c0df36a Rename docs/ to site/ ...
  ls /root/.cache/strata-src/docs/public/strata.llm.md  -> No such file or directory
  ls /root/.cache/strata-src/site/public/strata.llm.md  -> exists
  grep -n 'docs/public' scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh    -> 54:docs/public/strata.llm.md<TAB>strata-llm-reference.md<TAB>raw
  bb-checks.py strata-docs -> EXIT=1, 'error: source not found: /root/.cache/strata-src/docs/public/strata.llm.md', 'strata-docs FAILED (exit 2)'

The declared 'strata-docs' check therefore fails in any session whose strata checkout has fast-forwarded past c0df36a, which makes the next bead close in that container fail its gate. The SessionStart hook already advises running this script ('note: vendored strata docs are behind'), and running it now fails.

Not caused by run agent-plugins-59ic: head passed 12/12 twice during the run, and only this one check fails now. The hook fast-forwarded the checkout mid-session (built-commit moved from c8a8251 to c0df36a).

CI is unaffected — PR #38 shows 8/8 green — because CI has no strata checkout and validates the committed vendored copy. This is a developer-environment break, not a CI one, which is why nothing caught it.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] sync-strata-docs.sh resolves the source path against the upstream layout rather than hardcoding docs/public/
[ ] bb-checks.py strata-docs exits 0 against a strata checkout at or after c0df36a
[ ] The script fails with a nameable error, not a bare 'source not found', when upstream moves a path again
close_reason: sync-strata-docs.sh resolves MAP suffixes against the installed release's tree (v0.8.0 -> site/, v0.7.0 -> docs/); unresolvable or ambiguous suffix exits 2 naming the entry; bb-checks.py strata-docs EXIT=0. Branch claude/jolly-hypatia-wn2chb, PR brettcallaghan/agent-plugins#43.

title: An unverified check reports 'passed' in the same run that says it could not run
description:
`Report.Ran` overwrites the `CheckOutcomeUnverified` that `Report.Add` had
just recorded, so a rule that reported it could not run is rolled up as
`passed`.

In `cli/core/finding/finding.go`, `Report.Ran` reads:

    r.Request(rule)
    state := r.results[rule]
    if state.failed {
        state.outcome = specmodel.CheckOutcomeFailed
    } else {
        state.outcome = specmodel.CheckOutcomePassed
    }
    state.reason = ""

`state.failed` is set only in `Report.Add`'s non-unverified branch — the
branch guarded by `if f.Severity == SeverityUnverified` sets `outcome` but
NOT `failed`. `cli/cmd/check.go` calls `report.Add(f)` for every finding and
then `report.Ran(rule)` for every rule afterwards, so an unverified outcome is
always overwritten by `Passed`, and its reason string is wiped.

## Measured

On this branch (a852925), binary built from `cli/` with `go build -o spec
./spec`, against a throwaway corpus whose `specs.toml` declares workspace root
`docs` and profile `spec-driven-dev`, holding one approved ADR plus
`docs/features/zzz.feature` containing:

    # See [[#Anywhere]] for context.
    @FRD-EX-001
    Feature: Example

`spec check` printed BOTH of these in one report:

    docs/features/zzz.feature:
      reference/unresolved-anchor  unverified  1:9  check reference/unresolved-anchor could not run: no headings are recorded for docs/features/zzz.feature

    checks:
      reference/unresolved-anchor  passed

That is the vacuous pass the outcome accounting exists to prevent, and the
reading AC-SPECANCH-002.4 forbids ("the CLI does not report the anchor as
resolved").

## Why this run owns it

At `base_sha` 225751e the same shape existed in `Report.Ran` but was
unreachable: `cli/core/finding/finding.go` carried the comment "No constant
here names a check that reports [SeverityUnverified]", and
`git grep -n "finding.Unverified(" 225751e -- 'cli/**/*.go'` returns no
non-test emitter. This run added the first and only emitter —
`resolveAnchor`'s `NewAnchorResolutionUnverified` in
`cli/core/references/anchor.go`, surfaced through
`finding.Unverified(finding.RuleUnresolvedAnchor, ...)` in
`cli/core/corpus/check.go`. The latent bug is older; the observable defect is
this run's.

## Reachability (bounds the severity)

Measured: a Markdown corpus member with no headings does NOT hit this path. It
records an entry with an empty heading list, so `known` is true and the rule
correctly reports an error — measured output:

    reference/unresolved-anchor  error  12:7  no heading named "Ghost" in docs/adrs/adr-700-noheads.md

The unverified branch is reached only for a document whose path has no
headings entry at all — that is, a non-Markdown corpus document (a `.feature`
file) carrying an anchor reference. Narrow today; the accounting defect is
general and will bite the next check that reports unverified.

A second instance of the same mechanism, NOT separately measured: `Report.Add`
sets `outcome = Unverified` without consulting `state.failed`, so an unverified
finding added after an error would mask that failure for any consumer reading
the outcome without calling `Ran`.

No snapshot case covers an unverified outcome:
`grep -rl unverified cli/testdata/cases/` matches only `help-check`.

## Anchors

`Report.Ran` and `Report.Add` in `cli/core/finding/finding.go`; the `Add`/`Ran`
call order in `cli/cmd/check.go`; the emitter in `cli/core/corpus/check.go`.

Filed by review pass 1 of run agent-plugins-59ic.

title: The slug-less anchor form adr-012 blesses always reports reference/unresolved
description:
`[[#Heading]]` — a reference to a section of the referring document
itself — is the form specs/adrs/adr-012-reference-conventions.md
mandates: "A section of the referring document itself is referenced by
an anchor with the slug omitted: \`[[#Terminology]]\`." The anchor
resolves correctly (AC-SPECANCH-002.6 is implemented and covered), but
the SLUG half of the same reference reports an error every time, so the
form adr-012 blesses cannot be used in a corpus that gates on
`spec check --strict`.

Measured on a throwaway corpus with a document declaring
`slug: adr-098` whose body contains `[[#Overview]]` and whose own
`## Overview` heading exists:

  spec index --out - | jq '.references[] | select(.anchor != null)'
    -> resolution={"state":"unresolved"},
       anchor_resolution={"state":"resolved", heading "Overview"}

  spec check --strict
    -> docs/good.md:
         reference/unresolved  error  14:19
           [[#Overview]] matches no document's slug

This predates the anchor feature — the slug half has always resolved
against declared slugs and an empty slug matches none — but anchor
resolution is what makes the contradiction visible: the tool now says
the anchor resolved and the reference is broken, in the same run.

No reference in this repository's corpus uses the form today (all
eleven anchored references carry a slug), so no gate fails now.

The fix is a decision this bug does not make: either
`reference/unresolved` skips a reference whose slug half is empty and
whose anchor resolved against the containing document, or adr-012
withdraws the slug-less form. The first is the reading
AC-SPECANCH-002.6 implies.

Anchors: the `reference/unresolved` rule in
`cli/core/corpus/check.go`; `resolveAnchor` and its slug-less branch
in `cli/core/references/anchor.go`; the quoted sentence in
`specs/adrs/adr-012-reference-conventions.md`.

comments.author: review-59ic
comments.text:
review-59ic (run agent-plugins-59ic, review pass 1): the declared reviewer
re-found this defect independently. Not re-filed — this bead has it. Recording
two CONSEQUENCES this bead does not currently mention, both measured here,
because they change its blast radius from "check reports an error" to "the
run's own headline query under-reports".

Corpus used for both, on branch head a852925 with a binary built from `cli/`
via `go build -o spec ./spec`. `specs.toml` declares workspace root `docs`,
profile `spec-driven-dev`. One member, `docs/adrs/adr-800-current.md`, slug
`adr-800-current`, containing a `## Local Section` heading and the body text
`See [[#Local Section]] below.`

1. `spec refs` SILENTLY OMITS the reference. Measured:

       $ spec refs 'adr-800-current#Local Section'
       slug: adr-800-current
       anchor: Local Section
       direction: inbound
       declared: true
       references: []

   Exit 0. The document contains a reference whose anchor resolves to exactly
   that heading, and the blast-radius query — the thing agent-plugins-rc14.7
   was built for — returns an empty list. The cause is the same empty slug:
   `corpus.indexReferences` adds only RESOLVED references to the inbound
   index, and the slug half never resolves.

2. `spec links` cannot rewrite it. `mdlinks.resolveOne` takes its
   `!isCorpusDocument` branch for the same reason, so the reference is emitted
   as `links/unresolved` and is not rewritten. NOT independently measured here
   — `spec links` requires a path argument and I did not construct the case;
   stated from reading `cli/core/mdlinks/mdlinks.go`, so treat it as
   unverified until someone runs it.

Consequence 1 is measured and is the one that matters: this bead's note that
"no gate fails now" is true of `spec check --strict`, but `spec refs` gives a
WRONG answer rather than a failing one, and a wrong answer to a blast-radius
query is not visible to any gate.

Classification for this run's record: still out of the run's authorized scope.
The root cause — an empty slug never resolving — predates `base_sha` 225751e,
so this is a row-3 finding under the review skill's criteria, and
`admit_review_findings` is false for run agent-plugins-59ic in any case.

comments.author: coordinator-59ic
comments.text:
DECISION (owner, in review of PR #38 on rfc-0025 P6): EXEMPT THE FORM. An anchor-only reference to a heading in the enclosing document is valid and must not be reported. adr-012 keeps its slug-less bullet; AC-SPECANCH-002.6 stands. Do NOT take the withdraw-the-form alternative — it is now recorded as rejected.

Owner's words: 'It sounds like we do not support anchor only references to headings in the enclosing document -- we should. If I read this correctly, we are currently reporting an error for valid anchor only references inside the enclosing document. If the references point to a valid heading inside the document then no error should be reported so I think this is the option we want.'

So the work is: reference/unresolved skips a reference whose slug half is empty AND whose anchor resolved against the containing document; frd-spec-reference-integrity gains the criterion saying so. Raised to P1 — this is now a decided defect with a known fix, not an open question.

comments.author: dev-59ic-f
comments.text:
retro: The decision this bead carries was unambiguous and the fix was six
lines, but the bead's own anchors pointed at resolveAnchor in
cli/core/references/anchor.go as a place to change. It is not one: the
slug-less branch there (AnchorTarget returning ref.Path) is exactly what
AC-SPECANCH-002.6 requires and was already correct. The whole change lives
in unresolvedReferenceFinding in cli/core/corpus/check.go. Listing a file
as an anchor reads as "expect to edit this"; it cost a read of a file that
turned out to need nothing. An anchor list that separated "edit here" from

title: A work order must not state a value, signature or fix it derived by inference rather than measured
description:
## Problem

A work order may state a value, a signature or a fix that nobody ran — derived
by INFERENCE from something that was measured — and the Work Order Definition
of Ready has no check that catches it. The derived statement reads exactly like
the measured one beside it, so the implementing agent acts on it.

Three of the four beads dispatched in swarm run agent-plugins-d7w5's second
pass reported their defect CORRECTLY and prescribed something wrong or
unreachable. In every case the measurement in the order was sound and the
arithmetic, signature or fix built on top of it was not.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (quoted from the run's findings and beads; record:
docs/retros/2026-09-04-d7w5-spec-corpus-structure-extraction.md).

(1) A NON-EXISTENT AST FIELD. agent-plugins-d7w5.9's originating finding
proposed deciding a heading's written form by asking the AST — the bead records
it as "REJECTED — asking the AST node, which is what the review finding
proposed ('heading.Type()' / the AST kind)". Re-measured at the point of use by
the implementing agent, finding d7w5.9#2: "goldmark v1.8.5 in this container,
/root/go/pkg/mod/github.com/yuin/goldmark@v1.8.5. (1) sed -n '200,230p'
ast/block.go -> 'type Heading struct { BaseBlock; Level int }' ... one kind for
both forms. (2) grep -rn 'NewHeading(' parser/ ast/ ->
parser/setext_headings.go:70, parser/atx_heading.go:95, :103 all call
ast.NewHeading(level); no other constructor and no form argument. (3) the only
SetAttribute calls are author-written {#id} attributes gated on the opt-in
WithHeadingAttribute option; neither parser sets anything that names the written
form. Conclusion: the public AST genuinely does not carry the distinction on the
pinned version." The prescribed fix had nothing to read. This one was caught at
GROOMING and corrected before dispatch — which is the argument for putting the
rule in the readiness gate, since the other two were not.

(2) UNMEASURED STRING ARITHMETIC ON TOP OF A CORRECT TABLE. Finding d7w5.8#2
(kind stale): "The bead's Design states post-filter identifier values that the
chosen fix does not produce. Its MEASURED table (render output) is correct; the
sentence deriving identifiers from it is an unmeasured inference and two of its
four values are wrong. evidence: the Design says 'After Identifier's character
filter these give 1-overview, 2-overview, -bullet and 3-design-present', and the
Acceptance repeats 'Identifier(\"- Bullet\") is -bullet, and the identifier of
the heading text 3. `## Design` present is 3-design-present'. Measured with the
fix in place, via a temporary in-package probe calling rendered() and
Identifier(): '- Bullet' -> identifier '--bullet' (Design said '-bullet');
'3. `## Design` present' -> identifier '3--design-present' (Design said
'3-design-present'). Every RENDER above matches the Design's measured table byte
for byte, so the parser change is exactly what was specified; only the
arithmetic applied to it afterwards is wrong. Cause: the documented derivation
removes a disallowed character and then maps each REMAINING space to a hyphen,
and does not collapse or trim ... So '- Bullet' contributes the literal '-' AND
the space's '-'. The Design's derivation silently dropped one of the two." The
cost: finding d7w5.8#3 records that the bead "AMENDED an acceptance criterion
rather than the code", after weighing and rejecting four consequences of making
the AC's strings true instead.

(3) A PINNED SIGNATURE THAT COULD NOT EXPRESS WHAT ITS OWN CALLER NEEDED.
Finding d7w5.7#2: "An acceptance criterion is met in substance but not in its
literal wording, because the Design's own prescribed signature makes the literal
reading unreachable. evidence: AC — 'frontmatter.Parse and the exported locator
share one implementation — the delimiter constants are read in exactly one
function.' Design — 'export a locator ... e.g. func Locate(src []byte)
(span.Region, bool)'. With that signature Locate cannot distinguish 'src carries
no block' from 'a block is opened and never closed', yet Parse must, because
those are two of its three documented outcomes (a nil,nil versus a located
error). Parse therefore keeps the bytes.HasPrefix(src, []byte(openingDelimiter))
test and the len(openingDelimiter) it measures the error span with — so
openingDelimiter is read in two functions however the code is arranged, short of
changing the signature the Design pinned."

(4) AN ENUMERATED FIX THAT ASSERTED SUFFICIENCY. The fourth pass-2 bead did not
prescribe a wrong value, but its Design named the complete set of changes and
that set was incomplete — finding d7w5.11#3: "The bead's three named code fixes
would have left the guarantee still false; two further divergences existed that
the bead's reproduction did not reach. evidence: the Design named three changes
(tag-presence in jsonName, the flatten guard, the PkgPath skip). Implementing
only those leaves structFields as a DEPTH-FIRST walk with no conflict handling,
while encoding/json resolves fields BREADTH-first and then applies dominance
rules. ... (a) A shallower field does not hide a promoted one of the same name
... YAML with only the three named fixes: would be ['name' 'deep' 'name'] — the
key 'name' TWICE, carrying two different values." The agent ported
encoding/json's typeFields in full instead; cost, from the same finding:
"cli/cmd/yaml.go grew by roughly 180 lines". An enumeration of fixes is a claim
about code nobody has written, and it reads to a fresh agent as the boundary of
the work.

WHAT IT COSTS. Each of the three cost the implementing agent an acceptance-
criterion amendment or a mid-bead scope decision, taken alone, mid-session,
against a work order that read as already decided. That is the specific failure
the Definition of Ready exists to prevent: a fresh agent with no session context
cannot tell a measured value from one inferred from a measurement, so it either
implements the wrong thing or spends the session re-deriving what the order
claimed to have settled. The second cost is silent: where the derivation happens
to be right, nothing distinguishes it from the case where it is not, so the
practice survives every run it does not break.

THE RULE ALREADY EXISTS ONE DOCUMENT LATER. AGENTS.md's "Tool claims are
measured at the point of use" binds an agent stating a claim: "Before you act on
such a claim, or restate it anywhere, run the command and read the output ...
Where you cannot run it, mark the claim unverified and say what would settle
it." A work order is exactly the surface that section's own table names as
"read by the implementing agent, cold, without the conversation that retracted
it", audited by "grooming, once; after that nobody". This bead moves that
requirement one step earlier, to the gate that grooming runs.

ANCHORS.

* specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md — the single definition of
  ready. Its "## Contents" section opens "The nine checks a work order must pass
  before dispatch:" and the numbered checks live under "## The checks". This is
  where the rule lands.
* scripts/sync-shared-references.sh — its MAP maps that file to both groom-beads
  and spec; the generated copies are
  plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md
  and plugin/skills/spec/references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md.
  Declared check id shared-refs runs it with --check.
* plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md — must NOT grow. Measured at the point of
  use, 2026-09-04: `wc -c plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md` -> 19825, and
  `grep -n BODY_BYTE_MAX scripts/check-skills.sh` -> "43:BODY_BYTE_MAX = 20000"
  with the size test at line 130 calling warn(); `--strict` turns warnings into
  errors (line 207: "if errors or (strict and warnings)"). So 175 bytes of
  headroom before a strict run fails. The rule cannot live there, which is a
  second reason it belongs in the standard.

RELATED WORK. agent-plugins-3oiv edits the same standard (check 8) in the same
retro round; whoever takes the second of the two lands on a changed file and a
bumped version. The two rules are independent — 3oiv is about declaring a
change's blast radius, this one about the provenance of a stated value.
design:
## Design

CHOSEN: add a tenth check to specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md
— "Stated values are measured, not derived" — and update the "## Contents"
list and its opening line ("The nine checks a work order must pass before
dispatch:" becomes "The ten checks ...") in the same edit.

WHAT THE CHECK SAYS. A work order SHALL state, as a fact, only what was
measured. Any literal value, signature, identifier, file path, count or
enumerated fix that a groomer DERIVED from a measurement rather than observing
directly is either (a) run, and the check names the command and its output
beside the value, or (b) marked unverified in place, naming what would settle
it. The check applies to the Problem, Design and Acceptance sections alike,
because the three measured instances that produced it landed one in each: a
prescribed API that does not exist on the pinned dependency, an acceptance
criterion asserting two identifier strings computed by hand from a correct
render table, and a Design-pinned function signature that could not express
what its own caller needed.

Two clauses the wording must carry, because both were paid on run
agent-plugins-d7w5:

1. AN ENUMERATED FIX ASSERTS SUFFICIENCY. "These three changes close it" is a
   claim about code nobody wrote yet, and it carries the same burden as a
   literal value. Where a groomer names the fix, the order says whether the fix
   was run; where it was not, the order says the implementing agent is to
   re-derive it and that the enumeration is not a boundary on scope.
2. A DERIVATION IS NOT A MEASUREMENT, however short. The one that cost this run
   an amended acceptance criterion was two hyphens deep: a correct measured
   render table, then one sentence applying the documented character filter to
   it by hand.

WHERE, AND WHY NOT ELSEWHERE. Rejected: folding the rule into check 3
(`## Design` present) and check 4 (`## Acceptance` criteria) as two sentences.
It applies to any order that states a literal in any of its three text
sections, so splitting it gives two half-statements that each read as local
advice about that section; and check 9 ("No open decisions") is its neighbour
in spirit — an unverified derived value IS an open decision wearing a settled
value's clothes — but check 9 is about a choice the order declines to make,
not about a claim it makes without grounds. A tenth check is the honest shape.
Rejected: a script. "Which of these values was inferred" is not mechanizable
from the text; the check is enforced by grooming, which is what every check in
this document is.

FORM. Prose under a new "### 10. Stated values are measured, not derived"
heading, with one worked example drawn from the measured instance — a correct
render table, the sentence deriving identifiers from it by hand, and the two
values that came out wrong — and the two clauses above stated as requirements
rather than as narrative. Keep the example to the shape of the mistake; the
run's own history belongs in the commit message, not in the standard.

CONSTRAINT. specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md carries
version: "1.5" in its frontmatter and the generated copies repeat it in their
header banner. Bump it and regenerate with scripts/sync-shared-references.sh in
the same change, or the declared check shared-refs
(scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check) fails.

NOT IN SCOPE. The rule is not retro-applied to open work orders in this
tracker; it binds grooming from the point it lands.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md carries a tenth check
stating that a work order states as fact only what was measured, and that any
value, signature, identifier or enumerated fix DERIVED from a measurement is
either accompanied by the command and output that establish it, or marked
unverified in place with what would settle it
[ ] That check states explicitly that it applies to the Problem, Design and
Acceptance sections alike
[ ] That check states that an enumerated fix ("these three changes close it")
asserts sufficiency and carries the same burden as a literal value, and that
where the fix was not run the order says the implementing agent is to re-derive
it and that the enumeration does not bound scope
[ ] The check carries one worked example of a derivation applied by hand to a
correct measurement, with the wrong values it produced
[ ] The document's "## Contents" section lists the new check and its opening
line reads "The ten checks a work order must pass before dispatch:" — no
occurrence of "nine checks" remains in that file
[ ] The document's frontmatter version is bumped from "1.5"
[ ] Both generated copies —
plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md
and plugin/skills/spec/references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md —
are regenerated in the same change and carry the bumped version in their banner
[ ] scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check exits 0
[ ] scripts/check-skills.sh --strict exits 0
[ ] plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md is unchanged in size or smaller; the
rule is not copied into it
[ ] The three findings that produced the rule are not cited by id in the
standard or in either generated copy — a skill file is exported to other
projects, where this project's issue ids resolve to nothing; cite them in the
commit message instead

metadata.tier_reason: Authors a normative readiness rule that must separate a measured statement from one inferred from a measurement without demanding a citation for every word a groomer writes, inside a generated-copy pipeline where the source, two vendored copies and a version banner land together.

title: The outbox README and triage-issue still say we vend every skill we run, so triage would sweep the swarm deliveries into this backlog
description:
Two documents in this repository still say this project is its own downstream for
every skill issue it files. It no longer is, and the consequence is not
theoretical: `triage-issue` would sweep the ten swarm-plugin issues run
`agent-plugins-d7w5`'s retro just wrote into `.sf/outbox/swarm/` straight back
into this backlog — a backlog that cannot act on them, which is exactly the
accumulation the audience split exists to prevent.

WHAT IS THERE NOW (verified 2026-09-04 by reading each file).

1. `.sf/outbox/README.md`, final section headed "## In this repository":

   > **We vend the skills we run**, so we are our own downstream: `triage-issue`
   > sweeps this directory into our own tracker rather than anyone forwarding
   > anything. The mechanism is identical; the hop is just short.

2. `.claude/skills/triage-issue/SKILL.md`, under "## Inputs", the first bullet
   (line-number hint: around 43-47, but match on the quoted string):

   > - **`.sf/outbox/<skill>/*.md`** — a project that ran a sprint and
   >   reported a finding about a skill it does not own. The common case, and
   >   **this repository's own outbox is one of them**: we vend the skills we
   >   run, so we are our own downstream and sweep `.sf/outbox/` here without
   >   anyone forwarding anything.

3. `swarm.toml`'s `[retros]` block says the opposite, and is the authority both
   the run and this bead follow:

   > this repository vends the `sf` skills — `spec`, `groom-beads`,
   > `groom-feature-blueprint`, `retro-spec`, `retro-skill` — so an issue about
   > one of those is ordinary work in this tracker and belongs in it as a bead.
   >
   > It no longer vends `bead-bonanza` or the sprint subprocesses; those are the
   > `swarm` plugin's (brettcallaghan/swarm). A finding against one of THOSE
   > cannot be acted on here. ... file such a finding into `.sf/outbox` for
   > delivery there, and leave this key unset so everything else stays a bead.

MEASURED, so the split is not a matter of opinion:

    $ ls plugin/skills/
    groom-beads  groom-feature-blueprint  retro-skill  retro-spec  spec

    $ ls plugin/skills/triage-issue
    ls: cannot access 'plugin/skills/triage-issue': No such file or directory

Five vended skills, none of them `swarm` and none of them `triage-issue`.
`.claude/skills/` holds symlinks to those five plus two real directories,
`strata` and `triage-issue`, which are repo-local and are not vended.
`agent-plugins-g990` records the 2026-09-03 migration of the swarm work to
`brettcallaghan/swarm`.

WHAT IT COSTS. `.sf/outbox/swarm/` now holds ten issues against a plugin this
repository does not own. Under the rule as written, the next triage pass adopts
them as beads here. Each is then either worked in the wrong repository, or sits
open forever as a proposal nobody here can act on — and a channel that
accumulates un-actionable proposals is one its owners learn to ignore, which is
the failure the outbox README itself names two paragraphs above the sentence
that causes it.

ANCHORS.
- `.sf/outbox/README.md` — the section headed "## In this repository".
- `.claude/skills/triage-issue/SKILL.md` — the "## Inputs" bullet beginning
  "**`.sf/outbox/<skill>/*.md`**".
- `swarm.toml` — the `[retros]` block, the authority; not edited by this bead.
- `.sf/outbox/swarm/` — ten files dated 2026-09-04, the instances at stake.
design:
Correct both documents to state the split `swarm.toml` already declares, and
state it as a per-directory rule rather than as a fact about this repository —
so it stays true the next time a plugin moves in or out.

THE RULE BOTH DOCUMENTS ADOPT. `.sf/outbox/<skill>/` is swept into this tracker
only where `<skill>` is one this repository vends. The vended set is exactly what
`plugin/skills/` contains — today `spec`, `groom-beads`,
`groom-feature-blueprint`, `retro-spec`, `retro-skill`. A subdirectory naming
anything else is a DELIVERY: it is forwarded to the repository that vends that
skill and is never adopted as a bead here. `.sf/outbox/swarm/` is the current
instance, and its destination is `brettcallaghan/swarm`.

Anchoring the rule on `plugin/skills/` rather than on a written list is the point
of the change: a list is a second place to be wrong, and the reason these two
documents are wrong today is that the vended set moved on 2026-09-03
(`agent-plugins-g990`) and the prose did not. Rejected: naming the five skills
inline in both files, which reproduces the same failure the next time one moves.

`.sf/outbox/README.md`. Replace the body of "## In this repository" with the
rule. Keep the section — a reader arriving at the outbox needs to know what
happens to what they put there — and keep the surrounding paragraphs unchanged,
including "Nothing here is ever filed in this project's own tracker", which is
what the corrected section must stop contradicting for the vended-skill case.
The correct reading is that a vended skill's issue is not "filed from the
outbox"; it is ordinary work that a retro files as a bead directly, per
`swarm.toml`'s `[retros]`. Say that, rather than describing a sweep.

`.claude/skills/triage-issue/SKILL.md`. Rewrite the `.sf/outbox/<skill>/*.md`
input bullet so the channel it describes is the one that actually exists: issues
about skills this repository does NOT vend, held for delivery and not triaged
here. If the skill needs an inbox bullet for its own vended-skill issues, that is
the bullet immediately below it ("This repository's own retro output"), which is
already correct and needs no change.

CONSTRAINT. `.claude/skills/triage-issue/` is a real directory, not a symlink
into `plugin/skills/`, so `triage-issue` is repo-local and its SKILL.md is edited
in place — there is no vendored copy and `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` does
not touch it. It is still a skill, so `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` governs
its size and shape; the rewrite is a replacement of comparable length, not an
addition.

NOT IN SCOPE. Changing `swarm.toml`, changing what `triage-issue` does with a
delivery once forwarding exists, and building a forwarding mechanism. This bead
makes the documents true; who carries a delivery to `brettcallaghan/swarm` is the
outbox owner's call, which `.sf/outbox/README.md` already says.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `.sf/outbox/README.md`'s "## In this repository" section states that `.sf/outbox/<skill>/` is swept into this tracker only when `<skill>` is one this repository vends, and that any other subdirectory is a delivery to the repository that vends that skill
- [ ] That section identifies the vended set as the contents of `plugin/skills/`, rather than listing skill names inline
- [ ] It names `.sf/outbox/swarm/` as a current delivery whose destination is `brettcallaghan/swarm`, and states that its contents are not adopted as beads here
- [ ] `.claude/skills/triage-issue/SKILL.md`'s `.sf/outbox/<skill>/*.md` input bullet no longer asserts that this repository sweeps its own outbox for every skill, and instead states the vended/not-vended split
- [ ] Neither document contradicts `swarm.toml`'s `[retros]` block; `swarm.toml` itself is unchanged
- [ ] `.sf/outbox/README.md`'s existing statement "Nothing here is ever filed in this project's own tracker" is either kept and made consistent with the corrected section, or replaced by text that draws the same line without contradicting it
- [ ] The ten files under `.sf/outbox/swarm/` are untouched — no pruning, no adoption
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` exits 0

metadata.tier_reason: A bounded two-file prose correction whose target text, replacement rule and authority are all quoted on the bead; the only care needed is keeping the outbox README internally consistent while it changes.

title: groom-beads has no rule that a 'declare and regenerate' bead must declare the emitter, fixtures, snapshots and standards its regeneration reaches
description:
A bead scoped to "declare the shape and regenerate" cannot be delivered inside
that scope, and the Work Order Definition of Ready has no check that catches it.
Three of the four beads in swarm run `agent-plugins-d7w5` under-declared their
surface in the same direction, each measured and recorded as a `retro:scope`
finding.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (quoted from the run's findings; record:
docs/retros/2026-09-04-d7w5-spec-corpus-structure-extraction.md).

`f6tl.1#2` — "Declaring the two properties as REQUIRED lists forced changes
outside 'declare in Strata and regenerate' — the emitter, two hand-maintained
input fixtures and three unit tests — none of which the bead's Design or Anchors
anticipate. The bead's Design is 'Declare the shapes in schemas/index.strata and
regenerate', Anchors name only schemas/index.strata,
cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json and cli/core/specmodel. Measured after
regenerating, before any further edit — 'cd cli && go test ./...' rc=1 with three
distinct failures: (a) specindex_test.go 'unmarshal: IndexEntry: required field
\"headings\" is missing or null'; (b) cache_test.go 'Open rebuilt an index whose
inputs are unchanged'; (c) portability_test.go index-default, the emitted index
carrying '\"headings\": null, \"record_blocks\": null'."

`f6tl.3#2` — "Delivering this item required adding a function to
cli/core/markdown (HeadingsFrom), which is the HEAD item's surface, not this
one's. The item scopes itself to wiring — 'Corpus holds no parsing logic of its
own' — and anchors only corpus.go and corpus.Open."

`f6tl.4#4` — "Landing this item made cli-output-standards' own status text false,
so the standards document had to change with it — the item's c4_docs names only
spec-cli-container.md."

WHAT IT COSTS. `c4_docs` and `c4_changes` are what a run's partitioner reads to
compute co-edit collision edges and serialize beads that touch the same surface.
A bead that edits a file it did not declare is invisible to that computation, so
two such beads are dispatched concurrently onto one file with nothing serializing
them. Run d7w5 had a strict dependency chain and zero parallelism, so this cost
nothing there — the graph was wrong, not merely lucky. The second cost is paid
every time regardless: an agent handed a "regenerate" bead discovers mid-session
that the honest change is four times the declared one, and either widens scope
silently or files a bounce.

RELATED WORK. Partially overlaps `agent-plugins-d7w5.15` (deferred), a review
finding that filed the third instance above as a collision-graph risk and
suggested a grooming prompt for the standards-document case specifically. This
bead is the general rule across all three instances; whoever takes either should
read both and close the other or narrow it.

ANCHORS.
- `specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md` — check 8, headed
  "### 8. C4 blast radius declared (IF the repo uses C4)". This is where the rule
  lands.
- `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` — its `MAP` maps that file to both
  `groom-beads` and `spec`; the generated copies are
  `plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md`
  and `plugin/skills/spec/references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md`.
- `plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md` — must NOT grow: measured 19,825 bytes
  against `scripts/check-skills.sh`'s `BODY_BYTE_MAX = 20000`, i.e. 175 bytes of
  headroom. The rule cannot live there.
design:
Land the rule in the Definition of Ready, not in the grooming skill's body.

WHERE. `specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md`, check 8 ("C4 blast
radius declared"). That file is the single definition of ready; `groom-beads` and
`groom-feature-blueprint` enforce it, and `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh`
already vendors it into `groom-beads` and `spec`, so one edit reaches both
consumers and `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` (declared check id
`shared-refs`) keeps the copies in step. Rejected: adding the rule to
`plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md`, which has 175 bytes of headroom against the
20,000-byte body cap `scripts/check-skills.sh` enforces — the edit does not fit
and the skill is the wrong owner for a readiness check anyway.

WHAT THE RULE SAYS. Extend check 8 so a work order whose change regenerates or
re-declares a generated artifact declares, in `c4_changes`/`c4_docs`, the whole
set the regeneration reaches — not only the source it edits. Concretely, the
check requires the order to have asked and answered four questions, and to name
what each turns up:

1. What EMITS the artifact? A declaration change that makes a field required
   changes what the emitter must produce.
2. What FIXTURES and SNAPSHOTS are hand-maintained inputs to, or committed
   outputs of, that emitter?
3. What TESTS construct the changed type by hand and round-trip it?
4. What DOCUMENT asserts something over the surface that this change makes
   false? A standards document carrying a universal claim ("no command conforms
   today", "every X does Y") is falsified by the first instance that does not
   fit it, and that dependency is not visible from the change's own C4 elements.

Where the answer to any of the four is "none", the order says so rather than
leaving the field short — an absent declaration and a declaration of nothing are
what the check exists to separate.

FORM. Written as prose inside check 8 with a short worked example drawn from the
measured instance (a Strata declaration whose regeneration reached the emitter,
two fixtures and three tests). It is a declaration-completeness rule, not a new
numbered check: making it check 10 would imply it applies to orders that touch no
generated artifact, and the C4 check is already the one that asks "what does this
change reach".

Rejected: a script that derives the set. Deriving "which document asserts
something this change makes false" is not mechanizable, and the other three would
need a build of the generator per bead at grooming time. The rule is enforced by
grooming, which is what check 8 already is.

CONSTRAINT. `specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md` carries a
`version` in its frontmatter and the generated copies carry it in their header
banner; bump it and regenerate with `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` in the
same change, or `shared-refs` fails.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md`'s check 8 states that a work order regenerating or re-declaring a generated artifact declares the emitter, the hand-maintained fixtures and snapshots, the tests that construct the changed type, and any document asserting something the change makes false
- [ ] The same section states that where one of those is genuinely empty the order says so, rather than omitting the declaration
- [ ] The rule names why it is a declaration and not a courtesy: `c4_docs` and `c4_changes` are what a run's partitioner reads to serialize beads sharing a surface, so an undeclared file is invisible to that computation
- [ ] `plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md` is unchanged in size or smaller; the rule is not copied into it
- [ ] The document's frontmatter `version` is bumped and both generated copies under `plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/` and `plugin/skills/spec/references/shared/` are regenerated in the same change
- [ ] `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` exits 0
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` exits 0
- [ ] The change is cross-referenced against `agent-plugins-d7w5.15` — either that bead is closed as covered, or its remaining scope is narrowed in its description to what this rule does not cover

metadata.tier_reason: Authors a normative readiness rule that must be right in both directions — strict enough to catch a silent under-declaration, narrow enough not to demand a declaration from every order — inside a generated-copy pipeline where the source, two vendored copies and a version banner must land together.

title: renderYAML's structFields diverges from encoding/json, falsifying the container doc's "cannot drift" claim
description:
## Problem

`specs/containers/spec-cli/spec-cli-container.md`, edited by this run,
claims of the YAML renderer (in the passage beginning "**`headings` is the
first command written to [[cli-output-standards]].**"):

    The YAML rendering lives in `cli/cmd`, in `renderYAML`, and walks the
    same struct `encoding/json` marshals — the same `json` tags in the
    same field order — so the two renderings cannot drift into carrying
    different values.

That is false as implemented. `structFields` in `cli/cmd/yaml.go` does not
reproduce `encoding/json`'s field promotion, and a struct exists for which
the two renderings carry different values.

## Steps to Reproduce

Probes in package `cmd`, on this run's merged tree:

(1) An embedded struct is not flattened.

    type ProbeInner3 struct { A string `json:"a"` }
    type probeOuter3 struct { ProbeInner3; B string `json:"b"` }

    JSON: {"a":"x","b":"y"}
    YAML: ProbeInner3:
            a: x
          b: y

(2) An embedded struct of an UNEXPORTED type loses its fields entirely.

    type probeInner struct { A string `json:"a"` }
    type probeOuter struct {
        probeInner
        B    string            `json:"b"`
        NilS []string          `json:"nil_s"`
        NilM map[string]string `json:"nil_m"`
    }

    JSON: {"a":"x","b":"y","nil_s":null,"nil_m":null}
    YAML: b: y
          nil_s: []
          nil_m: {}

    structFields keys: "b", "nil_s", "nil_m"  — no "a" at all.

TWO CAUSES, both in `structFields`:

a. The `if f.PkgPath != ""` skip drops an embedded field whose TYPE is
   unexported. `encoding/json` promotes the exported fields of such a
   type; this skips the whole embedded field.

b. The flatten branch is guarded
   `f.Anonymous && indirect(value).Kind() == reflect.Struct && name == ""`,
   but `jsonName` returns `f.Name` when a field carries no `json` tag — so
   `name` is never `""` for an untagged embedded field, and the branch is
   UNREACHABLE for exactly the case its own comment names ("An embedded
   struct with no tag flattens into its parent, exactly as encoding/json
   flattens it"). It fires only for an embedded field tagged with an empty
   name, which is not what `encoding/json` flattens.

A third difference exists and is NOT a defect — see Design: a nil slice or
map renders `[]` / `{}` here and `null` in JSON.

WHERE IT MANIFESTS: latent today. `headingMatch` in `cli/cmd/headings.go`,
the only type `renderYAML` is called on, embeds no struct and carries no
nil slice or map. But the container doc presents this renderer as the one
every other command adopts during migration, and presents it WITH the
guarantee that does not hold, so the next command migrated could silently
lose a field.

Filed as a review finding against run agent-plugins-d7w5 pass 1;
`cli/cmd/yaml.go` is new in this run (absent at
70dddef4af906e3e506db20e5512848ac9053c66).
design:
## Design

Two halves: fix the promotion bug in code, and make the container doc's
claim true rather than deleting it.

CODE — make `structFields` mirror `encoding/json` for promoted fields.

1. Have `jsonName` report whether a `json` tag was PRESENT, distinct from
   the name it yields, e.g. return `(name string, opts map[string]bool,
   tagged bool, ok bool)` or a small struct. The current conflation — no
   tag returns `f.Name` — is what makes the flatten branch unreachable.
2. Guard the flatten branch on `f.Anonymous && !tagged &&
   indirect(value).Kind() == reflect.Struct`, not on `name == ""`.
3. Move the `f.PkgPath != ""` skip so it does not fire for an anonymous
   field of struct type. `encoding/json` promotes the exported fields of
   an embedded unexported struct type; only a genuinely unexported
   NON-embedded field is invisible to it.

NIL COLLECTIONS — DECIDED: do NOT change the renderer, and do not treat
this as a defect in it. `specs/standards/cli-output-standards.md` states
"An empty sequence SHALL be rendered `[]` and an empty mapping `{}`", so
`renderYAML`'s current behaviour is what the standards require; emitting
`null` would violate them. What is wrong is the container doc's unqualified
"cannot drift" sentence, which claims the two renderings agree in every
respect when they deliberately do not agree in this one.

DOC — rewrite that sentence in
`specs/containers/spec-cli/spec-cli-container.md` so it states the
guarantee that actually holds and names the one deliberate difference:
`renderYAML` reads the same `json` tags in the same declaration order and
promotes embedded fields the same way `encoding/json` does, so the two
renderings carry the same keys in the same order; empty and nil
collections render `[]` and `{}` per [[cli-output-standards]] where JSON
renders `null`, which is a difference the standards require rather than
drift. Keep the sentence's role in the document — it is the promise the
migration of other commands rests on.

TEST — add a differential test in package `cmd` that, for a table of
struct shapes, marshals the value with `encoding/json` and renders it with
`renderYAML` and compares the KEY SETS AND ORDER. Cover at least: an
embedded exported struct, an embedded unexported struct type, an embedded
struct WITH a `json` tag (which `encoding/json` does not flatten), a
`json:"-"` field, an `omitempty` field, and a nil slice and map — the last
asserted against the documented `[]` / `{}` rather than against JSON.
This is the test whose absence let the claim ship.

REJECTED — narrowing the doc claim only, with no code change. The
promotion divergence silently DROPS a value, which is the failure the
sentence exists to rule out; documenting it as a limitation leaves the trap
armed for the next command migrated.

REJECTED — making an unsupported shape a render-time error. It converts a
latent difference into a runtime failure on a code path no current type
reaches, and the promotion rules are cheap to implement correctly.

REJECTED — replacing `renderYAML` with a general YAML library. The
container doc lists the deliberate restrictions ("It is not a general YAML
library: block style, two-space indent, …"), so this is out of scope.

CONSTRAINT: this bead must not change any existing `expected/` artifact.
`headingMatch` embeds no struct and carries no nil collection, so the
`headings` command's output is unaffected; a golden diff means the change
went further than intended.

DO NOT run `scripts/coverage.sh` or commit `README.md` coverage figures.
The run's coordinator regenerates coverage once at the end; a per-bead
regeneration guarantees a `README.md` conflict between concurrent batches.
acceptance_criteria:
## Acceptance

- [ ] A struct embedding an exported struct renders flattened: the
      embedded type's fields appear at the parent's level under their own
      `json` names, with no key named after the embedded type.
- [ ] A struct embedding a struct of an UNEXPORTED type renders that
      type's exported fields at the parent's level; no field present in
      the `encoding/json` output is absent from the YAML.
- [ ] An embedded field that DOES carry a `json` tag still renders under
      that tag's name rather than being flattened, matching
      `encoding/json`.
- [ ] A differential test in package `cmd` compares, for a table of struct
      shapes, the key sequence `encoding/json` produces against the key
      sequence `renderYAML` produces, and fails on any difference in keys
      or order.
- [ ] A nil slice renders `[]` and a nil map renders `{}`, per
      `specs/standards/cli-output-standards.md`; the differential test
      asserts this documented difference rather than treating it as a
      failure.
- [ ] The "cannot drift" passage in
      `specs/containers/spec-cli/spec-cli-container.md` states the
      guarantee that holds — same keys, same order, embedded fields
      promoted as `encoding/json` promotes them — and names the empty- and
      nil-collection rendering as a difference the output standards
      require.
- [ ] Every `expected/` artifact under `cli/testdata/cases/` is unchanged
      by this bead (`git diff --stat cli/testdata` reports no files).
- [ ] The project's twelve declared checks in `swarm.toml` all pass —
      `format`, `vet`, `build`, `test-go`, `skills`, `shared-refs`,
      `strata-docs`, `schemas`, `corpus`, `ref-links`, `template-drift`,
      `skills-strict`.
notes: Admitted into run agent-plugins-d7w5 by the human as AMENDMENT 3 on the run epic, an explicit override of standing_auth.admit_review_findings=false. Groomed for batch 2 of the run (second groom & plan pass, base 1bb35e7). Supersedes the earlier note that said this finding was filed but not admitted.

comments.text:
retro:decision The Design's proposed flatten guard (`f.Anonymous && !tagged && Kind()==Struct`) is not what encoding/json does; implemented the tag-NAME test instead.

evidence: encoding/json flattens on an empty resolved tag NAME, not on the
ABSENCE of a tag. Its typeFields reads

    name, opts := parseTag(tag)
    if !isValidTag(name) { name = "" }
    ...
    if name != "" || !sf.Anonymous || ft.Kind() != reflect.Struct { ... render as one key ... }
    // else: explore the embedded struct

So an embedded struct tagged `json:",omitempty"` — tagged, but with an empty
name — still flattens, and one whose tag name is rejected by isValidTag
flattens too. The Design's `!tagged` would have rendered the first as a key
named after its type.

Measured against the shipped code, case "embedded struct tagged with options
only" in cli/cmd/yaml_promotion_test.go:

    struct { PromotionTagged `json:",omitempty"`; B string `json:"b"` }
    JSON: ["t" "b"]   YAML: ["t" "b"]

reintroduces the same class of divergence the bead exists to close, one case
narrower. The bead's INTENT — "make structFields mirror encoding/json for
promoted fields" — is served by mirroring the actual condition. Cost of the
choice: `jsonName` was replaced by `parseJSONTag` + `validTagName` (a port of
encoding/json's isValidTag, including its punctuation set) rather than gaining
a fourth return value; the acceptance criterion that speaks to this ("an
embedded field that DOES carry a json tag still renders under that tag's name")
is satisfied either way, since it is about a tag that NAMES the field.
