title: prefixed() re-sniffs the raw line for ATX-vs-setext, so a heading inside a container block gets an overlapping span and an empty section
description:
## Problem

`prefixed()` in `cli/core/markdown/headings.go` decides whether a heading
is written with leading `#` markers (ATX) or underlined (setext) by
scanning FORWARD from the start of the heading's line for the first
non-space byte and testing it for `#`. Inside any container block — a
blockquote, a list item — that first byte is the container's own marker
(`>` or `-`), so an ATX heading is misread as setext, and the span-building
code beside it applies its setext-only correction `end = lineEnd(body,
end)`, extending the heading by one line to swallow an underline that is
not there.

## Steps to Reproduce

Probe in package `markdown_test`, on this run's merged tree, with
`src = "> ## A\n> ## B\n\ntail\n"`:

    h0 level=2 text="A" pos={Offset:0 Length:14 StartLine:1 EndLine:3} section=""
    h1 level=2 text="B" pos={Offset:7 Length:8  StartLine:2 EndLine:4} section="tail\n"

EXPECTED: heading A's `Position` covers only its own line, `[0,7)`, and
heading B's covers only its own, `[7,14)`.

ACTUAL: A's `Position` is `[0,14)` — it covers the whole of B's line as
well, so two heading positions OVERLAP. B's `Position` `[7,15)` runs one
byte past the end of its line.

Same shape for a list item, `src = "- # Item\n  body line\n"`: the heading
is treated as setext, its `Position` runs to the end of the source, and
its `Section` excludes `body line`.

WHERE IT MANIFESTS: `Position` and `Section` are what the index model
documents as a document's structure, and the corpus persists both. An
overlapping pair of heading spans is not a structure, and a `Section` that
excludes a heading's own content makes `spec headings … --emit` return
nothing for a heading that plainly has content. Headings inside
blockquotes and list items occur in this corpus's own templates and
examples.

NOTE ON THE ORIGINAL FINDING, corrected at grooming: the review reported
"A's Section is EMPTY" as part of the defect. With the discriminator fixed,
A's `Section` is still empty and that is CORRECT — B's heading line begins
immediately after A's, so A stands over nothing, and the model documents
"a heading standing over nothing carries an empty span rather than an
absent one". The defect to fix is the OVERLAPPING `Position` spans and the
list-item `Section` that excludes real content; do not chase the empty
section in the blockquote case.

Filed as a review finding against run agent-plugins-d7w5 pass 1;
`cli/core/markdown/headings.go` is new in this run.
design:
## Design

CHOSEN: decide ATX-vs-setext from where goldmark placed the heading's TEXT
segment relative to the start of its line, instead of from the first
non-space byte of the line.

For an ATX heading goldmark's first text segment begins past the `#`
marker run, so the bytes between the line start and the text start contain
a `#`. For a setext heading the text segment begins at the text itself, so
those bytes contain the container's markers and no `#`. Replace `prefixed`
with a two-offset form and call it with the text-segment start that
`locate()` already has in hand:

    // prefixed reports whether the heading whose text begins at textAt,
    // on the line beginning at lineAt, is written with leading markers
    // rather than underlined beneath its text.
    func prefixed(body []byte, lineAt, textAt int) bool {
        if textAt < lineAt || textAt > len(body) {
            return false
        }
        return bytes.IndexByte(body[lineAt:textAt], '#') >= 0
    }

In `locate()`, the call becomes `prefixed(body, start, first.Start)`.
Nothing else in the span arithmetic changes.

MEASURED on goldmark v1.8.5 against both the current and the proposed
predicate, so this is not a guess. `old` is today's forward scan, `new` the
predicate above; `pos` is the resulting `Position` extent.

    "> ## A\n> ## B\n\ntail\n"   A: old prefixed=false pos=[0,14)  new prefixed=true  pos=[0,7)
                                B: old prefixed=false pos=[7,15)  new prefixed=true  pos=[7,14)
    "- # Item\n  body line\n"      old prefixed=false pos=[0,21)  new prefixed=true  pos=[0,9)
    "# A\nbody\n"                  old prefixed=true  pos=[0,4)   new prefixed=true  pos=[0,4)
    "A\n---\nbody\n"               old prefixed=false pos=[0,6)   new prefixed=false pos=[0,6)
    "> A\n> ---\n> body\n"         old prefixed=false pos=[0,10)  new prefixed=false pos=[0,10)
    "   ## Indented\nbody\n"       old prefixed=true  pos=[0,15)  new prefixed=true  pos=[0,15)
    "## # Hashy\nbody\n"           old prefixed=true  pos=[0,11)  new prefixed=true  pos=[0,11)
    "a # b\n===\nbody\n"           old prefixed=false pos=[0,10)  new prefixed=false pos=[0,10)

The last six are the cases the current code already gets right, including
the two where a `#` appears in the heading's own text; the predicate agrees
with the old one on all of them.

REJECTED — asking the AST node, which is what the review finding proposed
("`heading.Type()` / the AST kind"). MEASURED: goldmark v1.8.5's
`ast.Heading` carries only `BaseBlock` and `Level`
(`/root/go/pkg/mod/github.com/yuin/goldmark@v1.8.5/ast/block.go:205`), both
`atx_heading.go` and `setext_headings.go` construct it with
`ast.NewHeading(level)` and neither sets a distinguishing attribute, and
`Type()` returns `ast.TypeBlock` for both. The public AST does not carry
the distinction, so the proposed fix is not available on the pinned
version. This is the same limitation the package doc already records for
fences ("goldmark's public AST does not distinguish a fence that closed on
a real closing delimiter from one that simply absorbed the rest of the
document at EOF").

REJECTED — skipping the container-marker prefix before the forward scan.
That needs a hand-rolled recogniser for every container CommonMark
defines, nested to any depth, which is a second parser again.

Because the AST genuinely cannot answer this, keep a short comment on
`prefixed` saying why the offsets are compared rather than the node asked,
so the next reader does not "simplify" it back.

Update the Markdown Structure component block of
`specs/modules/document-core/document-core-module.md` — the passage "A
heading underlined rather than prefixed carries its underline inside
`Position`" — to state that the two written forms are told apart by the

The run's coordinator regenerates coverage once at the end; a per-bead
regeneration guarantees a `README.md` conflict between concurrent batches.

title: markdown.Identifier parses heading text as a document, so a leading list marker or ordinal is consumed
description:
## Problem

`markdown.Identifier` in `cli/core/markdown/headings.go` silently drops any
block-level marker that opens a heading's text, because the helper it
calls, `rendered()`, feeds that text to the markdown parser as a whole
DOCUMENT. A leading ordinal, bullet or blockquote marker is then consumed
as block syntax and never reaches the identifier.

## Steps to Reproduce

Probe in package `markdown_test`, on this run's merged tree:

    Identifier("1. Overview")            = "overview"     want "1-overview"
    Identifier("2. Overview")            = "overview"     want "2-overview"
    Identifier("- Bullet")               = "bullet"       want "-bullet"
    Identifier("3. `## Design` present") = "-design-present"  want "3-design-present"

And on this repository's own corpus, with a binary built from the run
branch (`go build -C cli -o spec ./spec`):

    spec headings specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md --json

    "1. Self-contained Problem statement (the fresh-agent test)"
        -> self-contained-problem-statement-the-fresh-agent-test
    "3. `## Design` present (non-trivial, non-epic orders)"
        -> -design-present-non-trivial-non-epic-orders
    "4. `## Acceptance` criteria (`kind: bug` & `kind: feature`)"
        -> -acceptance-criteria-kind-bug--kind-feature

Nine numbered headings in that one document all lose their ordinal, and two
produce an identifier that STARTS WITH A HYPHEN.

TWO CONSEQUENCES:

1. Numbered sibling headings collide. Headings written "1. Overview" and
   "2. Overview" both yield "overview", so `#overview` addresses neither.
   The run's own AC-SPECSTR-003.2 says only that "letter case and
   punctuation do not decide a match" — an ordinal is neither, so this is
   not the licensed behaviour.
2. The identifiers diverge from the anchor convention a reader would
   guess: GitHub renders "1. Self-contained…" as `1-self-contained-…`.

WHERE IT MANIFESTS: the identifier is the whole key of the addressing
grammar `<document>#<heading>`. `markdown.Identifier` is called only from
`cli/cmd/headings.go` (match key and rendered field), so the blast radius
is the `headings` command's matching and output.

Filed as a review finding against run agent-plugins-d7w5 pass 1;
`cli/core/markdown/headings.go` is new in this run (absent at
70dddef4af906e3e506db20e5512848ac9053c66).
design:
## Design

CHOSEN: give `rendered()` a parser that has no block parsers except the
paragraph parser, so nothing in the text can be consumed as block syntax
while inline rendering stays exactly as it is.

Add a second package-level parser beside the existing `parser` var in
`cli/core/markdown/markdown.go` (or in `headings.go` next to `rendered`):

    var inline = parser.NewParser(
        parser.WithBlockParsers(util.Prioritized(parser.NewParagraphParser(), 1000)),
        parser.WithInlineParsers(parser.DefaultInlineParsers()...),
        parser.WithParagraphTransformers(parser.DefaultParagraphTransformers()...),
    )

and have `rendered()` parse with it instead of with `parser`. Imports
needed: `github.com/yuin/goldmark/parser` and
`github.com/yuin/goldmark/util`; all four constructors are exported in the
pinned goldmark v1.8.5. The existing `parser` var stays as it is — the
heading and fence SEARCHES must keep full CommonMark block recognition;
only `rendered()` changes.

MEASURED with exactly that parser on goldmark v1.8.5, so this is not a
guess:

    "1. Overview"                    -> "1. Overview"
    "2. Overview"                    -> "2. Overview"
    "- Bullet"                       -> "- Bullet"
    "3. `## Design` present"         -> "3. ## Design present"
    "## Not a heading here"          -> "## Not a heading here"
    "> quoted"                       -> "> quoted"
    "The `Profile` interface"        -> "The Profile interface"
    "A [link](http://x) here"        -> "A link here"
    "*emph* and _under_"             -> "emph and under"

The last three are the behaviours already documented and tested; they are
unchanged. After `Identifier`'s character filter these give `1-overview`,
`2-overview`, `-bullet` and `3-design-present`.

REJECTED — pre-escaping the leading marker with a backslash. It needs a
second, hand-rolled recogniser for every block construct CommonMark
defines, which is the same class of duplicated-rule defect as re-deriving
the frontmatter delimiter.

REJECTED — prefixing a sentinel character, parsing, then stripping it. A
leading letter changes inline semantics: `_under_` does not emphasise when
preceded by a word character, so the sentinel would silently alter the
rendering of some headings.

REJECTED — stripping ordinals with a regexp before rendering. That keeps
the collision (it deletes the ordinal rather than preserving it) and adds
a rule the identifier documentation does not carry.

Update the `Identifier` paragraph in the Markdown Structure component
block of `specs/modules/document-core/document-core-module.md` (the
passage beginning "The package also exposes `Identifier`") to say that the
text is rendered as inline content, so a block-level marker in a heading's
text is a literal character of the heading's name.

DO NOT run `scripts/coverage.sh` or commit `README.md` coverage figures.
The run's coordinator regenerates coverage once at the end; a per-bead
regeneration guarantees a `README.md` conflict between concurrent batches.
acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] `Identifier("1. Overview")` is `1-overview` and
      `Identifier("2. Overview")` is `2-overview` — two numbered siblings
      reading the same produce different identifiers.
- [ ] `Identifier("- Bullet")` is `-bullet`, and the identifier of the
      heading text ``3. `## Design` present`` is `3-design-present`; no
      identifier derived from a heading whose text begins with a digit
      begins with a hyphen.
- [ ] The existing inline-rendering behaviour is unchanged:
      ``Identifier("The `Profile` interface")`` is `the-profile-interface`,
      a link's target does not leak into the identifier, and emphasis
      markers are removed rather than retained.
- [ ] `spec headings specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md --json`
      returns an identifier carrying the ordinal for each of that
      document's numbered headings.
- [ ] Heading and fenced-block SEARCH behaviour is unchanged: the parser
      used by `Headings`, `HeadingsFrom` and `Fenced` still recognises
      every CommonMark block construct, and their existing tests pass
      untouched.
- [ ] Every `expected/` artifact under `cli/testdata/cases/` is either

      carries an ordinal heading, so no change is expected.)
- [ ] The `Identifier` paragraph in the Markdown Structure component block

- [ ] The project's twelve declared checks in `swarm.toml` all pass —

title: headingsOf's frontmatter fallback uses "---" as the closing delimiter and indexes the block as a heading
description:
## Problem

`headingsOf` in `cli/core/corpus/corpus.go` indexes a document's frontmatter
block as a heading whenever the frontmatter failed to parse AND the block
contains a `---` inside one of its values.

The function locates the body by asking `span.Find` for the frontmatter
block, and in its `default:` branch (the one taken when `doc == nil`) it
passes the constant `frontmatterDelimiter` — declared in the same file as
`"---"` — as BOTH the opening and the closing delimiter:

    if region, ok := span.Find(src, frontmatterDelimiter, frontmatterDelimiter, 0); ok && region.Outer.Offset == 0 {

The Frontmatter component does not use the same delimiter for both ends.
`cli/core/frontmatter/frontmatter.go` declares `openingDelimiter = "---"`
and `closingDelimiter = "\n---"`, with the comment "The closing delimiter
carries its leading newline so that only a --- beginning a line ends the
block: a run of three hyphens inside a value is content". The fallback
therefore closes the block at the first `---` ANYWHERE, including inside a
value, and `from` lands mid-block. Everything after that offset — the rest
of the YAML — is handed to `markdown.HeadingsFrom`, which reads the block's
real closing `---` as a setext underline.

The comment above that branch, "The same test frontmatter.Parse applies",
is false as written.

## Steps to Reproduce

Probe in package `corpus`, on this run's merged tree:

    src := []byte("---\ntitle: a---b\nstatus: [unclosed\n---\n\n# Real heading\n\nbody\n")
    headingsOf(src, nil)

EXPECTED: one heading, `# Real heading`.

ACTUAL: two.

    heading 0: level=2 text="b\nstatus: [unclosed" pos={Offset:15 Length:24 StartLine:2}
    heading 1: level=1 text="Real heading"        pos={Offset:40 Length:15 StartLine:6}

The frontmatter block is indexed as a level-2 setext heading — precisely
the failure `headingsOf`'s own doc comment says it exists to prevent ("a
whole-file search reports the entire block as a level-2 heading").

WHERE IT MANIFESTS: the `doc == nil` branch is the documented path for "a
member whose frontmatter failed to parse still carries its headings". A
member needs only (a) frontmatter that fails to parse and (b) a `---`
inside a value. The spurious heading is persisted into the corpus index,
so `spec headings` can match it and `--emit` can print a document's YAML
envelope as though it were a section.

Filed as a review finding against run agent-plugins-d7w5 pass 1; the code
is new in this run (`git show 70dddef:cli/core/corpus/corpus.go | grep -c
"headingsOf\|frontmatterDelimiter"` returns 0).
design:
## Design

CHOSEN: move the block-location rule into the Frontmatter component and
have `headingsOf` call it, deleting `frontmatterDelimiter` from

comments.text:
retro:decision An acceptance criterion is met in substance but not in its literal wording, because the Design's own prescribed signature makes the literal reading unreachable. Reviewers should confirm this at the pull request.
evidence: AC — "frontmatter.Parse and the exported locator share one implementation — the delimiter constants are read in exactly one function." Design — "export a locator ... e.g. func Locate(src []byte) (span.Region, bool)".
With that signature Locate cannot distinguish "src carries no block" from "a block is opened and never closed", yet Parse must, because those are two of its three documented outcomes (a nil,nil versus a located error). Parse therefore keeps the bytes.HasPrefix(src, []byte(openingDelimiter)) test and the len(openingDelimiter) it measures the error span with — so openingDelimiter is read in two functions however the code is arranged, short of changing the signature the Design pinned.
Measured on the finished tree: grep -rn "openingDelimiter|closingDelimiter" --include=*.go . returns, for this package, frontmatter.go:49 and :50 (the declarations), :137 inside Locate, and :163 and :166 inside Parse's unclosed-block error. The DELIMITER PAIR — the block-location rule, which is what the bug was — is read in exactly one function, Locate; Parse's two remaining reads are the opening delimiter alone, for reporting, and cannot close a block anywhere.
The AC's substance holds and is verified: grep -rn "frontmatterDelimiter" . --include=*.go returns nothing (exit 1), so corpus.go declares no delimiter constant, and span.Find over the frontmatter delimiters appears once in the tree.
REJECTED — widening Locate to return the opened-but-unclosed case (a third return value, or an error) so Parse reads no constant. It would satisfy the wording, and it changes an exported signature the Design fixed, to move a string used for an error message. Rejected as the more invasive answer to a criterion whose stated purpose — the Design says "so there is one implementation rather than two" — is already met.

title: Verify the Definition of Done and retire the anchor blueprint
description:
The feature is done when the documentation set is truthful again and
every acceptance criterion is verified at the level the blueprint
declares.

Blueprint:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-blueprint.md`,
Definition of Done. FRD:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-frd.md`.

The feature's closure set is exactly
`bd list --label feature-spec-anchor-references`.

This item is the verification backstop for every criterion whose proving
item landed after a participating item.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Verify rather than implement. Walk the blueprint's Definition of Done,
confirm each entry, then retire the document and run the retro.

- Every delta is folded into its owning blueprint: `module-document-core`
  (References, Markdown Structure, Markdown Links, Findings, Corpus),
  `module-spec-profile` (the citation type), and `container-spec-cli`
  (Command Surface, for the anchor-qualified `refs` form).
- No ADR was authored by this feature.
- Every AC in the coverage table is verified at its declared level and
  cited from its tests. Enumerate them with `spec feature
  FEAT-SPECANCH-001`, `FEAT-SPECANCH-002` and `FEAT-SPECANCH-003`
  rather than by reading the FRD, and grep the suite for `AC:`
  citations.
- `frd-spec-markdown-links`'s revised fragment criteria are verified by
  the MDL item's tests, since this feature is what makes them true.
- No issue is listed as subsumed; `agent-plugins-bem` is a prerequisite
  and `agent-plugins-z8r` and `agent-plugins-im99` are out-of-scope.
- Set the blueprint's status to `retired`.

Then run the `retro-spec` skill over the implementation phase,
aggregating the `retro:` comments recorded on this feature's items. The
approved plan is the standing authorization for that retro; the RFCs it
produces stay human-gated at review.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every delta is folded into `module-document-core`, `module-spec-profile` and `container-spec-cli`, and each fold is visible in those documents
- [ ] Every AC that `spec feature` enumerates for FEAT-SPECANCH-001, 002 and 003 is cited by at least one test at its declared level
- [ ] `frd-spec-markdown-links`'s AC-SPECMD-001.3 and AC-SPECMD-001.7 are cited by tests
- [ ] `spec check --strict` reports no findings over the corpus
- [ ] The blueprint's status is `retired`
- [ ] `retro-spec` has been run over this feature's items and its findings aggregated

reasoning creates is the opposite of an unverified claim: an agent who
measures the same thing would conclude the branch is dead and collapse

title: Answer refs by heading
description:
`refs` answers what cites a document. The question an anchor creates is
narrower — what cites this heading — and that is the question an author
renaming a heading needs answered before they rename it.

Blueprint:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-blueprint.md`,
delta CMD. FRD:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-frd.md`.

Anchors: `cli/cmd/refs.go`; `cli/cmd/registry.go`; the snapshot cases
under `cli/testdata/cases/`.

**ACs:** proves AC-SPECANCH-003.1, 003.3 and 003.4 at the
**integration** level — this item owes a citation comment for each per
`ac-traceability-standards`. Participates in 002.9 (proved by CHK).

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Extend `refs` to take an anchor-qualified operand; the reference
notation already carries one, so the argument needs no new syntax.

- Given `<slug>#<anchor>`, list every reference whose anchor resolves to
  that heading, each with its referring document and span.
- A reference whose anchor matches more than one heading is listed for
  every heading it matches, marked as matching more than one — an
  ambiguous reference resolves to no heading, and the author renaming
  one of those headings is exactly the reader who has to see it.
- Where no reference names the given anchor, report that and exit zero.
- `--help` derives from the declaration that defines the flag.

Output conforms to `cli-output-standards`: YAML by default, JSON under
`--json`, both carrying the same values in the same order, rendered as a
sequence of mappings rather than formatted lines.

This changes observable output, so regenerate the snapshot cases and
review every diff in the same change.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `spec refs '<slug>#<anchor>'` lists every reference resolving to that heading, with referring document and span
- [ ] A reference matching more than one heading is listed for each, marked as matching more than one
- [ ] An anchor nothing references reports that and exits zero
- [ ] Output is YAML by default and JSON under `--json`, carrying the same values in the same order
- [ ] Tests cite `AC: AC-SPECANCH-003.1`, `AC-SPECANCH-003.3` and `AC-SPECANCH-003.4` at the integration level
- [ ] The snapshot cases are regenerated and every diff reviewed in this change
- [ ] `container-spec-cli`'s Command Surface records the anchor-qualified form

comments.text:
retro:decision The bead's 'output conforms to cli-output-standards' pulled the whole refs command off its formatted-line rendering, not just the anchored form.
evidence: specs/standards/cli-output-standards.md's conformance table row for refs read 'prints today: path:line:col  slug per line; --json a compact object | to conform: render the sequence of references as YAML mappings', and the paragraph under it reads 'Migration is per command and belongs to whichever feature next touches it.' This bead is that feature. Decided: migrate refs entirely — YAML by default, JSON under --json, one mapping per reference, and the two prose outcome lines ('X: referenced by no corpus member', 'X: not declared by any corpus member') replaced by the declared/references properties that carry the same two facts. Rejected: rendering only the anchor-qualified form as YAML, which would have left one command printing two grammars depending on its argument. comments.author: dev-59ic-b
comments.text:
retro:tooling:project The YAML renderer did not honour json.Marshaler, so a union rendered its Go shape and the two renderings disagreed — a latent defect this bead is the first command answer to hit.
evidence: measured before the fix, renderYAML over a specmodel.Reference printed 'origin:
  Value: {}' and 'resolution:
  Value:
    target_path: docs/b.md' where json.Marshal of the same value produced '"origin":{"kind":"body"}' and '"resolution":{"state":"resolved","target_path":"docs/b.md"}' — the variant tag absent and a Go field name in its place. cli/cmd/yaml.go's own header claimed the opposite: 'The renderer walks the same struct encoding/json marshals ... deriving one rendering from the other's declaration is what makes it true by construction'. headings, the only prior YAML command, carries no union and never exposed it. Fixed in the renderer (marshaledValue + an order-preserving JSON decode) rather than by projecting Reference into hand-written command-local fields, because cli-output-standards' own References cite [[adr-016]] — 'a rendering is a view over a generated shape rather than a second declaration of it' — and a hand projection is that second declaration. Rejected alternative cost: ~40 lines of switch in cmd/refs.go duplicating the generated model's JSON shape, silently drifting whenever schemas/index.strata changes.

comments.author: dev-59ic-b
comments.text:
retro:proof The renderer fix is pinned by two tests with a measured negative control.
evidence: TestAValueThatMarshalsItselfRendersFromItsOwnJSON and TestTheTwoRenderingsCarryTheSameKeysInTheSameOrder in cli/cmd/yaml_test.go. Negative control: with 'if !ok || true { return v }' substituted into marshaledValue, 'go test ./cmd/ -run "TestAValueThatMarshalsItself|TestTheTwoRenderings"' exits 1 and prints the pre-fix rendering ('origin:\n  Value:\n    property: superseded_by'); with the line restored it exits 0. A third test covers the fallback path — a union holding no variant, whose MarshalJSON errors, still renders from its Go fields rather than vanishing.

comments.text:
retro:gap Neither the bead nor the CMD delta says what 'refs --outbound <slug>#<anchor>' means, and the combination is reachable from the command line.
evidence: the CMD delta in specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-blueprint.md states only 'WHEN refs is given an argument qualified by an anchor, the CLI SHALL list every reference whose anchor resolves to that heading' — every AC-SPECANCH-003.x scenario is inbound. The existing --outbound flag lists the references OUT of the named document, whose anchors name headings of other documents, so 'the references out of X into heading Y of X' names no set. comments.author: dev-59ic-b
comments.text:
retro:decision The 'marked as matching more than one heading' mark is a new ambiguous_anchor property on the answer, not a new property of the generated Reference.
evidence: AC-SPECANCH-003.4 requires the mark; specmodel.Reference already carries anchor_resolution with state 'ambiguous' and every match, so the fact is present but implicit. title: Report an anchor that matches no heading or several
description:
Nothing reports an anchor's breakage. Measured on this corpus: nine
references name an anchor and every one of them resolves today by luck
rather than by verification — a heading rename would break them
silently, in files the renaming author never opened.

Blueprint:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-blueprint.md`,
delta CHK. FRD:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-frd.md`.

Anchors: `cli/core/corpus/check.go`; the snapshot cases under
`cli/testdata/cases/`.

**ACs:** proves AC-SPECANCH-002.1, 002.4, 002.5, 002.8 and 002.9 at the
**unit** level, and AC-SPECANCH-003.2 at the **integration** level —
this item owes a citation comment for each per
`ac-traceability-standards`.

**Prerequisite, from the blueprint's Tracker Reconciliation:**
`agent-plugins-bem` — the relational reference checks read documents off
disk on the warm single-document path, which is the path this item
extends with per-reference heading lookups. Land it first rather than
compounding the budget defect; the edge is wired.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Register the two anchor checks in `Corpus`, reporting at the document a
reader must open — for a reference, the referring document.

- An anchor matching no heading of a target whose headings are available
  is an `error` naming the target document and the anchor.
- An anchor matching more than one heading is an `error` naming every
  matching heading and its span.
- Headings unavailable reports the reference `unverified`, naming what
  is missing.
- A reference whose slug resolves to no corpus member gets no anchor
  finding: one mistake, one finding. The parent feature already reports
  the unresolved slug.
- Both checks run over every reference carrying an anchor in an ordinary
  corpus check, not behind an option, each under its own rule identifier
  so `--only` can select it.
- A single-document check reports inbound anchor references to that
  document that no longer resolve, each at the span in the referring
  document — AC-SPECREF-002.9 extended to the anchor half.

Output conforms to `cli-output-standards`. This changes observable
output, so regenerate the snapshot cases and review every diff in the
same change.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An anchor matching no heading reports `error` naming the target document and the anchor
- [ ] An ambiguous anchor reports `error` naming every matching heading and its span
- [ ] A target whose headings are unavailable reports `unverified` naming what is missing
- [ ] A reference whose slug resolves to nothing produces no anchor finding
- [ ] Both checks run in an ordinary corpus check, each under its own rule identifier selectable by `--only`
- [ ] A single-document check reports inbound anchor references that no longer resolve, at the span in the referring document
- [ ] Tests cite `AC: AC-SPECANCH-002.1`, `002.4`, `002.5`, `002.8`, `002.9` at unit and `AC-SPECANCH-003.2` at integration
- [ ] `spec check --strict` still reports no findings over this repository's corpus
- [ ] The snapshot cases are regenerated and every diff reviewed in this change
- [ ] `module-document-core`'s Corpus component records the two anchor checks and their rule identifiers

title: Derive the link fragment from the resolved heading
description:
`cli/core/mdlinks` holds a private heading-identifier derivation
(`slugifyAnchor`), and the structure feature exposes the one this
feature matches against. Left as two, they can disagree, and every
disagreement is a link the checks call resolved and a reader cannot
follow.

The rewriter also derives its fragment from the anchor's own text rather
than from the heading the anchor resolved to. Measured on this corpus,
that is already wrong for a nested path: `[[module-document-core#Components#Spans]]`
rewrites to `#componentsspans`, which matches no heading.

Blueprint:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-blueprint.md`,
delta MDL. FRD:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-frd.md`.
The criteria this makes true are `frd-spec-markdown-links`'s revised
AC-SPECMD-001.3 and AC-SPECMD-001.7.

Anchors: `slugifyAnchor` and `anchorFragment` in
`cli/core/mdlinks/mdlinks.go`.

**ACs (participating, not proving):** AC-SPECANCH-002.2, proved by the
ARES item. This item owes no AC citation for the anchor FRD, but it does
owe coverage of the markdown-links criteria named above.

**Depends on the structure feature** for the shared derivation
(`agent-plugins-f6tl.2`), and on ARES for the resolution it reads.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Make the rewriter a consumer rather than a second author of the
derivation, and settle which heading a fragment comes from.

- Derive a fragment through the heading identifier `Markdown Structure`
  exposes; delete the private derivation rather than leaving both.
- Where a reference's anchor resolves to a heading, derive the emitted
  fragment from that heading — not from the anchor's own text. The two
  agree wherever an anchor names a heading in full, and the resolved
  heading is what an exported copy must reach when they do not.
- Where a reference's anchor resolves to no heading, derive the fragment
  from the anchor as authored, so the rewrite stays total and the copy
  is no worse than the source.

This changes observable output, so `container-spec-cli`'s Change
Guidance applies: regenerate the snapshot cases and review every diff in
the same change.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `cli/core/mdlinks` holds no heading-identifier derivation of its own
- [ ] A reference whose anchor resolves emits a fragment derived from the resolved heading
- [ ] A reference whose anchor resolves to no heading still emits a fragment, derived from the anchor as authored
- [ ] Tests cite `AC: AC-SPECMD-001.3` and `AC: AC-SPECMD-001.7`
- [ ] The snapshot cases are regenerated and every diff reviewed in this change
- [ ] `module-document-core`'s Markdown Links component records the shared derivation

title: Resolve an anchor against the target's headings
description:
Resolution answers what a reference reached, and answers only the slug
half. An anchor rides in the index unexamined, so a reference into a
renamed section resolves as cleanly as one into a section that exists.

Blueprint:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-blueprint.md`,
delta ARES. FRD:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-frd.md`.

Anchors: `cli/core/references/resolve.go`; the resolution states in
`schemas/index.strata`.

**ACs:** proves AC-SPECANCH-002.2, 002.6 and 002.7 at the **unit**
level — this item owes a citation comment for each per
`ac-traceability-standards`. Participates in 002.1, 002.4, 002.5 and
002.8 (proved by CHK) and in 003.1 and 003.4 (proved by CMD).

**Verification timing:** the criteria CHK and CMD prove are not verified
when this item lands; both depend on it. The final Definition-of-Done
item is the backstop.

**Depends on the structure feature.** The heading tree and the
heading-identifier derivation come from `agent-plugins-f6tl.2`, and the
headings this reads are carried on the index by `agent-plugins-f6tl.3`.
Both edges are wired.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Extend resolution to the anchor, keeping the existing seam: extraction
knows a document, resolution knows a corpus, and matching a heading is a
corpus question.

- Match an anchor against a heading by deriving a heading identifier
  from each and comparing them — the derivation `Markdown Structure`
  exposes, never a second one.
- Exactly one heading matches: record the anchor as resolved to it.
- More than one matches: record the anchor as ambiguous and as resolved
  to no heading, carrying every match. No positional selector is
  offered; the author disambiguates by renaming a heading.
- A reference naming an anchor and no slug resolves against the document
  containing the reference.
- Where the target document's headings are unavailable, record the
  anchor as unverified rather than as resolved — the runtime case is a
  target whose frontmatter failed to parse.
- Resolve an embed exactly as the equivalent link.

Resolution stays a lookup over data already in the index: it opens no
document and re-parses no frontmatter, so the same references over the
same index resolve identically on every platform and every run.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An anchor and a heading are compared as heading identifiers derived by the same rule
- [ ] Exactly one match records the anchor as resolved to that heading
- [ ] More than one match records the anchor as ambiguous, resolved to no heading, carrying every match
- [ ] An anchor with no slug resolves against the document containing the reference
- [ ] Headings unavailable records the anchor as unverified, never as resolved
- [ ] An embed resolves exactly as the equivalent link
- [ ] Tests cite `AC: AC-SPECANCH-002.2`, `AC-SPECANCH-002.6` and `AC-SPECANCH-002.7` at the unit level
- [ ] `module-document-core`'s References component records anchor resolution

metadata.tier_reason: Six resolution states including ambiguity and unverified, consuming a derivation another feature owns, with the index resolution states to extend.

title: Let a frontmatter citation carry an anchor
description:
A reference-bearing frontmatter property is typed `Slug`, and the slug
pattern admits no `#`, so a citation carrying an anchor fails schema
validation before anything resolves it. Measured: a document declaring
`sources: ["adr-012#Decision"]` reports
`frontmatter/schema error /sources/0: does not satisfy $ref`, while the
extractor and resolver already handle the anchor correctly.

The identity a document declares and a citation of someone else's
identity are two different types wearing one name.

Blueprint:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-blueprint.md`,
delta SREF. FRD:
`specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-frd.md`.

Anchors: `schemas/vocabulary.strata` (the `Slug` alias);
`schemas/frontmatter.strata` (the reference-bearing properties);
`scripts/generate-schemas.sh`.

**ACs:** proves AC-SPECANCH-001.6 at the **integration** level — this
item owes the citation comment per `ac-traceability-standards`.
Participates with the AEX item, which records the anchor.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Add a citation type beside `Slug` rather than widening `Slug` itself.
`Slug` also types a document's own `slug` property, and widening it
would let a document declare its identity as `adr-012#Decision`,
breaking uniqueness and resolution.

- Declare a citation type admitting a slug optionally followed by `#`
  and a non-empty anchor. A trailing `#` with nothing after it is
  rejected.
- Retype every reference-bearing property to it — in
  `schemas/frontmatter.strata` these are `superseded_by`,
  `contracts_provided`, `contracts_consumed`, `sources`, `provider`,
  `consumers`, `system`, `contained_by` and `frd`.
- Leave a document's own `slug` typed `Slug`.

Uniform across every reference-bearing property: resolution, pairing and
type-matching all operate on the slug half already, so nothing
downstream can be confused by an anchor on any of them. Regenerate with
`scripts/generate-schemas.sh` and commit the generated artifacts in the
same change.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A citation type admits `slug` and `slug#anchor`, and rejects a trailing `#` with no anchor
- [ ] Every reference-bearing frontmatter property is typed as a citation
- [ ] A document's own `slug` still rejects an anchor
- [ ] A document declaring `sources: ["adr-012#Decision"]` passes `spec check` and appears in the index with slug and anchor recorded separately
- [ ] A test cites `AC: AC-SPECANCH-001.6` at the integration level
- [ ] `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` passes against the committed artifacts
- [ ] `module-spec-profile` records the citation type in its registered frontmatter schema

title: Spec corpus anchor references
description:
Resolve the anchor half of a wikilink against the target document's
headings, and report an anchor that names no heading or names several.

- Blueprint:
  `specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-blueprint.md`
  ([[feature-spec-anchor-references]])
- FRD: `specs/features/reference-integrity/anchors/anchor-references-frd.md`
  ([[frd-spec-anchor-references]])

**Delivery unit: staged.** Two stages, each a reviewable increment.

- **Stage 1 — the anchor in the index:** FIND, SREF, AEX. The extraction
  semantics are pinned and tested, a frontmatter citation may carry an
  anchor, and the finding vocabulary exists. No check runs, no finding is
  raised, and no exit status changes.
- **Stage 2 — matching, checks and query:** MDL, ARES, CHK, CMD. Anchors
  resolve, the checks report, `refs` answers by heading, and exit status
  becomes sensitive to anchors for the first time.

**Stage 2 depends on the structure feature** (epic
`agent-plugins-f6tl`), which builds the heading tree and the
heading-identifier derivation this feature matches against. Those edges
are wired: the items that need them depend on `agent-plugins-f6tl.2` and
`agent-plugins-f6tl.3` directly. Shipping stage 2 before them would
report `unverified` for every anchored reference in the corpus, and this
repository's own gates run `spec check --strict`, which fails on
`unverified`.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Stage 1 lands: anchors are recorded as authored, from a body
      wikilink and a frontmatter citation alike, and the finding
      vocabulary exists
- [ ] Stage 2 lands: an anchor matching no heading or several is
      reported, and `spec refs` answers by heading
- [ ] Every criterion of FEAT-SPECANCH-001, 002 and 003 is cited by a
      test at the level the blueprint declares
- [ ] The nine anchored references in this corpus resolve under the new
      checks, and `spec check --strict` still reports no findings
- [ ] Every delta is folded into its owning blueprint and the blueprint
      is retired

title: Record registered record blocks and attach them to their heading
description:
Fenced already returns the blocks whose info string matches a registered tag, and stops there: nothing records them in the index or attaches them where a reader would look. An element declared in a component block is invisible to every consumer of the index.

Design (revised 2026-09-26, commit 3e596be): the index records each registered block's tag and span against the innermost heading whose section contains it, and does NOT carry the block's content — Strata has no open value type, so an arbitrary YAML record has no typed home in the generated model. Provide one function that reads a recorded block's content through its span and decodes it as YAML into a caller-supplied Go value, so every command and check decodes records the same way. Validation (valid YAML, a mapping, optional JSON Schema) is the check's job — AC-SPECSTR-002.7 to 002.10 in frd-spec-structure-conformance — not the indexer's; the index records a block whether or not its content is valid.

Blueprint: specs/features/structure/structure-blueprint.md, deltas XPT and REC.
FRD: specs/features/structure/structure-frd.md.

Anchors: Fenced in cli/core/markdown; RecordBlock in schemas/index.strata.

**ACs:** proves AC-SPECSTR-001.2 at the **unit** level — this item owes the citation comment per ac-traceability-standards.

**Stage 2.** Lands after the record-block tag registration frd-spec-structure-conformance specifies in FEAT-SPECSTR-004: a registration point no profile fills leaves this item inert. No work order for that registration exists yet, so no dependency edge points at it — confirm the registration is in place before starting.
design:
Parse a registered block's content in the format its tag declares, and
attach the parsed result to the innermost heading whose section span
contains it — to the document where no heading does. That is where a
reader looks for an element declaration: under the heading that declares
the element.

Where a registered block's content does not parse, report a finding
carrying the parse error at the position the block opens, and carry on
with the rest of the document. One malformed block does not cost a
reader the other blocks in the file.

The attachment reads the heading tree the HEAD item builds and the
section spans it computes; the shapes the parsed block occupies are the
ones the MODEL item declares.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A registered block's content is parsed in the format its tag declares
- [ ] A parsed block is attached to the innermost heading whose section contains it
- [ ] A block inside no heading's section is attached to the document
- [ ] A block whose content does not parse yields a finding at the position it opens, and the rest of the document is still processed
- [ ] A test cites `AC: AC-SPECSTR-001.2` at the unit level
- [ ] `module-document-core`'s Markdown Structure component records record-block parsing and attachment as built

metadata.tier_reason: Parse-and-attach over an existing block locator and an existing heading tree; the attachment rule is stated.

title: Let a profile register record-block tags
description:
A fenced block is a record block only where the active profile says its
info string is one, and the `Profile` interface has no way to say it.
`cli/profile` registers the Gherkin fence tag and nothing else, so record
blocks cannot be recognised at all.

The host must learn that a tag exists without learning what a
`component` block means: this item adds the registration and nothing
else. The vocabulary that fills it belongs to
`frd-spec-structure-conformance`.

Blueprint: `specs/features/structure/structure-blueprint.md`, delta XPT.
FRD: `specs/features/structure/structure-frd.md`.

Anchors: the `Profile` interface in `cli/core/corpus/profile.go`;
`corpus.ValidateRegistration`.

**ACs (participating, not proving):** AC-SPECSTR-001.2 (unit, proved by
the REC item). This item owes no AC citation.

**Verification timing:** REC proves the criterion and depends on this
item, so nothing here is verified when it lands. The final
Definition-of-Done item is the backstop.

**Stage 2.** The blueprint places this item in stage 2, which lands
after the record-block tag registration `frd-spec-structure-conformance`
specifies in FEAT-SPECSTR-004. No work order for that registration
exists yet, so no dependency edge points at it.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Widen the `Profile` interface so a profile can register record-block
tags, each with the format its content is parsed as — following the
precedent the reference-integrity feature set when it widened the same
extension point for reference-bearing properties.

- The module names no particular tag. A profile that registers none
  yields a corpus with no record blocks rather than an error.
- Where a profile registers a tag whose format the module does not
  support, `corpus.ValidateRegistration` reports it rather than
  defaulting — a registration defect is never defaulted around.

`contract-specs-configuration` describes the internal registration
surface and does not yet mention record-block tags. Revise it in place
as part of this item: the revision is additive and to the internal half
only, which that contract's change policy exempts from versioning while
both modules are `visibility: internal`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A profile can register record-block tags, each with the format its content is parsed as
- [ ] The module names no particular tag anywhere
- [ ] A profile registering no tag yields a corpus with no record blocks and no error
- [ ] A tag whose format the module does not support is reported by registration validation rather than defaulted
- [ ] `contract-specs-configuration`'s internal registration surface names the record-block tag registration
- [ ] `module-document-core`'s Profile extension point records the registration

title: Add the headings query command
description:
A reviewing agent that wants the normative text of many documents has to
read each one whole. The index will carry every heading with its section
span, and nothing on the command surface answers a question about them.

Blueprint: `specs/features/structure/structure-blueprint.md`, delta CMD.
FRD: `specs/features/structure/structure-frd.md`.

Anchors: `cli/cmd/registry.go` and the query commands beside it
(`cli/cmd/refs.go`, `cli/cmd/feature.go`); the snapshot cases under
`cli/testdata/cases/`.

**ACs:** proves AC-SPECSTR-003.1, 003.2, 003.3, 003.4, 003.5 and 003.6,
all at the **integration** level — this item owes a citation comment for
each per `ac-traceability-standards`.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
One flat `headings` command, following the surface's existing
discipline: open the corpus warm as `check`, `refs`, `slug-exists` and
`next-id` do, convert flags into one core call, carry the result back
out with no domain logic in the command. No subcommand of its own —
every command on this surface is flat.

The selection is one operand written `<document>#<heading>`, either half
omittable:

- `<document>` alone selects every heading in that document.
- `#<heading>` alone selects that heading in every corpus member.
- An absent operand selects every heading in the corpus.

Where the operand's document half holds a path separator or ends in
`.md`, read it as a repository-relative path; otherwise read it as a
slug. Match a heading selection on the heading identifier `Markdown
Structure` exposes, so letter case and punctuation do not decide a
match. When a selection matches a heading, also return every heading
within that heading's section, each carrying its own level.

Each match reports its file path, heading text, heading identifier,
level and the span of the content beneath it. When the caller asks for
it, emit the content each matched heading stands over, read through the
recorded span. Where nothing matches, report that and exit zero.

Output conforms to `cli-output-standards`: matches render as YAML by
default and as JSON under `--json`, both carrying the same values in the
same order; the emitted content is a document payload written as itself,
with no envelope. `--help` derives from the declaration that defines the
command.

This changes observable output, so `container-spec-cli`'s Change
Guidance applies: regenerate the snapshot cases and review every diff in
the same change.

**This item introduces the YAML rendering the whole surface will use.**
Nothing in `cli/` emits YAML today — every command prints hand-rolled
text or compact JSON — so conforming to `cli-output-standards` means
building the renderer here, in a form the other commands can adopt: block
style, two-space indent, `[]`/`{}` for empty collections, block scalars
for multi-line values trimmed at the edges, plain scalars where they
round-trip and double quotes where they do not, and the same values in
the same order under `--json`. Two items in the anchor-references epic
consume it and depend on this one.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `spec headings <document>` lists that document's headings with path, text, identifier, level and section span
- [ ] `spec headings '#<heading>'` answers from every corpus member, and a bare invocation answers from the whole corpus
- [ ] A document half holding a path separator or ending `.md` is read as a path; otherwise as a slug
- [ ] A selection matches on heading identifier, so case and punctuation do not decide it
- [ ] A matched heading is returned with every heading inside its section, each carrying its level
- [ ] The emit form writes the content a matched heading stands over, as itself, with no envelope
- [ ] Output is YAML by default and JSON under `--json`, carrying the same values in the same order
- [ ] A selection matching nothing reports that and exits zero
- [ ] Tests cite `AC: AC-SPECSTR-003.1` through `AC-SPECSTR-003.6` at the integration level
- [ ] The snapshot cases are regenerated and every diff reviewed in this change
- [ ] `container-spec-cli`'s Command Surface records the new command

metadata.tier_reason: Introduces the YAML rendering the output standards require, which nothing in the CLI has yet, on top of a new command with an addressing grammar and six integration criteria.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:decision --emit skips a section already contained in one just written. The two ACs it sits between do not settle this and, read literally, produce duplicated output.
evidence: AC-SPECSTR-003.4 requires a matched heading to be returned with every heading nested inside its section, and AC-SPECSTR-003.5 requires the emit form to return 'the text of each match's section'. Applied literally to a match on a heading with children, the parent's span already covers the children's text, so each nested section is written twice. Measured before the fix, on the headings-emit snapshot case ('headings adr-001-first#Decision --emit'): the expected artifact contained 'The part that only matters once you have decided.' twice — once inside Decision's section and once as Detail's own. Decided to write only the outermost matched section, since what is skipped is always a byte-identical copy of text already emitted, and this query exists to spend a reader's attention once on the text it selected (the FRD: 'I review only the normative text of many documents instead of reading them whole'). Rejected: emitting every span faithfully, whose cost is a reader paying twice for the same passage and having no way to tell the repeat from a real repetition in the document. Recorded in specs/containers/spec-cli/spec-cli-container.md so the behaviour is not read as a bug later.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:decision The YAML renderer is hand-written and reflects over the same struct encoding/json marshals, rather than being goccy/go-yaml (already a module dependency) configured into shape.
evidence: cli-output-standards' YAML Style section fixes every choice a library would offer — block style only, two-space indent, '[]' and '{}' for empty collections, block scalars trimmed at the edges with '|-', plain scalars only where they round-trip, no comments, anchors, aliases, tags or document markers, no folding. It also requires that 'Both renderings SHALL carry the same values in the same order', which reflecting over the json tags makes true by construction: a field cannot appear in --json and not in the YAML. A library would have to be constrained into all of that and still could not give the second guarantee. Rejected: goccy/go-yaml with options, whose cost is a larger surface making the same promises less legibly and no parity guarantee. The renderer is ~250 lines in cli/cmd/yaml.go with cli/cmd/yaml_test.go pinning each style rule, and every case parses its own output back through goccy/go-yaml so the tests check what the bytes MEAN and not only how they look.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:decision The answer carries only 'matches' — the selection is not echoed back — which differs from the nearest sibling on the surface.
evidence: cli-output-standards: 'A command's answer SHALL be a YAML mapping whose keys are the properties the command established ... and SHALL contain nothing else. No header naming the command — the caller typed it.' refs does echo its input (refsResult carries Slug and Direction), but refs is listed in that document's own Current conformance table as not conforming, so it is not the precedent to copy. An empty result is therefore 'matches: []', which satisfies AC-SPECSTR-003.6's 'reports that and exits zero' without a message: the empty collection IS the report, per 'An empty answer is an answer'.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:decision --json and --emit are rejected together rather than one silently winning.
evidence: The item specifies both flags and does not say what their combination means. --emit writes a document payload as itself, which by cli-output-standards has no envelope and therefore no JSON form to select, so the pair names no output. feature already draws the same line for the same reason — cli/cmd/feature.go returns 'spec feature: --code and --json cannot be combined with --emit' — so this follows an established rule on the surface rather than inventing one. Rejected: letting --emit win, whose cost is a caller passing --json and getting bytes no JSON parser accepts, with nothing to tell them why.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:scope Landing this item made cli-output-standards' own status text false, so the standards document had to change with it — the item's c4_docs names only spec-cli-container.md.
evidence: The document read 'Status: approved, and not yet met' and its conformance table 'No command conforms today; the surface predates these standards.' Both become untrue the moment a conforming command exists, and the same document says 'A command specified after this document is written to conform from the start' — so the falsehood was built into it from the day it was written. Updated the status line, the table preamble and added a headings row rather than leaving a document that contradicts the tree; nothing else in it changed, and no other command's row was touched since none of them moved.

title: Build the heading tree, section spans and heading identifiers
description:
`module-document-core` records `Markdown Structure`'s heading tree as
"not yet built": only `Fenced` exists, and nothing in the module reads a
heading anywhere. Every capability that addresses a place inside a
document — anchor resolution, targeted review — has nothing to address.

Blueprint: `specs/features/structure/structure-blueprint.md`, delta
HEAD. FRD: `specs/features/structure/structure-frd.md`.

Anchors: `cli/core/markdown` (alongside `Fenced`); `goldmark` for
heading recognition, as `Fenced` already uses it for fences; `Of` in
`cli/core/span`.

**ACs:** proves AC-SPECSTR-001.1 at the **unit** level — this item owes
the citation comment per `ac-traceability-standards`. Participates in
AC-SPECSTR-003.1, 003.2, 003.4 and 003.5, which the CMD item proves.

**Verification timing:** the 003.x criteria are proved by the CMD item,
which depends on this one, so they are not verified when this item
lands. The final Definition-of-Done item is the backstop.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Build the heading half of `Markdown Structure`, beside `Fenced`.

- Return every heading of a document body in document order, each with
  its level and its text as authored.
- A heading's section span runs from the end of its heading line to the
  start of the next heading of the same or a higher level, and to the
  end of the document where there is none.
- Do not report a heading written inside a fenced code block or an
  inline code span. Take heading recognition from `goldmark` for that
  reason — the module's Change Guidance permits a markdown parser
  exactly where a capability must know which regions not to scan.
- Compute every span through `Spans` (`Of`), so a heading's position is
  comparable to a frontmatter, reference or fenced-block position.
- A document carrying no heading yields an empty result, not an error.

Also expose the heading identifier of a text: its rendered inline
content lowercased, with every character that is not a letter, digit,
hyphen, underscore or space removed, and each remaining space replaced
by a hyphen. It is a pure function of the text and derives no positional
suffix for a repeated heading. It lives here because it is a property of
a heading; the anchor-references feature matches against this same
derivation rather than a second one.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every heading of a body is returned in document order with its level and authored text
- [ ] A heading's section span ends at the next heading of the same or a higher level, or at the end of the document
- [ ] A heading written inside a fenced block or an inline code span is not reported
- [ ] Every returned span is computed through `Spans`
- [ ] A document with no heading yields an empty result rather than an error
- [ ] The heading identifier of a text is exposed, is a pure function of it, and derives no positional suffix
- [ ] A test cites `AC: AC-SPECSTR-001.1` at the unit level
- [ ] `module-document-core`'s Markdown Structure component records the heading tree and the identifier as built

metadata.tier_reason: One component, pinned rules, and an existing sibling (Fenced) to mirror for goldmark use and Spans positioning.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:decision Identifier renders inline content through goldmark rather than filtering the raw text; the blueprint says 'its rendered inline content lowercased' but the two readings only diverge on links, so the cheaper one would have passed unnoticed.
evidence: The spec's own character rule ('every character that is not a letter, digit, hyphen, underscore or space removed') already strips backticks, asterisks and wikilink brackets, so for 'The `Profile` interface' and 'Corpus in [[module-document-core]] (modified) — IDX' a filter-only implementation and a rendering one agree exactly. They disagree on a markdown link: measured with python over the spec's rule, filtering 'See [the guide](http://example.com/guide)' gives 'see-the-guidehttpexamplecomguide' — the URL leaking into the identifier — where rendering gives 'see-the-guide'. Measured the corpus: 623 headings under specs/, of which 0 contain a markdown link and 9 contain backticks, so nothing in the tree distinguishes the two today and a filter-only implementation would have shipped green. cli/core/markdown/headings_test.go pins the link case as a negative control so a later simplification to filtering fails rather than silently changing anchors.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:decision An underlined (setext) heading's Position covers its underline line as well as its text line. The item says 'the span of the heading line itself', which does not say where a heading written across two lines ends.
evidence: Decided so that Position ends exactly where Section begins in both written forms — otherwise the underline would fall inside the section, and a caller slicing a section back out of the body would get '==========' as the first line of the content. Measured on goldmark: an underlined heading's Lines() segment covers only the text line (probe on 'Setext H2\n---------' returned seg (66,75) "Setext H2" at level 2), so the underline has to be consumed deliberately; cli/core/markdown/headings.go does that via the prefixed() check on the first non-blank byte of the heading line. Pinned by TestAnUnderlinedHeadingCarriesItsUnderlineInThePositionSpan. No document in specs/ uses the form today, so this is unexercised by the corpus.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:decision Identifier is exposed as a package function taking a text, not as a field on Heading, and the module blueprint now records why.
evidence: The item's AC says 'The heading identifier of a text is exposed, is a pure function of it', and the preceding MODEL item's AC list gives Heading exactly text, level, heading-line span and section span with no identifier — so storing one would have contradicted the model that had just landed. specs/modules/document-core/document-core-module.md now states 'It is exposed as a function rather than recorded on a Heading, and the index model carries no identifier property for the same reason: it is recomputable from the text and is therefore not state.' The cost lands on the consumers rather than here: the CMD item returns an identifier per match (AC-SPECSTR-003.1) and anchor resolution matches on one, so both derive per call instead of reading a stored value.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:gap A heading nested inside a blockquote or a list item is reported like any other, and its section span is computed in document coordinates — neither the item nor the HEAD delta says whether it should be.
evidence: The blueprint says only 'every heading of a document body in document order'. Measured against the implementation on body '# Top

> ## Quoted
>
> text

- item
  ## In list

## Real

end
': four headings are returned, and the blockquoted one's section slices to '> text

- item
' — carrying the '>' markers and running past the end of the blockquote into the list that follows. That is the honest consequence of section spans being document ranges rather than container-relative ones, but it means a caller emitting such a section (the CMD item's AC-SPECSTR-003.5) would print quote markers. Left as-is rather than special-cased: measured 0 headings inside a blockquote or list item across specs/ (the 3 grep hits are indented YAML comments inside fenced blocks, which goldmark correctly does not treat as headings), so nothing in the corpus exercises it and inventing a rule with no instance to check it against would be guessing.

title: Populate every member's headings during the corpus walk
description:
Nothing populates a corpus member's headings. `Corpus` orchestrates the
parsing components during the walk and assembles the index every other
capability queries, so the heading extraction has to be called from
there and its result carried on each entry.

Blueprint: `specs/features/structure/structure-blueprint.md`, delta IDX.
FRD: `specs/features/structure/structure-frd.md`.

Anchors: `cli/core/corpus/corpus.go`; the warm-open path in
`corpus.Open`.

**ACs (participating, not proving):** AC-SPECSTR-001.1 (unit, proved by
HEAD), AC-SPECSTR-001.2 (unit, proved by REC), AC-SPECSTR-003.1 and
003.3 (integration, proved by CMD). This item owes no AC citation.

**Verification timing:** HEAD is in this item's dependency closure, but
REC and CMD are not — the criteria they prove are not verified when this
item lands. The final Definition-of-Done item is the backstop.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Call the heading extraction during the walk and populate each member's
entry. `Corpus` holds no parsing logic of its own — it orchestrates the
parsing components — so this is a wiring change, not a second parser.

- When the corpus is built, populate each member's headings from
  `Markdown Structure`.
- Order every member's headings by position in the document, so the
  emitted index stays byte-identical across platforms per AC-SPEC-009.7.
- Record a member's headings even where its frontmatter could not be
  parsed: a heading does not depend on a frontmatter envelope.
- A warm corpus answers for headings from the index it opened, reading
  no document off disk.

It also cuts against the nearest precedent: cli/core/corpus/features.go documents that 'The whole of src is offered to the fenced-block lookup, frontmatter included, so that every span a block yields is already in the document's own coordinates', which is safe for fences and not for headings. comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:scope Delivering this item required adding a function to cli/core/markdown (HeadingsFrom), which is the HEAD item's surface, not this one's. The item scopes itself to wiring — 'Corpus holds no parsing logic of its own' — and anchors only corpus.go and corpus.Open.
evidence: Two constraints met in the same place. Headings must be recorded in document coordinates, as every other index position is, and the search must skip the frontmatter. Slicing the body in Corpus and shifting offsets afterwards would not work: span.Of derives line and column from the start of the slice it is given, so a body-relative slice yields a heading on line 1 of a file where it is on line 10, and re-deriving them in Corpus would put position logic in the one component the module says computes none. HeadingsFrom parses the body slice but calls span.Of against the whole source, which keeps both rules. The alternative — widening the HEAD item retroactively — was rejected because it had already closed; the change is additive (Headings is now HeadingsFrom at offset zero) and both the module blueprint's Markdown Structure and Corpus sections record it.
