title: Declare the index model's structure properties in Strata
description:
`specmodel.IndexEntry` carries a path, a frontmatter envelope and a
parse error. A document's headings and its parsed record blocks have
nowhere to go, so nothing downstream can address a place inside a
document.

Blueprint: `specs/features/structure/structure-blueprint.md`, delta
MODEL. FRD: `specs/features/structure/structure-frd.md`.

Anchors: `schemas/index.strata`; the generated
`cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json` and `cli/core/specmodel`.

**ACs (participating, not proving):** AC-SPECSTR-001.1 (unit, proved by
the HEAD item) and AC-SPECSTR-001.2 (unit, proved by the REC item). This
item owes no AC citation.

**Verification timing:** both ACs are proved by items that depend on this
one, so nothing here is verified until HEAD and REC land. Code may
proceed as soon as this item is ready; the final Definition-of-Done item
is the backstop.

**Out of scope, from the blueprint's Tracker Reconciliation:**
`agent-plugins-gz3` (IndexEntry.frontmatter carries only the shared
envelope) — add properties beside `frontmatter`, do not change how it is
carried and do not treat this as fixing it. `agent-plugins-h6c` (index
schema and versioning ADR) — rely on the additive-at-1.0 rule
`container-spec-cli` already states; add no policy.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Declare the shapes in `schemas/index.strata` and regenerate; the index
crosses a boundary, so per ADR-016 the model is transpiled rather than
assembled by hand in the emitter.

- `IndexEntry` gains the document's headings in document order.
- A heading carries its text as authored, its level, the span of the
  heading line, and the span of the content beneath it.
- A heading carries the record blocks attached to it; `IndexEntry`
  carries those attached to the document rather than to a heading.
- A record block carries its tag, its parsed content and the span of the
  block as written.
- No section content is carried anywhere — only spans. A reader that
  wants the text reads it back through the span.
- `schema_version` stays `1.0`. Every property here is an addition under
  the additive rule `container-spec-cli` states, so the satisfying act
  for the module's lockstep rule is the recorded no-bump.

Regenerate with `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` and commit the generated
artifacts in the same change.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `schemas/index.strata` declares headings on `IndexEntry`, with text, level, heading-line span and section span
- [ ] A record block's tag, parsed content and span are declared, attachable to a heading or to the document
- [ ] No property anywhere carries section content
- [ ] `schema_version` is unchanged at `1.0`, and the no-bump is stated in the change
- [ ] `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` passes against the committed artifacts
- [ ] `module-document-core`'s index-model vocabulary records the new properties
notes: placeholder

metadata.tier_reason: Additive Strata declaration plus regeneration, mirroring the reference-integrity model delta; the trap is the strata build version, not the design.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:decision RecordBlock.content is typed [String: String]; the bead and the blueprint say only 'its parsed content' and Strata has no arbitrary-value type, so the type was mine to pick.
evidence: .claude/skills/strata/references/strata-llm-reference.md:16 — 'Closed shapes only. No additionalProperties: true, no untagged unions, no Bytes, no Any'; and its porting table — 'additionalProperties: true / open-shape records | Not supported. Strata is closed-shape'. Measured what the corpus actually holds: awk over every fenced 'component' block in specs/ gives 13 blocks / 1991 bytes, each exactly title+slug+description, all scalar strings — matching the blueprint's own 'thirteen blocks carry 1,991 bytes'. Rejected: a recursive JSON-value union. It is expressible (language-reference.md:707 'Union Recursion') but every union in this model carries a discriminator, so parsed content would reach specs.json as tagged variants rather than as the plain data a catalogue reads — the cost being an index no consumer can read an element declaration out of without unwrapping. The residual limit is that a tag registering a format with non-scalar values (BlockFormat admits json and toml) cannot be represented; the property's doc block in schemas/index.strata states this so the REC item cannot miss it.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:scope Declaring the two properties as REQUIRED lists forced changes outside 'declare in Strata and regenerate' — the emitter, two hand-maintained input fixtures and three unit tests — none of which the bead's Design or Anchors anticipate.
evidence: The bead's Design is 'Declare the shapes in schemas/index.strata and regenerate', Anchors name only schemas/index.strata, cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json and cli/core/specmodel. Measured after regenerating, before any further edit — 'cd cli && go test ./...' rc=1 with three distinct failures: (a) specindex_test.go:166 and :203 'unmarshal: IndexEntry: required field "headings" is missing or null' from entries built as Go literals and round-tripped; (b) cache_test.go:387 'Open rebuilt an index whose inputs are unchanged', because the planted entry marshalled headings as null and the warm read then rejected its own file; (c) portability_test.go:71 index-default, the emitted index carrying '"headings": null, "record_blocks": null'. Required-list was the right call — it is exactly how 'references' and 'features', the first two exercises of the additive-at-1.0 rule, are declared on SpecIndex, and the blueprint states 'No backward-compatibility window applies' — but the consequence is that a MODEL-only bead cannot land green without touching the emitter. The fix mirrors the rule cli/core/specindex/specindex.go:35 already states for the index's own collections ('Every collection is non-nil so that an index containing no members marshals its collections as [] rather than as null'), applied centrally in builder.addEntry so all four IndexEntry construction sites in corpus.go are covered.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:decision RecordBlock.position covers the fenced block INCLUDING its opening and closing fences; the bead says only 'the span of the block as written', which does not settle it.
evidence: Decided on ADR-008's promotion mechanic — 'Promotion lifts the block verbatim into the new document's frontmatter and replaces it with the link, in the same change' — so a rewrite addressing only the content would leave the fences orphaned. Follows the precedent already in this model: schemas/feature.strata:104 FeatureSourceBlock.block is 'The extent of the fenced block, opening and closing fences included', recorded because 'a caller that replaces or extracts the whole construct needs the fence too'. Rejected: an inner span over the content alone, which would have cost every promotion rewrite a second derivation of the fence extent.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:decision Heading carries NO identifier property, and I recorded that as a rule in the module blueprint rather than leaving it unstated.
evidence: The bead's AC lists exactly 'text, level, heading-line span and section span', and the blueprint's HEAD delta makes the identifier the component's — 'The derivation SHALL be a pure function of the text, deriving no positional suffix for a repeated heading' — so it is recomputable and not state. But CMD's AC-SPECSTR-003.1 returns the identifier on every match, so a later agent may reasonably expect to read it off the index; specs/modules/document-core/document-core-module.md now says 'A heading carries no identifier, because the identifier is a pure function of the text and is derived by the Markdown Structure component on demand' so the omission reads as a decision rather than a gap. Flagging because the cost lands on CMD, not here: the query derives an identifier per heading per run instead of reading one.

comments.author: dev-d7w5-1
comments.text:
retro:proof The regenerated snapshots change every index case's input_hash even though no corpus file changed; verified this is by design rather than accepting the diff.
evidence: git diff on cli/testdata/cases/index-default/expected/manifest.json shows input_hash sha256:3ae7797c... -> sha256:f9bb75b7... alongside the expected per-entry '"headings": []'. cli/core/corpus/hash.go's sum() folds in 'field(sum, "profile-schema", opts.Profile.Schema())' and its doc block states 'the active profile's schema and per-type table decide which candidates are members ... A change to any of them changes the index while every file on disk stands still, so all of them are folded in.' The profile's schema IS the regenerated cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json, so a model change necessarily moves the hash. Worth knowing for review: every future MODEL delta will rewrite input_hash in all five index snapshots, and that is correct, not snapshot churn to suppress.

comments.text: retro:filed:agent-plugins-3oiv — f6tl.1#2 (candidate P1, project audience)

title: Spec corpus structure extraction
description:
Extract each document's structure into the shared index and answer a
heading query over it.

- Blueprint: `specs/features/structure/structure-blueprint.md`
  ([[feature-spec-structure]])
- FRD: `specs/features/structure/structure-frd.md` ([[frd-spec-structure]])

**Delivery unit: staged.** Two stages, each a reviewable increment.

  document's headings with their section spans and identifiers, and the
  `headings` command answers. This is the whole of what the anchor
  references feature needs, and it depends on no configuration.
- **Stage 2 — record blocks:** XPT, REC. Blocks are parsed and attached

blueprint requires stage 2 to land after the record-block tag
registration `frd-spec-structure-conformance` specifies in
FEAT-SPECSTR-004, because a registration point no profile fills leaves
REC inert. No work order for that registration exists yet, so no
dependency edge could be wired to it — treat this note as the edge.

Nothing in this feature checks anything: no finding is raised and no exit
status changes, which is what lets the anchor feature depend on it
without inheriting a build gate.

- [ ] Stage 1 lands: the index carries every document's headings with

- [ ] Stage 2 lands: registered record blocks are parsed and attached to
      the heading whose section contains them
- [ ] Every criterion of FEAT-SPECSTR-001 and FEAT-SPECSTR-003 is cited
      by a test at the level the blueprint declares

      changed because of this feature
- [ ] Every delta is folded into its owning blueprint and the blueprint
      is retired

title: swarm dispatch accept can lose merged:true after an irreversible fast-forward
description:
In `foldIn` in `cli/swarm/cli/accept.go` (near line 625 today; anchor on the
symbols, the line moves), the post-fold `merged_sha` fact can be built carrying
zero invocations.

The invocation slice is built conditionally:

    var landedInv [][]string
    if rec, ok := report.Record(landedSteps.Answer()); ok {
        if argv := argvOf(rec); argv != nil {
            landedInv = append(landedInv, argv)
        }
    }

Both guards can fail. `Record.Failed()` is false for `StepSkipped`, and a
skipped record's `Invocation` is empty, so a skipped or absent merged-head
record leaves `landedInv` nil. It is then splatted into the fact:

    facts = append(facts, Unestablished("merged_sha", lerr.Error(), landedInv...))

`Result.Validate` refuses a fact carrying no invocation, and `finish` in
`cli/swarm/cli/command.go` replaces the WHOLE result with a bare refusal. The
reported outcome therefore loses `merged: true` and exits stop — after the
fast-forward has already happened and cannot be undone.

That is precisely what the comment above this branch says the branch exists to
prevent: it states that a failure here "degrades the report and never abandons
the accept", because "the fold DID happen; only the sha is unknown".

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Drive `swarm dispatch accept` to a completed fast-forward, so the fold lands.
2. Arrange the merged-head read to be skipped or absent, so
   `report.Record(landedSteps.Answer())` returns no record, or one whose status
   is `StepSkipped` with an empty `Invocation`.
3. Let the post-fold `revision` read fail, taking the `lerr != nil` arm.

Expected: the result reports `merged: true` with `merged_sha` unestablished,
carrying an invocation.
Actual: `Result.Validate` refuses the invocation-less fact and `finish`

title: swarm ready --dry-run inverts the breaker stop verdict for --completed N>0
description:
In `applyBreaker` in `cli/swarm/cli/ready.go` (near line 393 today; anchor on
the symbols, the line moves), the dry-run refusal branch decides the stop
verdict from `recorded` alone and ignores which direction the report goes:

    if recorded >= threshold {
        refusal.Stopped = true
        refusal.Summary = stoppedSummary(recorded, threshold)
    }

`--completed N` with N > 0 means the dispatch completed beads, which in execute
mode RESETS the count. Dry run never applies that reset before testing
`recorded >= threshold`, so it reports a stop that execute mode would not
produce.

Measured through `breakerPass` in both modes: with a recorded count of 3 and a
threshold of 3, `--dry-run --completed 2` reports `stopped=true` ("3 consecutive
dispatch(es) returned with no bead completed"), while the identical call in
execute mode resets the count and reports `stopped=false`.

The same refusal also carries the text

    "the write was refused: %s. The count stands at %d and would have become %d (threshold %d)"

so a single result says the count "would have become 0" beside a stop summary,
which is self-contradictory on its face.

The comment directly above the branch states the intended rule — a dry run "may
not INVENT a stop from a projection; it must not HIDE one the manifest already
carries". The first half is what is violated.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set the recorded consecutive-failure count to 3 and the threshold to 3.
2. Run `swarm ready` in dry-run mode with `--completed 2`.
3. Run the identical call in execute mode.

Expected: both modes agree on the stop verdict.
Actual: dry run reports stopped=true; execute resets the count and reports
stopped=false. The dry-run result additionally states the count would have
become 0 alongside a stop summary.

This is the dry-run/execute divergence class that retro candidate C2 proposes a
general test for; that broader test is a separate, deferred bead and is NOT in
scope here.

Found by the code-review pass on 2622f6c..37a9d83 that run e6xt never ran
(review_budget exhausted; retro candidate C13, accepted on PR #33).
design: Make the dry-run branch account for the direction of the report before it tests the threshold: apply the same reset execute mode applies for --completed N>0, so a positive --completed cannot report a stop execute would not produce. Preserve the other half of the stated rule — a dry run must still surface a stop the manifest already carries for --completed 0. Fix the refusal text so no single result states a count reset beside a stop summary. Scope is this branch only; do not build the general dry-run/execute parity harness, which is a separate deferred bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] For every combination of recorded count, threshold and --completed value, dry-run and execute agree on the stop verdict.
- [ ] With recorded 3, threshold 3 and --completed 2, dry-run reports stopped=false, matching execute.
- [ ] With --completed 0 and recorded >= threshold, dry-run still reports the stop the manifest carries.
- [ ] No result states a count reset alongside a stop summary.
- [ ] A regression test in cli/swarm/cli covers --completed N>0 both AT the threshold and ABOVE it, in BOTH dry-run and execute modes.
- [ ] The project's declared checks pass: format, vet, build, test-go (judge on ubuntu and macOS; go test (windows-latest) is red on this branch for a diff-independent reason tracked separately).

metadata.tier_reason: single-branch logic fix with a measured repro and a stated parity rule, plus a matrix regression test across two modes; contained but needs care not to break the other half of the rule

comments.author: dev-bguq-1
comments.text:
retro:unverifiable acceptance criterion 1 is false as written, and satisfying it literally would delete a committed test that pins deliberate behaviour; I implemented the bead's Design instead and am recording which reading I took
evidence: AC 1 reads "For every combination of recorded count, threshold and --completed value,
dry-run and execute agree on the stop verdict."

That is contradicted by a test already in the tree, and by the bead's own Design paragraph two
lines further down ("Preserve the other half of the stated rule — a dry run must still surface a
stop the manifest already carries for --completed 0").

The counterexample is recorded 2, threshold 3, --completed 0:

  - execute:  next = recorded + 1 = 3, and `if next >= threshold` -> stopped = true
  - dry run:  the write is refused, the verdict rests on recorded = 2 -> stopped = false

They disagree, deliberately. cli/swarm/cli/ready_test.go pins it:

  // The regression guard for the test above: BELOW the threshold a refused
  // write still leaves the run clear, so what that test asserts is a stop
  // resting on the RECORDED count rather than the stop test having been
  // moved onto the projection.
  func TestADryRunBelowTheThresholdStaysClear(t *testing.T) {
      ...
      if stopped {
          t.Errorf("a dry run stopped the run from a recorded 2 against a threshold of 3 "+
              "(summary %q); the 3 it would have written is a number nothing wrote", summary)
      }
  }

and the rule it enforces is stated in applyBreaker's own comment: "A dry run may not INVENT a stop
from a projection; it must not HIDE one the manifest already carries."

So AC 1 cannot mean universal parity. The reading I took, and implemented:

  The verdict follows whichever value execute would compare, WHENEVER that value is one the
  REPORT settles rather than one the write would have invented.

  --completed N>0 fixes the next count at 0 by itself — the caller supplied it, and execute
  applies the reset unconditionally. Not a projection, so dry run uses it. (the fix)
  --completed 0 only proposes recorded+1, which nothing wrote. A projection, so dry run does
  not use it. (unchanged)

Under that reading AC 2, 3, 4 and 5 all hold as written, and AC 1 holds for every case where the
two modes are comparing the same settled value. Rejected alternative: make dry run use `next`
unconditionally, which satisfies AC 1 literally. Cost: it deletes
TestADryRunBelowTheThresholdStaysClear and the stated rule it guards, turning the dry run into a
mode that invents stops — the failure the comment was written to prevent, and a change well
outside "Scope is this branch only".

What would settle it: an amendment to AC 1 scoping it to `--completed N>0`, or a statement from
whoever wrote it that the projection rule is being retired. I did not stop for that answer.

title: Add an e2e fixture modelling a concurrent world with a harness-named worktree
description:
Of the fixtures under `cli/testdata/swarm-fixtures/`, exactly one
(`dispatch-worktree`) declares a worktree, and none models the world the code
actually runs in. `dispatch-worktree`'s own `fixture.toml` says its branch
"takes the `bb/<dispatch-id>` form the coordinator creates, so a worktree
checked out on it is attributable to its dispatch by branch name alone" — but
the real harness does not name worktrees that way. It creates
`worktree-agent-<hash>`, which carries no dispatch id, as
`cli/swarm/e2e/worktree_attribution_test.go` already states and asserts against
a real capture.

No fixture combines that harness naming with a target ahead of the dispatch
branch, and that absence is why three known defects are green in this suite.
The three conditions the missing world carries, inlined so this order stands
alone:

1. Target ahead of the dispatch branch, so acceptance takes the concurrent
   case — rebase the dispatch branch onto the target, then fast-forward — while
   the dispatch's worktree is still standing. git refuses to rebase a branch
   another worktree has checked out. (Tracked separately as [deleted:agent-plugins-1vya].)
2. A bead assigned to a dispatch whose worktree stands on a branch carrying no
   dispatch id, so attribution must fall back to the bead its HEAD commit
   closed. (Tracked separately as [deleted:agent-plugins-gqwl].)
3. A standing worktree that has made no commit of its own, so its HEAD is still
   whatever the last accepted dispatch landed, and attribution by HEAD commit
   collapses distinct live dispatches onto a finished one.
   (Tracked separately as [deleted:agent-plugins-asv8].)

Those three beads are NOT in this run's scope and are not fixed here. This order
adds the world they will be fixed against, and the Change Guidance rule that
stops the next fixture from modelling a world that does not exist.

Findings: agent-plugins-o63s.11#7, o63s.13#6. Accepted from run
agent-plugins-e6xt's retro (docs/retros/2026-09-02-e6xt-swarm-dispatch.md),
reviewed on PR #33.
design:
Add ONE fixture directory under cli/testdata/swarm-fixtures/, derived as a branch from the core fixture as the Change Guidance requires, holding repository.bundle, tracker.jsonl and fixture.toml. Set kind = "variant" and contract_version equal to the current contract-swarm-json version (2.0 today), which is what the stamp test requires of a variant. The world: the target ahead of the dispatch branch, and a standing worktree declared with [[worktree]] in fixture.toml (a bundle cannot carry a worktree registration) whose branch is harness-named worktree-agent-<hash> and carries no dispatch id, sitting at the sprint head with no commit of its own. Pin commits with a fixed author, committer and date so the shas are stable.

DECIDED — add the fixture world and the doc rule ONLY; add NO case that asserts the three defects. Rationale, mechanically checkable rather than a preference: TestEveryFixtureRestores in cli/swarm/e2e/fixtures_test.go enumerates every directory under the fixtures dir, so this fixture is enrolled automatically, but that test asserts only that the world restores on the sprint branch, that the tracker carries the run epic, that declared worktrees stand and that a declared refusing remote refuses — it runs no accept, ready or status. So the fixture alone leaves the suite green, which the run's checks baseline (exit 0, everything passed) requires. The three defects are open beads outside this run's scope; a case demonstrating them would be red and could not close against that baseline. Cases belong to those beads, not to this one.

Then add the Change Guidance rule to specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md, beside the existing fixture rules in that section. Do not edit dispatch-worktree's misleading comment as part of this order — the new rule is what makes it obligatory to fix, and changing it here would widen scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A new fixture directory under cli/testdata/swarm-fixtures/ holds repository.bundle, tracker.jsonl and fixture.toml.
- [ ] Its fixture.toml declares kind = "variant" and a contract_version equal to the current contract-swarm-json version, and the stamp test accepts it.
- [ ] The world has the target ahead of the dispatch branch.
- [ ] It declares a [[worktree]] whose branch is harness-named (worktree-agent-<hash>) and carries no dispatch id, and that worktree sits at the sprint head with no commit of its own.
- [ ] A bead in its tracker.jsonl is assigned to the dispatch that worktree belongs to.
- [ ] TestEveryFixtureRestores passes for the new fixture: it restores on the sprint branch, the tracker carries the run epic, and the declared worktree stands.
- [ ] No new case is added, and test-go stays green — the three defects the world exposes are out of scope and remain open.
- [ ] specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md's Change Guidance carries: a fixture SHALL model the world the code runs in today; where it models a world after an adoption, its fixture.toml SHALL say so and name the adoption it presumes.
- [ ] The project's declared checks pass: format, vet, build, test-go, corpus, ref-links (judge on ubuntu and macOS; go test (windows-latest) is red on this branch for a diff-independent reason tracked separately).

metadata.tier_reason: authoring a git bundle and tracker export by hand with pinned shas, deriving it from the core fixture, and getting a three-condition world right in data rather than code; the doc rule is easy but the fixture is the hard part and a wrong world is silently useless
metadata.c4_changes_note: Targets the end-to-end fixtures (cli/testdata/swarm-fixtures/), which container-swarm-cli.md models under ## Data as the only data this container owns outright, not as a component in the ## Components roster. No component name applies, so c4_changes is empty by construction rather than untagged. Also edits specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md itself.

title: swarm branch verify-landed --dry-run reports landed from a stale tracking ref; the guard tests the divergence step instead of the refused fetch
description:
FOUND BY: sprint review of run agent-plugins-e6xt (reviewer: code-review, declared in sf.toml [review]).

WHAT. `swarm branch verify-landed --dry-run` reports `landed: true` from a STALE remote-tracking ref, with exit 0 - the exact failure the command's own help text promises it prevents. The guard that was written for this case tests the wrong step.

THE GUARANTEE IT BREAKS. `swarm branch verify-landed --help`, verbatim:

    "Fetches the remote and compares the branch against its counterpart there,
     so a stale local record of where the remote points cannot report a branch
     as landed."

and plugin/skills/sprint-recovery/SKILL.md step 1 repeats it: "it fetches the remote before comparing, so a stale local record of where the remote points cannot report a branch as landed."

MECHANISM. In cli/swarm/cli/branch.go the three steps are built as:

    fetchSteps       := vc.Fetch("fetch", remote)
    counterpartSteps := vc.Resolve("counterpart", remote+"/"+branch)
    divergeSteps     := vc.Divergence("divergence", branch, remote)

`Fetch` is a Write, so a dry run refuses it. `Resolve` and `Divergence` are Reads, so they still run against the stale local ref. The guard in `landingVerdict` reads:

    if !ok || divergeRec.Status != plan.StepRan {
        // "A dry run refused the fetch, but the reads still ran; a plan
        // that stopped before this is reported rather than guessed at."

It tests the DIVERGENCE record, which always ran. It never fires on a dry run. The step that was refused is `fetch`, and nothing consults it.

MEASURED, in a scratch repository built so the tracking ref is genuinely stale:

    real  origin/feat  = ac9c7cd   (force-pushed back one commit from another clone)
    local feat         = 43b9580   (NOT on the remote)
    local origin/feat  = 43b9580   (stale - never fetched since)

    $ swarm branch verify-landed --branch feat --remote origin --dry-run --full-result --json
    DRYRUN_EXIT=0
      "summary": "feat has landed: every commit on it is on origin/feat",
      facts: landed = true (flag),  unpushed = 0 (count)
      invocations:
        { "step": "fetch",       "status": "refused", "reason": "dry run: the step writes" }
        { "step": "counterpart", "status": "ran", "command": "git rev-parse --verify 'origin/feat^{commit}'" }
        { "step": "divergence",  "status": "ran", "command": "git rev-list --count --left-right feat...origin/feat" }

The same command WITHOUT --dry-run is correct, which confirms the defect is dry-run-specific:

    $ swarm branch verify-landed --branch feat --remote origin --json
    EXECUTE_EXIT=1
      "issues": ["feat is 1 commit(s) ahead of origin/feat; that much has not landed. ..."]

DURABLE ANCHOR. cli/swarm/cli/branch.go, function `landingVerdict`, the branch guarded by `divergeRec.Status != plan.StepRan` whose comment begins "A dry run refused the fetch, but the reads still ran". Grep handle:

    grep -n "A dry run refused the fetch" cli/swarm/cli/branch.go

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE FLAG. sprint-recovery calls this "the step that catches the invisible failure" - a coordinator that died between committing and pushing leaves every other signal reading finished. A false `landed: true` there is the one wrong answer that loses work silently.

FIX SHAPE (not attempted). Guard on the FETCH record's status rather than the divergence record's: where the fetch did not run, report `landed` unestablished ("the remote was not fetched, so the comparison rests on a possibly stale local record") with the existing attention outcome and re-run resolution. The `verdict` branch already there is the right shape; only the record it tests is wrong.

SCOPE: row 1 - introduced by this run's own diff. cli/swarm/cli/branch.go did not exist at base_sha 2490026ce2dc17d3813aeb5a1fed1a845c3da54e; it was added by agent-plugins-o63s.12 (LD).


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a scratch repository whose remote-tracking ref is genuinely stale: create branch `feat` one commit ahead of the default branch and push it; from a second clone, force-push `origin/feat` back one commit; do NOT fetch in the first clone. The first clone then holds local `feat` and local `origin/feat` at the same sha while the real `origin/feat` is one commit behind.
2. `swarm branch verify-landed --branch feat --remote origin --dry-run --full-result --json`

EXPECTED: not landed — the fetch was refused, so the comparison rests on a possibly stale local record.
ACTUAL: exit 0, `"summary": "feat has landed: every commit on it is on origin/feat"`, fact `landed = true`, `unpushed = 0`. The invocations show `fetch` with `"status": "refused"`, `"reason": "dry run: the step writes"`, while `counterpart` and `divergence` both show `"status": "ran"`.

3. The same command WITHOUT `--dry-run` exits 1 and reports `feat is 1 commit(s) ahead of origin/feat; that much has not landed.` — which confirms the defect is dry-run specific and execute mode is correct.
design:
Guard on the FETCH step's record instead of the divergence step's, in
`landingVerdict` (cli/swarm/cli/branch.go). The verdict branch that is already
there - the one whose comment begins "A dry run refused the fetch, but the reads
still ran" - is the right shape; only the record it consults is wrong. `Fetch`
is a Write so a dry run refuses it, while `Resolve` and `Divergence` are Reads
and always run, which is exactly why a test on the divergence record never
fires.

WHERE the fetch did not run, report `landed` as UNESTABLISHED with the existing
attention outcome and re-run resolution, worded so the reader knows the
comparison would otherwise rest on a possibly stale local record. Do not report
`landed: true` or `landed: false` from an unfetched comparison.

Leave execute mode alone. It is already correct: the same command without
`--dry-run` reports the branch as ahead of its counterpart and exits 1.

REJECTED: reclassifying `Fetch` as a Read so a dry run performs it. A fetch
mutates the local ref store, so that would make `--dry-run` write - the defect
this run is also fixing elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `swarm branch verify-landed --branch <b> --remote <r> --dry-run`, run in a repository whose remote-tracking ref is stale, does not report `landed: true`; it reports the landing verdict as unestablished and takes the attention outcome.
- [ ] Its resolution names what settles the question - re-running without `--dry-run`, or fetching first.
- [ ] The same command without `--dry-run` is unchanged: it fetches, compares, and reports a branch that is ahead of its counterpart as not landed.
- [ ] A dry run whose `fetch` step DID run (or a plan in which it is not refused) still produces the normal landed/not-landed verdict.
- [ ] A Go test builds a plan whose `fetch` record is refused and asserts the verdict is unestablished rather than landed.
- [ ] Both promises of the fetch-before-compare guarantee are true as written: `swarm branch verify-landed --help`, and step 1 of plugin/skills/sprint-recovery/SKILL.md.
- [ ] `specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md` is consistent with the fixed behaviour, or updated where it is not.
- [ ] All 13 checks pass: `python3 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-checks.py` exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: A one-record swap inside an existing verdict branch; the fix shape is named and the only subtlety is the unestablished wording

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b11
comments.text:
retro:decision the fetch guard runs BEFORE the counterpart check, and it also fires on a fetch that ran and FAILED — two points the bead Design left open
evidence: (1) ORDER. The Design says only to swap which record the existing branch consults. That branch sat AFTER the counterpart-missing branch, which returns an established `landed: false` ("has no counterpart on <remote>"). Left there, an unfetched dry run in a repository with no local tracking ref would still answer with an established false — the same defect in the other direction, since a missing LOCAL ref proves nothing about the remote when the remote was never consulted. The guard is therefore the first thing landingVerdict tests, before either read answer is read at all. REJECTED: leaving the order alone and accepting the established false; it is a wrong answer of exactly the kind the bead is about ("Do not report landed: true or landed: false from an unfetched comparison" is the Design own wording, and it applies to both branches).
(2) A FAILED FETCH. The guard is `!ok || fetchRec.Status != plan.StepRan || fetchRec.Failed()`. plan.Record.Failed() returns false unless Status == StepRan (cli/swarm/plan/plan.go:324-329), so the third clause is not redundant: it covers a fetch that really ran and failed — no network, a dead remote — after which the two reads still compare against the same stale ref and would report landed. The command help says the fetch is what makes a stale record unable to report a branch as landed; a fetch that failed did not do that. This is behaviour change in EXECUTE mode, which the Design says to leave alone, and it is deliberate: "leave execute mode alone" is about the ordinary verdict path, which is untouched — a successful fetch reaches exactly the code it reached before.
NOT COVERED BY A TEST: the failed-fetch case has no test of its own; the tests cover the refused (dry-run) case in both verbs plus the execute negative control. A test would need a fake whose `git fetch origin` recording exits non-zero while the two reads still answer.

title: the five new swarm commands report command/run/mode only on explain; a real dispatch accept reports mode: explain after merging
description:
FOUND BY: sprint review of run agent-plugins-e6xt (reviewer: code-review, declared in sf.toml [review]).

WHAT. The five commands this run added - `swarm phase close`, `swarm ready`, `swarm dispatch open`, `swarm dispatch accept`, `swarm branch verify-landed`/`push` - set `Result.Command`, `Result.Run` and `Result.Mode` ONLY on their `explain*` and refusal paths. Every real (execute or dry-run) result is built without them. Since `plan.ModeExplain` is `Mode`'s zero value, a destructive run reports `mode: explain`.

MEASURED, twice, on the built binary.

(1) A dry run of `swarm ready`:

    $ swarm ready --run agent-plugins-e6xt --dry-run --full-result --json
    {
      "contract_version": "2.0",
      "command": "",
      "run": "",
      "mode": "explain",
      ...
      "summary": "nothing in agent-plugins-e6xt is ready to dispatch",

(2) The one that matters - `swarm dispatch accept` AFTER it really merged. Probe e2e test against the `dispatch-stale-base` fixture, running `swarm dispatch accept --run fixture-run --dispatch dev-fixture-2 --no-push --json --full-result`, exit 0, branch folded into the target and deleted:

    PROBE result.command="" result.run="" result.mode="explain"

So a machine consumer routing on `mode` reads a run that merged a branch, removed a worktree and deleted a ref as a no-op.

CONTRAST WITH THE PRE-EXISTING COMMAND. `swarm status`, which predates this run, gets it right:

    $ swarm status --run agent-plugins-e6xt --full-result --json
      "command": "swarm status",
      "run": "agent-plugins-e6xt",
      "mode": "execute",

DURABLE ANCHOR. `grep -n "Command: req.Command" cli/swarm/cli/*.go` returns six hits. Five are inside `explainDispatchAccept`, `explainBranchLanding`, `explainDispatchOpen`, `explainPhaseClose` and `explainReady`. The sixth, in cli/swarm/cli/status.go, is on the real result. The real results in the five new commands look like accept.go's:

    result := Result{Outcome: OutcomeClear, Records: records}

Confirm the split with:

    awk '/^func /{fn=$0} /Command: req.Command/{print FILENAME": "fn}' cli/swarm/cli/*.go

WHY IT IS NOT CAUGHT BY newSubcommand. `newSubcommand` in cli/swarm/cli/command.go assigns `result.Command/Run/Mode` after `Interpret` for the commands it builds. These five are hand-declared cobra commands that do not go through it, and unlike the equally hand-declared `statusCmd` they do not set the fields themselves.

NOT ATTRIBUTABLE TO ONE BEAD. All five commands share the defect, so it is parented to the run epic rather than discovered-from a single origin. The five origins, from `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD -- <file>`: agent-plugins-o63s.5 (phase.go), .6/.7/.8 (ready.go), .9/.10 (dispatch.go), .11/.13 (accept.go), .12 (branch.go). o63s.5 (PC) landed first and is where the hand-declared pattern originated.

SCOPE: row 1 - introduced by this run's own diff. None of the five commands existed at base_sha 2490026ce2dc17d3813aeb5a1fed1a845c3da54e.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. `swarm ready --run <epic> --dry-run --full-result --json`

EXPECTED: `"command": "swarm ready"`, `"run": "<epic>"`, `"mode": "dry-run"`.
ACTUAL: `"command": ""`, `"run": ""`, `"mode": "explain"`.

2. Contrast with the pre-existing command, which is correct: `swarm status --run <epic> --full-result --json` reports `"command": "swarm status"`, `"run": "<epic>"`, `"mode": "execute"`.

3. The case that matters: against the `dispatch-stale-base` fixture, run `swarm dispatch accept --run fixture-run --dispatch dev-fixture-2 --no-push --json --full-result`. It exits 0, folds the branch into the target, removes the worktree and deletes the ref — and still reports `"mode": "explain"` with empty `command` and `run`.

Repeat for `swarm phase close`, `swarm dispatch open` and `swarm branch verify-landed` / `swarm branch push`: all five behave the same way on their real results.
design:
Set `Command`, `Run` and `Mode` on the REAL (execute and dry-run) results of all
five commands, the way `reportStatus` in cli/swarm/cli/status.go already does.
The sites are every real `Result{...}` construction in cli/swarm/cli/phase.go,
ready.go (BOTH arms - the whole-run report and the `--agent` queue report),
dispatch.go (BOTH - the early recorded-branch return and the created-branch
return), accept.go (both) and branch.go.

Prefer ONE helper over five copies: a small function in the package that stamps
`req.Command`, `req.Run` and `req.Mode` onto a Result, applied at each real
construction site, so a sixth hand-declared command cannot silently repeat the
omission.

DO NOT re-route these commands through `newSubcommand` (cli/swarm/cli/command.go),
which assigns the fields after Interpret for the commands it builds. These five
are hand-declared cobra commands; converting them is a larger change than the
defect and is out of this bead's scope.

`run` may legitimately stay empty for `swarm branch verify-landed` and
`swarm branch push`, which take `--branch`/`--remote` and no `--run`.
schemas/swarm/output.strata declares `run` as "The run epic this invocation was
scoped to. Empty for a command that is not run-scoped." Assert that emptiness
deliberately rather than leaving it incidental.

`mode` must name the interpreter that actually ran. `plan.ModeExplain` is Mode's
zero value, which is why a destructive run currently reports `mode: explain`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `swarm ready --run <epic> --dry-run --full-result --json` reports `command` as the invocation path, `run` as the run epic, and `mode` as `dry-run`.
- [ ] A `swarm dispatch accept` that really merges reports `mode` as `execute` with `command` and `run` filled, rather than `mode: explain`.
- [ ] Every real result of `swarm phase close`, `swarm ready` (both the whole-run and the `--agent` arm), `swarm dispatch open`, `swarm dispatch accept` and `swarm branch verify-landed` / `swarm branch push` carries a non-empty `command` and a `mode` naming the interpreter that ran.
- [ ] `run` is non-empty on every run-scoped command's real result; for a command that takes no `--run` it is empty, and that is asserted rather than incidental.
- [ ] The explain and refusal paths still report the same three fields they report today.
- [ ] A Go test covers all five commands' real results, so a further hand-declared command that omits the fields fails a check rather than shipping.
- [ ] `specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md` and specs/contracts/contract-swarm-json.md are consistent with the fixed behaviour, or updated where they are not.
- [ ] All 13 checks pass: `python3 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-checks.py` exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: Rote and uniform across five files, with the correct shape already demonstrated by status.go's reportStatus; breadth rather than difficulty
metadata.coedit_command: swarm phase close|swarm ready|swarm dispatch open|swarm dispatch accept|swarm branch

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b11
comments.text:
retro:proof the defect was observed failing before the fix, in the new test, for the stated reason
evidence: `go test ./swarm/cli/ -run TestEveryRealResultNamesTheInvocationThatProducedIt` on the unmodified tree failed 9 of 14 subtests, each with the same three lines, e.g. for `swarm dispatch accept` after it really merged:
    stamp_test.go:263: command = "", want "swarm dispatch accept"
    stamp_test.go:266: run = "", want "run-1"
    stamp_test.go:269: mode = "explain", want "execute" — the interpreter that actually ran
The five failing paths were exactly `swarm phase close`, `swarm ready` (both the whole-run and the --agent arm), `swarm dispatch open`, `swarm dispatch accept` (both the merged and the not-drained results), `swarm branch verify-landed` (both with and without --run) and `swarm branch push`. `swarm status` and the four `swarm manifest` subcommands passed unchanged, which is the contrast the bead cites.
After the fix, measured on a binary built from the worktree (`go build -o .../swarm ./swarm`):
    $ swarm ready --run agent-plugins-e6xt --dry-run --full-result --json
    {
      "contract_version": "2.0",
      "command": "swarm ready",
      "run": "agent-plugins-e6xt",
      "mode": "dry-run",
      "outcome": "clear",
      "status": 0,
where the bead measured "command": "", "run": "", "mode": "explain".

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b11
comments.text:
retro:decision the stamping helper was applied to EVERY result construction in the package, not only the five real ones the Design names, and the guard test enumerates the live command tree rather than a hand-written list of five
evidence: The Design asks for "ONE helper over five copies ... applied at each real construction site, so a sixth hand-declared command cannot silently repeat the omission". Applied only at the five real sites, the helper does not deliver that last clause: a sixth hand-declared command still omits the call. Two things were done about it.
(1) `Request.stamp` (cli/swarm/cli/command.go) is now the single place the three fields are set, and it is called from the refusal path, the explain paths of all six hand-declared commands, `reportStatus`, and `newSubcommand` (which previously assigned `result.Command`/`Run`/`Mode` inline). One definition of "stamped" rather than three spellings of it. No behaviour change on those paths — asserted by the pre-existing explain and refusal tests, all of which still pass.
(2) `TestEveryCommandInTheTreeHasARealResultCase` in cli/swarm/cli/stamp_test.go builds the real tree with `register(root, streams, fake)` — the one place root.go says a delta adding a command touches — walks its leaves, and fails any leaf with no case in `stampCases()`. All 11 leaves are covered today (the 5 new ones, `swarm status`, and the 4 `swarm manifest` subcommands), so a twelfth command fails the check until its own real result is asserted.
REJECTED: stamping inside `finish`, which is the single funnel every result already passes through and would make the omission structurally impossible. It was rejected because the Design explicitly scopes the change to the construction sites and forbids re-routing these commands through the surface; moving the assignment into `finish` is that same re-routing by another name, and it would also make the guard test above vacuous — nothing could fail it, including a command whose result was built wrong for some other reason. Cost accepted: a thirteenth command could still be written unstamped, and is caught by a test rather than by the type system.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b11
comments.text:
retro:gap the two specs the bead names were already consistent with the FIXED behaviour, so nothing in them could have caught the defect; one bullet was added to record the invariant on the component that now enforces it
evidence: `schemas/swarm/output.strata` lines 175-183 already declare command as "The invocation path, for example \"swarm manifest get\"", run as "The run epic this invocation was scoped to. Empty for a command that is not run-scoped", and mode as "Which interpreter ran." `specs/contracts/contract-swarm-json.md` states obligations about facts, invocations and versioning and says nothing about these three. So the schema described what the code did NOT do, and no check compares the two: the generated model makes every key optional on the wire, so an empty command and a zero-value mode validate.
Added to specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md, in the Swarm Command Surface bullet list: "Every result names the invocation that produced it ... and the surface stamps all three rather than each command setting them. A result built without them does not merely omit them: explain is the mode zero value ..." — so the invariant is recorded against the component that holds it rather than only in the schema that describes its output.
NOT FIXED, and out of this bead: nothing validates a rendered result against `cli/core/schema/swarm-model.schema.json`, which is why a five-command regression against a correct schema shipped. A test that rendered each command result and validated it would have caught this class without naming the three fields at all.

title: swarm ready --dry-run performs a real manifest write when --completed is given
description:
FOUND BY: sprint review of run agent-plugins-e6xt (reviewer: code-review, declared in sf.toml [review]).

WHAT. `applyBreaker` in cli/swarm/cli/ready.go runs BOTH its read plan and its write plan with a hard-coded `plan.ModeExecute`, ignoring `req.Mode`. So `swarm ready --run <epic> --dry-run --completed <n>` executes the tracker write for real.

THE GUARANTEE IT BREAKS. ready.go's own flag help, verbatim:

    "perform every read this command would perform - it writes nothing either way"

MEASURED. Probe unit test in package `cli` (cli/swarm/cli), calling applyBreaker directly with req.Mode = plan.ModeDryRun, report {Given: true, Completed: 0}, threshold 3, against the package's own exectest fake:

    PROBE call 0: [bd show run-1 --json]
    PROBE call 1: [bd show run-1 --json]
    PROBE call 2: [bd update run-1 --metadata {"consecutive_dispatch_failures":2} --json]
    PROBE total calls under ModeDryRun: 3

The `bd update` is the write. It ran under ModeDryRun.

DURABLE ANCHOR. cli/swarm/cli/ready.go, function `applyBreaker`. Two call sites pass the literal `plan.ModeExecute` to `deps.Runner.Run`: the one building the plan named `"read " + req.Run + "'s failure count"` (a Read, harmless) and the one building `"record " + req.Run + "'s failure count"` around the step `"advance-failure-count"` (the write, and the defect). Grep handle:

    grep -n "plan.ModeExecute" cli/swarm/cli/ready.go

WHY THIS IS THE EXCEPTION. `grep -rn "ModeExecute" cli/swarm/cli/*.go` shows every other occurrence in the package is the `default:` arm of a flag switch assigning `req.Mode`. ready.go is the only file that passes the constant straight into `Runner.Run`, and it does so twice.

BLAST RADIUS. The coordinator is told to run this command with `--completed` on every dispatch return (plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatching.md, "Report every dispatch's return to the breaker as you accept it"). Anyone who reaches for `--dry-run` to preview that call instead mutates the live run's `consecutive_dispatch_failures`, which is exactly the counter that stops a run.

FIX SHAPE (not attempted). Thread `req.Mode` into the write plan's `Runner.Run`, as every other command in the run's diff does, and give the refused-write path the same treatment the other commands give theirs (see `refused(report, steps)` in cli/swarm/cli/manifest.go) so the count is reported unestablished rather than guessed.

SCOPE: row 1 - introduced by this run's own diff. `applyBreaker` did not exist at base_sha 2490026ce2dc17d3813aeb5a1fed1a845c3da54e; it was added by agent-plugins-o63s.8 (CB), confirmed with `git log -S "func applyBreaker" 2490026..HEAD`.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Note the run's current `consecutive_dispatch_failures` (`swarm manifest get --run <epic> --json`).
2. Run `swarm ready --run <epic> --dry-run --completed 0`.
3. Re-read the count.

EXPECTED: unchanged — the flag help promises the command writes nothing either way.
ACTUAL: the count has advanced; the tracker write ran.

Unit-level, which is how it was measured: a probe in package `cli` (cli/swarm/cli) calling `applyBreaker` directly with `req.Mode = plan.ModeDryRun`, `breakerReport{Given: true, Completed: 0}` and threshold 3, against the package's own `exectest` fake, records three calls —

    call 0: [bd show run-1 --json]
    call 1: [bd show run-1 --json]
    call 2: [bd update run-1 --metadata {"consecutive_dispatch_failures":2} --json]

Call 2 is the write, and it ran under `ModeDryRun`.
design:
Thread `req.Mode` into the WRITE plan's `deps.Runner.Run` inside `applyBreaker`
(cli/swarm/cli/ready.go), replacing the literal `plan.ModeExecute` on the plan
named "record " + req.Run + "'s failure count" around the step
"advance-failure-count". Thread it into the sibling read plan
("read " + req.Run + "'s failure count") too, so the file holds no literal mode;
that plan is a Read, so every interpreter runs it and the change is
behaviour-preserving there.

Under a refused write, report the resulting failure count as UNESTABLISHED
rather than guessing the post-write value. Follow the pattern the other commands
already use for this: `refused(report, steps)` in cli/swarm/cli/manifest.go.

REJECTED: an early return guarded on `req.Mode != plan.ModeExecute`. It would
skip the write, but it leaves the read plan running under a hard-coded mode and
produces no `refused` step record, which is what a `--full-result` consumer
reads to see that the write was declined.

Explain mode is not in scope: it has its own path, `explainReady`. The defect is
dry-run-specific.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `swarm ready --run <epic> --dry-run --completed <n>` performs no tracker write: the `advance-failure-count` step is recorded as refused with a dry-run reason, and the run's `consecutive_dispatch_failures` is unchanged afterwards.
- [ ] The failure count a dry run reports is marked unestablished rather than carrying a guessed post-write value.
- [ ] The same invocation without `--dry-run` still advances the count on a return that completed no bead and resets it on one that completed at least one.
- [ ] No call site in cli/swarm/cli/ready.go passes the `plan.ModeExecute` constant straight into `deps.Runner.Run`; the mode comes from the request.
- [ ] A Go test in package `cli` (cli/swarm/cli) drives `applyBreaker` under `plan.ModeDryRun` against the package's exectest fake and asserts no `bd update` invocation is issued.
- [ ] The flag help "perform every read this command would perform - it writes nothing either way" is true as written.
- [ ] `specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md` is consistent with the fixed behaviour, or updated where it is not.
- [ ] All 13 checks pass: `python3 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-checks.py` exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: One call site's mode threading plus the existing refused-report pattern from manifest.go; the correct behaviour is fully pinned by the flag's own help text

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b11
comments.text:
retro:proof the write was observed happening under ModeDryRun before the fix, and refused after it — measured twice, once at unit level and once against this live run
evidence: BEFORE, `go test ./swarm/cli/ -run TestTheBreakerWritesNothingInADryRun` on the unmodified tree:
    ready_test.go:275: a dry run wrote: [bd update run-1 --metadata {"consecutive_dispatch_failures":2} --json]
    ready_test.go:283: the count is reported as established at &{count <nil> 0xc00059a500 <nil> <nil> <nil>}; a refused write leaves it unknown, not at the value the write would have set
NEGATIVE CONTROL, same commit: `TestTheBreakerStillWritesWhenItReallyRuns` (ModeExecute) PASSED before and after, so the assertion above is about the mode reaching the runner and not about the breaker having been switched off.
AFTER, against the live run epic with a binary built from the worktree:
    $ swarm manifest get --run agent-plugins-e6xt --key consecutive_dispatch_failures --json
    { "consecutive_dispatch_failures": { "ok": false, "value": null, "issues": ["consecutive_dispatch_failures is not set. ..."] } }   (exit 1)
    $ swarm ready --run agent-plugins-e6xt --dry-run --completed 0 --full-result --json     (exit 0)
      "mode": "dry-run",
      "name": "consecutive_dispatch_failures",
      "reason": "the write was refused: dry run: the step writes. The count stands at 0 and would have become 1 (threshold 3)",
      ... { "step": "advance-failure-count-write", "command": "", "status": "refused", "reason": "dry run: the step writes" }
    $ swarm manifest get --run agent-plugins-e6xt --key consecutive_dispatch_failures --json
    ... still not set (exit 1)
So the count is unchanged after a dry run that reported a return, the refused step reaches the full result with the runner own reason, and the fact is unestablished rather than carrying the post-write value.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b11
comments.text:
retro:decision a dry run no longer reports the run STOPPED, and applyBreaker now returns its plan records; neither is spelled out in the bead
evidence: (1) STOP VERDICT. Before, `stopped` was derived from `next >= threshold` where `next` is the post-write value. Under a refused write nothing wrote that value, so reporting the run stopped from it is the same untruth as the write: `swarm ready --dry-run --completed 0` on a run one short of the threshold would have exited 2 (stop) and told a coordinator to stop a run the tracker still records as running. A refused write therefore returns Stopped=false, and the projection is carried in the fact reason instead — measured above: "the write was refused: dry run: the step writes. The count stands at 0 and would have become 1 (threshold 3)". Nothing is lost: a caller previewing the breaker reads the same two numbers, in a field that cannot be mistaken for a measurement.
REJECTED: keeping the stop verdict and only marking the fact unestablished. It would leave the result self-contradictory — an unestablished count beside an outcome derived from it — and the outcome is what skills route on without reading the output.
(2) RECORDS. The bead AC asks that "the advance-failure-count step is recorded as refused with a dry-run reason". applyBreaker built records and returned none of them, so the refusal was invisible to a --full-result consumer even once the mode was threaded — reportReady appended only the ready query and status.Collect. applyBreaker now returns a `breakerOutcome` carrying Facts, Records, Stopped and Summary, and reportReady appends the records. Chose a struct over a fifth positional return because a fifth positional return is exactly how a caller drops the records without noticing; the six existing breaker tests unpack it through one test helper (breakerPass) rather than each restating the shape.
(3) The existing breaker tests all passed `Request{Run: "run-1"}`, whose zero-value Mode is ModeExplain. They only passed because the mode was hard-coded; once threaded, explain runs nothing and the read has no answer. Each now passes `Mode: plan.ModeExecute` explicitly. That the whole existing suite depended on the constant it was testing around is the clearest evidence the defect had no test.

title: DOD: verify the Definition of Done, retire the blueprint, run the retro
description:
The final work order. Verifies the blueprint's Definition of Done, closes
the beads this feature subsumes, retires the blueprint, and runs the
implementation retro.

Depends on every other item in this epic.


## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Anchors: `specs/features/swarm-dispatch/swarm-dispatch-blueprint.md`,
`specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md`,
`specs/architecture/module-bead-bonanza.md`.

Verify the AC citations by querying, not by reading: every one of the 58 ACs
must be cited from a test at its declared level.
acceptance_criteria:
Walk the blueprint's Definition of Done and verify each entry against the
tree, not against this epic's issue statuses:

- [ ] Every delta folded into its owning blueprint — FOLD-1, FOLD-2 and
      FOLD-3 landed, and `container-swarm-cli.md` and
      `module-bead-bonanza.md` describe no operation the code lacks
- [ ] `schemas/swarm/manifest.strata` carries
      `consecutive_dispatch_failures`, generated artifacts regenerated, the
      `core` fixture re-recorded against them
- [ ] `sf.toml`'s `[run]` documents `dispatch_failure_threshold` and `sprint-scope`'s
      gate table carries it as a seventh row
- [ ] [[contract-swarm-json]] unchanged, or its version raised in the same
      change as any schema change that removed, renamed or retyped anything
- [ ] Every AC in the coverage table verified at its declared level and cited
      from its tests per [[ac-traceability-standards]] — all 58
- [ ] Every prose section named in ADP-C and ADP-D deleted, and
      `scripts/check-skills.sh` passes
- [ ] `agent-plugins-offx.4`, `agent-plugins-y63n.7` and
      `agent-plugins-y63n.4` closed or re-scoped against the deltas that
      subsume them
- [ ] The blueprint's status set to `retired`

**Completion query:** the run's work is exactly
`bd list --parent agent-plugins-o63s --exclude-type=epic` — 19 beads. Verify
against that query, not against memory of what was created.

Do NOT use `bd list --label feature-swarm-dispatch` for this: measured, it
returns 35, sweeping in the run epic, its six ceremony epics, the
authorization-gate task, the target epic itself and the seven Tracker
Reconciliation beads. Followed literally it would try to close this run's own
ceremony epics.

Then run the `retro-spec` skill over the implementation phase, aggregating
the `retro:`-prefixed findings recorded on this feature's items.
Implementation is the phase that finally exercises the work orders, so this
is where their quality becomes evidence. **The approved plan is the standing
authorization for this retro — no further prompt is needed.** The RFCs it
produces remain human-gated at review.
notes:
**Out-of-scope coordination notes** — these three beads are NOT this
feature's to resolve, and must be left open:
- `agent-plugins-bhl` — this feature specifies how a concurrent dispatch's
  branch is merged, not whether or how widely a run may dispatch
  concurrently. The concurrency policy and its cap stay that bead's.
- `agent-plugins-89xd` — arming the `Stop` ready-loop hook is orchestration,
  which the CLI does not do. No delta here arms, schedules or monitors
  anything.
- `agent-plugins-hg9t.6` — PC closes whatever phase epics the run's shape
  declares. Whether that shape should carry seven of them is that bead's
  question.

**Prerequisite, already satisfied:** `agent-plugins-offx.2` — this feature's
FRD is that task's deliverable, and the FRD reached `approved` before
grooming started.
