**Blueprint:** `specs/features/swarm-dispatch/swarm-dispatch-blueprint.md`
**FRD:** `specs/features/swarm-dispatch/swarm-dispatch-frd.md`

**Delivery: `staged`** — three stages, per the blueprint's Sequencing
Constraints. Stage 1 is the capability layer (TRK, VCS, MFK, FIX); stage 2
is the loop (PC, QF, AQ, CB, BR, WT, MG, RM, LD); stage 3 is adoption
(ADP-C, ADP-D). Each stage ends with one fold work order that folds that
stage's deltas into the owning architecture blueprint — the blueprint's
per-stage fold constraint, which exists so the container blueprint does not
serialize every delta behind a single file.

Closure set for this feature is exactly `bd list --label feature-swarm-dispatch`.

title: Work the owner's review of the swarm output standard: structured values, one issue per issue, command strings, require validity
description:
The repository owner reviewed specs/standards/swarm-output-standards.md on PR #31 and answered every open question. Fourteen threads, each a design decision that changes the standard, the contract or the renderer.

Threads and what each asks for:

- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d33jR (L71) Remove every reference to the rejected earlier design and every historical measurement of a command still being built in this PR. Nothing has merged to main, so a reader has no way to reference a previous iteration. A standards document carries the standard and its rationale; historical records belong in an ADR.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d38qK (L134) 'value' is whatever the property currently holds. It may be non-null while the property still has an issue, because the value present is invalid.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d3-yy (L153) Each element of 'issues' is ONE issue: a description plus an optional recovery suggestion, in one string. Not a description element and a resolution element.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d4L-c (L335) Trimming leading and trailing whitespace from a multi-line string is acceptable, so the renderer may always use a block scalar.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d4PT3 (L407) Are require/validate semantics captured as ACs in the swarm FRD?
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d4Qss (L465) If the answer needs no new type, does the Shape section belong in the final draft?
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d4TpJ (L637) models must render as a YAML map.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d4UFN (L642) standing_auth must render as a YAML map.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d4WJZ (L686) The dispatches entry is a formatted string carrying three facts; it should say what it means structurally.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d4dfl (L724) A fact's invocations should each be a complete command string, not an array of arrays.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d4emd (L744) An invocation's argv should be a complete command string.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d6Gb- (L851) require means 'is set to a VALID value', settling the standard's open question.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d6HI3 (L860) Object-valued properties render as nested YAML; the owner names specific cases above.
- PRRT_kwDOTnszH86d6KGx (L867) Bulk output surfaced as a *_path property is an explicit per-command design decision, not a dynamic catch-all when a response gets large. No current use case in swarm manifest or swarm status.
acceptance_criteria:
Every one of the fourteen threads is addressed in code or in the standard, and answered on its own thread.
Object and composite values render as nested YAML in the answer and as real structure under --json.
A fact's invocations and an invocation's command are complete command strings.
require type-checks as well as checking presence, and the standard's open question is closed rather than left open.
The standard carries no reference to a rejected earlier design and no measurement of a command this PR is still changing.
contract-swarm-json and schemas/swarm/output.strata carry the new shapes, regenerated.
Every fixture under cli/testdata/swarm-cases is re-recorded and passes.
scripts/bb-checks.py exits 0 with no findings beyond the baseline.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro: three findings worth keeping from working this review.

1. I had documented a blocker instead of routing around it. The standard said an object-valued property could not render as nested YAML because the four fact kinds carry no object and the clean fifth kind is a discriminated union that does not compile under allowAdditionalProperties: false. Both halves were true and measured. The conclusion was not: a 'structured' kind whose field carries the JSON as text, parsed back by the renderer, gives the reader real nesting and keeps the wire form honest about being a workaround. A measured impossibility about ONE design is not an impossibility about the requirement, and I let it read as one for a whole draft.

2. The same defect appeared three times and I only recognised it once. models and standing_auth arriving as escaped JSON, dispatches arriving as 'dev-fixture-1: in progress: fixture-run.2', conflicts arriving as '<bead> held by <agent> at <worktree>' — all structure stuffed into a string. I wrote the first two up as a schema gap and hand-wrote the second two as deliberate formatting, in the same document. The owner saw them as one thing.

3. The historical prose rule has a blind spot for the branch you are standing on. AGENTS.md forbids narrating how a rule came to exist, and I applied it to the repository's history while writing a standards document that argued at length with a draft from earlier the same day — 'the rejected default was', 'that form was 24 lines and 3,914 bytes', a Shape section whose whole job was to reject a sketch. Nothing had merged, so no reader could ever reference what I was rejecting. The rule is not about age; it is about whether the reader can follow the reference.

title: Implement the swarm output standard in the renderer: YAML by default, the answer alone, --full-result for the rest
description:
specs/standards/swarm-output-standards.md (slug swarm-output-standards) says what every swarm command prints. It was authored under agent-plugins-dchf, which was scoped to the SPEC and not to the renderer. This bead is the reshaping that follows it.

The earlier revision of this bead pointed at specs/standards/swarm-output-layout-standards.md and a thirteen-row conformance table describing a bespoke line grammar. The repository owner rejected that design in full and it is deleted. Work the new standard's Conformance table instead; it names each requirement, whether the renderer meets it today, and the measurement behind that.

The design in one line: YAML by default and JSON under --json; a command prints its ANSWER unless --full-result is passed; a clear answer is the properties and their values and nothing else; a failing answer is the same properties, each with ok / value / issues; --full-result renders the EXISTING CommandResult field for field; --explain and --dry-run imply --full-result; nothing is truncated or elided.

Scope: cli/swarm/cli/result.go (Render, renderText, renderValue, renderBare), cli/swarm/cli/command.go (newSubcommand's flag declarations and finish), cli/swarm/plan explain output, and every fixture under cli/testdata/swarm-cases/*/expected/.

Measured gaps the standard records, each of which is work here:
- No YAML renderer exists at all.
- --full-result is declared only by a subcommand carrying Spec.Bare. Measured: swarm manifest require --run fixture-run --key branch --full-result exits 3 with 'Error: unknown flag: --full-result'. It must be on every subcommand.
- manifest require reports a flag where a value belongs: 'trailers = false' for an unwritten key. Under the standard require reports the same values get reports, and the verdict is the exit status.
- An empty list renders as nothing: 'scope_missing = ' is indistinguishable from an empty string and from an unset key. YAML renders it [].
- A multi-line value's continuation lines carry no marker and the provenance annotation lands at the end of the last one. YAML renders it as a block scalar with the chomping indicator that round-trips.

The standard's 'Shape' section states that the answer needs no new type in schemas/swarm/output.strata: it is a projection of CommandResult.facts. Do not add a second structure. The one shape gap it records — an object-valued property has no fact kind and arrives as escaped JSON — is blocked on the strata union defect in [deleted:agent-plugins-xxye] and is NOT this bead's to close.
acceptance_criteria:
Every 'no' or 'partly' row of the standard's Conformance table is satisfied, or the standard is amended to withdraw the requirement with a reason.
Every fixture under cli/testdata/swarm-cases is regenerated and passes.
The standard's worked examples are re-taken from a freshly built binary and match what the binary prints.
Assertions land alongside the renderer: the standard notes that no conformance row is enforced by a check today, and a table is not a check.
Any breaking change to contract-swarm-json raises its major version under that document's own Versioning and Change Policy, and schemas/swarm/output.strata is regenerated.
scripts/bb-checks.py exits 0 with no findings beyond the baseline.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: coordinator-bd97
comments.text: SUPERSEDED IN PART — do not start this bead against the spec as committed. agent-plugins-dchf's first draft was rejected in full by the repository owner on 2026-08-30 and is being rewritten to a different design: YAML by default rather than a bespoke line format, the answer alone on success, per-key ok/value/issues on failure, --full-result rendering the existing CommandResult, and no line budget or elision at all. This bead's 13-row Conformance table describes the REJECTED layout. Re-derive its scope from the rewritten standard once that lands.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro: the superseding comment above is spent — this bead was re-derived from the rewritten standard before it was started, and the rejected 13-row layout table is not what was built.

Two round-trip defects found by measuring the emitter rather than by reading the spec, and both are now guards in the renderer with tests beside them:

  - a literal block carries the line break and nothing else, so a carriage return in a value is folded into the break beside it and the value comes back shorter;
  - a block's last content line MAY end in white space by the YAML specification, and readers disagree about whether it does. Measured on 'v: |-' over 'a' then 'b ': PyYAML reads back 'a\nb ', goccy/go-yaml reads back 'a\nb'. Both cases are double-quoted instead, which is why the round-trip fixture's hazard value now comes back quoted rather than as a block scalar.

contract-swarm-json went to 2.0. No shape changed; what changed is which document --json alone selects, and a 1.0 consumer parsing it receives one with no contract_version in it.

One requirement is met and enforced by nobody, recorded as an open question in the standard rather than silently: 'bulk surfaces as a *_path property' binds a command at the point where it decides to produce bulk, and no check can tell a value that should have been a file from one that should not. collision_edges is a path not named for one and checks_baseline is inlined bulk; renaming either is a breaking change to the manifest contract.

title: swarm manifest get should return the value itself, not an envelope an agent must pipe through jq
description:
From review of PR #31 (plugin/skills/run-batch/SKILL.md:49), raised by the repository owner.

Today a key lookup reads:

    swarm manifest get --run <epic> --key branch --json | jq -r '.facts[0].value.text'

The owner's objection: 'Having to navigate the CommandResult shape seems troublesome for what most would expect to be a key/value store command. Intuitively, you would expect the get subcommand to just return the value, or the entire object if a key is not given.'

Proposed shape: 'get' prints the bare value (and the whole manifest object when no key is given), with a flag — '--full-result' or a better name — for callers that want the CommandResult envelope. The envelope stays right for longer-running workflows under --json; it is the wrong default for a key/value lookup.

The stated goal is concrete and worth keeping in the acceptance: an agent should not need the pipe operator every time it looks up a key. That also removes a standing hazard in this repository, whose own AGENTS.md documents at length that reading a verdict through a pipe is how status gets lost — every documented 'get | jq' is one more place to make that mistake.

Note the blast radius: several skill documents currently show the piped form, and each would simplify. Those edits are part of this change, not a follow-up.

Source: PR #31 review comment https://github.com/brettcallaghan/agent-plugins/pull/31#discussion_r3887050266
acceptance_criteria:
- 'swarm manifest get --run <epic> --key <k>' prints the value alone, with no jq required, and its exit status still distinguishes established from unestablished.
- 'get' with no key prints the whole manifest object.
- A flag produces the full CommandResult envelope for callers that want it; --json continues to behave as it does for longer-running commands.
- Every skill document showing the piped 'get | jq' form is updated to the direct form in the same change.
- A value containing whitespace, a newline or a leading dash round-trips correctly through the bare form.

metadata.tier_reason: Changes an output contract and must get quoting/edge cases right (whitespace, newline, leading dash), plus a sweep of every skill doc teaching the piped form.

comments.author: dev-bd97-7
comments.text:
retro:decision The bare form is a per-subcommand DECLARATION (Spec.Bare), not a new default for the surface, and --json now means 'the answer as JSON' for get rather than 'the CommandResult envelope'.

evidence: The bead named two constraints that pull against each other — 'get --key <k> prints the bare value' and '--json continues to behave as it does for longer-running commands'. Read literally together they are unsatisfiable for get: --json cannot both keep emitting the envelope and be the machine-readable rendering of a bare answer. What shipped: (a) Spec.Bare marks a subcommand whose answer is smaller than its report; only get sets it, so set/require/validate/status are untouched and --full-result is an unknown flag there (measured: 'manifest require --run <run> --key branch --full-result' exits 3). (b) For get, --json renders the SAME answer as JSON — a stored string comes back quoted. Measured on this branch: 'swarm manifest get --run agent-plugins-bd97 --key branch' -> claude/bead-bonanza-agent-plugins-ih18-2yjc8j ; '... --key branch --json' -> "claude/bead-bonanza-agent-plugins-ih18-2yjc8j" ; '... --key branch --full-result --json' -> the full CommandResult envelope, byte-identical in shape to what --json alone produced before this change.

rejected alternative: keep --json meaning 'envelope' and make --full-result only affect the text form. That would have left every existing 'get --json | jq .facts[0].value.text' working — but it makes --full-result redundant on the one command that has it, and leaves the surface with two flags meaning the same thing. Cost accepted: any caller outside this repository passing 'get --json' and parsing .facts breaks. Inside the repository the sweep is complete (see the scope finding).

comments.author: dev-bd97-7
comments.text:
retro:decision Two acceptance criteria of FEAT-SWARM-CORE-001 read as universals over 'a command' and the bare form does not satisfy them. Scoped them to the report rather than weakening them.

evidence: AC-SWARM-CORE-001.8 — 'When a command reports a fact / Then the line names the command a reader can re-run to reproduce it'. AC-SWARM-CORE-001.9 — 'the machine-readable form carries the same facts as the text form'. A bare value carries no invocation and no fact names, so 'get --key branch' satisfies neither as written.

What was decided: the bare form is a RENDERING of the answer, not a report of facts, so 001.8/.9 continue to bind the report — which is exactly what --full-result produces, unchanged. The surface's own tests for both ACs drive a synthetic 'probe' Spec that does not set Bare, so they still assert the universal over every reporting command (cli/swarm/cli/surface_test.go, TestEveryReportedFactNamesTheCommandThatEstablishedIt and TestTheMachineReadableFormCarriesTheSameFactsAsTheTextForm — both pass unmodified).

Recorded in the specs rather than left implicit: specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md gains a Command Surface bullet stating that a bare form is a declaration and not a default and that the status is unchanged by the form; specs/features/swarm-core/swarm-core-frd.md gains AC-SWARM-CORE-002.20/.21/.22 for the three bare behaviours and the status invariance.

rejected alternative: print the value plus its provenance on stderr on every bare read. It satisfies 001.8 literally and makes 'x=$(...)' noisy on a path that is now the common one; the provenance is one flag away and nothing consumes it in the common case.

Worth a reviewer's eye: agent-plugins-dchf (spec the output layout) is the natural home for a general statement of when a command may have a bare form. This bead states it once, for get.

comments.author: dev-bd97-7
comments.text:
retro:proof The quoting acceptance criterion is proved end to end through the real tracker, not only through the rendering.

evidence: New e2e case cli/testdata/swarm-cases/manifest-get-bare-round-trip/ writes one value carrying every hazard at once and reads it back bare. The write is 'swarm manifest set --run fixture-run --key findings_path --value '"'"'"docs/two  spaces\n  --leading-dash\tafter-a-tab "'"'"'' against a restored bd fixture; the read is 'swarm manifest get --run fixture-run --key findings_path', exit 0. The committed expected/after-0.stdout, shown with cat -A:

  docs/two  spaces$
    --leading-dash^Iafter-a-tab $

— inner double space, a real newline, a tab, a leading double dash on the second line, and a trailing space, all intact, terminated by the single newline the bare form adds. Nothing between the two invocations is faked: a tracker that trimmed whitespace or ate an escape would fail here and nowhere else.

Unit coverage beside it (cli/swarm/cli/manifest_test.go, TestGetRoundTripsAValueAShellWouldMangle) asserts the exact stdout bytes for six values including a lone dash, a value whose own last character is a newline, and one carrying quotes and a backslash.

One behaviour named rather than hidden: a value ending in its own newline reads back one character shorter through command substitution, because the bare form always terminates with a newline. That is what 'jq -r' does too, so nothing regressed; it is documented on renderBare in cli/swarm/cli/result.go.

comments.author: dev-bd97-7
comments.text:
retro:scope The doc sweep was found by grep, not guessed, and it reached one generated copy. Recording the search so a reviewer can re-run it.

evidence: search that found the sites — grep -rn 'manifest get.*jq|facts\[0\]' --include='*.md' --include='*.sh' --include='*.py' --include='*.toml' . Five hits outside docs/retros/:
  plugin/skills/run-batch/SKILL.md:49,50
  plugin/skills/sprint-review/SKILL.md:90
  plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md:26,28
  plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/epic-definition-of-ready.md:56  (source)
  plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/shared/epic-definition-of-ready.md:61  (GENERATED from the above)
The generated copy was updated by editing the source and re-running scripts/sync-shared-references.sh, not by hand; 'shared-refs' passes. The same grep after the change returns one hit, the word 'no jq' in the new run-record.md prose.

Deliberately NOT rewritten: docs/retros/2026-08-29-bd97-swarm-core.md carries the piped form inside quoted evidence of what was measured at the time. A retro records what happened; editing its quotations would destroy the evidence rather than update it.

Also swept, though they carried no jq: plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md's command listing now shows both get forms and states the three exit statuses; specs/features/swarm-core/swarm-core-frd.md's signature line gains --full-result; specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md's 'Two renderings a caller should expect from get' paragraph is rewritten, since it described only the report.

No durable trigger prompt or .sf/outbox issue carries the piped form — checked: 'ls .sf/outbox' does not exist in this tree.

comments.author: dev-bd97-7
comments.text:
retro:proof CORRECTION to the sweep finding above: I wrote '.sf/outbox does not exist in this tree' before running the check. It does exist.

evidence: 'ls -d .sf' -> the directory, exit 0. 'find .sf -type f' -> exactly one file, .sf/outbox/README.md. 'grep -rn "facts\[0\]|manifest get" .sf' -> no output, so the outbox carries no copy of the piped form and the sweep's conclusion is unchanged. The claim was right; it was inherited from an assumption rather than measured, which is the defect AGENTS.md's 'Tool claims are measured at the point of use' names. Recording it because the sweep finding would otherwise read as if both halves had been run.

comments.author: dev-bd97-7
comments.text:
retro:environment The swarm binary at /usr/local/bin/swarm is stale on this branch and must not be trusted for any measurement.

evidence: the dispatch prompt named this and it holds. Measured: 'cd cli && go build -o /tmp/swarm-new ./swarm' then '/tmp/swarm-new manifest get --run agent-plugins-bd97 --key branch' -> the branch alone, exit 0. Every command output quoted in these findings came from a freshly built binary, never from PATH. Anyone verifying this bead has to build first; 'swarm' on PATH predates the bare form and will still print the report.

comments.author: dev-bd97-7
comments.text:
retro:tooling An e2e golden artifact is recorded by reading the failure, which is worth knowing before hand-writing one.

evidence: cli/swarm/e2e/cases_test.go's compare() fatals on a missing expected/ artifact and prints 'what the run produced' in full. Creating manifest-get-bare-round-trip/case.toml with an empty expected/ and running 'go test ./swarm/e2e/ -run TestSwarmCases/manifest-get-bare-round-trip -v' printed the exact normalized stdout to paste. That is deliberate — the harness comment says so — and it means there is no --update flag to look for. It also means a golden is only ever as right as the run that produced it, so the assertion that matters here is after-0.stdout, which was written from the value the case declares rather than from the run.

title: Skills should say 'run the command and read the output' rather than documenting the output in advance
description:
From review of PR #31 (plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatching.md), stating the repository owner's motivating hypothesis for the swarm CLI:

'One of my motivating hypotheses behind providing a custom CLI for agentic skills is that by having the CLI commands produce readable output, we can simply instruct the agent to "to do ___, run the script and read the output" rather than documenting the output in advance. A goal is to make these skills more concise. Ask the agent to execute commands and then read what it produces, and then trust the agent to reason from there.'

This run went the other way in places: as commands were adopted, prose describing what they emit was written INTO the skills — exit-code tables, per-signal descriptions, restated key sets. That prose is a second copy of the command's behaviour, it competes for a fixed byte budget, and it goes stale the moment the command changes.

The work is an audit of the skill family for output documented in advance, and a replacement with an instruction to run and read. Two constraints keep it honest:

- It depends on the output actually being self-explanatory. Sequence this AFTER the output-layout spec bead; trusting the agent to read output that needs investigation is worse than documenting it.
- Some prose is not a description of output but a RULE about what to do with it — 'route on the exit status', 'a standing worktree means the dispatch is not yet accepted'. Those stay. The test is whether a reader who ran the command and read its output would still need the sentence.

Related and mutually reinforcing: the fixed 20 KB skill-body cap already forces correctness edits to compete with prose. Deleting pre-documented output is the cheapest way to buy that headroom back.

Source: PR #31 review comment https://github.com/brettcallaghan/agent-plugins/pull/31#discussion_r3886958919
acceptance_criteria:
- The skill family is audited for prose that describes what a swarm command emits, and each instance is either replaced by an instruction to run the command and read its output, or kept with a stated reason that it is a rule rather than a description.
- The distinction is written down once, so a future author knows which is which.
- Skill body sizes are measured before and after, and the reduction is recorded.
- This bead is not started before the output-layout spec is agreed.
close_reason: Closed

metadata.tier_reason: Every instance needs the same subtle judgement — is this prose a description of output (delete) or a rule about what to do with it (keep) — across the whole skill family.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro: the audit's own finding is that the reduction is small and the reason is worth stating. Measured, body sizes as scripts/check-skills.sh measures them: bead-bonanza/SKILL.md 19221 -> 19072, sprint-recovery/SKILL.md 8163 -> 7880, supervision.md 14646 -> 14349, run-record.md 15815 -> 15041; total 57845 -> 56342, -1503 bytes across four files. The other eight skills carry no prose describing swarm output at all — most of what reads like a description is a rule about what to do with the output, which the test keeps.

The headroom argument in the bead's description does not survive contact: the two files closest to the 20,000-byte cap are run-batch (19,969) and groom-beads (19,955), and neither carries any of this prose. Deleting pre-documented output buys headroom where there already was some. If the cap is the problem, that is a different bead.

One instance was a correction rather than a deletion, and it is the argument for the rule: supervision.md said 'swarm status prints the invocation behind every fact'. True when written; the provenance moved behind --full-result under agent-plugins-ih18.26, and nothing compares prose against a program, so the sentence went false in silence.

The test is written down once in specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md, beside the existing rule about asserting unmeasured tool behaviour — the same failure at a different distance from the command. Four kinds of sentence pass it and are kept: what to do with the output, what one invocation cannot show, an affordance the output does not advertise, and a meaning the output states without explaining.

scripts.md was left alone deliberately: it is an index of which script to run at all, read before anything has been run, so naming what each produces is discovery rather than a second copy.

title: Rewrite the swarm output standard: YAML by default, the answer only, --full-result for the rest
description:
From review of PR #31 (cli/testdata/swarm-cases/manifest-set-dry-run/expected/stdout), requested directly by the repository owner, who found the current output 'almost incomprehensible'.

The design intent, in the owner's words: 'It is really important that agents will be able to understand what the output means simply by reading it -- assume they know what command they ran. This feels like it would require investigation to comprehend.'

Specific things the current text form does not make self-evident:
- What a trailing '<- bd show fixture-run --json' means. Is it provenance for the line above it, or a step that was run? (It is provenance — the invocation that established the fact — but the reader had to ask.)
- Whether lines like 'set-guard: ran exit 0 <duration> sha256:<digest>' are process steps or facts. (They are step records.)
- Whether a summary may contain multiple lines.

The ask is not a patch. It is: define a SPEC for the layout of these responses, with real worked examples, to be reviewed and refined together until both a human and an agent can read the output without investigation.

This is the keystone of a larger hypothesis the owner stated elsewhere in the same review: if the output is genuinely self-explanatory, skills can shrink to 'run this command and read the output' instead of documenting the output in advance. The spec is what makes that safe to rely on.

Source: PR #31 review comment https://github.com/brettcallaghan/agent-plugins/pull/31#discussion_r3887202137
acceptance_criteria:
- The document is renamed `specs/standards/swarm-output-standards.md`; the layout-standards file and its bespoke line grammar are gone, not amended.
- YAML is the default rendering for every command; `--json` selects JSON. This holds for the answer and for `--full-result` alike.
- A successful command renders the properties and their values and nothing else — no header, no step records, no provenance, no summary, no outcome line.
- A failing command renders per-key `ok` / `value` / `issues`, so a caller reads which key failed and why without decoding anything.
- `--full-result` renders the EXISTING CommandResult structure. The standard does not define a second structure describing the same facts.
- `--explain` and `--dry-run` implicitly activate `--full-result`.
- A YAML style section pins the representations worth fixing, including `|` for multi-line text, and says what makes the output readable rather than merely valid.
- No line budget, no elision, no companion invocation: a command asked for a value returns the value whole, however long. Agents read long lines.
- Bulk that genuinely should not be inline surfaces as a `*_path` property naming a file.
- Where concrete per-command result types in strata are proposed, the proposal states the measured constraint that a `@discriminator` union under `allowAdditionalProperties: false` currently emits variants without the discriminator key ([deleted:agent-plugins-xxye]), and either carries the FactValue-style workaround or says plainly that it waits on upstream.
- The `require` / `validate` distinction is stated: `require` overrides optionality and demands presence; `validate` is stage-relative and type-checks. That `require` does NOT type-check is recorded as an open question for the owner, not silently decided.
- Every example is taken from a real invocation of a binary built from source, never invented.
notes: Draft committed at fadea86 (specs/standards/swarm-output-layout-standards.md, slug swarm-output-layout-standards), plus reference edges from container-swarm-cli and contract-swarm-json. All 13 declared checks exit 0 with no findings beyond the baseline. BLOCKED, not done: AC 5 requires the repository owner's review and agreement, which no agent can establish; AC 6 requires the swarm-case fixtures regenerated to match, which needs the renderer change this bead was explicitly scoped away from — filed as [deleted:agent-plugins-ih18].26. Unblock by reviewing the document with the owner and refining it; then close this bead, and ih18.26 carries the reshaping. Also filed while measuring: ih18.27 and ih18.28.

comments.author: dev-bd97-8
comments.text:
retro:proof The diagnosis handed to this bead was measured rather than inherited, and it was wrong about the count: the text form has SEVEN kinds of line, not three.

evidence: The dispatch prompt stated "the text form has at least three kinds of line — facts, provenance annotations, and step records" and asked that it be verified rather than inherited. Measured against a binary built at 80c9113 (cd cli && go build -o <path> ./swarm), one whole report:

  $ swarm manifest require --run agent-plugins-bd97 --key trailers --key branch
  swarm manifest require — run agent-plugins-bd97 (execute)
  bd show agent-plugins-bd97 --json
  branch = true    <- bd show agent-plugins-bd97 --json
  trailers = false    <- bd show agent-plugins-bd97 --json
  read: ran exit 0 472ms sha256:72f3b0a3...f732cbc sha256:e3b0c442...852b855    <- bd show agent-plugins-bd97 --json
  summary: trailers: not written
  what would resolve this: write each with: swarm manifest set --run agent-plugins-bd97 --key <key> --value <value>
  outcome: attention (exit 1)
  # exit 1

Eight lines, seven grammars: header, transcript, fact, step record, summary, resolution, outcome. Confirmed against cli/swarm/cli/result.go renderText, which emits exactly those seven in that order. The prompt said "at least three", so it is not false — but a reader taking three as the number would have built a three-way distinction and left four kinds unnamed.

Six further measurements, each of which changed a requirement in the spec:

1. The "    <- " suffix has TWO meanings. renderText emits `%s = %s    <- %s` for a fact (provenance: the invocation that established the value) and `line += "    <- " + plan.Argv(...)` for a step record (identity: the argv the step itself ran). One glyph, two relations. This is the owner's first question and the answer is "it depends which line you are on".

2. sha256:e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 appears as the stderr digest of every step record measured. printf "" | sha256sum prints exactly that. It means the tool wrote nothing to standard error, and no reader recovers that without knowing the constant.

3. A fact value ALREADY spans multiple lines. swarm manifest get --run agent-plugins-bd97 --full-result --key checks_baseline prints 344 lines; one fact element occupies lines 3 to 341 (339 lines, 18715 bytes measured by `... --key checks_baseline | wc -lc`). Its "    <- bd show ..." provenance arrives alone on line 341, directly after a line of three backticks that came out of the value itself. summary is line 343 and outcome is line 344. Continuation lines carry no marker of any kind.

4. swarm status --run agent-plugins-bd97 is 24 lines and 33,329 bytes. awk over it: nine fact lines each carry 53 occurrences of "bd list --parent" — 477 copies of 53 distinct commands — and those lines are 3,425 to 3,614 characters each.

5. An empty list renders as nothing: `scope_missing =     <- bd show agent-plugins-bd97 --json`. Indistinguishable from an empty string and from an unset key.

6. A list is joined with ", " and the manifest ledger has 7 items every one of which contains commas (measured: `... --key ledger --json | python3 -c "print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)))"` -> 7; the rendered fact line is 2,856 characters).

comments.author: dev-bd97-8
comments.text:
retro:decision Four decisions the spec had to settle that the bead did not pin, each with the alternative rejected. All four are in the document and reviewable at the pull request.

evidence:

1. DOCUMENT TYPE — standards, not ADR, not contract. Rejected the ADR because this is not one decision with alternatives but a set of obligations every command must satisfy; rejected extending contract-swarm-json because that document is generated shape over schemas/swarm/output.strata and a reading contract is not shape. Cost accepted: the layout now lives in a third document a reader must find, so container-swarm-cli and contract-swarm-json were each given a reference to it (both edited in this bead; build/spec check --strict passes at 67 documents, no findings).

2. THE MULTI-LINE QUESTION — the owner asked "whether a summary may contain multiple lines". Decided NO, and not only for a summary: no element may span more than one line, anywhere. The alternative was admitting continuations with a marker; rejected because a value whose own text begins with the marker breaks it, and the manifest checks_baseline value demonstrably contains markdown fences, blank lines and indented text. Where a value does not fit, the report states its kind, its size and an invocation that yields it whole. Cost accepted: a large value is no longer visible in the report at all — it is one flag or one bare invocation away.

3. WHICH STREAM CARRIES A REFUSAL — a command with no bare form keeps its report on standard output at EVERY exit status, including malformed. Measured as current behaviour: `swarm manifest require --key branch 2>/dev/null` still prints the whole report at exit 3. The conventional alternative (errors to standard error) was rejected because contract-swarm-json guarantees a consumer parsing --json never falls back to reading text to learn why, and moving refusals to stderr would force that consumer to merge two streams to find the envelope — the merge AC-SWARM-CORE-001.12 forbids elsewhere. Cost accepted: a caller who wants only failures routes on the exit status rather than on a stream.

4. WHEN A SUBCOMMAND MAY DECLARE A BARE FORM — this is the general statement agent-plugins-i47s explicitly left to this bead, having stated it only for `get`. Three tests, all of which must hold: (a) every clear invocation has exactly ONE answer — one value, not one per line; (b) the answer is smaller than the report and could otherwise only be had by parsing it; (c) the answer is RETRIEVED rather than derived. Test (c) is the one that decides the open cases: `get` is a lookup and is bare; `status` computes a verdict from twenty measurements, so its report IS its answer; `require` and `validate` answer with a verdict the exit status already carries, so a bare form would be a second copy of it. Rejected the simpler rule "bare where the output is short" because shortness is a property of the data, not of the command, and the same command would be bare or not depending on what it found.

comments.author: dev-bd97-8
comments.text:
retro:scope Two breaking changes to contract-swarm-json fall out of the layout, and they are named in the spec rather than discovered during implementation.

evidence: The spec section "What this asks of the envelope" states both.

(a) The envelope`s `transcript` array is removed. In execute and dry-run modes it carries the same argv the `invocations` array already carries; in explain mode it is the only body there is, and under the layout explain emits step and argv records like every other mode. It also is NOT the live stream it reads as — cli/swarm/cli/command.go builds `var transcript strings.Builder`, passes `Out: &transcript` to plan.Runner, and assigns `result.Transcript = lines(transcript.String())` after the command finishes, so the rendered report re-emits a buffer and nothing in it survives an interruption. That property is real inside plan.Runner and is lost by the time the surface prints.

(b) `facts[].invocations` becomes a list of source names rather than a list of argv vectors, with the argv living once in `invocations`. That is what removes the 477 duplicated commands measured in swarm status.

Both raise contract-swarm-json`s major version under its own Versioning and Change Policy. Filed with the renderer work as agent-plugins-ih18.26 rather than taken here.

comments.author: dev-bd97-8
comments.text:
retro:environment A worktree-isolated agent in this harness cannot run a compound bash command, and the refusal names neither the offending clause nor a workaround that works.

evidence: Four consecutive Bash calls in this dispatch were refused with:

  This agent is isolated in the worktree /home/user/agent-plugins/.claude/worktrees/agent-a0f77b5f20e685b90, but this command is too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree. Refusing to run it — a worktree-isolated agent`s git operations must target its own worktree. Split it into plain, separate commands and run them from <worktree>.

Refused: `git rev-parse --short HEAD && { git merge-base --is-ancestor 80c9113 HEAD; echo "ancestor-exit=$?"; }`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor $(git rev-parse <branch>) HEAD; echo $?`; and two `export VAR=...; <binary> ... ; echo $?` sequences whose only git content was none at all.

Accepted: the same commands one per call. Also accepted: `cd /path/cli && go build -o /tmp/... ./swarm 2>&1; echo "build-exit=$?"` — a three-clause compound with a cd and a redirect — so the trigger is not compound-ness alone and not paths outside the worktree.

Two costs. First, it took four calls to find the accepted form, and the message`s advice ("split it into plain, separate commands") is the fix but is buried under a git-specific explanation for commands containing no git. Second, and worse for this repository: AGENTS.md requires reading an exit status WITHOUT a pipe — `cmd >out 2>&1; echo $?` — and that is exactly the shape most often refused. The workaround used here was to run the command bare and read the harness`s own reported exit code, which works but is not the form AGENTS.md documents. An agent that did not notice would reach for a pipe.

comments.author: dev-bd97-8
comments.text:
retro:gap Three defects were found while measuring for the spec that are not layout problems and would survive any reshaping. All three are filed rather than fixed here.

evidence:

1. agent-plugins-ih18.27 — an unknown flag escapes contract-swarm-json`s "emit a conforming result on every exit status" guarantee entirely. Measured: `swarm manifest get --run agent-plugins-bd97 --bogus` exits 3 having printed `Error: unknown flag: --bogus` on standard error and nothing on standard output, and `--json` does not change it. Cobra rejects the flag during parsing, so cli.finish() — the only place a result becomes a status and a rendering — never runs.

2. agent-plugins-ih18.28, first half — a refusal taken before the mode is resolved reports the zero-valued mode, which is explain. Measured: `swarm manifest get --key branch` prints `swarm manifest get (explain)` although no mode flag was passed and execute is what would have run. The ordering that causes it is correct and required (AC-SWARM-CORE-001.14: nothing read or written outside the scope), so the fix is to the mode and not to the order.

3. agent-plugins-ih18.28, second half — a guard refusal emits a resolution byte-identical to its summary. Measured: `swarm manifest set --run agent-plugins-bd97 --dry-run --key review_passes --value 3` prints the same string after `summary: ` and after `what would resolve this: `. Result.Validate refuses an EMPTY resolution, which is necessary and not sufficient — this passes the check and tells the caller nothing.

The gap the three share: every one of them is a property nothing checks. The surface enforces "a fact names an invocation" and "an attention outcome names a resolution" structurally, and those two hold everywhere; the three above are enforced by nobody and each is broken. The spec`s value is that its Conformance table now names them, but a table is not a check either — agent-plugins-ih18.26 should land assertions, not just a renderer.

comments.author: coordinator-bd97
comments.text: RE-SCOPED by the repository owner's review of PR #31, three comments on 2026-08-30 (discussion_r3890065950, r3889941589, r3889982920). The first draft is rejected in full, not amended: it invented a nine-keyword line grammar to make a bespoke format decodable, which is solving the wrong problem when YAML exists. The owner's words: 'I have never experienced a command whose default output was so verbose' and 'This document needs to be rewritten entirely and renamed to swarm-output-standards.md.' Two further rulings, and both delete rules rather than add them: no line budget and no elision (agents read long lines), and a command asked for a value returns the value — the draft had --full-result answer with a description of the value plus instructions to re-run the same command without the flag, which inverts what the flag means.

comments.author: dev-bd97-8
comments.text:
retro:decision Six things the owner's direction did not pin, decided in the standard with the alternative named. All six are reviewable at the pull request.

evidence:

1. WHAT `require` REPORTS AS A VALUE. The owner's rule is "success renders the properties and their values". `require`'s facts today are flags: measured, `swarm manifest require --run fixture-run --key trailers --key findings_path` reports `findings_path = false` / `trailers = true`, where `false` means "not written" and not "holds false". Under the standard `require` reports the same VALUES `get` reports and the verdict is the exit status. Rejected keeping the flags, because a flag in the value position is exactly the ambiguity the bead was filed over. It costs `require` no extra invocation — it already reads the whole document in one `bd show`.

2. WHERE THE RESOLUTION GOES. The envelope carries one command-level `resolution`; the owner's failure sketch has no place for it. Decided: it goes inside the failing property's `issues`. Rejected a sibling top-level `resolution` key, because "the properties and nothing else" is the rule the success form keeps and a sibling key collides the first time a command reports a property by that name.

3. WHAT SELECTS THE TWO SHAPES. Decided: the exit status. Clear (0) renders the flat mapping; anything else renders the per-property mapping. Rejected one shape for both — the per-property form always — which would wrap three lines around every value in the common case, which is the verbosity the re-scope exists to remove.

4. A THIRD SHAPE, FOR A REFUSAL THAT NAMES NO PROPERTY. Measured: `swarm manifest get --key branch` with no `--run` exits 3 having established nothing, so there is no property to key on. Decided: a top-level `issues` sequence. It stays decodable because `issues` maps to a SEQUENCE where a property maps to a MAPPING.

5. MAPPING, NOT A SEQUENCE OF SINGLE-KEY MAPS. The owner's sketch wrote `trailers:` then `- ok: false` / `- value: null` / `- issues:`. That parses as a list of three separate single-key mappings, so a reader indexes by position to reach a named field. Changed to one mapping with three keys, and the document says so in a sentence so nobody re-derives the sketch.

6. `|-` NOT `|`. The owner's example wrote `trailers: |`. YAML's `|` clips to exactly ONE trailing newline; the value in his example has none. Measured: `yaml.safe_load` of the standard's block returns `'Do re me\nfa so la ti\ndo'` — the exact bytes the tracker holds — only with `|-`. The standard pins the indicator that round-trips (`|-` none, `|` one, `|+` more) rather than pinning `|`.

comments.author: dev-bd97-8
comments.text:
retro:gap The YAML design exposes one shape gap the four fact kinds cannot carry, and it is not a rendering problem.

evidence: `swarm manifest get --run fixture-run` answers with 19 properties. Two of them hold JSON objects, and the CLI reports an object as `text` carrying its JSON — `container-swarm-cli` says so deliberately ("the contract declares four kinds and inventing a fifth here would put a shape in the envelope the schema does not"). Under YAML that reads:

models: "{\"advanced\":\"opus\",\"frontier\":\"fable\",\"light\":\"haiku\",\"standard\":\"sonnet\"}"

standing_auth is the same, at 341 characters. Everything around them is readable YAML; these two are escaped JSON in the middle of it, and they are exactly the two properties a reader is most likely to want to read structurally.

The fix is a fifth fact kind whose value is one of the concrete structs `schemas/swarm/manifest.strata` already declares — `TierModels`, `StandingAuth`. That is a discriminated union, which does not compile correctly under `allowAdditionalProperties: false` (measured; see the proof comment and agent-plugins-xxye). Strata offers no `Any` to fall back on (measured: `Unknown type 'Any'`). The remaining option is the FactValue-style hand-rolled workaround extended by one optional field per concrete object type, which does not scale as the manifest grows object-valued keys.

The standard records this as an open question and does NOT require it, so nothing here is blocked. But it is the one place where "run the command and read the output" still needs a footnote, and it is blocked on upstream rather than on us.

comments.author: dev-bd97-8
comments.text:
retro:environment The worktree-isolation refusal recurred, and this run found the shape that triggers it: a heredoc whose body contains a heredoc, not compound-ness.

evidence: Three Bash calls in this dispatch were refused with "This agent is isolated in the worktree /home/user/agent-plugins/.claude/worktrees/agent-aeb5f251276017221, but this command is too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree. Refusing to run it — a worktree-isolated agent's git operations must target its own worktree. Split it into plain, separate commands and run them from <path>."

Refused:
1. `export BEADS_ACTOR=...; git rev-parse --show-toplevel && git status --porcelain && echo ... && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` — actual git content, plausible trigger.
2. `git merge-base --is-ancestor $(git rev-parse <branch>) HEAD; echo "base-exit=$?"` — a command substitution inside a git argument.
3. `mkdir -p D && cd D && cp ... && cat > u.strata <<'EOF' ... EOF && ls` — NO git content at all.
4. `cat > mkst.sh <<'SH' ... cat > "$D/u.strata" <<'EOF' ... EOF ... SH` — no git content, and refused where the same script written with a single heredoc was accepted.

Accepted, repeatedly: `cat > /path/script.sh <<'SH' ... SH` followed by `sh /path/script.sh` — including scripts whose bodies contain `cd`, redirects, `$?` reads and git commands. Also accepted: `cd .../cli && go build -o /tmp/... ./swarm 2>&1; echo "build-exit=$?"`, and `python3 - <<'PY' ... PY`.

So the trigger is not compound-ness, not `cd`, not paths outside the worktree, and not the presence of git. It is nesting: a heredoc containing a heredoc, and a command substitution embedded in a git argument.

The workaround that works every time, and which AGENTS.md's "read the exit status without a pipe" rule needs: write a small script file (Write tool, or one `cat > file <<'SH'`), then `sh file`. Inside the script, `cmd >out 2>&1; echo $?` runs fine. The prior pass's note that the harness "sometimes refuses compound bash commands" was right; this narrows it to a shape an agent can avoid on the first try instead of the fourth.

Cost this run: three refused calls, ~2 minutes. The refusal message's advice ("split it into plain, separate commands") is still buried under a git-specific explanation for commands containing no git.

comments.author: dev-bd97-8
comments.text:
retro:proof Every claim in the standard was measured here rather than inherited from the dispatch prompt, and two of the three handed-over claims came out sharper than they were handed over.

evidence:

BINARY. `cd cli && go build -o /tmp/.../swarm ./swarm` from the worktree at 6fb18cd, exit 0. The PATH binary was not used. All command measurements below are that binary.

ISOLATED WORLD. The e2e `core` fixture was restored by hand the way `cli/swarm/e2e/harness_test.go` restores it — `git clone` of `cli/testdata/swarm-fixtures/core/repository.bundle`, `git checkout claude/bead-bonanza-fixture`, `bd init --prefix fixture`, `bd import .../tracker.jsonl`, with HOME, BEADS_ACTOR, LC_ALL and TZ pinned as `world.env()` pins them. Nothing was written to this repository's tracker to produce an example. `swarm manifest set --run fixture-run --key trailers --value '"Do re me\nfa so la ti\ndo"'` in that world is what produced the owner's own example value.

1. require vs validate — CONFIRMED as handed over. `swarm manifest validate --run agent-plugins-bd97` → `summary: every rule holds at the retro stage`, `outcome: clear (exit 0)`, trailers never mentioned. `swarm manifest require --run agent-plugins-bd97 --key trailers` → `summary: trailers: not written`, `outcome: attention (exit 1)`. And `grep -c checkType cli/swarm/manifest/validate.go` → 3, with `Require` (validate.go:403) performing exactly two tests per key: `Lookup(name)` for declaredness and `doc.Get(name)` for presence. Recorded as an open question, not settled.

2. strata generic unions — CONFIRMED, and measured from a probe I wrote rather than from the prior run's note. `@discriminator("kind") union Answer { @tag("text") TextAnswer  @tag("count") CountAnswer }` under this repo's `strata.config.json`: `strata build . --target json-schema` exits 0 and emits `TextAnswer` as `{"additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"text": ...}, "required": ["text"]}` — no `kind` — while `--target go` emits a `MarshalJSON` that builds `{"kind":"text",` + the variant's own object. The union's `allOf` branch is `then: {"$ref": "#/definitions/TextAnswer"}`, so the Go target's own output fails `additionalProperties: false`. Both variants.

3. NEW, and it changed the proposal: an `alias` to a map IS a legal root type and emits a BARE root mapping. `alias FailingAnswer: [String: PropertyVerdict]` → `{"additionalProperties": {"$ref": ".../PropertyVerdict"}, "propertyNames": {"type": "string"}, "type": "object"}`. A `struct` wrapping the same map nests it one level deeper, which would not be the wire form. The block printed in the standard was compiled AS PRINTED, extracted from the markdown by script into a package alongside the real `schemas/swarm/output.strata`: `--target json-schema` exit 0 and `--target go` exit 0.

4. NEW: strata has no `Any`. A probe declaring `value: Any` fails with `Unknown type 'Any'`. This is what makes the object-valued-property gap wait on upstream rather than being routed around.

5. EVERY YAML EXAMPLE IS GENERATED, NOT TYPED. A 100-line renderer applies the standard's own style rules to the measured `--json` envelopes; a second script re-extracts every ```yaml block from the committed document and asserts it is byte-identical to the generator's output. Result: blocks 0,1,4,5,6,7,8,9 match a generated file exactly; blocks 2 and 10 are the refusal shape, derived from the measured refusal text, and their scalars satisfy the standard's own plain-scalar predicate; block 3 is one line lifted from block 6. All eleven parse under `yaml.safe_load`.

6. THE SIZE CLAIMS. `swarm status --run fixture-run` text form: 24 lines, 3,914 bytes (`wc -lc`). Its answer under the standard: 22 lines, 765 bytes. `swarm manifest get --run fixture-run` text form: 29 lines, 2,077 bytes; answer: 32 lines, 1,218 bytes. On the real run epic, `swarm status --run agent-plugins-bd97`: 25 lines, 35,856 bytes — my own measurement, which supersedes the "24 lines, 33,329 bytes" the prior pass recorded (state moved; the run is now at an attention outcome, adding a resolution line). `swarm manifest get --run agent-plugins-bd97 --key checks_baseline`: 339 lines, 18,715 bytes — the prior pass's figure, reproduced exactly.

comments.author: dev-bd97-8
comments.text:
retro:scope Two things found while writing the standard were filed rather than done, and one bead I own was rewritten because it pointed at a deleted file.

title: partitioning.md's sequencing query reads c4_impacts inverted and orders producers last
description:
partitioning.md and groom-beads define c4_impacts in OPPOSITE directions, and the reference's jq acts on its own definition.

- partitioning.md: 'Bead B whose c4_impacts intersects bead A's c4_changes consumes a contract A is changing.'
- groom-beads' SKILL.md: impacts are 'downstream components affected but not edited'.

Measured over run agent-plugins-bd97's 19 beads, the reference's query emitted:

    sequence agent-plugins-ih18.2 after agent-plugins-ih18.6
    sequence agent-plugins-ih18.2 after agent-plugins-ih18.5

but .2 (PROC) is the producer both are built on, and the feature blueprint's Sequencing Constraints state 'The PROC delta SHALL land before the TRK and VCS deltas.' 12 of the 33 sequence lines it emitted are inverted this way.

A planner that trusted the output would build the dependency graph backwards and serialize the run in the wrong order. That is worse than having no signal, because it looks like one. The run's planner did not trust it — it used the blueprint's stated constraints instead, and said so — but that was a judgement call an agent had to make against its own reference.

Source: retro candidate C2, run agent-plugins-bd97, finding bd97.3#2. Accepted by the human at the retro's single ask.
acceptance_criteria:
- The sequencing query in partitioning.md matches groom-beads' definition: a bead whose c4_changes intersects another's c4_impacts is the PRODUCER and sequences first.
- The direction is stated in one sentence beside the query, so the two documents cannot drift apart silently again.
- Re-running the corrected query over run agent-plugins-bd97's 19 beads orders PROC before TRK and VCS, matching the blueprint's Stage 2.

title: bd-health.sh's repo-global exit status cannot gate one epic's readiness
description:
groom-beads' SKILL.md says "Do not declare the set ready while it exits non-zero." The script's exit status reflects the WHOLE REPOSITORY, not the queue being gated, so the instruction is unfollowable in any repository with pre-existing beads.

Measured in run agent-plugins-bd97:

    bash .claude/skills/groom-beads/scripts/bd-health.sh
    -> exit 1, 'RESULT: hard problems found in: swarm validate'

Every id it named was FOREIGN to the run — agent-plugins-qozp.6, agent-plugins-so39.2 and others — each reading 'is not an epic or molecule (type: task)'. Meanwhile the queue actually being gated was clean:

    bd swarm validate agent-plugins-ih18
    -> exit 0, 'Swarmable: YES', 19 issues, max parallelism 3, 12 waves

The cost is not a false alarm, it is a DEAD GATE. A check that can never go green in a real repository gets ignored, and a genuine graph problem inside the queue would then be invisible in the noise it is already producing.

Source: retro candidate C1, run agent-plugins-bd97, finding bd97.3#1. Accepted by the human at the retro's single ask.
acceptance_criteria:
- The readiness gate reads a status scoped to the epic being gated, not to the repository.
- Either bd-health.sh takes an epic and filters findings to that epic's descendants, or groom-beads' SKILL.md instructs reading the per-epic 'bd swarm validate <epic>' status instead of the script's global exit.
- Re-running against run agent-plugins-bd97's queue reproduces exit 0 for agent-plugins-ih18 while foreign beads remain broken.

title: sprint-cleanup.sh can force-remove a live worktree it misattributed to the previous dispatch
description:
## Problem

`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh` now attributes a
worktree to a dispatch through the bead its HEAD commit closed
(`owner_for_worktree`, which replaced `owner_for_branch`). A worktree that has
not yet produced a close commit of its own inherits the sprint branch's tip —
i.e. the PREVIOUS dispatch's close commit — so it is attributed to that
dispatch. If that dispatch has drained, `handle_worktree` takes the removal
path and runs:

    run "remove worktree ($_hw_who drained)" git worktree remove --force "$1"

`--force` removes a worktree with uncommitted changes. The two ways this is
reached in practice: a subagent that crashed before its first close (the case
`recovery.md` says to finish from inside that worktree), and a recovering
session running the script while a dispatch is still on its first bead — the
header itself invites that ("A recovering session may run it too").

The retired branch-name scheme did not have this hole: a worktree was owned
from birth by the branch it was created on, so a dispatch with no commits yet
still resolved to itself and was left standing.

## Evidence

Attribution, measured in a scratch repo:

    git commit -m "demo-r7k.1 P1 the previous bead"
    git worktree add /…/fresh -b bb/dev-r7k-2 HEAD
    git -C /…/fresh log -1 --format=%s
    -> demo-r7k.1 P1 the previous bead        # the PREVIOUS dispatch's bead

Destructiveness, same repo:

    echo "uncommitted work" > /…/fresh/inprogress.txt
    git -C /…/fresh status --short   -> ?? inprogress.txt
    git worktree remove --force /…/fresh   -> exit 0
    ls /…/fresh -> No such file or directory   # the file is gone

Code: `owner_for_worktree()` and `handle_worktree()` in
`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh`; the removal line quoted
above.

The script's self-test does not cover this: every `worktree owner` case drives
`owner_for_worktree` with a stubbed `git log` that returns a close commit, and
the guard cases stub `owner_for_worktree` itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A worktree whose HEAD commit is not a commit that worktree itself made is
  never removed on the strength of the previous dispatch's assignee — it is
  reported LEFT, per the script's own "NEVER DESTRUCTIVE ON AMBIGUITY" rule.
- A dirty worktree is never `--force`-removed, or the removal is gated on the
  tree being clean.
- `--self-test` gains a case for a worktree whose HEAD commit predates it.

## Steps to Reproduce

From a clean checkout at 24f97e3:

1. `git init` a scratch repo, commit once with the subject `demo-r7k.1 P1 the previous bead`.
2. `git worktree add /tmp/fresh -b bb/dev-r7k-2 HEAD` — the new worktree makes no commit of its own.
3. `git -C /tmp/fresh log -1 --format=%s` prints the PREVIOUS bead's subject, which is what `owner_for_worktree` parses.
4. Write an uncommitted file into `/tmp/fresh`, then `git worktree remove --force /tmp/fresh` — it succeeds and the file is gone.

In the script, step 3 resolves the owner to the previous dispatch; if that dispatch has drained, `handle_worktree` runs step 4.

title: A dev agent cannot tell a coordinator's deliberate write from a tool anomaly, and silently reverts run decisions
description:
A dispatch agent observed two of its own filed beads carrying field values it had not passed, diagnosed them as a bd create anomaly, and 'repaired' both. Both values were deliberate coordinator writes, and the repair reverted two run decisions without anyone noticing until the coordinator re-read the tracker.

Sequence, all within run agent-plugins-bd97:

1. dev-bd97-4 filed agent-plugins-ih18.21 (03:41:30Z) and .22 (03:41:47Z) as out-of-scope work found while implementing ADOPT-MAN. Both arrived unassigned with null metadata.
2. The coordinator triaged them: ADMITTED .21 (assigned it to dev-bd97-4, tiered it, wired .19<-.21) and DEFERRED .22 out of the run (bd defer --until=+30d), recording both as amendments on the run epic with reasons. Both states were VERIFIED in place immediately after the writes: '.21 status=open assignee=dev-bd97-4' and '.22 status=deferred', the latter also verified absent from the ready front.
3. dev-bd97-4 then reported: 'Three creates with identical flag shapes gave three different results for fields I never passed: one bead assigned to $BEADS_ACTOR (and it then appeared in my own dispatch queue), one deferred to 2026-09-28 and hidden from bd ready, one clean. Both repaired by hand (--defer "", --assignee "").'
4. Measured after its return: .21 assignee empty, .22 status open, deferred_until empty, and .22 back in the ready front. updated_at on both is 03:52:4xZ, eleven minutes after creation and after the coordinator's writes.

The agent's reasoning was locally sound — it did not pass those flags, so something else set them — and its conclusion was wrong. There is no bd create anomaly here: 'assigned to $BEADS_ACTOR' is exactly the coordinator's assignment of .21 to dev-bd97-4, which IS that agent's actor string, and '2026-09-28' is exactly +30d from the coordinator's defer of .22. A third bead it filed (.23) was triaged later and its assignment survived, because the agent had already finished repairing by then.

The defect is structural, not the agent's judgement:

- Nothing in a bead records WHO set a field or WHY. An assignee is a plain string and a defer is a date; neither carries provenance, so a deliberate triage decision and a tool bug are indistinguishable from inside a dispatch.
- The coordinator writes to beads a dispatch agent is concurrently reading, and the run has no channel telling an agent 'this bead has been triaged, its fields are now the coordinator's'.
- The consequence is silent. Both reverts exited 0, the batch reported success truthfully, and the run's own scope-creep check went on passing because the bead was still a child of the target — only the exclusion was gone.

Also worth noting: the anomaly report itself propagated. It was stated as measured fact in a batch return, and would have entered the retro as a bd defect had the coordinator not held the contradicting evidence.

Done when: a dispatch agent has a stated rule for fields it did not set, and the run has a way to make a triage decision durable against one.
acceptance_criteria:
- run-batch states the rule: a field you did not pass is not yours to clear; report it, do not repair it.
- The coordinator's triage of a mid-run bead is recorded on the bead itself (metadata carrying admitted/deferred and by whom), so an agent reading it can tell a decision from an anomaly.
- Re-running this scenario — coordinator assigns and defers beads a live dispatch filed — ends with both decisions intact.
- Where an agent does report an unexpected field value, the report names it as unexplained rather than as a tool defect, unless it has evidence beyond 'I did not set it'.

title: swarm manifest refuses `trailers`, the one stageless declared key
description:
Adopting `swarm manifest` into the skills (ADOPT-MAN) found that the command cannot read, require or write the `trailers` key at all — it reports it as undeclared, which is false: it IS declared, on `RunManifest` itself rather than in a stage struct.

Measured on this tree (binary built from cli/ at the end-to-end fixture commit):

    swarm manifest get     --run <epic> --key trailers
      -> summary: trailers: not a declared manifest key
      -> outcome: malformed (exit 3)
    swarm manifest require --run <epic> --key branch --key checks_baseline --key trailers
      -> summary: trailers: not a declared manifest key
      -> outcome: malformed (exit 3)
    swarm manifest set     --run <epic> --key trailers --value '"x"' --dry-run
      -> summary: manifest: refusing the write, and storing none of it — "trailers" is not a declared manifest key
      -> outcome: malformed (exit 3)

Cause, by reading the code: `cli/swarm/manifest/manifest.go`, `buildKeys()` builds the declared set from `contract.StageDeclarations()` alone, which enumerates the five stage structs. `swarmmodel.RunManifest.Trailers` carries the json tag `trailers,omitempty` and appears in no stage struct — that placement is deliberate, and `contract.AlwaysOptional()` exists precisely to derive it — so `manifest.Lookup("trailers")` misses and `declared()` in `cli/swarm/cli/manifest.go` refuses the key.

`specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md`, the paragraph beginning "A key whose absence is legitimate at every stage has no stage", says such a key "is not reported at all — a reader told pending would wait for something that is never coming", and names `trailers` as the one today. That justifies leaving it out of VALIDATE findings. It does not justify refusing an explicit `--key trailers` on `get`, `require` or `set`, and the message given ("not a declared manifest key") is false either way.

Consequence, live today: `run-batch` cannot ask the manifest whether the run resolved commit trailers, so `plugin/skills/run-batch/SKILL.md` now instructs it to pass `--trailers-from` and read `bb-close-bead.sh`'s exit 2 instead. That is a workaround around a command that should answer.

Done when: the always-optional keys are readable, requirable and writable through `swarm manifest`, with unit coverage naming `trailers` specifically; `validate` still reports no pending finding for a stageless key; and `plugin/skills/run-batch/SKILL.md` plus the "trailers is the one key the command does not serve" bullet in `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md` are updated to the command form.

Adjacent, not blocking: ADOPT-MAN landed without it.

metadata.admitted_as: amendment — bug in this run's own output, found by dev-bd97-4 during ADOPT-MAN
metadata.tier_reason: A correctness fix in the declared-key derivation plus a behavioural distinction validate must keep (stageless keys stay out of pending findings while becoming addressable), and three documents to bring into step.

comments.author: dev-bd97-4
comments.text:
retro:decision the fix names the stageless-ness on the Key itself, and validate.go now branches on that rather than keeping a second derivation of the same set
evidence:
Two ways to make a stageless key addressable were open.

Rejected: leave `buildKeys()` alone and special-case `trailers` (or
`contract.AlwaysOptional()`) at each of the three call sites that refuse an
unknown key — `declared()` in cli/swarm/cli/manifest.go, `manifest.Check`, and
`manifest.Require`. Cost: three places to keep in step, and a key added to
`RunManifest` tomorrow would still be refused by whichever one was forgotten.

Taken: `buildKeys()` appends the keys `contract.AlwaysOptional()` reports, with
an EMPTY `Key.Stage`, and the field's doc says empty means "required at no
stage", never "unknown". Every reader of the declared set then gets the key for
free — `Lookup`, `Keys`, `Check`, `Require`, `Validate`, `declared()`,
`declaredNames()` — and a new stageless key needs no code change at all.

Consequence checked, not assumed: `reached()` in cli/swarm/cli/manifest.go
skips any key whose `Stage != stage`, so an empty stage matches no real stage
and the derived-stage calculation is unaffected.

Second decision inside that one: `validate.go` held its own `alwaysOptional`
map, built from `contract.AlwaysOptional()`, used solely to keep such a key out
of the pending findings. With the stageless-ness now on the Key, that map was a
second derivation of the same fact, so it is deleted and the switch branches on
`key.Stage == ""`. Rejected the alternative of keeping both: the package's own
header says the declared key set has one source and "this package cannot hold a
fourth opinion about any of them", and two derivations is how the opinions
start. The behaviour is unchanged and is pinned by the pre-existing assertion in
TestValidationSeparatesAKeyNotYetWrittenFromOneThatIsWrong that `trailers` is
reported at no severity at all.

title: Plan phase should emit an ASCII wave graph so a serialized run is visible before dispatch
description:
The plan phase returns its partition as prose. A reader cannot see from it whether the run will actually run in parallel, and the failure mode is silent: the run dispatches, looks healthy on every check, and is single-threaded.

## What this run did, and why prose was not enough

Run agent-plugins-bd97 over agent-plugins-ih18 (20 beads, 37 blocks edges). The planner DID report the numbers — '17 waves at max parallelism 2', and the pre-edge baseline '12 waves at max 3'. Both were accurate. The shape they describe was still not apparent to anyone until the run had been executing for some time and a human asked why it was slow.

Computed from the loaded graph:

    beads=20 edges=37 waves=17
    width histogram: {1: 14, 2: 3}
    mean width = 1.18    critical path = 17 waves

    wave  width  beads
       1      1  #    1(sta)
       2      1  #    2(adv)
       3      1  #    3(adv)
       4      1  #    4(sta)
       5      2  ##   5(adv) 12(lig)
       6      1  #    6(sta)
       7      1  #    7(adv)
       8      1  #    8(adv)
       9      1  #    9(sta)
      10      1  #    10(sta)
      11      1  #    11(adv)
      12      1  #    13(adv)
      13      1  #    14(adv)
      14      1  #    15(sta)
      15      2  ##   16(adv) 18(sta)
      16      2  ##   17(lig) 20(lig)
      17      1  #    19(adv)

Fourteen of seventeen waves are width 1. The run provisioned four dispatch agents and could work one at a time; dev-bd97-4 and dev-bd97-5 had never had a single ready bead by wave 11. 'Max width 2' and 'this is a serial run with two brief exceptions' are the same fact, and only the second is actionable.

## What to build

The plan phase computes the wave decomposition already — it must, to state a wave count. Emit it as a rendered artifact rather than a number, in the return AND recorded durably (the run epic's metadata or a file the manifest points at, so a resuming session and the retro can both read it).

At minimum the render should carry: wave index, width, a bar, and each bead with its tier. Tier belongs in it because the same picture answers a second question — this run's original partition mixed tiers in all three batches (see the tier-split bead) and a per-wave tier column makes an incoherent batch visible in the same glance.

Worth considering, not prescribed:
- A summary line a human can act on: mean width, critical path length, and the count of waves at width 1.
- Marking WHY each edge exists — real dependency vs collision vs sequencing — since the actionable question is almost always 'which of these edges did we add ourselves'. On this run the C4 component signal contributed zero edges and c4_docs contributed all the collision ones.
- A before/after render when collision edges are added, so the cost of the serialization decision is priced at the moment it is taken. This run traded 12 waves at width 3 for 17 at width 2 and the trade was recorded in prose; as two graphs it would have been obvious.
- A threshold the plan states rather than the reader computing: e.g. name it explicitly when mean width < 1.5 or when the dispatch count exceeds the max width, because provisioning four agents for a graph that admits two is itself the finding.

## Why it belongs in the plan phase

It is the last point where the shape is cheap to change. After dispatch the edges are loaded, worktrees exist and beads are in flight; the only remaining lever is dropping edges mid-run, which is exactly the decision nobody wants to take under way. The plan phase already holds the graph and already emits a verdict — this makes the verdict legible.

Related: the collision-granularity bead (the run's real contention was one shared document, unmodelled by the component signal) and the tier-split bead (nothing enforces tier coherence at dispatch). This bead does not fix either; it makes both visible earlier.
design: Do not add a new graph computation. The wave decomposition is already performed to produce the wave count the plan reports; this renders what is computed. Keep it dependency-free ASCII — it is read in a terminal, in a task notification and in a retro document, and none of those render images.
acceptance_criteria:
- The plan phase emits an ASCII wave graph covering every bead in the queue, with wave index, width and per-bead tier.
- The render is recorded durably, not only in the return: a resuming session and the retro can both retrieve it from the run epic.
- Re-running it against run agent-plugins-bd97's loaded graph reproduces 17 waves, a width histogram of {1:14, 2:3}, and mean width 1.18.
- The output distinguishes edges the plan ADDED (collision, sequencing) from pre-existing dependency edges, so a reader can tell which serialization is the plan's own doing.
- A run whose graph admits less parallelism than the dispatch count provisions is named as such by the plan, rather than left for a reader to infer.

title: Collision avoidance is component-granular; the real contention is a single shared document
description:
A sprint over agent-plugins-ih18 (run agent-plugins-bd97, 19 beads) measured its collision front and found the C4-component signal the partitioner is built on caught none of the real contention, while an unmodelled signal caught all of it.

Measured on that run:

- The C4 co-edit query returned 8 pairs on 3 components (Swarm Command Surface, Manifest, Coordinator). EVERY ONE was already ordered by a real dependency edge, so the declared mechanism contributed zero edges.
- The contention that mattered came from 'c4_docs': 15 of the 19 beads name specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md and 4 name specs/architecture/module-bead-bonanza.md, because every bead carries the acceptance line 'This delta is folded into its owning blueprint.' That is up to 15 branches appending to one markdown roster and diagram.
- c4_docs is not named as a collision signal anywhere in partitioning.md, and it is invisible to both declared layers: it is not a component edit, and the path lives in acceptance_criteria rather than the description the layer-2 path scan reads.
- Cost of serializing it: the queue went from 12 waves at max width 3 to 17 waves at max width 2. Essentially a serial run of a 19-bead sprint.

The mechanism is too coarse in one direction and mis-aimed in the other: components do not predict document contention, and a whole document is far coarser than the actual unit of conflict, which is a roster row or a diagram block.

Four candidate directions, to be evaluated rather than assumed:

1. Defer the spec fold. One terminal task updates the owning blueprint for every delta in the run, so no two implementation beads ever touch it. Removes the contention entirely; costs a bead that must not be skipped, and the blueprint is stale until it runs.
2. Split the document. Encourage per-component files under the container blueprint so 15 deltas append to 15 files. Structural fix, but pushes work into the spec corpus and into the spec skill's templates.
3. Make the collision key granular. Replace component-level keys with file+section (a heading path) or file+function keys, so two beads appending different sections of one markdown file are correctly seen as non-colliding. Most precise; needs a way for grooming to state the section a delta lands in, and a way to verify it.
4. Read c4_docs as a first-class collision signal. The smallest change; would have caught this run's contention exactly. Does nothing about granularity, so it keeps the serialization cost.

These are not exclusive: 4 is the cheap correctness fix, 3 is the one that recovers the parallelism, 1 and 2 change what gets written rather than how it is scheduled.

Done when: partitioning.md names the signals it actually needs, the collision key's granularity is decided and specified, and a sprint over a corpus-editing epic like ih18 no longer serializes on one document by construction.
acceptance_criteria:
- The measurement above is reproduced or corrected against the current partitioner.
- A decision is recorded (ADR or standards update) on the collision key's granularity and on where the spec fold happens.
- partitioning.md's collision layers are updated to match that decision, including whichever of c4_docs / file+section / deferred-fold is adopted.
- A dry-run partition over an epic with a shared owning blueprint shows the intended wave count rather than a serial chain.
