title: sprint-plan and grooming-prompt.md describe two different topologies; only one can be right
description:
MEASURED by reading both files on the post-f78def4 tree.

grooming-prompt.md (sprint-plan/references/) is a prompt the COORDINATOR dispatches. Its last instruction: "FINALLY, as your last act, invoke the sprint-plan skill and follow it to produce the run collision-edge file... You have just read every bead, which is why planning is yours and not a second agent second." So the topology it describes is: coordinator -> grooming agent -> (in-process) sprint-plan. ONE subagent.

sprint-plan/SKILL.md section 2 says the opposite: "Dispatch a grooming subagent over the ungroomed subset (template below); it runs groom-beads... Its final act is to invoke sprint-plan." So sprint-plan dispatches grooming, and grooming re-invokes sprint-plan. TWO subagents, and sprint-plan runs twice.

bead-bonanza/SKILL.md asserts "One subagent, never two."

All three cannot hold. The consequence is not cosmetic: it decides WHO runs the readiness triage, and therefore whether sprint-plan needs the per-bead Definition of Ready at all.

- Under the grooming-prompt topology, grooming runs first over the whole queue. groom-beads step 1 is already "Scope the grooming set - find what actually needs grooming", so the triage is grooming own and sprint-plan needs no copy of the checklist.
- Under the SKILL.md topology, sprint-plan triages first, so it must apply the per-bead DoR - which is why the vendored copy exists.

DECIDE the topology, then the DoR copy follows from it rather than being argued separately. See also agent-plugins-hg9t.4, which closed on the second reading.

UNVERIFIED: groom-beads behaviour when handed a queue that is already entirely ready. Its checklist implies a no-op scan at step 1, but no run has been observed doing it, and the cheap-check optimisation in sprint-plan exists precisely to avoid paying for that case.
notes:
DECIDED by the owner 2026-08-25: Reading B, one subagent doing both jobs in one context. The coordinator dispatches sprint-plan; sprint-plan invokes groom-beads itself and then plans, with every description it just read still in context.

The deciding argument is one I had underweighted, and the owner supplied it: c4_changes / c4_impacts are OPTIONAL metadata. sprint-plan/SKILL.md:228 already says so — 'File paths — fallback and corroborator. Scan each bead's description for fixture names + source paths. It is the whole signal where c4_* is absent.' So on a repo that documents no architecture the collision signal IS the prose, grooming has just read all of it, and a two-agent split would re-read every description while a metadata-only planner would silently under-detect collisions on exactly those repos.

That also inverts my objection to the partition preview. Under a two-agent split it was a boundary violation — grooming guessing at what planning recomputes. In one context it is the opposite: signal captured at the one moment it is cheap, with Plan still the source of truth on packing. Kept, and the blueprint says why.

Landed: grooming-prompt.md deleted (4.1KB, its only citation removed); sprint-plan section 1 now invokes groom-beads in-process rather than 'asking' it ambiguously; bead-bonanza says one subagent and why; the flat-split rule added (a grooming split stays siblings-with-edges, never a sub-epic, or bounces for re-admission as a second target); the queue query corrected to bd list --parent <target> --status open, since bd ready excludes the blocked and deferred beads that most need grooming.

module-bead-bonanza now has zero open questions.

comments.author: claude-simplify
comments.text:
SHARPENED 2026-08-25 after the DoR extraction (commit 414bc27) narrowed it. sprint-plan no longer says 'dispatch a grooming subagent', so the contradiction is now four concrete differences rather than a flat 'two subagents vs one':

| | Reading A (grooming-prompt.md) | Reading B (sprint-plan/SKILL.md) |
|---|---|---|
| coordinator dispatches | the GROOMING agent | the PLAN agent |
| who invokes whom | grooming -> sprint-plan, last act | plan -> groom-beads, first act |
| who resolves the queue | the coordinator, into {ID_1}..{PLAN_IDS} | sprint-plan, from the epic |
| grooming-prompt.md | live, the run's real entry point | DEAD, nothing would send it |

Both satisfy bead-bonanza's 'One subagent, never two', so the coordinator's text does not settle it.

RECOMMENDATION: Reading B. It puts the queue with the component that owns it, and it is the only reading under which the dispatch-by-assignee treatment (agent-plugins-hg9t.1) applies uniformly — A keeps a second placeholder-heavy prompt, which is the surface that carried a false tool claim into three dispatches in run 3.

Choosing B deletes plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/grooming-prompt.md (4.1KB, cited once, from sprint-plan/SKILL.md:177). Choosing A means rewriting sprint-plan's readiness gate to run BEFORE grooming rather than ask it — which would undo the extraction in 414bc27.

Recorded as the one remaining Open Question on [[module-bead-bonanza]].

title: 3. Two files named references/run-record.md, and the manifest schema is in the wrong one
description:
MEASURED: plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md (9,867 bytes) and plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md (18,502 bytes) are both hand-authored, are not generated copies, and share exactly one heading (## Contents). Their content is complementary, not duplicated — which is worse than a duplicate, because the same citation string 'references/run-record.md' resolves to two different documents depending on which skill is reading.

THE INVERSION: sprint-plan's copy opens 'The manifest is the orchestrator's, not yours. Read it; never rewrite it.' — and then carries the manifest's full key schema. bead-bonanza's copy, whose skill OWNS the manifest, has to cite it by role with no path (check-skills rule 3 forbids the path), saying 'the full key set is the JSON block the sprint-plan skill writes, in its own run-record reference'. The owner of a document cannot link its specification.

FIX: move the manifest schema to the coordinator's file, leave the planner with what a planner produces (collision edges, C4 overlap, the edge file, concurrency cap), and give the two files distinct names so a citation resolves unambiguously.
notes: Landed in commit f78def4 on claude/bead-bonanza-simplify-5oapp4. All 13 declared checks green.

title: 2. Strip sub-skill detail out of the coordinator: 30% of its body describes what it invokes
description:
MEASURED on bead-bonanza/SKILL.md (18,117 body bytes across sections):

  1,568  Opening a run — pre-flight, then sprint-scope
  1,433  Groom & plan — invoke sprint-plan
  1,433  Retro — invoke sprint-retro
  1,053  Review the run's own diff — invoke sprint-review
  -----
  5,487  = 30% of the body, describing what four sub-skills do

The coordinator's own opening line is 'routing is the only thing you do... you never hold a subprocess's method'. Routing needs three things per phase: the id to invoke, what it returns, and the condition that decides what happens next. Everything else — how sprint-plan grooms, what sprint-retro harvests, how sprint-review resolves a reviewer — is the sub-skill's, is already stated there, and drifts the moment either copy is edited.

TARGET: those four sections at ~200 bytes each. The freed budget is what pays for anything else the coordinator needs, and it is currently 313 bytes from a hard cap.

TEST FOR WHAT STAYS: if the coordinator would behave identically without the sentence, it belongs in the sub-skill. If the sentence changes which phase runs next, it stays.
notes: Landed in commit f78def4 on claude/bead-bonanza-simplify-5oapp4. All 13 declared checks green.

title: 1. Dispatch by assignee: the prompt becomes four lines, and run-bead becomes run-batch
description:
MEASURED: 16 of the 19 placeholders in prompt-dispatch.md are derivable by the subagent itself from three the coordinator must supply.

NOT derivable: {DISPATCH_ID} (the coordinator mints it), {EPIC} (the run id), {SCRIPTS} (an absolute path into the coordinator's skill directory).
Derivable: {WORKTREE} (git rev-parse --show-toplevel — the agent is standing in it), {BRANCH} / {CHECKS_BASELINE_TEXT} / trailers (manifest), {CHECKS_IDS} (bb-checks.py --ids), every {ID_n}/{PRIORITY_n}/{TITLE_n} (bd ready --assignee), every {DECISION_n}/{IMPLICIT_n} (bd show).

So the dispatch becomes: 'create a subagent to run the run-batch skill over the beads assigned to <dispatch-id> in run <epic>; scripts are at <path>'. The skill resolves the rest.

WHAT THIS KILLS: the unsubstituted-placeholder defect class outright, since there is almost nothing to substitute; agent-plugins-y63n.23 (a prompt naming two different owned-file sets, with nothing reconciling them) becomes impossible because the prompt names no file set; and the dispatch prompt stops being an authoring surface with no reviewer, which the run-3 retro named as the highest-reach carrier of a false claim in the system.

RENAME: run-bead -> run-batch. It takes a batch (of one or more) and is user-invocable: false; the name should say batch. Sweep every citation.

SURFACE: {SURFACE} and {SURFACE_TARGETED_TESTS} are the only two with no home today. Either move them onto the manifest per dispatch id, or drop them — the batch's beads name their own tests.
notes: Landed in commit f78def4 on claude/bead-bonanza-simplify-5oapp4. All 13 declared checks green.

title: Worktree removal is ordered by prose, not guarded: a merge that exited 128 was followed by a successful removal
description:
audience: skill · target: `bead-bonanza` (`references/worktree-mechanics.md`) · recurrence: 0

## What is wrong, and what it costs

`worktree-mechanics.md` makes worktree presence THE in-flight signal — "you
remove it as the final act of accepting, after the last of its branches merges."
It states the ordering and relies on the coordinator following it. Nothing
enforces it, and a shell without `&&` between two commands is enough to break it.

Review loop 2, batch 10 of this run: `git merge --ff-only bb/dev-mpnf-10`,
`git worktree remove` and the acceptance check were issued as one chained
command. The merge exited **128** ("Not possible to fast-forward" — batch 9 had
already moved the head from `22c86ab` to `e2b69ad`). **The removal ran anyway,
and succeeded.**

For ~90 seconds a removed worktree coexisted with an unmerged branch — the state
the corpus asserts cannot occur. `bb-status.sh bead` reported it faithfully and
exited 2:

    OK   3 -> STOP 3 NOT merged into HEAD
    OK   4 worktree: gone

Signal 4 read "accepted" while signal 3 read "not merged". The check is not
wrong; the PAIR is only meaningful because the coordinator is supposed to
establish 3 before 4.

Cost this time: none — the branch still carried the commit and a rebase onto
`e2b69ad` fixed it (`4b0c304` -> `78b34e1`, acceptance then exit 0, all five OK).
Cost in general: a removed worktree is the signal every recovery path reads as
"this agent is done". `sprint-recovery` reconstructing from durable sources
would conclude the batch was accepted. `sprint-cleanup` would find nothing to
clean. The unmerged branch is invisible to both.

## Evidence

- `agent-plugins-mpnf#6` — "Review loop 2, batch 10. I ran `git merge --ff-only`,
  `git worktree remove`, and the acceptance check as one chained command. The
  merge exited 128 ... but the removal ran anyway and succeeded. ... for ~90
  seconds a removed worktree coexisted with an unmerged branch."

Note this finding was recorded as `retro:incident:<slug>` — `incident` is a
severity, not a kind — so the routing table sends it to UNROUTED. It reached
this issue because a human read it. See `agent-plugins-y63n.17`.

## Proposed change

Put the removal behind a guard rather than behind a sentence.
`worktree-mechanics.md`'s acceptance step gains an explicit precondition, and
the coordinator's removal is expressed as a single guarded form:

    git merge --ff-only "$branch" || { report; exit; }
    git merge-base --is-ancestor "$branch" HEAD || { echo "REFUSING: $branch is not an ancestor of HEAD"; exit 1; }
    git worktree remove "$dir"

with the reference stating the rule as a refusal, not as an order: **a worktree
whose branch is not an ancestor of HEAD is never removed**, and merge and removal
are never issued in one shell without `&&`. The ancestor test is what makes the
guard hold regardless of how the merge was invoked or why it failed.

---
Provenance: run `agent-plugins-mpnf` · branch `claude/bead-bonanza-design-review-ne1plu` · report `docs/research/sprint-findings/2026-08-25-agent-plugins-mpnf.md` · model `claude-opus-5` (the run manifest records no `models` or `effort` key — see agent-plugins-y63n.10) · filed by `retro-mpnf`.
notes: Done: worktree removal goes behind git merge-base --is-ancestor '<branch>' HEAD, in worktree-mechanics.md's lifecycle step 4, with the ninety-second incident named as why an && is not a guard. Commit 76d61c4.

title: Scope the CLI as a thin capability layer over bd and git, inside existing harnesses — not a new orchestrator
description:
Owner's hypothesis, stated 2026-08-25: 'by leaning into beads we can make this work inside existing harnesses rather than rolling our own.'

This CORRECTS this epic's own framing. The epic description was written before that hypothesis and reads as though the CLI should own orchestration. It should not. Read this bead before acting on the epic description.

## What the CLI IS

A thin, tested capability layer over `bd` and `git`. Each capability names an action the skills currently prescribe as a raw command sequence, owns the commands behind it, and is covered by a test. Examples at the owner's own granularity: 'patch run manifest', 'list all issues assigned to an agent that are ready', 'check run environment', 'accept a dispatch'.

## What the CLI IS NOT

- Not a scheduler. The harness dispatches agents; beads decides what is ready.
- Not a state store. The bead DAG is the source of truth — see the sibling bead retiring the `graph_plan` manifest copy.
- Not a replacement for the harness's worktree, subagent or notification mechanisms.

## Why this matters for sizing

'Swarm CLI' sounds like weeks of work because it sounds like an orchestrator. A tested wrapper over the ~30 command sequences the audit will enumerate is a much smaller thing, and it is the part that carries all three measured failure classes: commands that do not behave as documented, false universals about those commands, and ordering invariants enforced only by prose.

## Standing evidence that the swarm itself works

Three runs, 45 beads closed, every one landing as one commit with the project's full declared check set green. The orchestration model is not what is failing. The substrate is.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The FRD states these boundaries explicitly.
- [ ] No capability schedules, stores run state, or duplicates a harness mechanism.
- [ ] The epic description is corrected to match.
notes: Closed by agent-plugins-ih18.19's DoD audit: subsumed by frd-swarm-core's 'What this document does not do' and container-swarm-cli's Overview. Evidence quoted in the comment above.

title: Health must be DERIVED from progress, not asserted — it read healthy through a five-hour stall
description:
Owner's requirement, stated 2026-08-25: health exists 'to ensure the runs run and don't stop in the middle of the night'. As built it does not meet that requirement, and this run proved it.

## Evidence

Run agent-plugins-mpnf, 2026-08-25. Loop-3 grooming returned at 01:00 with eleven beads Ready and assigned. Nothing was dispatched. The session went idle until 06:09 — **five hours** — because the coordinator's turn ended.

Throughout that window the run's health label read `healthy`. When the coordinator set it at the start of the previous wave, `bd set-state` replied `(no change: health already set to healthy)`. Nothing observed the stall, because health is ASSERTED by the coordinator and the coordinator was not running.

That is the exact failure health exists to prevent, and health was green for it.

## The derived signal already exists and was correct

`bb-status.sh run <epic>` prints, from git and the tracker:

    health: healthy (worktrees: 0, last commit: 2 minutes ago)

`worktrees: 0` plus a stale `last commit` plus a non-empty ready front IS a stall, computable by anyone, at any time, with no cooperation from the coordinator. The parenthetical is doing the real work; the word before it is the asserted label that lied.

## What to build instead

A liveness verdict derived from observable state — last commit age, last bead close, worktree count against ready-front size — such that an external watcher (a Routine, a cron, a second session) can decide 'this run has stalled' WITHOUT the coordinator's cooperation. An asserted label cannot do this by construction: a dead coordinator asserts nothing, and the absence of an assertion is indistinguishable from a healthy run that has not reached a wave boundary.

Keep an asserted channel only for what cannot be derived — the coordinator's INTENT, e.g. 'deliberately paused pending a human answer'. That is a different field from liveness and should be named differently.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A liveness verdict is computable from git and the tracker alone, with no coordinator write.
- [ ] It returns STALLED for the 01:00-06:09 condition above: ready front non-empty, zero worktrees, no commit in N minutes.
- [ ] A test reproduces that condition and asserts the verdict.
- [ ] Whatever remains asserted is documented as intent, not liveness, and cannot be mistaken for it.
notes: Done: bb-status.sh run derives health from standing worktrees, the age of the last commit and the depth of the ready front; bd set-state is gone from the corpus and from sprint-cleanup. Four verdicts: working / drained / between dispatches / STALLED (exit 1). BB_STALL_SECONDS is the only tunable, default 1800. Commit 76d61c4.

comments.author: retro-mpnf
comments.text:
retro-mpnf — the retro for run agent-plugins-mpnf deduped against this bead and filed nothing new. Recording the framing it settled on, because it narrows what "derived" has to mean:

Health was not merely wrong. Health was ASSERTED BY THE COORDINATOR, AND THE COORDINATOR WAS THE THING THAT HAD STOPPED. A signal whose only writer is the component it monitors reports "no failure" and "no monitor" identically — the absence of an assertion is indistinguishable from a healthy run that has not reached a wave boundary.

That is why an asserted channel cannot be fixed by asserting more often, and why the parenthetical `(worktrees: 0, last commit: 2 minutes ago)` was already doing the real work while the word in front of it lied. The acceptance test for whatever replaces it: a watcher with NO cooperation from the coordinator — a Routine, a cron, a second session — must be able to reach the stall verdict from git and the tracker alone.

title: bb-status uses direct-children-only bd list --parent against the now-nested run epic: merge-slot release gate and "who holds work" are both always empty
description:
Filed by review pass 2 of run agent-plugins-mpnf. Reviewer: `code-review` (declared).

## What

`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh` queries the run epic's live
work with `bd list --parent`, at two sites this diff rewrote (agent-plugins-0913
migrated them off `--metadata-field dispatch_state=running`):

- line 327, `slot` mode — "Evidence 4 — the strongest ... a bead an agent has claimed", the signal that withholds a merge-slot release
- line 588, `run` mode — "who is still holding work"

`bd list --parent` returns **direct children only**. `agent-plugins-qozp.7` moved
the work beads a level deeper: the run epic now holds phase epics, and the work
beads are flat children of the TARGET. So both queries are structurally empty.

The same file already documents this exact trap at lines 369-372 —
"`bd list --parent` is direct-children-only too, unlike `bd ready --parent`
which is transitive ... so this walks the tree" — and has a recursive walker at
line 396 that these two call sites do not use.

## Measured (bd 1.2.2, scratch database)

Shape built to match sprint-scope's new one: run epic `zt-q4f` -> target epic
`zt-q4f.1` -> tasks `zt-q4f.1.1` (set `in_progress`, assignee `dev-x`) and `zt-q4f.1.2`.

```
$ bd list --parent zt-q4f    --status in_progress --json   ->  []
$ bd list --parent zt-q4f.1  --status in_progress --json   ->  [ zt-q4f.1.1 ]
$ bd ready --parent zt-q4f --exclude-type=epic --json      ->  ["zt-q4f.1.2"]
$ bd list --parent zt-q4f --json                           ->  ["zt-q4f.1"]
```

`bd ready --parent` is transitive; `bd list --parent` is not.

## Consequence

`bb-status.sh slot <epic>` prints "beads in progress: none" and its verdict
reads RELEASE IS DEFENSIBLE while an agent is mid-bead — the merge slot can be
taken from under a live merge. `bb-status.sh run <epic>` tells a resuming
session that nobody holds work, which is precisely the question a recovery asks.

## Remedy sketch

Use the transitive form. Either `bd ready --parent` semantics where they fit, or
route both call sites through the recursive walker `mode_run` already contains
(bb-status.sh:396), rather than adding a third traversal.
design:
## Chosen approach

Route both call sites through the recursive walker the same file already
carries, rather than adding a third traversal.

In `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh`:

- The file documents this exact trap in the comment beginning "`bd list
  --parent` is direct-children-only too, unlike `bd ready --parent` which is
  transitive", and `mode_run` already contains a recursive walker below it.
  That walker is the intended mechanism; the two rewritten call sites simply
  do not use it.
- **Site 1 — `slot` mode**, the query behind the comment "Evidence 4 — the
  strongest ... a bead an agent has claimed", which withholds a merge-slot
  release.
- **Site 2 — `run` mode**, the query behind "who is still holding work".

Extract the existing walk into a named helper if it is not already one, and
call it from both sites plus its current caller, so there is exactly ONE
traversal in the file. Do not introduce a second helper and do not inline a
third `bd list --parent` loop.

`bd ready --parent` IS transitive — confirmed on the installed CLI, whose
`--parent` help text reads "Filter to descendants of this bead/epic" — but it
is not a substitute here: both sites need beads by STATUS (`in_progress`,
claimed), and `bd ready` excludes exactly those. So the walker, not `bd ready`.

## Rejected

- **`bd ready --parent` at either site.** It excludes in-progress beads, which
  is the entire signal both sites are reading.
- **A third bespoke traversal.** The file already has one and the finding is
  partly that call sites drifted away from it; adding another repeats the
  defect.

## Constraints

- Behaviour-preserving apart from the traversal depth: the verdict logic,
  output format and exit codes stay as they are.
- Script file only — no capped SKILL.md body is touched.
- This bead does not touch the `null`-claim comment elsewhere in the file; that
  belongs to the sweep bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Against an epic whose work beads are grandchildren (run epic -> target epic -> tasks), `bb-status.sh slot <epic>` sees a claimed/in-progress bead and does NOT report the merge-slot release as defensible.
- [ ] Against the same shape, `bb-status.sh run <epic>` names the agent holding work rather than reporting that nobody does.
- [ ] Against a FLAT epic (work beads as direct children), both modes report exactly what they reported before this change — verified by running both modes before and after and diffing the output.
- [ ] `grep -c 'bd list --parent' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh` shows no new direct-children-only call site; the file contains exactly one traversal helper and both sites call it.
- [ ] The shape used for verification is built in a SCRATCH database, never the live tracker.
- [ ] `sh -n` / `shellcheck` report nothing new beyond the recorded baseline.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` passes with no findings beyond the recorded baseline.

metadata.tier_reason: Localized to two call sites in one file, with the correct mechanism already present in that file; execution over invention.

title: sprint-cleanup's agent_drained reads a FAILED bd query as "drained" and force-removes a live worktree: inverse of its own no-destruction-on-ambiguity header
description:
Filed by review pass 2 of run agent-plugins-mpnf. Reviewer: `code-review` (declared).

## What

`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh`, `agent_drained` (line 167)
and `json_empty` (line 173):

```sh
agent_drained() {
  _ad_ready="$(bd ready --assignee "$1" --json 2>/dev/null)"
  _ad_prog="$(bd list --assignee "$1" --status in_progress --json 2>/dev/null)"
  json_empty "$_ad_ready" && json_empty "$_ad_prog"
}
json_empty() { # 0 when null, [] or unreadable-as-a-list
  case "$1" in ''|null|'[]') return 0 ;; esac
  ...
}
```

Neither `bd` call's exit status is read, and `json_empty` deliberately treats
the empty string and anything unparseable as empty. So **"the tracker could not
answer" is indistinguishable from "the agent has drained"**, and `handle_worktree`
then runs `git worktree remove --force`.

This is AGENTS.md's "Pipes hide exit statuses" rule in its `>/dev/null 2>&1`
form: the status is available here and simply not read.

## Measured

Driving the real functions, copied verbatim out of the script:

```
json_empty ""                          -> EMPTY (reads as drained)
json_empty "Error: could not connect"  -> EMPTY (reads as drained)
```

Trigger: `bd list --all --json` succeeds at line 69, then the tracker becomes
briefly unavailable — a Dolt lock, a concurrent `bd dolt pull`, a `bd` whose
`ready --assignee` flag errors. Every registered worktree whose branch matches
a bead is then force-removed, taking uncommitted partial work with it.

This is the exact inverse of the script's own header, which this diff rewrote:
"NEVER DESTRUCTIVE ON AMBIGUITY / ... It leaves it alone and says so."

## Why this is not agent-plugins-mpnf.5

.5 was the BLOCKED bead whose worktree was torn down; its remedy (`status_for_branch`
plus the reordered `handle_worktree`) is correct and verified — I drove the
ordering and the blocked test does run before `agent_drained`. This is a
different input: a tracker that fails to answer at all, for which there is no
guard.

## Remedy sketch

Give `agent_drained` the shape the two new hooks already use — `count_json`
returns 1 on a failed query and each caller warns and declines to act. Distinguish
"counted zero" from "could not count", and treat "could not count" as LEFT,
raising `note_left` so the script exits RC_LEFT rather than 0.
design:
## Chosen approach

Distinguish "counted zero" from "could not count", and treat "could not count"
as LEFT. This is the fail-CLOSED direction for a destructive operation, and it
restores the script's own header contract ("NEVER DESTRUCTIVE ON AMBIGUITY").

In `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh`:

1. **Read the exit status of both `bd` calls in `agent_drained`.** They are
   currently discarded via `2>/dev/null` with no `||`. Capture into a variable,
   then test — never through a pipe, per this project's "Pipes hide exit
   statuses" rule.
2. **Give `agent_drained` three outcomes, not two.** Adopt the shape the two
   hooks already use (`count_json`-style: a non-zero return means "could not
   count"): 0 = drained, 1 = still holding, 2 = unknown. A `case` on the
   return keeps this POSIX-sh clean.
3. **`handle_worktree` treats unknown as LEFT.** It must not reach
   `git worktree remove --force`; it raises the existing `note_left` and the
   script exits `RC_LEFT` rather than 0, so a caller sees that cleanup was
   incomplete rather than believing it succeeded.
4. **Keep `json_empty`'s tolerance of non-list payloads** — accepting `''`,
   `null` and unparseable text as "not a list" is correct defensive parsing.
   What changes is that an unreadable payload is no longer reached with the
   query's failure already thrown away. The comment above `agent_drained`
   currently justifies this with a false claim about `bd ready --json`; that
   sentence belongs to the sweep bead that runs before this one in the batch —
   do not restate or reintroduce it.

## Rejected

- **Retrying the `bd` call.** Adds a timing dependency and a new failure mode
  to a cleanup path; "leave it standing and say so" is already the script's
  documented contract and costs nothing but a stale worktree.
- **Treating an unreadable payload as "still holding" inside `json_empty`.**
  That conflates a parse question with a query-failure question and would make
  `json_empty` untestable on its own; the distinction belongs at the call site.

## Constraints

- Last review loop: no behaviour change beyond the fail-closed guard. Do not
  reorder `handle_worktree`'s existing blocked-bead test, which is correct.
- Script file only — no capped SKILL.md body is touched.
- The script has self-tests; extend them rather than adding a new harness.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A failed tracker query during `agent_drained` never results in a `git worktree remove`; the worktree is left standing.
- [ ] The script reports the left worktree through the existing `note_left` path and exits `RC_LEFT`, not 0, when any worktree was left because the tracker could not be read.
- [ ] "Could not count" and "counted zero" are distinguishable at `agent_drained`'s call site — a drained agent still yields removal, an unreadable tracker does not.
- [ ] A self-test case in the script covers the failing-query path (a stub `bd` that exits non-zero) and asserts no removal is attempted; the existing self-tests still pass.
- [ ] `sh -n` and `shellcheck` (as `scripts/ci.sh` runs them) report nothing new beyond the recorded baseline.
- [ ] `json_empty` continues to read `''`, `null` and `[]` as empty and a one-item list as non-empty.
- [ ] No claim is added about what `bd ready --json` returns when empty; the edited text asserts nothing about that shape.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` passes with no findings beyond the recorded baseline.

metadata.tier_reason: Fail-closed guard on an irreversibly destructive path (git worktree remove --force takes uncommitted work with it); the failure mode is silent and the last review pass is spent.

  $ out="$(bd list --assignee nobody-xyz --status in_progress --json 2>&1)"; echo "rc=$?"; printf '%s\n' "$out"
  rc=0

  $ cd <empty scratch dir> && out="$(bd ready --assignee nobody-xyz --json 2>&1)"; echo "rc=$?"

title: Graph-plan examples parent merge beads with parent_key: "target", a key no plan contains: measured total abort, nothing created
description:
Filed by review pass 2 of run agent-plugins-mpnf. Reviewer: `code-review` (declared in sf.toml `[review]`).

## What

Every worked example of a graph-plan node in the diff parents its node with
`"parent_key": "target"`. Four sites:

- `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md:202` (collision-mark example)
- `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md:229` (THE MERGE BEAD — the agent-plugins-mpnf.3 remedy, landed 7120474)
- `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md:467` (the Schema block)
- `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md:145` (the merge bead again)

`parent_key` resolves **only against a `key` inside the same plan** — run-record.md:481
says so itself. But the target epic is created by `sprint-scope`, not by
`sprint-plan`: sprint-scope/SKILL.md's new "Build the shape, not just the epic"
section has scope create the run epic, the phase epics and the target in one act,
and run-record.md:369 confirms it ("`sprint-scope` admits them under the target").
`sprint-plan` "Takes the run epic" and reads a manifest the orchestrator already
wrote. So `target` is never a plan key when sprint-plan emits a plan.

## Measured (bd 1.2.2, scratch database, not the live tracker)

```
$ cat pa.json
{"nodes":[{"key":"m1","title":"Merge batch 1","type":"task","parent_key":"zt-q4f.1",
           "priority":1,"assignee":"merge-mb","labels":["merge"]}],"edges":[]}
$ bd create --graph pa.json ; echo $?
Error: invalid graph plan: node "m1": parent key "zt-q4f.1" not found in plan
1
$ bd list --status all --json | jq '[.[]|select(.title=="Merge batch 1")]|length'
0
```

Nothing is created. This is the SAME total-abort failure class as
agent-plugins-mpnf.3 and agent-plugins-mpnf.4 — the two P1s this loop just fixed —
arriving through `parent_key` instead of through an edge. The fix for .3 moved the
merge bead's fan-in to the sidecar and left its `parent_key` untouched, so the plan
still aborts at the first executable step of the run.

The correct field is `parent_id`, the documented escape hatch to a live id
(run-record.md:482, :501). Measured working: the same node with
`"parent_id":"zt-q4f.1"` created the bead with the right parent, assignee and
labels.

## Second facet, same root cause

run-record.md's **Worked example** (lines 555-575) has the graph plan create
`run`, `preflight`, `target` and `report` as nodes. Under the shape
sprint-scope now builds, all four already exist when sprint-plan runs; emitting
that plan duplicates the run's whole skeleton. That example is the only context
in which `parent_key: "target"` would resolve, which is why the three other
sites read as correct.

## Remedy sketch

Decide once who creates the target (sprint-scope, per its own SKILL.md), then:
switch all four `parent_key: "target"` sites to `parent_id: "<the target epic id>"`,
and rewrite the worked example so the plan creates only the beads the run adds
(merge beads, splits) beneath an existing target. Reference files only — no
sprint-plan/SKILL.md edit needed, which matters (see the 5-bytes-of-headroom bead).
design:
## Chosen approach

`parent_id` is the correct field, and `sprint-scope` — not `sprint-plan` —
creates the target. Both halves are settled, not open:

- `sprint-scope/SKILL.md`'s "Build the shape, not just the epic" has scope
  create the run epic, the phase epics and the target in one act.
- Measured in THIS repository's live tracker: the pass-2 plan
  (`.beads/plans/agent-plugins-mpnf-pass2.graph.json`) created three merge
  beads with `"parent_id": "agent-plugins-mpnf"` and they exist and are
  correctly parented. So `parent_id` against a live epic id is the working
  form, in production, not only in a scratch database.

Do exactly two things, both in reference files (uncapped):

1. **Switch the three node examples** that spell `"parent_key": "target"` to
   `"parent_id": "<the target epic id>"`, with a placeholder that reads as an
   id rather than as a plan key. Sites, quoted so they relocate under edits:
   - `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md` — the collision-mark
     example beginning `{"key": "b", "title": "…", "type": "task",`
   - same file — the merge-bead example beginning
     `{"key": "m1", "title": "Merge batch 1", "type": "task",`
   - same file — the Schema block under `### Schema`, the line containing
     `"assignee": "dev-<run-id>-1"`
   - `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md` — the merge
     bead example, likewise beginning `{"key": "m1", "title": "Merge batch 1",`

2. **Rewrite the Worked example** under `### Worked example` so the plan
   creates only what the run ADDS (the merge beads) beneath an already-existing
   target, reached by `parent_id`. It currently creates `run`, `preflight`,
   `target` and `report` as plan nodes, which duplicates the skeleton
   `sprint-scope` already built — and it is the only context in which
   `parent_key: "target"` resolves, which is why the other three sites read as
   correct.

Keep the field table's existing distinction between `parent_key` (a key in
THIS plan) and `parent_id` (an id that already exists) — it is correct; only
the examples contradict it.

## Rejected

- **Having `sprint-plan` create the target.** That would move ownership of the
  run's shape out of `sprint-scope`, contradict its SKILL.md, and duplicate an
  epic on any resumed run.
- **Leaving the Worked example alone and fixing only the three node sites.**
  The example would then be the sole surviving demonstration of a plan that
  rebuilds the whole skeleton, which is the behaviour this bead removes.

## Constraints

- **Reference files only.** No `SKILL.md` edit is needed or permitted here:
  `sprint-plan/SKILL.md` has 5 bytes of headroom under the 20,000-byte body cap.
- This is the last review loop; prefer the smallest change that makes every
  example loadable. Do not restructure the document beyond the example.
- Skill files are exported to other projects: cite no issue ids in the edited
  text.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No occurrence of `"parent_key": "target"` remains anywhere under `plugin/`, verified by `grep -rn 'parent_key.*target' plugin/` returning nothing.
- [ ] Every graph-plan node example that hangs off an epic the plan does not create uses `parent_id`, and the value reads as a tracker id rather than as a plan key.
- [ ] The Worked example in `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md` creates only beads the run adds, beneath an existing target reached by `parent_id`; it no longer creates `run`, `preflight`, `target` or `report` as plan nodes.
- [ ] Every JSON block edited is valid JSON, verified by extracting each fenced block and running `jq .` over it.
- [ ] The example plan actually loads: in a SCRATCH database (never the live tracker), create an epic, run `bd create --graph` over the edited merge-bead example with the placeholder replaced by that epic's real id, and observe a non-zero created count and the bead's parent set to the epic.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md` and `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` are unmodified by this bead, verified by `git diff --name-only`.
- [ ] The edited text cites no issue ids.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` passes with no findings beyond the recorded baseline.

title: Orchestrator loads only the graph plan, so the edge sidecar never reaches the tracker
description:
sprint-plan now emits TWO artifacts — `.beads/plans/<run-id>.graph.json` and `.beads/plans/<run-id>.edges.jsonl` — because a `bd create --graph` edge resolves only against keys inside the plan, so every edge between admitted beads (collision chains, sequencing constraints, merge fan-in) must load with `bd dep add --file`.

The orchestrator side still knows about one file only:

- `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md:142-146` — "**The graph plan**, plus one line per override of its own preview. Diff it, re-run its validators, load it with `bd create --graph <path>`, then record the path as `graph_plan` on the manifest."
- `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md:149-163` — "**`graph_plan` is yours to write and the planner's to produce.** The plan returns the path of the `bd create --graph` JSON document that builds the run; you load it and record the path here" plus the two loader rules.

CONSEQUENCE: an orchestrator following the shipped instruction loads the beads and never wires the edges. The run then has no collision serialization and no merge beads waiting on anything — silently, because the graph load reports success. This is the same failure the sidecar was introduced to fix, moved one step downstream.

WHAT IS NEEDED: bead-bonanza's load step becomes three steps (load the plan; substitute the printed key -> id into the sidecar; `bd dep add --file <sidecar>`), and the manifest gains `edges_sidecar` beside `graph_plan`. `sprint-plan/references/run-record.md` already documents the mechanism, the order of operations and the `edges_sidecar` manifest key — cite it, do not restate it.

BYTE CAP: `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` had 93 bytes free at 22c86ab, measured with the checker's method (`text.split('---', 2)[2]`). `references/run-record.md` is uncapped — prefer spending the mechanism there.
design:
## Chosen approach

Make the orchestrator's load step three steps, and put the mechanism in the
UNCAPPED reference rather than in the capped skill body.

**1. `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md` (uncapped — spend
here).** In the passage beginning "**`graph_plan` is yours to write and the
planner's to produce.**":

- State that the planner returns TWO paths, and that the load is three steps:
  `bd create --graph <plan>`; substitute each printed `key -> id` into the
  sidecar's `from` fields; `bd dep add --file <sidecar>`.
- Say why the second file exists in one sentence — a graph-plan edge resolves
  only against keys inside the plan, so every edge between beads that already
  exist must load separately — and then CITE the planner's own run-record
  reference for the mechanism, the orientation rule and the placeholder
  convention. Do not restate them; that document owns them.
- Add `edges_sidecar` beside `graph_plan` in the manifest key list.

**2. `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` (93 bytes free — trim within the
same item).** Rewrite return item 2 so it names both artifacts and the
three-step load. Pay for the added words out of the SAME item:

- **Delete "A failed load leaves half a graph behind"** — it is false. Measured
  on bd 1.2.2: a plan whose second node has an invalid type creates nothing,
  the valid first node included; the abort is total. Deleting it both frees
  bytes and removes a false claim.
- The neighbouring run-record.md sentence "A load that fails partway leaves the
  graph half-built" is the same false claim in the same file this bead edits —
  remove it here too, and let the surviving reason for diffing pre-load be the
  measured one: an unknown field is a *warning* that still exits 0.

## Scope boundary

The identical contradiction in `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/
run-record.md` belongs to the atomicity bead, which owns that file. This bead
touches only the two `bead-bonanza` files. The two beads share no file.

## Rejected

- **Spending the 93 bytes without trimming.** It would leave the body within a
  handful of bytes of the cap, and the cap bead is deferred, so nothing else
  can make room afterwards.
- **Cutting an unrelated rule from the body to buy space.** Out of bounds —
  trim only within the mechanism being rewritten.
- **Restating the sidecar mechanism in bead-bonanza's reference.** Two copies
  of a mechanism drift; the planner's reference is its home.

## Constraints

- Last review loop. Prefer the smallest edit that makes an orchestrator load
  both files; do not restructure the return list.
- Skill files are exported to other projects: cite no issue ids in the edited
  text.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An orchestrator reading `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` alone learns that the planner returns two artifacts and that the plan load is followed by a sidecar load; the three steps are discoverable from the cited reference.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md` names `edges_sidecar` as a manifest key beside `graph_plan`, and gives the three-step order with the id-substitution step between them.
- [ ] The sidecar's orientation rule, placeholder convention and all-or-nothing validation are CITED, not restated — `bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md` gains no second copy of them.
- [ ] `grep -rn 'half a graph\|half-built' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/` returns nothing.

Record the number in the close comment — do not estimate it.

title: Both hooks' block bound vanishes when the counter file cannot be written: measured 10 and 8 consecutive blocks against MAX=2
description:
Both new hooks state a BOUND as their central safety property — "at most N consecutive blocks per arming, then it stands down", "a bound that re-arms itself is not a bound" — and both hooks derive that bound entirely from a counter file whose write failure they explicitly swallow:

    n="$(cat "$cf" 2>/dev/null)"
    case "$n" in ''|*[!0-9]*) n=0 ;; esac
    n=$((n + 1))
    printf '%s\n' "$n" > "$cf" 2>/dev/null || true      # <-- failure ignored

If the counter cannot be written, `n` is recomputed as 0 on every invocation, never exceeds MAX, and the hook returns 2 forever. The bound does not exist. That also contradicts the stated third property: "Every path that is not 'armed, and the queue is provably non-empty' exits 0" — a path where the hook cannot account for its own budget still blocks.

MEASURED, review pass 1, in a scratch state directory, with `bd` stubbed to report a non-empty queue and MAX set to 2. The counter path was made unwritable by creating a DIRECTORY where the counter file goes (any write failure reproduces it — a full or read-only state filesystem does the same):

  bb-stop-ready-loop.sh, MAX=2, counter writable      -> 2 2 0 0 0            (bound holds)
  bb-stop-ready-loop.sh, MAX=2, `blocks` is a dir     -> 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2  (10/10 blocked)

  bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh, MAX=2, counter writable  -> 2 2 0 0 0            (bound holds)
  bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh, MAX=2, counter is a dir  -> 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2      (8/8 blocked)

Ten and eight consecutive blocks against a declared bound of two, in both hooks.

SEVERITY. This is the worst shape a defect in this diff can take: a Stop hook that will not let a session end. It is not unrecoverable — every block prints both kill switches (`--disarm`, `BB_STOP_HOOK=0` / `BB_SUBAGENT_HOOK=0`) — so an operator who reads the message can get out. But the bound is what makes these hooks a convenience rather than a trap, and it is one un-checked write away from absent.

FIX DIRECTION: make the counter write's failure fail OPEN. Test the redirect's status and `return 0` (with a warning) when it fails, instead of `|| true`. Both hooks, same line. Add a self-test assertion driving an unwritable counter, since neither current self-test covers it.

FILES: `plugin/hooks/bb-stop-ready-loop.sh` (~line 149), `plugin/hooks/bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh` (~line 207).
Reviewer: found by the review agent's own probing, beyond the `code-review` skill's report.


## Steps to Reproduce

Measured in review pass 1 with `bd` stubbed to report a non-empty queue, a
scratch state directory and MAX=2; the shell mechanism re-measured this
session.

1. Arm the hook and stub `bd` so the queue never drains.
2. Make the counter path unwritable by creating a DIRECTORY where the counter
   file goes: `mkdir -p "$d/blocks"` (a full or read-only state filesystem
   does the same).
3. Invoke the hook repeatedly and record each return code.

EXPECTED: at most MAX consecutive blocks, then the hook stands down — the
bound each hook states as its central safety property.

ACTUAL:
  bb-stop-ready-loop.sh,     MAX=2, counter writable  -> 2 2 0 0 0
  bb-stop-ready-loop.sh,     MAX=2, blocks is a dir   -> 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2
  bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh, MAX=2, counter writable  -> 2 2 0 0 0
  bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh, MAX=2, counter is a dir  -> 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2

Ten and eight consecutive blocks against a declared bound of two.

The mechanism, re-measured this session:
  sh -c 'cf=t9/blocks; printf "%s\n" 3 > "$cf" 2>/dev/null || true;
         echo "continued, status=$?"'   ->  continued, status=0
i.e. `|| true` discards the failure; `n` is then recomputed as 0 on every
invocation, never exceeds MAX, and the hook returns 2 forever.

WHERE IT MANIFESTS: plugin/hooks/bb-stop-ready-loop.sh and
plugin/hooks/bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh, on the counter-write line in each.
Recoverable by `--disarm` or BB_STOP_HOOK=0 / BB_SUBAGENT_HOOK=0.
design:
CHOSEN APPROACH. FAIL OPEN on an unwritable counter. Test the redirect's exit
status instead of discarding it with `|| true`; when the write fails, warn and
`return 0` rather than returning 2. A hook that cannot account for its own
budget must not spend it — which is also the third property both hooks already
claim ("Every path that is not 'armed, and the queue is provably non-empty'
exits 0") and currently violate.

Both hooks, the same shape. Replace:

    printf '%s\n' "$n" > "$cf" 2>/dev/null || true

with:

    if ! printf '%s\n' "$n" > "$cf" 2>/dev/null; then
      warn "cannot write the block counter ($cf); not blocking."
      return 0
    fi

(in bb-stop-ready-loop.sh the counter path is `$d/blocks`; in
bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh it is `$cf` = `$d/blocks-$(slug "$agent")`. Give
bb-stop-ready-loop.sh the same `cf` local so the two read alike.)

MEASURED, this session, /bin/sh (dash) and bash, counter path made
unwritable by putting a DIRECTORY where the file goes:

  sh -c 'cf=t9/blocks; if printf "%s\n" 3 > "$cf" 2>/dev/null; then
           echo "WROTE ok"; else echo "WRITE FAILED status=$?"; fi'
  -> sh: 1: cannot create t9/blocks: Is a directory
     WRITE FAILED status=2

  bash, same redirect, status read straight after -> status=1

  and the currently shipped form, for contrast:
  sh -c 'cf=t9/blocks; printf "%s\n" 3 > "$cf" 2>/dev/null || true;
         echo "continued, status=$?"'
  -> continued, status=0

So the failure IS observable; only `|| true` hides it. The status differs
between shells (2 in dash, 1 in bash), so test the redirect's success, never
a specific number.

TRAP FOR THE SELF-TEST, measured and non-obvious. Making the counter's
DIRECTORY read-only does NOT reproduce the failure when the tests run as
root, and these containers and CI run as root (`id -u` -> 0):

  mkdir t9b; chmod 555 t9b
  sh -c 'cf=t9b/blocks; if printf "%s\n" 3 > "$cf" 2>/dev/null; then
           echo "WROTE ok"; else echo "WRITE FAILED"; fi'
  -> WROTE ok

A self-test written that way passes while asserting nothing. The self-test
MUST make the counter PATH ITSELF A DIRECTORY (`mkdir -p "$d/blocks"`), which
fails for every user including root.

SECOND TRAP: `2>/dev/null` does NOT silence the shell's own "cannot create
...: Is a directory" diagnostic in either shell — measured above, the line
appeared on stderr in both. The hooks write their warnings to stderr anyway,
so this is cosmetic, but a self-test that matches stderr exactly must expect
that extra line.

SELF-TEST. Both hooks already have a `mode_self_test` that stubs `bd` on PATH
and uses a temp state directory, and both already assert the bound on a
writable counter (`2 2 0 0 0` against MAX=2). Add the mirror case: same
stubbed non-empty queue, same MAX, counter path a directory, and assert the
sequence of return codes is `0 0 0 ...` — every invocation exits 0. Assert the
SEQUENCE, not one call: the shipped defect produced 2 on all ten and eight
invocations respectively, and a single-call assertion would not distinguish
fail-open from a bound that has simply not been reached yet.

WHY FAIL OPEN RATHER THAN FAIL CLOSED. Blocking is the destructive direction
here: exit 2 on a Stop hook refuses to let a session end, and the whole
argument for shipping these hooks is that the bound makes that a convenience
rather than a trap. An unaccounted budget is exactly the state in which the
hook has no evidence it is still inside its bound, so it stands down. The
kill switches (--disarm, BB_STOP_HOOK=0 / BB_SUBAGENT_HOOK=0) stay as they
are; they are the recovery path, not a substitute for the bound.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] In both plugin/hooks/bb-stop-ready-loop.sh and plugin/hooks/bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh, a failure to write the block counter causes the hook to warn and exit 0, rather than to return 2.
- [ ] Neither hook discards the counter write's exit status; no `|| true` remains on that redirect in either file.
- [ ] Neither hook tests for a specific failure status number, since it differs between dash and bash.
- [ ] With the counter path unwritable and a non-empty queue, repeated invocations of each hook return 0 every time — asserted over a sequence of invocations, not a single call.
- [ ] With a writable counter, the existing bound is unchanged: each hook still blocks at most MAX consecutive times and then stands down.
- [ ] Each hook's `--self-test` gains a fail-open case that makes the counter PATH ITSELF A DIRECTORY, not one that chmods a parent directory (which does not fail for root, and these tests run as root).
- [ ] Both self-test suites pass and still need no database, no repository and no network.

title: sprint-cleanup force-removes a BLOCKED worker's worktree, destroying the partial work worktree-mechanics says to preserve
description:
`sprint-cleanup.sh`'s `handle_worktree` decides a worktree's fate from `agent_drained` alone and never reads the bead's own status:

    elif agent_drained "$_hw_who"; then
      run "remove worktree ($_hw_who drained)" git worktree remove --force "$1"

`agent_drained` is "`bd ready --assignee` empty AND nothing `in_progress`". A bead set to `blocked` satisfies both: `bd ready` excludes blocked beads and `--status in_progress` does not match them. The SubagentStop hook shipped in this same run states exactly that in its own measured table:

    blocked -> ready=0 in_progress=0  ALLOW

So a worker that took `run-bead`'s Blocked path reads DRAINED, and cleanup runs `git worktree remove --force` on it.

That directly contradicts `bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md` (~line 329): "WHEN a bead is blocked rather than finished, LEAVE ITS WORKTREE IN PLACE ... It holds the partial work, and its existence is the durable record that the bead is unfinished - there is nothing to stash and no WIP commit to make."

COST: uncommitted partial work on a blocked bead is destroyed, and the durable record that the bead was unfinished is destroyed with it. `--force` means git's own dirty-tree refusal does not save it.

The guard this replaced (`dispatch_state`, dropped by the same run) distinguished this row. The replacement does not.

FIX DIRECTION: `handle_worktree` should ask for the owning bead's status and treat `blocked` as LEFT, not as drained.

FILE: `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh` (~line 98, `handle_worktree`).
Reviewer: `code-review` skill (declared), high effort.


## Steps to Reproduce

Measured this session in a throwaway bd database, bd 1.2.2 (dev), prefix scr2.

1. `bd create --title "blocked worker bead" --assignee dev-scr` -> `scr2-xyu`.
2. `bd update scr2-xyu --status blocked` (what run-bead's Blocked path does).
3. Ask the two questions `agent_drained` asks:
   `bd ready --assignee dev-scr --json`                     -> []
   `bd list --assignee dev-scr --status in_progress --json` -> []

EXPECTED: the agent is holding unfinished work, so its worktree is preserved.

ACTUAL: both probes are empty, so `agent_drained` returns 0 and
`handle_worktree` reaches `run "remove worktree ($_hw_who drained)" git
worktree remove --force "$1"`. `--force` defeats git's own dirty-tree refusal,
so uncommitted partial work is destroyed along with the durable record that
the bead was unfinished.

The same database shows the status the guard should have read is already in
hand: `bd list --all --json` (what prune_worktrees passes as $3) carries
`scr2-xyu  blocked  dev-scr`, and the endswith-suffix lookup handle_worktree
already performs returns `blocked`.

WHERE IT MANIFESTS: plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh,
`handle_worktree`, on any run where a worker took the Blocked path.
design:
CHOSEN APPROACH. `handle_worktree` asks the OWNING BEAD'S OWN STATUS before
it consults `agent_drained`, and treats `blocked` as LEFT. The status comes
out of the beads JSON the function is ALREADY handed as `$3` — no new tracker
call, and the self-test keeps its "no database, no repository, no network"
property.

Add a parser beside `assignee_for_branch`, built the same way and for the
same reasons (its comment about the branch being a bead's hash SUFFIX applies
unchanged):

  status_for_branch() { # status_for_branch <branch>  < beads-json  ->  status|""
    [ -n "$1" ] || return 0
    jq -r --arg b "-$1" \
      'first(.[] | select(.id | endswith($b)) | .status // "") // ""' 2>/dev/null
  }

and reorder the guard so the bead's own status is consulted first:

  handle_worktree() { # handle_worktree <path> <branch> <beads-json>
    _hw_who="$(printf '%s' "$3" | assignee_for_branch "$2")"
    _hw_st="$(printf '%s' "$3" | status_for_branch "$2")"
    if [ -z "$_hw_who" ]; then
      line "LEFT" "worktree, no bead owns its branch" "$1"; note_left
    elif [ "$_hw_st" = blocked ]; then
      line "LEFT" "worktree, its bead is BLOCKED (partial work)" "$1"; note_left
    elif agent_drained "$_hw_who"; then
      run "remove worktree ($_hw_who drained)" git worktree remove --force "$1"
    else
      line "LEFT" "worktree, $_hw_who still has a queue" "$1"; note_left
    fi
  }

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: the blocked test must precede `agent_drained`, because
a blocked bead satisfies `agent_drained` and the first matching branch wins.

MEASURED, this session, throwaway scratch database, bd 1.2.2 (dev), prefix
scr2 — the defect end to end and the fix's data source in one pass. A bead
assigned to `dev-scr` and set `--status blocked`:

  bd ready --assignee dev-scr --json                    -> []
  bd list --assignee dev-scr --status in_progress --json -> []

  so agent_drained returns 0 (drained) and the current code reaches
  `git worktree remove --force`. The finding reproduces exactly.

  bd list --all --json  DOES carry the blocked bead, with its real status:
    scr2-xyu	blocked	dev-scr

  and the exact lookup handle_worktree already performs — the branch is the
  id's hash suffix — returns it:

  $ jq -r --arg b "-xyu" 'first(.[] | select(.id | endswith($b)) | .status // "") // ""' all.json
  blocked

So the status the guard needs is already inside `$3`. `prune_worktrees`
builds that JSON with `bd list --all --json`; it needs no change.

WHY NOT a `bd list --assignee <who> --status blocked` probe inside
`agent_drained`: it would make the drained predicate answer a question about
a DIFFERENT bead than the one whose worktree is being decided — an agent
holding a blocked bead elsewhere would keep an unrelated finished worktree
standing. The decision is per worktree, so read the per-worktree bead. It
also costs a tracker round trip per worktree and would need a stub in the
self-test, where the parser needs only synthetic JSON.

SELF-TEST. Extend the existing `handle_worktree` cases (which already stub
`agent_drained` and `run` and feed a synthetic `$_hw_beads`) with a row whose
bead is `"status":"blocked"` and whose assignee is the drained stub's
`dev-done`. Assert BOTH: the worktree is reported LEFT, and `run` was never
called — an assertion on the message alone would pass against a version that
prints LEFT and removes the tree anyway. Add a `status_for_branch` parser
case alongside the `assignee_for_branch` ones, including the empty-branch
(detached worktree) input, which must yield "".

The contract this restores is stated in
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md under "WHEN a
bead is blocked rather than finished": the worktree holds the partial work
and its existence is the durable record that the bead is unfinished. Quote
the heading, not the line number.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A worktree whose owning bead reads `blocked` is reported LEFT by `sprint-cleanup.sh` and is NOT removed, whatever `agent_drained` says about its assignee.
- [ ] The blocked test runs BEFORE the `agent_drained` branch, so a blocked bead cannot fall through to the drained arm.
- [ ] The owning bead's status is read from the beads JSON already passed into `handle_worktree`; the script makes no additional tracker call per worktree.
- [ ] `sprint-cleanup.sh --self-test` gains a case driving a blocked-bead worktree that asserts BOTH that it is reported LEFT and that the removal command was never invoked; it passes.
- [ ] `sprint-cleanup.sh --self-test` gains parser cases for the new status lookup, including an empty branch (a detached worktree) yielding the empty string.
- [ ] The whole self-test suite still passes and still requires no database, no repository and no network.
- [ ] A LEFT blocked worktree still makes the script's exit status reflect that something was left standing, exactly as the other LEFT paths do.
- [ ] The `script-self-tests` declared check passes.
- [ ] The project's declared checks pass (baseline: all 13 passed, exit 0 — so exit 0 is the bar).

title: Collision edges between admitted beads cannot be emitted in the graph plan, so nothing serializes a shared surface
description:
`qozp.8` replaced the wave table with collision EDGES: "N beads on one surface get N-1 edges in a line" (`sprint-plan/SKILL.md`, "Emit a collision edge between them"), and the plan's validator 3 requires both endpoints of a collision edge to carry `metadata.collision`.

Both endpoints of a collision edge are beads the run ADMITTED — they already exist in the tracker. `bd create --graph` rejects an edge naming an id that is not a plan-local key, and aborts the entire plan:

    Error: invalid graph plan: edge 0: to key "scr-w8e" not found in plan

(measured in review pass 1 on bd 1.2.2 in a throwaway scratch database; full transcript on the sibling finding about the merge bead's fan-in edge.)

So the collision edges cannot be emitted in the graph plan at all, and validator 3's `metadata.collision` requirement is unreachable for the beads it is written about.

WHY THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: collision edges are the entire replacement for the deleted wave table. "The ready front is safe to dispatch whole" is true only because collisions are edges that hold the second bead back. If they never get created, the ready front hands two agents the same file and the run has no serialization at all — silently, because the plan that failed to load them is the same plan that reports success for everything else.

`bd dep add` between two existing beads works and is the obvious repair path; the point of this finding is that the SHIPPED instruction does not.

FILES: `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md` (~line 236, collision-edge emission and validator 3), `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md`.
Reviewer: `code-review` skill (declared), high effort. Independently reproduced by the review agent.


## Steps to Reproduce

Throwaway bd database, bd 1.2.2 (dev). Reproduced independently this session
(prefix scr2) as well as in review pass 1 (prefix scr).

1. `bd create --title "pre-existing bead A"` -> an id, e.g. `scr2-xg5`.
2. Write a graph plan whose only edge names that id — which is what
   sprint-plan/SKILL.md's "Emit a collision edge between them" instructs,
   since both ends of a collision are beads the run admitted:

   {"nodes":[{"key":"m1","title":"merge bead","type":"task","priority":1}],
    "edges":[{"from_key":"m1","to_key":"scr2-xg5","type":"blocks"}]}

3. `bd create --graph g.json ; echo $?`

EXPECTED (per the shipped instruction): the edge is created and the two beads
cannot reach the ready front together.

ACTUAL: `Error: invalid graph plan: edge 0: to key "scr2-xg5" not found in
plan`, exit 1. `bd list --status all` afterwards shows nothing was created:
the abort is total, not partial.

WHERE IT MANIFESTS: every sprint. A run's beads exist before planning starts
(sprint-scope admits them; sprint-plan assigns them with `bd update
--assignee`), so a collision edge's endpoint is always a real id and never a
plan-local key. The instruction has no input on which it succeeds.
design:
CHOSEN APPROACH. Edges whose endpoints ALREADY EXIST in the tracker move out
of the graph plan into a companion EDGE SIDECAR, loaded with
`bd dep add --file` immediately after the plan loads. The graph plan keeps
its one job — creating beads — and stops trying to express relationships
between beads it did not create. `sprint-plan` therefore emits TWO artifacts:

  .beads/plans/<run-id>.graph.json    nodes the run creates, and edges among
                                      those nodes only
  .beads/plans/<run-id>.edges.jsonl   every edge with an endpoint that already
                                      exists — the collision chains included

and the collision MARKS are applied with `bd update --set-metadata` in the
same step that writes assignees, because a pre-existing bead's metadata
cannot be set from the plan either.

MEASURED, this session, throwaway scratch database, bd 1.2.2 (dev), prefix
scr2. Every claim below names the command and the observed output.

T1 — a plan edge naming an existing id, reproducing the finding independently
  {"nodes":[{"key":"m1",...}],
   "edges":[{"from_key":"m1","to_key":"scr2-xg5","type":"blocks"}]}
  $ bd create --graph t1.json ; echo $?
  Error: invalid graph plan: edge 0: to key "scr2-xg5" not found in plan
  1
  `bd list --status all` afterwards returned only the two pre-existing beads.
  The abort is total: nothing was created.

T2 — `bd dep add` between two beads that already exist
  $ bd dep add scr2-76i scr2-xg5 --type blocks ; echo $?
  ✓ Added dependency: scr2-76i (pre-existing bead B) depends on scr2-xg5
    (pre-existing bead A) (blocks)
  0
  `bd ready` then returned scr2-xg5 alone; `bd blocked` returned scr2-76i,
  "Blocked by 1 open dependencies: [scr2-xg5]".
  ORIENTATION: the first positional is the WAITER — the plan's `from_key` —
  and the second is what it waits for — `to_key`. Identical semantics, so a
  sidecar line is a faithful translation of a plan edge, not a new concept.

T3 — the bulk form, which is what makes this a sidecar and not N commands
  `bd dep add --file <f>` reads newline-delimited JSON, one object per line,
  fields "from" / "to" / "type" (aliases "issue_id" / "depends_on_id"
  accepted; `--file -` reads stdin) — from `bd dep add --help`.
  $ bd dep add --file edges.jsonl ; echo $?
  ✓ Added 1 dependencies
  0

T3b — ALL-OR-NOTHING, which is why this keeps the property the graph plan was
adopted for. A two-line file whose second line names a nonexistent id:
  $ bd dep add --file edges2.jsonl ; echo $?
  Error: bulk dependency validation failed:
    line 2: resolving dependency ID scr2-nope: resolving issue ID scr2-nope:
    no issue found matching "scr2-nope"
  1
  `bd dep list` on the FIRST line's subject then printed "has no
  dependencies" — the valid first edge did not land either. A malformed
  sidecar leaves no half-wired graph, exactly as a malformed plan leaves no
  half-built one. It is reviewable before it is loaded.

T6 — replaying the identical sidecar: exit 0, "✓ Added 1 dependencies", no
  duplicate-edge error. A resumed run may re-run it.

T4c — the collision MARK on a bead that already exists
  $ bd update scr2-xg5 --set-metadata collision=c4_changes:auth-service
  metadata afterwards: {"collision":"c4_changes:auth-service"}
  QUOTING TRAP, measured on the same flag: a JSON-quoted value
  (--set-metadata collision='"c4_changes:auth-service"') stores the quotes
  literally — metadata came back {"collision":"\"c4_changes:auth-service\""}.
  Write the BARE value. `bd update <id> --metadata '{"collision":"..."}'`
  also works and merges at the top level.

REJECTED — include the batch's beads as plan nodes. They already exist;
`bd create --graph` would mint duplicates rather than reference them.

REJECTED — an escape hatch on the edge object. `parent_id` exists as a NODE
field for hanging a plan off a live epic; the edge object accepts only
from_key, to_key and type, so there is nothing to reach a live id with.

VALIDATOR 3 becomes reachable and is restated against the sidecar: for each
line emitted as a collision, both endpoint beads must carry
`metadata.collision` with the same value, and no bead may carry the mark
without a line justifying it. As shipped it is written about edges that
cannot exist, so it can never fire.

SCOPE. This bead owns the MECHANISM — the two artifacts, the sidecar's
format and semantics, the collision chain and its marking, and validator 3.
The merge bead's fan-in is the same mechanism applied to a second consumer
and belongs to the sibling bead that waits on this one; do not fix it here,
and do not restate the mechanism there.

BYTE CAP. sprint-plan/SKILL.md is 52 bytes under the 20,000-byte body cap
(measured at grooming with the checker's own method,
`text.split('---',2)[2]`). Re-measure before and after; net-negative wording
is available because the shipped text describes a mechanism that does not
work. If a required rule will not fit, take run-bead's Blocked path — no
rule is cut for space.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md no longer instructs that a collision between two queued beads is emitted as an edge in the graph plan; it names the edge sidecar and `bd dep add --file` as where such an edge goes.
- [ ] plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md documents both artifacts (the graph plan and the edge sidecar) and states, quoting the measured error text, that a graph-plan edge resolves only against keys inside the plan and that a violating plan aborts whole and creates nothing.
- [ ] The sidecar's format is documented as `bd dep add --file` newline-delimited JSON with "from" / "to" / "type", with "from" named as the WAITER so it cannot be read backwards.
- [ ] The sidecar's all-or-nothing validation is stated, so a reader knows a bad line wires nothing rather than wiring a prefix.
- [ ] The collision mark's write path for a pre-existing bead is documented as `bd update <id> --set-metadata collision=<surface>` with the bare, unquoted value, and the JSON-quoting trap is named.
- [ ] Validator 3 is restated so that it validates the edge sidecar, and is reachable — it applies to edges that can actually be created.
- [ ] A reader following the changed instruction end to end would produce a plan that loads: no remaining instruction anywhere in sprint-plan/ tells a planner to put a pre-existing bead id in a graph-plan edge.
- [ ] plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md stays within the 20,000-byte body cap, measured with the checker's method, not estimated.
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh` passes.
- [ ] The project's declared checks pass (baseline: all 13 passed, exit 0 — so exit 0 is the bar).

title: Merge bead's fan-in edge names an existing bead id: bd create --graph rejects it and aborts the whole plan
description:
`sprint-plan/references/run-record.md` and `bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md` both document the merge bead's fan-in as a `bd create --graph` edge whose `to_key` is a bead that already exists in the tracker:

    {"from_key": "m1", "to_key": "<each bead in the batch>", "type": "blocks"}

`bd create --graph` accepts only plan-local keys on an edge. An edge naming a real tracker id aborts the WHOLE plan and creates nothing.

MEASURED, review pass 1, bd 1.2.2 (dev), throwaway scratch database (prefix `scr`):

    $ bd create --title "pre-existing bead" ...     -> scr-w8e
    $ cat g.json
    {"nodes":[{"key":"m1","title":"merge bead","issue_type":"task","priority":2}],
     "edges":[{"from_key":"m1","to_key":"scr-w8e","type":"blocks"}]}
    $ bd create --graph g.json ; echo $?
    Error: invalid graph plan: edge 0: to key "scr-w8e" not found in plan
    1

Nothing is created — the run stops at "load the graph plan", which is the first executable step of the new planning model.

The batch's beads DO already exist by the time the plan is loaded: `sprint-scope` admits them under the target, and `sprint-plan` assigns them with `bd update <id> --assignee`. So the documented shape can never load.

There is no escape hatch on an edge. Nodes carry `parent_id` for attaching to a pre-existing bead (verified working); edges accept only `from_key`, `to_key`, `type`.

WHY IT MATTERS: the merge bead plus the merge slot is what `qozp.11` put in place of the merge-queue prose. As documented it is unloadable.

Fix directions (not chosen here): create the merge bead with plain `bd create` and wire its fan-in with `bd dep add` after the plan loads; or include the batch beads as plan nodes, which they cannot be because they already exist.

FILES: `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md` (~line 203), `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md` (~line 148).
Reviewer: `code-review` skill (declared in sf.toml [review]), high effort. Independently reproduced by the review agent.


## Steps to Reproduce

Throwaway bd database, bd 1.2.2 (dev), reproduced this session (prefix scr2)
and in review pass 1 (prefix scr).

1. `bd create --title "pre-existing bead A"` -> e.g. `scr2-xg5`; repeat for a
   second batch bead.
2. Write the fan-in exactly as run-record.md and worktree-mechanics.md show
   it:

   {"nodes":[{"key":"m1","title":"Merge batch 1","type":"task","priority":1,
              "assignee":"merge-<run-id>","labels":["merge"]}],
    "edges":[{"from_key":"m1","to_key":"scr2-xg5","type":"blocks"}]}

3. `bd create --graph g.json ; echo $?`

EXPECTED: the merge bead is created and waits on the batch's beads.

ACTUAL: `Error: invalid graph plan: edge 0: to key "scr2-xg5" not found in
plan`, exit 1. The merge bead is not created either — the plan aborts whole.

WHERE IT MANIFESTS: at "load the graph plan", the first executable step of
the planning model, on any run that batches. The beads a merge bead fans in
from always pre-exist, so the documented shape can never load.
design:
CHOSEN APPROACH. The merge bead itself STAYS a plan node — it is new, so the
plan can and should create it. Only its FAN-IN moves out, into the edge
sidecar the sibling bead introduces (`.beads/plans/<run-id>.edges.jsonl`,
loaded with `bd dep add --file`), because every one of those edges names a
batch bead that already exists.

This bead does NOT define the sidecar. It applies it to the merge bead, in
the two places that document the fan-in, and cites the mechanism rather than
restating it. Read the sibling bead's Design for the sidecar's format,
semantics and measurements before starting; that bead lands first and this
one waits on it.

WHY THE MERGE BEAD CAN STILL BE A PLAN NODE. `bd create --graph` prints the
plan key to issue id mapping on load, so the merge bead's real id is known
immediately and the sidecar can be written against it. Measured this session,
scratch database scr2, bd 1.2.2 (dev):

  $ bd create --graph t7.json
  Created 2 issues
    m2 -> scr2-crh
    m3 -> scr2-c70

ORDER OF OPERATIONS, which is the substance of the fix:
  1. `bd create --graph <plan>` — creates the merge bead (and every other new
     node), printing key -> id.
  2. Substitute the merge bead's real id into the sidecar's `from` fields.
  3. `bd dep add --file <sidecar>` — wires the fan-in onto the batch's
     pre-existing beads.

MEASURED — the documented behaviour survives the change intact. Merge bead
created and its fan-in wired the new way, over two pre-existing beads:

  $ bd create --title "Merge batch 1" -p 1 --assignee merge-scr --label merge -t task
    -> scr2-rh0
  $ cat merge-edges.jsonl
    {"from":"scr2-rh0","to":"scr2-xg5","type":"blocks"}
    {"from":"scr2-rh0","to":"scr2-76i","type":"blocks"}
  $ bd dep add --file merge-edges.jsonl ; echo $?
    ✓ Added 2 dependencies
    0

  bd ready --assignee merge-scr --json, both inputs open   -> []
  bd ready --assignee merge-scr --json, after closing one  -> []
  bd ready --assignee merge-scr --json, after closing both -> scr2-rh0
  bd ready --label merge --json, after closing both        -> scr2-rh0

That is exactly what run-record.md and worktree-mechanics.md already claim
for the fan-in, so the CLAIM is correct and only the MECHANISM was wrong.
Preserve the claim and its measurement; replace the JSON that cannot load.

NOTE ON THE `from_key`/`to_key` ORIENTATION SENTENCE. run-record.md's
"Remember the orientation: `from_key` waits for `to_key`, so the merge bead
is the `from_key` on every one of those edges" is still true and still needed
— it carries over to the sidecar's `from` / `to` unchanged (measured: `bd dep
add <waiter> <waited-for>` puts the waiter in `bd blocked`). Rewrite it to
name the sidecar's fields; do not delete it.

SITES. plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md, "### The merge
bead" (the two fenced blocks, the second of which is the unloadable edge);
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md, "### The merge
bead" under step 3 "Merge, per dispatch — and the merge is a BEAD" (same two
fenced blocks). Both are references, which are UNCAPPED — no byte pressure
here.

COORDINATION. This bead and its sibling both edit run-record.md. They are one
agent's batch, taken in order, so there is no concurrent edit; the sibling
lands the mechanism first and this bead cites it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md's "### The merge bead" no longer shows the fan-in as a `bd create --graph` edge naming a bead id; it shows the sidecar line and names `bd dep add --file` as what loads it.
- [ ] plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md's merge-bead section carries the same corrected fan-in, and does not restate the sidecar mechanism — it cites the owning skill by role.
- [ ] The three-step order of operations (load the plan; substitute the printed key -> id; load the sidecar) is documented wherever the merge bead's creation is described, so a reader knows the merge bead's id exists before the sidecar is written.
- [ ] The measured `bd ready --assignee merge-<run-id>` / `bd ready --label merge` behaviour is retained as the fan-in's justification, restated as measured through the sidecar rather than through a graph-plan edge.
- [ ] The `from_key` waits for `to_key` orientation warning survives, rewritten for the sidecar's "from" / "to" fields.
- [ ] No instruction remains in either file that would put a pre-existing bead id in a graph-plan edge.
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh` passes, and every backticked reference path in the changed files still resolves from its own directory.
- [ ] The project's declared checks pass (baseline: all 13 passed, exit 0 — so exit 0 is the bar).

metadata.tier_reason: applies a mechanism the sibling bead defines to two documented sites; low ambiguity once that lands, and the behavioural claim it must preserve is already measured on the bead
