title: bd search excludes closed issues by default — add the ledger entry and retract the "non-functional" claim
description:
Retro candidate C1 (P1) from the sprint retro of run epic agent-plugins-so39.
Findings: so39#11 (measured, corrects so39#9), so39#9, so39#1.
Report: rfcs/sprints/2026-08-24-run-2-coordination-corrections-findings.md (section 5, C1 — drafted verbatim there).

WHAT IS WRONG, AND WHAT IT COSTS

The run recorded, and this retro's own dispatch brief restated as a hard constraint,
that `bd search` is non-functional on this build. It is not. It EXCLUDES CLOSED ISSUES
BY DEFAULT — the same trap the findings-capture protocol already documents for `bd list`,
and for the same reason that protocol mandates `bd export` over `bd list` when harvesting
a drained run.

The cost already landed twice. The recorded fix for the run's duplicate-filing incident
("run `bd search` before `bd create`") was written off as unworkable, and the next
ceremony was dispatched with a false premise in its brief. AGENTS.md's
environmental-failure ledger is where the next agent will look, and it says nothing
about this.

PROPOSED CHANGE

One entry in AGENTS.md's environmental-failure ledger, in the ledger's own form — the
measurement, not the date:

  `bd search` excludes closed issues by default; `--status all` includes them.
  `bd search --help` line 1 states it ("Search issues across title and ID (excludes
  closed issues by default)"), line 5 names the flag. Measured on bd 1.2.2 (dev)
  against this tracker: `bd search metadata` -> 2 hits, both deferred;
  `bd search metadata --status all` -> 6 hits, matching
  `jq -r '.title' <export> | grep -ci metadata` -> 6. `bd search probe --status all`
  -> 54 hits. A zero result from the default is not evidence of a broken index.

AND RETRACT THE "NON-FUNCTIONAL" CLAIM wherever this project states it. It entered the
record as a generalisation from a single negative observation: review-so39 measured
"zero hits even for metadata across 440 beads", which is exactly what the default filter
returns when every matching bead is closed and the two open ones did not yet exist.

RELATED, NOT DUPLICATE

agent-plugins-r9yj (P1 in that bead's own text, currently P3, open) appends three OTHER
measured environment facts to the same ledger, from run 1's retro. Same file, same
ledger, different facts. Whoever picks up either should consider doing both in one edit;
neither blocks the other.


CITATION REPAIR (2026-08-25): the `rfcs/sprints/2026-08-24-*` documents this bead cites were DELETED in commit 9cc8844 at the owner's instruction, so the pointer no longer resolves. The text survives only in git history on branch claude/bead-bonanza-design-review-ne1plu. This bead's own body below carries what it needs; do not go looking for the report. Run 2's record now lives on epic agent-plugins-so39, and run 3's analysis in docs/research/sprint-findings/2026-08-25-agent-plugins-mpnf.md.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md's environmental-failure ledger carries an entry stating, with the command that measured it, that `bd search` excludes closed issues by default and that `--status all` includes them; and no document in this repository still asserts that `bd search` is non-functional or broken on this build.

scope_notes: THIS RUN MODIFIES ITS OWN MACHINERY WHILE USING IT. The bead-bonanza skill set is both the subject and the tooling of this run. Any agent that reads a skill file mid-run may be reading a version a sibling bead has already changed, and the ceremony agents dispatched after those beads land will not behave the way the ones dispatched before them did.

Consequences to carry, not to rediscover: (a) re-read a skill file at the point of use rather than trusting a copy taken at run start; (b) the four wave-related beads (qozp.21, .24, .25, .26, .27) and b1gl are excluded precisely because item 8 deletes the code they report against - closing them as fixed would be wrong, they are retired by item 8; (c) a resumed session must read this note before dispatching, because the machinery it resumes into is not the machinery the run opened with.

agent-plugins-x5tk carries a 'related' edge to agent-plugins-so39.5, which is EXCLUDED and deferred. comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro:tooling:coordinator incident — the coordinator suppressed an exit status and lost an error message, in the run whose queue contains agent-plugins-x5tk about exactly this. Wiring the sequencing edges, 'bd dep add agent-plugins-0913 agent-plugins-qozp.8' was run as '>/dev/null 2>&1' and treated as done. It had exited 1 with: 'dependency agent-plugins-0913 -> agent-plugins-qozp.8 already exists with type "related" (requested "blocks"); remove it first with bd dep remove then re-add'. The related edges came from the coordinator's own earlier filing of 0913. Caught only because the ready front was re-queried afterwards and 0913 appeared in it when it should have been blocked.

Two rules broken, both already written down. AGENTS.md: 'never read $? through a pipe... capture, then test' - the same defect with redirection instead of a pipe, which the section does not name. And bd's own refusal to UPGRADE an edge type is undocumented in this corpus: 'related' does not silently become 'blocks', it errors.

Consequence had it gone unnoticed: agent-plugins-0913 edits the same files as items 8 and 9 and would have been dispatched concurrently with them. Repaired by dep remove then dep add, reading every status; front now correctly holds 0913 back. Candidate: extend AGENTS.md's pipes section to cover discarded status generally, and record the edge-upgrade refusal.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro:proof:sprint-scope — CORRECTION to the coordinator's own scope-note 4, found by plan-mpnf. Scope recorded that no admitted bead has an open blocker outside the epic and predicted 'bd swarm validate should raise no outside-dependency warning'. It raised SIX: qozp.13<-qozp.12, qozp.14<-qozp.2, qozp.14<-qozp.12, qozp.15<-qozp.12, qozp.7<-qozp.1, qozp.9<-qozp.2. All six point at CLOSED beads and are harmless in fact, so scope's underlying observation was right; the prediction about the tool's behaviour was wrong. bd swarm validate warns on an edge to an out-of-epic bead whether or not that bead is closed.

The consequence is not cosmetic: run-record.md's rule for trusting the preview is unconditional - 'if it warns about an outside dependency, do not use its partition' - so the prediction, had it been believed, would have licensed using a partition the rule forbids. plan-mpnf followed the rule instead and derived packing from the re-queried ready front, which is the right call. Recorded as another instance of a coordinator claim about tool behaviour that was reasoned rather than measured.

retro:gap:coordinator — the dispatch prompt for agent-plugins-qozp.6 was SELF-INCONSISTENT: its Scope list named plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md, bead-bonanza/SKILL.md and bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md as owned, while its byte-budget paragraph named sprint-plan/references/run-record.md as the place detail should go. No sibling in the wave owned it, so no collision resulted.

The defect is the coordinator's: two parts of one prompt described different file sets and nothing reconciled them before sending. Same class as the sync_dir misattribution in run 2 - a dispatch prompt is an authoring surface with no reviewer, which is exactly what agent-plugins-x5tk (merged earlier this wave) now documents. The agent's handling was correct and is the reason this cost nothing.

retro:proof:bd-graph incident — bd create --graph's EDGE ORIENTATION IS THE REVERSE OF THE NATURAL READING, and the corpus had it the natural way.   edges: [{"from_key":"first","to_key":"second","type":"blocks"}]

comments.text:
retro:process:coordinator incident — SECOND STALL of this session, and a recurrence of an invariant filed and approved during it. After admitting four review findings and re-entering the loop, the coordinator ended the turn having described the next dispatch rather than performing it. The queue was not dry, no bead carried human, the circuit breaker had not tripped — none of the three conditions that permit ending a turn. The human had to say 'go ahead'.

This is the exact invariant from run 2's retro candidate C11, approved by the owner and shipped this run as .sf/outbox/bead-bonanza/2026-08-24-naming-the-next-ceremony-is-not-dispatching-it.md: 'a coordinator turn ends with work in flight, a question to the human, or the run's terminal state — naming the next ceremony is not dispatching it.' RECURRENCE 1, in the run that filed it.

The first stall (before sprint-retro) had no particular cause. This one does, and it is worth recording because a rule alone will not fix it: the pending act was OVERRIDING THE AUTHORIZATION GATE, reversing what runs 1 and 2 did. Stopping let the decision be vetoed without the coordinator owning it. That is not a scheduling slip; it is hedging wearing the shape of a pause, and the operating principle names it — 'a coordinator that escalates has converted an autonomous run into a supervised one without saying so'.

The distinction the outbox issue should carry: if a coordinator believes a decision genuinely needs the human, the compliant move is to ASK, explicitly, which the principle permits as one of the three turn-ending conditions. Announcing a decision and then falling silent is neither deciding nor asking, and it reads to the human as the run having finished.

comments.author: bb-coordinator-mpnf
comments.text:
retro:incident:coordinator-removed-worktree-before-the-merge-succeeded

Review loop 2, batch 10. I ran `git merge --ff-only bb/dev-mpnf-10`, `git worktree remove`, and the acceptance check as one chained command. The merge exited 128 ("Not possible to fast-forward" — the concurrent-wave case, because batch 9 had already moved the head from 22c86ab to e2b69ad) but the removal ran anyway and succeeded.

Nothing was lost: the branch still carried the commit and the remedy is a rebase, not a recovery. But the state it produced is the one the corpus says cannot happen. `worktree-mechanics.md` makes worktree presence the in-flight signal — "you remove it as the final act of accepting, after the last of its branches merges" — and for ~90 seconds a removed worktree coexisted with an unmerged branch. `bb-status.sh bead` reported it faithfully and exited 2:

  OK   3 -> STOP 3 NOT merged into HEAD
  OK   4 worktree: gone

Signal 4 read "accepted" while signal 3 read "not merged". The check is not wrong — it reports what it observes — but the pair is only meaningful because the coordinator is supposed to establish 3 before 4, and nothing enforces that ordering.

Two candidates for the retro, both against bead-bonanza rather than against this run:

1. The reference tells the coordinator the correct order and relies on it being followed. A merge and a removal issued in one shell without `&&` between them breaks it silently. Either the guidance should say "never chain these", or the removal belongs behind a guard that refuses when the branch is not an ancestor of HEAD.

2. `worktree-mechanics.md` says a `--ff-only` refusal in a concurrent wave "is not a fault" and gives the rebase remedy — and that is exactly what happened and what fixed it. But the coordinator checklist has no step that anticipates it, so the refusal arrives looking like the serialized case (which says STOP AND REPORT, do not resolve inline). Reading it wrong stops a healthy run. Worth a line at the merge step naming which case you are in before you read the refusal.

Evidence: /tmp/m10.out (exit 128), /tmp/wr10.out (exit 0), /tmp/acc10.out (exit 2, signal 3 STOP), then rebase onto e2b69ad -> 78b34e1, /tmp/acc10b.out (exit 0, all five OK). Note the sha moved 4b0c304 -> 78b34e1 in the rebase; the acceptance check found it anyway because it greps by bead id rather than trusting a sha recorded earlier, which is the run-2 hand-off defect already fixed.

title: Drop dispatch_state and terminal_state; let bead status carry the dispatch lifecycle
description:
Decision by the owner, 2026-08-24: remove both keys rather than repair the write path. The direction is to simplify and lean into beads, reintroducing a parallel record only if something is measurably lost.

The evidence that settled it: both keys were NULL on several beads across two successful runs and NOTHING BROKE. Measured on run agent-plugins-so39 — agent-plugins-4tjk and agent-plugins-qozp.20 (dispatched straight to run-bead) returned with both null, while beads dispatched through sprint-batch carried them. Every acceptance check still passed, every merge was verified, and the run reached a correct terminal state. A field whose absence changes no verdict is not being consumed.

What the keys were supposed to buy, and what already answers it:
- 'is this dispatch live' — dispatch_state=running is largely redundant with status=in_progress; both mean claimed-and-not-done.
- 'where did a batch die' — recovery.md keys off the bead whose dispatch_state is not returned. Each bead also CLOSES as it completes, so status discriminates the same boundary.
- 'did it complete, block, or skip' — terminal_state is the one genuinely non-redundant case, because blocked and skipped are not bead statuses. That is the thing to watch for after removal, and the owner's instruction is to let it go and reintroduce only if it is missed.
design:
Remove the keys and every read of them. Known sites, to be re-derived by grep rather than trusted from this list: plugin/skills/sprint-wave/SKILL.md (writes both, and its worktree/dispatch_state table), plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/prompt-per-bead.md (writes both), references/recovery.md (reads dispatch_state to locate where a batch died), references/scripts.md (documents the sprint-cleanup contract), bead-bonanza/SKILL.md (the live-worker-or-dead paragraph), scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh (its live-worker guard AND its self-test fixtures), scripts/bb-status.sh (two dispatch_state=running queries).

sprint-cleanup.sh is the one with teeth. Its exit-1 'something was left standing on purpose' path is built on dispatch_state=running. Replace the signal rather than deleting the guard: a standing worktree whose bead is not closed is the same question, asked of state beads already carry.

SEQUENCING, and it is why this belongs in run 3 rather than before it: plan item 8 (agent-plugins-qozp.8) DELETES sprint-wave outright and item 9 (agent-plugins-qozp.9) replaces batch bookkeeping with assignment. Both touch the same files. Do this bead alongside them or after them, never in a wave that races them.

Do NOT reintroduce an equivalent under another name. If terminal_state turns out to be load-bearing, that is a new decision with new evidence, not a rename.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] grep -rn 'dispatch_state\|terminal_state' plugin/ scripts/ returns no hits outside historical prose.
- [ ] sprint-cleanup.sh still refuses to tear down a worktree whose bead is not closed, and its self-tests cover that case with the new signal.
- [ ] bb-status.sh's 'dispatches still running' line either reads a signal beads already carry, or is removed with a stated reason.
- [ ] recovery.md locates a died-mid-batch bead without either key.
- [ ] Demonstrated in a scratch database: a batch that dies on its second of three beads is still locatable.
- [ ] No replacement key is introduced under a different name.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.
notes: MEASURED FILE SET (plan-mpnf). `grep -rln "dispatch_state\|terminal_state" plugin/ scripts/` -> sprint-wave/SKILL.md (DELETED by agent-plugins-qozp.8, which runs earlier in this run), bead-bonanza/{SKILL.md, references/recovery.md, references/scripts.md, references/prompt-per-bead.md, scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh, scripts/bb-status.sh}, sprint-batch/SKILL.md, sprint-recovery/SKILL.md. `dispatched_at` additionally appears in sprint-batch/SKILL.md and prompt-per-bead.md. docs/plans/* also match and are historical plan documents, not machinery — leave them. Re-run the grep at the point of use: qozp.8 and qozp.9 both edit these files earlier in this run.

metadata.tier_reason: removal across skills and two shell scripts, and sprint-cleanup's guard must be re-signalled rather than deleted

comments.text:
SCOPE CHANGED BY A SIBLING, measured before dispatch. agent-plugins-qozp.9 (item 9, merged in wave 2 as b552648) replaced the dispatch bookkeeping wholesale, and 'grep -rn dispatch_state\|terminal_state plugin/ scripts/ sf.toml' now returns ZERO live hits. The removal this bead was filed to perform has already happened.

title: Measure tool behaviour at the point of use; audit the surfaces that carry copies of a belief
description:
Run agent-plugins-so39 was opened to stop documents asserting unmeasured tool behaviour from propagating errors. It corrected three such documents successfully and then committed the same error four times itself, at four different tiers, inside the same run. Correcting instances did not touch the habit, which is why this is its own bead rather than a fifth correction.

The four, each verified on bd 1.2.2 or by control:

1. IN THE CORRECTED PARAGRAPH. agent-plugins-4tjk fixed 'bd update --metadata replaces the entire metadata object' and shipped '--set-metadata stores every value as a string' in its place. Measured: num=5 -> number, b=true -> boolean, f=1.5 -> number, n=null -> null; only arrays, objects and non-numeric text are stringified. Filed as agent-plugins-so39.5.

2. IN A DISPATCH PROMPT. The coordinator told dev-so39-4 that sync_dir does 'rm -rf $dest' then 'cp -r' in sync-shared-references.sh, and built an argument on it. That function is in generate-schemas.sh; sync-shared-references.sh's render() ends 'cat $1'. The bead measured it rather than believing it, and the shipped rule rests on the real mechanic.

3. IN OUR OWN SCRIPT. agent-plugins-b9ft: sync-shared-references.sh's orphan guard uses 'printf ... | grep -qxF' under 'set -o pipefail' - grep -q closes the pipe, printf takes SIGPIPE, pipefail inverts a match into a failure. 2 failures in 30 runs on an unchanged tree; herestring control 100/100 clean. AGENTS.md documents this exact trap.

4. IN AN ARMED TRIGGER. The coordinator relayed 'bd search is non-functional' into an epic comment AND into a durable recovery trigger's prompt. Measured false: it excludes closed issues by default ('bd search metadata' -> 2 hits, '--status all' -> 6). Worse, 'bd search strata --status all' returns agent-plugins-vcka as its second hit, so the coordinator's own duplicate filing was preventable by the very step it then declared impossible. Found by report-so39; the trigger was deleted before firing.

What makes these one defect rather than four: in every case a claim arrived as an inherited premise and was acted on without being measured where it was used. Three of the four were then COPIED onto a surface nobody re-reads.
design:
Two halves, and the second is the one nothing covers today.

THE RULE. State, where an agent is told to rely on tool behaviour, that a claim about what a command does is measured at the point of use or marked unverified - inheriting it from a document, a prompt, or a prior run is not sufficient. This repository already has the shape of this rule in AGENTS.md's environmental-failure ledger ('entries are admitted on evidence, not on reasoning'), and every one of the four instances violated it. So the question is why a rule that exists did not bind, not what the rule should say. Consider whether it needs to move from the ledger section to somewhere a dispatching agent reads.

THE SURFACES. A belief gets copied onto surfaces that are never re-read after writing, so a later correction cannot reach them. Enumerate them and say who audits each:
  - a dispatch prompt - dies with its agent, but can mislead several agents at once
  - a DURABLE TRIGGER PROMPT - outlives the session; a resuming agent inherits it with no way to know it was retracted. This is the worst of them and nothing in the corpus mentions it.
  - a .sf/outbox issue - retro candidate C6 is exactly this: a run-1 outbox file, already human-approved, asserts the --set-metadata universal this run measured false, so triaging it as written would write the false claim into run-record.md
  - an AGENTS.md ledger entry, a plan document, a bead description

Not proposed as a checklist to run. The useful output is knowing which surfaces need re-checking when a claim is retracted, and a habit of retracting on all of them rather than the one in front of you.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The measure-at-point-of-use rule is stated where a dispatching or implementing agent will read it, not only in the ledger section, and names inheritance from a document or prompt as insufficient.
- [ ] The surfaces that carry an unaudited copy of a belief are enumerated, with the durable trigger prompt named explicitly since nothing covers it today.
- [ ] A retraction procedure exists: when a tool claim is found false, the surfaces to sweep are named rather than left to memory.
- [ ] The four instances above are cited as evidence with their measurements, per the environmental-failure ledger rules.
- [ ] Explains why AGENTS.md's existing evidence rule did not bind in these four cases - the analysis, not just a restatement of the rule.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.
notes:
SCOPE PIN (plan-mpnf, run agent-plugins-mpnf) — 'somewhere a dispatching agent reads' is resolved to these files, so the bead does not choose its own blast radius mid-run:
  - AGENTS.md — keep the ledger rule; add the SURFACE ENUMERATION and the RETRACTION PROCEDURE there (repo-local, may cite bead ids).
  - specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md — the authoring rule, for skills vended out of this repo. Re-run scripts/sync-shared-references.sh if it is a vendored source.
  - plugin/skills/run-bead/SKILL.md — the point-of-use rule for the IMPLEMENTING agent (measured 14,119 bytes of body, 5,881 free under the 20,000-byte cap).
DO NOT EDIT plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md (measured 19,240 bytes, 760 free) or its references/dispatch-policy.md, prompt-per-bead.md, prompt-batch.md — agent-plugins-qozp.8, .9, .17 and agent-plugins-0913 all edit those in later waves of this run and this bead runs concurrently with none of them.

The 'durable trigger prompt' surface is the one nothing covers today; name it explicitly, per the bead's own acceptance box.

title: sync-shared-references.sh --check flakes: pipefail + grep -q makes the orphan guard misreport a random mapped file
description:
`scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` fails intermittently, naming a
DIFFERENT correctly-mapped vendored file as an ORPHAN on each failure. Measured
in worktree agent-a2c5301b15d893e08: 2 failures in 30 consecutive runs, no
repo change between them, reporting
`plugin/skills/sprint-retro/references/shared/findings-capture-protocol.md`
once and `plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md`
once. Both have MAP entries. It also fired once inside `bb-checks.py` naming
`plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/shared/epic-definition-of-ready.md`,
which is how it was found — a red gate that is nobody's change.

Cause: the orphan guard's membership test is a pipeline, and the script runs
under `set -euo pipefail`.

    managed_dests=$(printf '%s\n' "$ENTRIES" | cut -f1)
    ...
    if printf '%s\n' "$managed_dests" | grep -qxF -- "$rel"; then
        continue    # generated by the loop above, and diffed there
    fi

`grep -q` exits as soon as it matches; `printf` then dies on SIGPIPE, and
`pipefail` reports the whole pipeline as failed. The `if` reads that as "not
managed" and the file is declared an orphan. Which file loses the race depends
on scheduling, which is why it moves.

This is the exact hazard AGENTS.md's "Pipes hide exit statuses" section
documents ("Under `set -o pipefail`, a reader that closes the pipe early
inverts it"), reached here through a membership test rather than a status read.

## Proof

Negative control run in the same worktree, same tree state: a copy of the
script with only that one line changed to a herestring —

    if grep -qxF -- "$rel" <<< "$managed_dests"; then

— ran 100 consecutive times with 0 failures, against 2/30 for the unpatched
script. Nothing else was changed.

## Fix

Replace the pipeline with the herestring form above (or `case`/`grep` on a
variable). Then re-run the loop to confirm 0/100.

Audit the rest of the script for the same shape while there: any
`cmd | grep -q` / `| head` / `| tail -n` under `pipefail` has it.

## Why this was not fixed in the bead that found it

That bead owns `scripts/check-skills.sh` and `AGENTS.md` only. The defect is in
`scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` — a different file and a different class of
change (a flaky gate, not an authoring rule).


## Steps to Reproduce

1. From the repository root, on an unchanged tree, run
   `for i in $(seq 30); do scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check >/tmp/r$i.txt 2>&1 || echo "FAIL $i"; done`
   (redirect to a file and test the status; do not read it through a pipe).
2. Expected: 30 clean runs, `RESULT: all N vendored references are current.`
3. Actual: roughly 2 runs in 30 exit non-zero and name a *different*
   correctly-mapped vendored file as an ORPHAN each time. Which file loses the
   race depends on process scheduling, so it moves between runs.
4. It also fires from inside `bb-checks.py` as the `shared-refs` check, which is
   how it was found — a red gate that is nobody's change.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The membership test in scripts/sync-shared-references.sh no longer pipes into `grep -q`; it uses a herestring (or a `case`/variable test) so no writer can take SIGPIPE under `set -o pipefail`.
- [ ] The rest of the script is audited for the same shape: every `cmd | grep -q`, `| head`, `| tail -n` under pipefail is either fixed or shown not to be a status read. Name what was found.
- [ ] `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` runs 100 consecutive times on an unchanged tree with 0 failures, and the run count and result are recorded on the bead. The pre-fix rate was 2 failures in 30.
- [ ] No vendored file is added to or removed from the MAP as part of this fix; the ORPHAN reports were false, not real.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: exact one-line fix and a 100-run verification protocol are given; no design judgment, but the pipefail audit of the rest of the script needs care

comments.author: dev-mpnf-1
comments.text: retro:proof:agent-plugins-b9ft Reproduced the root-cause mechanism deterministically, not just on the production-size data. A minimal isolation of the exact shape (printf <bighaystack> | grep -qxF -- <val-on-line-1>) with a 50000-line haystack (>pipe buffer) hit the SIGPIPE race on 300/300 iterations — grep matched instantly and exited, printf died mid-write on SIGPIPE, and under pipefail the pipeline reported failure even though the value was genuinely present. This confirms the mechanism. On the real script's small (35-entry) managed_dests list, the race is much rarer because printf's single write() usually completes before grep even starts reading (well under the ~64KB pipe buffer) — consistent with the bead's own 2/30 in one environment and my own attempts here: 30 runs then 150 runs of the unpatched script on this container produced 0 failures (4-core container; scheduling/load-dependent, not code-dependent — the bug is real regardless of whether it fires in a given run).

comments.author: dev-mpnf-1
comments.text: retro:tooling:scripts/sync-shared-references.sh Audit of the whole file for the same shape (every cmd | grep -q / | head / | tail -n under set -euo pipefail) found two more instances beyond the reported line-227 orphan-guard bug: source_version()'s two `... | head -1` captures (lines 138-139 pre-fix) and the orphan guard's `regen=$(... | head -1)` (lines 231-232 pre-fix). These differ from the line-227 bug in failure mode: they are plain `v=$(...)` assignments, not if/while test conditions, so a pipefail-induced nonzero from a SIGPIPE'd writer would trip 'set -e' and abort the whole script (a crash), not silently misreport a false ORPHAN — same root hazard (AGENTS.md 'Pipes hide exit statuses'), different symptom. Low real-world likelihood (needs >1 matching 'version:'/'Version:' line, or >10 header lines matching 'Regenerate with:'), but the fix is free: drop the trailing '| head -1' and take the first line in the shell via ${v%%$'\n'*} instead, eliminating the extra process and the race entirely. Fixed all three sites the same way.

comments.text: retro:proof:progress-streaming — CORRECTION to the coordinator's own stall finding, in the coordinator's favour but worth recording accurately. The stall was real: the coordinator ended a turn saying 'moving to the retro' with nothing dispatched and nothing in flight, and the human asked before anything resumed. But the claim that no mechanical signal could have caught it is FALSE. The durable recovery trigger armed at first dispatch (trig_01Tr5qJXx7ZnRFVvZohSZpwc) fired at 17:57:32 carrying exactly the right instruction - 'if that run already finished, cancel this and do nothing; otherwise invoke sprint-recovery' - and the run had not finished, so it would have resumed the ceremony. So the watchdog design works and needs no new mechanism; what it cannot do is close the gap between a stall and the next firing, which was set at 50 minutes for this run. The finding worth keeping is about the INTERVAL and about the coordinator, not about a missing signal.

retro:proof:coordinator incident — CORRECTION, verified by the coordinator: 'bd search is non-functional on this build' is FALSE, and the coordinator relayed it twice — into an epic comment and into the retro's own brief — without measuring it. Measured on bd 1.2.2 against the live tracker:

Each was inherited or relayed rather than measured at the point of use, which is the precise failure agent-plugins-4tjk was opened to fix. comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:stale:report — the coordinator's hand-off to report-so39 carried a WRONG SHA for agent-plugins-gu3i and the report caught it. The hand-off said cfcdcd6; that commit exists but is the PRE-REBASE worktree commit and is not an ancestor of the branch (git merge-base --is-ancestor exits 1). As landed it is d6ad144. Cause: the coordinator copied the sha from the batch agent's return line, which reported its own worktree commit, and did not re-read it after the cherry-pick rewrote it. Every merge this run rebased, so every returned sha was stale by construction - the other nine happened to be re-read from git before use. Candidate fix: a returned sha is a worktree sha; the coordinator must resolve the landed sha from git after merging and never carry the returned one forward.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:proof:coordinator incident — the retracted 'bd search is non-functional' claim had a FIFTH propagation site the coordinator did not know about, found by report-so39: the armed durable recovery trigger (trig_01TQcbztLi1xirmBeGHxjJar, next fire 18:24Z) carried it as a HARD CONSTRAINT in its prompt. A session resuming from that trigger would have inherited the error with no way to know it had been retracted, because a trigger prompt is write-once and nothing re-reads it. Deleted at 18:12Z rather than left to post-flight. The general lesson is not about this claim: a durable trigger's prompt is an UNAUDITED COPY of the coordinator's beliefs at arming time, and every correction made after arming leaves it stale. Same class as the dispatch-prompt finding (C7), one level more durable, because a dispatch prompt dies with its agent and a trigger outlives the session.

title: Diff the ready front against manifest.admitted at every dispatch decision
description:
A run's authorized scope is already recorded — sprint-scope writes manifest.admitted and manifest.excluded, and both were populated correctly on run agent-plugins-qozp. What nothing does is COMPARE the live ready front against it.

Measured on that run: sprint-review filed 11 findings as open beads parented to the run epic, so all 11 entered 'bd ready --parent <epic> --exclude-type=epic' on creation — including one the gate had just refused at P0. Nothing flagged it. The coordinator noticed by eye and deferred all 11 by hand. Had it not noticed, the next dispatch decision would have picked them up and the run would have grown past its authorized scope with the gate reading as honoured.

Filing findings deferred (the sprint-review fix) closes THIS entry point. It does not close the class: anything that parents an open bead to the run epic mid-run reopens it — a discovered-from bead an agent files, a groom that undefers something, a human adding work to the epic while the run is live.
design:
A set difference, computed where the run already re-queries:

    front    = {b.id for b in bd ready --parent <epic> --exclude-type=epic --json}
    admitted = set(manifest.admitted)
    creep    = front - admitted

Non-empty creep is NAMED, not silently dispatched. Two possible dispositions and the choice is the coordinator's, not the check's: admit it as an amendment (recording it in manifest.admitted, which is what happened for agent-plugins-h3j8) or defer it out of the front. What the check owes is that neither happens by accident.

Where it goes: bb-status.sh already computes both sides — it reads the ready front and reads manifest.admitted for its 'every admitted bead is closed' check — so this is a new line in an existing report rather than new machinery. State it in the coordinator's wave/dispatch step too, since the report is advisory and the dispatch decision is where it binds.

Note the interaction with item 8 (agent-plugins-qozp.8): when waves are deleted and dispatch becomes continuous from the ready front, this check moves from a wave boundary to every dispatch decision. That makes it MORE important, not less — there is no longer a natural pause at which a human-shaped review of the front happens.

## Where the code already is — do not re-derive it

`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh` already holds both sides:

- the manifest read and the `admitted` list, around the `admitted =
  md.get("admitted") or []` / `outstanding = [...]` / `print("ADMITTED|%d" ...)`
  lines in its embedded python;
- the report side, around the `line FAIL "$_out_n admitted bead(s) not closed"`
  / `line OK "every admitted bead is closed"` pair.

The new line goes alongside those, reading the same two values. It is a report
line, not a gate: a non-empty difference is NAMED and does not change the exit
status.

## Co-edit collisions — both real, and both resolved by the plan

- **`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md`** — `agent-plugins-qozp.19` rewrites
  the *same paragraph* this bead adds to: the one beginning "Re-query the ready
  front at every wave boundary — two commands, in order". Same batch, taken in
  order, one agent. They also share a byte budget: that file's body is 18,835
  bytes against the 20,000-byte cap `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict`
  enforces — 1,165 bytes of headroom for BOTH beads. Two agents each budgeting
  independently against it would each pass alone and break the cap on merge.
- **`bb-status.sh`** — `agent-plugins-xpn8` adds a manifest-shape validator to
  the same read path. It is planned into a LATER wave, so it branches from a
  tree that already carries this bead's line and wraps it rather than racing
  it. Nothing to do here beyond leaving the code readable.

## Scope fence

Rollout item 8 (`agent-plugins-qozp.8`) deletes the wave table and makes
dispatch continuous. It is NOT in this run. Write the coordinator's dispatch-
step sentence so it holds under either shape — "before dispatching" rather than
"at each wave boundary" — but do not implement item 8 and do not undefer it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh` reports the ready-front-minus-`manifest.admitted` difference, naming each bead by id.
- [ ] The line does not change the script's exit status — a non-empty difference is a decision for the coordinator, not a defect.
- [ ] With the difference empty, the line still prints, so a reader can tell "checked and clear" from "not checked".
- [ ] The coordinator's dispatch step in `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` states that a non-empty difference is resolved — admitted as an amendment, or deferred out of the front — before dispatching, and never dispatched unexamined.
- [ ] Demonstrated in a THROWAWAY scratch database: an open bead parented to a run epic but absent from `manifest.admitted` appears in the report by id.
- [ ] Demonstrated in the same scratch database: with the difference empty, the line says so.
- [ ] No bead was created in this project's tracker by either demonstration.
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` exits 0 — `bead-bonanza/SKILL.md`'s body stays under 20,000 bytes.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: A set difference added to an existing report path plus one paragraph of skill prose; the code location is pinned and the only judgement left is keeping the shared byte budget.

title: Define bead metadata manifests in .strata, and validate before every write
description:
Nothing validates the shape of a bead's metadata manifest today — not before a write, not before a read. Verified by grep across plugin/skills/**/scripts: the only shape-aware line is bb-status.sh:574 ('manifest records no admitted set'), which is a presence check, not a type check.

That absence has already cost this project twice in one run. 'admitted' stored as a string rather than a list made bb-status.sh iterate it character by character and report 'FAIL 116 admitted bead(s) not closed: [ " a g e n t - p l u g i n s ...' — 116 being a character count. 'excluded' entries written as {"ids":[...]} instead of {"id":...} made it print 'None (reason); None (reason)'. Both are valid JSON and both produced confident, plausible, wrong output.

The pipeline to fix it already exists in this repository. schemas/ holds 7 .strata files; scripts/generate-schemas.sh builds them with --target ast (validation), --target json-schema, --target go and --target markdown, and carries a --check mode that fails when any generated artifact is stale. Adding a manifest schema rides all of it.
design:
Add schemas/bead-manifest.strata (or one file per manifest type) covering, at minimum, the RUN MANIFEST on the run epic — admitted, excluded, moved, branch, base_sha, standing_auth, checks_ids, checks_baseline, checks_baseline_status, concurrency_cap, review_passes, review_budget, findings_path, report_path, retro_* — and the DISPATCH RECORD on a bead (dispatch_id, dispatch_state, terminal_state, outcome, worktree, dispatched_at, tier, tier_reason). Model the manifest types as inheriting document types so generate-schemas.sh's existing non-empty-required assertion covers them.

TWO CALL SITES, and a schema enforces nothing without them:
  1. BEFORE WRITE — plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh's manifest_merge() helper (added by agent-plugins-qozp.18, commit a3e7d38). It already fails loudly on an unreadable manifest; add a validate step on the merged object before bd update, so a bad shape never lands.
  2. BEFORE READ — bb-status.sh, replacing its untyped iteration with a validate-then-use, so a wrong type is a FAIL naming the key and the observed type rather than a character count.

Write the validator in Python against the generated JSON Schema (the repo already depends on python3; groom-beads/scripts/validate_beads.py sets the precedent of using jsonschema where installed and falling back to built-in checks otherwise). One script, both call sites.

The generated markdown replaces run-record.md's hand-written key table, which is the same document a separate finding reports as incomplete about HOW to write these keys — so this removes the drift rather than documenting around it.

NOTE the storage reality: the manifest lives in bd metadata, not a file on disk, so nothing validates it implicitly. Validation is a step something calls, which is why the two call sites are part of this bead and not a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] schemas/*.strata defines the run manifest and the bead dispatch record.
- [ ] scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check exits 0 with the new schema and its generated artifacts committed.
- [ ] A Python validator validates a JSON object against the generated schema and exits non-zero with the offending key and observed type named.
- [ ] manifest_merge() in pre-flight-check.sh validates the merged object before bd update; an invalid shape is refused, not written.
- [ ] bb-status.sh validates before use; demonstrated in a scratch database that 'admitted' stored as a string reports a shape error naming the key and type, NOT a character count.
- [ ] Demonstrated in a scratch database that an 'excluded' entry carrying 'ids' rather than 'id' is refused at write time.
- [ ] run-record.md's hand-written manifest key table is replaced by, or generated from, the schema.
- [ ] No bead was created in this project's tracker by any demonstration.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

title: The corpus states 'bd update --metadata replaces the entire metadata object'; on bd 1.2.2 it merges
description:
plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/capability-tier.md:57-60 states:

  `--metadata '<json>'` takes real JSON types but **replaces the entire
  metadata object**. Use it to write a bead's metadata in one shot (at
  creation); do NOT reach for it to add a key, or you will silently drop
  every key you did not restate.

plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md:240 repeats it as 'the trap that `--metadata` REPLACES where `--set-metadata` adds'.

Measured against bd version 1.2.2 (dev) in a throwaway database, bead mmlab-doq:

  bd update <id> --metadata '{"alpha":1,"beta":"two","gamma":["x","y"]}'
  bd update <id> --metadata '{"delta":9}'
  bd show <id> --json | jq -c '.[0].metadata'
  -> {"beta":"two","alpha":1,"delta":9,"gamma":["x","y"]}

Omitted keys survive. It merges at the TOP LEVEL. A follow-up write of '{"alpha":99}' changed only alpha and left beta, gamma and delta.

The claim is not wholly wrong — the merge is SHALLOW. A nested object value IS replaced wholesale: seeded '{"nest":{"a":1,"b":2}}', then '{"nest":{"c":3}}', read back '{"c":3}'. That matters directly, because the run manifest's standing_auth is a nested object.

Why this is P1 rather than a doc nit: the false premise PROPAGATED. It produced a P0 review finding against pre-flight-check.sh (agent-plugins-qozp.18) claiming a silent data-loss path that does not exist, and a coordinator 'independent verification' that confirmed the code shape without measuring the consequence. Two agents reasoned from the document instead of from the tool, and the document was wrong. Corpus claims about tool behaviour are load-bearing in exactly this way.

Note the separately-measured and STILL-TRUE trap that likely seeded the confusion: --set-metadata stores every value as a string, so an array written with it comes back as the literal string '["a","b"]'. That is real and is why --metadata is reached for at all.

## Steps to Reproduce

In a THROWAWAY scratch database only — never this project's tracker:

```
bd create "probe" ; id=<minted id>
bd update $id --metadata '{"alpha":1,"beta":"two","gamma":["x","y"]}'
bd update $id --metadata '{"delta":9}'
bd show $id --json | jq -c '.[0].metadata'
```

Expected, per `capability-tier.md` as written: `{"delta":9}` — every
unrestated key dropped. Actual, on bd 1.2.2: the omitted keys survive and the
object merges at the TOP LEVEL. A nested object value is a different story and
IS replaced wholesale: seed `{"nest":{"a":1,"b":2}}`, write `{"nest":{"c":3}}`,
read back `{"c":3}`.

## The grep is already done — do not re-derive it

`grep -rniE "metadata.{0,40}(replace|entire metadata)" plugin/ scripts/ docs/
specs/ --include=*.md --include=*.sh`, excluding generated
`references/shared/` copies, returns exactly three sites and no others:

- `plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/capability-tier.md:57`
- `plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md:240`
- `plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md:259`

Re-run it after editing to confirm nothing was missed; the acceptance criterion
asking for the grep is satisfied by that re-run, not by a fresh search of the
tree.
design:
Correct the claim at the three measured sites, keeping the guidance that told
an author which flag to reach for and why.

The corrected statement, in one sentence: `--metadata '<json>'` MERGES at the
top level — keys you do not restate survive — but a nested object value is
replaced wholesale, so a partial write of a nested key such as `standing_auth`
discards its siblings. That nested-replacement half is the part that matters
operationally, since the run manifest's `standing_auth` is exactly a nested
object.

Keep, do not delete: `--set-metadata` stores every value as a STRING, arrays
included, so an array written with it reads back as the literal string
`["a","b"]`. That is separately measured, still true, and is the real reason
`--metadata` is reached for at all. The rewritten guidance must still leave an
author able to pick a flag.

Cite the command and the observed output at the reference site, per this
repository's environmental-failure-ledger rules — the failure this bead repairs
is two agents reasoning from a document instead of from the tool, and an
uncited restatement invites the same thing again.

BYTE BUDGET — read this before writing. `groom-beads/SKILL.md`'s body is 19,872
bytes against the 20,000-byte cap `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` enforces
(measured with the checker's own method, `text.split('---', 2)[2]`): **128
bytes of headroom, roughly one and a half lines.** The corrected claim is
longer than the wrong one it replaces, so SKILL.md's two restatements must get
SHORTER or stay level — put the measurement and the citation in
`references/capability-tier.md`, which has room, and leave SKILL.md pointing at
it. `skills-strict` is green in this run's baseline and a bead is expected to
leave it that way.

Out of scope: `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/scripts.md`'s phrase
"merging rather than replacing" — that describes `pre-flight-check.sh`'s own
`manifest_merge` helper, not bd's flag, and it is accurate.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] capability-tier.md states the measured behaviour: --metadata merges at the top level on bd 1.2.2, and a nested object value is replaced wholesale.
- [ ] The command and output that establish it are cited, per this repository's environmental-failure ledger rules.
- [ ] groom-beads/SKILL.md:240's one-line restatement agrees with the reference rather than contradicting it.
- [ ] Any other corpus location asserting the replace semantics is found (grep) and corrected.
- [ ] The guidance still tells an author which flag to use and why, since --set-metadata's string-only storage remains a real reason to prefer --metadata for arrays.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: The measurement is already recorded on the bead and the three sites are enumerated; what remains is careful prose that must stay correct in both directions inside 128 bytes of headroom.

description:

scripts/check-skills.sh rule 3 errors on any `../<skill>/references/` path and rule 2
requires a backticked `*.md` path to resolve from the citing file's own directory.
Together they make it impossible for one skill to cite another's reference, and the
checker's error text names exactly one remedy — vendor it through
scripts/sync-shared-references.sh. Nothing states when that remedy is right.

Two beads in ONE run hit the rule and resolved it OPPOSITE ways, neither knowing about
the other: agent-plugins-qozp.2 cited the roster by role in prose and explicitly
rejected vendoring (its acceptance criterion forbade a second copy), while
agent-plugins-qozp.5 vendored, adding a MAP line and a generated
plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/shared/epic-definition-of-ready.md. Both are
defensible against their own acceptance criteria and the corpus now demonstrates two
incompatible answers to one question.

Cost: the next bead picks whichever it reads first, and the vended skills accumulate
both patterns — one of which leaves a reader with an unlinked hop and the other of
which adds a file shared-refs must keep current forever (34 -> 35 this run).
design:
State the rule and put it where the agent hits the wall: in scripts/check-skills.sh's
rule-3 error text and in this repository's authoring guidance.

The rule, concretely:
  - VENDOR when the cited text is normative for the citing skill and must travel with it.
  - CITE BY ROLE in prose when the cited file has a single sanctioned home that a second
    copy would contradict.

The error text must name both branches and the test that chooses between them, so the two
resolutions this run produced are no longer both defensible.

Scope note carried from the retro draft: the fix lands in scripts/check-skills.sh and in
this repository's authoring guidance. The draft does not name which authoring-guidance
file; pick the one that already governs skill references and say so in the commit.

## Grooming decision — the authoring-guidance file is now NAMED

The design above left it open: "pick the one that already governs skill
references and say so in the commit." Resolved by measurement rather than by
preference. `grep -rln check-skills --include=*.md .` returns only
`docs/plans/`, `docs/research/` and `rfcs/` — planning and retrospective
documents, none of them normative. No file under `docs/` or `specs/` governs
skill-file authoring.

**`AGENTS.md` is the file.** It already carries this repository's only
normative rules for authoring `plugin/skills/**` — its "Historical prose:
don't" section ends with "**Do not cross-reference issue ids in skill files.**
… This applies to `plugin/skills/**` and anything vendored from it." A
vendor-or-cite rule is the same kind of rule about the same tree, and putting
it anywhere else creates a second home for skill-authoring guidance where one
exists. Add it to `AGENTS.md`; do not create a new document.

## Anchors for acceptance criterion 3

The rule must resolve the two opposite resolutions this run produced. Both are
in the tree now:

- **`agent-plugins-qozp.2`'s form** — the agent roster cited by role in prose,
  in `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatch-policy.md` under "Ids are
  DERIVED from the run epic id, never minted". No second copy.
- **`agent-plugins-qozp.5`'s form** — vendored:
  `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh`'s MAP carries the line
  `sprint-plan<TAB>groom-beads/references/epic-definition-of-ready.md`, which
  generates `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/shared/epic-definition-of-ready.md`.

The rule-3 error text this bead rewrites is in `scripts/check-skills.sh`, in
the `# ---- 3. no skill reaches outside its own directory` block; today it
reads "cites a sibling skill's references directly; vendor it into
references/shared/ via scripts/sync-shared-references.sh" and names only the
one remedy.

## Sequencing note, not a file collision

`agent-plugins-qozp.20` edits
`plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/epic-definition-of-ready.md` and
regenerates its vendored twin — the very artefact this bead's criterion 3 rules
on. The two share no file (this bead touches `scripts/check-skills.sh` and
`AGENTS.md`), and this bead does NOT authorize un-vendoring anything: it
classifies, it does not migrate. If the rule as written implies the epic-DoR
vendoring was the wrong form, say so and file it; do not delete the twin here.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh's rule-3 error text names both branches (vendor / cite by role) and the test that chooses between them.
- [ ] This repository's authoring guidance states the same rule, in the same words.
- [ ] The rule resolves the two opposite resolutions this run produced: applied to agent-plugins-qozp.2's roster citation and to agent-plugins-qozp.5's epic-DoR vendoring, it names one of them as the correct form for each case.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

title: sprint-batch issues bd update calls but never exports BEADS_ACTOR
description:
`grep -rn BEADS_ACTOR plugin/skills/` hits dispatch-policy.md, prompt-batch.md, prompt-per-bead.md, worktree-mechanics.md, run-bead/SKILL.md and sprint-wave/SKILL.md — and NOT sprint-batch/SKILL.md.

sprint-batch is a bd writer: SKILL.md:58 runs `bd update <id> --set-metadata dispatch_id={DISPATCH_ID} ...` and SKILL.md:122 runs `bd update <id> --set-metadata dispatch_state=returned`. It is handed {DISPATCH_ID} at SKILL.md:28 but is never told to export it as BEADS_ACTOR.

Shell environment does not survive between an agent's tool calls, so an export done in a dispatching prompt does not reach sprint-batch's own bash invocations. Per the measured table in dispatch-policy.md (bd 1.2.2): unset assignee plus unset $BEADS_ACTOR means the assignee SILENTLY becomes the harness default (git user.name), exit 0, nothing reported.

This is a gap in item 4's own dev path, which qozp.17 explicitly scopes out (that bead covers CEREMONY dispatch sites).

FIX DIRECTION: sprint-batch/SKILL.md states `export BEADS_ACTOR={DISPATCH_ID}` in every shell, before its first bd call, the same wording prompt-batch.md uses.

Evidence: grep over plugin/skills/; sprint-batch/SKILL.md:28,58,122; dispatch-policy.md measured claim table.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -rn BEADS_ACTOR plugin/skills/sprint-batch/` — returns nothing.
2. `grep -n 'bd update' plugin/skills/sprint-batch/SKILL.md` — returns the
   `--set-metadata dispatch_id=` and `--set-metadata dispatch_state=returned`
   writes.
3. Expected: a `bd`-writing skill states `export BEADS_ACTOR=...` before its
   first `bd` call, as `prompt-batch.md` and `run-bead/SKILL.md` do.
   Actual: it does not, so every `bd` call sprint-batch makes runs with
   `$BEADS_ACTOR` unset.
design:
Single site, single change: `plugin/skills/sprint-batch/SKILL.md` states
`export BEADS_ACTOR={DISPATCH_ID}` in every shell, before its first `bd` call,
using the same wording `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/prompt-batch.md`
already uses. Copy that wording rather than inventing a second phrasing —
one vocabulary for one rule.

`{DISPATCH_ID}` is already handed to sprint-batch in its own placeholder table
(SKILL.md, the "Accepting the assignment" section), so nothing new has to be
plumbed through; the instruction to export it is the whole change.

Budget: `sprint-batch/SKILL.md`'s body is 6,435 bytes against the 20,000-byte
cap `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` enforces — 13,565 bytes of headroom, so
this bead has no size pressure. (Measured with the checker's own method,
`text.split('---', 2)[2]`.)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `plugin/skills/sprint-batch/SKILL.md` instructs the agent to `export BEADS_ACTOR={DISPATCH_ID}` in every shell, before its first `bd` call.
- [ ] The instruction appears before the first `bd update` the file issues, not after it.
- [ ] The wording matches `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/prompt-batch.md`'s, so the corpus states the rule one way.
- [ ] `grep -rn BEADS_ACTOR plugin/skills/sprint-batch/` returns at least one hit.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` exits 0.

title: batch-id is 'position in its wave', so agent ids collide across waves of the same run
description:
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatch-policy.md:61-64 defines '<batch-id> is the batch's position in its wave'.

Wave 1's first batch and wave 2's first batch both derive `dev-<run-id>-1`. Same run, same shared tracker, two different subagents with the same agent id.

This breaks the section's own stated purpose. `bd ready --assignee dev-<run-id>-1` returns the union of both batches' queues; a resumed session 'recomputes the same string' and finds the wrong agent's work; and the run's merge-slot hold is keyed on a string two agents answer to. The paragraph immediately below correctly identifies that a bare `dev-3` collides ACROSS runs and adds <run-id> to fix it — the same argument applies WITHIN a run across waves, and is not made.

FIX DIRECTION: include the wave ordinal in the derivation (`dev-<run-id>-<wave>-<batch>`), which stays recomputable from the wave table.

Evidence: dispatch-policy.md:61-70.

title: The new epic-DoR assignee gate has no producer and runs before assignees can exist
description:
plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/epic-definition-of-ready.md:20-28 (and its vendored twin at plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/shared/epic-definition-of-ready.md) adds: 'Every child carries an assignee, and the check NAMES the ones that do not.'

TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS IT CANNOT PASS:

1. NO PRODUCER. `grep -rn -- '--assignee' plugin/skills/` returns nothing outside read-side queries (`bd ready --assignee`, `bd list`). No skill in the corpus ever WRITES an assignee. Agents acquire one only as a side effect of `bd update --claim` at dispatch time, which is after grooming.

2. WRONG ORDERING. sprint-plan/SKILL.md:111-116 runs this gate at step 1b; grooming is step 2 and the wave table comes after that. The assignee value the roster specifies is `dev-<run-id>-<batch-id>`, and `<batch-id>` is 'the batch's position in its wave' (dispatch-policy.md:63) — derived from a wave table that does not exist when the gate runs. The gate demands a value whose input is downstream of it.

So the gate fails on every epic, every run, and names every child. A check that always fires is indistinguishable from one that never fires.

NOT A DUPLICATE of agent-plugins-qozp.17, which is about ceremony dispatch sites exporting BEADS_ACTOR; this is about the dev-side assignee having no writer at all and about the gate's position in sprint-plan's sequence.

FIX DIRECTION: either move the gate after the wave table is built and give sprint-plan an explicit assign step, or weaken it to a report rather than a gate until a producer exists.

Evidence: grep over plugin/skills/; sprint-plan/SKILL.md:111-128; dispatch-policy.md:61-64.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -rn -- '--assignee' plugin/skills/` — every hit is a read-side query
   (`bd ready --assignee`, `bd list`). No skill writes an assignee.
2. Read `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md`'s step "1b. Gate the EPIC as well
   as its beads": it runs the epic Definition of Ready, whose assignee check is
   in `plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/epic-definition-of-ready.md`.
   Grooming is step 2 and the wave table comes after it.
3. `bd list --parent <any run epic> --status all --json | jq -r '.[] |
   select((.assignee // "") == "") | .id'` at step 1b — expected: names the
   unassigned children. Actual: names ALL of them, on every epic, every run,
   because the value they need does not exist yet and nothing produces it.

## Grooming decisions — both open choices are now SELECTED

**(1) Which fix direction.** The description offered "move the gate after the
wave table and give sprint-plan an explicit assign step" or "weaken it to a
report until a producer exists". **The first is selected.** A producer exists
the moment sprint-plan is told to assign, and sprint-plan is the only agent
that holds what the assignee value needs: `dev-<run-id>-<batch-id>` is derived
from the wave table, which sprint-plan builds. Weakening the gate to a report
would leave the corpus with a check that names a value nothing writes — the
same defect in a quieter form.

**(2) How `<batch-id>` is formed.** Folded in here because this bead owns the
assign step and the defect is inside it.
`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatch-policy.md` defines `<batch-id>`
as "the batch's position in its wave". Measured against this run's own plan:
wave 1's first batch and wave 2's first batch both resolve to `dev-so39-1`, so
two different agents in one run share an id — and the resumed-session
recomputation that section promises returns an ambiguous answer. The assign
step must number batches once across the whole run, not per wave.
design:
Three changes; the first is the substance and the others follow from it.

1. `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md` gains an explicit ASSIGN step, placed
   after the wave table is built, and the epic-DoR gate moves to after that
   step. Assignment is what makes the gate satisfiable: sprint-plan writes
   `dev-<run-id>-<batch-id>` onto every planned bead with
   `bd update <id> --assignee <id>`, and the ceremony beads keep the ids
   dispatch-policy.md already defines.

2. `<batch-id>` is defined as the batch's position in the RUN, numbered once
   across all waves, in `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatch-policy.md`
   under "Ids are DERIVED from the run epic id, never minted". The current
   "position in its wave" collides across waves (see the description) and
   breaks the recomputation that same section promises.

3. The epic-DoR assignee check is reworded so it reads as a check on a value
   that now has a writer, and names sprint-plan's assign step as the producer.

EDIT THE SOURCE, NOT THE TWIN.
`plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/shared/epic-definition-of-ready.md` is a
GENERATED COPY — its header says so. Edit
`plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/epic-definition-of-ready.md`, then run
`scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` and commit both. Editing the twin by hand
leaves the `shared-refs` check failing and the two copies disagreeing.

BYTE BUDGET — read this before writing. `sprint-plan/SKILL.md`'s body is
19,750 bytes against the 20,000-byte cap `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict`
enforces (measured with the checker's own method, `text.split('---', 2)[2]`):
**250 bytes of headroom, about three lines.** Moving step 1b relocates existing
bytes and is roughly neutral; the assign step is net new. Budget for it by
cutting from the same file, or the `skills-strict` check — green in this run's
baseline — turns red. `groom-beads/SKILL.md` is worse at 128 bytes of headroom,
but this bead does not touch it.

Out of scope: implementing rollout items 6-14, and any change to how the
coordinator dispatches.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md` carries an explicit step that assigns every planned bead, and it is positioned after the wave table is built.
- [ ] The epic Definition-of-Ready assignee gate runs after that assign step, not before it.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/epic-definition-of-ready.md` names sprint-plan's assign step as the producer of the assignee value, so the check no longer demands a value nothing writes.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatch-policy.md` defines `<batch-id>` as the batch's position in the run, numbered once across all waves, and no longer as its position in its wave.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/shared/epic-definition-of-ready.md` was regenerated by `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` rather than hand-edited, and both copies are committed.
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` exits 0 — `sprint-plan/SKILL.md`'s body stays under 20,000 bytes.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: Restructures a skill's step order and introduces a producer for a value nothing writes, across three files plus a generated twin, inside 250 bytes of headroom on a hard size cap.

title: bd epic close-eligible takes no epic argument — the coordinator loop closes epics repo-wide
description:
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md:218 instructs the coordinator to run `bd epic close-eligible` then `bd ready --parent <epic> ...` at every wave boundary. The second command is epic-scoped; the first is not.

MEASURED (bd 1.2.2, `bd epic close-eligible --help`): the usage line is `bd epic close-eligible [flags]` and the only flag is `--dry-run`. There is no epic positional. An epic id passed anyway is silently ignored, so the obvious 'fix' of writing `bd epic close-eligible <epic>` reads as scoped and is not.

CONSEQUENCE: in this project's shared tracker the command closes EVERY eligible epic in the database at each wave boundary — including epics belonging to other runs, other humans, and beads this run was explicitly told not to touch. A run's routine loop step performs unrelated writes it never reports.

The deadlock the instruction prevents is real (an epic does not close when its children do), so the instruction should not simply be dropped.

FIX DIRECTION: either scope it by hand (enumerate this epic's ceremony sub-epics and close the eligible ones explicitly), or run `--dry-run` first and close only ids under this run epic, or file upstream for an epic-scoped form. Whichever is chosen, SKILL.md must state that the bare command is repo-wide.

Evidence: `bd epic close-eligible --help` on bd 1.2.2 in this container.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `bd epic close-eligible --help` on bd 1.2.2 — the usage line is
   `bd epic close-eligible [flags]` and the only flag is `--dry-run`. There is
   no epic positional.
2. Read `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md`, the paragraph beginning
   "Re-query the ready front at every wave boundary — two commands, in order",
   and `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/supervision.md`, the paragraph
   beginning "Re-querying the ready front is two commands, in order".
3. Expected: the loop's writes stay inside the run's epic, as the second
   command does. Actual: the first command is unscoped, so on this project's
   shared tracker it closes every eligible epic in the database at each wave
   boundary — including epics belonging to other runs and other humans.

## Grooming decision — the fix direction is now SELECTED, not open

The description offered three: (a) hand-enumerate this run's ceremony
sub-epics, (b) `--dry-run` first and close only ids under this run epic,
(c) file upstream for an epic-scoped form.

**(b) is selected.** (a) presupposes the ceremony-epic shape that rollout item
7 introduces and that has not landed — there are no ceremony sub-epics to
enumerate today, so it is unimplementable now. (c) is not a change this
repository can make and leaves the corpus wrong in the meantime; it is worth
filing separately but does not close this bead. (b) is implementable against
bd 1.2.2 as installed and needs nothing from the rollout plan.
design:
Replace the unscoped instruction at BOTH sites with a scoped procedure, and
say plainly that the bare command is repo-wide. The deadlock the instruction
prevents is real, so the instruction is corrected, never dropped.

The procedure: run `bd epic close-eligible --dry-run` first, intersect what it
names with the epics under this run, and close only those explicitly. State
the reason inline — `bd epic close-eligible` takes NO epic positional (bd
1.2.2, `--help`), and an epic id passed anyway is silently ignored, so the
obvious "fix" of writing `bd epic close-eligible <epic>` reads as scoped and is
not. Naming that wrong answer is the point: without it the next reader
re-invents it.

Two sites, and they must agree:
- `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` — the paragraph beginning "Re-query the
  ready front at every wave boundary — two commands, in order".
- `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/supervision.md` — the paragraph
  beginning "Re-querying the ready front is two commands, in order".

BYTE BUDGET — read this before writing. `bead-bonanza/SKILL.md`'s body is
18,835 bytes against the 20,000-byte cap `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict`
enforces (measured with the checker's own method,
`text.split('---', 2)[2]`), i.e. 1,165 bytes of headroom. That headroom is
SHARED with `agent-plugins-d6zz`, which adds to the same paragraph and is
planned into the same batch. Take the long form into `supervision.md`, which
has room, and keep SKILL.md's version to the rule plus the one-line warning.
Two agents each budgeting independently against 1,165 bytes would both pass
alone and break the cap on merge — which is why these two beads share one
agent.

Out of scope: filing the upstream request for an epic-scoped form, and
implementing rollout item 7's ceremony-epic shape.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` no longer instructs a bare `bd epic close-eligible` at the wave boundary; it states a procedure whose writes are confined to epics under the run epic.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/supervision.md` states the same procedure, and the two do not disagree.
- [ ] At least one of the two states explicitly that `bd epic close-eligible` takes no epic positional, that a passed id is silently ignored, and that the bare command is therefore repo-wide.
- [ ] The deadlock rationale (an epic does not close on its own when its children do, so a finished ceremony phase stays open and an empty front reads as done) is preserved, not dropped.
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` exits 0 — `bead-bonanza/SKILL.md`'s body stays under 20,000 bytes.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` exits 0.

title: pre-flight-check.sh does not emit concurrency_cap into the run manifest
description:
sprint-plan/references/run-record.md now specifies concurrency_cap as a run-manifest key (source: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS, default 20) and sprint-plan/SKILL.md states the N_dev <= cap - 1 planning rule against it. Nothing writes the key.

plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh is what populates the manifest (its header comment reads 'Manifest + emitted: checks_ids, checks_baseline, the model lineup'; it sets checks_baseline_status and checks_baseline around lines 667-669). It does not set concurrency_cap, so a plan reading manifest.concurrency_cap gets null and the DoR check that compares the dev-assignee count against it has nothing to compare with.

Fix: have pre-flight-check.sh resolve ${CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS:-20} and merge it into the manifest object alongside checks_baseline_status, and update the script header's emitted-keys comment.

Out of scope for the bead that specified the key: that bead owns plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md and plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md only, and pre-flight-check.sh is a bead-bonanza script another wave-1 bead may hold.
design:
WHERE THE KEY IS WRITTEN. pre-flight-check.sh's only manifest write is the
python heredoc near the end of section 8 — the block that reads the epic's
existing metadata, sets cur["checks_ids"], cur["checks_baseline_status"] and
cur["checks_baseline"], then runs `bd update <epic> --metadata`. That block
sits inside the "checks were declared" branch (its else-arm says "not captured
— no checks were declared"), so writing concurrency_cap there and nowhere else
would skip any run whose sf.toml declares no checks. Write it on ANY pass that
was given an epic id: either hoist the merge out of that branch, or add a
second merge that runs whenever EPIC is set. Merge, never replace — read the
current metadata first, exactly as the existing block does, so the admission
record (admitted / excluded / moved) and branch / base_sha / standing_auth
survive.

VALUE AND SHAPE. `${CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS:-20}`, written as a
JSON number so it matches the shape documented in
plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md ("concurrency_cap": 20). A
set-but-non-numeric environment value falls back to 20 rather than writing a
string — a consumer comparing a count against a string is the failure this key
exists to prevent.

MANIFEST *AND* EMITTED. The script header's own rule decides this: "A fact
about the RUN is durable: write it to the epic's manifest AND emit it." So
also `emit BB_CONCURRENCY_CAP "$cap"` alongside the other run facts. This is
deliberately classed as a RUN fact and not a container fact even though its
source is a session environment variable: run-record.md records it so a run
resumed on a differently-configured session knows what the plan assumed, not
to describe the current container. Do not "correct" it to emitted-only.

SELF-TEST. `pre-flight-check.sh --self-test` asserts "--json carries the same
keys as the eval block". Add the variable through the shared emit calls so it
reaches both paths; adding it to one path only breaks the script-self-tests
check.

HEADER COMMENT. Add concurrency_cap to the header's "Manifest + emitted:" list
and BB_CONCURRENCY_CAP to the "Emitted only:" neighbours' list as appropriate
(concurrency_cap belongs on the "Manifest + emitted" line).

DEMONSTRATE AGAINST A SCRATCH DATABASE, NOT THIS TRACKER. Verifying the write
means running pre-flight-check.sh against an epic id; run it against a scratch
beads database (its own directory, its own `bd init --prefix`, selected with
`bd --db <scratch>` / `-C`), never against agent-plugins-qozp. A pass against
the live run epic would rewrite this run's checks_baseline from a worktree
mid-flight. Create no bead in this project's tracker.

SCOPE. This bead owns plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh
only. plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md and
plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md already specify the key and
the N_dev <= cap - 1 rule; they belong to other beads. Do not edit them.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] After a `pre-flight-check.sh <epic-id>` pass against a scratch database,
      `bd show <epic-id> --json | jq '.[0].metadata.concurrency_cap'` returns a
      JSON number, not null.
- [ ] The value is CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS where the session sets
      it and 20 where it does not; a set-but-non-numeric value falls back to 20.
- [ ] The key is written on an epic-id pass even when no checks are declared.
- [ ] The merge preserves manifest keys already present — demonstrated by
      writing a metadata object first and finding it intact afterwards.
- [ ] `eval "$(pre-flight-check.sh <epic-id>)"` sets BB_CONCURRENCY_CAP, and
      `pre-flight-check.sh --json` carries the same key.
- [ ] The script header names concurrency_cap on its "Manifest + emitted" line
      and BB_CONCURRENCY_CAP among the emitted variables.
- [ ] `pre-flight-check.sh --self-test` exits 0, including "--json carries the
      same keys as the eval block".
- [ ] No bead was created in this project's tracker and this run's epic
      metadata was not rewritten by any demonstration.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: One localized bash+python edit in a single script whose own --self-test pins the contract; the design fixes the placement, the JSON shape and the RUN-vs-container classification, so no judgement is left open.

title: DECISION D1: where do the orchestration hooks live?
description: Items 12-14 have no home until this is answered. The sf plugin ships skills/ only — no hooks/ and no monitors/. Two options, and it is a judgement rather than a measurement. (b) A new plugin/hooks/hooks.json and plugin/monitors/monitors.json: travels with the plugin, but every adopter inherits them. title: Item 7: the run-epic shape, flat target, one swarm
description: Plan: docs/plans/beads-coordination-rollout.md item 7. Ceremony as epics under a run epic, with the target epic as the swarmed payload. Forced by the type rules: bd dep add refuses task->epic and epic->task, so anything that must block the target has to be an epic. One epic->epic edge then blocks every bead under the target, and beads added mid-run inherit the block structurally (measured).
design: Shape: run epic (never swarmed) containing preflight/scope/plan/TARGET/review/retro/report/postflight, ceremony chained epic->epic, target swarmed. THE TARGET IS FLAT — tasks only. Measured: bd swarm validate on epic->child epic->2 tasks reports 'Total issues: 1' and treats the child epic as work, with no warning; the flat form reports 2. Work that genuinely decomposes into sub-epics becomes a SECOND target under the run epic, swarmed separately. GATES ATTACH TO TASK CHILDREN, never to a ceremony epic: a gate bead is a task and gating an epic needs the refused task->epic edge, so the authorization gate lives on a task child of the scope epic (verified end to end).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The shape is documented in bead-bonanza/SKILL.md and built by sprint-scope.
- [ ] The target epic is created flat, and the flatness rule is stated as an ADMISSION rule for mid-run additions, not only a planning rule.
- [ ] bd swarm is called on the TARGET epic, never the run epic.
- [ ] The authorization gate is created against a task child of the scope epic.
- [ ] Demonstrated: beads under the target are blocked until pre-flight's epic closes via bd epic close-eligible; bd swarm validate reports the true leaf count; a bead added mid-run is blocked without being wired.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

comments.text:
retro:proof:the-queue-expression-survives-the-shape the shape does NOT change `bd ready --parent <run-epic> --exclude-type=epic`, and I checked rather than assuming it — a run epic full of ceremony TASKS could plausibly have polluted the work queue.
evidence: same scratch run, advanced to the point the target opens. Resolved the gate, closed demo-oop, ran `bd epic close-eligible` (which closed scope), added and closed a task under the plan epic, ran close-eligible again -> "Closed 1 epic(s) - demo-ny3". Then `bd ready --parent demo-7ct --exclude-type=epic` returned exactly three rows, all three the target children: demo-056.1 (the mid-run addition), demo-bt7, demo-fy2. Nothing from the ceremony epics.

The chain does the filtering. So the run epic stays the one id recovery needs, and only `bd swarm` takes the target — recorded as a manifest key `target` and returned by sprint-scope as BB_TARGET. No sweep of --parent call sites was needed.

title: Item 6: planning emits a bd create --graph JSON plan
description: Plan: docs/plans/beads-coordination-rollout.md item 6. THE KEYSTONE. Planning's output stops being prose plus a wave table and becomes one JSON document that builds the run. Measured: one --graph call created a 9-issue run (ceremony epics, target, work beads, parentage, assignees) with 5 edges, after which bd ready correctly showed only the pre-flight check.
design: Schema (measured): {nodes:[{key,title,type,parent_key|parent_id,assignee,priority,description}], edges:[{from_key,to_key,type}]}. bd's unknown-field warnings name the correct keys when you guess wrong. TWO VALIDATIONS BEFORE LOADING, because both failures are silent: (1) --graph reports unknown fields as warnings and DROPS them, so a typo in a key name is a silently missing assignee, not an error — validate against the known field set; (2) no node whose parent_key is the target epic may have type epic, because a nested target makes bd swarm count the child epic as one issue and never see the real beads (measured: 'Total issues: 1' vs 2). Pull the flatness check in here rather than leaving it to item 7.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] sprint-plan emits a graph plan file; the path is recorded in the manifest.
- [ ] bead-bonanza loads it with bd create --graph.
- [ ] A validator rejects unknown node/edge fields BEFORE loading, with the offending key named.
- [ ] A validator rejects any node parented to the target with type epic.
- [ ] Demonstrated end to end: emit for a real epic, diff the plan, load into a scratch db, assert node count, every edge, every bead assigned, and the expected ready front.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.
