## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `<id>.handoff.md` is no longer written by any template or script.
- [ ] The caveat is recorded on the bead itself; the mechanism is named in the skill.
- [ ] The 'write the handoff BEFORE the close' ordering rule is removed.
- [ ] `references/recovery.md`'s crash-resilient-close section is removed.

title: ADR: a plugin install script, and what belongs in it vs an onboarding agent
description:
Installing the sf plugin leaves repo-level setup undone, and the skills paper over it with rules that only hold where someone already did the work by hand. Three known cases: (1) the harness worktree directory must be gitignored or in-flight worktrees read as uncommitted work and a stop hook demands they be committed — .claude/worktrees/ is in THIS repo's .gitignore:41, which an install inherits nothing of; (2) the beads database bootstrap, whose failure modes are documented at length in CLAUDE.md precisely because nothing runs at install time; (3) the SessionStart hook, which Claude Code loads only from the project root, so a multi-root workspace never registers it — CLAUDE.md carries a manual fallback for exactly this.

Owner direction (2026-08-17): produce an ADR with an initial list of what an install script might need to do; an FRD follows later. The question the ADR must answer: HOW MUCH IS MECHANICAL (a script) VERSUS INSTRUCTIONS FOR AN ONBOARDING AGENT/SKILL?
design: The mechanical/agent split is the decision, not a detail. Appending gitignore lines is mechanical. Choosing a gate profile, or reconciling an existing AGENTS.md, is judgement. A script that attempts the judgement half produces wrong config silently; an agent that attempts the mechanical half is slower and less repeatable than a script and cannot be re-run idempotently in CI. Relates to the checkpoint-scripts ADR: if projects supply hook scripts, install-time scaffolding of those scripts is one of the mechanical items.
acceptance_criteria: ADR written per the spec skill, stating: the decision on mechanical vs agent-driven with rationale; an enumerated initial list of install-time actions with each classified; how the script is invoked and whether it is idempotent; and how it interacts with the SessionStart hook's project-root limitation. Names the follow-up FRD as out of scope.

title: ADR: project-supplied checkpoint scripts replace AGENTS.md gate parsing
description:
bead-bonanza recovers machine intent by regex-parsing prose in AGENTS.md: gate_cmd() in scripts/pre-flight-check.sh takes the first backticked span from a Markdown bullet. Measured on this repo's own AGENTS.md, the 'Test (full suite)' bullet has no backticked span (the command is a fenced bash block, because three checks must run independently rather than chained with &&), so the parser emits 'unparsed (no command in backticks)' and --gate-baseline records NO baseline for the one gate that is known-red. Write an ADR replacing the parsed gate profile with project-supplied checkpoint scripts.

Owner direction (2026-08-17): discovery via a .specs/hooks/<name> convention (plugin-level, not per-skill) OR optional fields in specs.toml referencing scripts by repo-root-relative path. Focus only on the load-bearing hooks AGENTS.md provides instructions for today: (a) a pre-flight check run as the last step of pre-flight, (b) a CI check run after every bead's implementation. The contract is likely guidelines agents use to help users write and check such scripts, rather than a rigid schema. Human readability is NOT a reason to keep the AGENTS.md block: it is the user's own script. An explicit goal is REDUCING AGENTS.md, which currently carries a lot of content applicable only when one skill runs.

---

**SUPERSEDED 2026-08-20 — both halves are delivered.**

The ADR this bead asked for exists: `specs/adrs/ADR-022-project-declared-checkpoint-scripts.md` (status: draft). The implementation is `agent-plugins-mknz`, which retired the AGENTS.md parser in favour of an executable `checks` script and took ADR-022's discovery decision — declaration in a plugin-scoped `sf.toml` — rather than the `.specs/hooks/<name>` convention floated in this bead's owner direction, which ADR-022 had already considered and rejected on `specs/` / `.specs/` confusability.

Two parts of ADR-022 are NOT yet implemented and carry their own beads rather than being lost here: `agent-plugins-1qc8.1` (the baseline must reach the subagent that runs the gate) and `agent-plugins-1qc8.2` (findings-with-paths, and whether `preflight` is a second checkpoint — or the ADR is amended).

title: The strata compiler is unavailable in a fresh session, so no schema change can be made
description:
MODEL (agent-plugins-wvd.1) begins by running scripts/generate-schemas.sh, which needs the strata compiler. In this session the compiler was never available: the SessionStart hook logged

  [session-start] cloning strata-lang/strata into /root/.cache/strata-src
  [session-start] WARNING: could not clone strata (see /root/.cache/strata-cli/build.log) — CLI unavailable

and every schema change on this branch was therefore authored WITHOUT
being compiled — which is exactly why agent-plugins-dc6 exists.

## What is not known

The underlying git error. The hook redirects it to
/root/.cache/strata-cli/build.log and prints only the summary line above;
that log was never read. Diagnosis has to start there.

Two facts narrow it. The line immediately above in the same hook run
reads 'verified write access to refs/dolt/*', so the PAT is present and
works against github.com for at least one push — this is not a plain
missing-token story. And strata-lang/strata is outside the GitHub scope
this session was granted, which is a plausible place for a brokered
credential to produce a 403 where the raw PAT would not.

## Steps to reproduce

Start a session and check for the compiler:
  command -v strata            # absent
  cat /root/.cache/strata-cli/build.log

## Why it is in this sprint

It is the first blocker in dependency order. MODEL is item 1 of 13 and
every other item depends on it, so an execution environment that cannot
compile a .strata file stalls the entire sprint at the first step. It is
also the reason feature.strata shipped uncompiled in the first place.
design: Read /root/.cache/strata-cli/build.log first. Then re-run the clone by hand with GIT_TRACE=1 and GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1 to get git's own stderr rather than the hook's summary, and check whether the request is going through the egress proxy — CLAUDE.md records that the proxy substitutes a brokered GitHub App token which 403s on paths the raw PAT can reach. Do not disable TLS verification or unset HTTPS_PROXY.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh session has a working strata compiler, or the failure is diagnosed and the fix is documented in docs/session-bootstrap.md and the SessionStart hook. scripts/generate-schemas.sh completes in a fresh session. The hook fails loudly rather than warning and continuing, matching how it already treats refs/dolt write access as a precondition.

metadata.tier_reason: an undiagnosed environment failure whose only evidence is an unread log, with a proxy/credential interaction that has already misled one full session

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
DIAGNOSED at bead-bonanza pre-flight, run 1786766873-20. The build log finally read; the error is not a missing token.

Verbatim, repeated for every clone attempt in ~/.cache/strata-cli/build.log:

  remote: Write access to repository not granted.
  fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/strata-lang/strata.git/': The requested URL returned error: 403

A WRITE-ACCESS error on a read-only clone. That is the signature CLAUDE.md
already documents for refs/dolt/*: the egress proxy substitutes a brokered
GitHub App token, and that token holds no grant for strata-lang/strata, so
even a fetch is refused with a write-shaped message. It is not the PAT — the
same session verified refs/dolt/* write access against github.com in the same
hook run.

Attaching the repo to the session was tried and is not available:

  add_repo strata-lang/strata -> cross-tier adds are not supported in v1:
  session already has repos from owner(s) [brettcallaghan]

So two remedies remain, and neither is reachable from inside a running
container:
  1. STRATA_ACCESS_TOKEN set on the ENVIRONMENT at container creation, per
     docs/session-bootstrap.md, so the hook's clone uses a credential the
     proxy does not replace. This is the same shape as AGENT_PLUGINS_ACCESS_TOKEN.
  2. Start the session with strata-lang/strata as an initial source, or point
     STRATA_SRC_DIR at a checkout that is already present.

Also still true and still worth fixing here: the hook WARNS and continues when
the clone fails, so a session silently proceeds with no compiler. That is how
schemas/feature.strata came to be authored and committed without ever being
compiled. The hook already treats refs/dolt write access as a hard precondition
and exits 1; it should treat the compiler the same way.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the previous comment, and the actual root cause — reproduced both ways.

The earlier comment blamed the egress proxy substituting a brokered token. That
is WRONG. The proxy bypass is already in effect: the hook sets
http.https://github.com/.proxy = '' globally at line 150, before the strata
clone at line 290, and 'git config --global --get http.https://github.com/.proxy'
confirms it is empty in a live session.

The real cause is credential-helper ordering. The Dolt block installs a GLOBAL
helper (line 148):

  git config --global credential.helper \
    '!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo "password=$AGENT_PLUGINS_ACCESS_TOKEN"; }; f'

It is unguarded: no [ "$1" = get ] check, no host check, no empty-token check.
It answers EVERY credential request for EVERY host. credential.helper is
multi-valued and git tries helpers in listed order — global before the
clone's own '-c' helper — so the strata clone authenticates with
AGENT_PLUGINS_ACCESS_TOKEN, a PAT scoped to brettcallaghan/agent-plugins with
no access to strata-lang/strata. GitHub answers 403 'Write access to repository
not granted'.

Measured in this container, same command, only the helper list differing:

  A) git clone --filter=blob:none -c "credential.helper=$H" <strata>
     -> remote: Write access to repository not granted.
        fatal: ... The requested URL returned error: 403

  B) git clone --filter=blob:none -c credential.helper= -c "credential.helper=$H" <strata>
     -> CLONE SUCCEEDED

The empty value in B resets the helper list so only the strata helper answers.

Nothing changed about STRATA_ACCESS_TOKEN. What changed is a neighbour:
  ae623c8 (#17) taught the strata clone to authenticate — worked.
  4443f24 (#19, 2026-08-12) 'the Dolt remote as the tracker' added the global
          helper, which now answers first.
The strata clone has been broken since #19 landed.

FIX (one line, in the strata clone at line 295 and its full-clone fallback at
298): add '-c credential.helper=' before the '-c credential.helper=$STRATA_CRED_HELPER'
argument, so the list is reset and only the strata helper answers for this clone.
The reassert at line 316 needs the same treatment.

Consider also hardening the Dolt helper itself — guard it with [ "$1" = get ]
and a host check — so it stops answering for repositories it has no business
authenticating. That is the general defect; the reset is the local fix.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: The failure message actively misled. GitHub answers a read-only clone with 'remote: Write access to repository not granted' plus 403 when the presented PAT simply cannot see the repo, which reads as a permissions-scope or proxy problem. I diagnosed it as the egress proxy first and recorded that on this bead before the reproduction disproved it. The distinguishing test is cheap and should be the first move next time: run the same clone with '-c credential.helper=' prepended, and if it succeeds the cause is helper ordering, not the proxy.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Two features that are each correct in isolation combined into a silent breakage. #17 taught the strata clone to authenticate; #19 added a GLOBAL credential helper for the Dolt remote that answers unconditionally for every host. Neither change is wrong on its own and neither mentions the other. The general defect is the unguarded global helper, not the strata clone: it will capture the credentials of the next private-repo clone too. Left unfixed here deliberately — the remote URL carries no .git suffix, so URL-scoping it risks breaking tracker sync, which is a precondition of this repository. Filed as follow-up rather than attempted under this bead.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Implicit decision — the bead's acceptance said the hook should 'fail loudly rather than warning and continuing'. Implemented as exit 1, mirroring BB_DOLT_FATAL, but gated on STRATA_CLI_SKIP being unset so a session that deliberately does no schema work still has a documented way in. Without that escape hatch a strata outage would lock every session out of the repository, which is a worse failure than the one being fixed.

title: AC-SPEC-009.1/.2 generate P1 regressions from correctness work; fix the requirement, not the code
description:
agent-plugins-uoe is the case that forces this. PR #14 made every generated model emit UnmarshalJSON — needed for the models to round-trip, and not going away. It cost warm-path p95 24.9ms -> 46.3ms locally, and on the ubuntu CI leg it crossed AC-SPEC-009.1's 50ms budget (bursts 82.2 -> 69.6 -> 52.5ms). That was filed as a P1 bug against the code.

It is the requirement that is wrong, not the code. A correctness-motivated change that costs milliseconds should not produce a P1 regression against an absolute number that names no hardware.

## What the requirement says now

specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md, FEAT-SPEC-009:
  AC-SPEC-009.1  corpus query, warm index, 1,000 documents: 50ms p95
  AC-SPEC-009.2  single-document check, warm index:        100ms p95
  AC-SPEC-009.3  cold index build:                          1s p95

None names the hardware it is stated against. agent-plugins-7ek already
records the consequence: macOS measured 69.1ms and Windows 123.6ms on
identical code, so TestWarmQueriesAndChecksMeetTheirBudgets in
cli/core/corpus/cache_test.go now enforces on Linux only via
referencePlatform() and reports elsewhere. That resolved the flake and
left the underlying question open.

## Decide

Pick one and amend the FRD:
  a. State a reference platform AND hardware class the absolute numbers
     hold on, and keep them gating there. Subsumes agent-plugins-7ek.
  b. Make the budget RELATIVE — no more than an X% regression against a
     recorded baseline — so a real regression still fails and a
     platform difference does not.
  c. Keep the numbers as advisory targets, tracked and reported but not
     gating, on the argument that no adopter has reported a latency
     problem and the measured margin on Linux is wide (13.7ms against 50).
  d. Raise the absolute numbers to a level that survives ordinary
     correctness work on a contended shared runner.

Whichever is chosen, the criteria are edited in place under adr-020 (FRDs
evolve in place; deltas keyed on AC identifiers), the enforcing test is
updated in the same change, and agent-plugins-uoe is closed by this
decision rather than by a code fix.

## Why it is in this sprint

MODEL adds Feature and Criterion to the same generator, so the sprint
adds more UnmarshalJSON to the warm read path. Under the current gate the
sprint can go red on a budget nobody intends to defend. Settle the
requirement before MODEL lands, not after.
design: Read agent-plugins-uoe's measurements and agent-plugins-7ek's cross-platform table first — between them they are the whole evidence base, and neither needs re-measuring. The decision is a spec judgement, not a benchmarking exercise.
acceptance_criteria: FEAT-SPEC-009's latency criteria state what they are measured against, or no longer gate. The FRD, cli/core/corpus/cache_test.go and any citing blueprint agree. agent-plugins-uoe is closed against this decision, and agent-plugins-7ek is closed or explicitly folded in.

metadata.tier_reason: a requirements judgement with four defensible answers and a CI gate riding on it; wrong call either over-constrains every future change or removes a real guard

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Gate baseline measured at bead-bonanza pre-flight, run 1786766873-20, on the untouched tree: format pass, lint pass, build pass. check-skills.sh --strict exits 1 with 0 errors and 1 warning (bead-bonanza/SKILL.md body size) — the known-red entry in AGENTS.md's ledger, unrelated to this bead.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Adopted option (c) — the three latency figures become advisory targets, measured and reported everywhere, gating only where an operator declares a reference environment (SPEC_LATENCY_REFERENCE_ENVIRONMENT). (a) was rejected because the margin a hardware class would preserve is ~4ms locally (46.3 against 50) and this sprint adds more UnmarshalJSON, so it would go red again within the sprint; (b) was rejected because a relative budget would still have flagged the 1.8x correctness change as a regression, which is the exact outcome this bead exists to stop; (d) was rejected as an unhardwared number chosen to survive noise.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Decided silently to extend the change to AC-SPEC-009.3 (cold build, 1s) and its two enforcing tests, though the bead names only .1/.2 — same class of unhardwared figure, same shared-runner exposure, and leaving one of three gating would have been a hybrid. Also decided silently that 'advisory' needed vocabulary rather than a marker: ac-traceability-standards defines only '(manual)', so inventing '(advisory)' would have changed a cross-cutting standard from inside a feature FRD. Instead Terminology gained 'latency target' and 'reference environment' and a new AC-SPEC-009.9 carries the measure-and-report obligation, which the three tests now cite.

comments.text: retro: Two things drifted out of the FRD's control and had to be corrected in the same change: referencePlatform() encoded the whole policy argument in a test comment (7ek's actual complaint) and is now deleted — the env-var declaration subsumes the GOOS check — and container-spec-cli's serve-mode Open Question asserted 'the measured margin against FEAT-SPEC-009.1 is wide', which stopped being true post-#14. The env var was renamed STRATA_ENFORCE_WARM_BUDGET -> SPEC_LATENCY_REFERENCE_ENVIRONMENT (nothing else referenced it; the old name said 'strata' in the spec CLI and 'warm' for a switch that now covers the cold build).

title: Definition of Ready and work-order template: require durable anchors, not line numbers (RFC B-P1)
description:
groom-beads groomed 17 beads that bead-bonanza then executed in one sprint over
a single skill bundle (run 1786562615-17). Fourteen of the seventeen cited
file:line positions in their Description or Design, and EVERY cited position had
moved by the time its bead was dispatched, because earlier beads in the same run
edited the same files. The sprint's own analysis calls this its dominant
friction.

Six beads recorded it independently, in their own words:

- b13: "the bead's cited line numbers (pre-flight-check.sh:269,:284,:455,
  :494-495; SKILL.md:1106-1113; bb-close-bead.sh:159-165) had all moved -- four
  earlier-sprint beads (q1h, td1, 9p4, 8mv) touched pre-flight-check.sh. Located
  each effect by content..."
- 8ef.1: "Every line number in the description is stale, as warned..."
- 8ef.2: "every line number in the description had moved, but every named
  passage was still findable by content... The offsets are roughly uniform
  (-72 lines...)"
- 8ef.3: "the bead's Category-D line-number citations were mostly stale, as
  warned."
- new: "Every line number in the Design was stale. recovery.md was 17,277 bytes
  / 251 lines, not 18,767 / 263 -- the cited ranges... all shifted."
- b5z: "Every cited line range was stale. Phase 2.5 was SKILL.md:494-726, not
  :559-818..."

The Definition of Ready asks for this at check 1: a Problem statement "SHALL
name concrete anchors -- file paths, function/class names, endpoints, tables,
user-facing behavior". A line number reads as the most concrete anchor
available, so a groomer reaching for concreteness reaches for it. The check does
not say that concreteness and durability are different properties.

Nothing was mis-edited, because the orchestrator improvised a mitigation -- it
added "locate by content, not by line number, and report the drift" to every
dispatch prompt. That is why this is a snag and not a blocker, but it was
per-run and unprescribed. The failure mode when it is NOT anticipated is not a
mis-edit; it is silence: an agent that trusts a stale range edits the wrong
region, or reports the cited content "already fixed" because what is at those
lines now is something else.

Source: rfcs/inbox/groom-beads/rfc-self-line-anchors-rot-across-a-sprint.md, P1.
Approved adopt-now at triage on 2026-08-13, widened per Design.
design:
## Extent -- this is TWO source files, not one

The RFC proposes changing only work-order-definition-of-ready.md. A triage
extent check (grep -rn 'concrete anchors' plugin/ specs/) found the phrase in
two spec-owned sources, each with vendored copies -- six files total:

  plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-definition-of-ready.md        (source)
  plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/shared/work-order-defin...       (vendored)
  plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/work-order-defin...        (vendored)
  plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md                   (source)
  plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/work-order-template.md     (vendored)
  plugin/skills/groom-feature-blueprint/references/shared/work-order-... (vendored)

In the DoR the phrase sits in check 1, under the heading "### 1. Self-contained
Problem statement (the fresh-agent test)", in the sentence beginning "It SHALL
name concrete anchors". In the template it sits in the `## Problem` instruction
block, in the sentence beginning "reads first, so it SHALL survive the
fresh-agent test -- name concrete anchors". Locate both by those phrases.

Changing the DoR alone leaves work-order-template.md telling an author to "name
concrete anchors (file paths, symbols, endpoints, tables, user-facing
behavior)" with no durability qualifier -- and the template is what an author
writes INTO, so it is read at least as often as the gate. Both sources change.

## 1. work-order-definition-of-ready.md, check 1 ("### 1. Self-contained Problem
statement (the fresh-agent test)")

After the existing "concrete anchors" sentence, add:

> An anchor SHALL be durable under edits to the same file. File paths, symbol
> names, headings and short quoted strings are durable; line numbers and line
> ranges are not, and neither are byte counts or item counts. WHERE a work order
> names a position, it SHALL name the content at that position -- quote the
> heading or the first few words -- and MAY give a line number only as a
> convenience alongside it. In a queue where several orders touch one file,
> every line number is stale before the second order is dispatched.

## 2. work-order-template.md, the Problem instruction block

Add a short durability clause to the "name concrete anchors" guidance -- quote
the content at a position, line numbers only alongside it. Keep it to a clause
or two; the template's instruction blocks are terse by convention and the full
rule belongs in the DoR.

## 3. Regenerate, never hand-edit, the vendored copies

The sources live in the spec skill. Run scripts/sync-shared-references.sh to
regenerate, then scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check to verify no drift.
Never edit a file under references/shared/ directly.

## Version bumps (this bead owns both)

- work-order-definition-of-ready.md frontmatter version 1.3 -> 1.4
- work-order-template.md instruction-block "Version: 1.4" -> 1.5 (this template
  versions in its instruction block, not in frontmatter)

Bump the SOURCES and let the regeneration carry the bumps into the vendored
copies.

- [ ] It requires naming the content at a position, permitting a line number only as a convenience alongside it

- [ ] Both changes were made to the spec-skill sources, not to any references/shared/ copy

title: bead-bonanza: chain each bead in a batch onto its predecessor's branch, not repo HEAD (RFC A-P2)
description:
The "## Shared batch preamble" block in
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/subagent-prompts.md instructs every batch
subagent, under the line beginning "Worktrees: one per bead, created by YOU,
held ONE AT A TIME. Before each bead:":

  git -C <repo> worktree add -b <suffix> <repo>/../.bb-worktrees/<suffix> HEAD

Repo HEAD advances only when the ORCHESTRATOR merges an accepted bead, and that
happens after the whole batch returns. So every bead in a batch branches from
the same commit and the beads cannot see each other's work.

This contradicts the worktree lifecycle in the same file, which states that
branching from HEAD -- "the sprint branch as it stands *now*, after the previous
bead merged" -- is what makes each bead build on the last. That rule is correct
for the SEQUENTIAL path it documents; the batch preamble's HEAD is not the HEAD
that rule means.

Observed in sprint run 1786562615-17: harmless in wave 1 (two beads; d6x rebased
cleanly onto txq). Wave 2A would have produced four conflicting branches on one
file -- q1h, td1, 9p4 and 8mv all edit scripts/pre-flight-check.sh. The
orchestrator detected it and overrode the template by hand with explicit
chaining (worktree add -b td1 <path> q1h) for every subsequent batch; all five
batches then merged as single fast-forwards.

It compounds with the merge invariant: SKILL.md's per-bead acceptance check
("The branch merged into the sprint branch. The merge is `--ff-only`") requires
that merge to be a fast-forward, and N branches off one base cannot all
fast-forward. The template as written cannot satisfy the skill's own merge rule
for any batch of two or more beads that touch a shared file.

Source: rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/rfc-self-report-citations-and-batch-base.md, P2.
Approved adopt-now at triage on 2026-08-13, with the refinements in Design.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Groom two or more beads that edit the same file (e.g. both edit
   scripts/pre-flight-check.sh) and bucket them into one shared-surface batch.
2. Dispatch the batch with the shared batch preamble from
   references/subagent-prompts.md as written.
3. Observe each bead's worktree is created with 'worktree add -b <id> <path>
   HEAD', and that HEAD is identical for every bead in the batch -- the
   orchestrator merges only after the batch returns.

Expected: each bead builds on the previous bead's work, and the batch merges
into the sprint branch as a single fast-forward, per SKILL.md's acceptance
check "The branch merged into the sprint branch. The merge is `--ff-only`".

Actual: every bead branches from the same commit, none can see the others'
work, and they conflict on the shared file. N branches off one base cannot all
fast-forward, so the merge invariant cannot be satisfied.

Observed in sprint run 1786562615-17, wave 2A: q1h, td1, 9p4 and 8mv all edit
scripts/pre-flight-check.sh and would have produced four conflicting branches.
The orchestrator detected it and overrode the template by hand.
design:
Two edits.

## 1. references/subagent-prompts.md, the "## Shared batch preamble" block

Replace the single worktree-creation line so the first bead branches from HEAD
and each later bead branches from its predecessor's branch:

> First bead: git -C <repo> worktree add -b <id-1> <path-1> HEAD
> Each later bead: git -C <repo> worktree add -b <id-N> <path-N> <id-N-1>
> -- branch from the PREVIOUS bead's branch, not from HEAD. Inside a batch HEAD
> does not move: the orchestrator merges only after the batch returns, so
> branching every bead from HEAD gives beads that cannot see each other's work
> and conflict on any shared file.

Keep the intent sentence. The orchestrator that overrode this template did so
because it understood the intent; one that does not will follow the literal
instruction.

## 2. SKILL.md, the paragraph beginning "**Merge policy.** The **orchestrator**
merges each bead's branch into the sprint branch as it is accepted"

Add one sentence: a chained batch is merged by fast-forwarding the LAST bead's
branch, which carries its predecessors -- not by merging each bead's branch in
turn. Without it the merge policy ("the orchestrator merges each bead's branch
into the sprint branch as it is accepted, one at a time") reads as N separate
merges, which contradicts chaining and cannot be --ff-only.

## Explicitly do NOT change the worktree-creation block in the lifecycle section

The RFC names a second worktree-creation line besides the batch preamble's. It
sits inside the section headed "### The worktree lifecycle -- create, dispatch,
merge, remove", which is the orchestrator-owned SEQUENTIAL per-bead path, where
the previous bead HAS merged and HEAD is therefore correct. It is the very
passage the RFC quotes approvingly as the right rule -- the paragraph beginning
"Branching from `HEAD` -- the sprint branch as it stands *now*, after the
previous bead merged". Changing it would break the sequential path. Locate both
blocks by their section headings, not by line number: an earlier bead in this
chain edits SKILL.md and this file's offsets shift as you work.

## Version bumps

Do NOT add a version property to references/subagent-prompts.md. All six of
bead-bonanza references (main-loop-fallback, operating-principles,
progress-streaming, project-setup, recovery, subagent-prompts) carry no
frontmatter and no version: this skill versions as a BUNDLE, and SKILL.md is
where that version lives. specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md requires
incrementing the SKILL version when normative content changes and imposes no
per-reference version; RFC A cited these files by git sha at b8b36d1, not by
file version, which is the bundle model working as intended. Adding one here
would leave a lone versioned file among six unversioned siblings.

This bead does NOT own the SKILL.md version bump; a later bead in this chain
does.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The block headed 'Shared batch preamble' in references/subagent-prompts.md instructs the first bead to branch from HEAD and every later bead to branch from the previous bead's branch
- [ ] The instruction carries the intent sentence explaining that HEAD does not move inside a batch
- [ ] The worktree-creation block inside the section headed 'The worktree lifecycle -- create, dispatch, merge, remove' still branches from HEAD and is unchanged
- [ ] SKILL.md's merge policy states that a chained batch is merged by fast-forwarding the last bead's branch, which carries its predecessors
- [ ] No version property was added to references/subagent-prompts.md; it and its five sibling references remain unversioned, per the skill's bundle-versioning convention
- [ ] plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md frontmatter version is NOT bumped by this bead

title: bead-bonanza Phase 4: number harvested findings per bead so citations can resolve (RFC A-P1a)
description:
Phase 4's sprint-report step requires the report to cite its evidence, and
specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md requires it generally: where a skill's
workflow ends in a report to a human, that step "SHALL require every factual
claim to cite the artifact it derives from", and citation is "mechanically
checkable: a sentence either names its source or it does not."

The report complies in form and fails in substance. Sprint run 1786562615-17
(epic agent-plugins-41z, 17 beads, 73 findings) produced
rfcs/sprints/2026-08-12-bead-bonanza-hardening.md, whose analysis cites findings
by a GLOBALLY sequential number -- "(finding 15)", "(findings 29, 30)". Every
citation in it points at a finding belonging to a different bead than the claim
is about. Two confirmed by hand at triage:

- The report says "8ef.1 promises eighteen rules and names fourteen (finding
  15)". Finding 15 belongs to q1h and reads "decided silently -- gave the moved
  probe its own numbered section...". The finding that actually says it is 37.
- The report says "x8r shipped out1-out4 in its close commit (finding 63)".
  Finding 63 belongs to b5z and reads "Every cited line range was stale. Phase
  2.5 was SKILL.md:494-726...". The correct finding is 73.

The failure is structural, not clerical. A global counter is assigned only once
all beads' findings are concatenated, while the analysis is written per theme --
so the author is citing a number that does not exist until the document is
assembled. That every citation is wrong, rather than a scattered few, is what
that looks like, and it is why "be careful" is not the fix.

Consequence: the report is the run's only durable evidence record, triage-rfc
defers on recurrence and therefore reads these findings across runs, and a
reader who follows a citation lands on unrelated text.

Source: rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/rfc-self-report-citations-and-batch-base.md, P1
(first half). Approved adopt-now at triage on 2026-08-13.
design:
In Phase 4's sprint-report step in plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md (the
"Write one sprint report per run" paragraph and the surrounding retro
specification), require harvested findings to be numbered PER BEAD rather than
globally: 8ef.1#3, x8r#1.

Why per-bead: the id is stable at the moment the finding is harvested, so a
claim can cite it while the analysis is being written rather than after the
document is assembled. That removes the cause rather than asking for more care.

The report already groups verbatim findings under "### `agent-plugins-<id>`"
headings, so the per-bead ordinal is well-defined by position within its
heading and needs no separate bookkeeping.

State the citation form explicitly so it is mechanically recognisable -- a
bead id, "#", and the ordinal -- because a downstream checker keys on it. Do NOT
add the checker in this bead; it is held for human review as A-P1b and depends
on this id scheme existing.

Do not change what the report contains (every finding verbatim, including the
tail that warrants no RFC) -- only how findings are identified and cited.

This bead does NOT own the SKILL.md version bump: two further approved
proposals edit the same file and the bump belongs to whichever lands last.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Phase 4's report step in plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md requires harvested findings to be numbered per bead, not globally
- [ ] The citation form is stated explicitly as <bead-id>#<ordinal> (e.g. 8ef.1#3) so it is mechanically recognisable
- [ ] The rationale is stated in one sentence: a per-bead id is stable at harvest time, a global one does not exist until the document is assembled
- [ ] The report's existing contents requirement (every harvested finding verbatim, including the tail warranting no RFC) is unchanged
- [ ] No citation-checking script is added in this bead
- [ ] plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md frontmatter version is NOT bumped by this bead

title: work-order is not in the DocumentType vocabulary, so the output of the only complete flow is unmodeled
description:
plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md declares `type: work-order`. The DocumentType enum in cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json has 11 values (adr, frd, contract, standards, the five blueprint kinds, rfc, guide) and work-order is not among them, so there is no definition to validate a work order against.

Consequence: work orders are the output artifact of the greenfield feature -> work orders flow, and no gate can check one. A document declaring the type is recorded as excluded with reason unknown-type rather than checked.

Decide whether work-order joins the vocabulary as a document type (it has frontmatter shaped like one: title, description, slug, type, kind, priority, updated_at, sources) or whether work orders are deliberately outside the corpus, in which case work-order-template.md should not declare a `type` that looks like a corpus type.

Note the template also fails frontmatter parse independently (mapping value is not allowed in this context, at line 28), which is worth fixing whichever way the modelling question lands.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
scripts/check-template-drift.py
```

Expected: no finding against plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md.

Actual: `template/unknown-type: work-order is not in the DocumentType
vocabulary (adr, component-blueprint, container-blueprint, contract,
feature-blueprint, frd, guide, module-blueprint, rfc, standards,
system-blueprint)`.

Second, independent fault in the same file — the frontmatter does not parse:

```
python3 -c "import yaml,io;yaml.safe_load(open('plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md').read().split('---')[1])"
```

Expected: parses. Actual: `mapping value is not allowed in this context`,
from the unquoted `:` inside the tier_reason placeholder at line 28.

Manifests in: plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md, and its
two vendored copies under groom-beads and groom-feature-blueprint.
design:
DECIDED 2026-08-12 by the owner: option (b) — work orders are outside the corpus TODAY. Do not add `work-order` to the DocumentType vocabulary.

Rationale to record in the change: a work order materializes into a tracker issue (a bead) and then stops existing as a document. Corpus membership implies a document that persists, is cited by slug, and appears in the index; a work order does none of those. groom-beads carries its own references/bead.schema.json for that materialization, which is where a work orders shape is actually governed.

REVISIT CONDITION, stated by the owner and to be recorded in the change so this is not re-litigated blindly: this may change for environments that do NOT use beads, where work orders would persist as files rather than being materialized into a tracker. Leave the door open — prefer the smallest edit that stops the false claim, not a redesign.

Three edits.

1. STOP DECLARING A CORPUS TYPE. plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md declares `type: work-order`, which matches no DocumentType and so claims corpus membership it does not have. Remove the `type` property. Do not substitute a real corpus type — a work order is not an adr/frd/standards document.

2. FIX THE FRONTMATTER PARSE FAILURE. Independent of the modelling question and needed either way: line 28 reads
     tier_reason: <one line: what about this order drove the tier choice>
   The unquoted `:` inside the placeholder makes the YAML invalid ("mapping value is not allowed in this context"). Quote the value, or reword the placeholder to remove the colon. Check the whole block for the same fault rather than only line 28.

3. TEACH THE DRIFT CHECK. With the type gone, scripts/check-template-drift.py reports `template/no-type` against this file; with the type present it reports `template/unknown-type`. Neither is a defect once (b) is decided, so the check must stop flagging it.

   Chosen: a named exclusion in check-template-drift.py, in the same explicit style as its existing SEARCH comment about references/shared/ — a short constant listing this file with the reason "materializes into a tracker issue, not a corpus document". Reversible in one line if the revisit condition above ever fires.

   Rejected: giving the check a general notion of non-corpus templates, or adding a `corpus: false` frontmatter marker. Both invent vocabulary for a single instance of a question the owner has flagged as possibly temporary.

VENDORED — scripts/sync-shared-references.sh lines 58 and 62 map work-order-template.md into groom-beads and groom-feature-blueprint. After editing the source, run scripts/sync-shared-references.sh (no --check) and commit all three files. CI runs --check and fails on a stale copy.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] work-order-template.md declares no `type` property
- [ ] Its frontmatter parses as valid YAML
- [ ] The change records why work orders are outside the corpus, and the revisit condition for non-beads environments
- [ ] `work-order` is NOT added to the DocumentType vocabulary or the schema
- [ ] scripts/check-template-drift.py reports no finding against work-order-template.md, and its exclusion states the reason
- [ ] Both vendored copies under groom-beads and groom-feature-blueprint are regenerated and committed
- [ ] scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check exits 0
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0

metadata.tier_reason: decision supplied and edits are small, but they span a source template, two vendored copies and a gate script, and the revisit condition must survive in the record

title: retro-spec's rfc-template.md has drifted from the Rfc schema and from every RFC authored
description:
plugin/skills/retro-spec/references/rfc-template.md declares six fewer properties than the Rfc definition in cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json requires, and declares one the model does not define.

Missing required: effort, model, runs_observed, severity, skill, skill_version.
Not in schema: audience.

plugin/skills/retro-spec/SKILL.md:149 instructs agents to file a qualifying finding as `audience: project`, and SKILL.md:159 refers to an `audience: skill-authors` RFC.

Measured against the corpus: of 28 documents under rfcs/ declaring `type: rfc`, 28 carry `skill:` and 0 carry `audience:`. The authored documents follow the schema; the template and the skill instructions do not.

Three artifacts disagree — the schema, the template, and SKILL.md — and nothing in the repository detects it. Deciding which is stale is the work: either `audience` is a legitimate concept the model is missing (the skill distinguishes project RFCs from skill-authors RFCs and the model has no way to say so), or it was abandoned and two files were left behind.

Found while assessing whether the Spec CLI could replace scripts/validate-corpus.py. Neither gate covers templates: validate-corpus.py skips any filename containing "template", and templates sit outside the CLI corpus root.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
scripts/check-template-drift.py
```

Expected: no finding against plugin/skills/retro-spec/references/rfc-template.md.

Actual: seven findings — six `template/missing-required` (effort, model,
runs_observed, severity, skill, skill_version) and one
`template/unknown-property` (audience).

Corroborating measurement, showing the authored documents follow the schema
and the template does not:

```
for f in $(find rfcs -name '*.md'); do head -25 "$f" | grep -q '^type: rfc' \

title: Split recovery.md by read-probability and extract orchestrator-resume into a private skill a fresh session can invoke by name
description:
TWO CHANGES IN ONE FILE. The split is the larger measurable win; the skill is the correctness fix.

THE SPLIT (~14,000 bytes saved on the ~90% path). references/recovery.md is 18,767 bytes and is read as one unit, but it is three documents with three different probabilities:
  • orchestrator crash / context loss — resuming a run: :24-150, 7,210 bytes, read on ~10% of runs
  • subagent crash / mid-step timeout: :151-171, 4,385 bytes, ~20%
  • mid-stream visibility and the durable trigger: :172-250, 4,704 bytes, ~90%
  • crash-resilient close: :251-263, 1,469 bytes, ~0% — already restated at SKILL.md:252-256 and subagent-prompts.md:93-98, and deletes wholesale

SKILL.md:243-245 triggers a read of the whole file for 'any subagent expected to run past 5 minutes — any non-trivial bead, given full test runs', i.e. nearly every run. Today that costs 18,767 bytes to obtain the 4,704 bytes of Monitor and durable-trigger guidance. Splitting is a reference-file change requiring no new mechanism.

THE SKILL (orchestrator-resume only, 7,210 bytes). Justified by REACHABILITY, not tokens. recovery.md:232-236 already requires the durable trigger's message to be 'self-contained — carry the RUN_DIR path, the epic id, and an instruction to run this file's orchestrator-recovery procedure.' A trigger firing into a FRESH SESSION cannot say 'read references/recovery.md': that agent has no bundle loaded and no path to resolve. It can say 'invoke recover-sprint'. The same argument covers the post-compaction case at SKILL.md:25-31 — a skill name is a more robust handle after truncation than a relative path.

DO NOT make the other two pieces skills. They are read by a live orchestrator that already holds the bundle; a skill buys them nothing and costs a permanent description.
design:
INTERFACE for recover-sprint. In: nothing required — that is the point. Optionally RUN_DIR, run id, branch. Out: the reconstructed run state (branch, completed set from git log, in-flight set from git worktree list, per-bead classification) plus an explicit statement of which source each fact came from, per recovery.md:148-150.

KEEP IN BOTH PLACES, deliberately: 'git worktree prune before git worktree list' and 'the live run directory is authoritative; a snapshot never is'. A recovering orchestrator enters at the recovery document with no memory and will not have read the worktree section or the snapshot-writing rule.

Coordinate with the redundancy epic: recovery.md:251-262 is also listed for deletion there, and recovery.md:160 carries a live data-loss defect tracked as agent-plugins-0z0. Whichever lands first should take those lines.
acceptance_criteria:
1. recovery.md is split so the Monitor/durable-trigger guidance can be read without loading the crash procedures.
2. SKILL.md's past-5-minutes trigger points at the small file, not the whole corpus.
3. A recover-sprint skill exists with user-invocable: false and reconstructs run state with no prior context.
4. The durable trigger's message names the skill rather than a file path.
5. Facts in the reconstructed state name the source they were read from.

metadata.tier_reason: file surgery plus a new skill plus a reachability contract for a fresh session with no bundle loaded; splitting wrongly costs recovery correctness

title: Deduplicate SKILL.md against itself and trim rationale prose the repo's own standard bans
description:
Categories B, C and F of the redundancy analysis: ~10,900 characters, all inside SKILL.md except where noted.

WITHIN-SKILL.md duplication (~5,772):
  • B1 the under-/over-routing asymmetry, 4x: :871-879, :891-894, :923-927, :1055-1058. Canonical: :871-879. ~800
  • B11 Monitor + durable trigger, 3-4x: :236-249, :1028-1035, :906-909 (canonical lives in recovery.md:213-249). ~700
  • B10 concurrent-wave entry conditions 3x: :622-641, :675-680, plus subagent-prompts.md:355-367. ~600
  • B4 the mid-run scope test 2x: :506-554 and :1066-1078. ~550
  • B7 targeted tests non-negotiable 4x — cut only the SKILL.md copies, never the two prompt copies. ~400
  • B2 CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL 2x, B3 main-loop fallback 2x, B5 groom-before-dispatch 2x, B6 bias-toward-batching 2x, B9 red-before-green 2x, B12 circuit breaker 2x, B13, B14. ~2,370
  • B15 :63-67 'How this document is ordered' — an account of a past reorganization ('out of numeric order. Phase numbers are unchanged'). Keep at most the first clause. ~352

RATIONALE / HISTORICAL PROSE (~4,790). CLAUDE.md's 'Historical prose: don't' applies, and its test is: would a reader who has never seen this project's history behave differently for having read this sentence? Offenders include SKILL.md:860-869 (~700, re-argues a rule stated at :850-859), :403-411 (~300 — narrates THIS repository's SessionStart-hook history inside an exported skill, which also breaks skill self-containment), :290-296 (~450), :1104-1109 (~300), :965-978 (~350), :143-168 (~450), :634-641 (~330), plus dispatch-plan.md:117-136 (~690) and subagent-prompts.md:217 (~278).

COUNTS STATED BESIDE THEIR OWN ENUMERATION (~150, and a maintenance hazard beyond the bytes — adding an item makes the prose lie). specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md:421 forbids these. Confirmed at SKILL.md:170 'five signals', :238 'Three things', :260 'The four dispatch prompts', :290 'The five scripts/ entries', :391 'Two things', :516 'Three shapes', :796 'Three of its rules', :946 'Answer four questions', plus scripts/bb-close-bead.sh:7 and recovery.md:15.

One count could not be verified and should be checked rather than assumed: SKILL.md:294 'pre-flight's ten probes across two platforms' — the script has nine numbered sections, the ninth being a verdict rather than a probe.
design:
Three passes over one file, in this order, because each makes the next easier to see.

PASS 1 — within-file duplication (category B). The description lists each rule with every line range it occupies and names the canonical one. Delete the others. B1 (the under-/over-routing asymmetry, four times) is the largest single win and the clearest: keep SKILL.md:871-879, delete the three restatements.

PASS 2 — rationale prose (category C). Apply CLAUDE.md's test literally, sentence by sentence: would a reader who has never seen this project's history behave differently for having read this? If no, delete. Keep the three narrow exceptions CLAUDE.md allows — a rule that looks removable but is not, a trap with a plausible wrong answer, and a non-obvious measured constraint — but state them as current fact, never as a discovery narrative. SKILL.md:403-411 is the clearest offender: it narrates THIS repository's SessionStart-hook history inside a skill that ships to other projects.

PASS 3 — counts (category F2). Drop the numeral, keep the enumeration.

GUARDRAIL. This bead deletes more prose than any other in the epic, in the file with the least margin for error. Before deleting any passage, confirm the rule it carries survives somewhere. The keep-list in the epic's design is binding: SKILL.md:25-31's post-compaction instruction is redundant BY DESIGN and stays; the published script usage block duplicates the script headers BY DESIGN and stays.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Each rule listed in category B appears once in SKILL.md.
2. No sentence in SKILL.md narrates how a rule came to exist, per CLAUDE.md's test.
3. No count is stated adjacent to the enumeration it counts.
4. SKILL.md:294's 'ten probes' claim is either corrected against the script or restated without a count.
5. SKILL.md:25-31 and the published script usage block are unchanged.
6. Every rule present before the change is still stated somewhere in the bundle.

title: Deduplicate rules stated in both SKILL.md and a reference file, choosing one canonical location each
description:
Category A of the redundancy analysis: ~12,700 characters. Eighteen rules are stated in SKILL.md and again in one or more reference files, several at full length in both.

The larger ones, with the canonical location the analysis recommends:
  • A1 base-ref gate 3x — SKILL.md:100-111, :413-417, subagent-prompts.md:237-255. Canonical: subagent-prompts.md:237-269 (it alone carries the remedy JSON). ~1,050
  • A5 handoff-file rule 4x — SKILL.md:251-256, subagent-prompts.md:93-98, recovery.md:157, recovery.md:251-262. Canonical: subagent-prompts.md:93-98 for the write, recovery.md:156-164 for the read. recovery.md:251-262 deletes wholesale. ~1,570
  • A7 bb-backup-run.sh 4x — SKILL.md:212-226, :343-356, :1124-1129, recovery.md:50-77. Canonical: SKILL.md:343-356. ~1,400
  • A6 bb-close-bead.sh 5x — SKILL.md:327-342, :1118-1123, subagent-prompts.md:103-107, recovery.md:159, :257. Canonical: SKILL.md:327-342. ~1,300
  • A2 merge policy 2x at full length — SKILL.md:113-127 vs subagent-prompts.md:306-334. Canonical: the latter. ~800
  • A3 worktree location/removal/prune 4x. Canonical: subagent-prompts.md:283-353. ~700
  • A11 findings harvest 3x. Canonical: operating-principles.md:40-94. ~700
  • A13 foreign dirt / tracker writes 3x. Canonical: operating-principles.md:96-131. ~600
  • A4 'bd is not an obstacle' 3x. Canonical: subagent-prompts.md:271-281. ~500
  • A8 'the plan names beads, never a filter' 3x. Canonical: dispatch-plan.md:57-61. ~500
  • A17 Definition-of-Ready restated at SKILL.md:457-476 in defiance of :451-455's own instruction not to. ~500
  • A9 Amendments rule 2x, A10 'every run gets a plan' 3x, A14-A16, A18 reference-header routing. ~2,080

CARRY-OVERS that look like duplicates and are NOT (do not cut these):
  • The per-wave cadence clause on the base-ref gate must survive IN SKILL.md at the point waves are dispatched — the orchestrator may never reopen subagent-prompts.md between waves.
  • 'git worktree prune before git worktree list' must stay in BOTH recovery.md and pre-flight's description: recovery is entered by an orchestrator with no memory that will not have read the worktree section.
  • 'The live run directory is authoritative; a snapshot never is' stays in both SKILL.md:353-356 (governs writing) and recovery.md:62-68 (governs reading, and a recovering orchestrator enters there).
design:
Work file-pair by file-pair, not rule-by-rule, so each decision is made once with both texts in view.

METHOD. For each of the eighteen rules listed in the description: open both locations, pick the canonical one (the description names a recommendation for each — follow it unless the texts show it is wrong, and say so in the retro if you deviate), leave the full statement there, and at the other site either delete outright or leave a one-line pointer where a reader arriving cold would otherwise be stranded.

THE TEST for pointer-vs-delete: who arrives at this file, and have they read the other one? A reader entering references/recovery.md after a crash has read nothing else — they need the statement or a pointer. A reader in SKILL.md's Phase 3 already has the bundle and can be pointed.

DO NOT compress prose to save bytes. specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md:151-155 is explicit that extraction beats compression because compression loses the specificity that makes guidance followable. Every byte in this bead comes from deleting a SECOND statement of something, never from tightening a first.

Three carry-overs are named in the description and are not negotiable — the per-wave cadence clause, the prune instruction in both places, and the authoritative-run-directory rule in both places.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Each of the eighteen rules is stated in full exactly once across the bundle.
2. For each rule, a reader entering the non-canonical file cold can still reach the statement — by pointer where they would otherwise be stranded.
3. The three named carry-overs remain present in both their locations.
4. No table of contents was modified.
5. No rule was removed from inside a fenced dispatch-prompt template.
6. scripts/check-skills.sh reports a smaller SKILL.md body than before the change.

metadata.tier_reason: eighteen rules deduplicated across six files, each needing a judgment about which location is canonical, with a hard constraint that no rule may be lost; high blast radius over the whole bundle

title: Cut bead-bonanza's redundancy: ~28,300 characters of restatement, no rule lost
description:
Successor to the closed agent-plugins-8ef, which was closed by user decision to be revisited in a dedicated analysis round. This is that round's output.

SKILL.md body is 65,451 bytes (~16,362 tokens) against scripts/check-skills.sh's BODY_BYTE_MAX of 20,000 (the ~5,000-token post-compaction re-injection cap) and specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md:140's softer 40,000-character budget. The editable bundle (SKILL.md plus references/, excluding the generated shared/ copy) is 131,424 characters.

NEW INFORMATION SINCE 8ef. 8ef's close note concluded 'extraction alone tops out near 24,000 bytes of savings' and 'fitting under the cap is a rewrite, not an extraction'. That assessment measured extraction only. A separate pass measured DEDUPLICATION — rules stated two, three, four and five times across the bundle — at ~28,300 characters, of which ~18,400 is in SKILL.md itself (a 28% cut to the body). This is additive to extraction and was not counted in 8ef.

Worst offenders, all verified with file:line ranges:
  • the handoff-file rule, 4x — including references/recovery.md:251-262, an entire section restating a rule AND re-listing four recovery steps given verbatim 90 lines earlier
  • bb-close-bead.sh's behaviour described 5x
  • bb-backup-run.sh described 4x
  • the under-/over-routing asymmetry 4x within SKILL.md alone
  • the worktree base-ref gate 3x
  • SKILL.md:451-455 says 'do not restate the checklist here' and SKILL.md:457-476 then restates six of the nine Definition-of-Ready checks

Every finding names a surviving canonical location. No rule is deleted — only its duplicate statements.
design:

Where a rule appears both in SKILL.md and inside a fenced template in references/subagent-prompts.md, cut the SKILL.md copy and never the template copy. The published script usage block duplicates each script's own header by design, because the skill forbids opening the scripts to learn an interface. The generated references/shared/ copy is not editable here.

4. SHARED SURFACE. Every child bead touches SKILL.md or a file another child also touches. These MUST run as one shared-surface batch or strictly sequentially — never as a concurrent worktree wave. Dispatching them concurrently will produce conflicting edits to the same regions.

title: SKILL.md calls worktree.baseRef a 'Hard gate ... both are checked'; pre-flight-check.sh calls it 'advisory, never blocking'
description:
Direct contradiction between the skill and its own script.

SKILL.md:100-101: 'Hard gate — every worktree must branch from the sprint's own branch, never the default branch. Two conditions produce that, and both are checked'. references/subagent-prompts.md:239-240 repeats it.

scripts/pre-flight-check.sh:396 comment: '# worktree.baseRef — advisory, never blocking.' Line 407 prints 'worktree.baseRef: $WORKTREE_BASEREF (advisory)'. Only the other condition (HEAD != default branch) calls block(), at line 344.

The script's stated reason for advisory status — 'Most runs never dispatch a worktree wave' — is stale. SKILL.md:69 says every bead runs in its own worktree: 'This is universal, not opt-in.'

Consequence when baseRef is unset: each worktree branches from the default branch instead of session HEAD, so every bead silently loses every commit the sprint branch carries, including beads that landed earlier in the same run. The wave completes and merges garbage; nothing errors.

This is the second instance of the same defect class as the BB_DOLT_WRITE bead: prose is load-bearing precisely because the script declined to gate.

## Steps to Reproduce

From the repository root, read the two claims side by side:

    sed -n '100,101p' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md
    sed -n '396p;407p' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh
    grep -n 'block' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh | sed -n '1,20p'

EXPECTED: if SKILL.md calls this a hard gate whose two conditions are 'both checked', both conditions call block().
ACTUAL: only the HEAD-vs-default-branch condition blocks (line 344). The baseRef condition is commented 'advisory, never blocking' and prints '(advisory)'.
design:
DECIDED: make it block. Do not treat this as a choice at implementation time.

The remedy text is already written and printed at scripts/pre-flight-check.sh:409-411; promote that path from say() to block() and let the script exit non-zero.

Rejected alternative, recorded so it is not re-litigated: leaving the check advisory and instead deleting 'and both are checked' from SKILL.md:101 and subagent-prompts.md:240. Rejected because the consequence of an unset baseRef is silent and total — each worktree branches from the default branch, so every bead loses every commit the sprint branch carries, and the wave still completes and merges. A condition that destroys work silently is exactly what a gate is for; documenting it as advisory only makes the documents honest about a weak check rather than making the check strong.

CADENCE CONSTRAINT, which the script cannot own. worktree.baseRef is user-scope global state readable from $HOME/.claude/settings.json and can change mid-run. The gate must therefore be re-run before the first worktree of EVERY wave, not once per run. A per-invocation script cannot enforce its own re-invocation, so that cadence sentence stays stated in SKILL.md — it is the one part of this rule that remains prose by necessity.
acceptance_criteria:
1. pre-flight-check.sh exits non-zero when worktree.baseRef is not 'head'.
2. No file in plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/ describes the check as advisory while another calls it a hard gate.
3. The per-wave re-run cadence is stated exactly once, in SKILL.md.
notes:
SHARED SURFACE. This bead edits plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh, and so do agent-plugins-q1h, agent-plugins-9p4, agent-plugins-8mv and agent-plugins-b13. Dispatch these four as ONE shared-surface batch, or strictly sequentially. They must NOT go into a concurrent worktree wave: all four touch the same regions of one file and would produce conflicting edits.

They are deliberately left unchained by dependencies so a batch remains possible.

metadata.tier_reason: one say()->block() promotion plus a cadence sentence in SKILL.md; low ambiguity but it changes a gate that can halt a run

title: pre-flight-check.sh measures BB_DOLT_WRITE after the verdict, so a container that cannot write refs/dolt/* is told 'safe to proceed'
description:
SKILL.md:403 states: 'BB_DOLT_WRITE is a blocking fact where it reads no. Stop and fix the environment; do not run and hope.'

The script does not implement that. scripts/pre-flight-check.sh computes DOLT_WRITE at lines 491-500, which is AFTER the verdict block at lines 470-478 and after REPORT_FAIL is final. It never calls block(). The script ends 'exit $REPORT_FAIL' at line 527, and REPORT_FAIL is untouched by the Dolt probe.

Consequence: a container that cannot write refs/dolt/data gets exit 0 and the message 'OK — safe to proceed to Phase 1'. Every bead the run closes then dies with the container — the exact loss the close ceremony exists to prevent, and the repository deliberately provides no JSONL fallback.

Violates specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md:289 'A bundled script SHALL exit non-zero when a check it performs does not pass', whose rationale names this shape: 'A gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate: it launders an unverified condition as a verified one.'

## Steps to Reproduce

From the repository root:

    sed -n '470,478p;491,500p;527p' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh

Observe that the verdict block and 'exit $REPORT_FAIL' both precede the DOLT_WRITE computation, and that no block() call appears between them:

    awk 'NR>=470 && NR<=527 && /block|REPORT_FAIL|DOLT_WRITE/' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh

EXPECTED: a container without refs/dolt/* write access exits non-zero and is named in the BLOCKED list.
ACTUAL: DOLT_WRITE is computed after the exit status is final; the script exits 0 and prints 'OK — safe to proceed to Phase 1'.
design: Move the DOLT_WRITE probe above the verdict block and call block() when it reads 'no'. The blocker text should carry the measurement (the probe command and its failure), the consequence in one sentence, the fix, and the re-check — see the failure-output pattern bead in this set.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A container without refs/dolt/* write access causes pre-flight-check.sh to exit non-zero.
2. The BLOCKED list names the tracker-durability failure.
3. The probe runs before the verdict block, verified by line order.
4. SKILL.md's claim that BB_DOLT_WRITE=no is blocking is now true of the script.
notes:

Dispatch these four as ONE shared-surface batch, or strictly sequentially. They must NOT go into a concurrent worktree wave: all four touch the same regions of one file and would produce conflicting edits.

They are deliberately left unchained by dependencies so a batch remains possible.

title: bd bootstrap never clones the tracker: sync.remote in config.yaml is rejected as a git URL and bootstrap still exits 0
description:
A session that bootstraps this repo gets a tracker that is NOT the remote, silently.

Measured 2026-08-12 with bd 1.2.1, in a fresh container and reproduced in a clean scratch clone:

    $ bd bootstrap --dry-run
    error: sync.remote "git+https://github.com/brettcallaghan/agent-plugins" looks
    like a git code-repository URL, not a Dolt remote — skipping clone
    ✓ Database already exists: /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads
      Nothing to do.

Two faults compound. bd rejects the sync.remote value in .beads/config.yaml as not-a-Dolt-remote and skips the clone; then its 'database already exists' probe matches the .beads DIRECTORY rather than a database, so it reports nothing to do even with no database present (verified after rm -rf .beads/embeddeddolt). It exits 0 either way, so the SessionStart hook's 'bd bootstrap >/dev/null 2>&1' sees success and logs nothing.

Consequence measured this session: the local tracker held 112 issues against the remote's 165 — an exact import of .beads/issues.jsonl as committed at ae623c8, three days stale. 54 beads were invisible, 14 shared beads were behind, and 4 beads already closed on the remote (34g, 8ef, ht3, jh6) were offered by 'bd ready' as available work.

Deleting the sync: block makes bootstrap clone from the IDENTICAL url, which it then reads from metadata.json:

    Bootstrap plan: clone from remote
      Remote: git+https://github.com/brettcallaghan/agent-plugins
      Database: spec_driven_dev

So the URL is fine and only the config.yaml validation path rejects it.
design:
Two candidate fixes, in preference order:

1. Configure the Dolt remote where bd accepts it (bd dolt remote add / metadata.json) and drop sync.remote from config.yaml, keeping the prose that explains why the shared https URL is required.
2. Keep sync.remote and fix bd's validator to accept a git+https:// URL, upstream.

Independently, the hook must stop trusting bootstrap's exit status: assert a non-empty database afterwards (bd stats, or a row count) and treat 'cloned nothing' as fatal, the way the refs/dolt write probe already does.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A fresh container's tracker matches refs/dolt/data on issue count and ids, verified by comparing bd export against a scratch clone bootstrapped from the remote.
- [ ] bd bootstrap in a clone with no database either clones or fails non-zero; it never reports 'nothing to do'.
- [ ] The SessionStart hook fails loudly when the post-bootstrap database is empty or absent.
notes:
REPRODUCED AND WORKED AROUND 2026-08-12, in a session that had already diverged. Adds a third fault and a working recovery path.

REPRODUCTION matched the bead exactly: 'bd dolt pull' reported 'Local and remote Dolt histories have diverged ... no common merge base'. Local held 111 issues (newest updated_at 2026-08-09); the remote's refs/dolt/data had been pushed the same day at 16:46 and held 167. Epic agent-plugins-92q and its 27 children existed only on the remote.

THIRD FAULT, not in the bead: metadata.json can point at a DIFFERENT Dolt database name than the remote's. Local .beads/metadata.json read dolt_database: "spec_driven_dev"; the remote clone's read "beads". After swapping in the remote database, 'bd stats' reported 0 issues and SILENTLY CREATED an empty spec_driven_dev database rather than reporting the mismatch. This is the same second-namespace hazard CLAUDE.md documents for issue_prefix, but on the database name, and it is equally silent.

RECOVERY PATH THAT WORKED, without force-pushing or losing anything:
  1. Back up .beads and 'bd export' the local issues first.
  2. Bootstrap the REMOTE into a scratch git repo that has origin set and refs/dolt/* fetched. bd bootstrap succeeds there because no .beads directory exists yet — the 'already exists' probe is what blocks it in the real repo.
  3. Diff the id sets. Here local was a STRICT SUBSET: 0 local-only, 56 remote-only. That made the choice safe and evidence-based rather than a guess.
  4. Copy the scratch clone's .beads/embeddeddolt into the real repo and set metadata.json's dolt_database to match.
  5. Verify with bd stats and a real 'bd dolt push'.

The diff in step 3 is the part worth keeping in any fix: 'discard local' and 'overwrite remote' are both destructive, and the id-set comparison is what turns the choice into a measurement.

---

RECURRED AGAIN 2026-08-12, in a later session. Second recorded occurrence; the recovery below differs from the one above because the id sets were NOT a strict subset this time.

Local held 127 issues (a stale snapshot predating the previous sprint), the remote 184. The SessionStart hook reported "verified write access to refs/dolt/*" and looked healthy, but nothing had cloned: bootstrap rejects sync.remote as a git code-repository URL, then reports "Database already exists / Nothing to do" and exits 0. Every bead created in the session went into a fork with no common ancestor.

BOTH offered recoveries were destructive here: bootstrap would have dropped the 16 session beads, --force would have dropped 73 remote issues and reverted 11 closures. The id-set diff (step 3 above) is what made that visible.

RECOVERY, for the not-a-subset case:
  1. bd export both sides before touching anything.
  2. Diff the id sets to get the three-way picture: remote-only, local-only, and status-differs. The last one matters — 11 issues were open locally and closed on the remote, which is what proved local was stale rather than merely behind.
  3. Comment out the sync: block in .beads/config.yaml. This is the fault this bead is about, and it blocks bootstrap even with no database present.
  4. rm -rf .beads/embeddeddolt .beads/embeddeddolt.gate.lock .beads/metadata.json .beads/export-state.json .beads/.local_version
  5. bd bootstrap --yes  (now clones), then restore config.yaml.
  6. bd import <local-only beads>. 'bd export' preserves parent-child and blocks edges, so hierarchy and dependencies survive the round trip.
  7. bd dolt push, then re-clone into a scratch repo and diff again to prove nothing was lost.

TRAP: the divergence hint printed by 'bd dolt push' says to 'rm -rf .beads/dolt'. That path does not exist — the database is .beads/embeddeddolt. Following the hint deletes nothing, bootstrap then reports "already exists", and the stale database survives while appearing to have been reset.

A staleness check at session start would catch this before any work is done: verifying write access to refs/dolt/* is not the same as verifying the local database descends from it.

title: subagent-prompts.md still documents the old ':!.beads' staging pathspec
description:
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/subagent-prompts.md line 107 describes bb-close-bead.sh as staging with `git add -A -- ':!.beads'`. The script now uses ':!.beads/*.jsonl' so tracked config under .beads/ stages normally. The prompt text therefore tells a subagent the close will drop its whole .beads/ directory, which is no longer true.

Found while correcting the bb-close-bead.sh header one-liner; the staging pathspec was out of that bead's scope.

AC:
- subagent-prompts.md names the same pathspec the script uses
- grep across plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/ finds no other reference to the whole-directory exclusion

## Steps to Reproduce

From the repository root:

    sed -n '147p' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-close-bead.sh
    grep -rn ":\!\.beads'" plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/ | grep -v 'jsonl'

EXPECTED: every document describes the same pathspec the script uses.
ACTUAL: the script stages with ':!.beads/*.jsonl'; SKILL.md:1119-1120, subagent-prompts.md:107 and recovery.md:159-160 all say ':!.beads'. recovery.md:160 instructs the agent to RUN that form by hand, which drops tracked tracker config from the commit while the close still reports success.
design:
Replace ':!.beads' with ':!.beads/*.jsonl' at the three documentation sites, and DELETE the by-hand replay at references/recovery.md:160 rather than correcting it.

The four sites are listed in this bead's notes. Deleting :160 outright is preferred over fixing its pathspec because it is a second, drift-prone hand implementation of bb-close-bead.sh inside a skill whose stated rule is that scripts are executed rather than reproduced — and this defect is the proof of that rule. Replace it with an instruction to fix and re-run the script.

Coordinate with agent-plugins-8ef.3, which also targets recovery.md:160 for deletion; whichever lands first takes the line.

Verify with a grep across plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/ for the whole-directory exclusion, which must return nothing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No file under plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/ describes the close as staging with the whole-directory exclusion.
2. Every remaining description of the staging pathspec matches scripts/bb-close-bead.sh:147.
3. references/recovery.md no longer instructs an agent to replay the close ceremony by hand.
4. A grep for ':!.beads' not followed by /*.jsonl returns no matches in the skill.
notes:
SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-08-12 (bead-bonanza refinement analysis). The pathspec disagreement is in FOUR places, not one, and the most dangerous is not subagent-prompts.md:

  • SKILL.md:1119-1120        — 'everything modified except .beads/'
  • subagent-prompts.md:107   — "stage code only (git add -A -- ':!.beads')"
  • recovery.md:159           — same sentence again
  • recovery.md:160           — THE DANGEROUS ONE: 'Only if the script cannot run, replay its order by hand: ... then git add -A -- ":!.beads"'

recovery.md:160 instructs an agent to EXECUTE the exact command that bb-close-bead.sh's own comment (:140-143) identifies as a silent-data-loss defect: 'Excluding the whole directory silently drops tracked tracker config — config.yaml, .gitignore, the bd hooks — from the commit ... and the close still reports success.' The script itself uses ':!.beads/*.jsonl' at :147.

Raised P3 -> P1: a by-hand replay is run precisely when the script is broken, i.e. during recovery, when the orchestrator is least able to notice a silently under-complete commit.

This bead's existing AC ('grep across plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/ finds no other reference to the whole-directory exclusion') already covers all four sites, so no additional bead was filed.

title: bb-close-bead.sh excludes all of .beads/, silently dropping legitimate config changes
description:
Found by agent-plugins-6uo while editing .beads/config.yaml as in-scope work.

bb-close-bead.sh stages with `git add -A -- ":!.beads"`, which excludes the ENTIRE .beads/ directory. The intent was to keep the untracked JSONL exports out of close commits. The effect is broader: any bead whose scope legitimately includes a TRACKED file under .beads/ — config.yaml, .gitignore, the bd git hooks, metadata.json — has that change silently dropped from its commit.

Silently is the problem. The close reported success; the commit simply did not contain the file. 6uo only noticed because it checked its own commit contents, and had to amend to repair it.

FIX: narrow the pathspec to the exports it was actually aimed at, e.g. `:!.beads/*.jsonl`, so tracked config under .beads/ stages normally.

Introduced by agent-plugins-92q.31 when the export staging was retired.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The pathspec excludes only the JSONL exports, not the whole .beads/ directory
- [ ] A bead editing .beads/config.yaml has that change land in its close commit, verified by running the close and inspecting git show --stat
- [ ] A bead NOT editing .beads/ still produces a commit with no .beads/*.jsonl in it

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Pre-fix failure reproduced. With .beads/config.yaml modified alongside the script edit, `git add -A -- ':!.beads'` then `git diff --cached --stat` printed only 'plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-close-bead.sh | 7 ++++++-' / '1 file changed' — config.yaml absent, exit 0, no warning. With ':!.beads/*.jsonl' the same command staged both files: '.beads/config.yaml | 1 +' and the script.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: The JSONL exports are already untracked and gitignored in this repo — `git check-ignore -v .beads/issues.jsonl` returns '.beads/.gitignore:87:issues.jsonl' and `git ls-files .beads/` lists no *.jsonl. The explicit exclusion is kept as belt-and-braces because gitignore state is a property of the consuming project and this script ships elsewhere.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Silent decision a diff-reader would not see as a choice — plain `:!.beads/*.jsonl` was used rather than `:(exclude)(glob).beads/*.jsonl`. Without :(glob) magic the `*` also crosses directory separators, so a nested export like .beads/sub/x.jsonl is excluded too; that is wanted here, not an oversight.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Negative case verified beyond the ignore rule. With a real .beads/issues.jsonl on disk, both `git add -A -- ':!.beads/*.jsonl'` and the ignore-overriding `git add -A -f -- ':!.beads/*.jsonl'` staged only config.yaml and the script — so the exclusion holds on its own, not merely because .gitignore covers it.

title: Cut historical prose: config.yaml + session-bootstrap
