title: retired-target and type-mismatch are silent on a single-document check, and report 'passed'
description:
agent-plugins-fe1 established the principle: a finding whose cause is an edit to
document X but whose location is a *referring* document is invisible to a
single-document check on X, because the narrowing is by path. The fix let
`reference/unresolved` survive that narrowing.

Two sibling rules have exactly the same property and were not covered:

**reference/retired-target.** Measured 2026-08-09 on this repo — setting
ADR-018 to `status: retired`:
  spec check                  -> 4 x reference/retired-target warning
  spec check <the ADR's path> -> no findings, exit 0,
                                 'reference/retired-target  passed'

**reference/type-mismatch.** Changing the reference-integrity FRD's type from
`frd` to `adr`:
  spec check                  -> reference/type-mismatch error against the
                                 feature blueprint (its typed `frd` property)
  spec check <the FRD's path> -> 'reference/type-mismatch  passed'

`reference/pairing-incomplete` is structurally the same; it is inert for this
profile by design, so it cannot be demonstrated here, but an adopting profile
that registers a pairing would hit it.

**The report is affirmatively wrong, not merely incomplete.** AC-SPEC-006.8's
whole point is that a run distinguishes a rule that passed from one that was
not requested. These rules print `passed` — 'ran, found nothing' — when the
same corpus, checked whole, reports findings the narrowing dropped. A reader
cannot tell this apart from a genuinely clean result.

**This is the workflow the skill prescribes.** SKILL.md step 5 tells an author
that retiring a document produces a retired-target warning, and step 7 tells
them to run `spec check <path>` before flipping status. Those two instructions
do not compose. The skill docs have been corrected to say so
(plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md, references/spec-cli.md,
references/document-readiness-checklist.md); this bead is the CLI half.

**Scope question for whoever takes this.** AC-SPECREF-002.9 is worded around
references that 'no longer resolve', so retired-target and type-mismatch are
arguably outside it and this may need a new criterion in
reference-integrity-frd.md rather than a widened implementation. Decide that
before coding. The mechanical change is small — these three rules already walk
the whole reference collection, exactly as unresolved does, so the fix is the
same narrowing exception — but widening a check's blast radius is a spec
decision, and REQ-SPECREF-002's rationale reasons about it explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: A single-document check on a document whose retirement or type change breaks a relational reference reports it against the referring document, or the report stops claiming those rules 'passed' when the narrowing dropped their findings. Either outcome is recorded as a criterion in the FRD before it is implemented.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Fixed, spec first. AC-SPECREF-002.11 added to reference-integrity-frd.md generalizing AC-SPECREF-002.9's narrowing exception to every reference rule, with the rationale that the argument was always a property of references rather than of unresolved ones, and that reporting 'passed' over discarded findings is worse than not running the rule. Implemented as finding.IsReferenceRule over the four rule constants — membership defined by where a rule's findings land, not by the reference/ prefix. TestCheckForNarrowsLifecycleAndRelationalFindingsToTheCheckedFile asserted the defect and is replaced by TestCheckForReportsLifecycleFindingsAgainstTheReferringDocument. Verified end to end: retiring ADR-018 and checking that one file now reports 3 retired-target warnings; re-typing the FRD reports the type-mismatch against the blueprint.

title: spec check <path> accepts a non-member path and reports every rule passed
description:
`spec check <path>` never tells the caller that the path it was given is not a
corpus member. check() filters index entries by `entry.Path != *only`; a path
matching no entry simply selects nothing, and the run reports 'no findings',
every rule 'passed', exit 0.

Measured 2026-08-09 on this repo, green corpus:

  spec check specs/adrs/does-not-exist.md   -> no findings, all passed, exit 0
  spec check README.md                      -> no findings, all passed, exit 0
  spec check specs/                         -> no findings, all passed, exit 0

A typo, a file outside the spec root, a directory, and a file with no
frontmatter are all indistinguishable from a clean document.

This is the vacuous-success failure mode AC-SPECREF-004.3's rationale names as
having already hit this project in three separate tools, on the surface the
spec skill tells an author to run before every status flip (SKILL.md step 7:
'run spec check <path>'). An agent that mistypes a path is told it passed.

agent-plugins-fe1's fix makes the symptom stranger rather than louder: since
unresolved references now survive the narrowing, checking a made-up path in a
corpus that has broken links reports those links and exits 1 — findings that
have nothing to do with the path asked about, and no indication the path was
never found.

Distinguish the cases the corpus already knows apart: a member, a candidate
recorded as excluded (report the exclusion reason it already holds), and a
path that is no candidate at all (an error naming it).
acceptance_criteria: A path that names no corpus member is reported as such and exits non-zero rather than reporting checks passed. A path recorded as excluded reports the exclusion reason the index already carries. A path that is a corpus member is unaffected.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Fixed. CheckFor returns ErrNotAMember for a path occupying no entry, distinguishing a candidate the index excluded (reporting the recorded reason) from one discovery never saw. cmd/check.go renders it as an error rather than a report, since a report with no findings is what a passing document looks like. Verified: missing path, README.md outside the spec root, a directory, and a frontmatter-less file under the spec root all exit 1 with a message naming the path; a real member is unaffected. Covered by TestCheckForRejectsAPathThatIsNotACorpusMember and the check-path-not-a-member snapshot case.

title: Establish whether worktree-parallel is safe: isolation:worktree branches from the default branch, not session HEAD
description:
`bead-bonanza`'s worktree-parallel mode assumes each subagent branches from the
run's working branch and that the orchestrator merges back into it. The
platform default is different.

Claude Code docs (`code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents`, frontmatter): setting
`isolation: worktree` gives the subagent "an isolated copy of the repository
**branched by default from your default branch rather than the parent
session's `HEAD`**". And `code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees`: `"head"`: branch
from your current local `HEAD` ... **Use this when isolating subagents that
need to operate on in-progress work.**

So with the default `worktree.baseRef: "fresh"`, every worktree subagent
branches from `origin/main`. Consequences for a bead-bonanza run:

- Every merge back carries the delta between `main` and the working branch.
- **Any bead built on an earlier bead's commit in the same run silently loses
  that foundation.** Run 1786121603-ri would have been badly hit: 9kb.2-9kb.9
  all build on 9kb.1's model, and the wave plan explicitly sequenced them.

Neither `SKILL.md`'s dispatch-mode section nor the "Worktree parallel notes" in
`references/subagent-prompts.md` mentions `worktree.baseRef` at all.

This is a prerequisite for using worktree-parallel at all. The sibling bead
corrects the false claim that the mode is impossible; this one establishes
whether it is SAFE.


## Retro — implementation

**Findings** (also filed as `retro:` comments on this bead)

1. Conclusions 3 and 4 combine into a merge hazard this bead did not have a
   mandate to fix. All worktree agents share ONE database (conclusion 3), so
   the mandated `bd export > .beads/issues.jsonl` (conclusion 4) makes every
   worktree branch commit a near-identical FULL export of the same shared
   tracker. With no merge driver configured for that file (CLAUDE.md), two or
   more worktree branches in a wave will conflict textually on
   `.beads/issues.jsonl` at merge time — every time, by construction. The
   orchestrator should expect it and resolve by re-exporting on the merged
   tree, the same way a regen step resolves a fixture conflict. This belongs
   with the skip conditions owned by `agent-plugins-92q.9`, not here.

**What I tried that did not work** — nothing failed. No probes were re-run;
the measurements were handed over intact.

**What I decided silently**

- Took the optional pre-flight probe. `pre-flight-check.sh` now reads
  `.worktree.baseRef` from the user-scope settings file (the jq plumbing was
  already there for the telemetry deny) and reports it as an **advisory** line
  plus `BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF`, never a blocker — most runs never dispatch a
  worktree wave, and blocking them on a global setting they do not use would
  be wrong. Verified: self-test PASS (26 checks), live run emits
  `worktree.baseRef: head (advisory)` and `BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF='head'`.
- Cited the fact in SKILL.md through `BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF` rather than by
  naming the settings file and key, so Phase 0's "do not re-assert from memory
  what the script just measured" rule holds and the bullet stays 5 lines.
  Net SKILL.md growth: 43,621 -> 43,986 bytes.
- Structured the reference section as a two-row measured table plus a copy-
  pasteable verification instruction for the first worktree subagent, so the
  orchestrator can paste rather than compose it under load.
- Left Phase 2.5's "Skip this mode if..." list untouched per the handover;
  `agent-plugins-92q.9` owns it.

**Observed results** (measured by the orchestrator; quoted, not re-run)

Session HEAD `0ccc092` on `claude/bead-bonanza-improvements-j6jxjv`, 8 commits
ahead of default branch `main` at `5390f1d`. Two read-only `isolation:
"worktree"` probes. Discriminator: `scripts/pre-flight-check.sh` and the string
`After any compaction` in bead-bonanza's SKILL.md exist only on the branch.

Probe 1 — no `worktree` key in the user settings file:

    git rev-parse --short HEAD                -> 5390f1d   (DEFAULT BRANCH)
    git merge-base --is-ancestor 0ccc092 HEAD -> exit 1    (HEAD not an ancestor)
    git rev-list --count 5390f1d..HEAD        -> 0
    test -e .../scripts/pre-flight-check.sh   -> exit 1    (absent)
    wc -l .beads/issues.jsonl                 -> 105       (main checkout: 128)
    git rev-parse --git-common-dir            -> /home/user/agent-plugins/.git
    ls -d .beads/embeddeddolt                 -> No such file or directory
    bd where -> /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads
                database: /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads/embeddeddolt
    bd worktree info -> Main repo: /home/user/agent-plugins
                        Beads: local (no redirect)
    bd list                                   -> 63 issues

Probe 2 — after setting baseRef to head in user-scope settings:

    git rev-parse --short HEAD                -> 0ccc092   (SESSION HEAD)
    git merge-base --is-ancestor 0ccc092 HEAD -> exit 0
    git rev-list --count 5390f1d..HEAD        -> 8
    test -e .../scripts/pre-flight-check.sh   -> exit 0    (present)
    grep -c "After any compaction" .../SKILL.md -> 1
    wc -l .beads/issues.jsonl                 -> 128       (current)
    ls -d .beads/embeddeddolt                 -> No such file or directory
    bd where -> /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads (main checkout)

Acceptance outcome **(a)**: worktree-parallel is SAFE, conditional on
`baseRef: "head"` plus the per-wave ancestor check. The setting takes effect
immediately — probe 2 ran minutes after the write, in the same session.
Conclusion 3 independently reproduces `agent-plugins-t09` in this repository.

**Limits, stated not papered over**

- Project-root `.claude/settings.json` was NOT tested as a location for the
  key. Only user scope is verified; the docs say so rather than implying the
  project file works.
- This repository has no `.worktreeinclude` (`ls` -> No such file or
  directory), so gitignored-file copying was observed only in its default
  form: `.beads/embeddeddolt/` absent from both worktrees — which turned out
  not to matter, because of conclusion 3.
design:
**Test before trusting either setting.** The docs describe the behaviour; this
run has never exercised it.

1. Dispatch two throwaway worktree subagents from a branch that is ahead of the
   default branch. Have each report `git merge-base --is-ancestor <working-branch-head> HEAD`
   and `git log --oneline -3` from inside its worktree. Confirm whether they
   branched from the default branch or from session HEAD.
2. Repeat with `worktree.baseRef: "head"` configured. Confirm the worktree
   carries the working branch's commits.
3. Establish where the setting belongs. Project-root `.claude/settings.json` is
   NOT read in a multi-root session (verified: `/home/user/.claude` does not
   exist), but user-scope `~/.claude/settings.json` IS honoured here — Phase 0
   already writes a telemetry deny to it. If `baseRef` must be set per-session,
   Phase 0 is the place, and that is a skill change.
4. Also verify the interaction with `.worktreeinclude`: gitignored files are not
   copied into a Claude-created worktree by default, which matters for anything
   the run needs that git does not track.

**Acceptance:** either (a) worktree-parallel is documented as safe with a
stated `baseRef` setting and a verification step in the dispatch template, or
(b) it is documented as unsafe for runs whose beads build on each other, with
the specific reason. Do not enable the mode in `SKILL.md` until one of those
is established.

Depends on the outcome, not the text, of the ledger-correction bead — they can
proceed in parallel but the mode should not be enabled until both land.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Two throwaway worktree subagents were dispatched from a branch ahead of the default branch, and each reported 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <working-branch-head> HEAD' and 'git log --oneline -3' from inside its worktree
- [ ] The observed base ref (default branch vs session HEAD) is recorded with that output
- [ ] The same test was repeated with worktree.baseRef: head configured, and the result recorded
- [ ] Where the baseRef setting must live is established, including whether user-scope ~/.claude/settings.json is required in a multi-root session
- [ ] The interaction with .worktreeinclude for gitignored files the run needs is verified
- [ ] The outcome is one of: (a) worktree-parallel documented as safe with a stated baseRef setting and a dispatch-template verification step, or (b) documented as unsafe for runs whose beads build on each other, with the specific reason
- [ ] worktree-parallel is not enabled in SKILL.md by this bead

metadata.tier_reason: Empirical: dispatch throwaway worktrees, test two baseRef settings, establish where the setting belongs. The output is a verdict others depend on, so a wrong one is expensive.

title: Correct the false 'worktree-parallel is unusable with bd' claim in both repos' ledgers
description:
Both repos' agent instructions assert that worktree-parallel dispatch is
impossible for any bead that runs `bd`. **The claim is false and was never
tested.** It has been costing real parallelism: every bead of run
1786121603-ri was dispatched sequentially on the strength of it.

Where it lives:
- `/home/user/strata/AGENTS.md:493` — "**Corollary: worktree-parallel dispatch
  is unusable for any bead that runs `bd`** ... `.beads/embeddeddolt/` is
  gitignored, so a `git worktree` does not receive the Dolt DB and `bd` either
  fails or silently re-inits an empty one inside it."
- `.bonanza/1786121603-ri/dispatch.md:7-9` — same claim, run-scoped.

**Measured refutation.** `bd` 1.1.2 resolves the shared database through git's
common directory. From a worktree created off this repo, with `BEADS_DIR`
UNSET:

```
$ bd where
/home/user/agent-plugins/.beads
  database: /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads/embeddeddolt
$ bd worktree info
  Main repo: /home/user/agent-plugins
$ bd list        → 36 issues (identical ID set to the main checkout)
```

No `embeddeddolt/` and no redirect file were created in the worktree. Writes
from the worktree land in the shared DB and are immediately visible from main.
`bd worktree --help` states the mechanism: "Worktrees automatically share the
same beads database as the main repository via git common directory discovery
— no manual redirect configuration needed."

**Concurrency is also safe** (tested in an isolated repo, not the live DB): 8
concurrent `bd create` → 8 successes; 4 concurrent `bd label add` on the SAME
issue → all four labels present, no lost update; 4 concurrent writes across
main + 3 worktrees → all landed; `bd export` afterwards byte-valid, 0
malformed lines. Embedded Dolt takes a process-level lock and serializes at
~2 writes/sec, which is irrelevant next to agent think-time.

The premise (`embeddeddolt/` is gitignored) is true. The inference drawn from
it does not follow, and nobody ran the command.


## Steps to Reproduce

The defect is a false claim in a durable instruction, so the repro is the
command the claim says will fail. From a git worktree created off this repo,
with `BEADS_DIR` unset:

```
$ bd where
/home/user/agent-plugins/.beads
  database: /home/user/agent-plugins/.beads/embeddeddolt
$ bd worktree info
  Main repo: /home/user/agent-plugins
$ bd list
36 issues            # identical ID set to the main checkout
$ ls .beads/
                     # no embeddeddolt/, no redirect file created
```

**Claimed** (strata `AGENTS.md:493`, and the run-scoped copy in
`.bonanza/1786121603-ri/dispatch.md:7-9`): "a git worktree does not receive the
Dolt DB and `bd` either fails or silently re-inits an empty one inside it."

**Actual:** `bd` resolves the main checkout's `.beads/` through git's common
directory. Writes from the worktree land in the shared DB and are immediately
visible from main. Concurrency tested separately in an isolated repo: 8
concurrent `bd create` → 8 successes; 4 concurrent `bd label add` on one issue
→ all four labels present; 4 concurrent writes across main + 3 worktrees → all
landed, `bd export` byte-valid with 0 malformed lines.
design:
**Replace the AGENTS.md bullet** with the corrected version, keeping it a trap
warning rather than deleting the history:

> - **Corollary: worktree-parallel dispatch IS available for beads that run
>   `bd`.** `.beads/embeddeddolt/` is gitignored, but `bd` never looks for a DB
>   inside the worktree — it resolves the main checkout's `.beads/` through
>   git's common directory (`bd worktree info` → "Main repo: ..."; `bd where`
>   in a worktree prints the main path). Reads and writes from a worktree hit
>   the one shared DB with no `BEADS_DIR` and no redirect file, and concurrent
>   writers are lock-serialized (8 concurrent `bd create` → 8 successes;
>   concurrent label writes to one issue all merged; no corruption). The real
>   constraints are git-side, not DB-side — see below.

**Then document the constraints that ARE real**, because they are sharper than
the imagined one and a naive worktree run would hit all three:

1. **A worktree's own `.beads/issues.jsonl` goes stale while `git status`
   reads clean.** Auto-export always writes the MAIN checkout's copy. Measured:
   DB 28 issues, main file 28 lines, worktree file 23 lines, and the worktree
   reported no changes. Any worktree agent MUST run `bd export >
   .beads/issues.jsonl` in its own directory before committing.
2. **Auto-export is best-effort and was observed to miss** — three creates sat
   unexported for 20+ seconds, flushing only on a later main-context write.
3. **`export.git-add: true` stages into the main index from writes issued
   elsewhere.** This is the case the `git commit -- <pathspec>` guard exists
   for; keep commits pathspec-scoped.

**Do NOT enable worktree-parallel dispatch as part of this bead.** Correcting
the claim and enabling the mode are separate: the sibling bead covers the
`worktree.baseRef` defect that must be resolved first.

Note the ledger convention this episode argues for: an entry asserting
something is IMPOSSIBLE should cite the command that proved it. Four such
claims in this session turned out to be untested inferences.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The strata AGENTS.md ledger entry no longer claims worktree-parallel is unusable for beads that run bd, and states the common-directory mechanism instead
- [ ] The corrected entry cites the commands that proved it (bd where, bd worktree info, bd list from a worktree) rather than asserting the conclusion
- [ ] The three real constraints are documented: the worktree's own issues.jsonl going stale while git status reads clean, best-effort auto-export, and export.git-add staging into the main index
- [ ] The entry is preserved as a trap warning rather than deleted, per the existing ledger convention
- [ ] worktree-parallel dispatch is NOT enabled by this bead
- [ ] The run-scoped copy of the claim in any committed dispatch plan is corrected or annotated
notes: PATH AUDIT 2026-08-12: the .bonanza/1786121603-ri run directory was never committed — it appears in no commit, and .bonanza/README.md has never existed. The only committed run directory is .bonanza/1786345424-bbh. Citations to decisions.md, dispatch.md or README.md under that run are unresolvable; treat the quoted content in this bead as the surviving record.
close_reason: Fixed and verified 2026-08-12. The false claim is gone from AGENTS.md (grep for 'unusable with bd' and 'worktree-parallel' returns nothing). The correction now lives in the skill itself at plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md:93-98 ('bd is not an obstacle ... resolves the shared tracker database through git's common directory'). The three 'real constraints' the bead listed are moot: .beads/.gitignore:87-89 untracks issues.jsonl, so no worktree-local JSONL staleness is possible.

title: Reshape the per-bead retro: mechanical description dump, trigger list, and own the retro: comment channel
description:
Measured across run 1786121603-ri by tracing every quoted span >=40 chars in
`rfcs/inbox/feature-blueprint/rfc-0015-implementing-reference-integrity.md`
back to its source:

| Channel | Generated volume | Yield |
|---|---|---|
| 10 `.retro.md` files | 137,146 bytes (~34k output tokens) | 1 item, in *Considered and Not Proposed*. Zero proposals. |
| 34 `retro:` bd comments | 16,411 bytes (~4.1k output tokens) | 12 of 12 traceable Evidence quotes; 5 of 7 proposals |

**8.4x the cost for ~1/12 the findings.** `agent-plugins-9kb.6` — no retro
file at all, one 482-character comment — carries proposal P2. Conversely
`tix`, `ml9` and `j7f` wrote 38,205 bytes of retro files between them and are
cited zero times.

Three structural causes:

1. **The template asks for categories, not triggers.** `findings-capture.md`
   defines a trigger list (record WHEN you needed information the bead did not
   carry, WHEN the bead contradicted repo reality...), which filters.
   `references/subagent-prompts.md:82` asks for a category ("implicit decisions
   you made"), which enumerates. Implicit decisions are the largest bucket
   (32,892 bytes, 39% of retro prose) and produced zero RFC quotes on their own.

2. **The skill does not own the channel that works.** `grep -c
   "findings-capture\|retro:" references/subagent-prompts.md` returns **0**. The
   `retro:` comment instruction reached subagents only because the groomed
   `9kb.*` bead descriptions carried it themselves. `tix`, `ml9` and `j7f` were
   prerequisites outside that groomed plan, which is exactly why they produced
   files and no findings.

3. **The ceremony destroys the instruction.** `bb-close-bead.sh:58` runs `bd
   update --status closed --body-file <retro>`, and `--body-file` REPLACES the
   description. Agents hand-retype the description into the retro file and drop
   content. Verified on `agent-plugins-9kb.1`: the original description (from
   `git show f019922^:.beads/issues.jsonl`) ends with a `## Retro` section
   containing "one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
   findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`". The current
   description has a `## Retro` heading but no `findings-capture` and no
   `prefixed`. The collision is structural: the bead already has a `## Retro`
   section and the instruction says to append one with the same name.

Standing cost: 79% of description bytes in the committed `.beads/issues.jsonl`
are retro payload, rewritten and re-committed on every close.


## Retro — implementation

### Findings
- AC 8 ("measured retro output on the next run is materially smaller than the ~34k-token baseline") cannot be satisfied by the bead that changes the template — it is an observation about a later run. - The `retro:` comment obligation is stated inside finding item 1 rather than as its own bullet, so the instruction sits where the finding is written and cannot be read as an optional extra step.

title: Verify bead-bonanza SKILL.md fits under the 5,000-token re-injection cap, trim the residual, and retire the KNOWN RED exception
description:
The re-injection cap is a size, so "did the restructure work" is a measurement,
not a judgment. This bead is that measurement, plus the tidy-up that follows it.

Measured 2026-08-10 on `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` (45,983 bytes, 869
lines):

```
$ head -c 20000 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md | wc -l
406            # "### Choose a dispatch mode per bucket"
```

An invoked skill's body is re-injected after compaction capped at 5,000 tokens,
truncating from the start of the file
(`code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window`), and
`CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=80` is set in this cloud environment. So
everything past line 406 — the whole close ceremony, the anti-paraphrase rule,
the retro-anchor rule, the script interfaces, Phase 3, Phase 4, Operating
principles — leaves the orchestrator's context precisely when it loses context.

This is the causal root of run `1786121603-ri`'s central failure: beads
`9kb.5`, `9kb.6` and `9kb.7` are exactly the three dispatched after that run's
context loss, and all three closed with no progress ledger and no retro anchor
because their briefs were hand-written. The rule forbidding hand-written briefs
had been truncated away.

**Scope note — this bead was re-planned on 2026-08-10.** As originally filed it
was a single heroic restructure of a file whose contents were about to change.
The content-reducing work (pre-flight extraction, Phase 2 deletion, dispatch-plan
lean-path removal) accounts for 9,472 bytes of the ~26,000-byte gap and is now
tracked by sibling beads, as is the extraction of the explanatory prose. What
remains here is the verification that the whole set actually cleared the cap,
the residual trimming if it did not, and retiring the ledger exception the
oversize file has been carrying.

Full write-up: `rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/rfc-self-silent-ceremony-loss-and-the-stale-twin.md`,
Finding 7 and P3.
design:
Runs last in the SKILL.md chain. Depends on the pre-flight extraction, the
Phase 2 deletion, the dispatch-plan rewrite and the references extraction all
having landed.

**1. Measure.**

```bash
wc -c plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md
head -c 20000 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md | tail -20
```

The acceptance criterion is positional, not just numeric: the content at the
20,000-byte mark SHALL fall **after** the Reference-files table and its
published script interfaces. Body under ~20,000 bytes total is the stronger
form and the target.

**2. Trim the residual** if the measurement misses. Trim in this order, because
it removes the least operative material first:
   - duplicated statements of the same rule in two phases (the skill restates
     several rules in both a phase and Operating principles — after the
     extraction, the phase copy is the one that stays);
   - worked examples where one suffices;
   - the four dispatch-mode descriptions, which can lose prose without losing
     the decision criteria.
   Do NOT trim by rewrapping to longer lines. The 80-column convention is good
   for diffs and does not affect token count materially (~640 tokens of the
   ~11,500 body are newlines); rewrapping would satisfy a line-based gate while
   changing nothing real.

**3. Add the compaction trigger to Phase 2.5.** Compaction is going to happen;
the orchestrator should choose when:

> Compact deliberately at a bucket boundary — never mid-bucket, never with a
> subagent in flight. Check context after each bucket and compact at ~60%
> rather than letting the automatic pass at 80% choose the moment.

**4. Retire the baseline exception.** With the file under the byte threshold,
remove the "KNOWN RED, pre-existing — `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict`" entry
from `AGENTS.md`'s environmental-failure ledger, and confirm
`scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` now exits 0 on a clean tree. That entry has
been copied into every bead-bonanza dispatch prompt; retiring it removes a
standing instruction to ignore a red gate, which is worth more than the bytes.

**5. Bump** the skill's frontmatter `version` 1.3 -> 1.4 for the whole set of
changes in this epic, per [[template-authoring-standards]] — one bump for the
file, landing with whichever change is last, which is this one.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] SKILL.md's body size and the position of the 20,000-byte mark are both measured and reported
- [ ] The report states whether content at the 20,000-byte mark falls after the Reference-files table, and by how much the body is over or under 20,000
- [ ] WHEN still over, the report names each remaining section by size and what moving it would cost, rather than claiming a pass
- [ ] No operative rule was moved out of SKILL.md to reach a number
- [ ] Any residual trimming removed duplicated rules or surplus examples, not line rewrapping
- [ ] Phase 2.5 carries the deliberate-compaction trigger (bucket boundary, ~60%, never with a subagent in flight)
- [ ] The KNOWN RED check-skills entry in AGENTS.md is retired IF and only IF the file is genuinely under the threshold; otherwise the entry is updated with the current measured size
- [ ] The bead-bonanza SKILL.md frontmatter version is bumped 1.3 -> 1.4
notes:
Re-planned 2026-08-10. This bead was originally the whole restructure; the content-reducing and extraction work is now tracked by sibling beads and this one is the verification and tidy-up. The check-skills.sh unit fix that lived in this bead's notes is now its own bead.
## Constraint relaxed 2026-08-10 (user decision)

The hard byte target is **no longer an acceptance criterion**. The instruction:
'let's do our best but not constrain ourselves with the hard acceptance criteria
for 8ef at this time — we are doing a lot of modifications to SKILL.md and I
think it's important to first make the functional changes we want and then
optimize SKILL size from there.'

Consequences, both already wired:

- **The extraction bead no longer blocks the content beads.** It was gating
  eleven of them, which is backwards under functional-changes-first. The
  dependency is inverted: content beads edit SKILL.md in place now, and the
  extraction runs over whatever exists afterwards.
- **This bead runs last and reports rather than gates.** Measure the body, run
  the positional check, and state the result plainly — including WHEN the file
  is still over. An honest 'still N bytes over, here is what remains and what it
  would cost to move it' is the deliverable; a pass claimed by moving an
  operative rule out of context is not.

The positional criterion stays the useful one: content at the 20,000-byte mark
should fall after the Reference-files table, because that is what determines
whether the ceremony survives a compaction. Report it either way.
## FROZEN 2026-08-11 — pending the worktree and sync re-scope

Do not dispatch. Two decisions from the PR #18 review put this on hold:

1. The user relaxed 8ef's hard byte target: 'first make the functional changes we
   want and then optimize SKILL size from there.'
2. agent-plugins-92q.30 (worktrees) and agent-plugins-92q.31 (sync) between them DELETE a
   large share of what this bead was scheduled to extract — the WIP-commit
   exception, the foreign-dirt guard, the pathspec discipline, the mtime liveness
   table, and much of the close ceremony's compensating logic.

Extracting text that is about to be deleted is worse than doing nothing: it
makes the deletion harder and buries the rules in reference files first.

I told the user this work was orthogonal to the epic. It is not, and the
reviewer caught it: 'Based on what I'm seeing in this PR I'm starting to
question whether context-budget work is in fact orthogonal to the epic.' That
was correct.

Unfreeze only after the worktree and sync beads land or are formally declined,
then re-measure before planning — the section sizes this bead's Design cites
will be wrong by then.
close_reason:
Closed by user decision, 2026-08-12, to be revisited in a dedicated analysis round rather than carried as a standing open bead. Force-closed: bd blocked it on ordering edges to 92q.7 and 92q.19, which are sequencing constraints rather than correctness conditions, and the decision to defer supersedes the ordering.

This bead was to verify SKILL.md against the ~5,000-token re-injection cap, trim the residual, and retire the KNOWN RED check-skills --strict exception. Its acceptance criterion had already been relaxed once (hard byte target -> measured report) after a hard target caused a subagent to trim three unrelated passages to clear it.

STATE AT CLOSE, so the next round starts from measurement rather than re-deriving it:
- SKILL.md is ~60,800 bytes (~15,200 tokens) against a ~20,000-byte / ~5,000-token effective cap. Roughly 41,000 bytes over.
- The reference corpus is ~66,000 bytes across five files.
- This sprint CUT ~8,900 bytes of historical prose and dead surface, having earlier ADDED ~18,000 via retirement notes. History was never the bulk; what remains is operative content.
- Extraction alone tops out near 24,000 bytes of savings, still leaving ~40,000. Fitting under the cap is a rewrite, not an extraction.
- The cap truncates from the START and keeps the first 20,000 bytes, so ordering matters more than total size. That lever is what 92q.7 now takes, on its own.
- check-skills.sh --strict remains RED on two SKILL.md size warnings (bead-bonanza, spec). Non-strict PASSES and CI runs non-strict, so this does not block CI.

The open question for the next round: meet the epic's literal criterion (whole file under 20,000) or restate it as 'everything a compacted orchestrator needs is above the cut'. A literal 20,000 means deleting rules, and the worst size-to-value material left is the measured constraints and traps — the least reproducible content in the repo.

title: brokenInboundReferences is unreachable in production, so AC-SPECREF-002.9 is not delivered
description:
`brokenInboundReferences` (`cli/core/corpus/check.go:352`) can never fire in
production, so AC-SPECREF-002.9 — the criterion that a write-time check on one
file catches the referrers that file just broke — is not actually delivered.

**Why it cannot fire.** It compares the warm index's recorded inbound edges
against the checked document's slug read fresh from disk. But `Open`'s
fingerprint covers every candidate file's content, all-or-nothing
(`cli/core/corpus/hash.go`), so any edit to the document invalidates the warm
index and forces a cold rebuild. The rebuilt graph resolves the referrers
against the *new* slug, so they are recorded as unresolved rather than as
inbound edges to this path — `InboundReferences(path)` returns empty and the
function returns nil before `slugsMatch` is ever consulted.

**Reproduced 2026-08-07** on the repo's own corpus at `b259452`:

    /tmp/spec check                       # warm the index; exit 0
    sed -i 's/^slug: adr-018$/slug: adr-018-renamed/' \
      specs/adrs/ADR-018-references-as-index-edges.md
    /tmp/spec check specs/adrs/ADR-018-references-as-index-edges.md
      -> "reference/unresolved  passed", every rule passed, EXIT 0
    /tmp/spec check
      -> reference/unresolved error x10 (module-document-core.md:422:14 and
         9 more) "[[adr-018]] matches no document's slug"

The single-document check — the one the criterion exists for — is silent
exactly when the corpus-wide check is loud.

**The two covering tests know.** `check_test.go:788-794` states it outright:
"The mismatch is planted directly in the persisted index rather than produced
by editing a real file on disk, because editing adr-002.md's slug would change
the corpus's input hash and force a cold rebuild ... there is no way to make
one file's real bytes disagree with the rest of a warm index." So the two
`AC: AC-SPECREF-002.9` citations pass against a state production cannot reach,
and AC coverage reads green.
design:
This needs a decision before any code moves; do not pick one unilaterally.

**Option A — preserve the pre-edit index as the "before" snapshot.** Keep the
persisted index available across a rebuild so the comparison has a real prior
state. Delivers the criterion as written. Cost: a second index in memory (or a
re-read of the persisted file before it is overwritten), and a decision about
what "before" means when the index is cold or absent.

**Option B — derive the breakage without a prior graph.** On a single-document
check, additionally report unresolved references corpus-wide. Catches the
scenario, but over-reports: it cannot distinguish references broken by *this*
edit from references that were already broken, and it re-introduces the corpus
walk AC-SPEC-009.2's budget exists to prevent.

**Option C — revise the criterion.** Accept that a content-addressed
all-or-nothing fingerprint and a single-file write-time check are in tension,
and re-state AC-SPECREF-002.9 as something reachable. If this is chosen, the
two tests must stop planting a phantom row, and the FRD needs the change.

Whichever is chosen, the two tests at `check_test.go:796` and `:869` must end
up exercising a state a real edit can produce, or stop citing the AC.
close_reason: Delivered AC-SPECREF-002.9 via option B: unresolved references survive CheckFor's narrowing. Follow-up enhancement tracked as agent-plugins-h6c.1.

title: The 'test' gate short-circuits: check-skills.sh --strict is permanently red, so the two && checks after it never run
description:
AGENTS.md "## bead-bonanza gates" defines the full test gate as:

  scripts/check-skills.sh --strict && scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check && scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check

`check-skills.sh --strict` is documented in the same file's environmental-failure
ledger as KNOWN RED and pre-existing: it exits 1 on a warning (bead-bonanza
SKILL.md is 859 lines against an "under 500" guideline), with zero errors. The
documented instruction is to judge it against the `0 error(s), 1 warning(s)`
baseline rather than expecting exit 0.

Both statements are individually correct, and together they create a hole: because
the first command in the chain always exits non-zero, `&&` short-circuits and
**`sync-shared-references.sh --check` and `sync-strata-docs.sh --check` never
execute at all.** Anyone following the documented gate sees exit 1, compares it to
the known baseline, and concludes the gate passed — while two of its three checks
were never run.

Demonstrated 2026-08-07: `sync-strata-docs.sh --check` had been failing (3 of 3
vendored docs stale) and no bead's gate run surfaced it. It was found only by
running the check on its own. See agent-plugins-ml9.

## Suggested fix

State the three checks as INDEPENDENT gate steps rather than one `&&` chain, so a
failure in any one is visible regardless of the others. Whatever the mechanism,
the property to preserve is: a permanently-red check must not be able to mask the
checks positioned after it.

Consider also whether `check-skills.sh --strict` should stay in the gate at all
while its only finding is an editorial line-count warning — a gate that is red by
design trains everyone to ignore its exit status, which is what happened here.

## Steps to Reproduce

From the repository root:

    sed -n '52p' AGENTS.md
    bash scripts/check-skills.sh --strict; echo "exit=$?"

EXPECTED: all three checks in the gate run and report.
ACTUAL: check-skills.sh --strict prints 'RESULT: FAIL' on two size warnings, so the && chain stops there and sync-shared-references.sh --check and sync-strata-docs.sh --check never execute. Their status is unknown, not green.
design:
Replace the && chain in AGENTS.md:52 with a form that runs every check and reports each independently, then fails if any failed.

The current chain is: check-skills.sh --strict && sync-shared-references.sh --check && sync-strata-docs.sh --check. Because --strict currently exits 1, the two sync checks never execute, and their status is unknown rather than green.

Run all three unconditionally, capture each exit status, print a per-check line, and exit non-zero if any check failed. The point is that a red first check must not hide the state of the other two.

Do NOT make --strict pass as part of this bead. The two size warnings it reports are real and are owned by agent-plugins-41z and agent-plugins-d70. This bead only stops one failure from masking the others.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Running the test gate executes all three checks regardless of any individual failure.
2. Each check's outcome is reported separately and identifiably.
3. The gate's overall exit status is non-zero when any check fails.
4. With --strict currently red, the two sync checks' real status is visible in the output.

metadata.tier_reason: split one && chain in AGENTS.md so each check runs and reports independently; mechanical

title: Adopt strata HEAD: drop the removed optionalStyle option, take the null-clearing regeneration, and stop the warm-path budget test from gating
description:
# agent-plugins-tix — Adopt strata HEAD: drop the removed optionalStyle option, take the null-clearing regeneration, and stop the warm-path budget test from gating

## Bead description (full, as read via `bd show agent-plugins-tix`)

Prerequisite for the reference-integrity run. The repo cannot regenerate its
Strata artifacts with any currently-provisionable strata binary, and the run's
12 beads each gate on `go test ./...`, so this must land before wave 1.

### Measured this session

Three strata builds, same sources, three outcomes:

| strata commit | result |
|---|---|
| `44c1955` (what `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` built before) | schema DESTROYED — every document type's inherited properties regenerate as `{}` |
| `840f9ba` | correct; byte-identical to committed artifacts at that time |
| `ce18d66` (HEAD) | hard error: `/go/optionalStyle: unknown property` |

Version strings cannot tell these apart — all report `strata-cli 0.7.0`.

### Decision (2026-08-07, user)

Adopt HEAD, and stop the warm-path budget test from gating.

### What this bead does

1. **Drop `go.optionalStyle` from `schemas/strata.config.json`.** Upstream
   #296 removed the option. Pointer was already the default, so removing the
   key changes no generated output — it only stops HEAD rejecting the
   manifest.
2. **Regenerate via `scripts/generate-schemas.sh`.** Verified: the ONLY delta
   is in `cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go`, where every optional-field guard
   drops `&& string(m) != "null"`. The JSON Schema and Markdown outputs are
   byte-identical. That delta is upstream's bugfix — an explicit JSON null
   now clears its field instead of leaving the previous value in place.
3. **Stop `TestWarmQueriesAndChecksMeetTheirBudgets` failing the build.**
   Keep measuring and keep logging; stop asserting. `cache_test.go:397-416`
   already argues that a latency budget is "a product requirement about a
   developer's machine", not a shared runner, and already has a first-class
   reported-not-enforced mode — this extends that reasoning to the cloud
   container. Prefer making enforcement opt-in (an env var CI can set) over
   deleting the assertion; do NOT delete the measurement or the AC
   citations. Measured on this container, one test, 10 runs each:
   - committed artifacts: 6 pass / 4 fail (51.5ms, 54.9ms vs a 50ms budget)
   - HEAD-regenerated: 1 pass / 9 fail

   It is already unreliable here BEFORE any change; HEAD makes it worse.
4. **Correct the AGENTS.md environmental-failure ledger.** Its strata entry
   says building from HEAD "produces output byte-identical to what is
   committed". That was true on 2026-08-04 and is false now. Replace it with
   the table above and the fact that HEAD is the supported build once
   optionalStyle is gone.

### Out of scope — file, do not fix

- The underlying warm-path slowness is agent-plugins-uoe (PR #14 regressed
  the warm-index path ~1.8x by emitting UnmarshalJSON on every model). Do NOT
  fix it here.
- Recording the reference platform in the FRD is agent-plugins-7ek.
- If downgrading enforcement weakens how AC-SPEC-009.1/.2 are verified, file
  a bead noting it and link it; do not edit the FRD in this bead.

## Notes (full)

### WHY THE BUDGET TEST MUST STOP GATING (user, 2026-08-07)

Do not read the warm-path slowdown as a defect to be undone. The user's
statement, recorded verbatim in substance:

> The speed test fails because we introduced UnmarshalJSON implementations on
> every Go struct, and we HAD to do it. Without it, when a JSON key is missing
> or null for a REQUIRED property, Go sets scalars to their zero value
> (false, 0, ""), and reports no failure at all — which is very wrong.

So the cost is deliberate and bought real correctness. The 50ms budget in
AC-SPEC-009.1 was written BEFORE that correctness feature existed, which
makes the budget stale rather than the code slow. That is the justification
for reporting instead of asserting — not mere convenience on a noisy
container.

Two consequences for whoever implements this bead:

- NOTHING here removes UnmarshalJSON, and nothing may. strata HEAD keeps it.
  Upstream #296 removed only the SEPARATE `generateValidation` / `Validate()`
  emitter, whose docstring gives the same reason the user gives: it inferred
  "missing" from a Go zero value and could not distinguish a legitimate
  0/""/false from an absent field, so UnmarshalJSON supersedes it. The sole
  change to generated code in this bead is the null-clearing guard.
- agent-plugins-uoe frames UnmarshalJSON as a regression ("PR #14 regressed
  the warm-index path ~1.8x by emitting UnmarshalJSON on every generated
  model"). That premise is now contested by the user: the emission is
  required. uoe is OUT OF SCOPE here — do not touch it — but note in your
  retro that its framing needs re-scoping, from "undo the emission" to at
  most "make the required emission cheaper, or restate the budget".

## Acceptance criteria (as given)

- `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` exits 0 with a strata built from
  strata-lang/strata HEAD (ce18d66 or later).
- `schemas/strata.config.json` no longer sets `go.optionalStyle`.
- The regenerated `cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go` is committed, and the
  diff contains ONLY the removal of `&& string(m) != "null"` guards. Any
  other change in that file means something else moved — stop and report.
- `cd cli && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` exits 0 across
  ten consecutive runs, with the warm budget no longer able to fail the
  suite.
- The warm-path measurement still runs and still logs its p95 numbers; it is
  reported, not deleted, and its `AC:` citations are intact.
- The AGENTS.md ledger no longer claims HEAD reproduces the committed
  artifacts byte-for-byte.

---

## Retro

### Approach taken

1. Removed the `"go": { "optionalStyle": "Pointer" }` block entirely from
   `schemas/strata.config.json` (the whole `go` key, since `optionalStyle`
   was its only member — an empty `"go": {}` would have been pointless).
2. Ran `scripts/generate-schemas.sh`. `git status` showed exactly one file
   changed: `cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go`. Diffed it and confirmed every
   changed line matched the pattern `-...&& string(m) != "null" {` /
   `+...{` — i.e. only the null-clearing guard removal upstream's #296
   bugfix produces, nothing else. JSON Schema and Markdown outputs were
   untouched, matching the pre-measured expectation in fact 3.
3. Added an opt-in enforcement switch to `cache_test.go` rather than
   deleting or weakening the assertion:
   - New `warmBudgetEnforceEnv = "STRATA_ENFORCE_WARM_BUDGET"` constant and
     `enforceWarmBudget()` helper (`referencePlatform() &&
     os.Getenv(warmBudgetEnforceEnv) != ""`).
   - The existing `if !referencePlatform() { ... return }` gate in
     `TestWarmQueriesAndChecksMeetTheirBudgets` became
     `if !enforceWarmBudget() { ... return }`, keeping the exact same
     "log if over budget, then return without failing" shape it already had
     for non-reference platforms — Linux now behaves like "not the
     reference platform" unless the env var is set.
   - Kept `referencePlatform()` itself unchanged (still just `GOOS ==
     "linux"`) since its existing doc comment and reasoning about OS-level
     noise are still accurate and still relevant to who *would* set the env
     var.
   - Extended the doc comments with the user's UnmarshalJSON-correctness
     reasoning from the bead's Notes section, plus the 6/4 and 1/9
     measurements, so a future reader hits the "why" without needing to dig
     up this bead.
   - The `t.Logf` measurement, the p95 computation, and both `AC:` citations
     (`AC-SPEC-009.1, AC-SPEC-009.2, AC-SPEC-010.5`) are byte-for-byte
     untouched.
4. Rewrote the AGENTS.md strata ledger entry (see below).
5. Did not touch `agent-plugins-uoe` or any FRD, per the bead's explicit
   out-of-scope list.

### Observed pre-change and post-change test behaviour

**Pre-change** (recorded by the orchestrator before this bead started,
fact 4 — not independently re-measured, per "do NOT re-diagnose"):
10 runs each of `TestWarmQueriesAndChecksMeetTheirBudgets`:
- committed artifacts (pre-regen): 6 pass / 4 fail (over-budget runs at
  51.5ms, 54.9ms against the 50ms query budget)
- HEAD-regenerated artifacts: 1 pass / 9 fail

**Post-change** (measured this run, this container):
- `cd cli && go test ./...` (the full package suite, all tests) run 10
  consecutive times: **10/10 exit 0**. No flake, because the budget
  assertion can no longer fire without `STRATA_ENFORCE_WARM_BUDGET` set,
  and it is unset here.
- Isolated 3 runs of `go test ./core/corpus/... -run
  TestWarmQueriesAndChecksMeetTheirBudgets -v` to confirm the measurement
  still executes and logs:
  ```
  cache_test.go:506: linux/amd64: warm query p95 = 47.419413ms (budget 50ms), warm check p95 = 49.029456ms (budget 100ms)
  --- PASS: TestWarmQueriesAndChecksMeetTheirBudgets (2.06s)
  ```
  (Identical across all 3 runs — this container ran fast enough this time
  that even enforcement would have passed on this particular sample; the
  point of the fix is that it no longer matters either way.)
- Confirmed via code reading (not by forcing a slow run) that setting
  `STRATA_ENFORCE_WARM_BUDGET=1` on `linux` restores the original
  `t.Errorf` behavior exactly, so a real reference machine can still opt in
  to hard enforcement.

### Implicit decisions and why

- **Env var name and shape**: `STRATA_ENFORCE_WARM_BUDGET` (unset/empty =
  off, any non-empty value = on), gated through a small `enforceWarmBudget()`
  helper rather than inlining `os.Getenv` at the call site, so the "what
  turns enforcement on" logic has one place to read and one place to change
  later (e.g. if a reference-platform bead wants to flip the default).
  Chose a `STRATA_`-prefixed name to match this file's existing "strata"
  vocabulary (the repo's own env vars for the compiler are
  `STRATA_SRC_DIR`, `STRATA_CLI_SKIP` per AGENTS.md) even though this
  particular knob is about the corpus/cache test suite, not the strata
  compiler — kept the prefix for consistency with the rest of the repo's
  env-var namespace rather than inventing a `SPEC_` or `CORPUS_` prefix.
- **Did not wire the env var into `.github/workflows/cli.yml`.** The bead
  says "opt-in via an environment variable that CI can set" — CI *can* set
  it, but nothing in the bead's four numbered items or its acceptance
  criteria asks me to edit the GitHub Actions workflow, and doing so would
  be a policy decision (should the *real* CI runner assert this budget
  going forward, given the user's own reasoning that the budget itself is
  now stale?) that belongs to a human or a separate bead, not an implicit
  call for me to make silently in a workflow file. Left `cli.yml` untouched;
  its `go test ./...` step therefore also gets the new report-only default
  the next time it runs, which is consistent with "stop the test from
  gating" as stated.
- **Kept `referencePlatform()` as a separate, unchanged function** rather
  than folding its logic directly into `enforceWarmBudget()`, since its
  existing doc comment (macOS/Windows noise measurements) is still true and
  still worth keeping intact and citable on its own.
- **Removed the entire `"go": {...}` object** from
  `schemas/strata.config.json` rather than leaving `"go": {}`. The bead says
  "drop `go.optionalStyle`"; `optionalStyle` was the object's only key, so
  an empty object would have been dead configuration. Verified the
  regeneration is unaffected by this choice (the only diff is still
  confined to the null-clearing guards).
- **AGENTS.md ledger**: the bead's paraphrase ("produces output
  byte-identical to what is committed") doesn't appear verbatim anywhere in
  `AGENTS.md` — grepped the whole file and the whole repo for
  "byte-identical", "byte-for-byte", "reproduces". The closest real content
  is the existing `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check fails when the
  installed strata predates strata-lang/strata@8997153` entry, which
  implicitly claims "any strata at or after 8997153 regenerates the correct,
  committed artifacts" — true when written (2026-08-04, build `8997153`),
  false now that `#296` (between `840f9ba` and `ce18d66`) removed
  `optionalStyle` and would hard-error on the old manifest. I appended a new
  ledger bullet directly under that entry (rather than rewriting it in
  place) that: (a) gives the three-commit table from the bead description,
  (b) explains *why* HEAD failed closed instead of emitting silently-wrong
  output (the removed option, not a new inheritance bug), (c) states plainly
  that the manifest no longer sets `optionalStyle` so HEAD builds this repo
  again, (d) explicitly retracts the "any post-8997153 build reproduces
  committed output byte-for-byte" reading, and (e) states the new rule:
  build from strata HEAD (`ce18d66` or later) against the manifest as
  committed. Left the original `8997153` bullet's guidance (never commit
  regenerated output from a too-old binary; how to fix the binary) intact
  since it is still correct advice for that specific old-binary failure
  mode.

### What differed from the instructions

- **Discovered an out-of-scope gate failure and filed a bead for it,
  `agent-plugins-ml9`** (`discovered-from: agent-plugins-tix`, marked
  **adjacent, not blocking**): `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` reports
  all 3 vendored strata skill reference docs as STALE
  (`compiler-options.md`, `strata-llm-reference.md`, `language-reference.md`
  under `.claude/skills/strata/references/`), because the `/home/user/strata`
  checkout that script reads from is now at HEAD (`ce18d66`) while those
  vendored copies are stamped from older commits (`8997153`,
  `179d49029f4e`). This is unrelated to `optionalStyle` — a doc-sync
  mechanism, not a schema/codegen one — so I did not touch it. It does not
  affect this bead's gating: the "test" gate as literally specified is
  `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict && scripts/sync-shared-references.sh
  --check && scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check`, and `check-skills.sh
  --strict` already exits 1 on its known, pre-existing baseline warning
  (fact 2), which short-circuits the `&&` chain before `sync-strata-docs.sh
  --check` ever runs — verified by running that exact compound command and
  observing it stop at `check-skills` with the documented `0 error(s), 1
  warning(s)` output. Ran `sync-shared-references.sh --check` and
  `sync-strata-docs.sh --check` individually anyway, for diagnostic
  completeness, which is how the staleness was found in the first place.
- Everything else followed the workflow as given: claimed, read the bead in
  full (description + notes), implemented the four numbered items in order,
  ran the gates in the specified order (`generate-schemas.sh` before tests,
  then format/lint/build/test/custom), ran `go test ./...` ten consecutive
  times rather than once.

### Anything surprising

- The "reproduce the defect first" instruction was correctly pre-satisfied
  by fact 4's numbers, and I didn't need to re-run the pre-change state —
  but it was worth independently confirming *why* the post-change state is
  reliable: the fix makes the assertion path structurally unreachable by
  default (an `os.Getenv` check with nothing setting the var anywhere in
  this repo or its CI config), not merely "usually fast enough now". A
  10/10 clean run on this container could otherwise look like the flake
  just didn't happen to trigger this time.
- The specmodel.go diff was exactly and only the null-clearing guards, with
  zero surprises — no unexpected import changes, no reordering, no doc
  comment drift. Matches fact 3 precisely.
- The AGENTS.md "byte-identical" phrase from the bead description turned out
  to be a paraphrase of the *implication* of an existing bullet rather than
  a literal quote anywhere in the file — worth flagging in case whoever
  wrote the bead was looking at a different revision of AGENTS.md, or at
  strata's own AGENTS.md (a different repo) which has similar ledger
  language. I treated the paraphrase as accurately describing the *effect*
  of the existing `8997153` bullet and corrected that effect, which is the
  substantive fix regardless of exact wording.

### Note on agent-plugins-uoe's framing (as requested by the bead)

Per the bead's Notes section, flagging here (not touching agent-plugins-uoe
itself): its current framing — "PR #14 regressed the warm-index path ~1.8x
by emitting UnmarshalJSON on every generated model" — treats the emission
itself as the regression to undo. The user's reasoning recorded in this
bead's Notes contests that: UnmarshalJSON is required for correctness
(distinguishing an absent required field from a legitimate zero value), and
strata HEAD's own removal of the separate `Validate()` emitter — for the
identical reason — corroborates that the emission is the correct design,
not a defect. agent-plugins-uoe needs re-scoping from "undo the emission" to
at most "make the required emission cheaper" (e.g. avoid the raw
`map[string]json.RawMessage` round-trip per field, or generate a leaner
decode path) "or restate the budget" (accept that ~50ms warm-path latency is
the real cost of the correctness guarantee and move AC-SPEC-009.1's number
accordingly). I did not implement either alternative — out of scope here —
only recording the re-scoping note as instructed.

# agent-plugins-9kb.10 — Verify the Definition of Done, retire the blueprint, run the retro

```
◐ agent-plugins-9kb.10 · Verify the Definition of Done, retire the blueprint, run the retro   [● P1 · IN_PROGRESS]
Owner: Claude · Type: task
Created: 2026-08-07 · Started: 2026-08-07 · Updated: 2026-08-07

DESCRIPTION

  **Blueprint:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-
  blueprint.md — Definition of Done.
  **FRD:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md.
  **Delivery:** staged (stage 2 of 2); this feature's closure set is bd list -
  -label feature-spec-reference-integrity.

  The final item of the feature. Verify the blueprint's Definition of Done —
  every delta folded, every acceptance criterion cited at its declared level —
  retire the blueprint, and run the retro over the implementation phase.

  **This is a verification item, not a transcription item.** Read the
  delivered
  code and the delivered documents. A blueprint statement that contradicts the
  code is worse than an absent one, and an AC ticked without a citation
  defeats
  the point of the gate.

  **Already satisfied when this plan was groomed** (confirm, do not redo):

  • [[adr-018]] is already status: approved — the DoD's "draft → approved"
  step
  is done.
  • specs/adrs/README.md already carries its index entry for [[adr-018]].
  • The remaining half of that DoD entry — [[adr-018]] referenced from
  [[module-document-core]]'s Key Decisions — travels with the MODEL item's
  fold. Verify it landed.

  **Standing authorization for the retro.** The approved plan is the
  authorization to run the retro-spec skill; no further prompt is needed. The
  RFCs it produces remain human-gated at review.

  ## Retro

  Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
  one bd comment per finding, prefixed retro: — following the
  findings capture protocol in rfcs/findings-capture.md. Friction
  only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
  the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
  plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.



DESIGN

  Work in this order:

  1. **Verify every delta is folded** into its owning blueprint, reading the
  delivered code rather than the plan:
      • [[module-document-core]] — References marked **built** with the
      package
      that realizes it and its pinned semantics; the Corpus index-model
      vocabulary carries Reference and the references collection; the
      Findings vocabulary carries the new FindingDetail variants; the
      Interface section records the widened Profile and DocumentTypeRules;
      the Frontmatter component records per-item spans for sequence values;
      the
      Change Guidance rule on the Spans scanner records the goldmark
      narrowing; Key Decisions carries [[adr-018]]; version is 0.3.
      • [[module-spec-profile]] — Profile Registration records the reference,
      typed-reference and lifecycle registrations; Lifecycle Rules is
      reconciled
      from a planned package to a registration, with the checks located in
      Document Core; Interface records the widened Profile members; version
      is 0.3.
      • [[container-spec-cli]] — Command Surface records the refs subcommand
      and
      the profile-registration finding; the Components prose reflects the
      widened module surfaces. ContainerBlueprint declares no version
      property, so **no bump is possible here** (agent-plugins-e0t).
  2. **Verify [****[****contract-specs-configuration]]** was revised in place
  with
  version unchanged and the reason recorded.
  3. **Audit AC coverage.** All **24** acceptance criteria in the blueprint's
  AC
  Coverage table are cited from tests at their declared level, per
  [[testing-standards]] and the AC: citation format. The proving delta owes
  the citation; participating deltas do not. Expected owners: XPT 004.1; REX
  001.1, 001.2, 001.4, 001.5, 001.7; RES 001.3, 001.6, 002.2, 002.7, 002.8;
  PREG 004.2; CHK 002.1, 002.3, 002.9; LIFE 002.5, 002.6, 002.10; CMD 003.1,
  003.2, 003.3, 003.4, 003.5, 004.3. MODEL proves none.
  4. **Run the profile self-application gate** over this repository's own
  specs/
  corpus and confirm the run is green at the severities these checks assign.
  Triage each finding as a corpus defect or a profile defect; do not silence
  one by loosening the other.
  5. **Reconcile the tracker.** Close or re-scope the subsumed issues
  agent-plugins-dgn (superseded by MODEL) and agent-plugins-3md
  (superseded by LIFE). Confirm the prerequisite agent-plugins-j7f was
  resolved before MODEL landed. The out-of-scope issues — agent-plugins-gz3,
  -h6c, -a7m, -006, -9jo, -krb, -9ko, -vg1, -e0t — stay open
  and unchanged; confirm none was silently absorbed.
  6. **Retire the blueprint:** set
  specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-blueprint.md to
  status: retired and update updated_at.
  7. **Run the **retro-spec** skill** over the implementation phase,
  aggregating the
  retro:-prefixed findings recorded on every item in
  bd list --label feature-spec-reference-integrity. Implementation is the
  phase that finally exercises the work orders, so this is where their quality
  becomes evidence.



NOTES

  tier: advanced — Cross-cutting verification: 24 ACs audited against test
  citations, three architecture blueprints reconciled against delivered code
  rather than the plan, eleven tracker issues triaged, self-application
  findings split between corpus and profile defects, and the retro-spec run. A
  missed gap defeats the point of the gate.

  [ ] Every delta is folded into its owning blueprint as itemized in Design,
  verified against the delivered code rather than the plan.
  [ ] [[module-document-core]] and [[module-spec-profile]] are both at

  reason recorded.
  [ ] [[adr-018]] is approved, indexed in specs/adrs/README.md, and referenced
  from [[module-document-core]]'s Key Decisions.
  [ ] All 24 acceptance criteria are cited from tests at their declared level,
  with no uncovered AC and no orphaned citation.
  [ ] The profile self-application gate runs over this repository's own specs/
  corpus and is green at the severities these checks assign.
  [ ] agent-plugins-dgn and agent-plugins-3md are closed or re-scoped; agent-
  plugins-j7f is confirmed resolved; the nine out-of-scope issues remain open
  and unabsorbed.
  [ ] The feature blueprint's status is retired.
  [ ] The retro-spec skill has been run over the implementation phase,
  aggregating the retro findings recorded on this feature's items.

# agent-plugins-9kb.8 — Add the refs subcommand and wire the new rules into the run report

## Original description

**Blueprint:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-blueprint.md — delta **CMD**, section "Command Surface in [[container-spec-cli]] (modified) — CMD".
**FRD:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 2 of 2); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-reference-integrity`.

Expose the graph as a fifth subcommand and wire the new rules into the accounting the command surface already does. This extends the surface REQ-SPEC-011 fixed **without renaming or repurposing any of its four subcommands**, which is the growth that requirement anticipated.

**The command surface holds no domain logic:** refs converts a slug and a direction into a corpus lookup and the result into stdout. A check that lives here rather than in a module is a layering defect, because it would be unavailable to a future API or MCP wrapper.

**Verification timing.** This item proves AC-SPECREF-003.1 through -003.5 and -004.3 (all integration) and owes those citations. Every other criterion it participates in is proved by an item already in its dependency closure, so it carries no waiting-on note. This is the last code item in the feature.

**Coordination — agent-plugins-krb:** this item alters observable output. Run scripts/regenerate-cli-snapshots.sh and review every diff **in this change**.

### Design

Anchors: cli/cmd (Execute and the existing four subcommands, Registry and Load for the profile-activation path); snapshot cases under cli/testdata/cases/; scripts/regenerate-cli-snapshots.sh.

**The `refs` subcommand:**

- Takes one slug, returning **by default** every corpus member whose body or registered frontmatter properties reference it (AC-SPECREF-003.1), and returning the documents that slug references instead when `--outbound` is given (AC-SPECREF-003.2).
- `refs --json` emits each returned reference with its **file path and span** (AC-SPECREF-003.3).
- Opens the corpus **warm** and answers within the budget AC-SPEC-009.1 sets for a corpus query (AC-SPECREF-003.4).
- WHEN no corpus member references the named slug, reports that and **exits zero** (AC-SPECREF-003.5).
- WHEN no corpus member **declares** the named slug at all, reports that **distinctly** from the case above — these are different answers.
- WHEN the named slug is undeclared, still **exits zero**, matching the contract slug-exists sets in AC-SPEC-007.2.
- Appears in the subcommand listing with its own flags, **derived from the same declaration that defines it**, per the container's Change Guidance (AC-SPEC-011.5). No hand-written help text.

**Rule accounting and profile activation:**

- Declare the **three** new rule identifiers (reference/unresolved, reference/retired-target, reference/type-mismatch) plus reference/pairing-incomplete to the run report, so `--only` names them and `--strict` reaches the reference/retired-target warning.
- WHEN activating a profile whose registration the XPT validation **rejects**, report each defect as a finding naming the offending key, positioned at the `[profile].name` value in specs.toml — the only file position a compiled-in registration has (AC-SPECREF-004.3).
- IF a registration defect is reported, do **not** fall back to a default for the offending key.

### Notes

tier: standard — Broad but shallow: one new cobra subcommand with two flags, rule declaration, and a profile-activation defect path, with all domain logic already built in the modules. Six integration ACs, each individually pinned including the exit-zero and distinct-message cases.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `spec refs <slug>` returns every corpus member referencing that slug, from body or registered frontmatter properties (proves AC-SPECREF-003.1, integration).
- [x] `spec refs <slug> --outbound` returns the documents that slug references instead (proves AC-SPECREF-003.2, integration).
- [x] `spec refs <slug> --json` emits each reference with its file path and span (proves AC-SPECREF-003.3, integration).
- [x] refs answers from the warm index within the AC-SPEC-009.1 corpus-query budget (proves AC-SPECREF-003.4, integration).
- [x] A slug no member references is reported as such and exits zero (proves AC-SPECREF-003.5, integration).
- [x] A profile registration defect is reported as a finding naming the offending key, positioned at `[profile].name` in specs.toml, with no fallback to a default (proves AC-SPECREF-004.3, integration).
- [x] An undeclared slug is reported distinctly from a declared-but-unreferenced one, and both exit zero.
- [x] refs appears in the subcommand listing with its own flags, derived from its declaration; no hand-written help text is added.
- [x] All four new rule identifiers are declared to the run report; `--only` can name each, and `--strict` reaches the reference/retired-target warning.
- [x] The existing four subcommands are neither renamed nor repurposed.
- [x] scripts/regenerate-cli-snapshots.sh has been run with every resulting diff reviewed in this change.
- [x] All citations use the AC: marker adjacent to the test declaration per [[testing-standards]].
- [x] [[container-spec-cli]] is folded: Command Surface records the refs subcommand and the profile-registration finding; the Components prose reflects the widened module surfaces. (ContainerBlueprint declares no version property, so no bump is possible — agent-plugins-e0t.)
