title: Declare the reference, finding and registration models in Strata
description:
# agent-plugins-9kb.1 — Declare the reference, finding and registration models in Strata

**Blueprint:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-blueprint.md
— delta **MODEL**, section "Reference, finding and registration models in
Strata (added) — MODEL".
**FRD:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 2); this feature's closure set is
`bd list --label feature-spec-reference-integrity`.

Three generated models have to grow before any Go code in this feature can be
written, and all three are declared in Strata and regenerated by one script per
[[adr-016]] — so they change at their source, in one block, rather than being
edited into the generated output. The index gains somewhere to put a reference,
the finding model gains variants for the defects this feature reports, and the
profile registration model gains the two lifecycle facts Document Core cannot
know without being told.

**Regeneration is the whole risk in this block.** This item was blocked on
agent-plugins-j7f: `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` had no strata version floor, and
run with an older binary it regenerated the bundled schema with every inherited
envelope property dropped while reporting success. Committing a destroyed schema
would silently disable the frontmatter checks CI depends on. j7f is closed
(69098fe) and the script now carries a post-generation sanity assertion.

**Verification timing.** This item proves no acceptance criterion on its own. It
participates in AC-SPECREF-001.1, -001.3, -001.5, -001.7, -003.3 and -004.1, each
of which is proved by a later item (REX, RES, XPT, CMD).

**Coordination — agent-plugins-a7m** (out of scope, not fixed here):
`generate-schemas.sh` wipes `cli/core/specmodel`, so a test placed beside the
generated models is destroyed on the next run. Tests for the reference model
therefore live in the consuming packages, as they already do.

**Coordination — agent-plugins-h6c** (out of scope, not fixed here): promoting
the index to a contract document with a formal versioning policy still waits on a
second, independently-built consumer. [[adr-018]] settles the reference shape
only, and the additive-under-1.0 rule this item obeys is what makes shipping
before then safe.

**Supersedes agent-plugins-dgn** — "model references as a separate edge
collection, not only object properties". [[adr-018]] takes exactly that decision
and this item implements it. dgn is left open; the epic's Definition-of-Done item
(agent-plugins-9kb.10) owns closing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `schemas/index.strata` declares a `Reference` carrying path, text, slug,
      anchor, origin, position and resolution, and a top-level `references` list
      on `SpecIndex`.
- [x] `schemas/finding.strata` declares the four new `FindingDetail` variants
      (unresolved reference, retired target, incomplete pairing, reference-type
      mismatch).
- [x] `schemas/profile.strata` declares `live_statuses`, `retired_statuses` and
      `successor_property` on `ProfileRegistration`.
- [x] `schema_version` remains `"1.0"`, and the reason (additive under
      [[container-spec-cli]]'s rule) is recorded in the fold rather than left as
      an omission.
- [x] Generated artifacts are regenerated from the Strata sources and committed,
      and the generation check passes.
- [x] The regenerated schema retains every inherited envelope property —
      verified explicitly.
- [x] [[module-document-core]] is folded: the Corpus index-model vocabulary gains
      `Reference` and the `references` collection; the Findings vocabulary gains
      the new `FindingDetail` variants; Key Decisions gains [[adr-018]]; version
      set to 0.3.
- [x] No test is placed beside the generated models in `cli/core/specmodel`.

## Retro

### Approach taken

1. Read the bead, the blueprint's MODEL delta, the whole FRD, ADR-018, the three
   `.strata` sources and the fold target (`module-document-core.md`).
2. Probed the strata compiler on PATH with a scratch schema
   (`/tmp/.../scratchpad/emptystruct`) to confirm that a **field-less struct** is
   accepted as a union variant and generates clean Go and JSON Schema. It is —
   this is what made a discriminated `ReferenceOrigin` / `ReferenceResolution`
   possible rather than a flat enum plus a bag of optional siblings.
3. Wrote the three source deltas, regenerated, reviewed the whole regeneration
   diff, then made the minimal emitter-side updates the new required property
   forced.
4. Folded `module-document-core.md`.

### Model shape as landed

`schemas/index.strata` (all new declarations placed between `IndexExclusion` and
`SpecIndex`, keeping the file's existing dependency order):

- `ReferenceBodyOrigin` (empty) / `ReferenceFrontmatterOrigin { property }`, and
  `@discriminator("kind") union ReferenceOrigin { body, frontmatter-property }`.
- `ReferenceResolved { target_path }` / `ReferenceUnresolved` (empty) /
  `ReferenceNonMember { path, reason?, parse_error? }`, and
  `@discriminator("state") union ReferenceResolution { resolved, unresolved,
  non-member }`.
- `Reference { path, text, slug, anchor?, origin, position, resolution }`.
- `SpecIndex.references: [Reference]` — **required**, like `entries` and
  `exclusions`.

`schemas/finding.strata`: `FindingUnresolvedReference { slug, origin,
non_member? }`, `FindingRetiredTarget { slug, successor? }`,
`FindingIncompletePairing { property, counterpart, source_path, target_path }`,
`FindingReferenceType { property, slug, expected_type, actual_type }`, plus four
variants appended to the `FindingDetail` union with tags `unresolved-reference`,
`retired-target`, `incomplete-pairing`, `reference-type`.

`schemas/profile.strata`: `live_statuses: [Status]?`, `retired_statuses:
[Status]?`, `successor_property: String?` on `ProfileRegistration`, placed after
`placeholder_patterns` and before `conventions`.

### Implicit decisions and why

1. **`references` is required on `SpecIndex`, not optional.** `entries` and
   `exclusions` are required lists, and the model already carries a test
   (`TestNewEmitsEmptyCollectionsRatherThanNull`) whose whole point is that a
   collection consumers iterate must never be `null`. An optional `references`
   would have cost zero Go changes but reintroduced exactly the absent-vs-empty
   ambiguity that test exists to prevent. Cost: `specindex.New` now seeds
   `References: []specmodel.Reference{}`, `corpus.fromIndex` gained the matching
   nil-guard, one golden string and one shape assertion in `specindex_test.go`
   moved, and the three `index-*` snapshot manifests gained `"references": []`.
   Safe on the warm path: `openWarm` reports no errors and rebuilds on any decode
   failure, so a stale `specs.json` written before this change rebuilds rather
   than erroring.
2. **Origin and resolution are discriminated unions over (sometimes empty)
   structs, not enums with optional siblings.** The blueprint says a reference
   "carries" a property name only in the frontmatter case and an exclusion reason
   only in the non-member case; a union makes the unrepresentable states
   unrepresentable, and it matches the `FindingDetail` pattern already in the
   package. Verified empty structs compile and generate correctly before
   committing to it.
3. **Discriminator names: `"kind"` for `ReferenceOrigin`, `"state"` for
   `ReferenceResolution`.** `kind` matches the existing `FindingDetail`
   convention; `state` reads correctly for a resolution outcome and the two
   unions never share an object, so there is no collision.
4. **`Reference.slug` is `String`, not the constrained `Slug` alias.** A
   reference is hand-written and may name something that is not a well-formed
   slug; constraining it would make the very reference that must be reported
   unrepresentable in the index. Recorded in the property's doc comment.
5. **`FindingIncompletePairing` names both ends explicitly (`source_path` /
   `target_path`) rather than following `FindingDuplicateSlug`'s `other_path`.**
   The finding is emitted against *both* documents (AC-SPECREF-002.5) and the two
   copies must describe the relationship in the same direction; `other_path`
   would invert between them.
6. **`FindingReferenceType` carries `slug` in addition to the three facts the
   blueprint names.** AC-SPECREF-002.10's own example message names the target
   ("target 'adr-009' declares type 'adr'"), and the blueprint's stated intent is
   that each variant is self-contained without reopening a document. Additive, so
   no later item is constrained by it.
7. **New union variants appended at the end of `FindingDetail`** rather than
   interleaved by topic, keeping the change purely additive and the generated
   diff minimal.
8. **No wikilinks in `.strata` doc comments.** Existing doc comments name
   documents in prose ("See the Document Relationship Standard"), and the
   generated markdown ships in the plugin rather than the corpus, so a `[[…]]`
   there would be a reference nothing resolves. Followed the existing convention.
9. **Fold scope held to `module-document-core.md`.** The bead's `c4_docs` also
   names `module-spec-profile.md`, but the AC list names only Document Core, and
   the profile-interface widening (and therefore that document's fold) is
   agent-plugins-9kb.2 (XPT). ADR-018's Context sentence "today it carries
   `entries` and `exclusions`" was left alone: an ADR Context describes the state
   at decision time.

### Gates — each run independently, exit status reported

| Gate | Command | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| format | `cd cli && gofmt -l .` | 0, printed nothing |
| lint | `scripts/check-skills.sh` | 0 (`0 error(s), 1 warning(s)`, the known bead-bonanza length warning) |
| lint | `cd cli && go vet ./...` | 0 |
| build | `cd cli && go build ./...` | 0 |
| regen | `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` | 0 |
| custom | `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` | 0 — "generated artifacts are up to date" |
| test a | `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` | 1 — **known-red baseline, unchanged**: `0 error(s), 1 warning(s)`, no new findings |
| test b | `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` | 0 — all 11 vendored references current |
| test c | `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` | 0 — all 3 vendored strata docs match |
| test d | `cd cli && go test ./...` | 0 — every package ok, including the `cli/profile` self-application gate over this repository's own corpus |

Explicit AC-6 verification (envelope retention), run against the regenerated
bundle rather than trusting the script's own assertion:

```
Adr              required: description, slug, status, title, type, updated_at
FeatureBlueprint required: delivery, description, frd, slug, status, title, type, updated_at
ModuleBlueprint  required: description, kind, slug, status, title, type, updated_at, visibility
SpecIndex        required: schema_version, workspace, entries, exclusions, references
```

### Regeneration diffstat

```
 cli/core/corpus/cache.go                           |   3 +
 cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json             | 455 ++++++++++++-
 cli/core/specindex/specindex.go                    |   3 +-
 cli/core/specindex/specindex_test.go               |   4 +-
 cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go                    | 730 ++++++++++++++++++++-
 cli/testdata/cases/index-default/expected/manifest.json    |   3 +-
 cli/testdata/cases/index-out-custom/expected/manifest.json |   3 +-
 cli/testdata/cases/index-out-stdout/expected/manifest.json |   3 +-
 plugin/skills/spec/references/generated/finding.md |  77 +++
 plugin/skills/spec/references/generated/index.md   | 132 ++++
 plugin/skills/spec/references/generated/profile.md |   3 +
 schemas/finding.strata                             | 124 ++++
 schemas/index.strata                               | 204 ++++++
 schemas/profile.strata                             |  33 +
 specs/architecture/module-document-core.md         |  85 ++-
```

Every deletion in the regenerated output was inspected and is benign: a trailing
comma appearing on `"unverified"` and `"exclusions"` because their JSON lists
grew, and gofmt re-aligning the six existing `isFindingDetailVariant()` marker
methods now that longer type names joined the block. Nothing else moved.

### Differences from the dispatch instructions

- The instructions describe this as a Strata-sources-only change. Making
  `references` a required property forced six small non-generated edits
  (constructor, warm-path nil guard, two test expectations, three snapshot
  manifests). Judged in-scope: without them the tree does not compile clean and
  `go test ./...` cannot pass. No test was added anywhere, and nothing was placed
  in `cli/core/specmodel`.

### Surprises

- The three `index-*` snapshot manifests' `input_hash` values changed even though
  no fixture document did. `Fingerprint` folds the active profile's schema into
  the hash, and the profile's schema is the regenerated bundle — so a model change
  correctly invalidates every warm index. Expected behaviour, but not obvious
  from the failure output, which reads as a corrupted fixture.
- `strata` accepts a field-less struct and emits `{"additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {}}` plus a bare Go `struct{}` that satisfies the union
  interface. Nothing in the vendored language reference states this either way;
  it was established by probe.
design:
Strata sources under `schemas/`; regenerate with `scripts/generate-schemas.sh`,
which rebuilds `cli/core/specmodel/`, `cli/core/schema/` and the plugin
markdown.

**`index.strata`** gains a `Reference` struct and a top-level `references` list
on `SpecIndex`, per [[adr-018]]. A `Reference` carries:

- the `path` of the document the reference occurs in;
- the reference `text` as written, and the `slug` half of it;
- the `anchor` half, uninterpreted and absent where the reference names none
  (AC-SPECREF-002.2);
- the `origin`, distinguishing a reference parsed from the body from one held
  by a named frontmatter property and carrying that property name
  (AC-SPECREF-001.7);
- the `position`, as the existing `Span`;
- the `resolution` — resolved, naming the target's path; unresolved; or
  matched-a-non-member, carrying the exclusion reason or the parse failure
  (AC-SPECREF-002.7).

`schema_version` stays `"1.0"`. This is an addition alongside the existing
shape, which [[container-spec-cli]]'s additive rule permits at the same
version; the model and the emitted index change together in one change, which
is how [[module-document-core]]'s lockstep rule on the index model is satisfied
here. The satisfying act is the recorded no-bump, not an omission — say so in
the fold.

`references` is a list whose order the emitter fixes: [[adr-018]] pins sorting
rows by path and then by position within the document, which satisfies
AC-SPECREF-001.5's document-order requirement and AC-SPEC-009.7's
byte-identical output in one rule.

**`finding.strata`** gains `FindingDetail` variants, each carrying enough to
make its finding self-contained without reopening a document:

- an unresolved reference, carrying the slug, the origin, and — where the slug
  matched a file the index recorded as excluded or unparsable — that reason and
  the file's path (AC-SPECREF-002.1, -002.3, -002.7);
- a retired target, carrying the target's slug and its successor value where it
  declares one (AC-SPECREF-002.6);
- an incomplete pairing, carrying both property names and both documents
  (AC-SPECREF-002.5);
- a reference-type mismatch, carrying the property, the expected `type` and the
  `type` the target declares (AC-SPECREF-002.10).

**`profile.strata`** gains, on `ProfileRegistration`: `live_statuses` and
`retired_statuses`, each a list of `Status`, and `successor_property`, the name
of the property a retired document names its replacement in. These are
profile-level rather than per-type because `status` and `superseded_by` are
envelope properties. `DocumentTypeRegistration` already carries
`reference_properties`, `typed_reference_properties` and `pairings`; this
feature is their first consumer and adds nothing to them (AC-SPECREF-004.1).

Field names and Strata structuring are yours to choose; the carried facts above
are not.

- [ ] `schemas/index.strata` declares a `Reference` carrying path, text, slug, anchor, origin, position and resolution, and a top-level `references` list on `SpecIndex`.
- [ ] `schemas/finding.strata` declares the four new `FindingDetail` variants (unresolved reference, retired target, incomplete pairing, reference-type mismatch).
- [ ] `schemas/profile.strata` declares `live_statuses`, `retired_statuses` and `successor_property` on `ProfileRegistration`.
- [ ] `schema_version` remains `"1.0"`, and the reason (additive under [[container-spec-cli]]'s rule) is recorded in the fold rather than left as an omission.
- [ ] Generated artifacts are regenerated from the Strata sources and committed, and the generation check passes.
- [ ] The regenerated schema retains every inherited envelope property — verify explicitly, since this is the failure `agent-plugins-j7f` describes.
- [ ] [[module-document-core]] is folded: the Corpus index-model vocabulary gains `Reference` and the `references` collection; the Findings vocabulary gains the new `FindingDetail` variants; Key Decisions gains [[adr-018]]. Set `version` to 0.3 if not already set.
- [ ] No test is placed beside the generated models in `cli/core/specmodel` (`agent-plugins-a7m`).
notes: tier: advanced — Foundation every other delta consumes: three generated models at once, plus the regeneration path agent-plugins-j7f shows is silently destructive. The Reference and FindingDetail shapes are pinned by ADR-018 and the blueprint, so the invention is low — but blast radius overrides, and a wrong shape is expensive once seven items depend on it.

title: Spec Corpus Reference Integrity
description:
Build the References component of Document Core: parse every cross-document
reference from a spec corpus, record the resolved graph in the shared index,
and report the references that resolve to nothing.

**Feature blueprint:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-blueprint.md
**FRD:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md

**Delivery unit:** staged — two reviewable increments:

- **Stage 1 — the graph in the index:** MODEL, XPT, REX, RES, PREG.
  `spec index` emits reference edges over this repository's own corpus; no new
  check runs, no finding is raised, and no exit status changes. The stage
  boundary is deliberate: it puts the extraction and resolution rules — the
  ones that produce false positives — in front of a reviewer before any of
  them can fail a build.
- **Stage 2 — checks and query:** CHK, LIFE, CMD. The checks report, `refs`
  answers, and exit status becomes sensitive to references for the first time.

Stage membership is carried as a `stage-N` label on each child. The dependency
edges encode the ordering the blueprint's Sequencing Constraints state; they do
not additionally serialise every stage-1 item ahead of every stage-2 item,
since the stages are review increments rather than a hard build order.

This feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-reference-integrity`.

**Prerequisite:** agent-plugins-j7f (generate-schemas.sh has no strata version
floor) must be resolved before MODEL lands — MODEL regenerates all three Strata
sources, and committing a destroyed schema would silently disable the
frontmatter checks CI depends on. The edge is wired.

**Deliberately out of scope** (each deferred, not overlooked): anchor
resolution beyond splitting on the first `#` (frd-spec-anchor-references),
heading extraction (frd-spec-structure-conformance), suggesting or performing
a repair (frd-spec-slug-rename), references to non-spec files by relative
path, and cross-workspace resolution.

## Success Criteria

title: [bug] PR #14 regressed the warm-index path ~1.8x by emitting UnmarshalJSON on every generated model
description:
Blocking CI on PR #15 (go test, ubuntu-latest), and not caused by that PR.

## Measured

Same machine, same test, back to back:
- 17822a0 (pre-#14): warm query p95 = 24.9 / 23.4 / 23.6 ms
- 08043d6 (post-#14): warm query p95 = 46.3 / 47.4 / 38.8 ms

That is ~1.8x. On the ubuntu CI runner the regression crosses the 50 ms budget of AC-SPEC-009.1: bursts of 82.2 -> 69.6 -> 52.5 ms, converging to a floor of ~52 ms. macOS and Windows are not enforced (referencePlatform), so only the ubuntu leg fails.

## Cause

6940ea8 (#14) regenerated cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go with 35 hand-rolled UnmarshalJSON methods that did not exist before:

  grep -c 'func (v \*.*) UnmarshalJSON' cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go
  17822a0: 0
  HEAD:    35

The file grew 1971 -> 3347 lines. Each of these decodes field by field through map[string]json.RawMessage instead of letting encoding/json decode the struct. corpus.Open unmarshals a 1000-entry SpecIndex on every warm query, so the cost lands directly on the path REQ-SPEC-009.1 budgets.

This was not intended. #14's own commit message says the generated artifacts were regenerated with strata pinned to 8997153 because 'HEAD adds unrelated UnmarshalJSON emission that belongs in its own change'. The emission landed anyway.

## Fix

Regenerate cli/core/specmodel with a strata that does not emit UnmarshalJSON, and re-measure. Needs the strata toolchain, which the session-start hook failed to install in the session that found this (clone failed, CLI unavailable), so it could not be done there. Relates to agent-plugins-j7f (no version floor in generate-schemas.sh) -- the same class of defect: the generated output depends on which strata happens to be on PATH, and nothing gates it.

## Note on the budget itself

Even pre-#14 the margin was not large (23-25 ms against 50 ms locally), and agent-plugins-7ek already owns the question of which platform REQ-SPEC-009 is stated against. Fixing this regression should restore headroom; it does not settle 7ek.
acceptance_criteria: cli/core/specmodel carries no generated UnmarshalJSON methods; warm query p95 returns to the pre-#14 range on the same hardware; go test (ubuntu-latest) passes on PR #15
notes:
CORRECTION AND CONFIRMATION (apples-to-apples).

The earlier 19.7 vs 2.8 ms figure compared the generated decoder against a HAND-WRITTEN shallow mirror that left frontmatter and parse_error as json.RawMessage, so it skipped nested decoding and understated the baseline. Redone properly: the SAME 295,086 bytes decoded into specmodel.SpecIndex at each commit, 20 iterations, same machine.

  17822a0 (0 UnmarshalJSON methods):  best 4.02 ms, worst 7.94 ms
  HEAD    (35 UnmarshalJSON methods): best 19.89 ms, worst 25.43 ms

~5x, delta ~16 ms. The warm query p95 moved 24 ms -> 42 ms, a delta of ~18 ms, so the decoder accounts for substantially all of the regression. Attribution confirmed; only the magnitude of the baseline was wrong (4.0 ms, not 2.8 ms).

Worth noting for whoever fixes this: decode is not the dominant cost of a warm query even now. At 17822a0 a warm query was ~24 ms of which only ~4 ms was decode; the rest is Fingerprint, which reads and hashes every candidate file. Removing the generated decoder returns the warm path to roughly its pre-#14 cost -- it does not create large headroom against the 50 ms budget, which is agent-plugins-7ek's question.

title: RFC-0012 P8: replace the C4 composition rosters with child back-pointers
description:
Adopted at triage of rfcs/inbox/spec/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md (P8) on 2026-08-06. Human approved both new back-pointers at triage.

## Problem
The composition rosters — containers on a system, components and modules on a
container, components on a module — are the last hand-maintained mirrors of an
edge the index derives. Three of the four C4 levels had no back-pointer to
derive a roster from, so removing a roster would have deleted the edge rather
than relocated it. Supplying the missing back-pointers removes that obstacle.

## Evidence (verified by triage 2026-08-06, matches the RFC exactly)
containers: 0 documents. system: 0 documents. components: present and EMPTY on
all three blueprint documents. modules: exactly one non-empty value corpus-wide
— container-spec-cli lists module-document-core and module-spec-profile.

## Change
1. schemas/frontmatter.strata:
   - ContainerBlueprint.system: Slug? — unchanged, already the back-pointer.
   - ComponentBlueprint.container: Slug? — NEW. Names the container OR module
     the component is composed into. Singular (adr-007: a component is
     promoted out of exactly one parent's roster). Optional for the same
     reason 'system' is — a parent with no blueprint of its own is a real
     state, and absence records it.
   - ModuleBlueprint.contained_by: [Slug]? — NEW. Names the containers, or
     modules, that compose this module. A list because a shared module is
     composed into more than one host — the fact adr-009 cites when it denies
     modules a context view and tells them to point at their host
     container(s) instead.
   - REMOVE SystemBlueprint.containers, ContainerBlueprint.components,
     ContainerBlueprint.modules, ModuleBlueprint.components.
   Then run scripts/generate-schemas.sh.
2. Corpus migration (the whole of it):
   - specs/architecture/module-document-core.md: delete 'components: []',
     add 'contained_by: ["container-spec-cli"]'
   - specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md: same
   - specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md: delete 'components: []' and
     the 'modules:' block
3. Templates — update frontmatter and any instruction-block prose naming a
   removed property, and bump each version:
   - system-blueprint-template.md (drop containers) 1.4 -> 1.5
   - container-blueprint-template.md (drop components, modules) 1.5 -> 1.6
   - module-blueprint-template.md (drop components, add contained_by) 0.7 -> 0.8
   - component-blueprint-template.md (add container) 1.5 -> 1.6
4. plugin/skills/spec/references/frontmatter-standards.md: reconcile the
   relationship-property listing with the vocabulary as it now stands. THIS
   bead owns this file's version bump: 0.1 -> 0.2, covering P3/P4/P5/P7/P8.
5. specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md: register
   'container' and 'contained_by' as reference-bearing in AC-SPECREF-004.2.
   Pair neither.

## What this does NOT change
adr-008's block-XOR-link invariant and adr-012's roster-heading convention
govern the parent's BODY, not its frontmatter. The roster SECTION and its
'### <Display Name>' headings are untouched, and a promoted component's
heading anchor keeps resolving.

## Acceptance
- generate-schemas.sh --check clean; sync-shared-references.sh --check clean
- validate-corpus.py passes; no roster property left in the vocabulary
close_reason: Landed in the RFC-0012 triage on 2026-08-06. See the Resolution in rfcs/retired/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md.

title: RFC-0012 P5: remove related from the document envelope
description:
Adopted at triage of rfcs/inbox/spec/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md (P5) on 2026-08-06.

## Problem
'related' is the property that most purely mirrors prose: every value in the
corpus is already cited in the document's body as a [[slug]], and no consumer
keys on it. Under the Document Relationship Standard it satisfies none of the
three justification tests.

## TRIAGE EXTENT FINDING — the real blast radius is 48 files, not 11
Enumerated on 2026-08-06 by matching '^related:' inside YAML frontmatter
across all *.md in the repo:
  - 12 documents under specs/
  - 15 RFCs (9 in rfcs/retired/, all carrying 'related: []' — lossless;
    6 in rfcs/inbox/, three with real values)
  - 13 templates under plugin/skills/*/references/ (all 'related: []')
  - 8 skill reference documents with real values
scripts/validate-corpus.py validates the RFC queue AND the skill reference
files against cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json, whose bundle sets
additionalProperties:false. So every one of these 48 files must migrate in
the same change or the corpus gate fails.

## TRIAGE SUFFICIENCY FINDING
The RFC's claim that every 'related' value is already cited in prose holds
for 47 of 48 files. The exception is specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md,
which lists 'frd-spec-validation-cli' in 'related' and cites it NOWHERE in
its body. Add [[frd-spec-validation-cli]] to that document's ## References
section BEFORE removing the property, or the edge is lost rather than derived.
(module-document-core.md and spec-index-blueprint.md list adr-015/adr-016 in
'related' and cite them in the body but not under ## References — no action
needed; the index parses the whole body.)

## Change
1. schemas/frontmatter.strata: remove DocumentFrontmatter.related. Also fix
   the Adr and Guide struct doc-comments, which both say the type 'carries no
   relationship properties of its own beyond the envelope's related'.
2. Run scripts/generate-schemas.sh.
3. Remove the property from all 48 files. Do not hand-edit anything under
   references/shared/ — run scripts/sync-shared-references.sh after.
4. plugin/skills/spec/references/frontmatter-standards.md: remove 'related'
   from the relationship-property YAML block and the Contents summary line.
   No version bump here — P8 owns this file's bump.
5. Bump the frontmatter 'version' of each of the 8 skill reference documents
   whose own frontmatter loses the property: c4-guide, cross-document-
   references, document-readiness-checklist, ears-guide, template-authoring-
   standards, work-order-definition-of-ready, work-order-field-guide.
   (frontmatter-standards is in that set but its bump belongs to P8.)

## Acceptance
- no '^related:' in frontmatter anywhere in the repo
- generate-schemas.sh --check clean; sync-shared-references.sh --check clean
- validate-corpus.py passes

title: Migrate acceptance criteria in the three FRDs to Gherkin
description:
ADR-020 adoption work. Rewrite the acceptance criteria in the three FRDs under specs/features/ as tagged Gherkin blocks, and update frd-template.md, ears-guide.md, ac-traceability-standards.md and the spec skill to match.

Watch the two forms ADR-020 records as lossy: 26% of criteria are ubiquitous (become Then-only scenarios) and 12% contain SHALL NOT (become @negative-tagged prose in a Then step). Criteria carrying concrete example data should become Scenario Outline with an Examples table rather than prose examples — that is where the migration adds the most value.

ADR-002's scope narrows to non-AC normative statements; update it and both readiness checklists.
acceptance_criteria: All 73 criteria are tagged Gherkin scenarios. spec check passes. ADR-002 records its narrowed scope. Both readiness checklists cover the two notations and name which surface each applies to.
notes:
MAPPING CORRECTION (supersedes the structure implied by earlier notes). REQ maps to Feature, NOT to Rule:

  FRD          -> frontmatter slug + a @frd-<slug> tag on each Feature
  REQ          -> Feature:
  User Story   -> the Feature description (the canonical Cucumber idiom)
  AC           -> Scenario / Scenario Outline
  business rule grouping several ACs -> Rule:
  *Example:*   -> an Examples row
  rationale    -> markdown, or a Rule: name where it truly states a rule

The trial's first pass mapped REQ -> Rule and produced 'Rule: Configuration', 'Rule: Document Index' — topics, where the keyword means an assertion that can be true or false. That also left the user story homeless, since Rule.Description was spent on rationale.

Consequences of the correct mapping: a Gherkin document holds exactly ONE Feature, so one fenced block per REQ is the only legal arrangement; no synthetic wrapper is needed since each block declares its Feature (wrap=0); and the @frd-<slug> tag has a home that pickles inherit. For .feature emission, one FRD yields one file per requirement.

docs/spec-index-frd-gherkin.md has been rewritten to the correct mapping — all 52 ACs still extract.

metadata.tier_reason: translating 55+ prose criteria without changing their meaning, plus template, guide, checklist and skill updates; the lossy forms are named and need judgement

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: The guide said a Scenario description carries "per-criterion rationale only", but gherkin/scenario-prose reports ANY non-empty scenario description, so the slot the guide recommends is unusable. I discovered this by reading content.go rather than from the guide, and rerouted every per-criterion rationale into Feature descriptions and markdown notes. Fixed in the guide as part of this bead.

comments.text: retro: Constraint 14 (a wikilink anywhere in a Gherkin source is a reference) collides hard with the three FRDs whose subject IS wikilink syntax — markdown-links, anchors and rename are built almost entirely from illustrations like [[container-api#Request Router]], and backticks are not a code span inside a block. Every one of those had to move out to markdown beside the block, which is a real loss of locality the ADR's lossy-forms table does not name.

A bead whose acceptance criterion is a count of something the sprint itself keeps changing will always drift; naming the predicate ("no FRD under specs/features/ still carries prose criteria") would have survived.

comments.text: retro: Two traps cost real time and are now in the guide. A Rule: claims every scenario after it whatever the indentation, so dedenting a scenario back to feature level looks right and does nothing — unruled scenarios must be written before the first Rule:. And the guide's own Descriptions example was a live gherkin fence declaring @FEAT-SPEC-001, which became a corpus-wide duplicate identifier the moment spec-index was migrated; the guide already uses a plain-text fence for two other excerpts for exactly this reason and now uses it for the third.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: ADR-021 constraint 6 says a criterion with concrete example data SHOULD become a Scenario Outline, while the guide says below two instances an outline is ceremony. Most of the corpus's examples are single instances, so the two rules point opposite ways on the common case. I followed the guide, folded single examples into Given steps where they added precision, and kept the rest as backticked markdown notes citing their AC id — worth reconciling in one of the two documents.

title: AC index: extract acceptance criteria into the corpus index
description:
ADR-020 adopts Gherkin blocks at level 2. Build AC extraction over fenced ```gherkin blocks using github.com/cucumber/gherkin/go: extract each block from FRD markdown, wrap in a synthetic 'Feature:' header, parse, and walk the AST.

Index each criterion with: AC identifier (from its tag), parent REQ (from the enclosing Rule), typed steps (KeywordType Context/Action/Outcome), Examples rows where present, Description as rationale, tags (@negative, @manual, @level-*), and the source span mapped back with fence_line + (parser_line - 1).

Prototype verified: correct .md line numbers; Pickles() yields one denormalised row per Examples row with tags inherited. Conform the emitted records to cucumber/messages rather than inventing a shape.
design:
Extraction contract verified end to end — see docs/plans/gherkin-extraction-findings.md.

The AST is a plain Go pointer tree with json tags; it round-trips losslessly and its wire shape IS the cucumber/messages schema. Every target field extracts: ac_id from the Scenario tag, req from the enclosing Rule.Name, typed steps from Step.KeywordType (Context/Action/Outcome/Conjunction), examples from TableHeader zipped with TableBody rows, rationale from Rule/Scenario Description.

Five integration details, all with resolutions in the findings doc:
1. Location is START only — no end, no byte offset. Compute Span ourselves; end is line-granular, derived from the last Step or Examples row.
2. Columns count codepoints, matching cli/core/span exactly. No conversion layer needed.
3. Node Ids are positional counters and shift on any edit above them. Key identity on the @AC tag, NEVER on Id — critical for the knowledge graph.
4. The synthetic Feature: wrapper is CONDITIONAL — a block declaring its own Feature: fails with it. Line offset is fence_line + (parser_line - wrap).
5. Do not strip fence indentation; it shifts columns.

Use the AST for the index (preserves general/illustrative split); use Pickles() for publication (resolves it into one row per Examples row with tags inherited).
acceptance_criteria: spec index carries, for every FRD, its acceptance criteria as typed records: id, parent REQ, typed steps, example rows, rationale, tags, span. A query subcommand returns a criterion by id and lists criteria by FRD or REQ.
notes: ADR-020 measured that a fenced-gherkin extractor is ~40 lines and yields correct source line numbers via fence_line + (parser_line - 1). That mapping technique is reusable here regardless of notation: the AC index needs the same span arithmetic to point at a criterion inside a markdown document.

comments.text: Subsumed by agent-plugins-wvd.5 (DISC) @ 4642d13, as the blueprint's Tracker Reconciliation recorded. GHK extracts features and criteria; DISC records them in SpecIndex.features with a second discovery pass for .feature sources, which is the whole of what this bead asked for. Verified in the merged tree: cli/core/corpus/features.go exists, SpecIndex carries the features collection, and the index-features snapshot case covers both source forms.

title: [bug] generate-schemas.sh silently destroys the schema when run with strata older than the inheritance fix
description:
# agent-plugins-j7f — [bug] generate-schemas.sh silently destroys the schema when run with strata older than the inheritance fix

## Full bead description

scripts/generate-schemas.sh has no version floor for strata. Run it with
strata-cli 0.7.0 as installed by .claude/hooks/session-start.sh and it
regenerates cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json with EVERY inherited
envelope property dropped:

```
"Adr": { "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {} }
```

All twelve document types lose title, description, slug, type, status,
updated_at and their required entries — the file goes from 2202 lines to
1326. The script reports success. Committing that would silently disable
frontmatter/missing-property and frontmatter/schema for every document type,
i.e. destroy the checks this repo's CI now depends on.

Root cause is upstream and already FIXED there: strata-lang/strata commit
8997153 'Fix: allowAdditionalProperties: false silently dropped struct
inheritance (#289)'. Our schemas use 'struct Adr: DocumentFrontmatter {}'
together with additionalProperties: false, which is exactly the combination
that regressed. The binary the session-start hook installs predates the fix;
building from the strata checkout at HEAD produces output byte-identical to
what is committed.

Discovered 2026-08-05 while adding a FindingDetail variant for agent-
plugins-5xo: the regeneration required for that change would have shipped
the destroyed schema had the diff not been reviewed. What saved it was
reading the diff, not any gate.

Fix options, roughly in order of value:

1. Version floor in generate-schemas.sh — refuse to run below the
first strata release containing 8997153, naming the commit.
2. A post-generation sanity assertion: every document-type definition
must carry a non-empty required list. Cheap, and catches any future
regression of this shape rather than this one version.
3. Pin the strata version the session-start hook installs.
4. Wire generate-schemas.sh --check into CI. The checks.yml comment
already explains why it is not there (needs a Rust toolchain);
option 2 removes most of the need.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure the strata on PATH predates strata-lang/strata commit 8997153
("Fix: allowAdditionalProperties: false silently dropped struct
inheritance (#289)") — strata-cli 0.7.0, the version
.claude/hooks/session-start.sh installs, is such a build.
Check with strata --version.
2. From the repository root, run scripts/generate-schemas.sh.
3. Observe that the script reports success and exits zero.
4. Inspect the regenerated cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json.

**Expected:** the regenerated file is byte-identical to the committed one
(2202 lines), and every document-type definition retains its inherited
envelope properties (title, description, slug, type, status,
updated_at) and its required list. Building strata from a checkout at
HEAD and re-running produces exactly this.

**Actual:** the file is 1326 lines. All twelve document types lose every
inherited envelope property and their required entries, e.g.
"Adr": { "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {} }. The script
still reports success, so nothing signals the loss.

**Where it manifests:** scripts/generate-schemas.sh (no version floor) →
cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json → the Schema Registry component,
which silently stops enforcing frontmatter/missing-property and
frontmatter/schema for every document type.

### Notes / Decision

Prerequisite for the reference-integrity feature: work order agent-plugins-
9kb.1 (delta MODEL) regenerates all three Strata sources and is blocked on
this. Committing a schema regenerated by an older strata would silently
disable the frontmatter checks CI depends on.

**## DECISION (2026-08-07)**

All four options in the description were put to the user. Selected: 2 + 3.

1. Version floor naming 8997153 — NOT selected. Dominated by option 2: it
guards only the too-old case and would NOT have caught what actually
happened this session, since HEAD (ce18d66) is far above any such floor and
still produced wrong output. Version strings cannot discriminate here —
44c1955 (destroys the schema) and 840f9ba (correct) both report strata-cli
0.7.0.
2. Post-generation sanity assertion: every document-type definition must
carry a non-empty required list — SELECTED. This is the actual guard and
satisfies this bead's acceptance criterion verbatim. Version-independent,
so it catches this SHAPE of regression rather than one known-bad build.
3. Pin the strata the session-start hook installs — SELECTED, with an
adjustment. The user has since decided to adopt strata HEAD (agent-plugins-
tix, wired to block this bead). So "pin" does NOT mean pinning to 840f9ba.
It means making provisioning verifiably correct: the hook builds from the
checkout and stamps the built commit in ~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit,
and a stale stamp must not be able to leave an older binary installed while
reporting success.
4. Wire generate-schemas.sh --check into CI — NOT selected. Needs a Rust
toolchain, the documented reason it is absent from checks.yml, and option 2
removes most of the need. CI-gate expansion is agent-plugins-9ko.

Ordering: agent-plugins-tix adopts HEAD and regenerates. This bead adds the
guard that makes a future bad regeneration fail loudly. Do not redo tix's
work here.

### Acceptance Criteria

generate-schemas.sh fails loudly rather than emitting a schema whose
document types have no properties, when run with a strata that drops struct
inheritance.

---

## Retro

### Approach taken

Implemented both selected options.

**Option 2 (primary guard).** Added a step ("2.5") to `scripts/generate-
schemas.sh`, right after the bundled JSON Schema is built and before it (or
any other output) is synced into the tree. It shells a small inline
`python3` script (no external deps — `json` + `sys` stdlib only, consistent
with `scripts/validate-corpus.py`'s existing use of python3 in this repo)
against the freshly generated `spec-model.schema.json`. The script:

1. Reads `definitions.DocumentType.enum` — the kebab-case list of document
   type values (`"adr"`, `"system-blueprint"`, …).
2. Converts each value to the PascalCase struct name convention this repo's
   schemas use (`"system-blueprint"` → `SystemBlueprint`) to get the list of
   document-type definitions to check.
3. Asserts each such definition exists in `definitions` and has a non-empty
   `required` array. Missing definitions and empty/missing `required` lists
   are both reported (all offenders at once, not just the first), and the
   script exits 1 with a message pointing at the upstream commit, the fact
   that `strata --version` can't discriminate a good build from a bad one,
   and where to check the actual provenance
   (`~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit`).

**Option 3 (provisioning correctness).** Edited `.claude/hooks/session-
start.sh`'s strata-provisioning block. Added a `_fetch_unverified` flag,
set only when the `git fetch` + `git merge --ff-only` step against
upstream explicitly fails (not when the checkout is deliberately built
as-is because it's on a non-default branch or has uncommitted changes —
those are intentional, already self-explanatory in their own log lines,
and not a freshness gap). When the installed binary's stamp matches the
local HEAD *and* that fetch failed, the hook now emits a `WARNING:` line
explaining that the stamp match only proves the binary matches disk, not
that disk is caught up with upstream, instead of the plain "strata CLI
current" success line it printed before. This directly targets "a stale
stamp must not be able to leave an older binary installed while the hook
reports success" without pinning to an old commit and without needing an
actual network failure to reproduce (the branch is structurally new code —
verified with `bash -n` and by reading the modified control flow; the
failure-injection this guards against needs a real fetch failure against
github.com, which is out of scope to fabricate for this bead per the
explicit "Do NOT rebuild strata. Do NOT touch the /home/user/strata
checkout" instruction — this session's strata build is HEAD (ce18d66)
already, per the environmental facts).

### Observed pre-fix failure (RED before GREEN)

Could not cheaply reproduce a real strata-44c1955 build (needs a ~90s
cargo build against a different checkout per the environmental facts, and
the instructions explicitly say not to do this). Instead, synthesized the
exact corruption shape strata 44c1955 is documented to produce, applied it
to a copy of the real generated schema, and ran the assertion logic
against it directly:

```
python3 -c "
import json, copy
d = json.load(open('cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json'))
bad = copy.deepcopy(d)
bad['definitions']['Adr'] = {'additionalProperties': False, 'properties': {}}
json.dump(bad, open('/tmp/bad-schema.json','w'))
"
```

Running the assertion against `/tmp/bad-schema.json`:

```
error: generated schema has document type(s) with an empty or missing 'required' list: Adr
exit=1
```

**This is the rejection** — the guard fires and names the offending type,
exactly as the acceptance criterion requires ("fails loudly ... rather
than emitting a schema whose document types have no properties").

Running the same assertion against the real, correct, committed schema
(copied unmodified):

```
ok - all document types have non-empty required lists
exit=0
```

Then, separately, ran the actual `strata build` toolchain (this session's
HEAD build, ce18d66, which contains the upstream fix) via
`scripts/generate-schemas.sh` for real — the assertion ran silently (no
error) as part of that regeneration, and `scripts/generate-schemas.sh
--check` reported "generated artifacts are up to date" afterward, confirming
the guard doesn't produce false positives against a correct build.

### Implicit decisions and why

- **Where in the script:** placed the assertion immediately after step 2
  (the bundled JSON Schema is written to `$WORK/schema/spec-model.schema.json`)
  and before step 3 onward, so a corrupted bundle is caught before the specs-
  config overlay schema, the Go embed wrapper, the Go structs, or the
  Markdown reference are generated from (or alongside) it, and — critically —
  before `sync_dir` ever copies anything into the tracked tree. Nothing
  downstream of the corruption point runs before the check fires.
- **How to parse the schema:** a dependency-free inline `python3` heredoc
  (stdlib `json` only), matching the instruction to prefer a dependency-free
  approach and the existing precedent of `scripts/validate-corpus.py` using
  python3 in this repo (that script additionally needs `jsonschema`/`pyyaml`
  for its fuller job; this check needs neither).
- **How to identify "document type" definitions without hardcoding names:**
  derived the list from the generated schema's own `definitions.DocumentType`
  enum rather than a hardcoded name list or a second read of
  `schemas/vocabulary.strata`. This keeps the check honest against schema
  evolution (a renamed or newly added document type is picked up
  automatically) while staying self-contained to the one generated artifact
  the script already has in hand. It relies on this repo's existing naming
  convention (struct name = PascalCase of the enum's kebab-case value, e.g.
  `system-blueprint` → `SystemBlueprint`), which held for all 11 current
  document types when checked against `cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json`.
  Chose this over hardcoding partly because the enum itself is structurally
  immune to the bug being guarded against: it's a plain string enum with no
  struct inheritance, so it can't be corrupted the same way and remains a
  trustworthy anchor even in the exact scenario this check exists to catch.
- **Failure message phrasing:** named the upstream commit and PR
  (8997153, "Fix: allowAdditionalProperties: false silently dropped struct
  inheritance (#289)"), explained why `strata --version` can't be used to
  diagnose it, and pointed at `~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit` as the
  actual provenance signal — mirroring the diagnostic path a future agent
  hitting this would need, based on how this bead itself was diagnosed.
- **Bead says "twelve document types"; only 11 struct definitions inherit
  `DocumentFrontmatter`** in the current schema (`Adr`, `Frd`, `Contract`,
  `Standards`, `SystemBlueprint`, `ContainerBlueprint`, `ModuleBlueprint`,
  `ComponentBlueprint`, `FeatureBlueprint`, `Rfc`, `Guide` — confirmed by
  grepping `schemas/frontmatter.strata` and cross-checking
  `definitions.DocumentType.enum`, which also has 11 entries). Did not
  investigate or correct the bead text's count — it's descriptive prose
  about a historical repro, not a checkable claim the fix depends on, and
  the guard's correctness was verified directly (11/11 checked, both
  reject and accept cases confirmed) rather than against that number.
- **Option 3 scope:** interpreted "a stale stamp must not be able to leave
  an older binary installed while the hook reports success" narrowly, as a
  reporting/visibility fix (turn a silent false-success message into an
  explicit `WARNING:` naming exactly why freshness is unverified) rather
  than a behavioral fix that forces a rebuild whenever fetch fails.
  Rebuilding on a failed fetch wouldn't install anything different (the
  local checkout genuinely hasn't moved), so it would only cost ~2 minutes
  for the same binary — the actual gap was that the hook's log claimed
  verified freshness ("strata CLI current") in a case where it had not
  verified anything. Fixing the message is what closes that gap; a real
  behavioral retry/backoff on fetch failure is a larger, separate change
  this bead's scope doesn't call for.

### Deviations from the instructions

None. Followed the workflow as given: claimed, read the bead and its
decision notes in full, red-before-green with a synthetic bad schema
(since reproducing the real historical failure was explicitly ruled too
expensive and off-limits), implemented both selected options, ran the
full regeneration and gate suite, filed a discovered-from bead for the
one unrelated red gate found along the way instead of fixing it here.

### Surprises

- `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` is red on this branch — 3 vendored
  docs (`strata-llm-reference.md`, `language-reference.md`,
  `compiler-options.md`) reported STALE — independently of anything in this
  bead. Confirmed via `git stash` (stash my two edits, rerun the check, same
  3-file failure; pop the stash back) that this predates this bead's work
  and reproduces from `f20abeb` (the `tix` commit) alone, so it's not caused
  by anything here. Filed **agent-plugins-be4** (P2, `discovered-from:
  agent-plugins-j7f`, explicitly noted as adjacent-not-blocking) rather than
  fixing it in this bead's diff, per the "stay strictly in scope" instruction.
- The assertion script needed no `additionalProperties` distinction between
  "genuinely no required fields by design" and "corrupted" — every one of
  this repo's 11 document types happens to require at least the envelope's
  `title`/`description`/`slug`/`type`/`status`/`updated_at`, so "non-empty
  required" cleanly separates good from corrupted for the whole set with no
  false positives to special-case. Worth knowing if a future document type
  is ever added with a legitimately empty `required` list — this guard
  would need widening then, not before.

### Gate results

- `bash -n scripts/generate-schemas.sh` — OK
- `bash -n .claude/hooks/session-start.sh` — OK
- `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` — regenerated cleanly (HEAD strata,
  ce18d66); assertion passed silently
- `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` — "generated artifacts are up to
  date"
- `cd cli && gofmt -l .` — no output (clean)
- `scripts/check-skills.sh` — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s), PASS
- `cd cli && go vet ./...` — clean
- `cd cli && go build ./...` — clean
- `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` — FAIL, but matches the documented
  baseline exactly (0 error(s), 1 warning(s) — the pre-existing
  `bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` line-count warning). No new findings.
- `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` — "all 11 vendored references
  are current"
- `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` — FAIL, pre-existing and unrelated
  (see Surprises above); filed agent-plugins-be4, not fixed here
- `cd cli && go test ./...` — all packages pass

title: Dogfood the Spec CLI: gate this repo's own specs/ corpus in CI
description:
The spec CLI shipped in #9 but nothing runs it against this repository's own corpus. Worse, scripts/validate-corpus.py — the interim gate in .github/workflows/checks.yml — still globs docs/**/*.md, a path the specs/ reorg (4388c06) emptied. It reports 'checked 26 documents' but every one of them is a skill reference or an RFC; zero documents under specs/ have been checked in CI since the reorg.

Add a corpus job to checks.yml that builds cli/spec and runs 'spec index' plus 'spec check --strict' over specs/, and narrow validate-corpus.py to the areas outside the CLI's corpus root (rfcs/, plugin/skills/*/references/).
acceptance_criteria: checks.yml has a job that runs 'spec check --strict' over specs/ and fails the build on a finding; validate-corpus.py no longer globs the empty docs/ path and its scope is documented as complementary to the CLI's
close_reason: checks.yml corpus job builds cli/spec, emits and uploads the index, gates parse errors, and runs spec check --strict; validate-corpus.py narrowed to the areas outside the CLI root with overlap and underpopulation guards

title: Run the profile's schema and slug-pattern checks over the built corpus
description:
# agent-plugins-9d1 — Run the profile's schema and slug-pattern checks over the built corpus

## DESCRIPTION

Discovered while building agent-plugins-bge.8 (#Corpus). ADJACENT, does NOT
block bge.8 — every one of that item's fourteen ACs is proven without it.

The gap: no item in the feature-spec-validation-cli closure owns the
orchestration that runs the Schema Registry over each corpus member. The
blueprint's #Corpus Anchors say the component 'consumes #Frontmatter, the
Schema Registry, #Findings' (specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-
blueprint.md, '#Corpus in module-document-core (added) — CO'), and
specs/architecture/module-document-core.md says the same. But:

- bge.8's acceptance criteria name only membership, index assembly,
  duplicate slugs, the slug query, paths and determinism. The only Finding it
  raises is slug/duplicate. cli/core/corpus therefore does not import
  cli/core/schemaregistry at all.
- bge.12 (command tree) states it 'holds no domain logic — a check that
  lived here would be unavailable to a future API or MCP wrapper', binding
  Change Guidance from specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md. So the check
  loop cannot live in cli/cmd.
- bge.14 assumes it already exists: 'runs the corpus discovery and
  frontmatter checks over this repository's own corpus'.

Scope: a Check entry point in cli/core/corpus (or a sibling under cli/core)
that, for each member with parsed frontmatter, calls
schemaregistry.Registry.Validate with the member's declared type and
schemaregistry.CheckSlugPattern with the profile's per-type pattern, folds
the results into the same finding.Report the duplicate-slug findings already
flow through, and narrows to one file for a single-document check. This
needs the parsed *frontmatter.Document per member, which bge.8's Corpus
keeps internally and does not expose — expect to add an accessor.

Proves AC-SPEC-003.1, AC-SPEC-003.2 and AC-SPEC-003.5 at corpus level (the
Schema Registry item proved them at unit level against a fixture schema).

Blocks bge.12 and bge.14 in practice.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [x] A Check entry point in cli/core runs, for every corpus member with
      parsed frontmatter, the Schema Registry's validation for the member's
      declared type and the profile's per-type slug-pattern check.
- [x] Its findings fold into the SAME finding.Report the duplicate-slug
      findings already flow through — one report, one ordering, not a second
      channel.
- [x] A single-document check narrows output to that file while still
      resolving against the full corpus (the AC-SPEC-001.2 behaviour Corpus
      already implements).
- [x] Corpus exposes whatever accessor this needs for the parsed
      *frontmatter.Document per member; the check loop does NOT re-parse.
- [x] cli/core/corpus gains no dependency on cli/profile — the profile is
      reached through the Profile extension point only.
- [x] Tests cover a corpus with a schema-invalid member, a slug-pattern
      violation, and a clean corpus, cited // AC: AC-SPEC-003.1,
      AC-SPEC-003.2, AC-SPEC-003.5 at corpus level per
      specs/standards/testing-standards.md.
- [x] Ordering stays deterministic with the new findings present.
- [x] cd cli && gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go build ./... && go test ./...
      all clean.

## Retro

**Approach taken.** Added `Check()` and `CheckFor(path)` methods on
`*corpus.Corpus` in a new sibling file `cli/core/corpus/check.go`, alongside
a `Document(path)` accessor added to `corpus.go` itself. `Build` now also
retains, on the built `Corpus`: the active `Profile` (for `Schema()`), the
`map[string]DocumentTypeRules` it already computed once for exclusion
decisions, and a `map[string]*frontmatter.Document` of every member's parsed
frontmatter (populated in `classifyDocument` at the point the envelope
already decodes successfully, at zero extra parsing cost). `Check` compiles
a `schemaregistry.Registry` from the retained profile's schema lazily and
once (`sync.Once`), then for every member with frontmatter calls
`Registry.Validate` and, where the type's rules declare a pattern,
`schemaregistry.CheckSlugPattern`, adding every result into one
`finding.Report` that starts from the corpus's own precomputed
duplicate-slug findings. `CheckFor` reuses the identical path but skips
running the two document-level checks for every member except the one
requested, then narrows the final report to that member's path — so
duplicate-slug detection still sees the whole corpus (per AC-SPEC-001.2)
while schema/slug-pattern checking pays only for the named file.

**Implicit decisions and why.**

1. **Where the entry point lives.** The bead offered `cli/core/corpus` or a
   sibling under `cli/core`. I put it in `corpus` itself (as methods on
   `*Corpus`) rather than a new package, because
   `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`'s Corpus component
   ("Built — cli/core/corpus... Entry, Slug, FindingsFor") is exactly the
   list of query methods `Check`/`CheckFor`/`Document` extend, and the
   bead's own metadata records `c4_changes: ["Corpus"]` — a change to that
   component, not a new one. A sibling package would have needed its own
   accessor surface into `Corpus` internals with no clearer boundary.
2. **Storing `Profile` on `Corpus`.** `Build` already receives
   `opts.Profile` and previously discarded it after extracting
   `DocumentTypes()`. Retaining the whole interface value (not just the
   schema bytes) keeps `Check` symmetric with `Build` — both read the
   Profile extension point and neither imports `cli/profile` — and avoids
   the caller having to pass the profile a second time to `Check`.
3. **Lazy, cached Schema Registry compilation.** Not asked for explicitly,
   but `schemaregistry.New` compiles a JSON Schema and `Corpus` is
   documented as "read many times" from one `Build`. Caching with
   `sync.Once` means a caller invoking `CheckFor` once per file in a
   directory walk (the shape bge.14's own description implies) does not
   recompile the union schema per file. This does NOT touch `Build`'s
   documented error contract — schema-compile failure surfaces from
   `Check`/`CheckFor`, not `Build`, so "Build fails only when it cannot
   start" stays true.
4. **`docs` map keyed identically to `byPath`.** Reused the already-computed
   "reported path" as the map key rather than introducing a second
   normalization scheme, so `Document(path)` calls the same `normalize`
   helper `Entry` and `FindingsFor` already use.
5. **Test fixture for AC-SPEC-003.2 at corpus level.** Mirrored
   `schemaregistry_test.go`'s `TestValidateChecksRawTextAgainstAFormatConstraint`
   fixture (an unquoted numeric-looking value under a `format`-constrained
   property) end-to-end through `Corpus.Check`, rather than inventing a
   different corpus-specific scenario — the point of testing this AC at
   corpus level is proving the *wiring* passes the same `*frontmatter.Document`
   through unmodified, not re-deriving the raw-text substitution semantics
   schemaregistry already unit-tests.
6. **Architecture doc update.** The bead's own ACs did not list a
   "recorded in the architecture blueprint" item (unlike bge.8's and
   bge.11's), but the metadata's `c4_docs` names
   `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` and every closed sibling
   item in this delta updated that file as part of landing. Added two Rel
   edges (`corpus`→`schema`, `corpus`→`find`) to the C4 diagram and a
   paragraph under the Corpus "Built" section describing `Check`,
   `CheckFor`, and `Document`. Kept it minimal — no new component, no
   guarantee-list changes — since the bead's Design section did not ask for
   more.

**What differed from instructions.** Nothing structurally; the description's
approach was followed as given. One judgment call: the description says
"expect to add an accessor" (singular) for the parsed document — I added
`Document` as that accessor, and additionally stored `types` and `profile`
on `Corpus` (not explicitly named in the bead) because `Check` cannot be a
method on `*Corpus` without them, and the alternative (passing `Profile`
into `Check(profile)` as a parameter every call) seemed to needlessly
duplicate state `Build` already validated.

**Anything surprising.** The `$schema` draft declaration in a union schema
is load-bearing for whether `format` is enforced as an assertion at all
(`santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6` treats format as annotation-only without an
explicit draft that requires it). My first attempt at the AC-SPEC-003.2
fixture used a schema with no `$schema` key and got a `type` constraint
violation instead of the intended `format` one — the coerced non-string
value's *type* failure masked whether raw-text substitution had even run.
Only comparing against `schemaregistry_test.go`'s exact fixture (which does
declare `"$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"`) surfaced
this. Worth noting for anyone hand-writing a JSON Schema fixture for this
codebase: omit `$schema` and `format` silently stops being an assertion,
which fails in the "wrong" direction (looks like the raw-substitution logic
isn't running) rather than an obvious error.

No friction worth a `retro:` comment on the bead — the description's scope
and constraints held up exactly as written once the `$schema` fixture
detail above was worked out locally (not a defect in the description or
any spec, just a JSON Schema library detail encountered while writing a
fixture).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A Check entry point in `cli/core` runs, for every corpus member with
      parsed frontmatter, the Schema Registry's validation for the member's
      declared type and the profile's per-type slug-pattern check.
- [ ] Its findings fold into the SAME `finding.Report` the duplicate-slug
      findings already flow through — one report, one ordering, not a second
      channel.
- [ ] A single-document check narrows output to that file while still
      resolving against the full corpus (the AC-SPEC-001.2 behaviour Corpus
      already implements).
- [ ] Corpus exposes whatever accessor this needs for the parsed
      `*frontmatter.Document` per member; the check loop does NOT re-parse.
- [ ] `cli/core/corpus` gains no dependency on `cli/profile` — the profile is
      reached through the `Profile` extension point only.
- [ ] Tests cover a corpus with a schema-invalid member, a slug-pattern
      violation, and a clean corpus, cited `// AC: AC-SPEC-003.1`,
