title: Facts built from argvOf can still carry an empty invocation at sites f9lq did not enumerate
description:
agent-plugins-f9lq repaired the five sites its own analysis named, and
agent-plugins-4ca8 the sixth. The SHAPE is not exhausted: `argvOf` returns nil
for any record whose `Invocation.Name` is empty, and several more facts in
cli/swarm/cli are cited from it with no guard between.

## Evidence

`func mustRecord(report plan.Report, name string) plan.Record` in
cli/swarm/cli/dispatch.go DROPS the "record absent" signal:

    rec, _ := report.Record(name)
    return rec

An absent record yields the zero plan.Record, whose Invocation.Name is empty,
so argvOf answers nil for it. Three facts in `func acceptDispatch`
(cli/swarm/cli/accept.go) are cited from exactly that, with no nil guard:

    targetInv:  argvOf(mustRecord(report, targetStep.Answer())),
    branchInv:  argvOf(mustRecord(report, branchStep.Answer())),
    caseInv:    argvOf(caseRec),

reaching

    Text(\"target\", target, targetInv),
    Text(\"dispatch_branch\", dispatchBranch, m.branchInv),
    Text(\"case\", m.name(), m.caseInv))

A nil there is [][]string{nil} — length 1, argv empty — which trips
Result.Validate's second rule, and `func finish` in cli/swarm/cli/command.go
then replaces the whole result with a bare refusal.

Other unguarded argvOf-into-a-fact sites to audit, anchored on the surrounding
call rather than on a line number:

- cli/swarm/cli/accept.go: Flag(\"merged\", true, argvOf(ffRec)),
  Flag(\"merged\", false, argvOf(rec)), Text(\"unmerged_bead\", ...),
  Text(\"landed_bead\", ...)
- cli/swarm/cli/phase.go: List(\"released_ready\", released, beforeInv, afterInv),
  where both come from `func readyBeads` returning argvOf(rec)
- cli/swarm/cli/branch.go and cli/swarm/cli/ready.go: the argvOf results feeding
  their own facts
- cli/swarm/cli/dispatch.go: writeInv

## Reachability

Same standing as f9lq's five and 4ca8's sixth: LATENT. No path was found that
drives any of them today. They are broken defences, which is why this is P2.

## Two remedies, and the one f9lq deliberately deferred

f9lq's Design REJECTED the constructor-level rule — making the seven Fact
constructors in cli/swarm/cli/result.go refuse an empty invocation set at build
time — on measured grounds: the constructors return a bare Fact with no error
channel, and `grep -cE '\\b(Text|Count|Flag|List|Structured|Unestablished|Invalid)\\('`
over the nine non-test files in cli/swarm/cli counts 117 construction lines. It
said explicitly: \"If the constructor-level rule is still wanted afterwards, it
is a separate order.\" This is that order's home, and the decision between the
two shapes is open:

1. Repair each remaining site where it is written, as f9lq did — using
   `invocationOf(step, rec)` where the step is in scope, and refusing where no
   citation can honestly be made.
2. Adopt the constructor-level rule and stop repairing sites one at a time.

Deciding between them is part of this order, not settled by it. Where (1) is
chosen, `func mustRecord` is worth reconsidering on its own: a helper whose
whole job is discarding the signal that a record is missing is what makes this
class silent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every fact built in cli/swarm/cli names at least one non-empty
      invocation, or its site refuses naming what could not be cited.
- [ ] The choice between the per-site and constructor-level remedies is
      recorded with its reasoning.
- [ ] Result.Validate is unchanged.
- [ ] A unit test covers each repaired site on the never-ran-record path.
      cli/swarm/cli/citation_test.go carries the pattern, and records which
      paths are unreachable by construction and why.

title: Five more Swarm CLI facts can be built with zero invocations, the same way merged_sha could
description:
Five facts in the Swarm Command Surface are built from an invocation slice that
nothing guarantees is non-empty, and `Result.Validate` refuses each one
identically. The sixth instance of this shape was repaired by
agent-plugins-4ca8; these five were not.

`func (r Result) Validate` in `cli/swarm/cli/result.go` holds the two rules that
refuse them:

    for _, f := range r.Facts {
        if len(f.Invocations) == 0 {
            return fmt.Errorf("cli: fact %q names no invocation that established it", f.Name)
        }
        for _, argv := range f.Invocations {
            if len(argv) == 0 {
                return fmt.Errorf("cli: fact %q names an empty invocation", f.Name)
            }
        }

`func finish` in `cli/swarm/cli/command.go` then replaces the WHOLE result with a
bare refusal, so one unciteable fact costs every other fact beside it.

## The two producers

Both can answer with nothing. Anchor on the function names; the line numbers are
hints only.

- `func invocationsOf(records []plan.Record) [][]string` in
  `cli/swarm/cli/ready.go` (~line 668). Its doc comment says it reads "every
  record's resolved invocation, skipping a step that never ran". It returns an
  EMPTY slice when no record ran — tripping Validate's first rule.
- `func argvOf(rec plan.Record) []string` in `cli/swarm/cli/phase.go` (~line 442),
  "nil for a step that never ran (refused by a dry run, or skipped)". As a single
  element that becomes `[][]string{nil}` — length 1, argv empty — tripping
  Validate's second rule.

## The five sites

1. **`func acceptDispatch`, `cli/swarm/cli/accept.go`** (~line 234). Builds
   `queueInv := invocationsOf(qRecords)` and splats it into
   `Flag("drained", true, queueInv...)` (~line 254). The same `queueInv` is also
   passed to `func notDrained`, which builds three facts from it —
   `Flag("drained", false, inv...)`, `List("holding", held, inv...)` and
   `Count("holding_count", len(held), inv...)`. `qRecords` comes from
   `tracker.AgentQueue`, whose step declarations are not in scope here.

2. **`func recheckDispatchBeads`, `cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go`** (~line 434).
   Builds `beadsInv := invocationsOf(recs)`, appends it into `inv` (~line 478),
   and that `inv` feeds `Count("beads_checked", len(beads), inv...)` and
   `List("acceptance_failures", failures, inv...)`. `recs` comes from
   `tracker.Descendants`; its steps are not in scope here either. The other three
   contributors to `inv` (`commitInv`, `wtInv`, `ancestorInv`) are each appended
   under an `if ... != nil` guard, so none of them rescues an empty `beadsInv`.

3. **`func reportAgentQueue`, `cli/swarm/cli/ready.go`** (~lines 592-593). Builds
   `queueInv := invocationsOf(qRecords)` and `establishedInv := invocationsOf(dRecords)`,
   feeding four facts: `Flag("established", ...)`, `Structured("queue", ...)`,
   `Count("queue_count", ...)` and `Flag("drained", ...)`. Same two tracker
   helpers, same absent steps.

4. **`func closePhases`, `cli/swarm/cli/phase.go`** (~line 189). Builds
   `closableInv := argvOf(closableRec)` and reaches
   `List("closed_epics", closedIDs, append([][]string{closableInv}, closeInvs...)...)`
   (~line 225), and `leftOpenInv = [][]string{closableInv}` (~line 229). The guard
   above it is `if !ok || closableRec.Failed()`, and `func (r Record) Failed` in
   `cli/swarm/plan/plan.go` opens with `if r.Status != StepRan { return false }` —
   so a record that never ran passes the guard and yields `[][]string{nil}`.
   Unlike sites 1-3, the step IS in scope here: `closableStep := tr.ClosableEpics("closable", req.Run)`.

5. **`func reasonsFor` and `func closeEligible`, `cli/swarm/cli/phase.go`**
   (~lines 307 and 368). Both accumulate with
   `if argv := argvOf(rec); argv != nil { invs = append(invs, argv) }`, so both
   slices are empty when nothing ran. `closeEligible` additionally `continue`s on
   any record whose `rec.Status != plan.StepRan`. In both functions the steps are
   in scope as a local `steps` slice built alongside the record keys
   (`"reason-%d"` and `"close-%d"`), so `steps[i]` pairs with each record.

## Steps to Reproduce

Unit-level, in `cli/swarm/cli`. These paths are LATENT — see Reachability below —
so the state is constructed rather than driven through the command line. The
proven pattern is agent-plugins-4ca8's own regression test,
`TestASkippedMergedHeadResolveStillCitesAnInvocation` in
`cli/swarm/cli/accept_test.go`.

1. Take any one of the five sites — site 3, `reportAgentQueue`, is the smallest.
2. Arrange its records so that every record's `Invocation.Name` is empty (the
   state `argvOf` answers nil for: a step refused by a dry run, or skipped), so
   the producer returns an empty slice.
3. Let the function build its facts and call `Result.Validate` on the result.

Expected: the result validates, and every fact names at least one non-empty
invocation a reader could re-run.

Actual: `Validate` returns `cli: fact "<name>" names no invocation that
established it` (site 1-3, 5) or `cli: fact "<name>" names an empty invocation`
(site 4), and `finish` replaces the whole result with a bare refusal — losing
every other fact the command established.

## Reachability

LATENT, not live — the same standing as the bead this was discovered from. Each
site's records come from Read steps, which a dry run executes and which explain
mode does not record at all; in explain mode the earlier `!ok` guards refuse
first. No path was found that drives any of the five today. They are broken
defences rather than reproducible failures, which is why this is P2 and not P1.

## Discovered from

agent-plugins-4ca8, while fixing the sixth instance. Adjacent, not blocking:
that bead's own acceptance criteria are met without any of these.
design:
CHOSEN: repair each site where it is written, sourcing the citation from the step
declaration already in scope, and refusing where no citation can honestly be
made. No signature changes; the work stays inside cli/swarm/cli.

Two remedies, split by whether the site has its steps in hand. This split is
settled here — do not re-litigate it:

- **Sites 4 and 5 (`closePhases`, `reasonsFor`, `closeEligible` in
  `cli/swarm/cli/phase.go`): use `invocationOf`.** `func invocationOf(step
  plan.Step, rec plan.Record) []string` in `cli/swarm/cli/dispatch.go` already
  answers "the argv a step ran with, or — for a write a dry run refused — the
  argv it would have run with". The steps are in scope at all three: `closableStep`
  in `closePhases`, and the local `steps` slice indexed alongside `"reason-%d"` /
  `"close-%d"` in the other two. This is exactly the substitution agent-plugins-4ca8
  made for `merged_sha`.

  Note `invocationOf` itself returns nil when a step carries a reference argument
  (`if a.IsRef() { return nil }`), so it is a guarantee only for steps whose
  arguments are literals. Check that holds for these three; where it does not,
  the site falls to the refusal remedy below rather than shipping a
  `[][]string{nil}`.

- **Sites 1, 2 and 3 (`acceptDispatch` and `notDrained` in
  `cli/swarm/cli/accept.go`, `recheckDispatchBeads` in
  `cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go`, `reportAgentQueue` in
  `cli/swarm/cli/ready.go`): refuse rather than invent.** Their records come back
  from `tracker.AgentQueue` and `tracker.Descendants`, which return records but
  not the steps that produced them. Guard the empty case at the call site and
  return `RefuseUnrepairable` naming what could not be cited — a read that
  produced no invocation means the query never reached its answer, and reporting a
  fact from it would be the silent-success failure the Swarm Command Surface
  exists to remove ("defaulting to success is the silent failure this container
  exists to remove", specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md). Do NOT widen
  `tracker.AgentQueue` / `tracker.Descendants` to also return their steps: six
  call sites across three packages, and it puts a change into
  component-tracker and component-status-collector for a path that cannot be
  reached today.

REJECTED: a constructor-level rule making the `Fact` constructors in
`cli/swarm/cli/result.go` reject an empty invocation set at build time. It is the
shape that would have caught all six at once, and it does not fit. Measured: the
seven constructors (`Text`, `Count`, `Flag`, `List`, `Structured`, `Invalid`,
`Unestablished`) each return a bare `Fact` with no error channel, and
`grep -cE '\b(Text|Count|Flag|List|Structured|Unestablished|Invalid)\('` over the
nine non-test files in `cli/swarm/cli` counts 117 construction lines
(accept.go 19, accept_settle.go 16, branch.go 12, dispatch.go 10, manifest.go 15,
phase.go 3, ready.go 9, result.go 7, status.go 26). Adding an error return means
touching all of them; panicking instead converts a degraded report into a crash,
which is worse than the defect. Neither is one session's work. If the
constructor-level rule is still wanted afterwards, it is a separate order.

ALSO REJECTED: relaxing `Result.Validate`. The two rules it enforces are contract
obligations the container states for every command; the defect is the caller
building an unciteable fact, not the validator catching it.

OUT OF SCOPE, state it and move on: the blast-radius half of this — that one
unciteable fact costs every other fact in the result, because `finish` substitutes
a bare refusal. That is one place, not five, and it is a separate order.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each of the five sites builds every fact with at least one non-empty invocation, or refuses with the unrepairable outcome naming what could not be cited — no site can produce a fact carrying zero invocations or an empty argv.
- [ ] Site 4's `closed_epics` and left-open facts no longer reach `Result.Validate` as `[][]string{nil}` when the eligibility record never ran.
- [ ] `Result.Validate` is unchanged.
- [ ] A unit test in `cli/swarm/cli` covers each of the five sites on the never-ran-record path, asserting the result validates and the fact names a re-runnable invocation — following `TestASkippedMergedHeadResolveStillCitesAnInvocation` in `cli/swarm/cli/accept_test.go`.
- [ ] `tracker.AgentQueue` and `tracker.Descendants` keep their current signatures; no file outside `cli/swarm/cli` is changed.
- [ ] The project's declared checks pass: format, vet, build, test-go (judge on ubuntu and macOS; go test (windows-latest) is red on this branch for a diff-independent reason tracked separately).

metadata.tier_reason: five sites across four files in one component, but the design is pinned and the remedy mirrors an in-repo pattern (invocationOf, as agent-plugins-4ca8 applied it); the care is in tests that reach a latent never-ran-record path, not in the change itself

retro:unverifiable The acceptance criterion "a unit test covers each of the five sites on the never-ran-record path" cannot be satisfied as declared for sites 1, 2 and 3: that path is unreachable by construction, by three independent guards.

evidence: three arrangements were tried and each was blocked.

1. Drive the real helpers into the never-ran state. Both tracker.Descendants and tracker.AgentQueue (cli/swarm/tracker/descend.go, queue.go) refuse a record that did not run, because such a record carries a nil Value:

       func BeadsFrom(value any) ([]Bead, error) {
           if value == nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("tracker: the step produced no value") }

   plus AgentQueue's own `answered` map check ("a queue is not reported from one half"). So a skipped or refused record makes the helper return an ERROR, and all three sites return on that error before the citation is built.

2. Use a dry run to refuse the reads. Both helpers hardcode plan.ModeExecute in their own runner.Run calls, so req.Mode never reaches them.

3. Arrange a record that RAN but carries an empty Invocation.Name — the state the bead's own Steps to Reproduce prescribes ("Arrange its records so that every record's Invocation.Name is empty"). cli/swarm/plan/run.go sets `inv := swarmexec.Invocation{Name: s.Executable, ...}`, so this needs a step declaring no executable. Measured: a fake tracker returning such steps produced

       reason = "tracker: walking below run-uncited: plan: step \"children-0-0\" has no executable"

   from cli/swarm/plan/plan.go:400 — plan.Plan.Validate refuses it before anything runs.

Decision taken rather than escalated: sites 1-3 are covered at their guard (TestInvocationsRequiredRefusesAReadNoRecordCites) and on the reachable path end to end (TestAcceptCitesEveryFactItReports, TestAcceptCitesEveryFactWhenTheDispatchHasNotDrained, TestReadyAgentCitesEveryFactItReports, which assert every fact in the emitted JSON envelope names a non-empty invocation). — so a missing record yields the zero plan.Record, whose Invocation.Name is empty, which is exactly the state argvOf answers nil for. Three facts in acceptDispatch (cli/swarm/cli/accept.go) are cited from it with no guard between:

    targetInv:  argvOf(mustRecord(report, targetStep.Answer())),
    branchInv:  argvOf(mustRecord(report, branchStep.Answer())),
    caseInv:    argvOf(caseRec),

reaching Text("target", ...), Text("dispatch_branch", ...) and Text("case", ...) directly. Same standing as the five: latent, not live.

Not implemented here — this bead's AC names five sites and its Design pins a remedy per site, so repairing more would be a wider change than the order authorises, and the constructor-level alternative the Design rejected is the live question for the follow-up rather than for this one.

title: A failed post-fold resolve leaves swarm dispatch accept at OutcomeClear with an empty resolution
description:
In `foldIn` in `cli/swarm/cli/accept.go` (near line 620 today; anchor on the
symbols, the line moves — a sibling bead edits this same function), a failed
post-fold resolve leaves the accept reporting success with nothing to act on.

The branch reads:

    landed, lerr := revision(report, landedSteps, target+" after the fold")
    if lerr != nil {
        facts = append(facts, Unestablished("merged_sha", lerr.Error(), landedInv...))
    } else {
        facts = append(facts, Text("merged_sha", landed, landedInv...))
    }

The `lerr != nil` arm appends an unestablished fact and nothing else: the
outcome stays `OutcomeClear`, the command exits 0, and the resolution is empty.

Everywhere else in this package an unestablished fact takes `OutcomeAttention`
with a resolution naming the remedy — `breakerUnread` in `cli/swarm/cli/ready.go`
and `landingVerdict` in `cli/swarm/cli/branch.go` both do. A scripted caller (the
e2e consumer that unmarshals `merged_sha`) therefore sees success plus a null
sha, with nothing naming a remedy.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Drive `swarm dispatch accept` to a completed fast-forward.
2. Make the post-fold `revision(report, landedSteps, ...)` read fail, taking the
   `lerr != nil` arm.
3. Read the result and the exit status.

Expected: `OutcomeAttention`, a non-empty resolution naming the unestablished
`merged_sha` and what to run, and the package's attention exit status.
Actual: `OutcomeClear`, exit 0, empty resolution, `merged_sha` unestablished.

Found by the code-review pass on 2622f6c..37a9d83 that run e6xt never ran
(review_budget exhausted; retro candidate C13, accepted on PR #33).
design: In the lerr != nil arm, take OutcomeAttention and set a resolution, matching what breakerUnread (cli/swarm/cli/ready.go) and landingVerdict (cli/swarm/cli/branch.go) already do for an unestablished fact. Keep the fold's merged: true fact and the summary intact — the fold happened and must still be reported; only the outcome, the exit status and the resolution change. Do not turn this into a refusal: returning an error here would skip settleDispatch, which the comment above the branch forbids.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A failed post-fold resolve reports OutcomeAttention with a non-empty resolution.
- [ ] The exit status matches the package's convention for attention, as breakerUnread and landingVerdict produce it.
- [ ] The resolution names merged_sha's unestablished state and what the caller should run.
- [ ] merged: true and the fold summary are still reported on that path.
- [ ] A unit test in cli/swarm/cli covers the failed post-fold resolve.
- [ ] The project's declared checks pass: format, vet, build, test-go (judge on ubuntu and macOS; go test (windows-latest) is red on this branch for a diff-independent reason tracked separately).

title: swarm dispatch accept abandons a merge that already landed when the post-fold merged_sha resolve fails
description:
## What

`cli/swarm/cli/accept.go`, `foldIn`: the post-fold resolve added for
`merged_sha` is read with

    landed, lerr := revision(report, landedSteps, target+" after the fold")
    if lerr != nil {
        return mergeOutcome{}, records, lerr
    }

`revision` returns a `*Refusal` from `RefuseUnrepairable`, not an
`*acceptStop`, so `acceptDispatch`'s `errors.As(err, &stopped)` does not
match and it falls through to `return Result{}, err`. The whole accept is
then abandoned **after the fast-forward has already landed**:
`settleDispatch` never runs, so there is no ancestry guard, no post-merge
bead re-check, no worktree removal, no branch deletion and no push — and
because the result is a bare refusal, it carries no `merged` fact at all,
so the caller cannot tell that the merge happened.

This return sits AFTER the irreversible write. Before `0b8c2dd`,
`merged_sha` came from `m.branchSHA`, resolved in `readCase` before any
write, so no read taken after a successful fold could fail this way.

## Reachable how

The fast-forward succeeds and the `merged-head` `git rev-parse` then
fails or answers a non-string — a repository the runner momentarily
cannot read, a git invocation killed, a filesystem hiccup. Rare, and the
cost when it happens is a run left in a half-accepted state that reports
nothing about the merge it made.

## Why it matters

The whole point of the accept ceremony's ordering is that the removal
half is "reached only because the fold above did NOT return an error"
(the comment in `acceptDispatch` says so). A read that fails after the
write turns that guarantee inside out: the fold DID succeed, and the
command reports as though it did not.

## Suggested shape (not prescriptive)

Report an unestablished `merged_sha` on an otherwise complete accept
rather than aborting: the fold is established (the `merged` flag and the
fast-forward's own invocation), and only the sha is unknown. Whatever the
choice, a failure of a read taken after an irreversible write must not
erase the record of the write.

## Acceptance

- A `merged-head` resolve that fails after a successful fast-forward
  still reports `merged: true` and still reaches `settleDispatch`.
- `merged_sha` is reported unestablished in that case, naming the resolve
  that could not answer.
- A test covers it (a fake whose `git rev-parse <target>` fails only
  after the merge step).
design:
In `foldIn` (cli/swarm/cli/accept.go), the `default:` branch reads the post-fold
revision and aborts on failure:

    landed, lerr := revision(report, landedSteps, target+" after the fold")
    if lerr != nil {
        return mergeOutcome{}, records, lerr
    }

`revision` refuses through `RefuseUnrepairable`, which produces a `*Refusal`,
not an `*acceptStop` — so `acceptDispatch`'s `errors.As(err, &stopped)` does not
match and the whole accept is abandoned after the fast-forward has landed.

Chosen: degrade the report instead of aborting. Keep `Flag("merged", true,
argvOf(ffRec))` and, when the resolve fails, append `Unestablished("merged_sha",
<reason naming the resolve that could not answer>, <the resolve's invocation>)`
in place of `Text("merged_sha", landed, ...)`. Return a normal `mergeOutcome`
with `ran: true`, so `acceptDispatch` proceeds into `settleDispatch` and the
ancestry guard, the post-merge bead re-check, worktree removal, branch deletion
and push all still run. The summary is unchanged — it asserts only that the fold
happened, which it did.

Hazard to handle rather than inherit: the established path cites the invocation
via `argvOf(mustRecord(report, landedSteps.Answer()))`, and `mustRecord` is not
safe on the failure path — the record may be absent, which is one of the ways
`revision` fails. Read `revision` and `mustRecord` before choosing how to cite;
use the `report.Record(...)` + `invocationOf` form already used elsewhere in
this package, or cite nothing, rather than panicking on the path that exists to
handle a failure.

REJECTED: converting the refusal into an `*acceptStop` so `errors.As` matches.
It still stops the accept — no `settleDispatch`, no removal, no push — so the
half-accepted state the bead names survives; it only makes the abandonment
tidier.

REJECTED: resolving the merged sha before the fold, from `m.branchSHA`. That is
exactly the defect e6xt.10 fixed — the pre-fold branch sha is not the commit on
the target on the rebased arm — and it conflicts head-on with e6xt.20, which
removes that carrier.

Test the acceptance names: a fake whose `git rev-parse <target>` fails only
after the merge step. cli/swarm/e2e/dispatch_accept_test.go already exercises
both arms end to end and carries the merged_sha coverage; put the case there, or
in cli/swarm/cli/accept_test.go if a per-step failure is easier to express
against that fake.

BATCH: second of batch b12. e6xt.20 removes `mergeCase.branchSHA` from this same
file afterwards and re-verifies its deadness against what this bead leaves
behind.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b12
comments.text:
retro:stale this bead's own Design asserts a hazard that does not exist as
stated: mustRecord does not panic on the failure path
evidence: the Design reads "the established path cites the invocation via
argvOf(mustRecord(report, landedSteps.Answer())), and mustRecord is not safe on
the failure path -- the record may be absent, which is one of the ways revision
fails ... rather than panicking on the path that exists to handle a failure."
The same claim reached me in the dispatch prompt, worded "the established path
cites via mustRecord, which PANICS on the failure path".

Measured. cli/swarm/cli/dispatch.go:318 --

  func mustRecord(report plan.Report, name string) plan.Record {
      rec, _ := report.Record(name)
      return rec
  }

It discards the ok and returns whatever Record came back. cli/swarm/plan/plan.go:367 --

  func (r Report) Record(step string) (Record, bool) {
      for _, rec := range r.Records {
          if rec.Step == step {
              return rec, true
          }
      }
      return Record{}, false
  }

An absent record yields the ZERO Record, not a panic. And
cli/swarm/cli/phase.go:442 --

  func argvOf(rec plan.Record) []string {
      if rec.Invocation.Name == "" {
          return nil
      }
      return append([]string{rec.Invocation.Name}, rec.Invocation.Args...)
  }

-- guards the zero value explicitly and returns nil. There is no index, no
dereference and no map access on that path. mustRecord's own doc comment is
"reads a named record out of a report the caller has already established
carries it", which is a PRECONDITION, not a panic.

The underlying concern is real, only misattributed: the failure mode is a
SILENT one. argvOf(mustRecord(...)) on an absent record produces a nil argv
that is still passed as one variadic invocation, so the fact would be attributed
to an empty invocation rather than to none. That is what the fix guards, using
the report.Record(...) + argvOf form the Design also offers:

  var landedInv [][]string
  if rec, ok := report.Record(landedSteps.Answer()); ok {
      if argv := argvOf(rec); argv != nil {
          landedInv = append(landedInv, argv)
      }
  }

so both the established and the unestablished merged_sha cite the resolve when
there is one to cite and nothing when there is not.

  output: 11 hits, all Go call sites in cli/swarm/cli plus the definition and
  its doc comment. No document, skill or reference states the panic claim.
  command: grep -rn "PANICS|panics on the failure path" --include=*.md --include=*.go .
  output: no matches.

UNREACHED COPIES, recorded rather than fixed: the claim also stands in this
bead's pinned Design in the tracker (I have not rewritten a pinned Design) and
in batch b12's dispatch prompt, which is not in the repository and which I
cannot edit. A future agent reading either inherits it. Nothing in the repo
carries it.

comments.text:

The claim originated in the pinned Design written by the loop-2 planner. I then RESTATED IT VERBATIM in this batch's dispatch prompt, as "the planner flagged a hazard the bead itself missed: the established path cites via mustRecord, which PANICS on the failure path" — and I did not run anything to check it. AGENTS.md is explicit that this is the moment the rule binds: "Before you act on such a claim, or restate it anywhere, run the command and read the output." I acted on it and restated it, and did neither.

That is the THIRD inherited-claim failure in this run and the second of mine:
  1. ADP-C found /usr/local/bin/swarm stale, lacking every command the adopted prose instructs a coordinator to run.
  2. I published a false measurement onto e6xt.11 from a stale binary while correcting another agent's flagged concern, and retracted it.
  3. This one — I relayed a planner's unmeasured claim into a dispatch prompt.

title: swarm ready --dry-run --completed hides a stop verdict the recorded count already establishes
description:
## What

In `cli/swarm/cli/ready.go`, `applyBreaker`'s refused-write early return
drops the stop verdict along with the projected count. When the manifest
ALREADY records `consecutive_dispatch_failures` at or above the threshold
and `--completed` is given, a dry run reports the run **clear** (exit 0)
instead of **stopped** (exit 2).

The early return is the block introduced for the dry-run fix, keyed on
`if refused(writeReport, writeSteps) {` and returning

    breakerOutcome{Facts: []Fact{Unestablished("consecutive_dispatch_failures", ...)}, Records: records}

It returns before the `if next >= threshold` test that sets
`outcome.Stopped`. The reason quoted in the code — "a run is not stopped
by a number nothing wrote" — is true of the PROJECTED value `next`, and
is not true of `recorded`, which was read and IS established.

## Evidence (measured at 2622f6c, in-package probe against the fake runner)

Recorded count 3, threshold 3, ready set empty:

| invocation | exit | outcome | summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `swarm ready --run run-1 --dry-run` | 2 | stop | "the run is stopped: 3 consecutive dispatch(es) returned with no bead completed (threshold 3)" |
| `swarm ready --run run-1 --dry-run --completed 0` | **0** | **clear** | "nothing in run-1 is ready to dispatch" |
| `swarm ready --run run-1 --completed 0` (execute) | 2 | stop | "the run is stopped: 4 ..." |

In the failing row the count fact carries all the information the verdict
needed and still reports clear:

    "established": false,
    "reason": "the write was refused: dry run: the step writes. The count stands at 3 and would have become 4 (threshold 3)"

Adding `--completed 0` to a dry run therefore SUPPRESSES a stop verdict
the same dry run gives without it. The same holds on the `--agent` arm,
which reaches the identical `applyBreaker`.

## Why it matters

`--dry-run` is the "what would this do" invocation a coordinator uses
before dispatching. On a run the manifest already records as stopped it
now answers "clear — nothing ready", which is the circuit breaker
failing open in exactly the mode meant to be safe to run.

## Origin

Introduced by `5c2495f` (e6xt.7), which correctly threaded `req.Mode`
into both breaker plans but folded the stop test in behind the write.

## Suggested shape (not prescriptive)

Evaluate `recorded >= threshold` on the refused-write path and report the
run stopped from the RECORDED count, citing the read that established it,
while leaving the count fact unestablished as it is now. A dry run may
not invent a stop from a number nothing wrote; it must not hide one from
a number something did.

## Acceptance

- `swarm ready --run <r> --dry-run --completed 0` on a run whose recorded
  count is at or above the threshold exits 2 and says the run is stopped.
- The count fact stays unestablished, with the projection in its reason.
- A dry run BELOW the threshold still exits 0 (regression guard: recorded
  2, threshold 3, `--completed 0` must stay clear).
- The `--agent` arm behaves the same way.
design:
Extend `applyBreaker`'s refused-write early return in cli/swarm/cli/ready.go —
the block guarded by `if refused(writeReport, writeSteps)` — so it evaluates
`recorded >= threshold` and, when true, sets `Stopped: true` with a summary
phrased from the RECORDED count, citing the read invocation `from` that
established it.

The count Fact stays exactly as it is: `Unestablished("consecutive_dispatch_
failures", ...)` with the projection kept in the reason, so a refused write
still reports no measured count. Only the stop verdict is added, and it rests
on a number the read established rather than on `next`.

Also correct `breakerOutcome.Stopped`'s own doc comment, which today reads "A
refused write leaves it false: a run is not stopped by a number nothing wrote."
That sentence becomes false with this change. Rewrite it to say that `Stopped`
is a statement about the count that WAS recorded, and that a refused write
withholds only the PROJECTED advance — a run already at threshold is still
reported stopped.

REJECTED: testing `next >= threshold` on the refused path. That lets a dry run
invent a stop from a number nothing wrote, which is the untruth the original
guard exists to prevent.

REJECTED: deleting the early return and letting control fall through to the
shared `if next >= threshold` test below. That reports the count fact as
established from a write that was refused — the defect e6xt.7 fixed.

The `--agent` arm reaches this same function, so it inherits the fix; assert it
on both arms rather than assuming it.

Regression guard the acceptance requires: recorded 2, threshold 3, `--dry-run
--completed 0` must still exit 0.

BATCH: first of batch b12. e6xt.17 and e6xt.14 rewrite `reportAgentQueue`'s
handling of what this function returns, and e6xt.18 rewrites the doc comment
describing both arms — all three read the shape this bead settles, so land this
one before them.

metadata.tier_reason: One early-return block in applyBreaker plus a doc-comment correction on breakerOutcome.Stopped; the correct behaviour is fully pinned by the acceptance and by the established/unestablished wording convention already in the file

title: swarm ready silently drops --completed when --agent is given, losing the circuit breaker count
description:
FOUND BY: sprint review of run agent-plugins-e6xt (reviewer: code-review, declared in sf.toml [review]).

WHAT. `swarm ready --run <epic> --agent <id> --completed <n>` accepts `--completed`, exits 0, and never touches the circuit breaker. The dispatch return is lost with no diagnostic.

MECHANISM. In cli/swarm/cli/ready.go the RunE body forks:

    if agent != "" {
        result, err = reportAgentQueue(context.Background(), deps, req, agent)
    } else {
        report := breakerReport{Given: cmd.Flags().Changed("completed"), Completed: completed}
        result, err = reportReady(context.Background(), deps, req, report, threshold)
    }

`applyBreaker` has exactly one call site in the file, inside `reportReady`. The `--agent` arm never reads `--completed` and never advances `consecutive_dispatch_failures`.

MEASURED, on the built binary, using the command's own --explain (which writes nothing):

    $ swarm ready --run agent-plugins-e6xt --agent dev-e6xt-b1 --completed 0 --explain
    EXIT=0
    transcript:
      - "swarm ready --agent dev-e6xt-b1 reads the run's whole descendant set, ..."
      - "  one bd list --parent <bead> --all --limit 0 --json per level below agent-plugins-e6xt ..."
      - "  bd ready --parent agent-plugins-e6xt --assignee dev-e6xt-b1 --exclude-type epic --exclude-label human --limit 0 --json  (this dispatch's ready half)"
      - "  bd list --assignee dev-e6xt-b1 --status in_progress --limit 0 --json  (this dispatch's held half, ...)"

    $ swarm ready --run agent-plugins-e6xt --completed 0 --explain          # same --completed, no --agent
    EXIT=0
    transcript:
      - "swarm ready reads two things and joins them, then reads the circuit breaker's count, ..."
      - "  bd ready --parent agent-plugins-e6xt --exclude-type epic --exclude-label human --limit 0 --json  (the dispatch set)"
      - "  the same worktree-to-dispatch attribution `swarm status` performs ..."
      - "  bd show agent-plugins-e6xt --json                              (the failure count; --completed also writes it back)"

The breaker line is present in the second and absent from the first. Exit 0 both times; no refusal of the flag combination.

WHY IT IS REACHABLE. plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatching.md puts both forms under one heading, "The circuit breaker, and one dispatch's queue - both are `swarm ready`": it tells the coordinator to report every dispatch's return with `--completed <n>`, then four paragraphs later to query one dispatch's queue with `--agent <dispatch-id>`. Combining them at the moment a dispatch returns - which is when a coordinator wants both answers - silently drops the breaker count that stops a run.

DURABLE ANCHOR. cli/swarm/cli/ready.go, the `if agent != ""` fork in `readyCmd`'s RunE. Grep handle:

    grep -n "applyBreaker\|reportAgentQueue" cli/swarm/cli/ready.go

FIX SHAPE (not attempted), either one:
 - refuse the combination with a RefuseArguments, the way `--explain && --dry-run` is already refused two lines above; or
 - apply the breaker in both arms, so `--agent` narrows the answer without discarding the report.

SCOPE: row 1 - introduced by this run's own diff. `swarm ready` did not exist at base_sha 2490026ce2dc17d3813aeb5a1fed1a845c3da54e. The `--agent` arm landed with agent-plugins-o63s.7 (AQ) and the breaker with agent-plugins-o63s.8 (CB), which landed second and did not wire itself into the pre-existing arm.


## Steps to Reproduce

Neither invocation writes anything, so `--explain` is enough to see the defect.

1. `swarm ready --run <epic> --agent <dispatch-id> --completed 0 --explain`
2. `swarm ready --run <epic> --completed 0 --explain`

EXPECTED: both transcripts name the circuit breaker's read and its write-back.
ACTUAL: only the second does. The second's transcript carries `bd show <epic> --json  (the failure count; --completed also writes it back)`. The first's carries the descendant walk, the dispatch's ready half and its held half, and no breaker line at all.

Both exit 0. The flag combination is not refused, so `--completed` is accepted and silently discarded, and the dispatch return is lost with no diagnostic.
design:
Apply the breaker in BOTH arms of `readyCmd`'s RunE fork in
cli/swarm/cli/ready.go, so `--agent` narrows the answer without discarding the
dispatch return. Build the `breakerReport{Given: cmd.Flags().Changed("completed"),
Completed: completed}` once, before the `if agent != ""` fork, and pass it to
`reportAgentQueue` as well as to `reportReady`. `applyBreaker`, which today has
exactly one call site inside `reportReady`, gains a second.

This is what the feature blueprint requires, and it is why this option is chosen
over the alternative. specs/features/swarm-dispatch/swarm-dispatch-blueprint.md
specifies `swarm ready --agent` as "the same query with one more filter, so the
filter set is implemented once", and specifies the breaker unconditionally on
the command: "The command SHALL advance `consecutive_dispatch_failures` by one
WHEN a dispatch returns having completed no bead, and SHALL reset it to zero
WHEN a dispatch returns having completed at least one." Nothing there makes the
breaker conditional on the absence of `--agent`.

REJECTED: refusing the combination with a `RefuseArguments`, the way
`--explain && --dry-run` is already refused. It stops the silent loss, but it
also stops the one invocation a coordinator most wants at the moment a dispatch
returns - report the return and read that dispatch's remaining queue - and it
adds a refusal the blueprint does not declare.

The breaker's write must obey the request's mode, so this must be consistent
with the mode-threading fix in `applyBreaker`: a dry run of the `--agent` arm
must not write either.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `swarm ready --run <epic> --agent <id> --completed 0` advances `consecutive_dispatch_failures` exactly as the same invocation without `--agent` does.
- [ ] `swarm ready --run <epic> --agent <id> --completed 1` resets the count to zero, as the no-`--agent` form does.
- [ ] `swarm ready --run <epic> --agent <id> --completed <n> --explain` names the breaker's read and write in its transcript, as the no-`--agent` form already does.
- [ ] The `--agent` arm still returns only that dispatch's beads, still reaches beads at any depth beneath the run epic, still does not reach outside the run, and still reports the drain verdict.
- [ ] No invocation silently accepts `--completed` and ignores it: it is either applied or refused with a diagnostic.
- [ ] `swarm ready --run <epic> --agent <id> --completed <n> --dry-run` performs no tracker write.
- [ ] A Go test asserts the breaker is applied on the `--agent` arm.
- [ ] `specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md` is consistent with the fixed behaviour, or updated where it is not.
- [ ] All 13 checks pass: `python3 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-checks.py` exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: Small fork change; the choice between refusing and applying is settled by the blueprint, and it must compose with the mode threading in applyBreaker

title: swarm dispatch accept reports merged_sha as the pre-rebase sha on the concurrent arm; the commit it names is not on the target
description:
FOUND BY: sprint review of run agent-plugins-e6xt (reviewer: code-review, declared in sf.toml [review]).

WHAT. On the CONCURRENT arm of `swarm dispatch accept`, the `merged_sha` fact reports the dispatch branch's PRE-rebase sha. The rebase rewrites those commits, so the reported sha is not reachable from the target - it names a commit that did not land.

MECHANISM. In cli/swarm/cli/accept.go, `readCase` resolves `branchSHA` before any write (its own doc comment: "readCase decides serialized or concurrent, and does it BEFORE any" write). `foldIn` then appends the rebase step only on the concurrent arm:

    if !m.serialized {
        steps = append(steps, vc.Rebase("rebase", dispatchBranch, m.targetSHA)...)
    }

but the success fact is built the same way in BOTH arms:

    Text("merged_sha", m.branchSHA, m.branchInv))

THE CODEBASE ALREADY KNOWS THIS. cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go, the doc comment on `recheckDispatchBeads`, verbatim:

    "`committed` reads the TARGET rather than the dispatch branch, for two
     reasons that both only hold after the fold: the branch has just been
     deleted, and a concurrent dispatch's commits were rewritten by the
     rebase, so the branch's own shas are not the ones that landed."

The re-check honours that. The `merged_sha` fact does not.

MEASURED end-to-end. Probe e2e test against the `dispatch-stale-base` fixture (the concurrent world - no worktree, so the rebase succeeds), running `swarm dispatch accept --run fixture-run --dispatch dev-fixture-2 --no-push --json --full-result`, exit 0:

    PROBE branchBefore (pre-rebase) = 016160f623edf1d515e2a292874cbbdd42ea72df
    PROBE targetBefore             = d54d47f364f51d6a45e05c5de35dc5f603fae664
    PROBE targetAfter  (landed)    = 7bdff8a57501d28e797b71c1835871c65c3a5de5
    PROBE merged_sha   (reported)  = 016160f623edf1d515e2a292874cbbdd42ea72df
    PROBE VERDICT: merged_sha does NOT name the landed commit
    PROBE merged_sha object type: commit
    PROBE is merged_sha an ancestor of the target? exit=1

`git merge-base --is-ancestor <merged_sha> claude/bead-bonanza-fixture` exits 1: the reported commit is not on the target at all. A coordinator verifying the merge by that sha will not find it.

THE FACT IS UNASSERTED. `grep -rn "merged_sha" cli/ plugin/ specs/` returns exactly one hit - the line that produces it. No unit test, no e2e test and no specification asserts its value, which is why the existing concurrent e2e test (`TestDispatchAcceptRebasesAConcurrentBranchAndFastForwards`) passes while asserting, correctly, that `targetAfter != branchBefore`.

DURABLE ANCHOR. cli/swarm/cli/accept.go, function `foldIn`, the `default:` arm of the switch on `ffRec.Status`, the line `Text("merged_sha", m.branchSHA, m.branchInv))`. Grep handle:

    grep -rn "merged_sha" cli/swarm/

FIX SHAPE (not attempted). Read the target's head after the fast-forward and report that as `merged_sha` (it is what landed in both arms), or keep the pre-rebase value under a differently named fact and add the landed sha beside it. Whichever is chosen, add the assertion the fact currently lacks.

SCOPE: row 1 - introduced by this run's own diff. `merged_sha` did not exist at base_sha 2490026ce2dc17d3813aeb5a1fed1a845c3da54e; it was added by agent-plugins-o63s.11 (MG), confirmed with `git log -S 'merged_sha' 2490026..HEAD`.

NOTE ON REACHABILITY. agent-plugins-1vya records that the concurrent arm cannot rebase while a real dispatch worktree stands. That bug and this one are independent: this one is measurable today on the fixtures (which declare no worktree), and fixing 1vya does not fix it.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Against the `dispatch-stale-base` fixture — the concurrent world, which declares no worktree, so the rebase succeeds — record the dispatch branch's sha and the target's sha.
2. Run `swarm dispatch accept --run fixture-run --dispatch dev-fixture-2 --no-push --json --full-result`. It exits 0.
3. Compare the reported `merged_sha` fact against the target's head afterwards.

EXPECTED: the reported sha is reachable from the target.
ACTUAL: `merged_sha` is the PRE-rebase branch sha. As measured:

    branchBefore (pre-rebase) = 016160f623edf1d515e2a292874cbbdd42ea72df
    targetBefore              = d54d47f364f51d6a45e05c5de35dc5f603fae664
    targetAfter  (landed)     = 7bdff8a57501d28e797b71c1835871c65c3a5de5
    merged_sha   (reported)   = 016160f623edf1d515e2a292874cbbdd42ea72df

`git merge-base --is-ancestor <merged_sha> claude/bead-bonanza-fixture` exits 1: the commit it names is not on the target at all.
design:
Report the commit that LANDED. After the fast-forward succeeds, resolve the
TARGET's head and report that as `merged_sha`, in BOTH arms - it is what landed
in each. Today `foldIn` (cli/swarm/cli/accept.go) builds
`Text("merged_sha", m.branchSHA, m.branchInv)` in both arms from the pre-rebase
branch sha `readCase` resolved before any write, and the concurrent arm's rebase
rewrites those commits.

The codebase already holds this convention and this bead makes `merged_sha`
honour it. The doc comment on `recheckDispatchBeads`
(cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go) states it: `committed` reads the target rather
than the dispatch branch because the branch has just been deleted and "a
concurrent dispatch's commits were rewritten by the rebase, so the branch's own
shas are not the ones that landed."

The fact's invocation must be the one that ESTABLISHED the value it reports -
the target resolve performed after the fold - not `m.branchInv`, which
established the pre-rebase branch sha.

Read the target, not the branch: the branch is deleted as part of the fold.

REJECTED: keeping the pre-rebase value under `merged_sha` and adding the landed
sha beside it under a new name. That leaves a fact called `merged_sha` naming a
commit that did not merge, which is the defect itself. Nothing depends on the

title: pre-flight's worktree.baseRef gate reads user scope only, blocking on a setting project scope may already satisfy
description:
pre-flight-check.sh:700 resolves worktree.baseRef from $HOME/.claude/settings.json alone:

    WORKTREE_BASEREF="$(jq -r ".worktree.baseRef // \"unset\"" "$USER_SETTINGS" 2>/dev/null)"

with USER_SETTINGS="$HOME/.claude/settings.json" (line 698). When that file is absent it reports `unknown` (line 703) and block()s the run (line 709).

Claude Code settings precedence (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings) ranks shared project `.claude/settings.json` at level 4, ABOVE user `~/.claude/settings.json` at level 5 — project scope overrides user scope. Neither the settings page nor https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees names any scope restriction on worktree.baseRef; the latter says only "Set worktree.baseRef in settings".

So a repo committing {"worktree":{"baseRef":"head"}} to its own .claude/settings.json very likely satisfies the real requirement while pre-flight still blocks.

The skill references already concede this: worktree-mechanics.md:73 reads "Fix (set it in user scope; project scope is untested)". A blocking hard gate rests on an assumption the corpus marks untested.

MEASURED in this container (cloud session, agent-plugins attached alone):
- /root/.claude/settings.json absent; HOME=/root; /root/.claude/ exists with launcher-settings.json only
- project .claude/settings.json carries worktree.baseRef=head (commit 5d82354)
- pre-flight-check.sh exits 1, BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF=unknown
- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh writes no settings.json (grep: no match) — the writer is the environment setup script in docs/session-bootstrap.md, which is configured per cloud environment and did not run here
acceptance_criteria:
UNVERIFIED PREMISE FIRST: empirically confirm whether Claude Code honours worktree.baseRef from project-scope .claude/settings.json. Dispatch a subagent with isolation: worktree from a session whose HEAD carries commits absent from the default branch, and inspect what its worktree branched from. Record the invocation and the observed output.

THEN, if project scope is honoured:
- pre-flight resolves worktree.baseRef across the documented precedence chain (project local, shared project, user) rather than user scope alone, and blocks only when no scope supplies "head"
- worktree-mechanics.md:73 replaces "project scope is untested" with the measured result
- docs/session-bootstrap.md notes that a repo may commit the project-scope setting instead of relying on the environment setup script

If project scope is NOT honoured:
- the block stays, and worktree-mechanics.md:73 says so as a measured fact rather than as untested
- pre-flight names the environment setup script (docs/session-bootstrap.md) in its remedy text, since that is what supplies the file in cloud containers

Either way the claim stops being untested.
notes:
Discovered while opening a bead-bonanza run over epic agent-plugins-o63s: pre-flight blocked, and writes to /root/.claude/settings.json were denied by the permission classifier, leaving no in-session remedy.

NOTE the overlap with feature-swarm-dispatch: the ADP-C delta already specifies removing this block entirely — "pre-flight-check.sh's BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF block SHALL be removed, since the base is an argument the dispatch names and there is nothing left to assert." If that feature lands first this bug is moot for the dispatch path, but the resolution above still settles the untested claim for every other consumer.
close_reason: pre-flight now resolves worktree.baseRef across the full settings precedence chain; project scope confirmed honoured by measurement

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
MEASURED: project-scope .claude/settings.json IS honoured for worktree.baseRef.

A subagent dispatched with isolation: worktree from this session (HEAD 5d82354 on claude/swarm-dispatch-blueprint-5gob2e; origin/main at a1724b8) reported from inside its worktree:

  pwd                    -> /home/user/agent-plugins/.claude/worktrees/agent-a7b90e671470e45ad
  git rev-parse HEAD     -> 5d823540607bc37ee76bef18ff57eaf54210ac23
  git branch --show-current -> worktree-agent-a7b90e671470e45ad
  git merge-base --is-ancestor 8e6d12b HEAD -> exit=0
  git merge-base --is-ancestor 5d82354 HEAD -> exit=0
  grep '^status:' specs/features/swarm-dispatch/swarm-dispatch-blueprint.md -> status: in-progress

Conditions: /root/.claude/settings.json ABSENT (HOME=/root); worktree.baseRef set ONLY in the repository's own .claude/settings.json (commit 5d82354). The worktree came up on session HEAD, not the default branch, carrying both branch-only commits and the approved blueprint.

FIXED. pre-flight-check.sh now resolves the key across Claude Code's documented precedence, highest level first, taking the first file that DEFINES it: .claude/settings.local.json, then .claude/settings.json, then $HOME/.claude/settings.json. It emits BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF_SRC naming which file answered.

Precedence semantics verified by three cases against the patched script:
  local 'fresh' + project 'head'  -> reports fresh from settings.local.json, BLOCKS (higher level wins)
  local without the key           -> falls through to project 'head'
  local malformed JSON            -> level drops out, falls through to project 'head'

Docs corrected: worktree-mechanics.md (the 'project scope is untested' line, now the committed-file recommendation plus the precedence rule), SKILL.md, dispatching.md, docs/session-bootstrap.md.

NOT REACHED, deliberately: docs/research/swarm-cli/2026-08-25-capability-audit.md:159 (dated audit snapshot, left as the record of what was believed then) and specs/features/swarm-dispatch/swarm-dispatch-frd.md:550,588 ('a global setting no repository owns'). design:
Anchors: `cli/swarm/cli`, `cli/swarm/vcs`, `cli/swarm/tracker`.

Every ordering guarantee here is a property of the plan ([[adr-024]]), not of
a shell that would otherwise sequence it ([[adr-025]] — argv vectors, never a
command string for a shell interpreter). [[adr-026]] — no rollback: the
irreversible writes are ordered last, and the removal-behind-ancestry and
push-behind-post-merge orderings are instances of that rule.

AC-SWARM-DISP-004.6 is satisfied via the relied-upon `Plan Runner`'s ordering

acceptance_criteria:
Behavior lines from the delta:

- SHALL remove the worktree only WHEN the dispatch branch is an ancestor of
  the target, and WHEN it is not, leave the worktree in place, delete no
  branch, and take the stop status.
- The worktree SHALL be removed before its branch is deleted, and the branch
  SHALL NOT be deleted before the fast-forward has succeeded.
- WHEN the version control tool refuses a removal, SHALL NOT retry with force,
  and SHALL take the attention status naming what the tool refused over.
- WHERE a removal is refused because the worktree is locked, the resolution
  the command names SHALL be the unlock invocation, never the forcing form.
- After the merge and the removal, SHALL re-check every bead in the dispatch
  with no signal deferred, and attempt no push until every one has passed.
- WHERE `--no-push` is passed, SHALL complete every step before the push and
  report the branch as unlanded rather than pushing.
- WHEN run in dry-run mode, SHALL perform every read and no merge, removal,
  deletion or push.

**ACs — citations owed here:**
- AC-SWARM-DISP-004.1 — e2e — **proving delta** (MG participates)
- AC-SWARM-DISP-004.6 — unit (via relied-upon `Plan Runner`)
- AC-SWARM-DISP-004.9 — unit

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b7
comments.text:

evidence: `grep -n "signal" specs/features/swarm-dispatch/swarm-dispatch-frd.md` returns 9 hits, and every one uses the word without enumerating the set: line 679 "pre-merge acceptance the acceptance signals per bead, deferring the two a merge decides", 684 "post-merge acceptance the same signals with none deferred", 690 "a bead failing an acceptance signal at exit 2", 799 "each bead in the dispatch is checked again with no signal deferred", 806 "the failing signal is named". `grep -rn "acceptance" cli/swarm --include=*.go | grep -v _test` returns 5 hits, all doc comments, none a signal set. So the phrase "with no signal deferred" is unimplementable as written: nothing says which signals, nor which two a merge decides.
The set I implemented is plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh mode_bead: 1 closed in the tracker, 2 a commit carrying the id, 3 merged into HEAD, 4 the worktree is gone, 5 findings recorded — and its `--pre-merge` flag defers exactly 3 and 4 ("--pre-merge DEFERS SIGNALS 3 AND 4 ... both signals would fail by construction"), which is what identifies "the two a merge decides". `cli/swarm/tracker/tracker.go:280` is the corroboration inside the container: Findings is documented as "the tracker's half of a bead's acceptance signals: whether the work was recorded, beside the bead's own state."
The derivation is sound but it is a derivation. A reader of the FRD alone cannot make it, and the script it comes from is a skill this container is not allowed to depend on.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b7
comments.text:
retro:decision the pre-merge acceptance check (ceremony step 2) was filed, not implemented — filed as agent-plugins-bhaj
evidence: The FRD ceremony (swarm-dispatch-frd.md:679) has 8 steps; step 2 is "pre-merge acceptance the acceptance signals per bead, deferring the two a merge decides". Neither delta covers it. MG's behavior lines (blueprint "drain, case and merge") name the drain check, the case and the merge only; RM's name "After the merge and the removal, the command SHALL re-check every bead in the dispatch with no signal deferred". Reading the code: `acceptDispatch` in cli/swarm/cli/accept.go goes drain -> target -> case -> fold with nothing between, so MG shipped without it.
I implemented step 7 (recheckDispatchBeads) and left step 7's deferring twin unbuilt, because RM's acceptance criteria are satisfied without it and building it would add a fifth stop condition to MG's arm that no AC of this bead covers.
Rejected: wiring the same checker in ahead of readCase with the two signals deferred. It is ~10 lines given what this bead built, and the FRD calls for it ("Four things stop an acceptance ... a bead failing an acceptance signal at exit 2"). The cost of NOT doing it: an acceptance whose bead is unclosed or carries no finding now merges first and discovers it at step 7 — the work still lands and the run still stops before the push, so nothing is lost, but the FRD's second stop condition does not exist and the merge happens on a dispatch that should not have reached it.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b7
comments.text:
retro:decision --no-push exits CLEAR with landed=false, rather than attention
evidence: The behavior line is "WHERE --no-push is passed, the command SHALL complete every step before the push and report the branch as unlanded rather than pushing." It fixes the fact and not the status.
`swarm branch verify-landed` takes the attention status for an unlanded branch (AC-SWARM-DISP-005.1, .2 — see landingVerdict in cli/swarm/cli/branch.go, both arms return OutcomeAttention), so the consistent-looking choice was attention here too. Rejected: a coordinator routes on the exit status, and --no-push is a deliberate policy rather than a condition; exiting 1 would make every accepted dispatch in a no-push run read as needing attention, which is the signal the status exists to carry.
A second constraint settled the shape of the fact. `answer` in cli/swarm/cli/answer.go renders ONLY satisfied facts at a clear exit (`satisfied(f) = f.Established && f.Reason == ""`), so a `landed=false` carrying a Reason is silently dropped from the answer document — measured: the first version of this carried Reason "--no-push was passed, so nothing was pushed" and the test read `landed = <nil>` off the JSON. It is now a plain Flag with a Resolution and no Reason, which renders as `"landed": false`.
The fact's invocation is `swarm branch verify-landed --branch <target>` and not `swarm branch push`: an invocation on a fact is what REPRODUCES it, and the push would change it.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b7
comments.text:
retro:proof `git branch -d` after a rebase fails when the branch has an upstream — caught by the e2e, fixed in the fixture helper, not in the command
evidence: `go test ./swarm/e2e/ -run TestDispatchAcceptRebases` failed with exit 1 and the report line:
  bb/dev-fixture-2 was concurrent against claude/bead-bonanza-fixture, rebased onto d54d47f... and fast-forwarded into it; ... bb/dev-fixture-2 could not be deleted: plan: step "delete-branch": git: git exited 1: If you are sure you want to delete it, run "git branch -D bb/dev-fixture-2"
Cause: `git branch -d` checks the branch against its UPSTREAM when one is set, and against HEAD only when none is. The e2e helper standDispatchBranch created the local branch with `git branch bb/dev-fixture-2 origin/bb/dev-fixture-2`, which sets an upstream by default; after the rebase the new head is not in origin/bb/dev-fixture-2, so -d refused. A real run cuts the branch with `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <sha>` (openDispatchWorktree, cli/swarm/cli/dispatch.go), which sets NO upstream — so the world was wrong, not the command.
Fix: `--no-track` in standDispatchBranch, with the measurement recorded in its doc comment. Re-run: ok, 9.266s. The forcing form (-D) was never an option — vcs.VersionControl.DeleteBranch documents "-d rather than -D: -D would take unmerged commits with it".
The command still reports a refused deletion honestly rather than retrying it: attention, branch_deleted=false, and a resolution naming `git log <branch> --not HEAD`.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b7
comments.text:
retro:unverifiable AC-SWARM-DISP-004.1 cannot be verified at its declared e2e level — proved at unit instead, filed as agent-plugins-oyvf
evidence: The blueprint's AC Coverage table declares "AC-SWARM-DISP-004.1 | MG, RM (proves) | e2e". The criterion needs a dispatch branch that is NOT an ancestor of the target AFTER a merge step that did not stop the command. Against a real git those are mutually exclusive: a successful `git merge --ff-only <branch>` has by construction put the branch on the target, so `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> <target>` answers yes; and a fold that fails stops the acceptance at AC-SWARM-DISP-004.6, before the guard. The state exists only when a second actor moves the target between the two reads.
Proved at the unit tier instead — TestAWorktreeIsNotRemovedUnlessItsBranchIsAnAncestorOfTheTarget, where the fake answers the fold 0 and the ancestry read 1 independently: no `git worktree remove`, no `git branch -d`, no `git push`, exit 2, report says "not an ancestor". `go test ./swarm/cli/...` ok.
What would settle it at e2e: a fixture world carrying a real repository-local `post-merge` hook that moves the target — the same technique push-refused already uses for a rejection (a real pre-receive hook, standRefusingRemote in cli/swarm/e2e/harness_test.go). That needs a fixture-stamp declaration, which is the fixture harness's and not a command delta's.

comments.text:
retro:sequencing agent-plugins-1vya (MG cannot rebase while the dispatch worktree stands) was left untouched, and this bead did not have to decide anything that entrenches it
evidence: 1vya is about WHERE the rebase runs. This delta owns steps 5-8 of the ceremony — the ancestry guard, the removal, the post-merge re-check and the landing — all of which are strictly after the fold. The merge-before-removal order is fixed by the FRD ceremony (swarm-dispatch-frd.md:679-686) and was implemented by MG; nothing here moved it, and no acceptance criterion of this bead required choosing a `Dir` for the rebase. So the rebase still runs in the coordinator's own checkout, exactly as MG left it.
The two e2e cases this bead added or changed do not hide it either, and one of them is now the first case in the suite to accept a dispatch whose worktree really stands: TestDispatchAcceptRechecksEveryBeadAfterTheMergeAndTheRemoval uses the dispatch-worktree fixture, which declares [[worktree]] branch = "bb/dev-fixture-2". The concurrent case still runs against dispatch-stale-base, which declares no worktree.
A fixture that is both concurrent AND has a standing worktree would reproduce 1vya end to end today. None exists.

one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.

design:
Anchors: `cli/swarm/cli`, `cli/swarm/vcs`, `cli/swarm/tracker`.

acceptance_criteria:
Behavior lines from the delta:

- SHALL check that the dispatch has drained before anything else, and WHEN it
  has not, take the attention status naming what the agent still holds and
  merge or remove nothing.
- SHALL determine whether the dispatch was serialized or concurrent before it
  reads a fast-forward refusal, and report which case it read.
- The case SHALL be decided by comparing the dispatch branch's merge-base with
  the target against the target's current head: equal is serialized, anything
  else is concurrent. It SHALL NOT be inferred from how many worktrees are
  standing.
- WHEN the case is concurrent, SHALL rebase the dispatch branch onto the
  target as it stands at merge time and then fast-forward.
- WHEN the case is serialized and a fast-forward is refused, SHALL take the
  stop status without re-attempting the merge, and SHALL NOT re-attempt it
  with fast-forward-only relaxed.
- WHEN a rebase conflicts, SHALL record a sequencing finding naming both beads
  and every conflicting path, mark the unmerged bead blocked, leave the
  worktree standing, and resolve nothing itself.
- The finding SHALL be recorded through the `Tracker`'s comment operation in
  the run's existing finding convention.

**ACs — citations owed here:**
- AC-SWARM-DISP-004.2 — unit
- AC-SWARM-DISP-004.3 — e2e — **proving delta** (VCS participates)
- AC-SWARM-DISP-004.4 — e2e — **proving delta** (TRK participates)
- AC-SWARM-DISP-004.5 — unit

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text:
retro:gap the MG delta names no version-control operation for returning to the target after a rebase, and none existed. `git rebase <onto> <branch>` checks <branch> out, so the fast-forward that follows would advance the dispatch branch onto itself and leave the target unmoved. Added `Checkout(prefix, branch)` to `vcs.VersionControl` and its git implementation.
evidence: measured, git 2.43.0, scratch repo on `main`: `git rebase main bb/dev-1` -> exit 0, ""Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/bb/dev-1."", then `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` -> `bb/dev-1`. After `git checkout main; git merge --ff-only bb/dev-1` -> exit 0, "Updating eef6bea..43e1b46 / Fast-forward", and `git rev-parse main bb/dev-1` reports one sha twice.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text:
retro:decision the AC asks for the case to be decided by "comparing the dispatch branch merge-base with the target against the target current head". Implemented as the existing `VersionControl.Descends(target, dispatchBranch)` rather than a new merge-base-returning operation: `git merge-base --is-ancestor A B` is true exactly when merge-base(A,B) == A, so asking whether the target is an ancestor of the dispatch branch IS the equality the AC states, and it runs the same plumbing command. Rejected adding a `MergeBase` operation that returns a sha for the caller to compare: it would add a second way to ask one question and a second sha for a caller to mis-compare, for no extra information.
evidence: cli/swarm/vcs/git/git.go, `func (v VersionControl) Descends` -> `"merge-base", "--is-ancestor", ancestor, descendant`, with `s.Answers = []int{1}` so a legitimate "no" is an answer rather than a failure.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text:
retro:environment `bd init` COMMITS its own scaffolding onto the checked-out branch, so every restored end-to-end world had its sprint branch pointing at a `bd init` commit rather than at the sha its fixture stamp documents, and its index carrying the same files. Nothing caught it before, because no case had folded a branch. Fixed in the harness with a mixed reset back to the head read before `bd init`.
evidence: measured in a clone of `dispatch-rebase-conflict/repository.bundle` with HOME pinned to a fresh dir: `git log --format=%s -n 1 HEAD` -> "fixture-run.4 P1 the fourth bead of the run" after clone+checkout; -> "bd init: initialize beads issue tracking" after `bd init --prefix fixture`; unchanged by `bd import`. `git rebase <target-sha> bb/dev-fixture-2` there -> exit 1, "error: cannot rebase: Your index contains uncommitted changes. error: Please commit or stash them." After `git reset --quiet 078f2b6`: head reads "fixture-run.4 P1 ..." again, `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` is empty, and `bd show fixture-run.3 --json` still answers.

title: LD: swarm branch verify-landed and swarm branch push
description:
Implements the **LD** delta — `swarm branch verify-landed` and
`swarm branch push` in [[container-swarm-cli]] (added). Blueprint section:
"### `swarm branch verify-landed` and `swarm branch push` in
[[container-swarm-cli]] (added)".

A rejected push leaves every other signal reading finished. One fetch and one
comparison is what separates work that landed from work stranded on a
container about to be reclaimed.

Stage 2 (the loop). Lands before RM, which ends by calling it.


## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Anchors: `cli/swarm/cli`, `cli/swarm/vcs`, `cli/swarm/vcs/git`.

"Invocable with no run scope" is the exception to `Swarm Command Surface`'s
run-scope refusal — these two commands are the recovery path, and requiring
a scope defeats their purpose.

`push` is `verify-landed` with the push ordered before it. Build one plan,
not two commands that resemble each other.
acceptance_criteria:
Behavior lines from the delta:

- Both commands SHALL be invocable with no run scope, so a recovering session
  can run the landing check before it knows which run it is in.
- WHERE `--branch` is absent, the branch SHALL be the one currently checked
  out; WHERE `--remote` is absent, the remote SHALL be `origin`. Both defaults
  are read from the repository, so neither command consults configuration
  outside it.
- The landing check SHALL fetch the remote before comparing, so a stale local
  record of the remote's position cannot report a branch as landed.
- WHEN the local branch is ahead of its remote, SHALL name the number of
  unpushed commits and take the attention status.
- WHEN the branch has no counterpart on the remote, SHALL take the attention
  status rather than reporting it as landed.
- WHEN a push is rejected, SHALL report the rejection's cause, and WHERE the
  remote refuses one of the push's paths, SHALL report no commit in that push
  as landed and name the refused path.
- `swarm branch push` SHALL be `verify-landed` with the push ordered before
  it, one implementation rather than two.

**ACs — citations owed here:**
- AC-SWARM-DISP-005.1 — e2e
- AC-SWARM-DISP-005.2 — e2e
- AC-SWARM-DISP-005.3 — e2e
- AC-SWARM-DISP-005.4 — e2e
- AC-SWARM-DISP-005.5 — unit
- AC-SWARM-DISP-005.6 — unit
- AC-SWARM-DISP-005.7 — unit — **proving delta** (VCS participates)

metadata.tier_reason: Well-specified fetch-then-compare with named defaults; the ordering (push before verify) is the only subtlety

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text:
retro:decision the delta requires `--remote` to be honoured, but the landed `VersionControl.Divergence(prefix, branch)` compared against `<branch>@{upstream}`, which ignores the named remote and fails outright on a branch with no upstream configured even where the counterpart exists. Changed the signature to `Divergence(prefix, branch, remote)`, comparing `<branch>...<remote>/<branch>`. Rejected adding a second operation beside it: two operations answering one question is what the container is built to avoid, and Divergence had no production caller to break — only its own argv tests.
evidence: measured, git 2.43.0, scratch repo: `git rev-list --count --left-right main...origin/main` -> exit 0, "0\t0"; the same after one local commit -> "1\t0". `git rev-list --count --left-right claude/sprint...origin/claude/sprint` with no such remote-tracking ref -> exit 128, "fatal: ambiguous argument". `grep -rn "\.Divergence(" cli/ | grep -v _test.go` returned only the interface declaration and the git implementation.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text:
retro:gap AC-SWARM-DISP-005.3 and .7 require the rejection cause and the refused path to reach the caller, but `Push` decoded with `discard`, whose error is the LAST line of stderr — which for a refused push is `error: failed to push some refs to <url>`, naming neither. Added a `vcs.Rejection` type and a push decoder that reads the two lines that carry the answer. This is the "proving delta (VCS participates)" the item names, so the participation was expected; what the item did not say is that the landed decoder threw the evidence away.
evidence: measured, git 2.43.0 against a bare repo whose pre-receive hook declines refs/heads/claude/*: exit 1, stdout EMPTY, stderr = "remote: refusing refs/heads/claude/*: this remote does not accept sprint branches" / "To ../remote.git" / " ! [remote rejected] claude/sprint -> claude/sprint (pre-receive hook declined)" / "error: failed to push some refs to ../remote.git". `lastLine` over that returns the fourth line.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text:
retro:decision "invocable with no run scope" left open whether `--run` should exist on these commands at all. Kept the flag declared and made only the refusal conditional, because the surface has a test asserting that EVERY invocable command in the tree carries the five contract flags, `--run` among them — dropping it would have failed that test, and the delta asks for an exception to the refusal rather than to the flag set. The scope is carried into the result when given; the contract already anticipates an empty one.
evidence: cli/swarm/cli/surface_test.go, `TestEverySubcommandInTheTreeCarriesTheContractFlags`, which walks the tree and checks `cmd.Flags().Lookup(name)` for "explain", "dry-run", "json", "run", "full-result". schemas/swarm/output.strata on `run`: "The run epic this invocation was scoped to. Empty for a command that is not run-scoped."

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text:
retro:decision the delta says a branch with no counterpart takes the attention status, but the only measurement available conflates that with a broken comparison: `git rev-list --count --left-right A...origin/A` exits 128 for a missing counterpart AND for a malformed revision. Split it into two steps — a `Resolve` probe of `<remote>/<branch>` whose failure IS the no-counterpart answer, followed by the divergence count — so "no counterpart" (attention, exit 1) is never reported as "the comparison failed" (stop, exit 2). A caller routing on the status would otherwise halt a run over a branch that simply has not been pushed yet.
evidence: measured, git 2.43.0: `git rev-parse --verify origin/claude/sprint^{commit}` with no such ref -> exit 128, "fatal: Needed a single revision"; `git rev-list --count --left-right claude/sprint...origin/claude/sprint` -> exit 128, "fatal: ambiguous argument". Same status, two different conditions.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text:
retro:gap the delta names the branch default as "the one currently checked out" but the Version Control interface had no operation answering it — `Branches` lists every branch without saying which is checked out, and `Resolve` answers a sha. Added `CurrentBranch(prefix)`. It also forced a decision the delta does not cover: a detached HEAD. Refused with the attention status naming `--branch`, rather than checking a remote ref called `HEAD`, which would produce a true report about the wrong question.
evidence: measured, git 2.43.0: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints "main" on a branch and the literal "HEAD" after `git checkout --detach`, exit 0 both times.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text:
retro:tooling the answer document has TWO shapes and which one a case gets depends on the exit status — a clear exit prints each property value directly, every other status prints `{ok, value, issues}` per property. An e2e case asserting across both statuses (unpushed -> attention, then pushed -> clear) cannot use one struct for both, and the first attempt failed with "cannot unmarshal object into Go struct field landing.branch of type string". Nothing in the item or the output standards warns of it; the reader learns it from `cli/swarm/cli/answer.go`.
evidence: cli/swarm/cli/answer.go, `func answer(r Result)`: "if r.Status() == StatusClear { ... established } ... verdicts". Observed in `swarm branch verify-landed --json` at exit 1: {"issues":[...],"branch":{"ok":true,"value":"claude/bead-bonanza-fixture","issues":[]}, ...}.

title: WT: swarm dispatch open — the worktree
description:
Implements the **WT** delta — `swarm dispatch open` in
[[container-swarm-cli]] (added — the worktree). Blueprint section:
"### `swarm dispatch open` in [[container-swarm-cli]] (added — the
worktree)".

The coordinator creating the worktree is what makes the base an argument, the
path knowable and the branch name meaningful — three things the harness's own
isolation takes away.

Stage 2 (the loop). Lands after BR.


## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —

design:
Anchors: `cli/swarm/cli`, `cli/swarm/vcs`, `cli/swarm/vcs/git`.

The path and branch forms are pinned deliberately — they are the forms
standing worktrees already use, and changing either orphans every worktree
live at adoption. Renaming travels with the skill-family rename, not here.

"Stale worktree registrations SHALL be cleared before any decision reads the
worktree list" is an ordering guarantee and belongs in the plan, per
[[adr-024]] — not a shell conjunction.
acceptance_criteria:
Behavior lines from the delta:

- SHALL create exactly one worktree and one branch per dispatch, and name
  that branch for the dispatch id.
- The worktree path and branch name SHALL be derived from the run epic id and
  the dispatch id alone, so two sessions compute the same values.
- The worktree path SHALL be outside the repository's working tree: a sibling
  of the repository root, `<parent>/.bb-worktrees/<dispatch-id>`, which is the
  location the skills already create and clean up — a different one would
  orphan every worktree standing at adoption. The dispatch branch SHALL be
  `bb/<dispatch-id>`, likewise the form already in use.
- WHERE `--base` is absent, the base SHALL be the sprint branch's head read at
  that moment.
- SHALL NOT read any configuration outside the repository to determine the
  base.
- Stale worktree registrations SHALL be cleared before any decision reads the
  worktree list.
- WHEN a worktree for the dispatch already exists, SHALL report it and leave
  it untouched.
