comments.author: dev-e6xt-b6
comments.text: retro:gap The ACs are silent on whether --dispatch is required, while the FRD's command signature ("swarm dispatch open --run <id> --dispatch <dispatch-id> [--base <ref>] [--branch <name>]") gives it no brackets, which in this doc's own convention reads as required. But the two pre-existing e2e tests from BR (TestDispatchOpenRefusesACollidingBranchTheManifestDoesNotRecord, TestDispatchOpenCreatesAndRecordsTheSprintBranch, cli/swarm/e2e/dispatch_open_test.go) call `dispatch open` with no --dispatch at all and expect success. Decided: --dispatch stays optional at the flag level; absent, only the sprint-branch half runs (unchanged from before this bead), and the worktree half runs only when a non-empty --dispatch is given. Rejected alternative: making --dispatch mandatory, which would have broken both pre-existing tests (a baseline regression) for a requirement no AC actually states.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b6
comments.text: retro:decision No VCS method existed to read the repository's working-tree root, and cli/swarm/cli must never name "git" itself (cli/swarm/vcs/git/git_test.go's TestOnlyThisPackageNamesTheTool scans every non-test .go file under cli/swarm for the literal string "git" and fails any outside vcs/git that carries it). Added vcs.VersionControl.Root(prefix) (cli/swarm/vcs/vcs.go), implemented in git.go via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (decodeRoot in decode.go), so the coordinator's worktree path (a sibling of the repo root, per the pinned <parent>/.bb-worktrees/<dispatch-id> form) is computed from a real read rather than assuming the process's cwd is the root. Verified this bead's anchors cover it: the bead's own Design section names cli/swarm/vcs and cli/swarm/vcs/git as anchors alongside cli/swarm/cli, not cli/swarm/cli alone.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b6
comments.text: retro:proof Measured a pre-existing dry-run defect in the sprint-branch half (BR, agent-plugins-o63s.9), not introduced by this bead: `swarm dispatch open --run <fresh-run-with-no-recorded-branch> --dry-run --json` against the core e2e fixture exits status 2 with summary `plan: step "manifest-write-write" produced no value (refused)`, instead of the dry-run guarantee the command's own --dry-run help text states. Root cause: openSprintBranch's document(writeSteps, writeReport) call reads a StepRefused write's Value, which plan.Steps.ValueFrom (cli/swarm/plan/plan.go) always errors on since a dry-run-refused write's record.Value is never set (cli/swarm/plan/run.go's interpret(), ModeDryRun branch). This bead's own worktree-half facts avoid the same trap via a dry-run-safe fallback (invocationOf in dispatch.go, falling back to the step's own literal Args when a record's Invocation is empty) rather than depending on ValueFrom for anything the step's own literals already carry. Filed as agent-plugins-2ekn (discovered-from this bead) rather than fixed here — it is BR's delta's code, and a proper fix touches how document()/ValueFrom handle a refused write generally, which is broader than this bead's scope.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b6
comments.text: retro:decision Two decisions the ACs left to implementation: (1) an existing worktree "for the dispatch" (AC-SWARM-DISP-003.11) is matched by branch name (bb/<dispatch-id>) against vcs.Worktree.Branch, not by path — the FRD's own Intent paragraph for this delta says naming the branch for the dispatch id is what lets `git worktree list` say which dispatch a tree belongs to, so branch is the identifying field by the delta's own reasoning. (2) The single --base flag serves double duty across the two halves this command now performs: for the sprint branch (BR's half, unchanged) it is the ref the branch is cut from when the branch doesn't exist yet, defaulting to HEAD; for the worktree (this bead's half) it is the ref the worktree is cut from, defaulting to the sprint branch's own current head (resolved fresh via vc.Resolve, never the recorded base_sha, so AC-SWARM-DISP-003.10 "read at that moment" holds even on a resumed run whose sprint branch has since moved). No second --base-like flag was added; the FRD's command signature ("swarm dispatch open --run <id> --dispatch <dispatch-id> [--base <ref>] [--branch <name>]") names only one.

Anchors: `cli/swarm/cli`, `cli/swarm/manifest`, `cli/swarm/vcs`.

"In one manifest write" is literal: the branch name and the commit it was cut
from go into a single write, not two. [[adr-026]] — no rollback, so the

- WHERE `--branch` is absent and no branch is recorded, the branch name SHALL
  be `sprint/<run-epic-id>`, which is the form the skills already create and
  resume onto.
- WHEN a branch already carries the name this run would use and the manifest
  records no branch, SHALL take the attention status, name the existing
  branch, name passing an explicit branch name as the resolution, and create

comments.text: retro:tooling caught in my own session, not shipped: a test asserting on captured stdout from dispatch() must pass the SAME buffer as both ioStreams.out and dispatch()'s stdout parameter — surface_test.go's runSurface does this (streams built from &out, then dispatch(root, streams, args, &out, &errOut) with the identical &out), but a test that builds streams from one buffer and passes a SEPARATE buffer to dispatch() silently asserts against an always-empty buffer and passes vacuously. No AC covers it and no existing test in the package would have caught a REGRESSION here — a future test built by copy-paste from a --run-only refusal test (which never inspects stdout) risks the same silent pass.

- SHALL advance `consecutive_dispatch_failures` by one WHEN a dispatch
  returns having completed no bead, and reset it to zero WHEN a dispatch
  returns having completed at least one.
- A bead returned as not reached SHALL NOT advance the count on its own.
- SHALL read `consecutive_dispatch_failures` from the manifest and treat an
  absent value as zero, so a fresh run starts at zero and a resumed run
  continues from what it recorded.
- WHEN the count reaches the configured threshold, SHALL report the run as
  stopped and take the stop status.
- The threshold SHALL arrive as an argument to the command, and WHERE it is
  absent the command SHALL use 3.
- SHALL NOT read `sf.toml`, or any other configuration file, to resolve the
  threshold. Resolving it is the coordinator's, at the authorization gate
  where every other run policy is resolved, so the container gains no
  configuration-reading surface.

**ACs — citations owed here:**
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.4 — unit
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.5 — unit
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.6 — unit
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.11 — e2e — **proving delta** (MFK participates)
notes:
**Decision provenance.** The threshold's source was the blueprint's one
Open Question, resolved by the human to the `sf.toml` `[run]` mechanism with
a default of 3. The CLI takes it as an argument; `sprint-scope` resolves it
as a seventh authorization-gate row (ADP-C's work, not this item's).

**Key name DECIDED by the human:** the `sf.toml` `[run]` key is
`dispatch_failure_threshold`, chosen to match the manifest key
`consecutive_dispatch_failures` that the breaker reads. The flag name on
`swarm ready` stays deliberately unpinned per the blueprint's "anchors, not
signatures" rule. Nothing here is open.

title: PC: swarm phase close
description:
Implements the **PC** delta — `swarm phase close` in
[[container-swarm-cli]] (added). Blueprint section: "### `swarm phase close`
in [[container-swarm-cli]] (added)".

The tracker's own epic-closing command ignores its positional argument and
closes every eligible epic in the database at exit 0. This command exists so
that a scope is an argument the plan carries, and so that closing nothing is
a reported outcome rather than a silence.

Stage 2 (the loop).


## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
acceptance_criteria:
Behavior lines from the delta:

- SHALL derive the epics it may close from the run epic's own descendants,
  and close only epics found by that walk.
- SHALL report each epic it closed as a property, and report the beads a
  closure released as ready.
- WHEN no epic in the run is eligible, SHALL report that as its answer and
  exit clear.
- WHEN an epic is left open because a child is open, SHALL report the open
  child's id as the reason.
- WHEN the eligibility query fails, SHALL report the query as unanswered and
  take the stop status, never reporting an unanswered query as nothing
  eligible.
- An epic SHALL be eligible WHEN it is open and carries no open child, which
  is the tracker's own rule; what this command adds is the restriction to the
  run's descendants, never a second rule.

**ACs — this item owes every citation below at the level shown**
([[ac-traceability-standards]]):
- AC-SWARM-DISP-001.1 — e2e — **proving delta**
- AC-SWARM-DISP-001.2 — e2e
- AC-SWARM-DISP-001.3 — unit
- AC-SWARM-DISP-001.4 — e2e
- AC-SWARM-DISP-001.5 — unit
- AC-SWARM-DISP-001.6 — e2e — **proving delta**
- AC-SWARM-DISP-001.7 — e2e
- AC-SWARM-DISP-001.8 — e2e — **proving delta**
- AC-SWARM-DISP-001.9 — unit

metadata.tier_reason: Well-specified command over TRK operations, localized to the command surface; the eligibility rule is the tracker own and is not reimplemented here

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text: retro:environment bd's dependency rule refuses a task 'blocks' an epic directly. Measured on this bd: `bd dep add <task> <epic> --type blocks --json` -> {"error":"tasks can only block other tasks, not epics"}; the reverse (`bd dep add <epic> <task> --type blocks`) -> {"error":"epics can only block other epics, not tasks"}. Only epic-blocks-epic is accepted, and bd's ready query walks that edge transitively: with fixture-run.phase-b blocked-by fixture-run.phase-a (both epics), fixture-run.phase-b.1 (phase-b's own open child task) does not read as ready until phase-a closes — confirmed via a real bd in cli/swarm/e2e/phase_close_test.go's TestPhaseCloseClosesOnlyItsOwnRunAndNamesWhatItReleased. This is the only mechanism by which closing one phase epic releases another phase's beads as ready; a future bead wiring cross-phase dependencies should use epic-to-epic blocks, not a task blocking on an epic.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text: retro:decision the closed_epics fact reports the SAME id list in dry-run and execute mode — derived from the eligibility READ (bd epic status --eligible-only), never from the write's own record. Rejected alternative: mirror manifest set's dry-run convention (report the pre-write stored value, would-be state only in the summary prose) — that fits a manifest KEY that has an independently-readable stored value, but closed_epics has no such value to fall back to, and the FRD states 'a criterion below saying a command reports something is saying that thing is a property of the answer, not prose the caller has to parse,' so AC-SWARM-DISP-001.3's 'reports the epics it would close' has to be a real fact even under refusal. Cost of the rejected alternative: AC-SWARM-DISP-001.3 would have no fact to point at, only a summary line.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text: retro:decision AC-SWARM-DISP-001.6 asks for 'the open child's id' as the reason an ineligible epic stays open, but bd's own eligibility answer (bd epic status) carries only total_children/closed_children counts, not which child is open. Decision: query each ineligible epic's own children (tracker.Children) and name the lowest-id one not in tracker.StateDone as the reason — deterministic, but arbitrary when more than one child is open (the FRD names none as authoritative). Rejected alternative: name every open child rather than one — rejected because the AC's wording ('the open child's id', singular) and the fixture's own scenario (exactly one open child) both point at one id, and a list would still need a rule for which to lead with.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b4
comments.text: retro:gap the FRD and blueprint never say explicitly whether the RUN epic itself (as opposed to its descendants) is in this command's closing scope. Decision: never — the command's own scope is exactly tracker.Descendants(run), which by construction excludes the scope argument itself, so the run epic is left to whatever closes it at retro/post-flight. This reads as the intended split ('the target epic closes on the same rule as the ceremony phases' talks about descendants, never about the run epic), but it is inferred rather than stated.

title: QF: swarm ready — the dispatch set
description:
Implements the **QF** delta — `swarm ready` in [[container-swarm-cli]]
(added — the dispatch set). Blueprint section: "### `swarm ready` in
[[container-swarm-cli]] (added — the dispatch set)".

What may be dispatched now, with the run's filters applied inside the run's
scope. Four measured traps live here, and each is a filter or a guard rather
than a longer query.

Stage 2 (the loop). AQ narrows this query and CB reports through its answer,
so this item lands before both.


## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Anchors: `cli/swarm/cli`, `cli/swarm/tracker`, `cli/swarm/vcs`.

Relied upon, not duplicated: `Status Collector` supplies the completion tally
and the scope comparison for AC-SWARM-DISP-002.2 — do not reimplement it.

The filter set implemented here is reused by AQ; build it once so AQ adds one
filter rather than restating the set.
acceptance_criteria:
Behavior lines from the delta:

- SHALL refuse an empty or absent run scope with the malformed-invocation
  status, and SHALL NOT treat an absent scope as the whole repository.
- The ready set SHALL exclude epics, closed beads, deferred beads, and beads
  labelled for human attention.
- The ready set SHALL reach beads at any depth beneath the run epic, through
  the `Tracker`'s descendant walk rather than a single-level query, and SHALL
  span every dispatch in the run rather than any one of them — narrowing to a
  dispatch is `--agent`'s and nothing else's.
- Each bead SHALL be reported with the dispatch id it is assigned to; a bead
  assigned to none SHALL be reported as unassigned rather than omitted.
- WHEN a bead is assigned to a dispatch whose worktree is standing, SHALL
  report it as held rather than as available.
- A dispatch's standing worktree SHALL be matched to its dispatch by the
  branch that worktree has checked out, and WHERE that branch carries no
  dispatch id, by the assignee of the bead its head commit closed.
- WHEN a tracker response is not the shape a queue takes, SHALL take the stop
  status rather than reporting a length derived from it.

**ACs — citations owed here:**
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.1 — e2e
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.2 — e2e (via relied-upon `Status Collector`)
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.3 — unit
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.7 — e2e
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.8 — e2e
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.9 — e2e — **proving delta** (VCS participates)
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.10 — e2e — **proving delta** (TRK participates)
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.16 — unit — **proving delta** (TRK participates)
- AC-SWARM-DISP-002.17 — e2e — **proving delta** (TRK participates)
notes:
**Supersession.** `agent-plugins-y63n.4` (`bb-status.sh`'s human-queue check
is repo-wide, not run-scoped) is subsumed by this delta: a repo-wide check is
run-scoped by construction once the ready set refuses an absent scope and
derives its set from the run's own descendants. Close or re-scope that bead
when this item lands; the final DoD item is the backstop.

title: MFK: manifest gains consecutive_dispatch_failures
description:
Implements the **MFK** delta — `schemas/swarm/manifest.strata` and the
`Manifest` rule set (modified — the failure count). Blueprint section:
"### `schemas/swarm/manifest.strata` and the `Manifest` rule set (modified —
the failure count)".

The circuit breaker has to survive a resumed session, so its count is
durable. The manifest's key set is closed, so the key is declared before
anything writes it.

Stage 1 (capability layer).


## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Anchors: `schemas/swarm/manifest.strata`, `cli/swarm/manifest`,
`cli/testdata/swarm-fixtures/core`.

**This item carries a lockstep obligation and must not be split.**
[[container-swarm-cli]]'s Change Guidance couples four artifacts to a
manifest-key change, and the blueprint assigns all four to this one delta so
no cross-delta reconciliation is needed: `schemas/swarm/manifest.strata`, the
generated JSON Schema and Go model, the validation rules, and the re-recorded
`core` end-to-end fixture. All four land in this item's single change.

Schema work goes through Strata ([[adr-016]]) — `strata` is the one source;

acceptance_criteria:
Behavior lines from the delta:

- `RunManifest` SHALL carry `consecutive_dispatch_failures`, an optional
  `Int` declared on `DispatchKeys`, so its stage is dispatch and its absence
  before the run's first dispatch is legitimate.
- The `Manifest` component SHALL refuse a write that decreases
  `consecutive_dispatch_failures` by more than a reset to zero, since the
  only legitimate decrease is a dispatch that completed something.
- WHEN `consecutive_dispatch_failures` is absent, the `Manifest` component
  SHALL report it as absent rather than as zero; reading an absent count as
  zero is the caller's, not the record's.

**AC participated in:** AC-SWARM-DISP-002.11 (proved by CB, e2e). This item
owes no AC citation.
notes:
**Fixture note.** Re-record only the `core` fixture. Change Guidance:
"A fixture recorded to prove that an older manifest shape is still readable
SHALL NOT be re-recorded, since re-recording it destroys the only evidence
that reading an older shape works." Leave any `legacy`-kind fixture alone.

**Verification-timing note.** AC-SWARM-DISP-002.11 is proved by CB, which
depends on this item. Verification lands there.

comments.text:
retro:proof the backwards-refusal rule was proved by a negative control, not by a green test.
evidence: with checkFailureCount commented out of CheckWrite, `go test ./swarm/manifest/ -run TestTheDispatchFailureCount -v` → exit 1, 'validate_test.go:179: one lower: the write was accepted' and 'almost a reset: the write was accepted'. With the call restored → exit 0, PASS. The test also carries three positive controls (rise to 4, reset to 0, re-write the same 3) and a first-write-against-an-empty-record control, so a rule that refused every write to the key could not pass it.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b3
comments.text:
retro:decision the delta's second behavior line fixes three of the four boundaries and leaves one open; I settled it as 'equal is not a decrease'.
evidence: the line reads 'SHALL refuse a write that decreases consecutive_dispatch_failures by more than a reset to zero'. That settles rising (allowed), a reset to 0 (allowed) and any lower non-zero value (refused). It does not say what happens when the write equals the recorded count. I implemented next >= recorded as accepted, so re-writing 3 over 3 goes through — the same shape the write-once rule already takes for the branch, where re-writing the recorded value is what lets a resumed run reuse it rather than fail on finding it. Rejected alternative: refuse an equal write as a no-op that signals a confused caller; it would make an idempotent retry after a dropped connection fail, which is the exact situation a durable count exists for. cli/swarm/manifest/validate.go, 'next >= recorded'.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b3
comments.text:
retro:decision the third behavior line ('report an absent count as absent rather than as zero') needed no code — I pinned it with a test instead of adding a mechanism.
evidence: Document.Get and Document.Decode already return present/absent as a separate answer from the value (cli/swarm/manifest/manifest.go: 'Present-and-absent are separate answers on purpose'), and Validate already reports a dispatch-stage key absent at the scope stage as SeverityPending rather than a failure. Writing a bespoke accessor for this one key would have been a second opinion about a behaviour the Document already has. Rejected alternative: a typed reader returning (int, bool) on the manifest surface — it would add an API nothing calls, since the caller that needs it (CB) is a later bead. The absence semantics are now pinned by TestTheDispatchFailureCountRisesOrResetsToZeroAndIsAbsentBeforeItStarts, which asserts Get reports absent, Decode returns (false, nil) leaving the target untouched, and Validate at the scope stage raises no failure for the key.

comments.text:

title: VCS: Version Control and Git Version Control — the dispatch loop's writes
description:
Implements the **VCS** delta — `Version Control` and `Git Version Control`
in [[container-swarm-cli]] (modified — the dispatch loop's operations).
Blueprint section: "### `Version Control` and `Git Version Control` in
[[container-swarm-cli]] (modified — the dispatch loop's operations)".

The loop creates and removes worktrees, creates and deletes branches,
rebases, merges fast-forward-only, fetches and pushes. Ancestry comparison,
worktree listing with its prune, and remote comparison already exist; this
widens the interface to the writes and states them in the run's vocabulary.

Stage 1 (capability layer).


## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Anchors: `cli/swarm/vcs`, `cli/swarm/vcs/git`.

The no-force rule is an interface-shape obligation, not a runtime check:
the removal operation must have no force parameter at all.

Do not fold this delta into the container blueprint — the stage-1 fold work
order does that.
acceptance_criteria:
Behavior lines from the delta:

- The `Version Control` interface SHALL declare operations for creating a
  worktree at a named path on a named new branch from a named base, removing
  a worktree, creating a branch from a named base, deleting a branch,
  rebasing a branch onto a named commit, merging fast-forward-only, fetching
  a remote, and pushing a branch.
- The worktree-removal operation SHALL NOT accept a force argument, so no
  caller can reach the forcing form.
- WHEN a merge or a rebase is refused, `Git Version Control` SHALL decode the
  refusal into the run's vocabulary — which paths conflict, and whether the
  refusal was a non-fast-forward — rather than returning the tool's text for
  a caller to parse.
- Each operation whose invocation writes SHALL declare whether re-running it
  is safe, per [[adr-026]].
- A step whose answer is carried by its exit status SHALL declare the
  statuses it answers with, so a legitimate "no" is not read as a failure.

**ACs this item participates in (citations owed by the proving delta):**
AC-SWARM-DISP-002.9 (QF), 003.1 and 003.9 (WT), 004.3 and 004.7 (MG),
005.7 (LD). This item owes no AC citation.
notes:
**Verification-timing note.** All six participating ACs are proved by
stage-2 items (QF, WT, MG, LD) that depend on this one. Code may proceed
now; verification lands with those items.

metadata.tier_reason: Same decoder risk as TRK plus decoding merge and rebase refusals into the run vocabulary; the no-force rule is an interface-shape obligation, and every operation here writes

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b2
comments.text:
retro:proof Both load-bearing guards were confirmed by negative control before the bead closed — each was made to fail, then restored. evidence: (1) The no-force obligation. Injected the forcing form: sed -i 's|"worktree", "remove", path)|"worktree", "remove", "--force", path)|' swarm/vcs/git/git.go go test ./swarm/vcs/git/ -run 'TestTheWorktreeRemovalHasNoForcingForm|TestTheInvocationsItDeclares' -> exit 1 --- FAIL: TestTheInvocationsItDeclares git_test.go:130: remove a worktree: got [git worktree remove --force /w/dev-1] want [git worktree remove /w/dev-1] --- FAIL: TestTheWorktreeRemovalHasNoForcingForm git_test.go:273: the removal invocation carries the option "--force"; it is meant to carry none git_test.go:287: git.go names "--force" — the forcing form of a removal or a push Reverted; the same command then exits 0. (2) The write/dry-run declaration. Flipped Fetch from plan.Write to plan.Read: go test ./swarm/vcs/... -> exit 1 --- FAIL: TestADryRunPerformsNoneOfTheDispatchLoopsWrites vcs_test.go:189: a dry run ran [[git fetch origin]] vcs_test.go:198: "fetch" was "ran" in a dry run, want "refused"; it is not declared a write --- FAIL: TestEveryWriteDeclaresWhetherReRunningItIsSafe git_test.go:232: fetch is declared read, want write; a dry run would perform it Reverted; exit 0. Every Repeatable declaration on the eight new writes is a measurement taken in a scratch repository on git 2.43.0, not an inference. The three that matter, because they are the ones a recovery depends on: git merge --ff-only twice -> exit 0 both times, second says "Already up to date."; and a REFUSED --ff-only leaves `git status --porcelain` empty, HEAD unmoved, no MERGE_HEAD or rebase directory => Repeatable true git push origin main twice -> exit 0 both, second says "Everything up-to-date" => Repeatable true git worktree remove

twice -> exit 0 then exit 128, "fatal: '

' is not a working tree" => Repeatable false

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b2
comments.text:
retro:decision A merge or rebase refusal is a plan-STOPPING failure carrying a typed *vcs.Refusal, not an exit status declared through Step.Answers.
evidence: The bead carries two behavior lines that pull in opposite directions — "WHEN a merge or a rebase is refused, Git Version Control SHALL decode the refusal into the run's vocabulary" and "A step whose answer is carried by its exit status SHALL declare the statuses it answers with, so a legitimate 'no' is not read as a failure". A refused fast-forward reads like a legitimate "no", so declaring Answers=[128] on it was the obvious reading.

Rejected, for two reasons that are both mechanical rather than stylistic:
  - plan.Record.Failed() is `r.Err != nil || !r.Answered`. Declaring 128 an answer does not make the step succeed while its decoder returns an error, so the declaration would buy nothing and would misdescribe the step.
  - The existing Merge already documents the ordering guard it depends on: "a worktree removal chained after a merge that exited non-zero is the incident this design exists to prevent". A refused fast-forward that let the plan continue would reintroduce exactly that.

So: the refusal stops the plan, and the CALLER branches on it by reading the report's record and doing errors.As(record.Err, &refusal). Proved end to end by TestARefusalReachesTheCallerThroughTheReport in cli/swarm/vcs/vcs_test.go — the *Refusal survives the trip through the Plan Runner rather than being flattened to prose.

Cost of the alternative had I taken it: commands built on this in stage 2 (MG, RM) would have had steps that continue after a fold that did not happen.

Second decision, settled silently because the blueprint states the no-force rule only for worktree removal: the same discipline is applied to branch deletion and push. DeleteBranch uses `git branch -d`, never -D — a dispatch branch that is not merged is one whose work has not landed. Push carries no --force — measured, a refused push exits 1 with " ! [rejected]        main -> main (non-fast-forward)", which is a condition to report rather than to overwrite. Neither is required by an acceptance criterion; both are enforced by the package-wide literal scan in TestTheWorktreeRemovalHasNoForcingForm, which forbids "--force", "-f" and "-D" outright.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b2
comments.text:
retro:environment A sibling dispatch's `bd dolt pull` serializes every bd call in the shared container, and the project's own script-self-tests check calls bd — so this run's gate blocked for ~22 minutes behind another agent's tracker sync.
evidence: Dispatches in this run share one container. At 17:16 both `bd create` (mine) and `bb-checks.py` were queued behind a sibling's pull:

  ps -eo pid=,args=  ->
    27830 bd dolt pull          (started 17:10, dev-e6xt-b3)
    10282 bd where
    24764 bd where
    32522 bd create Decode ...

  ps -o pid=,lstart=,etime=,time=,args= -p 27830  ->
    27830 Tue Sep  1 17:10:13 2026   18:06  00:02:00  bd dolt pull

The pull was working, not hung (CPU climbing 1:49 -> 2:00 over two minutes of wall clock). It exited at 17:38:13, and both my `bd create` and the checks completed within seconds of that.

The part that matters for the run's own tooling: `bb-checks.py`'s script-self-tests check stalled mid-run at `pre-flight-check --self-test`, because
  plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh:608
    BD_DB="$(bd where 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *database: *//p' | head -1)"
runs bd unconditionally. So a project check — not just bead ceremony — can block indefinitely on another dispatch's tracker operation. There is no timeout on it and nothing in the output says why it is stopped; from outside it is indistinguishable from a hung check.

Two traps for whoever reads this next:
  - `pgrep -f "bd dolt pull"` is NOT a usable wait predicate here. Every sibling shell waiting on the pull carries that string in its own command line, so the pattern matches the waiters and the until-loop never terminates. Two sibling shells in this container were spinning on exactly that (pids 4645 and 9071). Wait on the pid (`ps -p <pid>`) or on the output file instead.
  - The gate's wall-clock time is not its cost. Re-running bb-checks.py on the final tree after the lock cleared took under a minute; the first run's ~22 minutes was all lock.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b2
comments.text:
retro:proof git prints merge and rebase CONFLICT lines on STDOUT, not stderr — a decoder reading stderr for the reason finds an empty stream.
evidence: Measured on git 2.43.0 in a scratch repository, conflicting `git merge --no-ff -m "merge dev" dev`:
  exit 1
  stdout:
    Auto-merging f.txt
    CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in f.txt
    Auto-merging g.txt
    CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in g.txt
    Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.
  stderr: (empty)

Conflicting `git rebase main dev`:
  exit 1
  stdout: the same CONFLICT lines
  stderr: Rebasing (1/1)error: could not apply 8a198f8... dev  + hints

Refused `git merge --ff-only dev` is the opposite — nothing on stdout, and the reason is on stderr behind several hint lines:
  exit 128
  stderr: ... hint: Diverging branches can't be fast-forwarded ...
          fatal: Not possible to fast-forward, aborting.

So the refusal decoder scans BOTH streams. Reading only stderr would have reported a conflicting merge as a refusal with no paths; reading only stdout would have missed every non-fast-forward.

Four conflict-line forms were measured, and the path decoder is held to them:
  CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in f.txt
  CONFLICT (add/add): Merge conflict in sp ace.txt
  CONFLICT (modify/delete): del.txt deleted in dev and modified in HEAD.  Version HEAD of del.txt left in tree.
  CONFLICT (rename/rename): a.txt renamed to c.txt in HEAD and to b.txt in dev.

A path is printed UNQUOTED, spaces included — `sp ace.txt` above is one path, and any whitespace split would have made it two. That is why the decoder takes everything after "Merge conflict in " to end of line rather than tokenising.

Residual limit, stated rather than hidden: a path containing the verb phrase " deleted in " or " renamed to " would be cut short by the second and third rules, and nothing in git's output distinguishes that case. Every CONFLICT line is therefore kept verbatim in Refusal.Detail regardless of whether a path was extracted, so a conflict this cannot parse is visible rather than silently absent (TestAConflictLineIsKeptEvenWhenItsPathCannotBeParsed).

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b2
comments.text:
retro:environment The tracker's Dolt remote cannot be pushed from this container: the pull that would make the push a fast forward aborts on a merge conflict that needs operator resolution. This bead's closure is in the LOCAL database only.
evidence: The close ceremony committed, then reported its own push failure:

  bb-close-bead.sh agent-plugins-o63s.2 2 "VCS: ..."
  -> exit 0
     ✓ Updated issue: agent-plugins-o63s.2
     bb-close-bead: WARNING — commit landed but `bd dolt push` failed. The closure is
     in the local database only; push it before the container is reclaimed.
     6f0f1f5

Retried by hand, twice, with no other bd process running (`ps -eo pid=,args= | grep "[b]d dolt"` empty before the first):

  bd dolt push
  -> exit 1
     Error: push to origin/main: Error 1105: To git+https://github.com/brettcallaghan/agent-plugins.git
      ! [rejected]            main -> main (non-fast-forward)
     hint: Updates were rejected because the tip of your current branch is behind
     hint: its remote counterpart. Integrate the remote changes (e.g. 'dolt pull ...')
     hint: before pushing again.

The documented remedy does not clear it:

  bd dolt pull
  -> exit 1
     Error: merge origin/main: merge conflicts in issues require operator resolution;
            merge aborted and working set restored

`bd dolt --help` exposes no conflict-resolution subcommand — only start/stop/status, show/set/test, commit/push/pull and remote add/list/remove. So this is not recoverable from inside a dispatch, and I did not attempt it: resolving tracker merge conflicts blind would rewrite bead states belonging to the sibling dispatches sharing this container.

State left behind, all verified rather than assumed:
  - `bd show agent-plugins-o63s.2 --json` -> "status": "closed", "assignee": "dev-e6xt-b2",
    "closed_at": "2026-09-01T17:41:10Z". The aborted pull restored the working set without
    losing the closure.
  - `git log --oneline -1` -> 6f0f1f5 agent-plugins-o63s.2 P2 VCS: Version Control and Git
    Version Control — the dispatch loop's writes
  - `git status --porcelain` -> empty.

So the code and the closure are both in the commit on the dispatch branch; only the tracker's remote copy is behind. Same container also showed a sibling's `bd dolt pull` running 28 minutes earlier (17:10:13 to 17:38:13), which is the likely other half of the race.

title: TRK: Tracker and Beads Tracker — the dispatch loop's operations
description:
Implements the **TRK** delta — `Tracker` and `Beads Tracker` in
[[container-swarm-cli]] (modified — the dispatch loop's operations).
Blueprint section: "### `Tracker` and `Beads Tracker` in
[[container-swarm-cli]] (modified — the dispatch loop's operations)".

The loop asks the tracker four questions the core feature did not need:
which epics under a run are eligible to close, what is ready under a scope
with the run's filters applied, what one assignee holds, and what a bead's
acceptance signals say. Each is stated in the run's vocabulary on the
interface and decoded once in the implementation, so commands stay free of
any tracker's spelling.

Stage 1 (capability layer). Every stage-2 command is a plan over the
operations added here.


## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
Anchors: `cli/swarm/tracker`, `cli/swarm/tracker/beads`.

Carry the blueprint's anchors; choose your own structure within them. Do not
fold this delta into `specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md` — the
stage-1 fold work order does that for every stage-1 delta at once.

Change Guidance that binds here: a component other than the two
implementations SHALL NOT name `bd` or reach the Process Runner; an
operation added to the interface SHALL be stated in the run's vocabulary
rather than the tool's.
acceptance_criteria:
Behavior lines from the delta, all of which this item must satisfy:

- The `Tracker` interface SHALL declare an operation returning the epics
  beneath a named run eligible to close, taking the run scope as an
  argument rather than reading a default.
- The `Tracker` interface SHALL declare an operation returning the beads
  ready beneath a named scope, excluding epics, and an operation returning
  the beads one assignee holds beneath that same scope, partitioned by
  whether each is ready or in progress.
- WHEN an operation's response is not the shape its decoder expects, the
  `Beads Tracker` SHALL report the step as failed rather than decoding a
  length or a field from it.
- Every operation added here SHALL return a plan step, and SHALL NOT reach
  the Process Runner itself.

**ACs this item participates in (citations owed by the proving delta, not
here):** AC-SWARM-DISP-001.1, 001.6, 001.8 (proved by PC); 002.10, 002.16,
002.17 (proved by QF); 004.4 (proved by MG); 004.11 (proved by RM).

This item owes no AC citation. It owes the operations and their decoders,
plus the unit case Change Guidance requires: "WHEN a decoder is added or
changed, a unit case SHALL pin every result shape that subcommand is known
to return, including its empty forms."
notes:
**Verification-timing note.** Every AC this item participates in is proved
by a delta outside its dependency closure (PC, QF, MG, RM all depend on this
item, not the reverse). Code work may proceed as soon as this item is ready;
verification of those ACs lands with the proving items. The final DoD item is
the backstop.

metadata.tier_reason: Interface design plus a decoder per subcommand in the one component allowed to name bd; a mis-decode returns a wrong answer at exit 0, which is the failure this container exists to remove

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b1
comments.text:
retro:proof `bd ready` silently truncated the ready set at 100, and this delta's operation was one of the callers — reproduced pre-fix, then fixed.

Measured on bd 1.2.2 (`bd version` -> `bd version 1.2.2 (6c124203e: HEAD@6c124203e771)`) against this repository's database:

    bd ready --json          | jq length  -> 100
    bd ready --limit 0 --json | jq length -> 106

`Tracker.Ready` built its argv without `--limit`, so every ready query the dispatch loop is built on would have stopped at 100 beads at exit 0. The unit reproduction, run BEFORE the fix with the assertion updated and the source still carrying the old argv:

    $ go test ./swarm/tracker/... -run TestTheInvocationsItDeclares
    --- FAIL: TestTheInvocationsItDeclares (0.00s)
        beads_test.go:113: the whole ready set:
              got  bd ready --parent run-1 --json
              want bd ready --parent run-1 --limit 0 --json
        beads_test.go:113: a filtered ready set:
              got  bd ready --parent run-1 --assignee dev-1 --exclude-type epic --exclude-label human --json
              want bd ready --parent run-1 --assignee dev-1 --exclude-type epic --exclude-label human --limit 0 --json
    FAIL
    exit=1

Same command after adding `--limit 0` to the argv: exit 0.

Note the asymmetry that makes this non-obvious, and that `Children`'s existing comment gets backwards for `ready`: the default DOES apply to `bd ready`'s JSON output but did NOT to `bd list`'s — `bd list --all --json | jq length` and `bd list --all --limit 0 --json | jq length` both returned 585. Neither flag can be reasoned from the other.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b1
comments.text:
retro:decision Two of the four operations CANNOT be scoped by their invocation, so the scope was moved into the decoded value instead of into the argv.

The delta requires each new operation to take the run scope as an argument and to return a plan step. bd cannot honour that for two of them, measured on 1.2.2:

    bd epic status --json | jq length                        -> 12
    bd epic status agent-plugins-e6xt --json | jq length     -> 12   (exit 0, stderr empty)

The positional argument is ignored — an invocation that LOOKS scoped is not. And for the assignee query:

    bd list --parent agent-plugins-e6xt --all --limit 0 --json | jq -r '.[].id'
    -> the run's seven DIRECT children only; no grandchild

    bd ready --parent agent-plugins-e6xt --assignee dev-e6xt-b1 --exclude-type=epic
    -> agent-plugins-o63s.1, a grandchild

So `--parent` is transitive on `bd ready` and direct-only on `bd list`, and there is no transitive assignee query at all.

DECIDED: `ClosableEpics` and `Holding` declare the widest correct invocation, and their decoders return `tracker.Closable` / `tracker.Held` — types that carry the scope asked about and whose ONLY accessor is `Within(beneath []Bead)`, taking the run's descendant set. A caller cannot read the wide answer as the run's without narrowing it, and a unit test asserts neither argv carries the scope (`TestTheTwoWideQueriesDoNotPretendToBeScoped`).

REJECTED: passing the scope to bd anyway. It costs nothing at the call site and is wrong in both directions — `bd list --parent` would silently drop every bead below the first level, and `bd epic status <run>` would read as filtered while returning the whole database. Both are exit-0 wrong answers, which is the failure this container exists to remove.

REJECTED: returning a plain `[]Bead`/`[]EpicClosure` and documenting that the caller must narrow. Prose does not stop a caller, and the caller here would close another run's epics.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b1
comments.text:
retro:decision The drain derivation (`tracker.AgentQueue`) was built HERE, in stage 1, rather than left to the AQ delta.

The blueprint's TRK behavior line asks the interface for 'an operation returning the beads one assignee holds beneath that same scope, PARTITIONED by whether each is ready or in progress'. No single bd invocation answers both halves — `bd ready` excludes in_progress by construction (its own help: 'Excludes in_progress, blocked, deferred, and hooked issues'), so the partition is necessarily two queries. A type alone (`tracker.Queue`) would satisfy the noun but not the word 'operation'.

DECIDED: `AgentQueue(ctx, t, runner, scope, agent, filter)` lives in `cli/swarm/tracker/queue.go`, composing `Ready` + `Holding` + the existing `Descendants` walk, and returning a `Queue` whose `Drained()` is true only when BOTH halves are empty. `tracker.Descendants` is the precedent: a derivation over steps, in this package, taking a `plan.Runner` and reaching no Process Runner.

REJECTED: leaving it to AQ. The AQ delta says 'The drain derivation SHALL be one implementation, reused by `swarm dispatch accept`'s drain check rather than restated in it' — two stage-2 deltas (AQ and MG) each need it, and a stage-1 home is the only one that is not one of them. The cost of the rejected option is the drain verdict being derived twice, which is precisely the duplication that line forbids.

Cost accepted: TRK now ships slightly more than the four operations its behavior lines enumerate. A reviewer who thinks the derivation belongs in stage 2 can move the file without touching the interface.

Note for whoever builds AQ: the two halves are scoped DIFFERENTLY and that is deliberate. `Ready` is scoped by bd's own transitive `--parent`; `Holding` cannot be, so it is narrowed against the walk. See `AgentQueue`'s doc comment.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b1
comments.text:
retro:gap The delta's intent names FOUR questions the loop asks the tracker; only two of them have a SHALL line, so the fourth had to be decided rather than read.

The intent (blueprint, '### `Tracker` and `Beads Tracker` … the dispatch loop's operations'): 'which epics under a run are eligible to close, what is ready under a scope with the run's filters applied, what one assignee holds, and WHAT A BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE SIGNALS SAY'. The four Behavior bullets under it cover the first three and the shape/plan-step rules. Nothing states what an acceptance-signal operation returns, and the AC table lists 004.11 as satisfied by TRK and proved by RM — so TRK owes something for it with no line saying what.

DECIDED from `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh`, which is the only place the five signals are enumerated: 1 closed in the tracker, 2 a commit carrying the id, 3 merged, 4 worktree gone, 5 findings recorded. Signals 2-4 are Version Control's (the VCS delta). Signals 1 and 5 are the tracker's: 1 is already `Bead`, 5 needed an operation, so TRK ships `Findings(name, id)` over `bd comments <id> --json`.

Evidence that 5 needed a NEW operation rather than a field of an existing one — measured on bd 1.2.2:

    bd show agent-plugins-qozp.1 --json \
      | jq -c '.[0] | {comment_count, has_comments_key: (has("comments"))}'
    -> {"comment_count":1,"has_comments_key":false}

`bd show` carries a count and no comments, so the notes are only reachable through `bd comments`.

What would have removed the guesswork: one Behavior bullet naming the acceptance-signal operation's answer, the way the other three are named. As it stands the operation's shape rests on a shell script that is not part of the spec corpus.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b1
comments.text:
retro:environment A sibling dispatch running `bd dolt pull` holds an exclusive lock on the Dolt database, and every other `bd` invocation in the run blocks on it until it finishes — no error, no timeout of its own.

Observed while measuring subcommand shapes for the decoders. `bd list --status in_progress --limit 0 --json` ran past 120s and was still running; `ps aux` showed:

    root 27830 11.2 0.9 2797936 156412 ? Sl 17:10 0:36 bd dolt pull        (BEADS_ACTOR=dev-e6xt-b3)
    root 29202  0.1 0.5 1919548  83972 ? Sl 17:10 0:00 bd list --status in_progress --limit 0 --json

and a second invocation issued while the pull held the lock returned, on stderr:

    Error: failed to open database: embeddeddolt: init schema: embeddeddolt: open db: failed to load database "beads": the database is locked by another dolt process

So the failure has two faces depending on timing: a hang (the first invocation waits) and an explicit lock error (a later one). Neither is recoverable by retrying immediately.

For the next agent: this is not a broken tracker and not worth diagnosing again. `bd dolt pull` took roughly five minutes here. Wrap tracker reads in `timeout`, and where a read must succeed, wait for `pgrep -f 'bd dolt pull'` to go quiet rather than retrying in a loop. Concurrent dispatches on one shared Dolt database make this reachable in any run with more than one agent.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b1
comments.text:
retro:proof Negative control on the one assertion that carries this delta's scoping claim, so it is not a test that passes for the wrong reason.

`TestAnAgentsQueueDoesNotReachOutsideTheRun` asserts that a bead the same dispatch id holds in ANOTHER run does not reach this run's queue. Control: widen the descendant set the narrowing is taken against, changing `held.Within(beneath)` to `held.Within(append(beneath, Bead{ID: "other-9.1"}))`:

    $ go test ./swarm/tracker/ -run TestAnAgentsQueueDoesNotReachOutsideTheRun
    --- FAIL: TestAnAgentsQueueDoesNotReachOutsideTheRun (0.00s)
        queue_test.go:50: InProgress = [other-9.1 run-1.2], want only run-1.2 — other-9.1 is another run's
    FAIL
    exit=1

Restored, exit 0. So the fake really does deliver both ids and the assertion is what removes the foreign one.

Also decided silently, and worth knowing: `AgentQueue` tracks which halves ANSWERED rather than only which failed. A step the plan runner SKIPS records no failure, so a failure check alone would let a skipped half arrive as an empty one — and an empty half is exactly what makes a queue read as drained. The guard is the `answered` map at the end of `AgentQueue`; `TestAHalfThatCouldNotBeReadIsNotAnEmptyHalf` covers the failing half, not the skipped one, which stays untested because the fake cannot produce a skip.

comments.text:

title: Generate the manifest key documentation from strata instead of hand-maintaining it in run-record.md
description:
From review of PR #31 (plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md:196), raised by the repository owner: 'This feels like documentation of the manifest -- and we can easily generate a markdown file from strata to provide that.'

run-record.md currently carries a hand-written description of the manifest's key set and their meanings. The manifest is defined in schemas/swarm/manifest.strata, and this repository already generates Markdown from strata sources — plugin/skills/spec/references/generated/ is produced exactly that way and kept current by scripts/generate-schemas.sh, with --check in the declared check set.

So the hand-written copy is a second source of truth for something already machine-described, and the machinery to retire it exists and is already wired into CI.

Worth deciding as part of this: whether the generated document is vendored into the skill (like the other generated references) or whether the skill simply tells the agent to ask the command. The second is cheaper and aligns with the run-and-read direction; the first keeps the key set readable without running anything.

Source: PR #31 review comment https://github.com/brettcallaghan/agent-plugins/pull/31#discussion_r3886975564
acceptance_criteria:
- The manifest key documentation is generated from schemas/swarm/manifest.strata rather than hand-written.
- generate-schemas.sh emits it and --check keeps it current, in the same way the existing generated references are kept current.
- run-record.md no longer restates the key set; it points at the generated document or at the command, whichever is decided.
- The decision between vendoring the generated document and telling the agent to ask the command is recorded with its reason.

metadata.tier_reason: Adding a markdown target and wiring it into an existing generator plus its --check; the pattern already exists for the spec model and is copied.

comments.author: dev-bd97-9
comments.text:
decision: vendor the generated manifest markdown into the skill (plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/generated/manifest.md), rather than telling the agent to run 'swarm manifest get --run <epic>' and read its output.

Reasoning: the review comment that opened this bead ('we can easily generate a markdown file from strata to provide that') names a file, not a command's output — the two are different artifacts. The otuj bead's 'run and read, don't pre-document' principle governs prose that restates what a COMMAND emits at runtime (its exit codes, its printed shape); the manifest key set is closer to the frontmatter shape reference the spec model already vendors the same way — a schema an agent may need to know about before any run epic exists to run a command against. Vendoring keeps that readable with nothing to run. The cost (one more generated artifact --check must keep current) is accepted the same way it already is for plugin/skills/spec/references/generated/.

Implementation: schemas/swarm's markdown target (already produced for schemas/swarm/output.strata's sibling models, since strata's markdown target runs per-package) is now wired into scripts/generate-schemas.sh alongside its existing json-schema and go targets, syncing to plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/generated/ with the same generated-by banner style as the spec model's. run-record.md's per-key 'what the keys mean' bullet list (which restated schemas/swarm/manifest.strata's own docstrings) is replaced by a pointer to the generated file; only the handful of facts about how a key is USED by this skill's own machinery (checks_baseline inlined into subagent prompts, review_passes/review_budget interaction, bb-close-bead.sh's --trailers-from read) stay, since those describe the skill, not the schema.

comments.author: dev-bd97-9
comments.text:
retro:tooling scripts/check-skills.sh's bundled-path rule (rule 2) resolves a backticked `path/to/file.ext` relative to the CITING file's directory, and a generated-file banner that names a real repo path with its extension (e.g. `cli/core/schema/swarm-model.schema.json`) from a file living several directories away fails it, since is_generated() only exempts files opening with the literal '<!-- GENERATED COPY' header — the plain '# Generated ...' banner style generate-schemas.sh already uses for the spec model is NOT exempt, it just happens to phrase its cross-reference as a bare directory ('under `cli/core/schema/`', no trailing filename) which the extension-matching regex never catches. Any future addition to that banner style must keep referencing paths by directory, not by filename with extension, or must resolve relative to the citing file's own directory.
evidence: first attempt used `cli/core/schema/swarm-model.schema.json` in plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/generated/README.md and scripts/check-skills.sh reported: 'ERROR plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/generated/README.md: backticked path does not resolve from this file: cli/core/schema/swarm-model.schema.json'. Rewording to 'the JSON Schema under `cli/core/schema/`' (matching plugin/skills/spec/references/generated/README.md's existing phrasing) made scripts/check-skills.sh exit 0.

title: The fixed 20KB skill-body cap makes a correctness edit compete with existing prose
description:
check-skills.sh sets BODY_BYTE_MAX = 20000 and --strict turns the warning into a failure. The cap does not distinguish a change that ADDS prose from one that CORRECTS a false statement, so at the boundary a correctness fix must win an argument against text it did not write.

Measured in run agent-plugins-bd97: run-batch/SKILL.md had TEN BYTES of headroom at HEAD (body 19990). ih18.21's Done-when required the file be updated to the command form, and every wording that both dropped the false claim and named the command measured 20004-20092 bytes — over the limit in every case. The correction landed, but the command itself, 'swarm manifest get --run <epic> --key trailers', went into two OTHER documents instead. ih18.13 hit the same wall on the same file and needed three rounds of trimming.

The finding states the shape better than a summary: 'A fixed byte budget on a skill file makes a CORRECTNESS edit compete with existing prose, and the loser is whichever the author judges least costly to drop. That is a bad trade to leave implicit in a check.'

agent-plugins-tnyu is filed and widens THAT ONE FILE's headroom. It does not change the trade, which recurs on the next skill file to approach 20 KB.

Source: retro candidate C6, run agent-plugins-bd97, findings ih18.21#3 and ih18.13#4. Accepted by the human at the retro's single ask.
acceptance_criteria:
- The check distinguishes 'over budget' from 'over budget AND this change added prose' — e.g. failing on growth past the limit while permitting a net-neutral or shrinking edit that stays over.
- A correctness fix is never blocked by prose it did not write.
- The cap still bites on a file that grows: the change must not simply raise or remove the limit.
- Replaying ih18.21's rejected wordings against the changed check lets the correct one land in run-batch/SKILL.md.

title: Add a tenth finding kind for a run's own conduct — agents have independently invented retro:process in three runs
description:
findings-capture-protocol's nine kinds describe what an IMPLEMENTING AGENT notices about work it was given. Two situations fall outside all nine, and run agent-plugins-bd97 produced both.

A COORDINATOR writing on a bead it did not implement — repairing a gate, recording that a bead's findings were supplied by someone other than its author — has no kind that fits (ih18.12#1, ih18.17#1). And an IMPLEMENTING AGENT STATING THAT ITS BEAD WAS CLEAN, which run-batch explicitly asks for, has none either: dev-bd97-2 wrote ih18.20#1 in good faith and had to invent 'retro:work-clean' to say it.

All three routed nowhere. They are not new:

- so39 — '2 findings unrouted (both retro:process:, both the coordinator's)'
- mpnf — 'third consecutive run at 2', plus an invented 'retro:incident:' that 'sent the run's most consequential finding to no audience at all'
- bd97 — 3 unrouted: two retro:process:, one retro:work-clean

retro:process has now been independently reached for by agents in at least three runs. A finding routed nowhere reaches its audience only if a human happens to read it, which is not a mechanism — and the mpnf precedent shows a run's most consequential finding can be the one that lands there.

Relationship to the clean-bead contradiction bead: that one fixes the CONTRADICTION (three documents, three instructions). This one gives the resulting finding somewhere to go. They are separable and both are needed.

Source: retro candidate C8, run agent-plugins-bd97, findings ih18.20#1, ih18.17#1, ih18.12#1, recurrence >=2 across so39 and mpnf. Accepted by the human at the retro's single ask.
acceptance_criteria:
- findings-capture-protocol.md defines a tenth kind covering HOW THE RUN WAS CONDUCTED, as distinct from what the work order contained.
- It spans both cases: an observation recorded by an agent other than the item's implementer, and an implementer's own statement that its bead was clean.
- The spelling is 'retro:process' — three runs' agents reached for it independently, which is stronger evidence of the right word than a fresh coinage.
- Its routing is defined (project audience — it is about the run, not the work order) and added to sprint-retro's routing table.
- Re-routing run agent-plugins-bd97's three unrouted findings under the new kind sends all three to an audience.

title: A bead's parent is encoded in its id, so --parent cannot re-home it and a ceremony epic can never close over filed-not-admitted findings
description:
Two facts that only bite together, both measured on bd 1.2.2.

**1. The parent-child hierarchy is the ID, not the field.** A bead created with '--parent=X' is minted as 'X.n'. Clearing the field afterwards succeeds and detaches nothing:

    bd update agent-plugins-bd97.4.6 --parent ''
    -> exit 0, '✓ Updated issue: ...'
    bd show agent-plugins-bd97.4.6 --json | jq .[0].parent   -> null

    bd list --parent agent-plugins-bd97.4 --status open --json | jq length
    -> 17, unchanged, INCLUDING the bead whose field was just cleared

Done for all 17 (each exit 0, 'moved=17 failed=none') and the count stayed 17. So '--parent' on an existing bead writes a field that neither 'bd list --parent' nor the epic-close child check reads. There is no re-homing operation; the id is the relationship, and it is fixed at creation.

**2. An epic cannot close over open children, and refuses by design.**

    bd close agent-plugins-bd97.4
    -> exit 1, 'cannot close epic agent-plugins-bd97.4: 17 open child issue(s); close children first or use --force to override'
    bd close agent-plugins-bd97.5
    -> exit 1, 'cannot close agent-plugins-bd97.5: blocked by open issues [agent-plugins-bd97.4] (use --force to override)'

**Together they make a specific instruction unworkable.** A sprint's review phase files findings and, under 'admit_review_findings=false', deliberately does NOT work them. Parenting those findings to the review PHASE epic — which is what this run's coordinator instructed, and it reads as the tidy choice — means that epic acquires children that will still be open when a future run picks them up. The phase epic can then never close, and because the ceremony phases are chained epic->epic, the retro and post-flight epics cannot close either. The run's own structure is held open by work it correctly decided not to do, and the mistake is unrecoverable after the fact because the ids are already minted.

The coordinator's own ten findings this run were filed at TOP LEVEL and caused none of this. The difference is entirely where they were parented at creation.

**What the coordinator did here, recorded rather than hidden:** closed the phase epics with '--force' after failing to re-home the findings, and said so. The findings are durable beads with their own ids and are named in the retro; closing the transient ceremony epic loses none of them.

Candidate directions, not prescribed:
- Say plainly, wherever a run is told to file findings, that a bead parented to a ceremony epic is parented there forever, and that filed-not-admitted findings therefore belong at top level or under a durable epic — never under a phase.
- Or give the ceremony-epic close path an explicit 'close over unadmitted findings' step so '--force' is not the only way through.
- Or ask bd for a re-home operation, so a parenting mistake is recoverable at all.
acceptance_criteria:
- Wherever a skill instructs an agent to file findings, it states where they must be parented and why a ceremony epic is the wrong home.
- A run whose review files findings under admit_review_findings=false can close its ceremony epics without --force.
- The id-encodes-parent behaviour is stated once as a measured fact, so no future agent attempts --parent as a re-home and reads exit 0 as success.

title: The AC coverage table declares a verification level testing-standards does not define
description:
MEASURED on this tree by agent-plugins-ih18.19's DoD audit.

specs/features/swarm-core/swarm-core-blueprint.md's AC Coverage table declares
three verification levels across its 45 rows: `unit` (38 rows), `e2e` (6 rows)
and `integration` (1 row, AC-SWARM-CORE-002.13).

specs/standards/testing-standards.md defines TWO layers, under '## Test Layers':
'### Unit Tests' and '### Snapshot Cases'. The string 'integration' does not
appear in that document at all:

    grep -n integration specs/standards/testing-standards.md   -> no output

The blueprint's 'Relied-upon elements (unchanged)' block names
[[testing-standards]] as 'the layer definitions the AC coverage table names',
so the table declares one row at a level its cited source does not define.

This is a vocabulary gap, not a coverage gap. AC-SWARM-CORE-002.13 IS verified,
twice, and both tests carry the citation comment:
  - cli/swarm/cli/manifest_test.go, 'func TestSetAppliesSeveralKeysAsOneMerge'
  - cli/swarm/manifest/beads/store_test.go,
    'func TestSeveralKeysInOneInvocationAreOneReadAndOneWrite'
Both exercise the command surface together with the store through a fake
process runner, which is what 'integration' ordinarily names and what neither
declared layer covers by name.

Two resolutions, and the choice is the point of the bead:
  a) testing-standards gains a third layer, defined, and every blueprint that
     already uses the word is checked against the definition; or
  b) the row is re-declared at a layer that exists, and the reason a
     cross-component test is a unit test here is written down once.

Not agent-plugins-ih18.19's to settle: it changes a cross-cutting standard that
governs every feature blueprint in the corpus, not this feature's own documents.
Adjacent, not blocking — the DoD records it as its one AC-coverage exception.

Done when: no blueprint's AC coverage table names a verification level that
specs/standards/testing-standards.md does not define.

title: bd refuses a blocks edge between beads already linked by discovered-from, silently leaving them unordered
description:
Measured on bd 1.2.2:

    bd dep add agent-plugins-ih18.24 agent-plugins-ih18.16
    -> exit 1
    Error: dependency agent-plugins-ih18.24 -> agent-plugins-ih18.16 already exists
    with type "discovered-from" (requested "blocks"); remove it first with
    'bd dep remove' then re-add

The pair is the common one, not an edge case. A dispatch agent that files work it discovers gets a 'discovered-from' edge to the bead it was working. Those are exactly the beads a coordinator then needs to ORDER — the discovered work usually must follow the bead that revealed it. The one relationship bd creates automatically is the one that blocks expressing the relationship that matters.

'discovered-from' does not gate readiness: agent-plugins-ih18.24 carried a discovered-from edge to ih18.16 and was in the ready front immediately, while ih18.16 was still open.

The failure is quiet in practice for two reasons. bd's message is good and its exit status is correct — but a coordinator scripting several 'bd dep add' calls in a row will typically redirect them, and one non-zero status in a batch of six is easy to lose. And nothing afterwards reports the absence: the run's own scope and lint checks do not audit that intended edges exist, so the graph silently differs from what the coordinator recorded in its amendments.

In run agent-plugins-bd97 this went unnoticed until a dispatch agent, blocking on the bead, reported 'No formal bd dep edge names this prerequisite' — the agent's audit of the graph was correct and the coordinator's account of it was wrong.

Candidate directions, not prescribed:
- Allow both edge types to coexist between a pair; they mean different things (provenance vs ordering) and neither implies the other.
- Or have bd upgrade in place when the requested type is strictly stronger, rather than refusing.
- Failing either, the ceremony that adds edges must read every status and re-audit the graph against what it intended, since a lost edge is invisible afterwards.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pair of beads can carry both a provenance edge (discovered-from) and an ordering edge (blocks), or bd's refusal is surfaced by whatever adds edges in a way that cannot be lost.
- Whatever wires edges in a run verifies afterwards that each intended edge exists with the intended type, and reports any that do not.
- Reproducing the run agent-plugins-bd97 case — a mid-run bead filed with discovered-from, then wired blocks by the coordinator — ends with the bead actually gated, or with a loud report that it is not.

title: Nothing provisions or version-checks the swarm binary the skills now require
description:
The bead-bonanza family now invokes `swarm manifest` (ADOPT-MAN) and `swarm status` (ADOPT-STAT) as required steps. Nothing installs, locates or version-checks that binary.

Measured in this run's dev worktree, 2026-08-29:

    $ grep -rn swarm .claude/hooks/session-start.sh
    (no output)
    $ grep -rn swarm plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh
    527:  # Monitor to tail, not a record. It is ephemeral by design - `swarm status`
    537:    say "\`swarm status --run $EPIC\` instead."
    $ ls -la /usr/local/bin/swarm
    -rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4859556 Aug 29 03:55 /usr/local/bin/swarm
    $ swarm status --help
    Error: unknown command "status" for "swarm"

So the binary on PATH is a hand-installed build that predates the status command, while the skills already tell an agent to run it. Two distinct failures:

1. **absent** - `swarm: command not found`, and the ceremony has no fallback.
2. **stale** - present but missing a subcommand, which is what the container shows right now.

`pre-flight-check.sh` is the component whose stated question is "can a run start in this environment at all?" (`specs/architecture/module-bead-bonanza.md`, Boundaries table) and it does not ask this one. A version or capability probe there - and a decision about who builds/installs the binary in a cloud session - is what closes it.

Anchors: `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh`; `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`; `specs/architecture/module-bead-bonanza.md`, the Environment Probe component.
acceptance_criteria:
- pre-flight-check.sh probes for the swarm binary and its required capability, not merely its presence, and reports a missing or too-old binary as a blocking condition with the remedy named.
- The capability probe is behavioural, not a version string: 'swarm status --help' exiting 3 with 'unknown command' is the measured failure to detect, and a version number would not have caught it.
- Who builds or installs the binary in a cloud session is decided and recorded — session-start hook, setup script, or an explicit precondition — and module-bead-bonanza's Environment Probe boundary says so.
- A session whose PATH carries a swarm predating the commands the skills invoke cannot start a run and is told why.

metadata.admitted_as: amendment — provisioning gap created by this run's own adoption deltas
metadata.tier_reason: A provisioning decision plus a capability probe; the measurement that proves it is already recorded on the bead.

comments.author: dev-bd97-5
comments.text: retro:decision Provisioning decided as: .claude/hooks/session-start.sh builds swarm from THIS repo's own cli/swarm on every cloud session (new step, section 4, before strata), mirroring how bd and strata are provisioned there. Unlike bd/strata this needs no clone and no network -- cli/swarm is already in the checkout -- so it is cheap and placed early rather than last. Idempotency uses the SAME behavioural probe as pre-flight-check.sh (swarm status --help) rather than a version string, since swarm carries none. Escape hatch SWARM_CLI_SKIP=1, matching STRATA_CLI_SKIP's naming.

comments.author: dev-bd97-5
comments.text: retro:proof Verified both directions live in this container. Before rebuilding: pre-flight-check.sh reported 'swarm: /usr/local/bin/swarm (STALE -- no status subcommand)' against the binary this run's own earlier bead had built before swarm status existed. Confirmed the exact measured failure mode the AC names: /tmp/.../scratchpad/swarm status --help (a preserved pre-status build) exits 3 with stderr 'Error: unknown command "status" for "swarm"'. After running (cd cli && go build -o /usr/local/bin/swarm ./swarm), the same probe reported plain 'swarm: /usr/local/bin/swarm' (ok). Also verified the session-start.sh addition's idempotency directly: with the now-capable binary in place it computed NEED_SWARM_BUILD=no and skipped the build; with a fake binary that exits 3 with 'unknown command' it computed NEED_SWARM_BUILD=yes and rebuilt successfully.

comments.author: dev-bd97-5
comments.text: retro:decision The swarm build in session-start.sh sits inside the hook's existing CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE-only gate (the same early-exit bd and strata already live behind), rather than running unconditionally. Rejected alternative: build swarm regardless of remote/local, since it is cheap and repo-local -- rejected because a local dev session may already have its own build in /usr/local/bin/swarm and silently overwriting it on every session start would be surprising, matching the hook's own stated reasoning for gating bd/strata the same way.

comments.author: dev-bd97-5
comments.text: retro:tooling Avoided AGENTS.md's documented pipe-hides-exit-status trap while writing the swarm capability classifier: the natural expression (printf '%s' "$err" | grep -qi 'unknown command') pipes a small writer into grep -q under set -o pipefail, which the ledger already measured as intermittent (2/30) for an identical shape in this same script's own orphan guard. Used a captured variable matched with case/glob instead (swarm_capability() in pre-flight-check.sh), with no pipe at all.

title: Re-home the readiness re-checks the retired bb-status.sh run mode carried
description:
`bb-status.sh run <epic>` was retired in favour of `swarm status --run <epic>` (ADOPT-STAT). `swarm status` measures worktrees, last commit, ready-front depth, per-dispatch drain, completion and scope — it does NOT carry three gates the retired mode also ran at every re-query:

1. `bd lint` findings intersected with THIS run's ready queue (`bd lint` exits 0 even when it warns, and has no scope flag, so the intersection was the whole point).
2. an open human-decision item — `bd list --label human --status open` (NOT `bd human list`, which keeps listing a bead after it closes).
3. every ready bead carries `metadata.tier` — without one, dispatch cannot resolve a model.

Each has an owner at PLAN time — `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md` requires `bd lint` clean per bead, grooming sets the tier, and `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md` documents the human-queue query. What is gone is the SUPERVISION-time re-check, which is where a bead added mid-run was caught.

Decide one of: (a) `swarm status` grows them, (b) the coordinator runs the three queries by hand at re-query and the ceremony says so, or (c) the plan-time gate is declared sufficient and that is stated where a reader looks for it.

Anchors: `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh` (the `run` case now exits 3 naming its replacement); `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md`, "Run checklist"; `specs/architecture/module-bead-bonanza.md`, the Swarm Status Probe component.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the three gates the retired run mode carried has a named owner and runs there: bd lint intersected with the run's own queue (bd lint exits 0 while warning and has no scope flag, so the intersection is the point); an open human-decision item via 'bd list --label human --status open' (NOT 'bd human list', which keeps listing a bead after it closes); and every ready bead carrying metadata.tier.
- The gates run at every re-query, not once at plan time — a bead admitted mid-run enters the dispatchable set after planning, which is when all three last failed in run agent-plugins-bd97.
- Retiring the old mode and landing the replacements happen together, so no window exists in which none of the three runs.
- Verified by reproducing run agent-plugins-bd97's own case: a mid-run bead with empty acceptance_criteria assigned to a dispatch is reported before it can be started.

title: A dispatch worktree's branch does not carry the bb/<dispatch-id> the collector matches on
description:
The Status Collector matches a standing worktree to the dispatch holding it through the tree's checked-out branch, `bb/<dispatch-id>`. That is the convention the module documents: `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md` creates each tree with `git worktree add -b "bb/<dispatch-id>" ...`, and `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh`'s `owner_for_branch` strips exactly that prefix.

The Agent tool's own worktree mechanism does not use it. Measured in this run's dev worktree:

    git worktree list --porcelain
    worktree /home/user/agent-plugins
    HEAD a47079aacc35e25d44683a4a67e209ff84b89a7c
    branch refs/heads/claude/bead-bonanza-agent-plugins-ih18-2yjc8j

    worktree /home/user/agent-plugins/.claude/worktrees/agent-add9532b34aa266aa
    HEAD ff34771ca17756ebf649dba6198587c0ea8bf45b
    branch refs/heads/worktree-agent-add9532b34aa266aa
    locked claude agent agent-add9532b34aa266aa (pid 520 start 897)

The dev worktree's branch is `worktree-agent-<hash>` — it carries neither the `bb/` prefix nor the dispatch id (`dev-bd97-4`), so nothing can match it to the agent holding it.

Consequences, both silent:

1. Every dispatch reports no standing worktree, so a report cannot distinguish "finished and cleaned up" from "the worker died" — the two rows of the module's own liveness table that differ only by a worktree's presence.
2. AC-SWARM-CORE-003.9 (a blocked bead whose dispatch's worktree still stands is an unresolved conflict) never fires, because no tree ever matches. The bead reads blocked and the partial work sitting on disk is reported by nothing.

`sprint-cleanup.sh` has the same exposure from the other side: a tree whose branch names no dispatch is reported LEFT rather than removed, which is the safe direction but leaves every harness-created worktree standing forever.

Not this bead's to close: the collector implements the documented convention, and choosing what the convention should be is the coordinator's. Adjacent, not blocking.

Done when: the coordinator and the collector agree on one rule for matching a worktree to its dispatch that holds for the worktrees a run actually creates in this harness — either the coordinator creates its own trees on `bb/<dispatch-id>` branches, or the matching rule is widened to a stated form the harness's names satisfy. `cli/swarm/status`'s `DispatchBranchPrefix` and its worktree tests, `worktree-mechanics.md` and `sprint-cleanup.sh`'s `owner_for_branch` all move together, and a test asserts the rule against a real `git worktree list --porcelain` capture rather than a hand-written one.


## Steps to Reproduce

Run any bead-bonanza dispatch in this harness (Agent tool, isolation:"worktree"),
then from the repository root:

    git worktree list --porcelain | grep '^branch'

Observed, across all four dispatches of run agent-plugins-bd97:

    refs/heads/worktree-agent-ae2cae840953892b6
    refs/heads/worktree-agent-ae92a1fe13db80510
    refs/heads/worktree-agent-add9532b34aa266aa
    refs/heads/worktree-agent-af74def6f06598357

Expected by the collector and by sprint-cleanup.sh's `owner_for_branch`:
`bb/<dispatch-id>`, e.g. `bb/dev-bd97-4`. No tree has ever carried one.

Then, with a worktree standing:

    swarm status ...        # the worktree is attributed to no dispatch
    scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh <epic>   # reports the tree LEFT, never removed

The coordinator's decision on which rule replaces the branch-name match is
recorded as a comment on this bead; read it before starting.
acceptance_criteria:
- The collector attributes a standing worktree to its dispatch for the worktrees this harness actually creates, without relying on the branch NAME, and without hard-coding the harness's current `worktree-agent-<agentId>` spelling.
- AC-SWARM-CORE-003.9 fires: a blocked bead whose dispatch's worktree still stands is reported as an unresolved conflict, proven against a real `git worktree list --porcelain` capture rather than a hand-written one.
- A worktree that cannot be attributed is still reported LEFT rather than removed — the safe direction sprint-cleanup.sh already takes.
- `cli/swarm/status`'s DispatchBranchPrefix and its worktree tests, `worktree-mechanics.md` and `sprint-cleanup.sh`'s owner_for_branch all move together and state one rule.
- worktree-mechanics.md no longer documents `git worktree add -b bb/<dispatch-id>` as the creation step, since the harness creates and names the tree and may place it inside the repository.
