title: Reconcile ADR-025's Windows .cmd-shim open question with container-swarm-cli
description:
ADR-025 asserts that the container blueprint carries the Windows executable-resolution hazard as an open question. It does not.

Measured on this tree:
- specs/adrs/ADR-025-argv-not-shell.md:101 — 'will land. `container-swarm-cli` carries it as an open question.' (the preceding sentence, line 98, names the case: 'On Windows a tool installed through npm is a `.cmd` shim rather than an executable, and Go applies its own rules to running one; the gateway is where that has to be handled')
- specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md, section '## Open Questions' — the entire body is 'None.'
- grep -rn '\\.cmd\\b|shim' specs/ returns exactly one hit, ADR-025:98. Nothing else in the corpus records the hazard.

Either the open question is added to specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md (naming what has to be decided: how the Process Runner resolves an executable on Windows when it is a .cmd shim, and what the fallback is), or ADR-025's sentence is corrected to say where it is actually carried. Adding it to the blueprint is the likelier resolution, since the ADR treats it as a live consequence rather than a settled one.

Not the Process Runner delta's to close: the runner as built resolves executables through os/exec's own rules and its callers are `bd` and `git`, neither of which is an npm shim, so nothing in that delta forces the decision. Adjacent, not blocking.

Done when: the two documents agree, and the hazard is recorded in exactly one place a reader of the container blueprint will find.
acceptance_criteria:
- specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md and specs/adrs/ADR-025-argv-not-shell.md agree: the Windows .cmd-shim executable-resolution hazard is recorded in exactly one place, and whichever document does not carry it does not claim the other does.
- Where the blueprint carries it, the open question names what must be decided — how the Process Runner resolves an executable on Windows when it is a .cmd shim, and what the fallback is — rather than merely noting that a hazard exists.
- ADR-025:101's sentence is true after the change, whichever way it is resolved.
- grep -rnE '\.cmd\b|shim' specs/ returns hits only in the document that now owns the hazard, plus any deliberate cross-reference to it.

title: groom-beads tells a retro to use bd remember, but memories are excluded from bd export
description:
plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md, in the retro-feedback section, says of a grooming miss:

  'Capture the PATTERN as bd remember "<insight>" so future grooming inherits it through bd prime, and propose it against the Definition of Ready, which the spec skill owns.'

MEASURED (bd 1.2.2, throwaway memory, since removed with bd forget):

  $ bd remember "PROBE-memtest: transient probe" --key probe-memtest
  $ bd memories                        -> lists it
  $ bd export | grep -c PROBE-memtest  -> 0     EXCLUDED FROM EXPORT
  $ bd prime  | grep -c PROBE-memtest  -> 1     injected at prime

So the mechanism works as described WITHIN a database: remember stores, prime injects. But memories do not appear in bd export.

This repository's own AGENTS.md already rules on it: 'bd remember memories are excluded from bd export and are not synced. Durable context belongs in an issue description, not a memory.' The skill contradicts that ruling.

UNVERIFIED: the 'not synced' half. Memories live in the Dolt database, so bd dolt push may carry them where the JSONL export does not. Cross-machine sync could not be tested from a single container. Settle by storing a memory, running bd dolt push, and checking whether it appears in a fresh clone bootstrapped from the remote. The EXPORT claim is measured and stands either way.
design:
Two options, owner's call:

(a) Drop the bd remember half; keep the Definition of Ready proposal. Consistent with AGENTS.md, loses a low-friction path.
(b) Keep it, explicitly scoped as a local convenience with the DoR proposal as the durable backing. Honest, but instructs an agent to do something that may not travel.

Leaning (a). Note groom-beads is a VENDED skill: it is exported to other projects, where a bd remember that does not sync fails silently and invisibly. That asymmetry argues against (b) more strongly than it would for a repo-local document.

Settle the sync question first — it changes which option is right.
acceptance_criteria: groom-beads' retro-feedback section is consistent with AGENTS.md's ruling on memories. If bd remember is retained, the skill states the export/sync limitation at the point of use. The sync question is either measured and recorded, or explicitly marked unverified with the command that would settle it.
notes: Raised by the owner in review: 'Could you describe how bd remember and bd prime work together on this -- this is the first time I am seeing adoption of these features in these specs. I am not saying do not use them but please tell me how they work and why we have chosen them.'

title: 5. run-bead carries the nine kinds inline AND vendors the protocol that defines them
description:
MEASURED: findings-capture-protocol.md is vendored into six skills, 56,736 bytes total. Five of the six only cite it. run-bead ALSO restates the nine kinds as a 9-row table in its own body (~900 bytes), which is the section 'The kinds' of the vendored file.

The inline table is deliberate — it costs a word at the moment the agent already knows the answer, with no hop. But run-bead is 258 bytes from the body cap, and the same nine rows exist one hop away in a file it already ships.

DECIDE, do not guess: either the inline table is the load-bearing copy and the vendored file is the reference (then keep both and say so), or the hop is acceptable (then cut the table and reclaim ~900 bytes). Measure it — dispatch a bead with the table removed and see whether the agent's findings still carry a valid kind.

NOT A CANDIDATE FOR 'one copy passed by path': four of the six consumers (retro-skill, retro-spec, groom-feature-blueprint, sprint-retro) are invoked without a coordinator, and a skill exported on its own must be self-contained. That is what the vendoring is for.
close_reason:
DECIDED: keep both copies. The inline nine-kinds table in run-batch is the load-bearing copy; the vendored findings-capture-protocol.md is the reference.

Rationale: the failure the table prevents is silent. A kind outside the nine routes nowhere and nothing errors, so an agent forced to hop to a reference file to learn the vocabulary guesses instead, and the guess reads as valid in every listing. 736 bytes of headroom does not buy that back.

The duplication retires on a condition rather than a measurement: FEAT-SWARM-011 (frd-swarm-cli) validates a finding's kind at write time, at which point the CLI's rejection message is the table, delivered at the point of need. Filed as agent-plugins-93yx, which carries the do-not-delete-early warning so a future duplication sweep does not cut it first.

Not measured by dispatch as the bead instructed: that measurement costs a run and answers a question the CLI work removes.

title: shellcheck is named in acceptance criteria, is not installed, and is in no declared check: every shell change ships unlinted
description:
audience: project · target: `sf.toml` and `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` · recurrence: 0

## What is wrong, and what it costs

Beads in this repository are groomed with acceptance criteria naming
`shellcheck`, and this repository has no `shellcheck`. Measured at `5cc2a58`:

    $ command -v shellcheck                                        -> not found
    $ grep -n 'shellcheck' scripts/ci.sh sf.toml                   -> no output
    $ grep -n 'sh -n\|bash -n' scripts/ci.sh sf.toml bb-checks.py  -> no output

The 13 declared check ids are `format vet build test-go skills shared-refs
strata-docs schemas corpus ref-links template-drift script-self-tests
skills-strict` — none is shellcheck.

Four of this run's beads touched shell scripts. Two carried a `shellcheck` AC and
recorded it UNVERIFIED; two more recorded the tool's absence as an environment
fact. **Every shell change this run shipped carries no lint verdict at all** —
including changes to `sprint-cleanup.sh`, `bb-status.sh` and both hooks, which
are the files whose defects this run existed to fix.

The repository is substantially shell. `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/` and
`plugin/hooks/` are its most-executed code and its least-checked.

## Evidence

- `agent-plugins-mpnf.16#4` — "the acceptance criterion '`sh -n` and shellcheck
  (as `scripts/ci.sh` runs them) report nothing new' cannot be satisfied as
  written: ci.sh runs NEITHER, and shellcheck is not installed in this
  container."
- `agent-plugins-mpnf.20#5` — the identical criterion, on a second bead, with the
  identical measurement.
- `agent-plugins-mpnf.17#3` — "No shellcheck binary, and no declared check

- `agent-plugins-mpnf.24#6` — "shellcheck is not part of sf.toml's declared

- `agent-plugins-mpnf.18#6` — "NOT VERIFIED: shellcheck. It is not installed in

id over `plugin/**/*.sh`, `scripts/*.sh` and `.claude/hooks/*.sh`, with a
severity level the current tree already passes — establish the baseline first and
fence to it, rather than blocking on a clean sweep.

If that is declined, the alternative is not to leave it: the AC text must stop
naming a tool this project does not run, which makes
`agent-plugins-y63n.25` (grooming checks the tools an AC names) the mechanism

title: findings-capture-protocol shows the right incident form but never states the wrong one; retro:incident: routes nowhere

    retro:incident:coordinator-removed-worktree-before-the-merge-succeeded

candidate. The cost was concrete and large: that finding is the run's ONLY record
of a state the corpus asserts cannot occur (a removed worktree coexisting with an
unmerged branch), and it names two remedies against `bead-bonanza`. It reached

Unrouted per run, from `rfcs/retro-log.md`:

| run | unrouted | invented kinds |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-plugins-qozp` | 2 | `retro:process:` |
| `agent-plugins-so39` | 2 | `retro:process:` (both the coordinator's) |
| `agent-plugins-mpnf` | 2 | `retro:process:` and `retro:incident:` |

Three consecutive runs at 2. `agent-plugins-y63n.17` records the first two and
proposes validating the kind; this issue is the cheaper half — one sentence, in
the document that causes the mistake.

## Evidence

- `agent-plugins-mpnf#11` — "`retro:incident:` was written as a KIND, so the
  run's most consequential finding routes nowhere — and the unrouted count has
  now been 2 for three consecutive runs."
- `agent-plugins-mpnf#6` — the finding itself, headed

- `agent-plugins-mpnf#5` — `retro:process:coordinator incident`, the other

In `specs/standards/findings-capture-protocol.md`, section "Incidents are a
severity, not a kind", after the example, add:

> whose kind slot holds `incident` routes to UNROUTED and reaches no audience,
> which is the opposite of what marking it as an incident is for.

Does NOT resolve `agent-plugins-y63n.17` (validating the kind mechanically);

title: Acceptance criteria that contradict the bead's own Design scope pass the readiness gate; two beads this run
description:
audience: skill · target: `groom-beads` (Definition of Ready) · recurrence: 0

## What is wrong, and what it costs

Two beads in this run carried an acceptance criterion that contradicted another
part of the same bead, and in both cases the implementing agent had to decide
which half to honour — alone, mid-work, with no way to ask.

`agent-plugins-mpnf.17`: AC 3 said a FLAT epic must report "exactly what it
reported before this change". It could not: the third column of the two rewired
lines is the COMMAND that established the reading, and the old text named a query
that returns the wrong answer on a nested epic. Honouring AC 3 literally would
have left a documented lie in the output that the next reader re-runs and is
misled by — the same class of failure the bead existed to remove. The agent
satisfied it in substance (state, verdict and exit code byte-identical on a flat
epic; one column of citation text differs) and recorded the divergence.

`agent-plugins-mpnf.4`: AC 7 ("no remaining instruction anywhere in
`sprint-plan/` tells a planner to put a pre-existing bead id in a graph-plan
edge") was in tension with the bead's own Design SCOPE, which explicitly said the
merge bead's fan-in "belongs to the sibling bead that waits on this one; do not
fix it here". The agent honoured the Design, and AC 7 held at batch end rather
than at that commit.

Both agents chose correctly and recorded an incident. The cost is that the
decision was made by whoever happened to be dispatched, silently, and a different
agent could reasonably have chosen the other way — satisfying the letter and
shipping the defect, or widening scope into a sibling's files and colliding.

## Evidence

- `agent-plugins-mpnf.17#2` — "acceptance criterion 3 says a FLAT epic must
  report 'exactly what it reported before this change'. It cannot, literally
  ... AC 3 is therefore satisfied in substance and not in letter."
- `agent-plugins-mpnf.4#7` — "AC7 ... is in tension with this bead's own Design
  SCOPE ... Decided: honour the Design."

## Proposed change

Add one check to the Definition of Ready, run at grooming rather than at
dispatch: **an acceptance criterion SHALL NOT contradict the bead's own Design
scope, and SHALL NOT pin verbatim output text where the file under change
declares a contract that output must satisfy.**

Two mechanical tests that catch both instances:

1. Every path or artifact an AC constrains appears in the Design's scope. AC 7
   constrained all of `sprint-plan/`; the Design scoped the bead out of one file
   inside it. That is visible without reading either for meaning.
2. An AC asserting byte-identical or verbatim output names WHICH properties must
   hold — state, verdict, exit code — rather than "exactly what it reported
   before". `mpnf.17`'s AC would have been satisfiable as written had it said so.

title: sprint-review files beads with file:line anchors that rot before dispatch; the durable-anchor rule is groom-beads-only
description:
audience: skill · target: `sprint-review` · recurrence: 1

## What is wrong, and what it costs

The durable-anchor rule already exists. `groom-beads` names unquoted `file:line`
citations as an anti-pattern, and `agent-plugins-61f.4` (closed 2026-08-13) put
it into the Definition of Ready and the work-order template — filed because in a
prior run fourteen of seventeen beads cited `file:line` positions and EVERY cited
position had moved by dispatch.

`sprint-review` files its findings as beads and does not apply that rule.
`agent-plugins-mpnf.18` was filed in review pass 2 with six line numbers. By the
time it was dispatched, two had moved:

    bb-status.sh:459          -> :560   (moved by sibling mpnf.17, in the same batch)
    bb-stop-ready-loop.sh:213 -> :228

The description's count was also wrong: it said "five NEW copies plus a sixth";
the measured set was **seven sites in five files**.

Cost: the bead survived only because its agent matched by STRING rather than by
line, and because a SIBLING agent volunteered that its own edit had moved one of
the cited lines. Neither is a mechanism. A review finding whose anchor rots
between filing and dispatch sends the implementing agent to the wrong place in
the file, or to a line that no longer exists — and review findings are dispatched
LAST, after the whole run's diff has moved every file they cite.

## Evidence

- `agent-plugins-mpnf.18#4` — "the bead's site inventory was stale on both count
  and position by the time it was dispatched, exactly as groom-beads'
  unquoted-file:line anti-pattern predicts. Matching by string rather than by
  line number was what made it survivable."
- `agent-plugins-mpnf.17#4` — "my change shifted the line number that
  agent-plugins-mpnf.18's finding cites, and I did NOT touch the claim itself.
  ... A bead dispatched with a line number rather than the string will miss it
  after any edit to the same file; the string is the durable handle."

Prior run in the recurrence window: `agent-plugins-61f.4`, which adopted the rule
for `groom-beads`' Definition of Ready and the work-order template.

## Proposed change

`sprint-review`'s finding→bead step applies the same anchor rule the Definition
of Ready applies: a bead it files SHALL cite each site by **path plus a quoted
distinctive string**, and MAY carry a line number only as a parenthetical hint
marked as such.

    yes:  plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh — `returns null (not` (≈:459)
    no:   plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh:459

Where the finding asserts a COUNT of sites, the bead carries the grep that
produces the count, not the number alone — `mpnf.18`'s "five NEW copies" was
wrong by two, and only the grep found that.

---

title: A --ff-only refusal reads as the serialized STOP case even when it is the benign concurrent one
description:
audience: skill · target: `bead-bonanza` (the coordinator merge step) · recurrence: 0

## What is wrong, and what it costs

`worktree-mechanics.md` already says that a `--ff-only` refusal in a CONCURRENT
wave "is not a fault" and gives the rebase remedy. It also says that in the
SERIALIZED case the coordinator must STOP AND REPORT and not resolve inline.
Those are opposite instructions for identical output — `git merge --ff-only`
prints "Not possible to fast-forward" either way.

The coordinator checklist has no step that anticipates the refusal, so it
arrives cold, and the first reading available is the serialized one. Reading it
wrong stops a healthy run: the coordinator reports a blocker to a human and
waits, when the correct action was a rebase it is authorised to perform.

This run hit it (batch 10, loop 2) and read it correctly, but only after the
worktree had already been torn down by the chained command — so the diagnosis
happened in the worst possible state rather than at the merge itself.

## Evidence

- `agent-plugins-mpnf#6` — "`worktree-mechanics.md` says a `--ff-only` refusal in
  a concurrent wave 'is not a fault' and gives the rebase remedy — and that is
  exactly what happened and what fixed it. But the coordinator checklist has no
  step that anticipates it, so the refusal arrives looking like the serialized
  case (which says STOP AND REPORT, do not resolve inline). Reading it wrong
  stops a healthy run."

## Proposed change

Add one line to the merge step, before the merge is read: **name which case you
are in.** The two are distinguishable mechanically, not by judgement —

    # concurrent: another batch moved HEAD since this branch forked
    git merge-base --is-ancestor "$base_sha" HEAD && [ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" != "$base_sha" ]

If HEAD has moved past the branch's recorded `base_sha`, a `--ff-only` refusal is
the concurrent case and the remedy is `git rebase` onto current HEAD, in-run, no
escalation. If HEAD is still at `base_sha`, the refusal is the serialized case
and the rule stands: STOP AND REPORT.

---

notes: Done: worktree-mechanics.md now names which --ff-only case you are in mechanically, before reading the refusal, and states both readings side by side. Commit 76d61c4.

title: sprint-retro hard-codes rfcs/sprints/ and .sf/outbox/; a project that retires either must override the skill in prose
description:
audience: skill · target: `sprint-retro` · recurrence: 0

## What is wrong, and what it costs

`sprint-retro` hard-codes two destinations as literal strings and offers no way
to say where a project keeps them instead.

Step 4(a):

    path="rfcs/sprints/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<epic-slug>-findings.md"

Step 6's table: `.sf/outbox/<skill>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`

Commit `9cc8844` ("Drain the outbox and the run-3 sprint docs into the tracker")
removed 15 `.sf/outbox` issue documents and the four 2026-08-24 sprint documents
at the owner's instruction. Measured at `5cc2a58`: `find .sf -type f` returns
only `.sf/outbox/README.md`, and `ls rfcs/sprints/ | grep 2026-08-24` returns
nothing.

Nothing can redirect either one. `sf.toml` has no key for it, and the run
manifest has none either — `jq -r 'select(.id=="agent-plugins-mpnf") | .metadata
| keys'` lists `moved branch ledger admitted base_sha excluded checks_ids
moved_note scope_notes excluded_note review_passes standing_auth checks_baseline
concurrency_cap checks_baseline_status`.

The cost: this run's retro had to be told in its dispatch prompt, in prose,
twice, to override its own skill. An agent running `sprint-retro` here without
that override writes into a channel the owner closed, and files a findings
document into a directory the project has stopped using — both silently, both
"successfully".

## Evidence

- `agent-plugins-mpnf#10` — "the skill hard-codes two destinations this project
  has retired, and offers no way to say where they went."
- `agent-plugins-mpnf#9` — "25 beads now cite a findings document that no longer
  exists." (the consequence of the same coupling, one step downstream)

## Proposed change

Both destinations become project configuration with the current values as
defaults. Add to the project's declaration (`sf.toml`, alongside `[run]`):

    [retro]
    findings_dir = "rfcs/sprints"     # default; this project sets "docs/research/sprint-findings"
    skill_issues = "outbox"           # "outbox" | "tracker"
    skill_issues_parent = ""          # when "tracker": the epic new skill issues are filed under

Step 4(a) reads `findings_dir`; step 6's table branches on `skill_issues`, filing
a bead under `skill_issues_parent` where the project vends its own skills — which
this repository does, so its skill issues and its project issues live in one
tracker rather than in a directory plus a tracker.

title: sprint-cleanup run from inside a run worktree treats THAT worktree as main and never tears it down
description:
Adjacent to agent-plugins-mpnf.20, not blocking it — found while measuring the scoped teardown with a live dry run.

## What

plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh, prune_worktrees:

    main="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"
    ...
    [ "$wt" = "$main" ] && continue

In a WORKTREE, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` returns that worktree's own
path, not the main checkout's. So a cleanup run from inside a run worktree
skips exactly the tree it is standing in, and reports the REAL main checkout
as 'LEFT — no bead owns its branch' because the sprint branch is not a bead
suffix.

## Measured

Run from /home/user/agent-plugins/.claude/worktrees/dev-mpnf-11 during the
sprint, against the live run epic:

    $ plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh agent-plugins-mpnf --dry-run
    sprint-cleanup: agent-plugins-mpnf (dry run)
      WOULD    prune stale registrations                git worktree prune
      LEFT     worktree, no bead owns its branch        /home/user/agent-plugins
      LEFT     worktree, no bead owns its branch        /home/user/agent-plugins/.claude/worktrees/dev-mpnf-14
      ...

/home/user/agent-plugins is the main checkout and is reported LEFT; the
worktree the command ran from (dev-mpnf-11) does not appear at all.

## Direction, not a decision

Two candidates, neither chosen here: derive the main checkout from
`git worktree list --porcelain` (its FIRST entry is the main working tree)
rather than from --show-toplevel, or refuse to run from inside a registered
worktree with a usage error. The first keeps the script runnable from
anywhere; the second matches the header's 'WHO RUNS IT — the ORCHESTRATOR'.

Non-destructive in both directions — the failure is a tree left standing and
a misleading LEFT line, never a removal.
notes: Done: sprint-cleanup finds the main checkout from git worktree list --porcelain's first entry rather than git rev-parse --show-toplevel, which returns the WORKTREE when run inside one. Measured in this session. Self-test asserts it; the worktree the cleanup stands in is reported LEFT. Commit 8afa18b.

title: Park the deferred human channel until the core works; it costs a footgun for a queue bd already answers
description:
Owner's read, 2026-08-25: the deferred human channel is 'my attempt at producing a clean queue of things that I should look at (maybe complexity we can drop until the core is working well)'. Agreed — park it.

## What it costs today

MEASURED (bd 1.2.2): **the `human` label does NOT hold a bead out of `bd ready`.** Only the parent phase epic does. So the whole mechanism rests on one rule — `--exclude-label human` must appear on the DISPATCH query and on no other query — and the consequences of getting it wrong point in opposite directions:

- Omit it on the dispatch query: an agent is handed a question meant for a person.
- Add it to a completion count: the run reports itself drained while a human still owes it an answer.

That is a footgun requiring two paragraphs in `run-record.md` and a cross-reference in `dispatching.md`, in service of a queue that `bd list --label human --status open` answers directly, on demand, with no run-time machinery at all.

## What to keep

The GOAL is good: a clean queue of things the owner should look at. Keep the label — it is free. Drop the phase-parenting, the dispatch-query exclusion rule, and the 'cannot close while it is open' gate, until the core is working well.

## Acceptance
- [ ] The channel's machinery is removed; the label survives.
- [ ] The owner's queue is a documented one-line query.
- [ ] The two paragraphs and the cross-reference come out with it.
notes: Done: the deferred human channel is deleted from run-bead and from the run-record's channel table, which is now two channels (authorization at the start, findings at the end). A bead that needs a human is BOUNCED at grooming with --add-label human, and the run goes narrower. Commit 76d61c4.

title: Remove the merge slot: it is not a lock and the property it protects holds by construction
description:
Owner's read, 2026-08-25: 'Maybe merge slots are overkill.' Agreed, on the skill's own evidence.

## The document argues its own case away

`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md` says: 'Only the merge agent merges, so within one run the serialization already holds by construction — the slot is not what makes merges one-at-a-time. It earns its place by making that state visible.'

Visibility is a weak justification for a mechanism with a lifecycle.

## Measured

- `bd merge-slot release` does NOT promote a waiter, and is not owner-protected — so it is not a lock.
- Run agent-plugins-mpnf, 2026-08-25: the coordinator acquired and released it four times across three merges. It never blocked anything. Cost: eight extra tool calls and two more failure modes (a slot held by a crashed session; a slot acquired under the wrong `BEADS_ACTOR`, which `worktree-mechanics.md` documents as a real hazard requiring its own paragraph).

## The case for keeping it, stated fairly

A second session resuming the same run finds the slot held rather than merging concurrently with the first. That is real but narrow, and it is better served by the derived liveness verdict (sibling bead) than by a lock that does not lock.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `bd merge-slot` calls removed from the skill family and its scripts.
- [ ] `sprint-cleanup.sh`'s slot-release step removed along with them.
- [ ] The concurrent-resume case it covered is either handled by the liveness verdict or explicitly accepted as a risk, in writing.
notes: Done, and wider: the merge BEAD went with the slot. The coordinator merges each dispatch's branch as that dispatch returns; one-merge-at-a-time already held by construction. Commit 76d61c4.

## What is wrong, and what it costs

`references/worktree-mechanics.md` mandates raw `git worktree remove` over
`bd worktree remove` specifically to preserve the dirty-tree check, arguing
that `bd`'s version can only proceed via `--force`, which skips every check.
But a harness-created worktree is **locked** — `git worktree list` showed
`locked` on all four of wave 1's — and plain `git worktree remove` refuses a
locked worktree. The orchestrator is forced to `--force` anyway, losing exactly
the guard the rule was written to keep. The rule silently converts into its own
opposite. A clean counter-case is on the record: wave 2's
`sprint-wave`-created worktree `/home/user/.bb-worktrees/dev-qozp-5` removed
**without** `--force`, so the lock comes from the harness, not from the skill's
mechanics.

## Evidence

- `qozp#2` — "retro:tooling:bead-bonanza — the worktree-removal rule collides with harness-created worktrees, and the collision silently drops the guard the rule exists to keep. references/worktree-mechanics.md says to use raw 'git worktree remove', NOT 'bd worktree remove', specifically so the dirty-tree check is preserved."

## Proposed change

In the removal step, state that a locked worktree is unlocked first —
`git worktree unlock <path> && git worktree remove <path>` — and that `--force`
is not the escape hatch for a lock, because it discards the dirty-tree check
the step exists to run. Done: `worktree-mechanics.md` carries the
unlock-then-remove form and names `--force` as the wrong reach.
notes:
SUPERSEDED BY agent-plugins-o63s.13 (RM) — a locked worktree defeating the removal guard is answered by the behavior line naming the unlock invocation as the resolution and refusing the forcing form. Close or re-scope when agent-plugins-o63s.13 lands. Backstop: agent-plugins-o63s.19.
CLOSED by agent-plugins-o63s.19 (DOD), superseded by agent-plugins-o63s.13 (RM). The removal guard is no longer prose an agent may drop: 'swarm dispatch accept' owns it. Measured in the landed source — cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go:366 sets the resolution to 'unlock it and accept the dispatch again: git worktree unlock <path>', and its header comment at :351 states 'Never --force: forcing discards' the check. Proved by cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle_test.go:290, which asserts the reported text contains 'worktree unlock <path>'. The issue's own proposed change (name unlock-then-remove, and name --force as the wrong reach) is therefore satisfied in a stronger form than proposed: the command states the unlock invocation and never offers the forcing form, rather than a document asking an agent to remember it.

# Evidence — what this issue rests on
findings: ["qozp#5"]
recurrence: 0
report: rfcs/sprints/2026-08-24-beads-coordination-rollout-findings.md

# Provenance — who and what produced this
run: agent-plugins-qozp
branch: claude/bead-bonanza-design-review-ne1plu
skill_version: "2.0"
model: <fill in — the model that ran this run> (coordinator)
---

## What is wrong, and what it costs

The check runs bare `bd human list` and failed the run's health with "human
queue: 1 item(s) awaiting a decision" for `agent-plugins-qozp.12`, a bead that
is **deferred and explicitly excluded at admission**. Every other check in the
same report scopes correctly — "bd lint: nothing flagged in this run's queue",
"every ready bead carries a tier". The cost is that a run can never read clean
while any deferred decision exists anywhere in the tracker, which trains the
operator to ignore the signal.

## Evidence

- `qozp#5` — "retro:tooling:bead-bonanza — bb-status.sh's human-queue check is not scoped to the run's admitted set. It reported 'FAIL human queue: 1 item(s) awaiting a decision' for agent-plugins-qozp.12 (DECISION D1), which is DEFERRED and explicitly excluded at admission."

## Status — DEFERRED pending a design

The owner deferred this on 2026-08-24: the mechanical fix below is correct
but too small a lens. `bd human` is the whole human-decision lifecycle —
flagging a decision, listing what is outstanding, answering it, withdrawing
it — and this run hit defects in three of those four steps, which suggests
the shape of the wrapper matters more than this one check. Reopen it behind
a design that settles how a run assigns a decision to a human and manages
its lifecycle; the fix below is then a consequence of that design rather
than a patch to a check.

What the design has to account for, all measured on bd 1.2.2:

- `bd human list` has no scope flag. It is repo-wide, and the intersection
  has to be computed by the caller.
- It counts CLOSED beads. `--status=open` fixes that half and already
  exists; a scratch database with one open and one closed human-labelled
  bead showed both under the bare call and only the open one under
  `--status=open`.
- `bd human list --json` returns `null`, not `[]`, when the queue is empty.
  A consumer that assumes a list breaks on the empty case.
- `bd human dismiss` fails with `storage is nil` while every other
  subcommand resolves the same id in the same shell. The working path is
  `bd update <id> --remove-label human`.
- There is no `bd human create`. A decision reaches the queue only by
  labelling: `bd update <id> --add-label human`.

## Proposed change

**Two defects, and only one needs code.**

`bd human list` counts CLOSED beads. Measured on bd 1.2.2 in a throwaway
database: a bead closed with `bd close` still appears in the listing, and in
this run `bd human list` printed `agent-plugins-qozp.12` with `Status: closed`
after it had been answered and closed. A flag already fixes this —
`bd human list --status=open` — and it is documented in the command's own
`--help`.

Scope needs an intersection, because there is no scope flag. Take the shape
from the `bd lint` check ten lines above, which solves the identical problem by
parsing ids and intersecting with the run's queue:

```python
run_ids  = manifest["admitted"] | descendants(epic)
queue    = {i["id"] for i in bd_json("human list --status=open") or []}
blocking = queue & run_ids
```

`or []` is load-bearing: `bd human list --json` returns **`null`**, not `[]`,
when the queue is empty (measured). Iterating that is the same class of trap
that produced the character-by-character `admitted` bug.

Report both halves, so the fix does not create a false signal in the other
direction:

```
FAIL  human queue: 1 item(s) awaiting a decision in this run: agent-plugins-qozp.12
OK    human queue: clear for this run (2 open elsewhere in the tracker)
```

Done: an open human-needed item outside `manifest.admitted` does not fail the
run's health, a closed one is never counted at all, and the OK line still says
how many exist elsewhere.
notes:
SUPERSEDED BY agent-plugins-o63s.6 (QF) — a repo-wide human-queue check is run-scoped by construction once the ready set refuses an absent scope and derives its set from the run's own descendants. Close or re-scope when agent-plugins-o63s.6 lands. Backstop: agent-plugins-o63s.19.
CLOSED by agent-plugins-o63s.19 (DOD), superseded by agent-plugins-o63s.6 (QF). The repo-wide check no longer exists and its replacement is run-scoped by construction. Measured: grep -n 'human' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh returns nothing, so bb-status.sh carries no human-queue check at all; the exclusion now lives in 'swarm ready', cli/swarm/cli/ready.go:142 -> 'bd ready --parent ' + req.Run + ' --exclude-type epic --exclude-label human --limit 0 --json  (the dispatch set)'. The --parent scope is the run epic and is required by the command, so the check cannot read outside the run's own descendants.

title: Drop the graph_plan manifest copy: the bead DAG is the source of truth after the plan loads
description:
Owner decision on PR #27 (plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md:149): 'My hope was the DAG for the run would be the source of truth after the plan skill was executed. What does storing a copy of the graph buy us?'

It buys nothing, and there is a contradiction proving it. run-record.md:149 justifies recording `graph_plan` so 'a recovering session can diff what the run was supposed to be against what the graph now holds'. On 2026-08-25 the coordinator gitignored `.beads/plans/` (commit 22c86ab) because the untracked artifacts blocked pre-flight and a stale plan outlives the graph it describes. Both cannot be true: if the file is not in the repo, a recovering session in a fresh container holds a manifest key pointing at nothing.

Resolution: the plan file is a LOADER INPUT — reviewable before it loads, inert after. The DAG is the record.

Interacts with the deferred agent-plugins-p567, agent-plugins-mpnf.15 and agent-plugins-mpnf.23, all of which correct text about the plan artifacts. Re-evaluate all three against this decision rather than implementing them as filed.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `graph_plan` and `edges_sidecar` are gone from the manifest, or their purpose is restated as something the gitignore does not contradict.
- [ ] The three deferred beads above are resolved against this decision — implemented, rewritten, or closed as moot, each with a reason.

title: Turn prose invariants into guards that exit non-zero
description:
Every ordering invariant in the skill family is enforced by an agent reading a paragraph and choosing to comply. Three measured failures of that model, all from 2026-08-24/25:

1. `worktree-mechanics.md` says remove the worktree AFTER the merge. The coordinator chained merge and removal in one shell without `&&`; the merge exited 128 and the removal ran anyway, producing a removed worktree beside an unmerged branch — the state the document says cannot happen. `bb-status.sh` reported it faithfully (STOP 3 NOT merged beside OK 4 worktree: gone) and exited 2.
2. `dispatching.md:44` warns that `bd epic close-eligible` takes no positional epic and will close every eligible epic in the database — then hands you the command. A warning is not a guard.
3. The coordinator ended a turn twice with a non-empty queue and nothing dispatched, which `operating-principles.md` names a defect.

## Acceptance
- [ ] accept-dispatch refuses to remove a worktree whose branch is not an ancestor of HEAD.
- [ ] close-eligible is wrapped so it cannot act outside the run epic.
- [ ] Each guard has a test that reproduces the original failure against pre-guard behaviour.
- [ ] The prose each guard replaces is deleted, not left as a duplicate.
notes:

comments.text:
retro-mpnf — run 3 evidence for this bead: a prose invariant was broken by its own author within hours of shipping it, and survived four independent chances to die. Deduped against this bead rather than re-filed.

The claim: "`bd ready --json` returns `null` when empty, but `[]` for an `--assignee`-filtered empty query." False on bd 1.2.2.

  1. A loop-2 GROOMING agent recorded it as a ledger entry, citing "the run's existing ledger records `null`". The coordinator's later sweep of the epic ledgers on mpnf, qozp and so39 found NO SUCH ENTRY — the citation named a surface that does not carry the claim, and nothing checked the citation. This is the only fabrication among the four; the rest are relays.
  2. The COORDINATOR relayed the whole entry into three dispatch prompts unmeasured — hours after the same coordinator shipped agent-plugins-x5tk, the AGENTS.md section forbidding exactly this.
  3. TWO of the three receiving agents (batches 9 and 10) did not challenge it. Nothing in either bead depended on it, so silence cost nothing — but silence is what it was.
  4. dev-mpnf-8 (batch 8) caught it: four configurations, `[]` in all four, flagged the contradiction rather than working around it (finding agent-plugins-mpnf.3#2). mpnf.18's agent then re-measured the REPLACEMENT across eleven configurations with a positive control (mpnf.18#1).

AGENTS.md predicts this about itself: "the rule has no automated check; it is enforced by authorial memory, which is the condition it exists to correct." Run 3 is the measurement behind that sentence.

The cheapest guard is not at the point of use — it is at chance 1. A ledger entry that cites another document rather than a command must name it precisely enough to be grepped, and be grepped, at admission. One command, by the agent doing the admitting. The other three chances are all relays of an entry that should never have been admitted.

Also relevant to what a guard must NOT assume: bd's empty-JSON shape is per-subcommand. `bd human list --json` returns `null` and `bd ready --json` returns `[]`, same database, same session, both exit 0 (agent-plugins-mpnf.18#2). title: Both hooks key state_dir off CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/PWD, which differ between the arming shell and the harness hook: --arm can silently never reach the hook
description:
Filed by review pass 2 of run agent-plugins-mpnf. Reviewer: `code-review` (declared).

## What

Both new hooks key their state directory off environment that is not guaranteed
to match between the shell that arms them and the harness process that runs them:

```sh
# plugin/hooks/bb-stop-ready-loop.sh:57   and  bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh:79
_root="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
_proj="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}"
_key="$(basename "$_proj")-$(printf '%s' "$_proj" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1)"
```

`--arm`, `--status`, `--disarm` and the hook invocation all resolve `state_dir`
independently. If any of the three variables differs between them, `--arm`
writes one directory, the hook reads another, `--status` reports "armed", and
the hook is inert with **no diagnostic** — the failure is silent in the
direction of not blocking.

## Measured, in this session

```
CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=[UNSET]   CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA=[UNSET]   TMPDIR=[UNSET]
PWD=[/home/user/agent-plugins]     git rev-parse --show-toplevel -> /home/user/agent-plugins
```

so an arming shell here keys on `$PWD`. Two plausible project roots give
different keys:

```
/home/user/agent-plugins  ->  agent-plugins-1480149875
/home/user                ->  user-1561763148
```

## The concrete case this repo already documents

`CLAUDE.md`'s "Session bootstrap" section describes the multi-root session:
when this repository is attached alongside another, both are cloned as siblings
and **the parent becomes the project root**. A hook then receives
`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` = the parent while a shell arming from inside the repo
resolves `$PWD` = the repo. Same divergence from arming inside a bead's worktree.

**Partly unverified**: I could not spawn a real harness hook invocation from
this session to observe the value `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` actually carries there.
What is measured is that the two inputs produce different keys and that the
arming path uses `$PWD` when the variable is unset. What would settle it: arm
from a repo checked out under a multi-root parent and invoke the hook through
the harness, comparing `--status` against the directory the hook reads.

## Relationship to the deferred agent-plugins-mpnf.11

.11 is `bb-events-monitor` resolving TMPDIR from the harness env — same family,
different script and different consequence (a monitor watching the wrong log
directory vs a block bound that never arms). Filed separately.

## Remedy sketch

Derive the key from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` — stable across worktrees,
project roots and the arming/hook split — or have `--arm` print the resolved
path and `--status` fail loudly when the directory it reads is not the one an
arm would write.
design:
## Decision (the bead's remedy sketch named two options; both are adopted, and
## the first is CORRECTED)

**The sketch's proposal — "derive the key from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`
— stable across worktrees" — is measurably WRONG on the worktree half, and must
not be implemented as written.** Measured in this repository, git 2.43.0:

```
main checkout:  git rev-parse --show-toplevel            -> /home/user/agent-plugins
inside a git worktree of it:
                git rev-parse --show-toplevel            -> <the worktree path>
main checkout:  git rev-parse --git-common-dir (abs)     -> /home/user/agent-plugins/.git
inside that worktree:
                git rev-parse --git-common-dir (abs)     -> /home/user/agent-plugins/.git
```

`--show-toplevel` returns the WORKTREE root, so an agent arming from inside a
bead's worktree would key a different directory than the main checkout — the
exact divergence this bead exists to remove, reintroduced by its own sketch.
**Use the common git directory instead**; it is the same primitive `bd` uses to
resolve one shared database from any worktree.

## Chosen approach

Both halves of the sketch, because they cover different failure modes: the
derivation makes the key stable, and the diagnostic makes a residual mismatch
loud instead of silent.

**Part A — a stable key.** In BOTH `plugin/hooks/bb-stop-ready-loop.sh` and
`plugin/hooks/bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh`, in the `state_dir` function (the
block computing `_proj` and `_key`):

- Derive the project identity from the absolute common git directory. A
  portable spelling that needs no recent-git flag, verified above to give the
  same answer from the main checkout and from a worktree:
  `cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" && pwd`.
- **Keep the existing derivation as a fallback** for a non-git directory or a
  missing `git`, and keep the `BB_STOP_HOOK_DIR` override ahead of everything —
  it is the escape hatch and must keep working unchanged.
- Keep the `basename`-plus-`cksum` shape so the directory name stays readable;
  only the input to it changes.

**Part B — a loud diagnostic.** `--status` currently reports "armed" by reading
whatever directory it resolves. Have `--arm` and `--status` both PRINT the
resolved `state_dir` path, so the two can be compared by eye, and have
`--status` say plainly when no state directory exists rather than reporting a
bare state. A hook that finds no armed state stays silent and non-blocking —
do not make the hook itself noisy or blocking on this.

## On the unverified half of the premise

The bead could not observe the value `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` carries inside a real
harness hook invocation, and this bead does not need to: the fix removes the
dependency on that variable altogether, so its value stops mattering. Do not
claim the harness behaviour was verified. What IS verified is the worktree
divergence measured above, which the fix must survive.

## Rejected

- **`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.** Measured unstable across worktrees; see
  above.
- **`--path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`.** Correct here, but it is a
  newer flag and these hooks must run wherever the plugin is installed; the
  `cd ... && pwd` form needs no flag support.
- **Making the hook fail loudly when no state directory is found.** A missing
  state directory is the normal unarmed case; failing there would block every
  session that never armed anything.

## Constraints

- Last review loop. Do not change the block/counter semantics, the `MAX`
  handling, or the fail-open direction — only where the state lives and what
  `--arm`/`--status` print.
- Hook scripts only — no capped SKILL.md body is touched.
- Both hooks must change together and stay consistent; they carry the same
  derivation today and must carry the same one after.
- Extend each hook's existing self-tests rather than adding a harness.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] In both hooks, `state_dir` resolves to the SAME path when invoked from the main checkout and from a git worktree of it — demonstrated by running `--status` (or the resolver directly) from both and comparing the printed paths.
- [ ] In both hooks, `state_dir` no longer depends on `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` or `$PWD` when the directory is inside a git repository; `grep -n 'CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR' plugin/hooks/*.sh` shows it only in a documented fallback path.
- [ ] `BB_STOP_HOOK_DIR` still overrides everything and is still consulted first; its existing self-test still passes.
- [ ] Outside a git repository, or with `git` absent, `state_dir` still returns a usable path via the previous derivation — verified by running the resolver with `PATH` lacking `git` and in a non-repo directory.
- [ ] `--arm` and `--status` each print the resolved state directory, so an operator can compare them without reading the source.
- [ ] `--status` distinguishes "no state directory" from an armed or disarmed state.
- [ ] The block/counter behaviour is unchanged: each hook's existing self-tests pass unmodified except where they assert a state path, and the fail-open direction on an unreadable counter is preserved.
- [ ] Both hooks carry the identical derivation, verified by diffing the two `state_dir` functions.
- [ ] No claim is added about what `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` contains inside a harness hook invocation.
- [ ] `sh -n` / `shellcheck` report nothing new beyond the recorded baseline.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` passes with no findings beyond the recorded baseline.

metadata.tier_reason: Two parallel edits to one small function plus a diagnostic; the hard part (the sketch naming an unstable primitive) is already resolved and measured in the Design.

title: run-record.md contradicts itself on graph-plan atomicity: "the abort is total" vs "fails partway through and leaves half a graph behind"; measured, nothing lands
description:
Filed by review pass 2 of run agent-plugins-mpnf. Reviewer: `code-review` (declared).

## What

`plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md` states both halves of a
contradiction about what a malformed graph plan leaves behind, ~50 lines apart:

- line 363: "**The abort is total.** `bd list --status all` afterwards returned only the two beads that pre-dated the attempt — the `m1` node in `nodes` was not created either."
- lines 413-414: "So a malformed sidecar leaves no half-wired graph, **exactly as a malformed plan leaves no half-built one**."
- lines 460-461: "Emit it, diff it, validate it, then load it. **A malformed plan fails partway through and leaves half a graph behind.**"
- line 531 also asserts the safe version: "A *parse* error is the opposite — it aborts before creating anything."

Three sites say the load is atomic; one says it is not. Both are load-bearing —
the atomic claim is what justifies "re-run it rather than reason about what
already landed" for a resumed run; the partial claim is the stated reason for
validating before loading.

## Measured (bd 1.2.2, scratch database)

Baseline 5 beads.

```
$ cat p_bad.json
{"nodes":[{"key":"n1","title":"good node","type":"task","priority":1},
          {"key":"n2","title":"bad node","type":"not-a-real-type","priority":1}],
 "edges":[]}
$ bd create --graph p_bad.json ; echo $?
Error: invalid graph plan: node "n2": invalid type "not-a-real-type"
1
$ bd list --status all --json | jq length
5
$ bd list --status all --json | jq -r '.[].title' | grep -c "good node"
0
```

The valid first node did not land. Same for an edge naming a key outside the
plan, and same for a type parse error (`metadata` holding a number:
`Error: parsing graph plan: json: cannot unmarshal number into ... type string`,
exit 1, nothing created). I could not construct a partial-creation failure.

So line 460-461 is the unmeasured one and it is false.

## Note on what survives

The "validate before loading" instruction is still right, but for the reason
the file gives two sections later — an **unknown field is a warning, exits 0,
and silently drops** — not because a bad plan half-lands. That reason is
measured and should carry the paragraph.

## Remedy sketch

Delete or rewrite lines 460-461 to match the measured behaviour, and re-anchor
the validate-first rationale on the fail-open unknown-field trap.
design:
## Chosen approach

Three sites in `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md` say the
graph-plan load is atomic; one says it is not. The measurement in this bead —
a plan whose second node carries an invalid type creates NOTHING, the valid
first node included — settles it: **the atomic claim is true and the partial
claim is false.**

1. **Rewrite the false sentence.** It is the one under "**Being reviewable
   before it is loaded is most of the value.**", reading "A malformed plan
   fails partway through and leaves half a graph behind." Replace it with the
   measured behaviour: a malformed plan creates nothing at all.
2. **Re-anchor the validate-first rationale on the reason that is true and
   measured.** Validating before loading is still right, but not because a bad
   plan half-lands. The real reason is two sections below and already measured:
   an unknown field on a node, an edge or the plan object is a *warning*, is
   silently dropped, and the load still exits 0 — so a mistyped `assignee` is a
   bead nobody owns and a mistyped edge key a dependency never wired. That is
   the fail-OPEN case a validator has to cover, and it should carry the
   paragraph. Cite it rather than duplicating the measurement.
3. **Leave the three correct sites as they are** — "The abort is total", "a
   malformed sidecar leaves no half-wired graph, exactly as a malformed plan
   leaves no half-built one", and "A *parse* error is the opposite — it aborts
   before creating anything." They are consistent with the measurement.

## Scope boundary

This bead owns `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md` ONLY. The
same false claim appears twice on the `bead-bonanza` side — in that skill's
body and in its own `run-record.md` — and both belong to the bead that
rewrites the orchestrator's load step, which is editing exactly those
passages. Do not edit any file under `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/`.

## Rejected

- **Deleting the "validate before loading" instruction along with its false
  justification.** The instruction is right; only its stated reason was wrong,
  and the correct reason is stronger.
- **Weakening the three atomic claims to "usually atomic".** Nothing measured
  supports a partial-creation mode; hedging would re-open a question the
  measurement closed and would undercut the resumed-run guidance that depends
  on replay being safe.

## Constraints

- Last review loop: rewrite one sentence and re-anchor one rationale. Do not
  restructure the document.
- Reference file only — `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md` has 5 bytes of
  headroom under the 20,000-byte body cap and must not be touched.
- Skill files are exported to other projects: cite no issue ids in the edited
  text.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md` contains no claim that a malformed graph plan leaves a partial or half-built graph; `grep -n 'half a graph\|half-built\|partway' ` on that file returns nothing that asserts partial creation.
- [ ] The document's statements about graph-plan atomicity agree with one another throughout: a malformed plan creates nothing.
- [ ] The instruction to validate and diff before loading survives, and its stated reason is the fail-open unknown-field behaviour (a warning, silently dropped, exit 0) rather than partial creation.
- [ ] The atomicity claim was re-measured on the installed `bd` in a SCRATCH database — a two-node plan whose second node is invalid — and the invocation, the error, the exit status and the resulting bead count appear in the close comment.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/` is modified by this bead, verified by `git diff --name-only`.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md` is unmodified, verified by `git diff --name-only`.
- [ ] The edited text cites no issue ids.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` passes with no findings beyond the recorded baseline.
notes: Moot: the run-record section that contradicted itself on graph-plan atomicity is deleted. What remains is the edge file, whose all-or-nothing loading is stated once. Commit 76d61c4.

title: dispatching.md's worktree table claims sprint-cleanup "applies exactly this rule": measured, row 3 is force-removed and the blocked row is absent
description:
Filed by review pass 2 of run agent-plugins-mpnf. Reviewer: `code-review` (declared).

## What

`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatching.md:270-283` publishes a
four-row table for reading a standing worktree and then asserts:

> `{SCRIPTS}/sprint-cleanup.sh` applies exactly this rule and removes only the
> unambiguous rows.

It does not. Two disagreements, in opposite directions:

**Row 3 — "open or `in_progress` | drained | the agent died holding it. Recover
the bead".** The script removes it. Measured by driving the real
`handle_worktree` with the real `assignee_for_branch` / `status_for_branch`
copied verbatim out of the script:

```
bead {"id":"acme-aa1","assignee":"dev-1","status":"open"}, agent_drained -> true
  => removal attempted: yes ; left flag: 0
```

An `open` bead held out of the ready front by a dependency is neither ready nor
`in_progress`, so `agent_drained` is true and the tree the doc says to keep for
recovery is force-removed.

**The `blocked` row is missing from the table.** The script has one — added by
the agent-plugins-mpnf.5 remedy (e2b69ad), and correct — but a reader of the
table alone does not know it exists.

## Why this is not agent-plugins-mpnf.5

.5 was the code defect: a BLOCKED bead's worktree being destroyed. Its remedy
landed and is verified correct — I drove the ordering and confirmed the blocked
test runs before `agent_drained`, exactly as its comment claims. This is the
doc half that was never updated to match, plus a row the two never agreed on.

## Why it matters

The table is the published contract; the script is what runs. Two readers of the
same run disagree about what happened to a worktree, and the disagreement is on
the destructive side.

## Remedy sketch

Settle which is right — the script's behaviour on row 3 is arguably the bug and
the table arguably the intent — then make one match the other. Add the `blocked`
row either way. If the table is right, this converges with the sibling bead on
`agent_drained` conflating "could not count" with "drained": both want
`handle_worktree` to leave more standing and raise `note_left`.
design:
## Decision (this was the bead's open question — it is now closed)

**The TABLE is right; the SCRIPT's row-3 behaviour is the bug.** Make the
script match the published table, and add the missing `blocked` row to the
table. Reasons, in order:

1. The table's row 3 — an `open` or `in_progress` bead whose agent has drained
   means the agent died holding it, so the tree is kept for recovery — is the
   safe reading. The script's reading destroys a tree that may hold the only
   copy of partial work.
2. The script's own header already commits to it: "NEVER DESTRUCTIVE ON
   AMBIGUITY". An unfinished bead with no live agent IS the ambiguous case.
3. The change strictly NARROWS removal, so it cannot destroy anything the
   current script preserves. That is the right direction for the last review
   loop, where no further pass will catch a regression.

## Chosen approach

**Part A — `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh`,
`handle_worktree`.** Removal currently requires only `agent_drained`. Require
in addition that the bead is CLOSED — the unambiguous "work finished and
landed" signal, and the only status for which the tree is certainly disposable.
The branch already has `status_for_branch`'s value to hand, so this is a
condition on the existing `elif`, not a new lookup:

- bead closed AND agent drained  -> remove (unchanged outcome)
- bead open/in_progress AND agent drained -> `LEFT`, "its agent drained holding
  an unfinished bead", `note_left` (this is the fix)
- bead `blocked` -> `LEFT` (unchanged; keep this test where it is, ahead of
  `agent_drained`)
- agent still has a queue -> `LEFT` (unchanged)

Preserve the existing ordering and the existing `note_left` / `RC_LEFT`
plumbing; add one condition and one message.

**Part B — `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatching.md`,** the
four-row worktree table ending in the sentence "applies exactly this rule and
removes only the unambiguous rows":

- Add the missing **`blocked`** row: a blocked bead's worktree holds the
  partial work and is left standing. The script has had this behaviour since
  the blocked-worktree guard landed; the table never mentioned it.
- Leave row 3 as written — the script is being changed to match it — and make
  the closing sentence true rather than aspirational by stating that removal
  requires a CLOSED bead and a drained agent.

## Scope boundary

This bead does not touch the sentence elsewhere in `dispatching.md` about what
`bd ready --json` returns when empty; the sweep bead earlier in this batch owns
it. It does not touch `prune_worktrees`' scoping, which is the preceding bead's.

## Rejected

- **Rewriting the table to describe the script's current row-3 behaviour.** It
  would publish "we force-remove the tree of a bead nobody finished" as
  intended design, and the destructive direction is the one to fix, not to
  document.
- **Folding this into the `agent_drained` tri-state bead.** That bead handles a
  different input — a tracker that cannot answer at all. This one is a tracker
  that answers correctly and a rule that draws the wrong conclusion.

## Constraints

- Reference file plus one script condition. No capped SKILL.md body is touched.
- Skill files are exported to other projects: cite no issue ids in the edited
  text.

- [ ] A worktree whose bead is `closed` and whose agent has drained is still removed — the ordinary success path is unchanged.
- [ ] A worktree whose bead is `blocked` is still LEFT, and that test still runs before the drained test.

- [ ] Every row of that table matches what the script does, checked row by row against `handle_worktree` and recorded in the close comment as a row-to-branch mapping.
- [ ] The table's closing sentence states the actual removal condition (bead closed AND agent drained) rather than asserting conformance in the abstract.
- [ ] Self-tests cover the open-bead-drained-agent case; existing self-tests still pass.
- [ ] `sh -n` / `shellcheck` report nothing new beyond the recorded baseline.

title: sprint-cleanup's prune_worktrees ignores its epic argument and tears down repo-wide: a concurrent sprint's worktree is force-removed
description:
Filed by review pass 2 of run agent-plugins-mpnf. Reviewer: `code-review` (declared).

## What

`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh`, `prune_worktrees` (line 52).
It still takes `<epic>` and assigns `epic="$1"` at line 53, and **never reads it
again** — verified: `awk '/^prune_worktrees\(\)/,/^}/' | grep epic` returns only
the signature comment, the assignment, and an unrelated comment word. The only
caller is line 327, `prune_worktrees "$EPIC"`.

The lookup that replaced it is repo-wide:

```sh
beads="$(bd list --all --json 2>/dev/null)" || beads='[]'
```

and matching is by branch-name-is-a-bead's-hash-suffix. So a worktree belonging
to a **different, concurrent sprint in the same clone** matches a bead, that
bead's assignee is checked, and if that other run's agent has drained the tree
is `git worktree remove --force`d.

## Why this is a regression, not just a scope simplification

The previous form was `bd list --all --has-metadata-key worktree --json`. A
worktree from another run whose beads carried no `worktree` key matched nothing
and was reported "LEFT — no dispatch record", standing and named. The new form
matches every bead in the database, so the same tree is now removed.

`agent-plugins-qozp.9` removed the `worktree` metadata key deliberately and the
assignment-based lookup is the right direction; the run-scoping that the metadata
key incidentally provided was dropped with it and not replaced.

## Remedy sketch

Either restore scoping — walk the run epic transitively (see the sibling bead on
`bd list --parent` being direct-children-only, and bb-status.sh:396's existing
walker) and match only against that set — or, if repo-wide is intended, delete
the dead `epic` parameter and say in the header that the teardown is repo-wide,
so the next reader is not misled by a signature that promises scoping.
design:
## Decision (this was the bead's open question — it is now closed)

**Restore run scoping. Do NOT keep the repo-wide behaviour and delete the
parameter.** Force-removing a concurrent sprint's worktree destroys uncommitted
work in a clone the operator did not ask this run to touch; a stale worktree
left standing costs disk and a log line. The asymmetry is decisive, and the
signature, the header and the sole call site all already promise scoping.

## Chosen approach

The current comment inside `prune_worktrees` states the reason scoping was
dropped: "Not scoped by `bd list --parent`: it returns DIRECT children only, so
on a nested run epic every leaf bead would go unmatched and its worktree be
left standing." That objection is correct and is answered by walking the tree
rather than by abandoning the scope.

In `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh`:

1. **Add a transitive descendants helper** — collect the epic's children with
   `bd list --parent <id> --all --json`, then recurse into any child that is
   itself an epic, accumulating ids. This mirrors the walker
   `bb-status.sh` already carries; sibling scripts cannot share shell
   functions, so implement it locally rather than sourcing across files.
2. **Filter the bead set to those descendants.** Keep `--all` — a finished bead
   is closed and `bd list` defaults to open, so dropping `--all` would
   reintroduce a different miss. Keep the branch-suffix matching as it is.
3. **Replace the stale comment** with what is now true: the set is scoped to
   the run epic's transitive descendants, so a worktree belonging to another
   run matches nothing.
4. **A worktree that matches no bead in the run keeps its current outcome** —
   `LEFT`, "no bead owns its branch", with `note_left`. That is the correct,
   non-destructive result for another run's tree, and it is what the previous
   metadata-key-scoped form produced.

## Rejected

- **Deleting the `epic` parameter and documenting teardown as repo-wide.** It
  makes a data-loss behaviour official rather than fixing it.
- **Restoring the old `--has-metadata-key worktree` lookup.** That key was
  removed deliberately when assignment replaced batch bookkeeping; reinstating
  it would revert a correct change to get a side effect it only supplied by
  accident.
- **Scoping by branch-name prefix instead of by the graph.** Branch naming is a
  convention, not a guarantee, and it would not survive a renamed branch.

## Constraints

- Last review loop: narrow the set of worktrees eligible for removal; do not
  widen it, and do not change what happens to a worktree once it is eligible.
- Script file only — no capped SKILL.md body is touched.
- Extend the script's existing self-tests rather than adding a harness.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `prune_worktrees` reads its `<epic>` argument; `awk '/^prune_worktrees\(\)/,/^}/' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh | grep -c epic` shows the parameter used beyond its assignment and comment.
- [ ] Measured in a SCRATCH database: with a run epic whose work beads are GRANDCHILDREN (run epic -> target epic -> tasks), every one of those tasks is found by the scoped lookup — the nested shape that motivated the repo-wide form is handled.
- [ ] Measured in the same scratch database: a bead belonging to a DIFFERENT epic is not in the scoped set, and a worktree whose branch matches that bead is reported `LEFT — no bead owns its branch` rather than removed.
- [ ] Closed beads are still matched (the lookup keeps `--all`); a worktree for a closed in-run bead whose agent has drained is still removed.
- [ ] No worktree that the pre-change script left standing is removed by the post-change script — the change only narrows removal.
- [ ] The comment explaining the lookup describes the transitive scoping actually implemented; no surviving comment claims the lookup is unscoped because `bd list --parent` is direct-children-only.
- [ ] A self-test covers the nested-epic shape and the foreign-bead shape; existing self-tests still pass.
- [ ] `sh -n` / `shellcheck` report nothing new beyond the recorded baseline.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` passes with no findings beyond the recorded baseline.

title: Merge beads are not excluded from the dispatch front: a sprint-batch subagent is handed a merge bead only the coordinator may run
description:
Filed by review pass 2 of run agent-plugins-mpnf. Reviewer: `code-review` (declared).

## What

`agent-plugins-qozp.11` introduced the merge bead: one per batch, a `task`
carrying the label `merge`, parented under the flat target, assigned to
`merge-<run-id>`, and blocked on every bead in its batch. It becomes ready
exactly when its batch closes.

The coordinator's dispatch front does not exclude it:

```
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatching.md:22
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md:205
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md:94
  bd ready --parent <epic> --exclude-type=epic --exclude-label human
```

`--exclude-label merge` appears nowhere in the tree — verified,
`grep -rn "exclude-label" plugin/` returns only the three `human` sites above.

dispatching.md's own loop instruction is "Re-query the front, **dispatch what is
in it and not already held**". A merge bead is in it, is not held, and is a task,
so it is handed to a `sprint-batch` subagent — which will take it into its own
worktree and try to work it as ordinary development, while worktree-mechanics.md
reserves merging for the coordinator acting as `merge-<run-id>` and holding
`bd merge-slot`.

## Note

`bd ready --label merge` is already documented (worktree-mechanics.md:170) as
the merge agent's own query, so the label is load-bearing in one direction and
absent in the other. `--exclude-label` is confirmed to exist on `bd ready`
(bd 1.2.2); the reviewer verified it independently.

## Remedy sketch

Add `--exclude-label merge` to the dispatch front at all three sites, and carry
dispatching.md's existing warning across: the exclusion is on the DISPATCH query
and nowhere else, so a completion or queue count that hides merge beads reports
a run as drained while batches are still unlanded.

Watch the byte budget — `bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` is one of the three sites.
design:
## Chosen approach

Add `--exclude-label merge` to the dispatch front at all three sites, and carry
the existing scoping warning across to it.

`--exclude-label` exists on `bd ready` in the installed CLI — confirmed from
`bd ready --help`, which lists "--exclude-label strings   Exclude issues that
have ANY of these labels". It takes a comma-separated list, so the front
becomes one flag with two values rather than two flags.

The three sites, quoted so they relocate under edits:

- `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatching.md` — the line containing
  `--exclude-type=epic --exclude-label human` in the opening paragraph about
  the complete set.
- `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` — the line beginning "**`bd ready
  --parent <epic> --exclude-type=epic --exclude-label human` IS the".
- `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md` — the line containing
  `--exclude-type=epic --exclude-label human`. Without that, the run hands a".

**Carry the warning.** `dispatching.md` already says "**`--exclude-label human`
is on the DISPATCH query and nowhere else.**" Extend that sentence to cover
`merge` rather than adding a second paragraph: a completion check or queue
count that hides merge beads would report a run as drained while batches are
still unlanded. That is the failure this exclusion could otherwise cause.

The label is already load-bearing in the other direction — the merge agent's
own query is `bd ready --label merge` — so nothing new has to be established
about how merge beads are marked.

## Rejected

- **Excluding by assignee (`merge-<run-id>`).** The label is the established
  marker, is already queried positively, and does not require the dispatcher to
  know the run's agent-id convention.
- **A custom issue type for merge beads.** Explicitly rejected upstream: it
  lives in per-clone local config, so a clone that has not run the setup step
  cannot create or filter those beads.

## Constraints

- **Byte cap.** `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` is one of the three
  sites and has very little headroom under the 20,000-byte body cap; the
  preceding bead in this batch frees some. Pay for the added characters within
  the same sentence you are editing — do not cut an unrelated rule. Re-measure
  with the checker's own method and, if the addition cannot be made to fit
  without cutting something unrelated, take the Blocked path and report it
  rather than trimming elsewhere.
- Skill files are exported to other projects: cite no issue ids in the edited
  text.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] All three dispatch-front sites read `--exclude-label human,merge` (or an equivalent that excludes both labels); `grep -rn 'exclude-label' plugin/` shows no dispatch-front site excluding only `human`.
- [ ] The merge agent's own positive query `bd ready --label merge` is unchanged and still documented.
- [ ] `dispatching.md`'s "on the DISPATCH query and nowhere else" warning covers `merge` as well as `human`, and names the consequence of over-applying it: a run reported drained while batches are unlanded.
- [ ] Measured in a SCRATCH database: with a merge bead (label `merge`) and an ordinary task both ready under one epic, `bd ready --parent <epic> --exclude-type=epic --exclude-label human,merge --json` returns the task and not the merge bead. The invocation and its output appear in the close comment.
- [ ] The body of `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` is at most 20000 bytes, measured with `python3 -c "import sys;print(len(open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8').read().split('---',2)[2].encode('utf-8')))" plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md`. Record the number in the close comment.
- [ ] No rule unrelated to the dispatch front was removed from the skill body, verified by reading `git diff` for that file in full.
- [ ] The edited text cites no issue ids.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` passes with no findings beyond the recorded baseline.
