title: The run's merged diff ships five new copies of the "bd ready --json returns null when empty" claim this same run retracted; one is labelled "this is measured"
description:
Filed by review pass 2 of run agent-plugins-mpnf. Reviewer: `code-review` (declared).
Not attributable to one bead — the claim was copied onto surfaces from four
different beads' commits, so this is parented to the run epic.

## What

This run **retracted** the claim "`bd ready --json` returns `null` when empty"
on its own epic — measured `[]` in every configuration tried, by two independent
agents. The run's merged diff then shipped five NEW copies of it:

| site | text |
|---|---|
| `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatching.md:258` | "`bd ready --json` answers `null` rather than `[]` when empty" |
| `plugin/hooks/bb-stop-ready-loop.sh:69` | "`bd ready --json` returns `null`, not `[]`, when the queue is empty" |
| `plugin/hooks/bb-subagent-stop-queue.sh:120` | same sentence |
| `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh:162` | "`bd ready --json` returns null rather than [] when empty" |
| `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh:249` | "`bd ready --json` answers null rather than [], so both spellings must read as empty" |

plus a self-test assertion whose NAME asserts it
(`bb-stop-ready-loop.sh:213`, "empty queue (null, not []) does not block").

`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-status.sh:459` carries a sixth copy that
pre-dates this diff and is therefore out of this finding's scope, but should be
swept at the same time.

**The dispatching.md instance is the worst of the six**: the sentence
immediately before it reads "Both are required and **this is measured**", so a
false claim inherits an explicit measurement badge.

## Measured (bd 1.2.2, scratch database, this session)

```
$ bd ready --json                                   -> []   exit 0   (empty tracker)
$ bd ready --assignee no-such-agent --json          -> []   exit 0   (empty tracker)
$ bd ready --assignee no-such-agent --json          -> []   exit 0   (one bead present)
$ bd ready --parent zt-nope --json                  -> []   exit 0
```

`null` was not produced in any configuration.

## Why it matters even though the code is right

Accepting both spellings is harmless defensive code and none of these scripts
misbehaves. The defect is the CLAIM, on six permanent surfaces, four of which
are files exported to other projects. AGENTS.md's "Tool claims are measured at
the point of use" — added to the tree by `agent-plugins-x5tk` in THIS SAME DIFF —
names this exact failure, and its table lists "a committed document" and "this
repository's own scripts" as surfaces audited "for shape — never for truth".
This is the run's own rule broken by the run's own diff.

## Remedy sketch

Replace each with what is true and still justifies the code: `bd ready --json`
returns `[]` when empty (measured, bd 1.2.2); the emptiness test accepts `null`
and the empty string as well because a defensive reader must not assume a list.
Rename the self-test assertion to say it is testing a non-list payload, not a
documented bd behaviour. Grep the distinctive phrasing BEFORE editing any source,
per AGENTS.md's "Retracting a claim found false" — the sixth copy in bb-status.sh
is what that step is for.
design:
## Chosen approach

A retraction sweep, run in the order this project's own procedure requires.

**The true claim, measured on bd 1.2.2 and to be re-measured before writing:**
`bd ready --json` returns `[]` when empty — measured in the empty-tracker,
`--parent`-filtered and `--assignee`-filtered configurations, and independently
by a second agent. `null` was not produced in any configuration. Do NOT assert
either shape as a universal without running it yourself first; record the
invocation and its output in the close comment.

**Step 1 — grep BEFORE editing anything.** The distinctive phrasings are gone
the moment the first site is fixed, so enumerate first and keep the list:

```
grep -rn "returns null\|returns \`null\`\|answers null\|answers \`null\`\|null, not \[\]\|null rather than \[\]\|\`null\` rather than" plugin/
```

At the time of grooming this returned SEVEN sites in five files. Treat that as
a starting list to re-derive, not as the answer.

**Step 2 — replace each with what is true and still justifies the code.** The
defensive parsing is correct and stays; only the CLAIM changes. The honest
replacement is of this shape: `bd ready --json` returns `[]` when empty
(measured); the emptiness test also accepts `null` and the empty string because
a defensive reader must not assume the payload is a list.

**Step 3 — rename the self-test assertion** in `plugin/hooks/
bb-stop-ready-loop.sh` whose NAME asserts the false claim ("empty queue (null,
not []) does not block"). It must say it exercises a NON-LIST payload, not a
documented `bd` behaviour. Keep the `null` stub itself — testing the defensive
branch is the point.

**Step 4 — include the pre-existing site in `bb-status.sh`.** It predates this
run's diff and is therefore outside the finding's strict scope, but leaving one
copy behind defeats a sweep. Sweep it.

## Scope boundary

This bead owns EVERY site the grep returns, including the one in
`references/dispatching.md` — the worst of them, since the sentence before it
reads "Both are required and **this is measured**", lending a false claim an
explicit measurement badge. Other beads in this run edit these same files at
other regions; they do not touch these sentences.

## Rejected

- **Splitting the sweep per file.** The value of a retraction is that it is one
  act with one enumeration; per-file children would each re-derive the list and
  the union is what has to be empty at the end.
- **Deleting the sentences rather than replacing them.** Each one is justifying
  real defensive code; removing the justification invites the code's removal.

## Constraints

- No behaviour change. Every script must behave identically before and after.
- Comment and prose edits only, plus one self-test NAME.
- Skill files are exported to other projects: cite no issue ids in the edited
  text.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The grep for the distinctive phrasings was run and its output recorded BEFORE any file was edited; the site list appears in the close comment.
- [ ] The true behaviour was re-measured on the installed `bd` in a SCRATCH database, and the invocation plus its output appear in the close comment.
- [ ] After the sweep, `grep -rn "returns null\|returns \`null\`\|answers null\|answers \`null\`\|null, not \[\]\|null rather than \[\]\|\`null\` rather than" plugin/` returns nothing.
- [ ] No surviving comment or prose in `plugin/` claims `bd ready --json` yields `null` when empty; every replacement states `[]` and attributes it to measurement.
- [ ] The defensive emptiness tests still accept `null`, `''` and `[]`, and their justification now rests on "do not assume a list" rather than on a claimed `bd` behaviour.
- [ ] The self-test assertion name in `plugin/hooks/bb-stop-ready-loop.sh` no longer asserts a `bd` behaviour; the test still exercises the non-list payload and still passes.
- [ ] Every script's self-tests pass and behaviour is unchanged: no non-comment line of shell is modified except the one self-test name string, verified by reading `git diff` in full.
- [ ] The edited text cites no issue ids.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` passes with no findings beyond the recorded baseline.

title: bd merge-slot release is not owner-protected — any actor can release another's slot
design:
MEASURED on bd 1.2.2 in a scratch database, while agent-plugins-qozp.17 was measuring that the slot records its holder as the actor:

  export BEADS_ACTOR=merge-scratch
  bd merge-slot create   -> exit 0, "Created merge slot: scratch-merge-slot"
  bd merge-slot acquire  -> exit 0, "Acquired merge slot ... Holder: merge-scratch"
  bd merge-slot check    -> "Merge slot held ... Holder: merge-scratch"
  export BEADS_ACTOR=someone-else
  bd merge-slot check    -> "Holder: merge-scratch"        (correct)
  bd merge-slot release  -> exit 0, "Released merge slot: scratch-merge-slot"   <-- THE HAZARD
  bd merge-slot check    -> "Merge slot available"

So acquisition is attributed to the actor but RELEASE is not checked against it. Any agent in the repository can release a slot it does not hold, exit 0, no warning. The slot is already documented as repository-wide and branch-unaware, so a second concurrent run is exactly the situation where this fires: run B releases run A slot mid-merge and both then believe they hold it.

Not fixed under qozp.17, whose scope is BEADS_ACTOR at ceremony dispatch sites. Filed rather than done.

WHAT TO DECIDE: whether bead-bonanza should (a) treat this as a bd defect to report upstream, (b) document it beside the existing KNOWN LIMITATION in bead-bonanza/references/worktree-mechanics.md so a reader does not assume release is protected, or (c) have the merge step re-check "bd merge-slot check" names its own id immediately before merging. (b) is cheap and strictly an improvement; (c) narrows the window but cannot close it.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] The measurement above is re-confirmed on the bd version in use at the time.
[ ] worktree-mechanics.md states whether release is owner-checked, either way.
[ ] If a re-check before merge is adopted, it is stated at the merge step, not only in prose.
notes: Moot: the merge slot is deleted. bd merge-slot is no longer called anywhere in the corpus. Commit 76d61c4.

title: capability-tier.md still claims --set-metadata 'stores every value as a string'; on bd 1.2.2 it JSON-parses scalars
description:
`plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/capability-tier.md`, in the very bullet the metadata correction rewrote:

> `--set-metadata key=value` is **repeatable and additive** ... It stores every value as a **string** - an array written this way reads back as the literal `["a","b"]`, not a list

The array half is correct. The universal is not. Measured on bd 1.2.2 in a throwaway scratch database, one `--set-metadata` per key on one bead:

```
b=true    -> true      (bool)
f=1.5     -> 1.5       (float)
num=5     -> 5         (int)
n=null    -> null      (null)
z=007     -> "007"     (str - leading zero preserved)
s=hello   -> "hello"   (str)
arr=[1,2] -> "[1,2]"   (str)
o={"a":1} -> "{\"a\":1}" (str)
```

So `--set-metadata` **parses scalars as JSON where it can** and falls back to a string. Arrays and objects come back as strings; numbers, booleans and null do not.

This is the same class of defect the bead that rewrote this bullet was filed to fix - a corpus sentence asserting tool behaviour that nobody measured - and it now sits inside the corrected text, carrying the authority of having been fixed. A reader following it would restate a numeric or boolean key under `--metadata` needlessly, and - worse - would write a check comparing `metadata.concurrency_cap` against a string when `pre-flight-check.sh` writes it as a JSON number.

**Fix.** Replace "stores every value as a string" with what was measured: scalars are JSON-parsed where parseable, everything else (arrays, objects, non-numeric text) is stored as a string - so `--metadata` is required for an array or object value, not for every non-string value.

title: capability-tier.md's corrected merge semantics never mention --unset-metadata, and run-record.md's write-back recipe can no longer delete a key
description:
The correction to `plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/capability-tier.md` established that `--metadata` MERGES at the top level rather than replacing. It did not follow that through to the consequence: **under merge semantics there is no way to DELETE a metadata key with `--metadata`.**

`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md` still carries the recipe that depends on replacement:

> **Merge, never replace.** ... Read it, update your keys, write it back:
> `bd show <epic> --json | jq '.[0].metadata'` -> edit -> `bd update <epic> --metadata @file.json`.

Measured on bd 1.2.2 in a throwaway scratch database:

```
bd update <id> --metadata '{"keep":1,"drop":2}'
printf '{"keep":1}' > m.json
bd update <id> --metadata @m.json          # exit 0
bd show <id> --json | jq -c '.[0].metadata'
-> {"drop":2,"keep":1, ...}                # "drop" SURVIVES the write-back

bd update <id> --unset-metadata drop       # exit 0
bd show <id> --json | jq -c '.[0].metadata'
-> {"keep":1, ...}                         # gone
```

`bd update --help` on 1.2.2 lists `--unset-metadata stringArray  Remove metadata key (repeatable)`. `capability-tier.md` does not mention it anywhere, and it is the only flag that removes a key.

**Why it matters beyond tidiness.** Anything that clears a key by omitting it from a write-back now silently leaves it set. `dispatch_state`/`dispatched_at`/`worktree` are the live case: a dead dispatch whose `dispatch_state=running` is "removed" by a read-edit-write-back keeps reading as running, and `bb-status.sh run` reports it under "dispatches still running".

**Fix.** Add `--unset-metadata` to `capability-tier.md`'s flag comparison as the only removal path, and correct `bead-bonanza/references/run-record.md`'s recipe so it does not present write-back as a way to drop a key.

title: Correct the unqualified BEADS_ACTOR claim premise in docs/plans/
description:

are a convenience; the durable anchor is the quoted sentence.)

Measured on bd 1.2.2 in a throwaway database, four arms: on an UNASSIGNED bead,
`env -u BEADS_ACTOR bd update <id> --claim` exits 0 and silently sets assignee to the

mode has exactly one entry point.

has already been corrected; the design doc and the rollout plan have not.

UNASSIGNED bead silently, and is refused loudly on an assigned one.

Keep the conclusion, which the measurement strengthens rather than weakens: "export
BEADS_ACTOR everywhere" and "every bead carries an assignee before dispatch" are belt and
braces, not alternatives. Do not weaken either instruction.

The three sites, by content rather than by line number:

**Site 1 — `docs/plans/beads-coordination-design.md`, the "Do first" table,

Note the backticks around `assignee`. That is why the acceptance criterion's

**Site 2 — same file, the BEADS_ACTOR discussion late in the document.** The

title: bd 1.2.2: 'bd human dismiss' fails with 'storage is nil'
description:
Measured 2026-08-24 on bd 1.2.2 in this repository, immediately after closing agent-plugins-qozp.12 (a bead carrying the 'human' label):

  $ bd human dismiss agent-plugins-qozp.12
  Error: resolving issue ID agent-plugins-qozp.12: cannot resolve issue ID "agent-plugins-qozp.12": storage is nil
  exit 1

The same id resolves fine for every other subcommand in the same shell — bd show, bd update, bd close and bd comment all succeeded against it before and after. So this is not an id-resolution problem; 'bd human dismiss' appears not to open storage before resolving.

Consequence: a bead flagged for a human cannot be taken off the human queue through the documented path. 'bd human list' keeps reporting it even after the bead is closed (measured: it printed the bead with 'Status: closed'), which makes any health check that reads the human queue permanently red.

Workaround that works: bd update <id> --remove-label human (exit 0; 'bd human list' then reports 'No human-needed beads found').

Also worth reporting alongside: 'bd human list' counts CLOSED beads. A closed bead is not awaiting a decision, so the queue should exclude it regardless of this bug.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Reported upstream to gastownhall/beads with the reproduction above.
- [ ] Either bd human dismiss works, or this project's health checks stop reading bd human list as authoritative.

title: pre-flight-check.sh reports a failed manifest read as a write success
description:
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh, step 8b (the python3 heredoc, ~line 713).

The read-modify-write reads the current manifest inside try/except and falls back to `cur = {}` on ANY failure — it never checks `r.returncode`, so a non-zero `bd show`, an empty stdout or malformed JSON all land in the same branch. It then calls `bd update <epic> --metadata json.dumps(cur)`, which REPLACES the metadata wholesale. The result is a manifest containing only {"concurrency_cap": N}: base_sha, branch, admitted, excluded, standing_auth, checks_baseline and checks_ids are all gone — including the baseline this same script wrote ~60 lines earlier in the same invocation.

It then prints the success line 'written: concurrency_cap on <epic>'. The failure is silent and the run continues with an unrecoverable manifest; sprint-review's own 'base_sha from the manifest, never a merge-base' rule then has nothing to read.

Compounding: references/scripts.md states pre-flight writes the baseline 'merging rather than replacing so grooming's and admission's keys survive'. On the except path that documented guarantee does not hold.

FIX DIRECTION: check r.returncode and distinguish 'metadata absent' (safe: start from {}) from 'could not read metadata' (fatal: block, do not write). Prefer a merge-style update over a full --metadata replace if bd offers one (--set-metadata writes a single key).

Evidence: source read at plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh:705-735.
close_reason: Fixed: both manifest writes now go through one manifest_merge helper that fails loudly on an unreadable manifest instead of guessing an empty one. Downgraded P0->P2 on measurement: bd update --metadata merges at the top level on bd 1.2.2, so the claimed data-loss path does not exist. Corpus correction filed as agent-plugins-4tjk. Commit a3e7d38.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: coordinator verification (review-qozp's finding independently confirmed against source, not accepted on testimony): pre-flight-check.sh's concurrency_cap block at lines 712-736 never reads bd show's return code - 'r = subprocess.run(...)' then 'json.loads(r.stdout)' with 'except Exception: cur = {}' - and then calls 'bd update --metadata json.dumps(cur)', which REPLACES the object. On any bd show failure the manifest is reduced to {"concurrency_cap": N}, destroying admitted, excluded, moved, branch, base_sha, standing_auth, checks_ids, checks_baseline, review_passes and review_budget, and the script prints 'written: concurrency_cap' - a success line over a wipe. IMPORTANT ADDITION not in the original finding: the IDENTICAL pattern is pre-existing at lines 653-672 (the checks_baseline write), so agent-plugins-h3j8 duplicated an existing defect rather than introducing a new class of one. A fix must repair BOTH sites, and the two should share one read-merge-write helper rather than a third copy. Suggested guard: treat r.returncode != 0, or a parse failure, as fatal - block rather than fall back to an empty dict, because an empty dict is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty manifest.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
CORRECTION — the P0 premise is FALSE, measured on bd 1.2.2. Both this finding and my own 'independent verification' of it asserted that 'bd update --metadata REPLACES the object'. It does not. Measured in a scratch database (mmlab-doq, bd version 1.2.2 (dev)):

  seed:  bd update <id> --metadata '{"alpha":1,"beta":"two","gamma":["x","y"]}'
  then:  bd update <id> --metadata '{"delta":9}'
  read:  {"beta":"two","alpha":1,"delta":9,"gamma":["x","y"]}   <- all four keys

Omitted keys SURVIVE; it merges at the top level. A second control drove the exact old code with a PATH shim making only 'bd show' fail (a transient read failure on an epic that exists), and the seeded manifest — admitted, branch, base_sha, standing_auth, review_passes — came through intact.

So there is no data-loss path here and this is not a P0. What IS true, and what the fix keeps: (a) the read error was reported as a write success, so the caller printed 'written: ...' having merged onto a guessed base; (b) the merge-at-top-level behaviour is UNDOCUMENTED and partial — a nested value is replaced wholesale (measured: {"a":1,"b":2} overwritten with {"c":3} yields {"c":3}), and standing_auth is a nested object — so the script should not stake the admission record on it.

Where the false premise came from: plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/capability-tier.md:57-60 states --metadata 'replaces the entire metadata object' and warns you will 'silently drop every key you did not restate'. That is wrong against bd 1.2.2 and it propagated into a review finding and into a coordinator verification. Filed separately.

My verification checked the CODE SHAPE (no returncode check, 'except: cur = {}') and did not check the CONSEQUENCE. Recording that as the lesson: a code-shape match plus a documented behaviour is not a measurement.

title: Settle which file owns the managed BEADS INTEGRATION block, and repair the split markers
description:
The `BEADS INTEGRATION` markers are split across two files, each half orphaned.
Measured on the current default branch:

    $ grep -n 'BEADS INTEGRATION' CLAUDE.md
    58:<!-- BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION v:1 profile:minimal hash:6cd5cc61 -->
    $ grep -n 'BEADS INTEGRATION' AGENTS.md
    413:<!-- END BEADS INTEGRATION -->

CLAUDE.md's BEGIN is the last line of the file: no body, no END. AGENTS.md's
END has no BEGIN, so every one of the 412 lines above it — including
"Where documents live" and "Historical prose: don't", which are ours — sits
inside what a naive tool would read as a managed region.

How each half got orphaned:

  - `3293ed5` moved CLAUDE.md's managed block and the hand-written
    "How beads persist in THIS project" section into AGENTS.md, and left the
    BEGIN line behind in CLAUDE.md.
  - `9f418f4` ("Move the model lineup and run defaults into sf.toml") deleted
    AGENTS.md's `<!-- BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION v:1 profile:minimal
    hash:970c3bf2 -->` line together with the model-lineup list it happened to
    sit under. Visible in `git show 9f418f4 -- AGENTS.md`.

## Why this is not a trivial marker repair

The obvious fix — restore a well-formed BEGIN..END pair in CLAUDE.md and let
`bd setup claude` fill it — installs 53 lines that are **already in AGENTS.md
byte for byte**. Measured: the body bd 1.2.2 installs and the body currently
in AGENTS.md (from `## Beads Issue Tracker` to the orphan END) are both 53
lines and `diff -u` between them exits 0. CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md with
`@AGENTS.md`, so every Claude Code session would load those 53 lines twice.
That is exactly the duplicate-Beads-section problem `3293ed5` set out to fix,
and it contradicts CLAUDE.md's own instruction: "Add ONLY Claude-specific
instructions below. Anything true for every agent belongs in AGENTS.md."

## The decision this bead needs

Which file, if any, carries a tool-managed Beads block:

  (a) AGENTS.md only — restore its BEGIN marker in the right place, delete
      CLAUDE.md's orphan BEGIN. `bd setup codex` is the recipe that writes
      AGENTS.md. `bd setup claude --check` then reports "not installed"
      rather than "stale", which is honest but permanently non-green.
  (b) CLAUDE.md only — accept the 53-line duplication, or first strip the
      block from AGENTS.md so the import no longer carries it.
  (c) Neither — delete both orphan markers and hand-maintain the guidance,
      accepting that `bd setup --check` never reports the integration
      installed.

Note a hazard against (a) and (c): the orphan BEGIN in CLAUDE.md is currently
the only thing stopping `bd setup claude` from appending a fresh 53-line
block. With no markers at all the tool takes its "add to existing file" path
and appends — measured in a throwaway project:
`✓ Added beads section to existing CLAUDE.md`. So deleting the orphan marker
without settling the question makes the duplication one accidental
`bd setup claude` away.
acceptance_criteria: One of options (a)/(b)/(c) is chosen by the owner and applied. No orphan BEGIN or END marker remains in either CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md — grep 'BEADS INTEGRATION' over both files returns either a matched pair in exactly one file or nothing. The 53-line block is not present twice in what a Claude Code session loads.

title: Report two bd setup defects upstream to gastownhall/beads
description:
Report upstream to gastownhall/beads. Two defects in `bd setup <recipe>`,
both measured on `bd version 1.2.2 (dev)`, both reproduced from scratch in a
throwaway project (not only in this repo).

## Defect 1 — silent no-op reported as success when the BEGIN marker is orphaned

If the target file contains `<!-- BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION ... -->` with no
matching `<!-- END BEADS INTEGRATION -->`, `bd setup claude`:

  - prints `✓ Updated existing beads section in CLAUDE.md`
  - exits 0
  - **writes nothing** (file bytes identical, md5 unchanged)
  - leaves `bd setup claude --check` reporting `stale`, exit 1, forever

There is no way out of the loop from the CLI: the command the check tells you
to run is the command that does nothing.

Reproduction (clean throwaway project, `.beads/metadata.json` +
`.beads/config.yaml` with `sync.remote` set so the expected template hash is
`970c3bf2`):

CLAUDE.md before:

    # Proj

    Hand-written intro.

    <!-- BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION v:1 profile:minimal hash:6cd5cc61 -->

Observed:

    $ bd setup claude --check ; echo $?
    ⚠ Claude Code integration installed but stale: .../CLAUDE.md
      Run: bd setup claude (to update)
    1
    $ bd setup claude ; echo $?
    ✓ Updated existing beads section in CLAUDE.md
    0
    $ md5sum before.md CLAUDE.md
    079602c9f186c6e9661b6c37509a35be  before.md
    079602c9f186c6e9661b6c37509a35be  CLAUDE.md
    $ diff -u before.md CLAUDE.md ; echo $?
    0
    $ bd setup claude --check ; echo $?
    ⚠ Claude Code integration installed but stale: .../CLAUDE.md
    1

Negative control, identical in every respect except that the block is
well-formed (`BEGIN` … `OLD MANAGED BODY` … `END`, hand-written prose above
and below): the update is performed correctly — the marker hash advances
`6cd5cc61` -> `970c3bf2`, the 53-line body is replaced, the hand-written text
above and below is preserved byte-for-byte, and `--check` then exits 0
`(current)`. So the update path itself is sound; only the unterminated-marker
case is broken.

Expected behaviour: either repair the region (treat the orphan BEGIN as the
start of a zero-length body and append the END), or refuse with a non-zero
exit and a message naming the missing END marker. Reporting `✓ Updated` while
writing nothing is the part that costs the user time — a caller has no way to
distinguish it from success.

## Defect 2 — `-C` changes project resolution but not the target file

`bd -C <dir> setup claude --check` resolves bd config from `<dir>` but
resolves the file it inspects from the **caller's cwd**. Measured from this
repository's worktree:

    $ bd -C /tmp/.../sandbox/case-both setup claude --check
    ✓ Project hooks installed: /home/user/.../worktrees/agent-adcd876dffcae791f/.claude/settings.json
    ✓ Claude Code integration installed: /home/user/.../worktrees/agent-adcd876dffcae791f/CLAUDE.md (current)

Both reported paths are the caller's cwd, not `-C`'s directory. The verdict
also flipped to `(current)` for a file the same binary called `stale` one
command earlier, because the *config* came from `-C` (no `sync.remote` there,
so the expected hash is `6cd5cc61` rather than `970c3bf2`) while the *file*
came from cwd. A caller using `-C` gets a verdict about one project's file
computed against another project's config.

`bd -C` is documented as "like git -C", which would move both.

## Context for the report

The staleness itself is not a defect: the expected template hash is
conditional on `sync.remote`. Without a remote the template omits
`bd dolt push` and hashes `6cd5cc61`; with one it includes it and hashes
`970c3bf2`. A block installed before a remote was configured is therefore
genuinely stale afterwards, which is correct — it is only the repair that
does not work.

Filing venue: https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues
acceptance_criteria: An issue exists at github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues carrying both reproductions; its URL is recorded on this bead as --external-ref.

title: Item 13: SubagentStop hook verifies the worker's queue
description: Plan: docs/plans/beads-coordination-rollout.md item 13. SubagentStop fires when a subagent finishes and can block, so a hook can reject a false completion claim. This moves acceptance from 'the coordinator verifies testimony' to 'the harness refuses the claim' — which is what the whole verify-against-state-never-testimony apparatus exists for. It CANNOT detect a stall: a stalled subagent never finishes, so the hook never fires, and absence of an event is not an event.
design: Sketch: left=$(bd ready --assignee $AGENT_ID --json | jq length); busy=$(bd list --assignee $AGENT_ID --status in_progress --json | jq length); [ $left -eq 0 ] && [ $busy -eq 0 ] || exit 2. RISK WORSE THAN ITEM 12: a genuinely BLOCKED worker would be refused forever, so the bound must distinguish 'not done' from 'cannot proceed' — a blocked bead is not an incomplete one. Target file depends on D1.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A worker that stops with an open ready bead is refused; one with an empty queue is allowed.
- [ ] A worker holding a BLOCKED bead is allowed to stop — demonstrated, because this is the failure mode that traps an agent forever.
- [ ] The bound exists and was tested before the happy path.
- [ ] The file lives where D1 says.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.
notes:

Neither directory exists yet (measured: `ls plugin/` -> `skills` and `.claude-plugin` only), so this bead creates its own. Do not re-open D1 and do not put the file in .claude/ at the repository root.

The hook is a SECOND entry in the same plugin/hooks/hooks.json that agent-plugins-qozp.13 creates, on the SubagentStop event. qozp.13 lands first in this run; extend that file, do not replace it.

comments.author: dev-so39-2
comments.text: Files-clause audit (from agent-plugins-bbtl, which audits rollout items 6-14 and does NOT undefer this bead): item 13 had no **Files.** clause, and there is a reader/writer NAME mismatch in it. The sketch reads `$AGENT_ID` (`bd ready --assignee \"\$AGENT_ID\"`), but item 4 writes `BEADS_ACTOR` — `grep -rn 'AGENT_ID' plugin/` finds no writer of that name anywhere. So as written the hook reads an unset variable, `bd ready --assignee ''` decides the worker's queue, and the hook's verdict is meaningless rather than wrong-looking. comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text:
From agent-plugins-qozp.13 (item 12), which lands plugin/hooks/hooks.json first. Item 13's sketch has the SAME three measured wedge modes as item 12's, and the fix is the same shape.

1. `[ "$left" -eq 0 ]` returns exit 2 when $left is not a number, and 2 is the BLOCK code. Measured: `bash -c 'left=""; [ "$left" -eq 0 ]; echo $?'` -> `[: : integer expression expected`, status 2 (dash prints `Illegal number:`, also 2). So `bd` or `jq` missing does not degrade -- it wedges. Measured end to end: `PATH=/nonexistent` around the sketch exits 2.

2. Hooks are spawned by the harness, not by the coordinator's shell, so an eval'd `BB_*`/`AGENT_ID` assignment NEVER reaches the hook process. Item 13's $AGENT_ID has the same problem item 12's $RUN_EPIC does; reconciling the NAME with BEADS_ACTOR does not fix it, because the variable is not in that process's environment under either name. It has to come from disk, or from the SubagentStop payload (which does carry agent_id -- that is item 13's advantage over item 12, and worth using).

3. Unscoped queries are not empty. Measured: `bd ready --parent "" --exclude-type=epic --json | jq length` -> 60 on this tracker. An unset id makes the hook block on unrelated work forever.

plugin/hooks/bb-stop-ready-loop.sh (landed by qozp.13) is the pattern to copy: inert until armed, an on-disk consecutive-block counter that does NOT reset at its cap, fail-open on every path that is not 'armed and provably non-empty', and a --self-test that stubs bd on PATH so the bound is a regression test rather than a one-off demonstration. It is registered in sf.toml's script-self-tests check.

Note item 13's extra hazard, which item 12 does not have: a worker BLOCKED on something it cannot resolve must not be refused forever. `bd ready --assignee` excludes blocked beads, but `bd list --assignee --status in_progress` does not -- an agent that took the run-bead Blocked path leaves its bead in_progress or blocked with work uncommitted, and a naive busy-check reads that as 'not done'. Distinguish blocked from incomplete explicitly.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-6
comments.text:
retro:proof:agent-plugins-qozp.14 — the blocked-vs-incomplete distinction, which is the trap this bead exists to avoid, was MEASURED against a real tracker before the hook was written, not inferred from the bd help text.
evidence: one bead in a throwaway scratch database (prefix `scratch`, bd 1.2.2), assignee dev-blk, walked through four states. Columns are `bd ready --assignee dev-blk --json | length` and `bd list --assignee dev-blk --status in_progress --json | length`:
    open        -> ready=1 in_progress=0   REFUSE   (assigned, never started)
    in_progress -> ready=0 in_progress=1   REFUSE   (claimed, not finished)
    blocked     -> ready=0 in_progress=0   ALLOW    <-- the trap, avoided
    closed      -> ready=0 in_progress=0   ALLOW
  A blocked bead beside a second unstarted one: ready=1 in_progress=0 -> REFUSE. So a blocked bead never SOFTENS the verdict, it is merely invisible to it.
  An assignee that owns nothing: ready=0 in_progress=0 -> ALLOW.
  THE HAZARD, confirmed on the same tracker: an EMPTY assignee is not an empty queue.
    bd ready --assignee ""                        -> 3
    bd list --assignee "" --status in_progress    -> 2
  ...on a tracker where dev-blk itself held nothing. That is why the hook exits 0 rather than guessing when the payload carries no agent id.
NEGATIVE CONTROL on the self-test — four breakages in a copy, each caught:
  1. drained case no longer allowed (blocked treated as incomplete):
     FAIL a worker holding only a BLOCKED bead may stop (expected 0, got 2)
     FAIL empty lists also read as drained / FAIL drained restores it / FAIL and it blocks from zero again
  2. bound removed: FAIL blocks exactly MAX times, then stands down (expected 222000, got 222222)
  3. bound re-arms itself at the cap: (expected 222000, got 222022) and FAIL stays stood down (expected 00, got 20)
  4. the empty-agent-id guard disabled (`if [ -z "$agent" ]` -> `if false`):
     FAIL no agent id in the payload does not block (expected 0, got 2)
     FAIL an empty agent id does not query unscoped (expected 0, got 2)
     FAIL an unparseable payload does not block (expected 0, got 2)
  My FIRST attempt at breakage 4 was itself wrong and is worth recording: I replaced only the warn line inside the guard and left its `return 0`, so the self-test passed and I briefly read that as "the assertion cannot fail". The break has to remove the RETURN, not the message.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-6
comments.text:
retro:unverifiable:agent-plugins-qozp.14 — the hook reads the agent id from the SubagentStop payload, and I could NOT verify that the payload actually carries one. The prior comment on this bead asserts it does ("the SubagentStop payload ... does carry agent_id — that is item 13's advantage over item 12"), but that is prose with no transcript behind it, and nothing in this session can fire a real SubagentStop event to check.
Designed so that being wrong is SAFE rather than silent: the hook accepts any of agent_id / subagent_id / agentId / subagentId / agent, and when none is present it warns "the SubagentStop payload carried no agent id; not blocking." and exits 0. So if the field does not exist the hook is inert and says why on every subagent stop, rather than blocking or guessing. There is deliberately NO on-disk fallback: a single id on disk cannot say WHICH of several concurrent workers stopped, and an unscoped query is the measured 3-rows-and-2-rows hazard above.
WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: arm the hook in a real Claude Code session, dispatch one subagent, and read the warning on stderr when it returns — "carried no agent id" means the field is absent under all five spellings; a refusal or a silent pass means it was found. Cheaper: log the raw payload from the hook once.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-6
comments.text:
retro:decision:agent-plugins-qozp.14 — four choices a diff-reader would not recognise as choices.
evidence:
  1. BOUND IS 3, not the Stop hook's 8, and it is PER AGENT rather than per project. A coordinator can dispatch its way out of a non-empty ready front; a worker refused at its own stop cannot do anything except finish or declare a block, so a long budget is just a longer trap. Per agent because the state directory is shared: one wedged worker spending a project-wide budget would silently disarm the hook for every healthy sibling. The counter file is blocks-<slug-of-agent-id>, the id reduced through `tr -c A-Za-z0-9._-` because an assignee is agent-chosen text, not a filename.
  2. `--arm` TAKES NO ARGUMENT, unlike bb-stop-ready-loop.sh --arm <epic>. There is nothing per-run to store: the scope comes from the payload, per stop. Passing an epic would look like it scoped something and scope nothing, so it is a usage error (asserted in the self-test).
  3. count_json RETURNS 1 rather than 0 when it cannot count. Conflating "counted zero" with "could not count" is precisely how a hook blocks on a missing dependency: `[ "$x" -eq 0 ]` on a non-number exits 2, and 2 IS the block code. Each caller checks for non-digits and exits 0 with a reason.
  4. NOT USED: the `stop_hook_active` payload field. It exists to stop Stop-hook loops, but I could not verify its shape or presence for SubagentStop, and the on-disk per-agent bound is a stronger guard that does not depend on the harness telling the truth.
  TRIED AND REJECTED: reading the agent id from the environment (BEADS_ACTOR). The prior comment on this bead already measured why - hooks are spawned by the harness, so nothing the coordinator or the worker exports is in that process. Reconciling the AGENT_ID/BEADS_ACTOR name mismatch the earlier audit found does not fix it, because the variable is absent under either name.

title: Item 12: Stop hook that exits 2 while bd ready is non-empty
description: Plan: docs/plans/beads-coordination-rollout.md item 12. Stop can BLOCK — exit 2 continues the conversation. comments.text:
retro:proof the bound was built and tested BEFORE the happy path, with negative controls first.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS (the plan's sketch, run verbatim, three ways it fails CLOSED):

   bash: line 1: [: : integer expression expected

One assumption I checked and it was WRONG, so it is not in the design rationale: I expected `jq length` to ERROR on bd's empty-queue `null`. It does not -- `printf null | jq length` prints 0, status 0. The null hazard is real for consumers that index the result, not for a bare length. The hook still guards it (`if type=="array" then length else 0 end`) because non-array output must count as 0 in the fail-OPEN direction, which is a different reason than the one I started with.

THE BOUND, under a stub (plugin/hooks/bb-stop-ready-loop.sh --self-test, MAX=3, fake bd on PATH, temp state dir): 14 assertions, RESULT: PASS. The load-bearing one asserts the exit sequence over six consecutive turns on a queue that never drains is exactly 222000 -- three blocks, then it stands down -- plus 'stays stood down' (00) proving it does not re-arm itself.

THE BOUND, against the LIVE tracker (armed on agent-plugins-mpnf, which had 1 ready bead and was not dispatched between runs), ten consecutive invocations:
   turn 1..8 -> exit 2
   turn 9    -> exit 0
   turn 10   -> exit 0

comments.text:
retro:gap:agent-plugins-qozp.12 incident -- D1 settled WHERE the hook file lives and said nothing about how the hook LEARNS the run epic, and the bead's sketch assumed an environment variable that cannot reach it. I decided the arming mechanism, which is the substance of the item.

Evidence that the assumed channel does not exist: a hook is a process the harness spawns, not a child of the coordinator's Bash-tool shell, and this session's own environment note states shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist between tool calls. pre-flight-check.sh:855 emits `BB_EPIC` into a block the coordinator EVALs in its own shell (emitq BB_EPIC "$EPIC"), so that value exists in exactly the process the hook is not. Combined with the measured `bd ready --parent "" -> 60`, a hook reading an unset variable does not no-op, it blocks on the whole repository.

DECIDED: arming is a file on disk, written by `--arm <epic>`, read by the hook.
- Outside the working tree. state_dir() resolves ${BB_STOP_HOOK_DIR} else ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/bb-stop-ready-loop/<basename-of-project>-<cksum-of-project-path>. In-tree would have shown as an untracked change, and bb-close-bead.sh stages everything dirty in the worktree (`git add -A -- ':!.beads/*.jsonl'`), so the kill switch would be committed by the next bead's close.
- Keyed by project path so two projects on one machine cannot share a block counter.
- Absent state means INERT, not error. Every adopter of this plugin inherits this hook; D1 accepted that on condition of a documented fallback, and 'does nothing until a run arms it' is what makes inheriting it harmless.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED AND REJECTED:
- Have pre-flight-check.sh `export` the epic. Does not work at all -- same wrong process; it would have looked like a fix and shipped the wedge.
- Put the arming file at .beads/bb-run or the repo root. Costs an edit to .beads/.gitignore (bd-managed, and its own header warns against editing) or to the root .gitignore, and one missed adopter commits their kill switch.
- Derive the epic from `bd ready` repo-wide and block on ANY ready bead. This is what the sketch degrades to, and it is the trap: 60 ready beads here, none of them this run's.

COST OF BEING WRONG: arming is now a step someone must take, and nothing takes it. Filed as agent-plugins-89xd (discovered-from this bead) rather than left implicit.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text:
retro:stale:docs/plans/beads-coordination-rollout.md item 12's sketch (lines ~478-482) is not merely under-specified, it is wedge-prone as written, and item 13's (lines ~512-517) repeats the defect. Both were left unedited -- item 12's is superseded by the landed hook, and item 13's belongs to agent-plugins-qozp.14, which now carries the measurements as a comment.

Quoted, item 12:
    left=$(bd ready --parent "$RUN_EPIC" --exclude-type=epic --json | jq 'length')
    [ "$left" -eq 0 ] || exit 2

Three ways that blocks when it should not: $RUN_EPIC unset makes the query repo-wide (measured: 60 ready beads); `bd` or `jq` absent leaves $left empty and `[` exits 2, which IS the block code; and nothing writes $RUN_EPIC into a hook's process in the first place -- the prior audit comment on this bead already established that grep -rn 'RUN_EPIC' plugin/ returns zero hits, and pointed at pre-flight-check.sh, but pre-flight emits into the coordinator's shell, not the hook's.

The plan's own risk paragraph says 'a Stop hook that ALWAYS exits 2 is an infinite loop'. The measured failure is worse and differently shaped: it exits 2 on MALFUNCTION, so the bound is necessary but not sufficient -- failing open on every non-affirmative path is the part the plan does not name.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text:
retro:environment two facts a hook author in any repo will hit.

1. A Claude Code hook does not inherit the coordinator's Bash-tool shell. This session's environment note states it directly ('Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist'), and hooks are spawned by the harness besides. Consequence for this project specifically: EVERY BB_* fact pre-flight-check.sh emits (SCRIPTS, BB_EPIC, BB_EVENT_LOG, BB_CHECKS_IDS, ...) is invisible to hooks and monitors. Any harness-integration item that reads one has to get it from disk instead.

2. Plugin hooks and monitors are AUTO-DISCOVERED at the plugin root -- hooks/hooks.json and monitors/monitors.json need no key in plugin.json (an explicit path may be given as experimental.monitors). Monitors are a bare ARRAY, not an object with a 'monitors' key, they run through a shell so ${VAR} expands, and each entry takes an optional "when": "always" | "on-skill-invoke:<skill>". Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference, fetched this session. Hook entries take "timeout" (Stop default 600s) and receive JSON on stdin including stop_hook_active and last_assistant_message; exit 2 blocks, any OTHER non-zero is a non-blocking error and the stop proceeds. Source: code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.

Not used, and worth knowing why: stop_hook_active looks like a ready-made bound but only distinguishes 'first stop' from 'continuing because a hook blocked', so it caps the loop at exactly one block. The on-disk counter gives a settable budget and survives the hook process, which is what a run needs.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text:
retro:tooling the worktree-isolation guard on the Bash tool refuses any compound command it cannot statically prove stays inside the worktree, and 'compound' includes command substitution and for-loops that touch no paths at all. Refused this session:

  export BEADS_ACTOR=... ; bd update <id> --set-metadata ... (a for-loop over two bead ids)
  git merge-base --is-ancestor "$(git rev-parse <branch>)" HEAD
  for i in 1 2 3 ... ; do ./plugin/hooks/bb-stop-ready-loop.sh; done

Error text each time: 'this command is too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree. Refusing to run it -- split it into plain, separate commands'.

Cost: the sprint-batch D1 base-ref check (`git merge-base --is-ancestor "$(git rev-parse {BRANCH})" HEAD`) is written as exactly the shape that gets refused, so it had to be done in two calls and compared by eye. The ten-invocation bound demonstration had to be written to a file in the scratchpad and run as `bash <file>`, which works and is the reliable workaround, but nothing says so. Both are worth a line wherever the skills give copy-pasteable multi-step shell.

title: Item 11: merge beads and the merge slot replace the merge-queue prose
description: Plan: docs/plans/beads-coordination-rollout.md item 11. A merge bead depending on every bead whose branch it lands becomes ready exactly when its inputs are done — the documented fan-in. The merge slot is already a waiter queue: acquire --wait registers and returns (metadata {holder, waiters}), so a waiter polls its position rather than holding a process open.
design: A merge bead per batch, assigned to merge-<run-id>, depending on every bead whose branch it lands; the merge agent holds the slot across the merge. Optionally register merge-request as a custom type: 'bd config set types.custom merge-request' works (the 'not a recognized config key' warning is misleading) and the type behaves as a task for segregation, which is what a fan-in bead needs — but it lives in LOCAL config, so it is a per-clone setup step and a clone that has not run it cannot create or filter those beads. If that is unacceptable, use task plus a label. KNOWN LIMITATION TO DOCUMENT, NOT FIX: the slot is repository-wide and branch-unaware, so concurrent runs on different branches contend. Live with it; record contention if it appears.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A merge bead per batch, assigned to the merge agent, depending on that batch's beads.
- [ ] The merge-queue prose in references/worktree-mechanics.md is replaced by the bead + slot mechanism.
- [ ] The custom-type decision is made and recorded, including the per-clone caveat if adopted.
- [ ] The branch-unaware slot limitation is documented where a reader will hit it.
- [ ] Demonstrated: a merge bead is absent from bd ready until both its inputs close, then present and assigned to the merge agent.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.
notes:
GROOMING DECISION (plan-mpnf, run agent-plugins-mpnf) — the custom-type option is CLOSED, so this bead carries no open decision. USE `task` PLUS A LABEL (`merge`). Do NOT run `bd config set types.custom merge-request`.

Reason, and it is precedent rather than a fresh judgment: the bead itself measures that a custom type lives in LOCAL config, making it a per-clone setup step, and that a clone which has not run it cannot create or filter those beads. D1 (agent-plugins-qozp.12, CLOSED) settled the same trade-off for hooks on the stated ground that portability is what this repository vends. A mechanism that silently degrades on a fresh clone fails that test the same way.

The third acceptance box therefore reads: RECORD this decision and its per-clone rationale where a reader of the merge mechanism will hit it. It is no longer "make the decision".

comments.author: dev-mpnf-5
comments.text:
retro:proof:bd-merge-slot the DESIGN claim about --wait is true, and there is a fourth behaviour beside it that nothing in the corpus carried. Measured, not inherited.
evidence, same scratch database:
  `bd merge-slot create` -> "Created merge slot: demo-merge-slot"
  as merge-demo: `bd merge-slot acquire` -> "Acquired"; `bd merge-slot check` -> "Merge slot held: demo-merge-slot / Holder: merge-demo"
  as other-agent: `bd merge-slot acquire --wait` -> RETURNED IMMEDIATELY with "Slot held by merge-demo, added to waiters queue (position 1)". It registers; it does not block. So a waiter polls its position rather than holding a process open, exactly as the bead said.
  slot bead metadata at that moment: {"holder": "merge-demo", "waiters": ["other-agent"]} — and NO branch field, which is the evidence for the branch-unaware limitation below.
  NEW: as merge-demo, `bd merge-slot release` -> "Released"; the slot bead then read status "open" with metadata {"waiters": ["other-agent"]}. RELEASE DOES NOT PROMOTE A WAITER. The waiter must re-acquire, and its entry in the list is an advertisement of intent, never a grant. Documented as a fourth measured behaviour in worktree-mechanics.md; a reader who assumed hand-off would wait forever.

retro:environment:bd-merge-slot the slot is repository-wide and branch-unaware, and this is now evidenced rather than asserted: there is one slot bead per project prefix (demo-merge-slot) and its metadata carries only holder and waiters. Two runs on two different branches therefore contend for it although their merges could not collide. Documented as a KNOWN LIMITATION to live with — the cost is a wait, never a wrong merge — with an explicit instruction not to work around it by creating a second slot, which would make `bd merge-slot check` ambiguous for every reader.

title: Item 10: gates for authorization; the deferred-review channel
description: Plan: docs/plans/beads-coordination-rollout.md item 10. A human gate removes a bead from bd ready until resolved and restores it on resolve (measured both directions). decision-required is ALREADY GONE repo-wide, so this bead does not include retiring it.
design: Authorization becomes a real bd gate create --type=human on a task child of the scope epic (item 7). Add the deferred-review channel: an agent that wants a human to look at a decision later files a bead labelled human under the review or report ceremony epic. Measured asymmetry — absent from bd ready (the run never dispatches it, so it does not interrupt work) but PRESENT in bd human list from the moment it is filed (a human can answer whenever). bd human respond closes it, releasing the late phase. Three channels result, separated by when the run consumes the answer: authorization (blocks at the start), incident (recorded, never blocks), deferred review (blocks only at the end).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] sprint-scope creates the authorization gate against a task child of the scope epic.
- [ ] run-bead documents how a worker files a deferred decision (human label, parented to a late ceremony epic).
- [ ] sprint-report surfaces open human beads before the report is handed over.
- [ ] The three-channel table is documented in one place.
- [ ] Demonstrated: the human bead is absent from bd ready and present in bd human list; bd human respond releases the late phase.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: three documented channels plus a demonstrated gate; the mechanics are already measured in the bead

comments.author: dev-mpnf-5
comments.text:
retro:proof:bd-ready--assignee batch completion is a query, and BOTH halves are load-bearing. Demonstrated in a throwaway scratch database, not this tracker.
evidence: plan3.json created three tasks under one target, all assignee=dev-demo-1, chained w2<-w1 and w3<-w2 (from_key waits for to_key).
  start           -> bd ready --assignee dev-demo-1 --json = [demo-6q1];  in_progress = []
  close two       -> ready = [demo-2nm];                                  in_progress = []      (batch UNFINISHED)
  third claimed   -> ready = NULL/EMPTY;                                  in_progress = [demo-2nm]
  close the third -> ready = NULL/EMPTY;  in_progress = [];  blocked = []                        (batch FINISHED)
The third row is the one that settles the design: `bd ready` documents itself as excluding in_progress, so a bead being worked RIGHT NOW empties the ready front. The ready query alone reports a live agent as finished. Hence the pair, plus a third read of --status blocked to tell drained-clean from drained-with-a-block. `bd ready --json` returned the string null rather than [] on the empty rows, which is why sprint-cleanup.sh json_empty accepts both.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-5
comments.text:
retro:decision:plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh a worktree is matched to its owner through its CHECKED-OUT BRANCH, not through a stored path. This is what let metadata.worktree go without losing the mapping.
Measured: `git worktree list` prints the current branch per registration, not the one it was created with - this worktree shows [qozp.9] after `git checkout -b qozp.9`, having been created on worktree-agent-ac75f3c478449e42c. title: Item 8: collisions as edges; delete the wave table and sprint-wave
description: Plan: docs/plans/beads-coordination-rollout.md item 8. bd ready already returns the complete ready front, so a wave is a decision to freeze it, dispatch, wait for all of it, and re-query — strictly worse than dispatching continuously, because the slowest bead holds up everything that became ready behind it. LABEL THE POLICY EDGES: a collision edge is a policy expressed as a dependency, which is the conflation this design rejects elsewhere — mark them so a reader can tell them from real dependencies. comments.text:
retro:decision:plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md how a collision edge is marked, and how a batch survives the removal of waves. Two choices a diff-reader would not see as choices.
(1) MARK: metadata.collision on BOTH endpoints, valued as the shared surface (e.g. c4_changes:auth-service). Chosen because it is the only carrier measured to survive the load (see the unknown-field proof). A blocked bead whose collision value matches its blockers was separated by policy; one with no mark, or a mark differing from its blockers, has a real dependency. Ambiguity remains where a real dependency happens to run between two beads on the same surface - stated as a limit rather than papered over.
(2) BATCH: a collision cluster is CHAINED (N-1 edges in a line), not fanned, and the whole chain takes ONE assignee. The assignee groups the batch, the edges order it, and bd ready --assignee returns its head. Alternative considered: fanning every bead in a cluster off one head - rejected, it leaves the rest of the cluster ready simultaneously, which is exactly what the collision edge exists to prevent.
