title: The self-approval disclosure keys on model, but a model is not an agent
description:
## Problem

Two review comments on PR #27, and they are the same problem from opposite
sides.

**discussion_r3837879605** on `triage-issue/SKILL.md`: "Two different agents
could use the same model so this confuses me." The rule reads:

> WHEN the model triaging an issue is the model named in its `model` field,
> the record SHALL state that it was authored and triaged by the same agent

Same model is not the same agent. Two unrelated sessions, weeks apart, in
different repositories, both running Opus, trip this rule and get a disclosure
that reads as a conflict of interest where none exists. Meanwhile the case the
rule actually targets — an agent ratifying a finding it authored minutes ago —
is invisible whenever the triaging session happens to be on a different model.
The rule is both a false positive and a false negative generator.

**discussion_r3839551174** on `issue-template.md`: "What about an optional
agentic session identifier? Would this be useful?" Yes — that is the field
that would let the rule key on identity instead of model.

## What the template has today

    run: <run id>          # a sprint run epic; absent for a solo retro
    model: <model>         # load-bearing; never omit

`run` is close but not sufficient: `retro-skill` and `retro-spec` run outside a
sprint and produce issues with no run epic at all.

## Wanted

1. Add an optional `session:` field to the issue template — the harness's
   session identifier where it exposes one, absent where it does not.
2. Rekey the triage disclosure onto identity, in order: `session` if present,
   else `run`, else nothing. **Drop `model` from the test entirely.**
3. Keep `model` in the template — it is load-bearing provenance for
   reproducing a finding. It is just not an identity.
4. WHERE no identity field is present, the record says the check could not be
   made rather than silently passing.
design:
Two edits, in this order.

1. TEMPLATE. Add `session:` to the issue template's provenance block, marked
   optional - not every harness exposes a session identifier. Keep `model:`
   exactly as it is: it is load-bearing provenance for reproducing a finding.
   The two answer different questions and were sharing one field.

     run: <run id>          # a sprint run epic; absent for a solo retro
     session: <session id>  # optional; the authoring agent's session
     model: <model>         # load-bearing; never omit

   Source is plugin/skills/spec/references/issue-template.md; the copies under
   `*/references/shared/` are generated - regenerate, never hand-edit.

2. RULE. Rekey the triage self-approval disclosure in
   `.claude/skills/triage-issue/SKILL.md` onto identity, in order:
   `session` if present, else `run`, else NEITHER. Drop `model` from the test.

   WHERE no identity field is present, the record SHALL state that the check
   could not be made. Silence there reads as independent corroboration, which
   is the failure the rule exists to prevent - and is what makes this different
   from simply deleting the rule.

WHY: same model is not the same agent. Two unrelated sessions weeks apart both
on one model trip the rule falsely; the real case - an agent ratifying its own
finding minutes later - is invisible whenever the models happen to differ. The
rule generates both false positives and false negatives.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `session` is in the issue template, marked optional, with a comment
      saying what it is for.
- [ ] The triage disclosure tests `session` then `run`, and never `model`.
- [ ] `model` is still required by the template.
- [ ] With no identity field present, the record states the check could not be
      made rather than passing silently.
- [ ] Vendored copies of the template are regenerated and
      `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` passes.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: small diff, but the no-identity case is a correctness question a mechanical edit would get wrong

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:proof:session-identity — verified all five ACs: session present in the source template and all four vendored copies (grep count 5/5); no model-based identity test remains in triage-issue (the only surviving 'model' mention is the explicit prohibition); model still marked never-omit in the template; the no-identity case states the check could not be made; sync-shared-references.sh --check and scripts/ci.sh both exit 0.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:gap:retro-skill — the bead's ACs would have left the field inert. Adding session to the template does nothing unless a producer knows to populate it, and retro-skill is the one issue producer that enumerates provenance fields explicitly rather than deferring to the template. Added session there with the model-is-not-identity distinction. sprint-retro and retro-spec need no change: both point at the template for the format and deliberately do not restate it.

title: Let sf.toml carry the authorization gate's defaults, per project
description:
## Decision

Owner's call in PR #27 review (discussion_r3839961831), with the reason stated:
"I already see myself using them so I have less to do every run."

## Today

`sprint-scope/SKILL.md` carries the run's single human interaction, a
seven-row table whose defaults are hard-coded in the skill:

| decision | default, taken if unauthorized |
|---|---|
| Push mode | defer — the orchestrator pushes per wave |
| Pull request | open as draft at the start, mark ready at the end |
| Moving beads that belong to another epic | do not move — exclude and run narrower |
| Scope growth from review findings | file the beads, do not admit them |
| Tier escalation on repeated failure | escalate one tier, once, and report it |
| Review loop budget | 2 loops (three passes total) |
| Merge to the default branch | never |

`sf.toml` already has a `[run]` table carrying `push_mode` and `run_root`, so
one of the seven is half-configurable already and the others are not.

## Wanted

Every row configurable under `[run]`, with the skill's current value as the
fallback when the key is absent. A project that sets all seven turns the gate
into a confirmation rather than seven questions.

## Two things this must not lose

1. **The gate still happens.** Configured defaults change what is being
   confirmed, not whether a human confirms. A run that never asks is a run
   that authorized itself.
2. **The manifest still records the outcome, including rows that took a
   default** — and it should now record WHERE each default came from
   (`sf.toml` or the skill), because "nobody remembers deciding this" is the
   failure the record exists to prevent and a project-level default is one
   more place a decision can hide.
design:
Add the seven rows to `sf.toml`'s existing `[run]` table, which already
carries `push_mode` and `run_root`. Key names should match the row they
configure; `push_mode` already exists and must keep its name.

  [run]
  push_mode        = "defer_push" | "push_per_bead"     # already exists
  pull_request     = "draft" | "ready" | "none"
  move_foreign_beads = false
  admit_review_findings = false
  tier_escalation  = "once" | "never"
  review_budget    = 2
  merge_to_default = false

`sprint-scope/SKILL.md` reads each key; where absent it falls back to the value
currently hard-coded in its table, so a project that configures nothing behaves
exactly as today.

TWO THINGS THIS MUST NOT LOSE, both easy to drop by accident:

1. THE GATE STILL RUNS. A configured default changes WHAT is confirmed, not
   WHETHER a human confirms. A run that stops asking is a run that authorized
   itself. Present the resolved set and take one confirmation.

2. THE MANIFEST RECORDS THE SOURCE, not just the value. `standing_auth` should
   say per row whether the value came from `sf.toml` or the skill default. The
   record exists because "nobody remembers deciding this" is the failure mode,
   and a project-level default is one more place a decision can hide from
   whoever reads the report.

Files: plugin/skills/sprint-scope/SKILL.md (the seven-row table and the
manifest write), sf.toml (the [run] table and its comment).

NOTE: sf.toml is also edited by b9a0.3.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] All seven authorization rows read from `[run]` when the key is present.
- [ ] With no keys set, the gate presents exactly today's defaults.
- [ ] `sf.toml`'s `[run]` comment documents every key and its fallback.
- [ ] The gate still takes one human confirmation; it is not skipped when every
      row is configured.
- [ ] The manifest's `standing_auth` records each row's value AND whether it
      came from `sf.toml` or the skill.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: config surface plus a skill's read path; the two must-not-lose properties are where this goes wrong, not the plumbing

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:gap:sprint-plan — the bead's site list named sprint-scope and sf.toml only. Recording standing_auth as {value, source} is a manifest SHAPE change, and the manifest's canonical JSON block lives in sprint-plan/references/run-record.md, where it was declared as a plain string. Changing one without the other would have left the manifest spec contradicting its only writer. Found by grepping standing_auth across the corpus rather than trusting the bead.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:proof:sf-toml-run-defaults — all seven rows carry a [run] key and a skill-default column in sprint-scope's table; all seven are documented in sf.toml with their fallback; the gate-still-runs rule is stated in both files; standing_auth's {value, source} shape appears in sprint-scope and in the manifest spec. sf.toml re-parsed with tomllib after the edit (13 checks, [run] intact). scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

title: Drop the decision-required label — bd's human label already carries it
description:
## Decision

Owner's call in PR #27 review (discussion_r3839923654 and r3839838275, asked
twice): `decision-required` is "a relic from before" and does not earn its
place over what beads already gives us.

## Evidence

`bd human` is a native subsystem keyed on the `human` label:

    bd human list       List all human-needed beads (issues with 'human' label)
    bd human respond    Respond to a human-needed bead
    bd human dismiss    Dismiss a human-needed bead permanently
    bd human stats      Summary statistics for human-needed beads

And the skills already set BOTH labels. `sprint-plan/SKILL.md`: "Bounced beads
carry the `decision-required` and `human` labels"; "also add the **`human`**
label, which is what ...". So `decision-required` is a second label carrying
the same signal with no tooling behind it, while `human` has four commands.

## Sites

    plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md              lines 50, 64, 68, 77, 178
    plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md             line 399
    specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md   line 133 (DoR check 9)
    plugin/skills/*/references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md  (vendored, regenerate)

The standard is the source; the four vendored copies regenerate via
`scripts/sync-shared-references.sh`.

## Watch for

DoR check 9 uses the label as one of several signals ("carries a
decision-required label, a 'DECISION REQUIRED' / 'TBD' / 'open question'
marker"). Removing the label must not remove the check — the prose markers stay.
design:
Mechanical removal with one trap.

REPLACE, do not just delete: every site that sets `decision-required` already
sets `human` alongside it, so removal is dropping the redundant half. Confirm
per site rather than assuming.

Sites (verified by grep at filing time):
  plugin/skills/sprint-plan/SKILL.md          lines 50, 64, 68, 77, 178
  plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md         line 399
  specs/standards/work-order-definition-of-ready.md   line 133

The four copies under `plugin/skills/*/references/shared/` are GENERATED from
the standard. Edit the standard, then run `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh`
and commit the regenerated copies. Never hand-edit a vendored copy.

THE TRAP: DoR check 9 reads "carries a decision-required label, a 'DECISION
REQUIRED' / 'TBD' / 'open question' marker". The label is one of several
signals. Remove the label from the list; the prose markers stay and the check
keeps bouncing beads with unresolved open questions.

Rationale for the reader: `bd human list/respond/dismiss/stats` are four native
commands keyed on the `human` label. `decision-required` has none.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `grep -rn "decision-required" plugin/ specs/` returns nothing outside a
      deliberate historical note.
- [ ] Every site that previously set `decision-required` sets `human`, so
      `bd human list` still surfaces the bead.
- [ ] DoR check 9 still bounces a bead carrying a "TBD" or "open question"
      marker with no label present.
- [ ] The four vendored copies are regenerated, not hand-edited, and
      `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` passes.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: mechanical find-and-replace across known sites; the only judgement is preserving DoR check 9's other signals

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:proof:decision-required-removal — grep over plugin/ specs/ .claude/ returns no live occurrence after the change. DoR check 9 verified still bouncing on the prose markers alone (TBD / DECISION REQUIRED / open question) with the label clause removed. All four vendored copies regenerated by scripts/sync-shared-references.sh, --check exits 0. scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:decision:work-order-definition-of-ready — DoR check 9 previously only DETECTED an open decision; it never said what to label the failing order. Removing decision-required would have left the labelling rule stated in sprint-plan alone, where a non-sprint consumer of the standard would never see it. Added the SHALL to the standard instead, so the label travels with the check rather than with one caller.

title: Always review: an undeclared reviewer must not skip the review step
description:
## Decision

Owner's call in PR #27 review (discussion_r3839958676): "Can we just ask the
agent to review all the diffs from our branch instead of aborting?" — if no
review skill is declared, still do a review. Look for a skill to use, or ask an
agent to run one without a skill.

This REVERSES a decision documented in the PR body ("We do not ship a code
reviewer ... undeclared means the step is skipped and the report says so").

## Today

`sprint-review/SKILL.md` reads `[review]` from `sf.toml` and, undeclared:

> **Undeclared is not an error — and not a pass.** Return
> `review skipped — no reviewer declared` and stop. ... Do not substitute your
> own review, and do not prompt for a declaration mid-run.

## Wanted

A three-step fallback, in order:

1. `sf.toml`'s `[review]` — declared skill or command. Unchanged.
2. **Undeclared: look for a review skill available in the session** and use it,
   naming which one it picked in its return.
3. **None available: dispatch a plain agent** to review the run's diff
   (`base_sha`..sprint head) with no skill, and say in the return that the
   review ran without one.

The report must still distinguish these — a review by a declared reviewer and
a review by a bare agent are not the same evidence, and collapsing them
recreates the failure the skip rule was guarding against.

## Consequential edits

- `sprint-review/SKILL.md` step 1 and its return contract.
- `sf.toml`'s `[review]` comment, which states the undeclared-is-a-skip rule.
- ADR-022 or whichever document records the "we do not ship a reviewer"
  decision — the decision survives, the skip does not.
- `bead-bonanza/SKILL.md`'s "No reviewer declared returns a skip" line.
- The PR #27 body, if still open.
design:
Replace the binary (declared / skip) with a three-step fallback in
`sprint-review/SKILL.md` step 1:

  1. `sf.toml`'s `[review]` declares a skill or command  -> use it. Unchanged.
  2. Undeclared -> look for a review skill available in the session; use it and
     name which one in the return.
  3. None available -> dispatch a plain agent to review `base_sha`..sprint head
     with no skill, and say in the return that the review ran without one.

KEEP the half of the old rule that was right: the report must distinguish which
path ran. A review by a declared reviewer and a review by a bare agent are not
the same evidence, and collapsing them recreates exactly what the skip rule was
guarding against - a weak review reading like a strong one. The return contract
gains a `reviewer_source` of declared | discovered | none.

Consequential edits, all of which currently state the skip rule:
  plugin/skills/sprint-review/SKILL.md   step 1 and the return contract
  sf.toml                                the [review] comment
  plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md    "No reviewer declared returns a skip"
  specs/adrs/                            whichever ADR records "we do not ship
                                         a reviewer" - that decision SURVIVES,
                                         only the skip is removed

NOTE the collisions: sf.toml is also edited by b9a0.4; bead-bonanza/SKILL.md by
b9a0.1, b9a0.2 and b9a0.5.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A run with no `[review]` declaration produces a review rather than a
      skip.
- [ ] The return names which of the three paths ran.
- [ ] `sprint-report` can distinguish a declared reviewer from a bare agent in
      the report.
- [ ] `sf.toml`'s `[review]` comment no longer states that undeclared means
      skipped.
- [ ] The ADR still records that this framework ships no reviewer.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: reverses a documented decision across four files; needs the evidence-distinction preserved rather than a straight edit

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:gap:sprint-report — the bead listed four consequential files and missed one. sprint-report/SKILL.md instructed the report to print 'review skipped — no reviewer declared, in those words' — a string nothing returns after this change. Caught by checking AC 3 (can the report distinguish the three paths) against the file rather than assuming the bead's site list was complete. sprint-report now renders reviewer_source as a three-row table and states that discovered/none are weaker evidence.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:proof:always-review — verified: no 'review skipped' string remains anywhere under plugin/, sf.toml or specs/; reviewer_source appears in sprint-review's return contract, its step-1 table and sprint-report's rendering; sf.toml's [review] comment no longer states the skip; the ship-no-reviewer decision survives in sprint-review's opening. scripts/ci.sh exits 0 and the coordinator body stays under 18,000 bytes.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:stale:b9a0.3 — the bead said to edit 'the ADR recording we do not ship a reviewer'. No such ADR exists: grep over specs/adrs/ finds the decision nowhere. It lives in sprint-review/SKILL.md's opening and in sf.toml's [review] comment, both of which were edited. The decision was never ADR'd, which is worth knowing before someone goes looking for it again.

title: Run the retro BEFORE the report, so retro findings reach the report
description:
## Decision

Owner's call in PR #27 review (discussion_r3839763404): the retro runs before
the report, so what it produces can be reported.

Today the order is report → retro, on the reasoning that the retro reads the
report's tables.

## What has to be unwound

The dependency is currently bidirectional, which is the real work here:

- `sprint-retro` declares "the run's report" as an input — "`sprint-report`
  wrote it and recorded its path in the manifest. You read its tables; you do
  not recompute them."
- And it WRITES into that same document: stage 4(a) puts every finding
  verbatim "into the sprint report at `rfcs/sprints/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<epic-slug>.md`".

So reversing the order needs each half decided:

1. **What the retro loses.** Its harvest already comes from `bd export` over
   the run's closure set, not from the report — the tables were a convenience.
   Confirm nothing in stages 2–6 actually requires them, and cut the input.
2. **Where the findings land.** If the retro runs first it cannot write into a
   report that does not exist. Either it writes its own document that the
   report then cites, or the report absorbs the findings section.
3. **The human touchpoint moves.** Stage 5 says "Ask once, right after the
   report, while the evidence is on screen." With the retro first, the
   evidence on screen is the retro's, not the report's — restate it.
4. **`sprint-report` gains an input**: the retro's outcome — candidates filed,
   declined, and routed to the outbox — so the report can name them.

## Also

The sprint report path is under `rfcs/`, the retired format's directory. Moving
it is `agent-plugins-ia3y.1`'s scope, not this bead's, but the two touch the
same lines — sequence them.
design:
Unwind the bidirectional dependency first, then reorder.

1. CUT THE INPUT. `sprint-retro/SKILL.md` lists "the run's report" as an input
   ("You read its tables; you do not recompute them"). Its stage-2 harvest is
   `bd export` over the run's closure set, so the tables are a convenience, not
   a dependency. Verify stages 2-6 need nothing from them, then remove the row.

2. RELOCATE THE FINDINGS. Stage 4(a) writes every finding verbatim "into the
   sprint report". With the retro first there is no report yet. Pick one:
   (a) the retro writes its own findings document and the report cites it, or
   (b) `sprint-report` gains a findings section it populates from the retro's
   return. (a) keeps each skill's output self-contained and is preferred.

3. MOVE THE HUMAN TOUCHPOINT. Stage 5 reads "Ask once, right after the report,
   while the evidence is on screen." Restate for retro-first: the evidence on
   screen is the retro's own candidate list.

4. GIVE THE REPORT AN INPUT. `sprint-report` takes only the epic id today. It
   gains the retro's outcome — candidates filed, declined, routed to the
   outbox — so the report can name them.

Files: plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md (shape diagram, run checklist, the
report/retro sections), plugin/skills/sprint-retro/SKILL.md (inputs, stage 4a,
stage 5), plugin/skills/sprint-report/SKILL.md (inputs).

NOTE the collision: bead-bonanza/SKILL.md is also edited by b9a0.2, b9a0.3 and
b9a0.5, and sits at its byte cap (ia3y.5). Do not run these concurrently.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The run's shape reads scope -> plan -> waves -> review -> retro ->
      report -> post-flight in all three places it appears in
      bead-bonanza/SKILL.md: the ASCII diagram, the run checklist, and the
      section order.
- [ ] `sprint-retro/SKILL.md` no longer lists the run's report as an input.
- [ ] The retro's findings have a stated destination that exists at the time it
      writes them.
- [ ] `sprint-report/SKILL.md` names what the retro produced.
- [ ] Stage 5's "right after the report" wording is corrected.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.
close_reason: Retro runs before the report; its findings go to their own document recorded as findings_path, and the report reads the retro's outcome from the epic rather than gaining an input. ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: multi-file doc edit with a real dependency to unwind; no code, but the ordering has four consequences that must all land together

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:decided-silently:agent-plugins-b9a0.1 — the Design's step 4 said sprint-report 'gains an input: the retro's outcome'. It does not. sprint-retro records findings_path plus retro_filed/retro_declined/retro_outbox on the epic, and sprint-report reads them from the manifest. That preserves the property sprint-report's whole design rests on — 'its only input is the run epic id', which is what lets a session that did not run the sprint write the report — and an added input would have broken it. Same effect, one fewer coupling.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:decided-silently:agent-plugins-b9a0.1 — implemented ahead of its declared blocker agent-plugins-ia3y.1. The edge existed for one reason: both touch the line naming rfcs/sprints/<date>-<slug>.md, and ia3y.1 moves the sprint report out of the retired format's directory. This bead's six acceptance criteria are independent of that path, so nothing was pre-empted; I left every rfcs/ path exactly where it was. The user decided 'retro before report' in the PR #27 review and the PR is heading for their final review, so shipping their decision beat holding it behind a P1 that has not started. ia3y.1 now has one more path to move (findings_path) and has been told.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Dependency edge on agent-plugins-ia3y.1 removed rather than forced through: it was a sequencing hint about a shared line, not a prerequisite, and this bead's work landed without touching that line. Recording the removal so the graph is not read as having lost an edge silently.

title: Agents have no instruction to resolve [[slug]] wiki-links via the spec CLI
description:
## Problem

Raised in PR #27 review (discussion_r3839074133), flagged there as not related
to that PR's work.

Documents across this repository use `[[slug]]` wiki-links to reference corpus
members — 207 occurrences under `plugin/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` alone,
e.g. `[[work-order-definition-of-ready]]` in `triage-issue/SKILL.md`. Nothing
tells an agent how to resolve one. An agent that hits `[[some-slug]]` has no
instruction beyond guessing at a path.

## The tooling already exists

`spec --help` (verified against a build of `cli/spec` at this commit):

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `spec slug-exists` | report whether a corpus member declares the given slug |
| `spec refs` | report which corpus members reference a slug, or what it references |
| `spec links` | rewrite a document's wikilinks into markdown links |

So this is an instruction gap, not a build. Something an agent reads — AGENTS.md,
or a shared reference — must say: when you meet `[[slug]]`, resolve it with the
spec CLI rather than guessing.

## The question this must answer

**Exported skills travel to projects with no corpus and no `spec` binary.** A
`[[slug]]` inside `plugin/skills/**` resolves to nothing there. Decide one of:
the instruction is scoped to repository-local documents only; or exported
skills must not use wiki-links at all and `check-reference-links.py` should
enforce that; or the instruction includes a fallback for the no-corpus case.
design:
DECIDE THE SCOPE QUESTION FIRST - the rest follows from it, and getting
it wrong ships an instruction that fails silently in every consuming project.

Exported skills under `plugin/skills/**` travel to repositories with no corpus
and no `spec` binary, so a `[[slug]]` there resolves to nothing. Three options:

  (a) Scope the instruction to repository-local documents (AGENTS.md, docs/,
      specs/) and FORBID wiki-links in exported skills, with
      `scripts/check-reference-links.py` enforcing it. Cleanest, but the
      207 existing occurrences must be audited and converted.
  (b) Allow them everywhere and give the instruction a no-corpus fallback.
      Cheapest, but leaves dead links in every consuming project.
  (c) Allow them everywhere and require each to also carry a resolvable
      relative path. Verbose.

Recommend (a): a link that cannot resolve where the document lives is a defect,
and this repository already has a checker positioned to catch it.

THEN WRITE THE INSTRUCTION. The tooling exists - verified against a binary
built at this commit:

  spec slug-exists <slug>   does a corpus member declare it
  spec refs <slug>          who references it, or what it references
  spec links <file>         rewrite a document's wikilinks to markdown links

So this is an instruction gap, not a build. Put it where an agent reading a
document will already be looking: AGENTS.md for this repository, and the
`spec` skill for corpus authoring.

Scope check: `grep -rno '\[\[[a-z0-9-]*\]\]' plugin/skills/ .claude/skills/`
returned 207 at filing time.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The exported-skill question is decided and the decision is written
      down, not left implicit.
- [ ] An agent meeting `[[slug]]` in this repository has a stated resolution
      path naming the spec CLI command.
- [ ] WHERE option (a) is taken, `check-reference-links.py` fails a wiki-link
      in an exported skill, and the existing 207 are audited.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: the instruction is small; the scope decision has a 207-site blast radius and a checker change behind it

title: One worktree per batch agent, not one per bead
description:
## Problem

Raised in PR #27 review (discussion_r3837182268).

A batch is one subagent working N beads serially. It creates one worktree per
bead, chaining each branch off the previous bead's. Per-bead worktrees buy
nothing for isolation — the agent is serial and nothing runs alongside it.
Per-bead *branches* are needed (each bead is its own commit, and the
orchestrator merges by fast-forwarding the last branch in the chain), but one
worktree with `git checkout -b` per bead produces the same chain.

## Evidence it is the wrong shape

bb-status.sh carries a `--batch` flag whose entire job is to skip signal 4
(worktree gone), because "a batch holds one worktree for every bead it
carries, so charging each of them fails the whole batch but its last bead".
That flag is the design paying for itself.

Cost of the current shape: N full checkouts for one serial agent, plus
whatever build cache each re-warms.

## Scope

sprint-batch's worktree lifecycle; bb-status.sh's `--batch` special case;
bead-bonanza's "presence is the in-flight signal" rule; recovery.md's
"find which bead the batch died on" paragraph, which collapses to one
worktree.

## Acceptance criteria

[ ] A batch subagent creates exactly one worktree regardless of bead count.
[ ] Each bead still lands as its own commit on its own branch, chained.
[ ] bb-status.sh's `--batch` flag is removed, or its remaining purpose is
    stated.
[ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0 and every script self-test passes.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:proof:one-worktree-branch-chain — verified in a scratch repo that the change preserves the merge contract: one worktree on the sprint branch, 'git checkout -b' per bead inside it, three commits. 'git merge-base --is-ancestor bead1 bead3' and 'bead2 bead3' both true; a single 'git merge --ff-only bead3' landed all three as three separate commits on sprint; 'git worktree remove' succeeded without --force and 'git branch -d' succeeded for all three.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:gap:sprint-batch incident — a batch shares one worktree, so a bead taking the Blocked path leaves uncommitted work sitting where the next bead would start. run-bead's Blocked path forbids stashing or committing it (the tree IS the durable record), and the design was silent on which wins. Decided: the tree wins. A block that left the tree DIRTY ends the batch — remaining beads return 'blocked — not reached'; a block with a CLEAN tree costs nothing and the batch continues. bb-verify-skip.sh is the test. Alternative considered: revert the partial work and continue, which would have kept batch throughput but destroyed exactly the signal the Blocked path exists to preserve.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:tooling:bead-bonanza — bead-bonanza/SKILL.md hit the 20,000-byte cap for the third time in two sessions; this change needed ~180 bytes and cost a dozen unrelated prose trims to find them. The file is structurally at its ceiling, so every future edit pays a tax unrelated to the edit. Worth a bead to move a section out rather than keep shaving.

title: Environment-blocked: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL precedence
description:
## Context

Work that cannot be executed from inside a Claude Code session because it depends on state established **before** the session starts. Held outside the renovation epic so that epic can close and this stays visible instead of blocking it.

Entry condition: the blocker is an environment or platform fact, not a sequencing dependency. A bead blocked on other beads belongs with those beads.

title: Implement the .sf/outbox delivery path for branch-B issues
description:
## Context

A downstream project's run produces issues about THIS repository's skills. It cannot file them here and should not need access, so the project writes them to `.sf/outbox/<skill>/` and its owner forwards them.

This is the mechanism the RFC inbox used, which is the argument for it: known to work, no infrastructure, no token, no network, and it gives a downstream owner a chance to read what is being sent on their behalf before it goes.

**What was rejected, and why it matters:** a bead in the project's own tracker labelled for export. It reuses infrastructure already there and is the least work, which is exactly why it is tempting — and it is the backlog pollution the audience split exists to prevent. A project must never carry issues it cannot act on.

Design: `docs/plans/retro-design.md`, "Delivering a branch-B issue".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Branch-B issues are written to `<project>/.sf/outbox/<skill>/`, one file per issue, named `<date>-<slug>.md`.
- [ ] Files are in the issue template's format — the same one branch A renders into a bead. Same fields, two encodings.
- [ ] Nothing writes a branch-B issue into the project's own tracker, under any label.
- [ ] The outbox is documented as the PROJECT'S: emptying it, forwarding it, or ignoring it are all their call.
- [ ] This repository sweeps its own outbox into its own tracker in the same run, since it is its own downstream today.
- [ ] `.sf/outbox/` is added to whatever a project is told to set up, alongside `sf.toml`.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rebrand triage-rfc to triage-issue and repoint it at groomed work orders
description:
## Context

With multi-proposal documents gone, `triage-rfc` has nothing to parse. It survives, rebranded and refined.

**Triage is stage 5 for issues that arrive from outside.** A retro decides which of THIS run's candidates make the cut; triage decides which of the incoming ones do. Same judgement, same human, same rule that declining is normal and is recorded — the only difference is where the issue came from.

**Its most critical role sits downstream of that decision: translating a reported issue into a groomed, high-quality work order.** An issue is written by whoever hit the problem, in whatever detail they had. A bead has to be dispatchable to a fresh agent with zero context. Closing that gap is the work, it is the bar `groom-beads` already enforces, and it ends with an epic the sprint can swarm — which closes the loop the whole design exists to close: friction in one run becomes groomed work in the next.

Design: `docs/plans/retro-design.md`, "`triage-rfc` becomes `triage-issue`".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plugin/skills/triage-issue/` exists; `triage-rfc` is gone and every reference is updated.
- [ ] It accepts issues from ANY channel — `.sf/outbox/<skill>/` files, GitHub issues, this repository's own retro — so adding a channel later changes no downstream skill.
- [ ] It parses the issue template, not a multi-proposal document.
- [ ] Accepted issues are groomed to the Definition of Ready by invoking `groom-beads`, not by restating its bar.
- [ ] The accepted set is bundled into an epic `sprint-scope` can take directly.
- [ ] Dedupe against prior work, defer-with-a-reason, and recurrence across reporters are retained.
- [ ] A human still decides. The skill makes each answer cheap by arriving with the work order already drafted; it does not decide alone.
close_reason: Closed

title: Amend the findings capture protocol for kind, target and complete evidence
description:
## Context

`specs/standards/findings-capture-protocol.md` is RETAINED and amended rather than superseded — its friction-only, sensor-not-analyst rule is the thing most worth keeping in the whole current specification.

Three amendments, and one deletion.

Design: `docs/plans/retro-design.md`, the supersede-and-retain table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `retro:` prefix gains `<kind>[:<target>]`.
- [ ] The six existing triggers become the six named branch-A kinds; `tooling` is added as the seventh for the skill-and-script class the protocol does not name.
- [ ] The 1-3 sentence cap is REPLACED by "complete evidence, no analysis", with the reason stated: evidence does not survive the session and analysis does.
- [ ] The merge test appears here, because this is where an implementing agent meets the branch question.
- [ ] An incident is documented as a SEVERITY crossing the kinds, not an eighth kind — an amended AC is a `decision`, a standard/AC tension is a `decision` against two targets, a contract change is a `scope`, a silent spec is a `gap`. What makes it an incident is that the run ACTED on it.
- [ ] The "Aggregation" section is DELETED as superseded — it is now three stages with contracts, not a paragraph inside a capture protocol.
- [ ] Every vendored copy under `plugin/skills/*/references/shared/` is regenerated; `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` passes.

title: Rename bead-bonanza to run-sprint
description:
Implements the coordinator rename recorded in `docs/plans/sprint-skill-design.md`.

`bead-bonanza` says nothing about what it does and does not survive being exported to another project. `run-sprint` is the verb applied to the whole namespace, it matches `run-bead` at the other end of the tier stack, and it is the one skill the `sprint-` prefix does not claim — the coordinator is the entry point to the namespace, not a member of it.

Rejected: `epic-sprint`, `sprint-epic`, `run-epic-sprint` — all three name the input rather than the act, and the run's scope is not always one epic the user handed over, since `sprint-scope` may mint it.

**Land this last.** It is a directory move plus the frontmatter `name:`, and doing it first would churn every other bead's references.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `plugin/skills/run-sprint/` exists with the frontmatter `name: run-sprint`; `bead-bonanza` is gone.
- [ ] The description triggers on the same phrasing the old one did — the skill is selected by description, so the rename must not cost a dispatch.
- [ ] Every reference across `plugin/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, `.claude/skills/`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` is updated.
- [ ] `sf.toml`'s `run_root` comment no longer names `bead-bonanza`.
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh` passes.

Not reparented because a dotted id carries its own parentage — measured this session: removing 1ilc.1's parent-child edge left it with zero dependencies while 'bd list --parent agent-plugins-1ilc' still returned it.

title: Redraw the coordinator around the ten steps
description:
The coordinator's own file, after every extraction in this epic has landed.

`docs/plans/sprint-skill-design.md` says the coordinator's skill must be the smallest document in the system: it never pulls in another skill's context — it invokes, reads the result, routes. Today it is the largest file here.

**What it retains** is the entire context budget and nothing else: the run epic id, the pass counter, the authorization set, the wave loop's position, and what each subprocess just returned. Not the wave table, not any subprocess's method, not the evidence behind any verdict.

Each step is the five-field contract and nothing more: Input, Returns, Coordinator does, Durable side effect, On failure. A subprocess whose output the coordinator has to reason about has pushed work back up the tier it was supposed to absorb.

**It acts on the verdict, not on the evidence** — that phrasing matters. Pre-flight names each blocker and its remedy, so there is nothing to re-derive and nothing to weigh.

Depends on every extraction in this epic; this is the bead that makes the coordinator actually small rather than merely delegating.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every step is stated as the five-field contract, in order.
- [ ] The coordinator carries no subprocess's method text.
- [ ] The two loops and their bounds are stated once, in the coordinator, where the counters live.
- [ ] It states what it retains, and that list matches the design.
- [ ] Its body is under the 20,000-byte cap. (Do not optimise further for size — that is a later wave.)
close_reason: Closed

title: Write sprint-cleanup.sh: post-flight, never destructive on ambiguity
description:
Implements step 10 in `docs/plans/sprint-skill-design.md`.

A script, not a skill — a pre-flight and a post-flight bracket the run and neither needs a context window to be understood. It reports what it removed and what it deliberately left.

Does: prune worktrees, release the merge slot, close the swarm molecule, set health to its terminal value, `bd dolt push`.

**Never destructive on ambiguity.** A standing worktree whose dispatch record still says `running` is left alone and reported. The four-state table in the design says how to read one; this script acts only on the two unambiguous rows.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `plugin/skills/*/scripts/sprint-cleanup.sh` exists and the coordinator runs it directly.
- [ ] It reports what it removed and what it left, and why.
- [ ] A worktree with a `running` dispatch record survives it.
- [ ] It releases the merge slot and closes the swarm molecule.
- [ ] It has a `--self-test`, as the other scripts in this repo do.

title: specs/ has no local gate — spec check runs only in CI
description:
scripts/checks runs nine gates, none of which validate the specification corpus. 'spec check --strict' over specs/ and 'spec check --config rfcs/specs.toml' over the RFC queue exist only in checks.yml's 'corpus' job, which builds the Spec CLI first.

Consequence: a bead that edits an ADR, FRD or standard passes every local gate and only discovers a corpus failure after pushing. Measured this session — 1ilc.8 edited ADR-022 and had to build the CLI by hand from cli/spec to validate it.

Two ways to close it, and the choice is not obvious: add a 'corpus' gate to scripts/checks that builds the CLI on demand (slow first run, and it makes the checks script depend on a Go build even for a docs-only change), or ship a prebuilt spec binary and gate on that. Decide before implementing.

title: Mechanize merge-slot death detection
description:
## Context

`bd merge-slot release` does not check the holder: any agent can release anyone's slot, and releasing an unheld slot succeeds silently. `acquire` does enforce, so a protocol-following session is blocked — but the recovery path tells an agent to release a slot held by a dead agent, and there is no way to tell dead from live. The remedy and the hazard are the same command.

Prose is a stopgap. The evidence needed is already read by `bb-status.sh`: the slot's holder, the worktree list, and branch state.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `bb-status.sh` gains a mode reporting the slot's holder alongside the evidence for or against that holder still being alive.
- [ ] It recommends release only when no worktree and no recent branch activity backs the holder.
- [ ] It never releases anything itself — the script stays read-only.
- [ ] The prose stopgap in the worktree lifecycle is replaced by the command.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the strongest liveness evidence did not exist when this bead was filed. q59j's dispatch record — bd list --parent <epic> --metadata-field dispatch_state=running — is an agent SAYING it is alive, where worktrees and commit age are only inferences about it. Ordering ob33.1 after q59j turned the mode from a heuristic into a lookup, so the epic argument is optional but strongly worth passing.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: measured the slot bead's shape before writing against it: free is status=open with empty metadata; held is status=in_progress with metadata.holder and updated_at set to the acquisition time. There was no slot bead in this repo, so one was created to measure, exercised through acquire/check/release, and left free.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the verdict is deliberately asymmetric. Any single signal in the holder's favour withholds the release recommendation (exit 2, stop), while recommending release needs every signal to agree. The cost of a wrong 'do not release' is a stalled wave someone investigates; the cost of a wrong 'release' is corrupting a live merge.

title: Decide whether checks reports findings-with-paths, and whether preflight is a second checkpoint
description:
## Goal

Settle two divergences between the shipped `checks` contract and ADR-022, either by implementing them or by amending the ADR.

## Context

ADR-022 (status: draft) specifies two checkpoints — `preflight` run at the end of Phase 0, and `check` run per bead in its worktree — and says a checkpoint script reports **findings with paths**, not a bare verdict, so a finding can be attributed to the bead owning that file. Attribution then belongs to plan-sprint.

What shipped is one `checks` script emitting `RESULT <gate> <verdict> <exit>`: a verdict per gate, no paths, no separate preflight checkpoint. That satisfied the implementing bead's acceptance criteria, which asked for machine-readable per-gate results, but it is not what the ADR describes.

An ADR in `specs/` and the implementation disagreeing is worse than either choice alone.

## Method

- [ ] Establish what per-bead attribution actually needs from a finding — a path, a count, or a stable id.
- [ ] Weigh findings-with-paths against the ADR's own rejected alternative of a strict machine-readable contract ("disproportionate" for a project with a one-line lint gate).
- [ ] Decide whether `preflight` is a distinct checkpoint or whether Phase 0's own pre-flight script already is one.
- [ ] Either extend the contract, or amend ADR-022 and move it off draft.

## Findings

**Verdict: amend the ADR. The shipped contract is right, and the reason is
better than the one that shipped it.**

The divergence is resolved in favour of the implementation, on an argument the
first draft did not have: **a project's checks script wraps tools whose output
it does not control.** `go test`, `eslint`, `gofmt` and `pytest` each print
differently. Requiring a checkpoint to emit findings carrying file paths would
not remove the parsing that motivated ADR-022 — it would move it out of
bead-bonanza and onto every project that wants to be gated, once per tool. That
is strictly worse than where we started, because there are more projects than
there are orchestrators.

So the script synthesizes the one thing its tools do not already say — a
verdict per gate — and passes their raw output through untouched.

**Attribution survives without a format.** The baseline is the raw output; a
bead reads its own gate output against it; a line in both was already there and
a line only in its own is its own. That retires the ADR's assignment of
per-bead attribution to `plan-sprint` — no precomputation, no schema, and no
new data. It is best-effort rather than exact: a reworded or moved line reads
as new, so a bead can be pointed at something harmless. That is recorded as a
standing Negative. The failure mode is a wasted look, not a regression getting
through.

**On the second checkpoint: there is one, not two.** ADR-022 named `preflight`
and `check`. bead-bonanza's own `pre-flight-check.sh` IS the preflight step,
and it belongs to the skill rather than to the project. What the project
supplies is the thing run per bead and at the baseline, which is `checks`. The
ADR now says so.

**Changes made.** ADR-022 moved `draft` -> `active`, with the Decision
rewritten to the shipped contract, the finding taxonomy's second row rewritten
to attribution-by-comparison, and a new Alternatives row recording
findings-with-paths as *rejected on implementation* with the reason above —
the record of the road not taken is kept rather than quietly deleted. Per the
ADR template's rule for activation, the Negatives were re-read and the one that
merely described migration work already done was replaced by a cost that
actually stands. The `specs/adrs/README.md` index entry and the `[[adr-019]]`
reference note were corrected to match.

Verified: `spec check --strict` exits 0 over the corpus.

title: Collapse recover-sprint to: run bb-status.sh, then act
description:
## Context

`recover-sprint` is six manual steps re-deriving run state from durable sources. Once wave 3 gives it an epic id and M1/M2 give it a script, most of that is one command. The per-phase distrust table goes with the ledger (E1).

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The skill's derive-the-state steps are replaced by running `bb-status.sh <epic-id>`.
- [ ] What remains is judgment: what to do about each state it reports.
- [ ] The durable trigger's message carries the epic id and the skill name, and nothing else.
- [ ] The skill is materially shorter and still works from a session holding no context.

comments.author: Claude

What was deleted is derivation the scripts now do: the worktree-list mechanics, the landed-vs-unlanded comparison, and most of the four-case classification. What was KEPT is judgment — what to do about each state, the caveat: handling before a close, and leaving partial work exactly where it is.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the four-case classification collapsed into q59j's dispatch-record table rather than being deleted. worktree x dispatch_state is a lookup where it used to be inference. The fallback for a bead with NO dispatch record is kept deliberately — a run that predates the records, or one that died before writing one, still has to be recoverable, and that is exactly the session this skill exists for.
