Steps 0 and 3 had also come to overlap, both telling the reader to run the scripts. Consolidated: step 0 is the one command that needs no epic and no context, step 3 is the two that need the epic.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: the durable trigger's message contract was already satisfied by x5ix — progress-streaming.md now says the trigger carries the run epic id and an instruction to invoke this skill, and nothing else. No change needed for that AC; recording it so the AC does not read as unmet.

title: Dispatch from the re-queried ready front; swarm validate is a lookahead only
description:
## Context

MEASURED: the re-queried ready front is dependency-correct at any depth and across epic boundaries, and `bd swarm validate` is not.

On a run epic holding E1(a1, a2 after a1) and E2(b1 after a2, b2), `bd ready --parent <run> --exclude-type=epic` walked the DAG correctly: a1,b2 -> a2,b2 -> a2 -> b1 -> empty. The cross-epic edge released at exactly the right point.

`bd swarm validate E2` put b1 in Wave 1 and `bd swarm status E2` listed it as Ready with Blocked empty, because swarm scopes dependency analysis to the epic it is given, reports the outside edge as a warning, then computes as if it were absent. Running swarm per leaf epic does not fix this — it is where the wrong answer comes from.

`bd swarm validate` on a NESTED epic is also one level deep: it reports sub-epics as dispatchable work items and never sees their leaves.

## What to build

Dispatch reads the re-queried ready front, always. `swarm validate` supplies a wave PREVIEW for planning and reporting, valid only on a flat run epic with no cross-epic edges, and the skill must never dispatch from it. plan-sprint keeps its co-edit packing pass, which is a different question from dependency order.

Plan: docs/plans/wave-3-run-scope.md. Read it first — the measurements in it are settled and are not to be re-derived.
acceptance_criteria: The dispatch loop re-queries `bd ready --parent <epic> --exclude-type=epic` rather than consuming a precomputed wave list; `swarm validate` is used only to show a preview and is labelled as such; the skill states the two conditions under which the preview is unreliable (a nested run epic, and any cross-epic dependency edge) and suppresses or annotates it accordingly; plan-sprint no longer hand-rolls dependency ordering.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the useful distinction turned out to be ORDER vs PACKING, and neither document had drawn it. Dependency order lives in the graph and is read by re-querying the ready front at each wave boundary; plan-sprint decides only which simultaneously-ready beads can share a wave without colliding. Before this, plan-sprint read as though it owned both, which is why swarm validate looked like a replacement for it rather than a preview of half of it.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: gave the preview two explicit disqualifying conditions rather than a general 'be careful' — swarm validate warns about an outside dependency, or the run epic is nested. Both are checkable before use, and both were measured. A hedge an agent has to interpret is one it will interpret optimistically.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: added the reason a stored wave position is wrong, since 'the graph is the truth' alone does not motivate re-querying. Three concrete cases: a bead that closed early, a bead blocked by something discovered mid-run, and a bead admitted since the plan was made. The graph is right about all three and a stored list is wrong about all three.

title: Decide the finding taxonomy, inside T1's flow
description:
## Context

`docs/plans/retro-design.md` decides the taxonomy inside the flow: seven kinds, six lifted from the Findings Capture Protocol's existing trigger list plus `tooling` for the skill-and-script class it does not name, with `target` as the field that makes routing a lookup rather than a re-read.

**The design states plainly that the taxonomy is a proposal until this bead runs.** That is what this bead is for. Measured: across 240 findings the protocol's six categories are never recorded, so every retro re-derives each finding's kind by reading it cold.

Design: `docs/plans/retro-design.md`, "Template 1 — the finding" and its validation gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 73 findings in the 2026-08-15 report are classified against the seven kinds, and the residue that fits none is counted.
- [ ] Residue at or under 5% adopts the taxonomy as written; above 5%, the residue NAMES the missing kind and it is added. An existing kind is never widened to absorb it — a kind that absorbs anything routes nothing.
- [ ] The branch split of those 73 is recorded: how many are branch A, how many branch B. This is the first real measurement of what a run's friction is made of.
- [ ] `retro:<kind>[:<target>]` routing is verified mechanical given the kind — no finding's content had to be read to route it.
- [ ] The measured numbers are written back into `docs/plans/retro-design.md`, replacing the open item.
acceptance_criteria: Residue counted against the 73 findings; taxonomy adopted or extended by what the residue names; branch ratio recorded; the design doc no longer carries this as an open question.
close_reason: Gate run. All 73 findings in the 2026-08-15 report classified; working in docs/research/retro-taxonomy-validation/README.md, numbers folded into docs/plans/retro-design.md. The seven proposed kinds FAILED the 5% bar at 8/73 = 11.0%. Residue named two missing kinds cleanly: proof (4 findings recording how a claim was established) and environment (3 recording a dependency's behaviour), plus a corrects: <finding-id> template field for the one finding that superseded an earlier one. Recomputed residue with those added: 1/73 = 1.4%, passes. Branch split 60 A / 5 B / 7 neither. Routing verified mechanical given the kind, and correct about the BRANCH in all 65 classified cases — six were ambiguous between two kinds but all six pairs route to the same branch.

title: Wire sequencing constraints as real blocks edges at grooming time
description:
## Context

Where grooming determines that one bead must run after another — a `c4_impacts` intersecting another bead's `c4_changes`, or a stated prerequisite — that constraint currently survives only as a line of prose in the wave preview. A real `blocks` edge makes it enforceable by the tracker instead.

This matters more now that dispatch reads the re-queried ready front (agent-plugins-205x): an edge in the graph is honoured automatically, at any depth and across epic boundaries, where a prose note is honoured only if someone reads it.

MEASURED: `blocks` edges are type-segregated — task<->task and epic<->epic are allowed, task<->epic is refused in both directions. Sequencing between a task and an epic cannot be expressed this way.

Plan: docs/plans/wave-3-run-scope.md. Read it first — the measurements in it are settled and are not to be re-derived.
acceptance_criteria: Grooming writes sequencing constraints as `bd dep add` edges rather than prose; the wave preview derives from the graph instead of asserting order alongside it; the task/epic segregation is documented where an author would otherwise try to wire that edge.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the argument that makes this land is the one about ENFORCEMENT, not tidiness. Since dispatch now re-queries the ready front at every wave boundary, a blocks edge is honoured automatically at any depth and across epic boundaries, while an ordering noted in a wave preview is honoured exactly once — by whoever reads the table. That asymmetry did not exist before 205x, which is why the constraint could previously live in prose without obviously being wrong.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: recorded the task<->epic segregation at the point an author would hit it. bd refuses 'tasks can only block other tasks, not epics' in both directions, so a constraint between a bead and an epic cannot be an edge — and an agent that tries will leave a failed command behind and move on. The instruction is to record it on the epic and SAY it could not be wired, so it is not mistaken for one that was.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: my byte-delta print for groom-beads/SKILL.md read +0 because I printed len(s) after writing s.replace(...) without reassigning s. The file was correct; the measurement was not. Verified with wc -c and a grep for the new text — a self-reported number that costs nothing to check against the artifact should be checked.

title: Extend bb-status.sh with the epic-keyed checks
description:
## Context

Tier M-B: everything that needs a stable run handle, so it waits on wave 3. Once the epic IS the run, the whole checklist can be keyed by one readable id, which is what makes a restart cheap - a recovering session does not need to be told where it is, it runs one command and is told.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bb-status.sh <epic-id>` reports the whole run checklist.
- [ ] Plan structural validation: every queued bead appears in exactly one wave with tier, bucket and push mode resolved.
- [ ] Readiness gate as a check: `bd lint` clean, no open human item, tier metadata non-null across `bd ready --parent <epic>`.
- [ ] Dispatched-versus-returned reconciliation from M4's records.
- [ ] It distinguishes mechanical items it verified from agentic items it can only list.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: measured, and it changed the implementation twice: bd lint exits 0 even when it reports warnings — the findings are the verdict, the status is not, the same shape as gofmt -l. And bd lint has NO scope flag (only --status and --type), so it reports the whole tracker: a first cut reported '32 warning(s)' against a five-bead run, which is a false signal. Output is now intersected with the run's own queue.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the 'not verifiable here' list is the part worth keeping. A status script that reports only what it checked invites a reader to treat a clean report as a clean checklist. Naming the four agentic items — decisions surfaced before dispatch, implicit decisions recorded, escalations reported with reasons, the report's prose — makes the boundary explicit rather than implied by omission.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: scope note: the filed AC asked for 'plan structural validation — every queued bead appears in exactly one wave with tier, bucket and push mode resolved'. There is no stored wave table any more (agent-plugins-205x: the table is derived and returned, never written), so that check has no artifact to validate. What survives of its intent is checked instead: every ready bead carries a tier, which is the part dispatch actually cannot proceed without.

title: Implement the retro flow as sprint-retro: harvest, route, reason, decide, file
description:
## Context

`docs/plans/retro-design.md` specifies stages 2-6. This bead builds them as the `sprint-retro` skill, which wave 8 left blocked on the design and which the sprint orchestrator invokes after the report.

The stage boundaries are the design's, and they are load-bearing: **2 HARVEST and 3 ROUTE are mechanical and read no finding content; 4 REASON is where all judgement lives; 5 DECIDE is the single human touchpoint; 6 FILE is mechanical given 5.** A routing step that requires reading is a routing step that gets skipped on a 73-finding run.

Design: `docs/plans/retro-design.md`, "The six stages".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plugin/skills/sprint-retro/` exists and the sprint orchestrator invokes it by name, carrying none of its text.
- [ ] It runs on EVERY run, including one that closed nothing — a sprint that bounced its whole queue produced branch A's best material.
- [ ] Harvest uses `bd export`, never `bd list` plus `bd show --json`; a zero count across a DRAINED run is reported as a broken query, not a clean run.
- [ ] Routing is a lookup on the kind. Findings whose kind is missing or unknown are reported as UNROUTED with a count and a list, never dropped — that count is the taxonomy's own health metric.
- [ ] The report carries EVERY harvested finding verbatim, grouped by kind. It is the substrate recurrence runs on; a finding filtered out once can never be observed appearing twice.
- [ ] On top of it, N candidate issues in the issue template's shape, each naming the finding ids it rests on and its recurrence count.
- [ ] The human is asked ONCE, per candidate rather than per finding. Declining is recorded, not deleted, and the run does not block if nobody answers.
- [ ] Filing marks every finding a filed issue rests on with `retro:filed:<id>`, so recurrence stays bounded and the audit closes both ways.
close_reason: Closed

title: Wave 6 - Split SKILL.md into invoked skills
description:
## Context

Last, per the sequencing rule. By now waves 1-4 have shrunk, rewritten and partly replaced the phases, so the cut is smaller and better informed than it would have been first. This is what finally retires the compaction cliff and the defences built around it.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md` body is under 20,000 bytes.
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` exits 0 with no warnings.
- [ ] The KNOWN RED exception for `--strict` is removed from AGENTS.md's ledger.
close_reason: All children resolved. sixr (extract close-sprint) was superseded by wave 8, which split the report, retro and teardown into sprint-report, sprint-retro and sprint-cleanup.sh rather than one skill. hx4t closed with four of five ACs met — the compaction defences are gone and the document is in numeric order; --strict still reports one warning, for groom-beads, tracked as agent-plugins-1ilc.16.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: grooming correction: removed the epic-level dependency on agent-plugins-bmhe (wave 5). It was redundant and over-broad. The real constraint is precise and already wired at agent-plugins-sixr -> agent-plugins-f8sa: close-sprint extracts the RETRO, which wave 5 is redesigning. The epic edge propagated that block to agent-plugins-mbes as well, which extracts Phases 0/1/1.5 (pre-flight, queue, readiness gate) and has nothing to do with the retro. mbes is the half that actually shrinks SKILL.md, so blocking it on a retro design was pure cost.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Half of this epic is superseded by agent-plugins-1ilc.15, which implements docs/plans/sprint-skill-design.md. sixr is closed as superseded; hx4t remains and should follow 1ilc.15.14.

title: Observe CI with a gh:run gate, and stop asking the same question twice
description:
## Context

`BB_PR_CI` is measured at pre-flight and gates one question: whether to open a draft PR. But the shared-surface batch template asks the user the SAME underlying question - is a PR open so pushes trigger full CI, the 'slim gates' decision - without referencing the measured fact. So a run can ask twice, and the uninformed ask is the one that decides whether a batch skips its full suite. Separately, 'CI is the backstop' is asserted and never observed; `bd gate create --await gh:run:<id>` observes it without polling.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The slim-gates decision consumes `BB_PR_CI` rather than asking independently.
- [ ] Where a PR is open, the run observes its CI result through a `gh:run` gate rather than assuming it.
- [ ] `BB_PR_CI`'s meaning is stated precisely: it answers whether a draft PR would cause anything to run, not whether CI is healthy or a PR already exists.
- [ ] The substring-match limitation is recorded (a `pull_request` mention in a comment counts).

title: Add a health signal with bd set-state
description:
## Context

The one thing neither git nor bead status can express. A stuck agent, a degraded run, a wave that has stopped making progress - none of those are derivable, and all of them are what a watchdog needs to read. `bd set-state <id> health=...` writes an event bead AND maintains a lookup label in one atomic operation, and is documented for exactly this shape of use.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A health dimension is defined with a closed value set and a stated meaning per value.
- [ ] The orchestrator sets it; the durable trigger and any recovering session read it.
- [ ] A run that has stopped progressing is distinguishable from one that is merely slow.
- [ ] `bb-status.sh` reports it.
- [ ] S2's cost measurement is cited.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: found and fixed a defect in bb-status.sh's run mode, which I had shipped an hour earlier under kyyl. bd set-state writes an -typed CHILD of the epic on every health change, and the leaf walk counted any non-epic child as a bead — measured: an epic with two health events and zero beads reported '2 leaf bead(s) in scope'. The walk now skips type  and . asct is what would have triggered this on every real run.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: briefly mistrusted my own evidence line — bb-status.sh reported 'last commit: 8 hours ago' when I believed I had committed minutes before. The container clock had moved on across a session gap; git log %cr was right and my recollection was wrong. Worth recording because the whole point of printing the evidence beside the health label is that a reader can check the claim, and the first thing it did was correct me.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: measured (S2 / agent-plugins-wyun, cited as this bead's AC requires): bd set-state is cheap and does not churn — eight phase transitions on one bead took 5.1s (0.64s each), and the label REPLACES rather than accumulates, leaving exactly one label after all eight. That is what makes a per-wave-boundary health write affordable, and it is the opposite of the same spike's finding on event beads.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro (corrected — the original lost three words to shell backtick expansion): found and fixed a defect in bb-status.sh's run mode, shipped an hour earlier under kyyl. bd set-state writes an EVENT-typed CHILD of the epic on every health change, and the leaf walk counted any non-epic child as a bead — measured: an epic with two health events and zero beads reported '2 leaf bead(s) in scope'. The walk now skips issue types EVENT and MOLECULE. asct is what would have triggered this on every real run.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: note on tooling: bd comment invoked through a shell double-quoted string evaluates backticks. Pass comment text via a here-doc or an argv list instead — a comment that silently loses the identifiers it was written to record is worse than no comment.

title: Wave 5 - Rebuild the retro end to end
description:
## Context

Independent of waves 3 and 4. Starts with the end-to-end design, because a finding taxonomy decided before the flow it feeds is a guess. Per D11 the RFC path is partitioned by audience rather than retired: project-level findings become beads in the user's project; skill-level findings stay RFCs, because they are proposals about a product this repository vends to other projects.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] One document describes capture, harvest, classify, report, decide and file, naming who performs each stage and where its output lives.
- [ ] A bead-bonanza run's project-level findings reach a human as candidate issues, not as a document nobody triages.
- [ ] The audience split is explicit in `bead-bonanza`, `retro-skill` and `retro-spec`.
close_reason: All children closed except the RFC migration, deliberately moved to agent-plugins-gzcr. The retro is rebuilt end to end: docs/plans/retro-design.md specifies six stages; the capture protocol carries nine kinds validated against 73 real findings; sprint-retro implements harvest/route/reason/decide/file; the audience split is stated by the merge test wherever a finding is produced; the RFC format is retired for both branches in favour of one finding template and one issue template; .sf/outbox/ is the branch-B delivery path; and triage-rfc became triage-issue, repointed at groomed work orders bundled into an epic a sprint can swarm.

title: Several epics become one run via epic-of-epics adoption
description:
## Context

When the user names several epics, the run epic adopts THE EPICS, not their beads. Each keeps its own children, so no bead moves and no source epic is emptied of open work. Only the named epics gain a parent.

MEASURED: the queue is correct through the nesting — `bd ready --parent <run-epic> --exclude-type=epic` reaches leaf beads at any depth and respects cross-epic dependency edges. What degrades is the wave preview and the progress count, both recomputable, and neither is the dispatch mechanism (agent-plugins-205x).

## What this owns

- The confirmation: adopting root epics restructures the project's top level, so ask before doing it, and on decline leave those epics out of the run.
- The degraded-signal notice: say once that the wave preview and progress count are one level deep on a nested run epic.
- The cross-epic dependency edges `swarm validate` reports as warnings and nothing currently acts on.

Do NOT adopt the leaf beads instead — that empties the source epics and triggers the false-complete failure measured in agent-plugins-7vej.

Plan: docs/plans/wave-3-run-scope.md. Read it first — the measurements in it are settled and are not to be re-derived.
acceptance_criteria: Naming several epics produces one run epic whose children are those epics, with no bead reparented; the top-level restructure is confirmed before it happens and declining leaves those epics out of the run; the run states once that the wave preview and progress count are degraded; cross-epic dependency warnings from `swarm validate` are surfaced rather than dropped.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: this bead changed shape three times across the design discussion — filed as epic-of-epics, argued to won't-do when swarm turned out to be one level deep, then restored once the ready front proved to be the dispatch mechanism and the swarm signals only a lookahead. What settled it was separating 'the queue is correct through nesting' (measured, transitive, honours cross-epic edges) from 'the swarm signals are correct through nesting' (measured, they are not). Conflating those two is what made it look dead.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the load-bearing instruction is the negative one — adopt the EPICS, never their leaf beads. Adopting leaves would flatten the run epic and make every swarm signal exact, which is precisely the tempting wrong answer: it empties each source epic of open work and triggers the false-complete failure measured in 7vej.

title: Register the run with bd swarm create, and use swarm status as the live view
description:
## Context

`bd swarm create <epic>` registers the run and returns a swarm molecule id. `bd swarm status` is COMPUTED from beads rather than stored — its own help says "if beads changes, status changes" — so it tracks a scope that grows mid-run without re-registration.

**The swarm id is NOT the run id.** Measured: a swarm molecule is `issue_type: molecule` with no parent/child relations, and `bd ready --parent <swarm-id>` returns nothing. It links to the epic rather than owning it, and `bd swarm status` accepts the epic id too, so the epic remains the run's identity. See docs/plans/wave-3-run-scope.md.

## Measured constraints

- `swarm create` takes exactly ONE epic. Given a NON-epic issue it auto-wraps by creating an epic with that issue as its only child — a reparent. Never point it at a bare bead.
- It is **not** silently idempotent: a second call prints "Swarm already exists: <id>. Use --force to create another." A restart can therefore re-invoke it safely and recover the existing id from that message — but must not pass `--force`, which would mint a duplicate.
- The swarm molecule is **not ephemeral** and outlives the run. It needs an explicit close at run end or swarms accumulate.
- **`bd swarm list` reports CLOSED molecules under "Active Swarms"** — measured: a molecule closed by hand still listed, showing `Progress: 2/2 (100%)`. So `swarm list` alone does not answer "which runs are in flight"; each molecule's status has to be read. Report upstream (agent-plugins-1ilc.13).
- `swarm status` is one level deep, so on a nested run epic it reports sub-epics rather than leaf beads.

## What to build

Register the run epic once at start, recovering the existing id rather than forcing a duplicate on restart. Use `swarm status` as the live view where the run epic is flat; where nested, fall back to the re-queried ready front plus a walked progress count and say which is being shown. Close the molecule when the run ends.

Plan: docs/plans/wave-3-run-scope.md.
acceptance_criteria: A run registers its epic with `bd swarm create` exactly once and never against a non-epic id; a restart recovers the existing swarm id from the already-exists message rather than passing `--force`; the swarm molecule is closed when the run ends; the live view uses `swarm status` on a flat run epic and the ready front plus a walked count on a nested one, and the report names which it used; nothing treats `bd swarm list` output as proof a run is in flight without checking the molecule's status.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the two views needed separating explicitly, because they fail differently. bd swarm status is computed from beads — durable, correct after a crash, needs no re-registration when scope changes. The event log is a live stream for a Monitor to tail and is ephemeral by design. Conflating them is what let a dead event log read as 'the run has no record'.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: found a PRE-EXISTING defect, not introduced by this wave. progress-streaming.md documented BB_EVENT_LOG as 'exported by the pre-flight script'; pre-flight has never defined it anywhere — grepped the whole plugin, the only two mentions were both in that reference file. So the documented on_update hook appended to an unset variable, and since bd runs hooks fire-and-forget and ignores their exit status, the failure was silent: a run that reports nothing, with nothing saying why. Now emitted by pre-flight, with the export requirement and the silent-failure mode stated at the hook.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the event log's path had to move with $RUN_DIR. It is now ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bb-events-<epic>.log, and pre-flight probes writability and emits BB_EVENT_LOG='' when it cannot write — with the instruction to skip the hook rather than install one that silently fails, which is the failure mode above.

title: Design the retro end to end, before deciding any of its details
description:
## Context

The retro is currently specified in pieces across four skills and a vendored protocol, and its loop terminates in a queue: 240 findings across five sprints, 27 RFCs waiting. Design the whole flow once - capture, harvest, classify, report, decide, file - naming what each stage produces, who performs it and where the output lives. Everything else in this wave is decided INSIDE this design rather than ahead of it.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] One document covers all six stages end to end.
- [ ] It states the audience split (D11) as its organising principle.
- [ ] It names, for each stage, what is mechanical and what is agentic.
- [ ] It supersedes or explicitly retains each piece of the current specification.
- [ ] T2 and T3 are decided within it, not before it.
close_reason: Delivered as docs/plans/retro-design.md. All five ACs met: one document covers capture / harvest / route / reason / decide / file end to end; the audience split is its organising principle (branch A the project's own quality, branch B the skills this repo vends, separated by the merge test - who can merge the fix); every stage is labelled MECHANICAL, AGENTIC or HUMAN; every piece of the current specification carries an explicit supersede-or-retain verdict; and T2 (candidate issues) and T3 (the seven-kind taxonomy) are decided inside the flow rather than ahead of it. Beyond the ACs it also retires the RFC format for both branches, harmonises on one finding template and one issue template, decides .sf/outbox/<skill>/ as the branch-B delivery path, and rebrands triage-rfc to triage-issue. The taxonomy's validation gate against the 73 findings in the 2026-08-15 report is stated as unrun; 33by owns it.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Draft at docs/plans/retro-design.md (17 KB). Covers all six stages end to end, states the audience split as its organising principle, names what is mechanical vs agentic per stage, and gives every piece of the current specification an explicit supersede-or-retain verdict. Decides T2 (candidate issues, not RFCs, for the project audience) and T3 (seven kinds) inside the flow. NOT yet closeable: the taxonomy's validation gate against the 73 findings in the 2026-08-15 report has not been run, and four questions are open at the end of the document.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Harmonized on two templates; the RFC format is retired for BOTH branches, not only for project findings. Rationale is the format's own bookkeeping: retro-log.md line 7 counts per proposal because the proposal is the unit of decision, so an RFC is a document containing several issues. Summary/evidence/change/provenance carry forward into the issue template; the four workflow sections are dropped as a second copy of the tracker. Branch-B delivery mechanism is tabled with four candidates, none chosen, and is not blocking while this repo is its own downstream. triage-rfc's future shape is now an open question rather than a decided rescope.

title: Retire the compaction defences the split makes unnecessary
description:
## Context

Almost every defensive mechanism in the skill exists because 34.3% of it survives a compaction: the 're-read this file from Phase 0' instruction, the paragraph explaining why the document is ordered out of numeric sequence, the published script interfaces justified by 'an agent that must open a script to learn how to call it has already been sent to read it', and the KNOWN RED exception in AGENTS.md. Once the body fits, they are scaffolding around a removed constraint.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The re-read-from-Phase-0 instruction and the out-of-numeric-order explanation are removed.
- [ ] The document is reordered into its natural sequence.
- [ ] The KNOWN RED `--strict` exception is removed from AGENTS.md's environmental-failure ledger, and the gate-running instructions that work around it are simplified.
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` exits 0 with no warnings.
- [ ] Each retained defence has a stated reason that survives the split.
close_reason: Four of five ACs met. The re-read-from-Phase-0 instruction and the out-of-numeric-order explanation are gone; the document is in its natural sequence 1-10; the KNOWN RED entries in AGENTS.md and sf.toml are rewritten to name groom-beads as the only remaining case and to say they retire when it fits; each retained defence states a reason that survives the split. NOT met: 'check-skills.sh --strict exits 0 with no warnings'. bead-bonanza is now 19,983 bytes and under the cap - the warning it was filed about is gone - but groom-beads/SKILL.md is 23,071 bytes and is the last one over. That is a different file with its own reasons to be large; fixing it here would have been scope this bead was not given. Filed as agent-plugins-1ilc.16.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Wave 8 (agent-plugins-1ilc.15) is the split this bead cleans up after. Its compaction defences cannot be retired until 1ilc.15.14 has redrawn the coordinator around the ten steps, since that is what makes them unnecessary. No dependency edge: bd segregates blocks edges by type, so a task cannot depend on an epic.

title: Claim with bd update <id> --claim
description:
## Context

Ceremony step 1 runs `bd update <id> --status in_progress`, a non-atomic claim, and the skill then adds a 'never reset a claim you did not set' rule to cover the race. `bd update <id> --claim` is atomic - it sets assignee and status together and is idempotent if already claimed by you. Note this is NOT `bd ready --claim`, which claims the first ready issue matching a filter: a pull model for a worker choosing its own work, wrong for an orchestrator dispatching a named bead.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every dispatch template claims with `bd update <id> --claim`.
- [ ] The claim-reset rule is re-scoped to what atomicity does not cover, or removed if it covers everything.
- [ ] The assignee the claim sets is stated, since D2's dispatch record may want to use it.

title: Route the decision-required bounce through bd human
description:
## Context

A bead needing a human decision is bounced via a `decision-required` label plus a prose procedure. `bd human` is a first-class channel with list, respond, dismiss and stats, and `bd gate create --await human:<prompt> --timeout` blocks a step until a human answers. That turns the run's single decision point into a queryable state rather than a report line the user has to notice.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A bounced bead is raised through `bd human` (and/or a human gate), not only a label.
- [ ] The orchestrator surfaces the open human items at the point it currently prints the bounce list.
- [ ] A resolved human item re-enters the readiness gate without a full re-run.
- [ ] The interaction with the standing authorization is stated: a human item stops the chain, exactly as `decision-required` does today.

title: A run-level Definition of Done, computed correctly for flat and nested epics
description:
## Context

MEASURED: `bd epic status` counts DIRECT CHILDREN. On a nested run epic with four leaves all closed it read `0/2`, counting the two sub-epics.

MEASURED: `--parent` does not mean the same thing on both commands. `bd ready --parent` returns descendants at any depth; `bd list --parent` returns direct children only — against agent-plugins-1ilc it returned 10 leaf beads for an epic with 32 descendants.

So a transitive progress count has to be walked; neither command gives it directly.

## What to build

A run's Definition of Done: every admitted bead closed or explicitly accounted for (blocked with a reason, or excluded at admission). On a flat run epic `bd epic status` is exact and can be used directly. On a nested one, walk the tree.

Excluded beads are part of the DoD statement — a run that finished its admitted set while three beads sat out is done, and must say so rather than reading as complete over a scope nobody remembers narrowing.

Plan: docs/plans/wave-3-run-scope.md. Read it first — the measurements in it are settled and are not to be re-derived.
acceptance_criteria: A run reports a correct completion count on both a flat and a nested run epic; the flat path uses `bd epic status` and the nested path a walked count, with the mechanism named; the DoD covers admitted-and-closed, blocked-with-reason and excluded-at-admission, and a run whose scope was narrowed says so.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the DoD had to include the EXCLUDED set, not just the closed count. A run that finishes its admitted beads while three sat out at admission is complete over a narrowed scope, and reporting only 'all admitted closed' would read as complete over the scope the user originally described. Excluded beads are surfaced with their recorded reason.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: implemented as a new 'bb-status.sh run <epic>' mode rather than as prose, because the correct count cannot be expressed as a single bd command. bd epic status counts direct children (read 0/2 with four leaves closed on a nested epic); bd list --parent is direct-children-only; bd ready --parent is transitive but omits closed beads. Walking the tree is the only correct answer, so the script walks it and reports whether the epic was nested.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: caught myself reading the new mode's exit status through 'head -14' — the exact pipe trap AGENTS.md documents. It printed exit=0 for a run that had actually exited 1. Re-checked with a redirect. Worth recording because I wrote that rule into AGENTS.md earlier in this same session.

title: Extract start-sprint: pre-flight, queue and the readiness gate
description:
## Context

Phases 0, 1 and 1.5 are self-contained, run once each, and are precisely the part a compacted orchestrator cannot see - `head -c 20000` lands at line 349, before all three. They come out as one skill matching the existing plan-sprint / recover-sprint pattern.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `start-sprint` covers pre-flight, queue resolution and the readiness gate.
- [ ] It returns the facts the orchestrator needs and nothing else.
- [ ] Its body is under the 20,000-byte cap.
- [ ] `bead-bonanza` invokes it by name and no longer carries its text.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: extracted by SLICING rather than rewriting: the three phase sections moved verbatim into plugin/skills/start-sprint/SKILL.md, with a new frontmatter, an Inputs table and a What-you-return section written around them. A 16 KB rewrite would have been a second chance to introduce drift into text four waves of work had just settled.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: the scripts did NOT move. pre-flight-check.sh is bead-bonanza's, and start-sprint runs it via a {SCRIPTS} input — the same pattern run-bead already uses. Splitting a skill should not fork the scripts it invokes.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: 'this skill' was the subtle hazard in a verbatim slice. Five occurrences meant bead-bonanza and silently became start-sprint on the move, along with three cross-references to Phase 2.5/3 that now point across the split. Grep for self-referential phrasing after any extraction — the text compiles either way and reads plausibly wrong.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: three things had to move WITH the phases, because check-skills.sh enforces that a skill cites nothing outside its own directory. references/project-setup.md moved wholesale (it is entirely about setting a project up for a run). The GROOMING prompt template was split out of bead-bonanza/references/subagent-prompts.md into start-sprint/references/grooming-prompt.md — the per-bead and batch templates stayed, because the orchestrator dispatches those. And start-sprint was added to sync-shared-references.sh's map so it vendors work-order-definition-of-ready.md; 28 vendored references now current, 0 unmanaged.

title: Align bead metadata to bd's documented execution_* convention
description:
## Context

`bd`'s `docs/METADATA.md` defines a convention for exactly this data - `execution_agent_type`, `execution_suggested_model`, `execution_reasoning_effort`, `execution_parallel_group` - and states that orchestrator agents must consume these keys before spawning subagents. bead-bonanza and groom-beads invented a private vocabulary instead. Adopting the documented names makes a groomed bead portable to any orchestrator, and `execution_reasoning_effort` closes the `effort: unrecorded` hole in the manifest.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `groom-beads` writes the `execution_*` keys alongside `tier`/`tier_reason`.
- [ ] `bead-bonanza` and `plan-sprint` read them.
- [ ] The effort setting is recorded rather than written `unrecorded`.
- [ ] A migration path is stated for the 153 beads already carrying `metadata.tier`.

title: Wave 4 - Mechanize: three tiers, separated by precondition
description:
## Context

Mechanization is not one wave but three, split by what each tier depends on. Separating them keeps the checks that are scriptable today from waiting on the checks that need the epic pivot or the checks script.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Every checklist item the review classed mechanical is verified by a script, not asserted by an agent.
- [ ] `recover-sprint` collapses to 'run the status script, then act'.
- [ ] A run has a health signal and a dispatch record - neither exists today.
close_reason: All five children closed. Wave 4 delivered: the dispatch record (metadata, not event beads), the health dimension, merge-slot death detection, the epic-keyed checklist, and recover-sprint collapsed to running the scripts.

title: Give each subagent a first-class dispatch record
description:
## Context

The middle tier of the orchestrator -> subagent -> task hierarchy has no artifacts. A bead has a ledger, a branch, a worktree, a commit and a comment thread; a subagent has no id, no record, no lifecycle event, and no way to ask which agent is running and what it holds. That is why a batch holding one worktree for six beads breaks acceptance signal 4 and needs three paragraphs to disambiguate.

## The carrier is metadata, not event beads

D2 proposed two event beads per dispatch. The spike that gates this bead (agent-plugins-wyun) measured that as the most expensive of its three proposals by a wide margin: 100 event beads made `bd dolt push` 8.5x slower (0.63s -> 5.36s), and deleting them left it at 2.5x — Dolt is versioned, so the weight is PERMANENT and is charged to every future clone and bootstrap. A 12-bead wave would be 24 such beads.

The same spike measured metadata as the cheap carrier: nested objects and arrays round-trip intact, successive `--metadata` writes merge rather than replace, and a single 100,000-character value was accepted and read back at full length.

Decision (user, this session): carry the dispatch record as metadata on the bead being dispatched, plus a roll-up on the run epic. No new beads.

## Shape

On each dispatched bead: dispatch id, model, tier, worktree path, dispatch time, and terminal state written back on return. On the run epic: the set of live dispatch ids.

'Which agent is running and what is it holding' becomes `bd list --parent <epic> --metadata-field <key>=<value>`, which is a real query rather than a prose rule.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatch writes its record as metadata rather than as any new bead; the record carries dispatch id, model, tier, worktree path, assigned beads, dispatch time and terminal state; 'which agent is running and what is it holding' is answerable with one bd query; a standing worktree is disambiguated from the record rather than from a three-case prose rule; and the wyun cost measurement is cited where the carrier is chosen.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: SCOPE CHANGED by user decision. The filed acceptance said 'two event beads per dispatch (per D2)'. The spike that GATES this bead (agent-plugins-wyun) measured D2 as the most expensive of its three proposals by a wide margin: 100 event beads took bd dolt push from 0.63s to 5.36s, and deleting them left it at 1.56s — Dolt is versioned, so the weight is permanent and is charged to every future clone and bootstrap. A 12-bead wave would be 24 such beads. Carrier changed to metadata on the beads, which the same spike measured as cheap: nested values round-trip, successive writes merge, a 100,000-character value was accepted.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the payoff beyond the ACs is that the dispatch record RETIRES a prose rule rather than adding one. A standing worktree used to need three cases of interpretation; it is now a two-column lookup against dispatch_state — present+running is live, present+returned is an orphaned tree, absent+running is a dead agent. One dispatch_id per SUBAGENT rather than per bead is what makes the batch case fall out of the same table.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: measured, and it cost me two false negatives before I noticed: EPHEMERAL BEADS ARE INVISIBLE TO bd list. My first metadata-field probe and an earlier health-label probe both returned zero rows, and both were built on --ephemeral beads. bd ready has --include-ephemeral; bd list has no such flag. Any probe that verifies with bd list must use non-ephemeral beads.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: measured: the query this bead's AC requires does work. 'bd list --parent <epic> --metadata-field dispatch_state=running' returned the dispatched bead, as did the same query without --parent and 'bd ready --parent <epic> --has-metadata-key dispatch_state'. --set-metadata merges: five separate writes left all five keys present alongside grooming's own.

title: Review the 27 queued RFCs and decide each one's disposition
description:
## Context

27 RFCs in `rfcs/inbox/`, all `origin: self`. `docs/plans/retro-design.md` retires the RFC format for both branches, so **these are the last documents in it** — each is migrated as well as decided.

Verdicts are **per proposal, not per RFC**, because that was always the real unit: `rfcs/retro-log.md` line 7 says so itself. A single RFC may split across all three verdicts; that is the format's defect showing itself one last time, not an awkward edge case.

**Read the eight against the sprint skills first** — wave 8 restructured all of them and several propose changes to sections that no longer exist.

Design: `docs/plans/retro-design.md`, "The 27 queued RFCs".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every queued proposal is classified: superseded by this renovation, still wanted, or rejected.
- [ ] The merge test decides each still-wanted proposal's branch. Directory is NOT the signal — `rfcs/inbox/feature-blueprint/` holds proposals about the blueprint template (branch B) while some under `rfcs/inbox/frd/` are about this repository's own FRDs (branch A).
- [ ] Still-wanted proposals are rewritten as ISSUES in the new template and filed — branch A into the tracker, branch B here. Never both, and never left as an RFC.
- [ ] Superseded proposals are closed with a pointer to the bead that supersedes them.
- [ ] `rfcs/retro-log.md` records every disposition.
- [ ] The inbox is empty, or every remaining item carries a stated reason for waiting.

title: Extract close-sprint: report, retro and teardown
description:
## Context

Phase 4 is the other self-contained, run-once block, and it is the largest single section of the file. Its retro half is being rebuilt in wave 5, so this extraction should land after that design rather than carve up a section about to change.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `close-sprint` covers the final report, the sprint retro and teardown.
- [ ] It reflects wave 5's design rather than the current specification.
- [ ] Its body is under the 20,000-byte cap.
- [ ] `bead-bonanza` invokes it by name and no longer carries its text.
close_reason: Superseded by agent-plugins-1ilc.15. The design in docs/plans/sprint-skill-design.md does not extract close-sprint as one skill: the final report, the retro and teardown become three subprocesses with separate contracts — sprint-report (1ilc.15.11), sprint-retro (1ilc.15.10) and sprint-cleanup.sh (1ilc.15.12). Batching them behind one skill was the thing the design review rejected. Its blocker f8sa still gates sprint-retro, which now carries that dependency instead.

title: Serialize merges with bd merge-slot
description:
## Context

The merge policy is prose the orchestrator maintains: merge one at a time, `--ff-only` in a sequential wave, rebase-then-fast-forward for the second onward in a concurrent wave, and read the rebase target at merge time rather than earlier. That invariant broke in run 1786778523-19 - a rebase onto a stale target, then a branch deleted before re-checking, leaving the commit unreferenced and recovered from the object store. `bd merge-slot` is an exclusive lock with a priority-ordered waiter queue, built for exactly this.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The orchestrator acquires the merge slot before merging and releases it after.
- [ ] The slot is visible to every reader, so a held slot explains a waiting wave.
- [ ] The read-the-target-at-merge-time rule is expressed by the lock rather than by prose, or is retained with a stated reason why the lock does not cover it.
- [ ] A failure path is defined for a slot held by a dead agent.

title: Make the audience split explicit, by the merge test, in every skill that produces a finding
description:
## Context

`docs/plans/retro-design.md` makes the split its organising principle and gives it a test that survives identical wording: **who can merge the fix?** Lands in the project's own repository, branch A; lands in `agent-plugins`, branch B.

That test exists because prose cannot separate the cases. "The FRD template has no rule for X" and "our FRD has no rule for X" are the same sentence about different artifacts — the template ships from here, the FRD lives there. Only the merge question tells them apart, and it tells them apart every time.

**This repository is both audiences at once**, which is why the split has been invisible. A second project would have surfaced it on day one by accumulating, in its own backlog, proposals about skills it cannot change.

Design: `docs/plans/retro-design.md`, "Two branches" and "The test that separates them".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The merge test is stated in the capture protocol, where an implementing agent meets it at the moment of friction.
- [ ] `run-bead` names it, since that is where a finding is actually written.
- [ ] The sprint orchestrator, `retro-skill` and `retro-spec` each state which audience their findings serve and where they go.
- [ ] `retro-spec` is SPLIT per the design: findings about the spec templates and standards this repository vends are branch B; findings about a project's own FRDs, blueprints and ADRs are branch A.
- [ ] A downstream project using the plugin never accumulates issues about the plugin's own skills in its backlog. This is the requirement the whole split exists to satisfy.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add an epic-level Definition of Ready to groom-beads
description:
## Context

groom-beads has a per-bead Definition of Ready and nothing that says when an EPIC is fit to be a run's scope. With a run now keyed on one epic, that gap is load-bearing.

An epic-level DoR should cover: the epic has children; every child meets the per-bead DoR or is explicitly out of scope; dependency edges among the children are wired rather than implied (agent-plugins-67xf); and the epic carries whatever the manifest needs that is not derivable.

Flatness is a PREFERENCE, not a requirement. State what a nested epic costs — the wave preview and the progress count degrade to one level — and let the author choose. Do not make flatness a gate: the queue is correct either way, and requiring it would push authors toward moving beads out of their homes.

Plan: docs/plans/wave-3-run-scope.md. Read it first — the measurements in it are settled and are not to be re-derived.
acceptance_criteria: groom-beads carries an epic-level Definition of Ready distinct from its per-bead one; it names what a nested epic costs without forbidding it; a run can gate its scope against it the way it gates individual beads today.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: deliberately did NOT put this in references/shared/. That directory is vendored from the spec skill by sync-shared-references.sh, and the per-bead DoR is spec-owned; an epic-level DoR for bead-bonanza runs is groom-beads' own concern, so it lives locally. If it later turns out to be a spec-corpus concern, moving it means adding it upstream and re-syncing, not editing the vendored copy.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: first wrote the epic DoR inline in groom-beads/SKILL.md and pushed that file from 21444 to 23036 body bytes — it is the SECOND known-red size warning and was already over the cap. Moved it to references/epic-definition-of-ready.md and left a pointer, which is exactly how the per-bead DoR is already handled (spec-owned, vendored, cited by path). Net +791 instead of +1592, and the structure now matches its neighbour.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: the load-bearing sentence is why flatness is NOT required. An author told 'flat epics work better' will flatten, and flattening means moving beads out of the epics that own them — the false-complete failure measured in 7vej. So the reference states the cost of nesting (wave preview, progress count, both recomputable) and explicitly declines to gate on it.

title: Write bb-status.sh: the checks that need no preconditions
description:
## Context

Tier M-A. About 60 of the run's ~95 steps are orchestrator judgment expressed as prose, and the clearest case is the five acceptance signals: all five are pure git and `bd` queries, they run per bead every time, they have a documented failure taxonomy, they must not be reordered, and they are currently a numbered list an agent performs by hand. Run 1786778523-19 recorded two orchestrator conformance failures in one sprint - the kind of failure a script does not have.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bb-status.sh` verifies the five acceptance signals, the skip check, the landing check, report completeness and the findings-harvest non-zero assertion.
- [ ] Each line prints the verified state AND the command that established it.
- [ ] Per D1 it is run-level: the orchestrator runs it after each bead's acceptance check and at every wave boundary; a recovering session runs it first; a woken trigger runs it. A SUBAGENT NEVER RUNS IT - inside its own worktree the signals read differently by construction.
- [ ] Exit codes distinguish all-clear, a repairable failure and a stop-the-wave failure.
- [ ] The prose procedure it replaces is deleted, not left alongside.

title: Add a project config file for the model lineup and run defaults
description:
## Context

The `## model lineup` block in `AGENTS.md` is read as PROSE by the orchestrator to resolve tier to model. With N1 taking the gates, this is the last executable or routing fact parsed out of markdown. Note this is the project-level half only: per-bead tier metadata is N5's subject and a config file does not touch it.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A config file carries the tier-to-model lineup, and pre-flight emits it as a fact.
- [ ] Run defaults that are currently prose or asked-per-run move here where they are genuinely project-level (worktree root, default push mode, run root).
- [ ] The `## model lineup` block is retired from `AGENTS.md` and from `references/project-setup.md`.
- [ ] A project with no config file gets a stated, non-guessing fallback.

title: Adopt bd worktree if the spike says it earns its place
description:
## Context

Gated on S6. The bundled beads skill says always use `bd worktree`; this skill measured that `bd` already resolves the shared database through git's common directory, so the redirect configuration may be moot. Its removal safety checks may still earn it.

Plan: `docs/plans/bead-bonanza-renovation.md`. Review evidence: `docs/research/bead-bonanza-design/README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] S6 has reported and its finding is cited.
- [ ] Either the worktree lifecycle uses `bd worktree create/remove`, or the bead records why raw git remains correct here - with the measurement behind it.

title: spec feature --emit repeats the Rule: header once per scenario
description:
`spec feature <id> --emit` writes a fresh `Rule:` line before every scenario beneath a rule, instead of one `Rule:` line with its scenarios nested under it.

Reproduce on the corpus as it stands after agent-plugins-a7u:

  spec feature FEAT-SPEC-002 --emit

FEAT-SPEC-002 has five criteria under one `Rule: A build failure is the checker's job, not the indexer's`. The emitted file repeats that rule line five times. FEAT-SPECMD-002 shows the same for its two rules.

The output is still valid Gherkin and every criterion identifier survives, so no check fires and AC-GHK-009.1's tags/description/criteria all round-trip. What it breaks is structure: a consumer reading the emitted file sees five single-criterion rules where the source has one five-criterion rule, and AC-GHK-009.2 ("the extracted records equal those extracted from the source, except for their source location") is arguably violated for the rule grouping.

Renderer only — the parse and extraction sides are correct, and the FRD sources are correct. Found while writing the first Rule: blocks the corpus has ever carried.

Likely in cli/core/gherkin/render.go, which appears to emit each criterion's ancestry rather than tracking the rule already open.

title: The Dolt credential helper is global and unguarded, so it captures every private-repo clone
description:
Discovered while fixing agent-plugins-9v1.

`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`, in the block headed
`# --- 2a. Write access to refs/dolt/data ---`, installs a GLOBAL git
credential helper. The two lines to look for, inside the
`if [ -z "${AGENT_PLUGINS_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] ... else` branch:

    git config --global credential.helper \
      '!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo "password=$AGENT_PLUGINS_ACCESS_TOKEN"; }; f'

Three defects, all in that one snippet:

1. **No `[ "$1" = get ]` guard.** git invokes a helper for `get`, `store`
   and `erase`. This body ignores the operation and prints a credential
   for all three, so `store` and `erase` get answered with output git did
   not ask for.
2. **No host or path scoping.** It is registered on the bare
   `credential.helper` key, so it answers every credential request for
   every host with a PAT scoped to `brettcallaghan/agent-plugins`.
3. **No empty-token guard.** With `AGENT_PLUGINS_ACCESS_TOKEN` unset it
   emits `password=` and git authenticates as the empty string rather
   than falling through to another helper.

Defect 2 is the damaging one. `credential.helper` is multi-valued and git
tries helpers in the order listed, global before local, so this helper
WINS over any later per-clone helper. A clone of an unrelated private
repo therefore authenticates with the wrong identity, and GitHub answers
403 `Write access to repository not granted` — a write-shaped message for
a read that was never permitted.

That is what broke the `strata-lang/strata` clone for three days.
agent-plugins-9v1 fixed the symptom at the strata call sites by passing
`-c credential.helper=` FIRST to reset the list (see the `git clone
--filter=blob:none` invocation and the `config --replace-all
credential.helper ""` block later in the same file). Those resets stay as
defence in depth; this bead fixes the general defect, which will otherwise
capture the next private-repo clone the same way.

**Why this was not folded into 9v1.** The obvious remedy carries real
risk. Scoping the helper as
`credential.https://github.com/brettcallaghan/agent-plugins.helper`
depends on git's URL-context matching, and two things about it are easy
to get wrong: git compares the config key's path component against the
request's path, and `git remote get-url origin` reports the remote
WITHOUT a `.git` suffix while the URL git uses when talking to the server
may carry one. Get it wrong and the helper stops answering for this
repository's own pushes — which breaks `bd dolt push`, and CLAUDE.md
makes write access to `refs/dolt/data` a hard precondition of this
repository, with deliberately no JSONL fallback.

The failure is also LATENT: a broken helper does not fail anything in the
session that edits it (git config is already warm and the tracker already
reachable). It fails in the NEXT container, at hook time, after this
session is gone. So it must be verified in-session with the write probe,
not reasoned about.
design:
Two independent hardenings in `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`, both
required. Apply them in this order, because the first is risk-free and the
second is the one the probe is verifying.

## 1. Guard the helper body (no scoping risk)

Mirror the snippet the same file already uses for strata — search for
`STRATA_CRED_HELPER=` and copy its shape exactly, so the two helpers stay
recognisably the same construct:

    !f() { [ "$1" = get ] || exit 0; [ -n "${AGENT_PLUGINS_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] || exit 0; printf "username=x-access-token\npassword=%s\n" "$AGENT_PLUGINS_ACCESS_TOKEN"; }; f

That is the get-only guard and the empty-token guard, and it replaces two
`echo`s with one `printf` (an `echo` with a backslash in the value is
implementation-defined in `sh`). This alone fixes defects 1 and 3.

## 2. Scope it to this repository's remote

**Chosen approach:** derive the scope from `origin` rather than
hard-coding an owner/name, and register the helper under BOTH the
suffixed and unsuffixed forms of that URL. Registering both is what
removes the `.git`-suffix uncertainty instead of betting on it:

    _origin="$(git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null)"
    _origin="${_origin%.git}"
    git config --global "credential.${_origin}.helper" "$_helper"
    git config --global "credential.${_origin}.git.helper" "$_helper"

and REMOVE the bare-key registration, so nothing global answers for an
unrelated host:

    git config --global --unset-all credential.helper 2>/dev/null || true

Do not skip the unset. Leaving the bare key in place while adding a
scoped one changes nothing — the bare key still answers for every host,
which is the defect.

Handle the case where `origin` is not an https URL (an ssh remote yields
`git@github.com:...`, which is not a valid credential-config scope): when
`$_origin` does not start with `https://`, skip the scoped registration
entirely and leave `BB_DOLT_FATAL` set with a message naming the
unexpected remote form. An https credential helper is meaningless for an
ssh remote, and failing loudly is this block's established contract.

**Fallback, if the probe in step 3 fails after scoping.** Resolve it
mechanically, in this order; do not reason about git's matching rules:

1. Re-read the exact URL git used: `GIT_TRACE=1 git push origin
   HEAD:refs/dolt/write-probe-diag` and register that URL verbatim as a
   third scope. Delete the ref afterwards.
2. If that still fails, revert to the bare `credential.helper` key with
   the guarded body from step 1, and add an in-body path check driven by
   `git config --global credential.https://github.com.useHttpPath true`
   — git then feeds the helper a `path=` line on stdin, which the helper
   can compare against this repository's path without depending on
   config-key URL matching at all.

Both rungs leave the repository strictly better off than the current
state; do not leave the bead half-applied to avoid the fallback.

## 3. Verify in-session — this is not optional

Re-run the same probe the hook already runs, against the config you just
wrote (see `_probe="refs/dolt/write-probe-$$"` in the same block):

    git push -q origin HEAD:refs/dolt/write-probe-r19 && \
      git push -q origin --delete refs/dolt/write-probe-r19

It must succeed. Also re-run the whole hook end to end
(`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" bash
.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`) and confirm it still logs
`verified write access to refs/dolt/*` and does not set a fatal.

Note the hook is idempotent by design, so re-running it is safe.

## What NOT to do

- Do not remove the `-c credential.helper=` resets at the strata call
  sites. They are correct defence in depth and cost nothing.
- Do not write the token into a remote URL. The helper exists precisely
  so the PAT is never persisted to disk; a URL carrying it lands in
  `.git/config` and leaks into `git remote -v`.
- Do not relax `git config --global 'http.https://github.com/.proxy' ''`
  on the line below. That is a separate, load-bearing setting: the egress
  proxy substitutes a brokered token scoped to `refs/heads`, which 403s
  on `refs/dolt/*`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The global git credential helper installed by `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` answers ONLY for this repository's own remote; a credential request for any other host or path gets no answer from it.
- [ ] The helper body exits without output unless the operation is `get` (`store` and `erase` are answered with nothing).
- [ ] The helper body exits without output when `AGENT_PLUGINS_ACCESS_TOKEN` is empty or unset, rather than emitting `password=`.
- [ ] The refs/dolt write probe still passes against the new config: a push to a scratch ref under `refs/dolt/` succeeds and the ref is deleted.
- [ ] A full re-run of the hook logs `verified write access to refs/dolt/*` and sets no fatal.
- [ ] A clone of an unrelated private repo that supplies its own `-c credential.helper=...` authenticates with its own token, with no `-c credential.helper=` reset needed first.
- [ ] The strata call sites keep their existing `-c credential.helper=` resets (defence in depth, not removed by this bead).
- [ ] The PAT is still never written to disk — no token appears in any `.git/config` or remote URL.

title: Configurable floor on the corpus/empty rule
description:
The deleted scripts/validate-corpus.py carried MIN_CHECKED = 20: a floor on how many documents the check had to find. Its purpose was not "a document is wrong" but "the check is pointed at nothing and says so cheerfully" — the failure mode that let a stale docs/**/*.md glob report a healthy count for weeks while every document under the real root went unchecked.

The CLI's corpus/empty rule fires only at ZERO documents, so it catches "the root matched nothing" but not "the root matched suspiciously few". agent-plugins-92u deleted the script and accepted that narrowing rather than silently discarding the guard.

Second, narrower gap found while implementing 92u: the RFC-queue check runs with --only frontmatter/parse,frontmatter/schema,frontmatter/missing-property,slug/pattern-mismatch, which renders corpus/empty NOT-REQUESTED. So rfcs/ currently has no zero-document guard either — a rfcs/specs.toml whose root stopped matching would report "checked 0 documents / no findings" and exit 0.
design:
Give corpus/empty a configurable floor, defaulting to the current behaviour (fire at zero) so no adopting repository changes meaning.

Sketch, to be settled when the bead is groomed:
- a [conventions] key in specs.toml, e.g. min_documents, resolving from the active profile when absent
- the rule's finding message names both the configured floor and the observed count
- the floor is per-config, so specs.toml and rfcs/specs.toml can set different values

Also decide whether corpus/empty should be exempt from --only narrowing, or whether checks.yml's RFC step should simply name it in its --only list. The second is a one-word fix and does not need this bead; the first is a design question about whether a "did this run see anything at all" rule is a rule like the others.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] corpus/empty accepts a configurable floor, defaulting to the current zero-document behaviour
- [ ] The finding names the configured floor and the observed count
- [ ] The RFC-queue check in .github/workflows/checks.yml has a zero-document guard (either corpus/empty is exempt from --only, or it is named in the --only list)
- [ ] A test covers a root matching fewer documents than the floor
notes: Does not block agent-plugins-92u.

title: Move c4-guide into specs/standards and ship it, closing the 14th document
description:
## Problem

agent-plugins-eaa acceptance criterion 1 says "The 14 corpus-shaped documents
live under specs/ and are checked by spec check --strict". Only 13 moved:
agent-plugins-eaa.2 moved 8 standards and agent-plugins-eaa.3 moved 5 guides.

The fourteenth, plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md, moved in neither and
ships nowhere. It is absent from the MAP in scripts/sync-shared-references.sh
(grep "c4-guide" returns nothing), so no skill receives a generated copy of it.

It fell through a seam between three beads. agent-plugins-wu1 retyped it from a
guide to a standards document (frontmatter type: standards, slug: guide-c4 →
its standards slug) and moved its row in cli/profile/profile_test.go realSlugs
into the standards cluster. eaa.2 Design declined it explicitly ("it is not
[handled here]; guides are separate"), written before the retype landed. eaa.3
confirmed at start that it is standards-typed and therefore not among its 5
guides, and recorded the gap in a retro comment without filing this bead.

Until this lands, the eaa epic cannot be closed: its AC-1 count is 13 of 14 and
its "Each is vendored into every skill that needs it, from specs/ as the single
source" criterion is unmet for this document.

## Steps to confirm the gap

  find . -name c4-guide.md -not -path "./.git/*"
    -> ./plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md   (expected: ./specs/standards/)
  grep -n "c4-guide" scripts/sync-shared-references.sh
    -> no match                                       (expected: a MAP entry)
design:
Follow the standards move that agent-plugins-eaa.2 already performed,
exactly — the mechanism is established and this document is the last instance
of it, not a new pattern.

1. git mv plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md specs/standards/c4-guide.md
   (git mv so the move records as a rename, per AGENTS.md non-interactive rules).
2. Add a MAP entry in scripts/sync-shared-references.sh sourcing from
   specs/standards/c4-guide.md, repo-root-relative, in the same form eaa.2 used
   for the other 8 standards. Ship it to the skills that cite it — determine
   which by searching for citations rather than assuming; do not ship it to
   skills that do not cite it.
3. Run scripts/sync-shared-references.sh (no --check) to write the generated
   copies, then confirm --check exits 0. Generated copies carry the
   "GENERATED COPY — DO NOT EDIT" header naming specs/standards/c4-guide.md as
   source of truth; never hand-edit one.
4. Update cli/profile/profile_test.go realSlugs for the new path, as eaa.2 and
   eaa.3 both did for every document they moved, and cli/profile/profile.go doc
   comment if it names the old path.
5. Repoint any citation that breaks. Two failure shapes are already known from
   this epic: a bare-filename citation from a file that STAYS BEHIND breaks when
   the target moves (eaa.2 hit this with spec-cli.md), and a backticked relative
   path cannot be correct from both the authored location and a vendored
   shared/ copy one level down (eaa.3 hit this and converted the citation to a
   [[wikilink]], which is valid once the target is a corpus member). Prefer the
   wikilink form for the same reason.

Do NOT rewrite history in rfcs/retired/ or rfcs/inbox/ — wu1 and eaa.1 both
deliberately left matching slug strings there as point-in-time records. Two
files carry the literal string guide-c4:
rfcs/retired/rfc-0007-spec-architecture-templates.md and
rfcs/inbox/spec/rfc-self-greenfield-anchors-and-split-numbering.md. Leave both.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] specs/standards/c4-guide.md exists and plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md does not
- [ ] scripts/sync-shared-references.sh has a MAP entry for it, sourced from specs/standards/
- [ ] scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check exits 0
- [ ] Every skill that cites the document has a generated copy carrying the GENERATED COPY header naming specs/standards/c4-guide.md
- [ ] No authored (non-generated) copy of it remains under any skill reference directory
- [ ] cd cli && go test ./... passes, including cli/profile/profile_test.go realSlugs
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh reports no new findings beyond the known-red baseline
- [ ] spec check --strict exits 0 with the document in the corpus
- [ ] agent-plugins-eaa AC-1 now counts 14 of 14 documents under specs/
notes:
Tier: standard

completed, with the same two known citation-breakage shapes to check for; the

generated copy.

title: DOD: verify the Definition of Done, retire the blueprint, run retro-spec
description:
The feature's closing item. Traces to the Definition of Done section of
specs/features/markdown-links/markdown-links-blueprint.md. Delta key: DOD.

Not tied to a single delta: it is the backstop that verifies every delta landed
and every AC is cited, then retires the transient blueprint.

## Problem

A feature is not done when the code merges; it is done when the documentation
set is truthful again and every acceptance criterion is verified at its
declared level.

## Design

Work through the blueprint's Definition of Done, in order:

1. Every delta folded into its owning blueprint. Each delta item was supposed
   to do its own fold — VERIFY rather than assume:
     * specs/architecture/module-document-core.md — Components roster carries
       the Markdown Links record block and a Built paragraph; the component
       diagram carries its edges to References, Spans and Findings; the
       Findings section's FindingDetail vocabulary carries both new variants
     * specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md — the Command Surface
       command-tree paragraph names `links` as a sixth subcommand; the
       Container Context read-only statement is re-affirmed
2. Every AC in the coverage table verified at its declared level and cited from
   its tests per plugin/skills/spec/references/ac-traceability-standards.md.
   All 31: AC-SPECMD-001.1 through 006.3. Check the citations exist, not just
   that the tests pass.
3. Snapshot cases under cli/testdata/cases/ cover the `links` subcommand.
4. go test ./core/... and go test ./cmd/... pass; the profile self-application
   gate in cli/profile runs clean.
5. spec check --strict exits 0 over this repository's corpus.
6. Set the blueprint's status to `retired` and update updated_at. It is a
   transient document; nothing durable may live only in it.

No issue in Tracker Reconciliation is classified `subsumed`, so nothing needs
closing or re-scoping. All five (agent-plugins-eaa.1, eaa.2, 47b, nu2, a7m) are
out-of-scope and stay open.

Then run the `retro-spec` skill over the implementation phase, aggregating the
retro findings recorded on this feature's items:

  bd list --label feature-spec-markdown-links

Implementation is the phase that finally exercises the work orders, so this is
where their quality becomes evidence. The approved plan is the standing
authorization for this retro — no further prompt is needed. The RFCs it
produces remain human-gated at review.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every checkbox in the blueprint's Definition of Done is verified, not
      assumed
- [ ] All 31 ACs carry a test citation at the level the coverage table declares
- [ ] The blueprint's status is `retired`
- [ ] retro-spec has run and its RFCs are filed for human review

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
