title: CMD: the links subcommand
description:
Delta: "Command Surface in [[container-spec-cli]] (modified — links) — CMD",
specs/features/markdown-links/markdown-links-blueprint.md.
Feature blueprint slug: feature-spec-markdown-links. Delta key: CMD.

## Problem

Wiring only. Per container-spec-cli's Change Guidance no judgement lands here:
the subcommand converts flags into one call against Markdown Links and its
result into two streams and an exit status. A check that lived here rather than
in a module would be a layering defect, unavailable to a future API or MCP
wrapper.

## Design

Per the delta's Behavior:
  * a `links` subcommand taking exactly ONE operand, the repository-relative
    path of the markdown document to rewrite
  * an optional `--map` option naming a link map file; the subcommand runs
    without one
  * the rewritten document to STANDARD OUTPUT; every finding and the
    replacement count to STANDARD ERROR, so redirecting the document to a file
    does not capture the report
  * the replacement count is the number of citations rewritten
  * any error finding -> no rewritten document, exit 1
  * only warning findings -> the rewritten document IS written, exit 0
  * creates, modifies and deletes no file
  * an unreadable operand -> error finding, no rewritten document
  * opens the corpus WARM, as check, refs, slug-exists and next-id do
  * NO `--strict` option. Warnings exit zero unconditionally under
    AC-SPECMD-002.8, so the option would contradict the criterion rather than
    narrow it.
  * --help text derived from the same declaration that defines it
  * the one-line synopsis distinguishes it from `refs`: refs answers what cites
    what, links emits one document with its citations rewritten

Anchors: cli/cmd, the cobra command tree Execute builds; cli/testdata/cases/
for the snapshot cases, replayed by cli/cmd/snapshot_test.go.

## Acceptance

Proving (this item owes the test citation), all integration:
  AC-SPECMD-002.2  error finding -> no rewritten document
  AC-SPECMD-002.6  warning only -> document still emitted
  AC-SPECMD-002.8  warnings only -> exit zero
  AC-SPECMD-003.1  the replacement count reported
  AC-SPECMD-003.2  the count on a stream other than the document's
  AC-SPECMD-005.1  exactly one document per invocation
  AC-SPECMD-005.2  rewritten document to standard output
  AC-SPECMD-005.3  no file created, modified or deleted
  AC-SPECMD-005.9  unreadable map -> no rewritten document
  AC-SPECMD-005.10 an invocation naming no link map is accepted

Tests cite their ACs per
plugin/skills/spec/references/ac-traceability-standards.md.

Gates: go test ./cmd/...; the snapshot cases under cli/testdata/cases/. WHEN
observable output changes, run scripts/regenerate-cli-snapshots.sh and review
every resulting diff before commit. Note agent-plugins-krb: that script was a
no-op once already.

## Documentation

Fold this delta into its owning blueprint in THIS item: the Command Surface
component's command-tree paragraph in specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md
names `links` as a SIXTH subcommand (the prose currently says five, in more
than one place — check all of them), and the Container Context's read-only
statement is re-affirmed against AC-SPECMD-005.3.

## Verification timing

None. Every AC this item covers is proven by this item.

## Coordination

agent-plugins-47b (out-of-scope): it verifies that a committed markdown link
lands on a co-located file. This subcommand checks reachability at rewrite
time, which cannot guard what is already committed. 47b reads the rewritten
copies; it does not reimplement resolution.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.

title: MAP: read the YAML link map in the command surface
description:
Delta: "Command Surface in [[container-spec-cli]] (modified — map) — MAP",
specs/features/markdown-links/markdown-links-blueprint.md.
Feature blueprint slug: feature-spec-markdown-links. Delta key: MAP.

## Problem

The link map is caller-supplied file input, which is the Command Surface's
concern and not a module's, on the same rule that puts specs.toml there. It is
read the same way — every defect reported through finding.Report in one run,
never defaulted around — so a malformed map reads like every other
configuration defect.

## Design

Per the delta's Behavior:
  * a named link map is read as YAML: a mapping whose KEYS are slugs and whose
    value per slug is a mapping carrying a `path` string
  * every property of a record other than `path` is IGNORED, so the map can
    carry the caller's own per-document data (e.g. `destinations` for the
    copying script) without the CLI knowing what it means
  * decoded with a YAML parser, so a map written in JSON is accepted unchanged
  * unreadable, unparseable, or a record with no `path` -> finding, severity
    error, naming the file and the fault; and no map resolved
  * a slug appearing twice as a key -> a parse fault, never one silently
    winning
  * a `path` value is never interpreted, resolved or normalized

Example map, for copies that land beside each other:

  template-authoring-standards:
    path: template-authoring-standards.md
    destinations:
      - plugin/skills/groom-feature-blueprint/references/shared/

Anchors: cli/cmd, beside Load and the specs.toml handling it already carries;
goccy/go-yaml, already a module dependency (adr-015).

## Acceptance

Proving (this item owes the test citation), all unit:
  AC-SPECMD-005.4  the YAML mapping shape, keyed by slug, with `path`
  AC-SPECMD-005.6  properties other than `path` ignored
  AC-SPECMD-005.7  a JSON map accepted, JSON being valid YAML
  AC-SPECMD-005.8  unreadable map or missing `path` -> error finding

Participating (listed, no citation owed here):
  AC-SPECMD-005.9  proven by the CMD item

Tests cite their ACs per
plugin/skills/spec/references/ac-traceability-standards.md.

Gates: go test ./cmd/...

Fold this delta into its owning blueprint in THIS item: the Command Surface
component of specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md gains the link-map
reading beside its existing configuration-resolution paragraph.

this one. Code work may proceed as soon as this item is ready. The final
Definition-of-Done item is the backstop.

one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item

title: MDL: substitute markdown links over resolved reference spans
description:
Delta: "Markdown Links in [[module-document-core]] (added — rewrite) — MDL",
specs/features/markdown-links/markdown-links-blueprint.md.
Feature blueprint slug: feature-spec-markdown-links. Delta key: MDL.

## Problem

Producing the rewritten bytes. Every guarantee here is about what is NOT
touched: substitution replaces the exact extent each reference occupies and
copies everything else through, which is what makes AC-SPECMD-001.5's "alters
nothing else" and AC-SPECMD-004.1's idempotence the same property rather than
two.

## Design

Per the delta's Behavior:
  * a reference with a resolved target -> replace the whole [[...]] construct
    with a markdown link whose TEXT is the reference's text as written and
    whose TARGET is the resolved path
  * an anchor -> keep it in the emitted link's text, and append the derived
    fragment to the emitted target
  * copy through every byte no reference's span covers, unchanged
  * a reference with no resolved target -> copy its [[...]] construct through
    unchanged
  * no reference resolves a target -> emit the document byte-identical
  * report the number of references replaced
  * read and write NO file

Anchors: cli/core/mdlinks; cli/core/span for the extents replaced. A
reference's Position covers the text BETWEEN the brackets, so the construct's
extent is derived from it rather than rescanned.

Code-region exclusion (AC-SPECMD-001.4) is satisfied entirely by consuming the
References component's output — do not rescan the document and do not
reimplement the mask.

## Acceptance

Proving (this item owes the test citation), all unit:
  AC-SPECMD-001.1  wikilink -> markdown link with the settled path
  AC-SPECMD-001.2  anchor preserved in the emitted link's text
  AC-SPECMD-001.4  no rewrite inside a code span, indented or fenced block
  AC-SPECMD-001.5  nothing but the wikilinks altered
  AC-SPECMD-001.6  no rewritable wikilink -> document emitted unchanged
  AC-SPECMD-002.7  an unresolvable wikilink left exactly as written

design:
Per the delta's Behavior:

  * a reference with a resolved target -> replace the whole `[[...]]` construct
    with a markdown link whose TEXT is the reference's text as written and
    whose TARGET is the resolved path
  * an anchor -> keep it in the emitted link's text, and append the derived
    fragment to the emitted target

    unchanged

reimplement the mask — References locates code regions with goldmark because
where an inline code span ends depends on matching backtick-run lengths and
where a fence ends depends on its fence length and info string. A hand-rolled
masker getting either wrong produces exactly the false positive the exclusion
exists to prevent.

Idempotence (AC-SPECMD-004.1) and "alters nothing else" (AC-SPECMD-001.5) are
the same property: replace only the spans, copy the rest. A second run finds no
wikilinks and so emits its input unchanged; nothing special-cases re-running.

## Problem

One judgement decides, per citation, what a link points at or why it cannot.
Keeping it apart from substitution is what lets the two modes REQ-SPECMD-005
and REQ-SPECMD-006 describe share one substitution path, and it puts both
reachability findings in one place rather than spread across the rewrite.

## Design

This item introduces the new **Markdown Links** component of Document Core.
Its record block, to be added to the module blueprint's Components roster:

  title: Markdown Links
  slug: component-markdown-links
  description: Wikilink-to-markdown-link substitution and target resolution

Resolution rules, per the delta's Behavior — implement all of them:
  * map given AND slug in it -> target is the mapped path exactly as held
  * map given AND slug names a corpus document the map omits -> finding,
    severity error, rule id `links/unmapped`
  * no map -> target is the cited document's repository-relative path taken
    relative to the DIRECTORY of the citing document's own repository-relative
    path, with no other normalization
  * map given -> derive NOTHING for any slug (AC-SPECMD-006.3). A given map is
    never completed by derivation; that is what makes the map a statement of
    the shipped set.
  * slug names no corpus document AND no map entry covers it -> finding,
    severity warning, rule id `links/unresolved`, and no target resolved
  * every reference resolved in one pass, every finding reported
  * anchor -> target fragment by GitHub's heading-anchor rule: lowercase the
    anchor text, remove every character that is not a letter, digit, space,
    hyphen or underscore, replace each space with a hyphen
  * the citing document's repository-relative path comes FROM THE CALLER, not
    derived — so a document outside the corpus resolves the same way one
    inside it does

specmodel.Reference values consumed, including each one's Resolution;

title: Decide whether work-order joins the DocumentType vocabulary
description:
Raised by the PR #22 review comment on work-order-template.md
(https://github.com/brettcallaghan/agent-plugins/pull/22#discussion_r3781123944):
"It seems cheaper than this paragraph to just have a work-order type -- that's
the direction we're going anyway, even if work orders are immediately
transferred to beads."

This reverses the decision taken in agent-plugins-j5n, which removed `type`
from the template and added a 12-line "Non-corpus" paragraph ending "do NOT add
work-order to the DocumentType vocabulary".

## Measured cost, so the trade is visible

DocumentFrontmatter is additionalProperties:false and every type extends it, so
a WorkOrder struct must declare all 18 of the template's properties. Four are
inherited (title, description, slug, updated_at). Fourteen are new: kind,
priority, sources, delta, parent_slug, depends_on, blocks, discovered_from,
tier, tier_reason, est_size, c4_changes, c4_impacts, c4_docs.

Three need vocabularies that do not exist. schemas/ has Severity, CheckOutcome,
ExclusionReason, BlockFormat, DocumentType, RfcSeverity, Status, Visibility,
BlueprintKind, Delivery — and nothing for work kind (epic|feature|task|bug|
chore), tier (light|standard|advanced|frontier) or size (XS|S|M|L|XL).

At this repo's docstring density that is ~80 lines of .strata against the
paragraph's 12, plus profile registration in cli/profile/profile.go, plus
regeneration, plus dropping the NON_CORPUS entry in
scripts/check-template-drift.py, plus re-syncing two vendored copies.

Not an argument against it — schema the CLI enforces beats prose asking people
not to do something — but it is an addition, not a simplification.

## The blocking question: status

The template declares no `status`, and a subtype cannot opt out. Measured
against strata 0.7.0:

  469 |   status: Status?
      |   ---+--
      |      +---- Invalid redeclaration of ancestor property
      |            'DocumentFrontmatter.status'
      | Note: Inherited members cannot be redeclared in derived types.

So adding the type FORCES every work order to carry one of draft |
ready-for-review | approved | in-progress | active | retired — a second
lifecycle beside the bead's open / in_progress / closed, for the same unit of
work.

Proposed answer: `status` means the Definition of Ready and nothing else —
draft = not yet Ready, approved = Ready and dispatchable — and it stops moving
at materialization, because the bead owns everything after that.

## Second call, smaller

sources, parent_slug, depends_on, blocks and discovered_from are slug-valued.
Registering them as reference-bearing would make spec check resolve them, and
every one would dangle while work orders materialize into beads rather than
persisting. Proposal: register none; revisit with the file-based path the
template's "Storage" section anticipates.

## Preconditions verified this session

scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check exits 0 with strata 0.7.0 on PATH, so the
installed binary reproduces the committed artifacts and regeneration is safe.
The stale-strata hazard recorded during the qz9.2 retro does not apply now.

BLOCKED on the owner's answer to the status question; the reply is posted on
the review thread.

title: Implement the wikilink-to-markdown rewrite specified by frd-spec-markdown-links
description:
Implements [[frd-spec-markdown-links]] — specs/features/markdown-links/
markdown-links-frd.md.

The FRD specifies 29 acceptance criteria across six requirements: rewrite
wikilinks to markdown links preserving anchors, refuse a citation the link
map does not cover, report what was rewritten, be repeatable, read an
optional YAML link map keyed by slug, and target the corpus's own layout
when no map is given.

Two modes, and the distinction is the point. Given a link map the CLI
substitutes the caller's path and derives nothing, because the caller is
writing copies into a layout the CLI cannot see. Given no map the CLI
targets each citation with the cited document's path relative to the citing
document, which is what makes a corpus exported whole browsable as pages.
A given map is never completed by derivation (AC-SPECMD-006.3): a slug the
map omits is an error, not a link the caller never asked for.

Why the CLI rather than the copying script: deciding what IS a reference is
corpus knowledge the CLI already owns. cli/core/references extracts
references and cli/core/references/code.go excludes anything overlapping a
code span or fenced block. A script rewriting with a regular expression
would not draw that distinction and would corrupt the teaching prose the
rewrite must preserve.

This is the enforcement point for the shipped-document invariant: a citation
with nothing to point at fails at rewrite time rather than in an adopting
repository.

Renamed from vendor-links 2026-08-13. The feature covers publication as well
as vendoring, so the AC prefix moved SPECVND -> SPECMD before any test or
work order cited it.
design:
Author a feature blueprint from the FRD before implementing — the FRD is the WHAT, and the element deltas, the command surface and the AC coverage table belong in a blueprint. Do not implement straight from the FRD.

Open questions the blueprint must settle, not the FRD:
  * The command surface. `spec refs` already exists and is reference-shaped; whether this is a flag on it, a new subcommand, or a library capability the copying script calls is a design decision. The FRD constrains it only to: one document per invocation, rewritten document on stdout, no file writes, link map optional (AC-SPECMD-005.1 through .3, .10).
  * What names the document to rewrite — a path, or a slug the CLI resolves through the index. The FRD deliberately does not say.
  * Anchor slugification. AC-SPECMD-001.3 requires a target fragment derived from the anchor, but the derivation rule (lowercase, spaces to hyphens, punctuation) is unstated because it depends on what renders the copies. Settle it against a named target rather than inventing one.

title: Verify every markdown link in a shipped reference resolves to a co-located file
description:
Once the wikilink rewrite converts [[slug#anchor]] to [slug#anchor](path#anchor)
in copies written outside the corpus, nothing checks that the path actually
lands on a file present in that skill's reference directory.

The failure this catches: a skill ships a document citing another document that
was not copied alongside it. The link is syntactically fine and dead in the
adopter's repo. That failure exists TODAY in wikilink form —
plugin/skills/spec/references/frontmatter-standards.md ships and cites
[[document-relationship-standards]] twice, which is a corpus member under
specs/standards/ that the plugin does not ship.

This is the payload-side half of the invariant, and it belongs in a script
rather than the CLI: the CLI checks the corpus, and a skill's reference
directory is not corpus. See the corpus/payload split — a check about what THIS
repository ships is a script; a check that travels to an adopting repository is
the CLI.

Depends on the markdown-link rewrite landing (specs/features/markdown-links/
markdown-links-frd.md, slug frd-spec-markdown-links). Until then the links this
would verify do not exist yet. Note the rewrite already reports the same failure
at rewrite time under AC-SPECMD-002.1 when a link map is given; this script is
the standing guard over what is committed, which the rewrite cannot be.
design:
A script over plugin/skills/*/references/**: for every markdown link in a shipped document, resolve the target relative to the citing file and assert the file exists.

Scope it to links that point at other reference documents. External URLs (http/https) are out of scope. Anchors are checked for the file half only unless the anchor rule is settled — do not invent anchor slugification here.

Two things it must NOT do:
  * Do not reimplement reference EXTRACTION. The Spec CLI owns that parser (cli/core/references), including the code-span skipping that stops illustrative examples counting. This script reads markdown links, which is a different and simpler syntax, and it should say so in its header to stop a later reader merging the two.
  * Do not check wikilinks. After the rewrite a shipped copy should contain none; if it does, that is the rewrite failing and belongs to that bead, not this one.

Carry the two conventions the sibling scripts established and the sprint retro found valuable: a floor on how many files were examined, so a glob that stops matching fails loudly rather than passing cheerfully, and no third-party dependency.

Wire it into .github/workflows/checks.yml alongside the other payload gates. NOTE: the credential in this container cannot push .github/workflows/** — that step must be applied through the GitHub App path, as agent-plugins-9fx also needs.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A dependency-free script verifies that every markdown link in plugin/skills/*/references/** resolves to a file that exists, relative to the citing file
- [ ] External URLs (http/https) are skipped
- [ ] Only the file half of a link is checked; no anchor slugification is invented here
- [ ] Wikilinks are NOT checked — a shipped copy should contain none after the rewrite, and one that does is the rewrite's defect
- [ ] Reference extraction is NOT reimplemented; the script's header says it reads markdown links, a different and simpler syntax than the Spec CLI's `[[...]]` parser, so a later reader does not merge the two
- [ ] The script carries a floor on how many files it examined and fails loudly when the glob stops matching, rather than passing cheerfully
- [ ] The script uses no third-party dependency
- [ ] Run against the current tree it reports the known live failure: frontmatter-standards.md citing document-relationship-standards, which ships without its target
- [ ] A step running it is wired into .github/workflows/checks.yml alongside the other payload gates
- [ ] The workflow edit is applied through the GitHub App path — the PAT in this container cannot push .github/workflows/**, the same constraint agent-plugins-9fx carries

title: Delete scripts/validate-corpus.py and move rfcs/ under spec check
description:
validate-corpus.py covers two things that belong in different places, which is why it has resisted deletion.

  * rfcs/**/*.md — corpus work. `spec check` does this today with no CLI change, and does it BETTER: it catches a slug/pattern-mismatch in rfcs/outbox that the script cannot see, because the script does not check slug patterns at all.
  * plugin/skills/*/references/*.md — payload work, and obviated once the shipped standards and guides move into specs/ (agent-plugins-eaa). What remains in that tree afterwards is templates, covered by check-template-drift.py, and frontmatter-less prose, which has nothing to check.

Two of the three original blockers are already gone: agent-plugins-qz9.2 landed the empty-corpus guard and agent-plugins-qz9.3 landed the count-and-exclusions report, both this sprint. The third was the template parse failures, which agent-plugins-eaa removes by making the CLI never walk plugin/ at all.

One residual gap to decide rather than lose: the script carries MIN_CHECKED = 20, a floor. The CLIs corpus/empty rule fires at ZERO documents. So the CLI catches "the root matched nothing" but not "the root matched suspiciously few". That is a real, if narrow, loss.
design:
Replace the "Frontmatter conforms outside the corpus root" step in
.github/workflows/checks.yml with a `spec check` invocation over rfcs/, using a
second specs.toml and the document-local rule set:

```
--only frontmatter/parse,frontmatter/schema,frontmatter/missing-property,slug/pattern-mismatch
```

The corpus-global rules are deliberately NOT requested: rfcs/ is its own slug
namespace and cross-root citations would report as unresolved. The report
renders them `not-requested` rather than `passed`, so the narrowed scope is
visible rather than implied.

Do NOT add a second root over plugin/. After agent-plugins-eaa there is nothing
there to check.

On the MIN_CHECKED gap — the script carries a floor of 20 checked documents and
the CLI's corpus/empty rule fires only at ZERO, so "the root matched
suspiciously few" is not covered by anything after the deletion — take option
(b): FILE A BEAD for a configurable floor on corpus/empty. Do not take option
(a) and accept the loss silently. Filing costs one bead and keeps a real if
narrow guard recoverable; accepting it discards the guard with nothing
recording that it existed. The new bead does not block this one.

The deletion also removes the script's delegation to
sync-shared-references.sh --check. That is intended: checks.yml already runs
that script as its own step, and 0 files currently carry the GENERATED COPY
header inside the script's search scope.

NOTE: editing .github/workflows/** requires the GitHub App credential; the PAT
in this container is rejected.

- [ ] A second specs.toml points a spec root at rfcs/ and is committed

- [ ] That step passes green — which requires agent-plugins-8ko resolved, since the rfcs/outbox slug currently fails slug/pattern-mismatch
- [ ] No second root over plugin/ is added
- [ ] A follow-up bead exists for a configurable floor on the corpus/empty rule, covering the MIN_CHECKED = 20 guard the deletion removes

- [ ] The workflow edit is applied through the GitHub App path — the PAT in this container cannot push .github/workflows/**

title: Move the 8 shipped standards into specs/standards and invert the sync direction
description:
Move the standards-typed documents the plugin ships out of plugin/skills/*/references/ and into specs/standards/, then reverse scripts/sync-shared-references.sh so specs/ is the source and skills receive copies.

The 8 (7 under spec/references, 1 under retro-spec/references):
  ac-traceability-standards, blueprint-readiness-checklist, cross-document-references,
  document-readiness-checklist, frontmatter-standards, template-authoring-standards,
  work-order-definition-of-ready, findings-capture-protocol

specs/standards/ already holds document-relationship-standards, skill-best-practices and testing-standards, so the destination and the precedent both exist.

Todays sync map has 12 entries over 8 distinct source documents and maps skill -> skill. After the inversion it maps specs/ document -> consuming skill, which makes the map the authoritative statement of what ships.

Not every document in specs/standards ships: testing-standards is about the Go CLIs own tests. The inverted map is what distinguishes them, so a document absent from the map is internal by construction.
design:
Order: move the files, then rewrite the map, then regenerate, then verify.

The vendored copies keep the GENERATED COPY header the script already writes — it is what makes them excluded as `no-frontmatter` from any corpus walk, which is why the plugin tree stops needing corpus checking at all. Do not drop it.

Every skills copy becomes generated, INCLUDING the spec skills own. That is a real workflow change: editing a standards document becomes "edit specs/, re-run the script", and editing the copy is now always wrong. Say so in the script header and in each copys header — the header already says "Fix the source named in each files header", and the named source changes.

Citations move with the documents. A document now inside the corpus may cite a sibling by `[[slug]]`; one that ships must only cite other shipped documents (the epics invariant). frontmatter-standards.md cites `[[document-relationship-standards]]`, which currently does not ship — either add it to the map or change the citation, and record which.

DEPENDS on agent-plugins-wu1 (retype c4-guide) only if that document is handled in this bead rather than the sibling guides bead — it is not; guides are separate.

Do NOT move the 12 templates or the 8 frontmatter-less prose files. Templates have placeholder slugs and can never be corpus members; prose has nothing to check. Both stay where they are.

title: Backtick illustrative wikilinks in the documents bound for specs/
description:
The 14 corpus-shaped reference documents use `[[...]]` for two different purposes, and only one of them is a citation.

Measured across those documents, resolving each target against the slug set that would exist after the move:

  RESOLVES  ~17   template-authoring-standards x12, document-relationship-standards x2,
                  work-order-definition-of-ready, frontmatter-standards, cross-document-references
  DANGLES   ~50   [[slug]] x18, [[document-slug]] x7, [[security-standards]] x4,
                  [[component-...]] x3, [[module-...]] x2, [[frd-checkout]] x2,
                  [[contract-payments-api]] x2, [[container-x]] x2, [[container-...]] x2,
                  [[wo-1234]], ...

Every one of the ~50 is an illustrative example inside a guide or standards document explaining how references work — the same class as c4-guide.mds `[[module-<name>]]`, which produced three unresolved-reference findings when that document was inside a corpus root during the qz9 investigation.

Move the documents without this and the reference checker reports ~50 unresolved references, none of which is a real broken citation.

Doing this FIRST makes the move safe and is independently correct: an example of reference syntax should not be indistinguishable from a reference.
design:
Wrap each illustrative `[[...]]` in backticks. The reference extractor already skips code spans and fenced blocks — cli/core/references/code.go locates them with goldmark and cli/core/references excludes any reference overlapping one — so backticking is sufficient and needs no change to the extractor.

Distinguish the two cases by whether the target names a real document:
  * a slug that exists (or will exist after the move) in the corpus -> a citation, leave it
  * a placeholder (`<name>` inside it), a worked example (`frd-checkout`, `container-api`, `wo-1234`), or a slug no document has -> illustrative, backtick it

`[[security-standards]]` x4 needs a judgement call rather than a rule: no such document exists today, so it is illustrative as things stand, but it reads like a document someone intended to write. Backtick it and note it; do not invent the document.

Do this while the documents are still in plugin/skills/ — they are not in a corpus yet, so nothing gates the work and it can land independently of the move.

Verify by pointing a throwaway corpus root at the documents before and after and comparing the unresolved-reference count; do not rely on reading the diff.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every illustrative `[[...]]` in the 14 corpus-shaped documents under plugin/skills/*/references/ is wrapped in backticks
- [ ] Every `[[...]]` naming a slug that exists, or will exist after the move, is left as a wikilink
- [ ] `[[security-standards]]` (4 occurrences) is backticked, and a note records that it reads like an intended document — no such document is invented
- [ ] Measured before and after by pointing a throwaway corpus root at the documents: the unresolved-reference count drops from ~50 to the number of genuine citations only, and the resolving citations (~17) are unchanged
- [ ] The before/after counts are recorded on this bead — the verification is a measurement, not a diff read
- [ ] No change to cli/core/references or any extractor: backticking is sufficient because code spans are already excluded
- [ ] `scripts/check-skills.sh` exits 0

title: Shipped standards and guides live in specs/ and are vendored outward into skills
description:
Today the 14 corpus-shaped documents the plugin ships live in plugin/skills/*/references/ and are vendored SIDEWAYS between skills. They are outside the corpus, so the Spec CLI never checks them.

Move them into specs/ and invert the vendoring: specs/ becomes the single source, copies go OUTWARD into every skill that needs one.

## What this buys, measured

The 34 files under plugin/skills/*/references/ break down as:
  * 14 corpus-shaped — 8 standards, 6 guides, all with real slugs
  * 12 templates — placeholder slugs (`adr-<nnn>`), can never be corpus members
  *  8 frontmatter-less prose (recovery.md, subagent-prompts.md, dispatch-plan.md, ...)

Moving the 14 means nothing left in references/ wants a corpus walk: templates are covered by scripts/check-template-drift.py, and prose has no frontmatter to check. So **the Spec CLI is never pointed at plugin/ at all**, and the template-parse blocker that stalled the validate-corpus.py deprecation stops existing rather than being worked around.

The 14 also land in the MAIN corpus, so they get the full rule set — reference integrity, duplicate slugs, typed references — not the four document-local rules a second root could have given them.

It also removes the need for specs.toml ignore patterns (agent-plugins-qz9.1) from the critical path. That bead stays deferred on its own merits (cli/testdata produces 183 duplicate-slug errors under any root covering it).

## A live defect this fixes

plugin/skills/spec/references/frontmatter-standards.md SHIPS and cites `[[document-relationship-standards]]`, which lives in specs/standards/ and does NOT ship. Every adopter has a dangling pointer today. The move forces it resolved.

## The invariant this creates

A shipped document may cite only other shipped documents. After the inversion the sync map IS the shipped set, so it doubles as the marker — no new mechanism needed. The markdown-link rewrite (epic agent-plugins-ia5, blueprint specs/features/markdown-links/markdown-links-blueprint.md, FRD slug frd-spec-markdown-links) makes the rewrite the enforcement point: a citation with nothing to point at fails at vendor time rather than in an adopter's repo, under AC-SPECMD-002.1.

## Sequencing

  * agent-plugins-wu1 (retype c4-guide) FIRST — its slug changes, and after the move a slug is a compatibility surface.
  * The markdown-link rewrite capability (agent-plugins-ia5.5) lands with or before the move, or the vendored copies carry wikilinks that resolve to nothing for a reader.
  * The illustrative-wikilink cleanup (agent-plugins-eaa.1) can land any time and makes the move safe.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The 14 corpus-shaped documents live under specs/ and are checked by `spec check --strict`
- [ ] Each is vendored into every skill that needs it, from specs/ as the single source
- [ ] No skill reference directory contains an authored (non-generated) copy of a moved document
- [ ] frontmatter-standards.md no longer ships a citation to a non-shipped document
- [ ] scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check exits 0
- [ ] `spec check --strict` exits 0 with the moved documents in the corpus
- [ ] No Spec CLI configuration points at plugin/

title: rfcs/outbox slug does not match the RFC slug pattern
description:
rfcs/outbox/retro-spec/rfc-agent-plugins-findings-capture-harvest.md declares slug `rfc-agent-plugins-findings-capture-harvest`, which the profile rejects.

## Steps to Reproduce

Build the CLI, point a throwaway config at rfcs/, and run the document-local rule set:

```
printf %s "[workspace]\nname = \"x\"\nroot = \"rfcs\"\n\n[profile]\nname = \"spec-driven-dev\"\n" > /tmp/r.toml
./spec check --config /tmp/r.toml --only slug/pattern-mismatch
```

Expected: no findings.

Actual:
```
rfcs/outbox/retro-spec/rfc-agent-plugins-findings-capture-harvest.md:
  slug/pattern-mismatch  error  7:7  "rfc-agent-plugins-findings-capture-harvest" does not match
  pattern "^rfc-([0-9]{4}(-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*)?|self-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*)$"
```

31 documents are checked under that root; this is the only finding.

Nothing catches it today: scripts/validate-corpus.py does not check slug patterns at all, and rfcs/ sits outside the Spec CLI corpus root, so `spec check` never sees it.

Blocks the deprecation of validate-corpus.py — that work moves rfcs/ under `spec check`, which cannot land green while this fails.
design:
The pattern admits exactly two RFC identifier schemes: numbered (`rfc-0007`, optionally with a description) and self-critique (`rfc-self-<description>`). This slug is neither — it is `rfc-<origin-project>-<description>`, a third scheme the retro-skill template produces for an RFC authored BY one project ABOUT a skill.

## Chosen: rename the document to the self-critique scheme

Rename `rfcs/outbox/retro-spec/rfc-agent-plugins-findings-capture-harvest.md` to `rfcs/outbox/retro-spec/rfc-self-findings-capture-harvest.md`, and change its frontmatter from `slug: rfc-agent-plugins-findings-capture-harvest` to `slug: rfc-self-findings-capture-harvest`.

The `self-` form is accurate here, not a workaround: the origin of this RFC IS this repository. Its own frontmatter already carries `origin: agent-plugins`, and the document is dogfooding — agent-plugins critiquing a skill that agent-plugins also ships. The sibling `rfcs/inbox/retro-skill/rfc-self-retro-skill-withheld-model.md` already carries the same shape in the same nested layout.

Rename the FILE as well as the slug. The RFC document type has a slug pattern and no path rule (`cli/profile/profile.go`, the `documentTypes` entry for `DocumentTypeRfc`), so the file name is not checked — but every sibling RFC's file name equals its slug, and leaving the two divergent invites a later reader to "fix" the slug back.

Leave the `origin: agent-plugins` frontmatter field alone. It records provenance and is a separate field from the slug; the rename does not lose it. Do not otherwise touch the body.

## Citations to update

Both known citations are backticked PATH references, not `[[slug]]` wikilinks, so a wikilink search alone finds nothing. Both are in `rfcs/retired/rfc-0016-close-ceremony-and-finding-harvest.md`:

* in the P2 row of the outcome table — "…travelled as its own RFC to the skill that owns the protocol, `rfcs/outbox/retro-spec/rfc-agent-plugins-findings-capture-harvest.md`."
* in the trailing affected-files list — "`rfcs/outbox/retro-spec/rfc-agent-plugins-findings-capture-harvest.md` (new)"

These are path fixes so the references stay resolvable; do not otherwise rewrite a retired document. Re-run the search rather than trusting this list — grep the whole old slug string across the repository, it is unique enough to find every hit.

## Rejected: widen the profile pattern

Recorded so it is not re-litigated. Option (b) was to widen the slug pattern in `cli/profile/profile.go` to admit `rfc-<origin>-<description>`. It argues the profile is wrong rather than the document, and it would permanently entrench a THIRD RFC identifier scheme — outbox RFCs carrying their origin project in the slug even after triage in the framework repo assigns them a number. It is also strictly more work: a profile change plus a case in `cli/profile/profile_test.go`, which enumerates expected slug/path pairs.

Do NOT modify `cli/profile/profile.go` in this bead.

## Out of scope: the template disagreement

`plugin/skills/retro-skill/references/skill-rfc-template.md` prescribes `slug: rfc-<origin>-<short-description>`, the form the profile rejects. Renaming this document does not fix the template, so the template still prescribes a rejected pattern.

FILE THAT AS A FOLLOW-UP BEAD. Do not resolve it inside this bead and do not edit the template here. Record the new bead's id on this bead.

## Verification

Re-run the reproduction in the Problem: a throwaway config rooted at `rfcs/`, then `spec check --only slug/pattern-mismatch`. Expect no findings.

- [ ] The document's `origin: agent-plugins` frontmatter field is unchanged, and its body is unchanged apart from the slug
- [ ] `spec check --only slug/pattern-mismatch` over a throwaway root at `rfcs/` reports no findings — the reproduction in the Problem, re-run

title: Retype c4-guide as a standards document
description:
plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md declares `type: guide` but is normative, not explanatory.

Measured across the guide-typed reference docs (SHALL/MUST occurrences vs word count):

  c4-guide.md                  15   3748 words
  document-type-boundaries.md   0    554
  anti-patterns.md              1    661
  work-order-field-guide.md     1   1255
  spec-cli.md                   0   1837

  (for comparison, a real standards doc)
  template-authoring-standards.md  25  1985
  ac-traceability-standards.md     12   793

Its SHALLs are genuine constraints on how a reader authors C4 documents, not illustrations:
  "Element names SHALL NOT use **internal acronyms**"
  "The arrow SHALL point in the direction of the **dependency**"
  "A message bus (broker, queue, topic) SHALL NOT appear as an element"

Not in scope: ears-guide.md scores 43 SHALLs in 1479 words, the densest in the repo, but that is an artifact — it is a guide ABOUT EARS syntax, so most of its SHALLs are specimens of the pattern being taught (`WHEN [event], the system SHALL [action]`). Only two lines are genuinely normative. Leave it a guide.

DO THIS BEFORE the specs/ move (agent-plugins-eaa). The retype changes the slug from `guide-c4`, and once the document is vendored to adopters its slug is a compatibility surface — renaming after the move is a breaking change, renaming before it is free.
design:
Change `type: guide` to `type: standards` and change the slug from `guide-c4`
to `c4-standards`.

The slug is pinned rather than left to the implementer because it is a
compatibility surface once the document ships, and because "prefer one ending
in -standards" is not a name. `c4-standards` matches the sibling convention
(template-authoring-standards, ac-traceability-standards, frontmatter-standards)
and satisfies the profile's standards pattern, which fixes no prefix
(`^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`).

Do NOT rename the file. It stays `c4-guide.md`. The bead is a retype, not a
restructure, and the filename is what scripts/sync-shared-references.sh and
check-skills.sh path references resolve against — leaving it alone keeps the
blast radius to the slug.

Update every citation of the old slug. Search BOTH `[[guide-c4]]` wikilinks and
backticked path references before renaming; `spec check --strict` will catch
wikilink breakage but NOT backticked paths, which check-skills.sh rule 2 owns.

The frontmatter must satisfy the Standards definition rather than Guide —
compare the two in cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json and add any property
the standards branch requires that the guide branch did not.

Do NOT restructure the body. The retype is about the declared type and the
obligations that follow from it, not a rewrite.

title: corpus/empty findings report detail.kind "frontmatter-parse", misleading every JSON consumer
description:
agent-plugins-qz9.2 added rule `corpus/empty`, but could not give it an honest FindingDetail.

FindingDetail is a CLOSED union declared in schemas/finding.strata. Its variants are generated Go types with unexported methods, so cli/core/finding cannot extend it, and the run gate baseline forbade both regenerating (the installed strata binary may predate strata-lang/strata@8997153) and hand-editing generated artifacts.

No existing variant fits "corpus-level, no document, freeform message". FindingUnverified{Reason} was considered and rejected: its tag is coupled 1:1 with SeverityUnverified everywhere else, and corpus/empty is SeverityError by design mandate.

Settled on reusing FindingFrontmatterParse{Message} — the one existing variant already precedented at SeverityError with a bare message field.

CONSEQUENCE: a JSON consumer keying off `detail.kind` sees "frontmatter-parse" for a finding whose rule is `corpus/empty`. The text rendering is correct; only the structured detail lies. This is the kind of mismatch a catalogue consuming the index would act on.

FIX: add a real CorpusEmpty variant to the FindingDetail union in schemas/finding.strata, regenerate, and switch the rule to it. Blocked on the strata binary question — `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` reports the committed (correct) artifacts as stale when the binary predates that commit, so regeneration needs a verified-current strata first.

Surfaced by the implementing agent as a retro finding rather than shipped silently.
acceptance_criteria: FindingDetail carries a variant that honestly describes a corpus-level finding; corpus/empty uses it; a JSON consumer reading detail.kind sees a kind matching the rule.

title: bead-bonanza: record the run's effort setting in the dispatch manifest, and carry it into routed RFCs (triage T1)
description:
A bead-bonanza run records which models it used and not how hard they were
run, so every RFC the run produces carries an unfillable provenance field.

SKILL.md's "The run manifest" step enumerates what the orchestrator writes into
dispatch.md's header:

  "the pre-flight stdout block, gate profile, gate baseline, model lineup,
   standing authorization and environmental ledger"

There is no effort setting in that list, and no artifact any run writes records
one.

The consumer requires it. references/skill-rfc-template.md in the retro-skill
skill sets `effort: <low | medium | high | xhigh | max>` in RFC frontmatter, and
its readiness gate makes it mandatory before an RFC can reach ready-for-review:

  "[ ] Frontmatter sets model + effort (and Provenance names the harness) — a
   skill defect is model-relative"

Both RFCs produced by sprint run 1786562615-17 shipped with `effort:
unrecorded`. rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/rfc-self-report-citations-and-batch-base.md
devotes a paragraph to why it refused to guess: "the template's own rationale is
that a defect is model-relative and triage cannot scope a fix from a fabricated
value." So the gate was satisfied by writing down that the answer is unknown.

Why it matters beyond neatness: specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md
justifies the whole provenance block as triage's input -- "Retrospective RFCs
cite the version they exercised, and triage answers 'is this already fixed?'
from that citation." Effort is part of what was exercised in the same way the
model is. A defect that appears only at low effort is a different defect, with a
different fix, from one that survives at max, and triage cannot tell them apart
from `unrecorded`.

The manifest already records the model lineup, so the slot exists and the
sibling field is already there. This is one item in a list the orchestrator
writes anyway.

## Origin

TRIAGE-ORIGINATED (T1), 2026-08-13. No reporter proposed this. The RFC recorded
it under Considered and Not Proposed and declined it as "one run cannot show it
changed an outcome". That is the correct bar for a claimed DEFECT and the wrong
one here: this is a provenance field, and its value was never that it changed
this run's outcome. Its absence permanently degrades every future triage of
anything the run produced -- and the evidence is not one run but two RFCs, both
shipped degraded, in the batch that triaged them. The reasoning is triage's own.
design:
Two halves. The field must be recorded AND read, or it is decoration.

## 1. Record it -- SKILL.md, "The run manifest"

Add the effort setting to the enumeration of what the orchestrator writes into
dispatch.md's header, alongside the model lineup it already names. One list
item; no new step, no new artifact.

Record what the run can actually observe. WHERE the harness exposes no effort
setting, write `unrecorded` rather than omitting the field or guessing -- an
absent field is indistinguishable from a forgotten one, which is the failure
being fixed, and a guessed value is worse than either.

## 2. Read it -- the sprint retro's routing step

The retro's declared inputs are the harvested retro: comments, the printed
tables, "dispatch.md's ## Amendments log", the per-bead handoff and progress
files, and git log. The manifest HEADER is not among them, so adding a field
there changes nothing on its own.

At the "Route them, as offers" step, require any RFC the retro routes to carry
the run's model lineup and effort from the manifest header into its Provenance.
That closes the loop: the manifest records it, the retro carries it, the RFC
template's readiness gate is satisfiable with a real value.

## Do not

- Do not add effort to the per-bead progress events. The phase vocabulary is
  closed (see the note in bb-progress.sh) and effort is a run-level property,
  not a per-bead one.
- Do not add a version property to any bead-bonanza reference file; the skill
  versions as a bundle.

## Version bump -- this bead owns it

This bead lands LAST of the five approved proposals editing
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md (per-bead finding numbering, batch
chaining, trigger disposition, Monitor lifetime, and this one). It therefore
OWNS the single frontmatter version bump for that file: 1.4 -> 1.5. Before
bumping, confirm the other four beads' changes are present in SKILL.md -- the
version announces the release, not the proposal count.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] SKILL.md's run-manifest step lists an effort setting among what the orchestrator writes into dispatch.md's header, alongside the model lineup
- [ ] It instructs writing 'unrecorded' where the harness exposes no effort setting, and forbids both omitting the field and guessing a value
- [ ] The sprint retro's routing step requires any routed RFC to carry the run's model lineup and effort from the manifest header into its Provenance
- [ ] No effort field was added to the per-bead progress event vocabulary
- [ ] No version property was added to any bead-bonanza reference file
- [ ] plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md frontmatter version is bumped exactly once, 1.4 -> 1.5, by this bead, after confirming the other four SKILL.md changes are present

title: bead-bonanza: arm the Monitor persistent and stop it explicitly, instead of inheriting a 5-minute default (RFC A-P4, reshaped)
description:
The skill requires a Monitor on any subagent running past 5 minutes, and the
Monitor it prescribes expires after 5 minutes.

references/progress-streaming.md, under the heading "## Monitor any subagent
past 5 minutes", gives the arming pattern:

  tail -n +1 -F <run-dir>/<bead-id>.progress.jsonl | grep -E --line-buffered '"phase":"(committed|blocked)"'

It specifies no timeout_ms, and neither does SKILL.md's paragraph beginning
"Without being sent anywhere, the orchestrator arms a `Monitor` on the progress
file", which restates the rule. Nothing anywhere in plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/ mentions timeout_ms,
persistent, or TaskStop (grep, 2026-08-13: zero hits). So every Monitor the
skill arms takes the tool default.

The Monitor tool's default timeout_ms is 300000 -- five minutes. The rule it
serves fires at "expected to run past 5 minutes (any non-trivial bead, given
full test runs)". The guidance and the default are in direct opposition: the
skill arms a Monitor precisely where the default kills it.

Observed in sprint run 1786562615-17: the Monitor expired three times, each
requiring a manual re-arm. Most beads ran 10-16 minutes and several batches ran
over an hour, so expiry was the guaranteed outcome rather than an edge case.

Two further facts from the Monitor tool schema:

- persistent: true runs "for the lifetime of the session (no timeout)", is
  documented for "session-length watches", and is stopped with TaskStop. That
  is this use case exactly.
- The schema warns that unbounded commands under a timeout are the wrong shape:
  "tail -f ... never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until
  timeout." The skill's prescribed pattern is an unbounded tail -F.

Consequence: the orchestrator loses live visibility partway through long beads
and must notice and re-arm by hand, which is the failure the rule exists to
prevent.

Source: rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/rfc-self-report-citations-and-batch-base.md,
P4, reshaped at triage on 2026-08-13. The RFC reported this as "Monitor caps at
30 minutes regardless of the timeout_ms requested". Triage could not verify that
figure and the tool schema documents timeout_ms max 3600000 (60 minutes), so the
cap claim is deliberately excluded -- see Design. The expiries the RFC observed
are real; their cause is the unset default, not a 30-minute cap.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch any non-trivial bead expected to run past 5 minutes.
2. Arm a Monitor exactly as references/progress-streaming.md:73-79 prescribes:
   the tail -F ... | grep --line-buffered pattern, with no timeout_ms and no
   persistent flag.
3. Let the bead run its full gates (10-16 minutes is typical; batches exceed an
   hour).

Expected: the orchestrator sees committed/blocked events for the whole life of
the subagent, which is what the rule 'Monitor any subagent past 5 minutes'
exists to provide.

Actual: the Monitor takes the tool default timeout_ms of 300000 (five minutes)
and is killed while the subagent is still live. Live visibility is lost and the
orchestrator must notice and re-arm by hand.

Observed three times in sprint run 1786562615-17.
design:
Three changes. The rule is "do not rely on a timeout at all", not "expect the
timeout and cope".

## 1. references/progress-streaming.md, under "## Monitor any subagent past 5 minutes"

Amend the arming guidance to specify the Monitor's lifetime, not just its
command:

> Arm it with persistent: true and stop it with TaskStop when the wave drains.
> The default timeout_ms is five minutes -- the exact threshold at which this
> rule requires a Monitor -- so a Monitor armed without it expires on precisely
> the runs that need it. The tail -F pattern above never exits on its own, so
> under a timeout it stays armed until it is killed rather than ending when the
> work does. WHEN a Monitor does expire while its subagent is still live,
> re-arm it; expiry is not information about the bead.

The last sentence is the fallback, not the rule: a Monitor can also be stopped
by an interrupt, and an orchestrator that reads any stoppage as a signal about
the subagent will draw a wrong conclusion.

## 2. SKILL.md, the paragraph beginning "Without being sent anywhere, the
orth orchestrator arms a `Monitor`"

That paragraph currently says the orchestrator arms a Monitor and arms the
durable trigger, "cancelling it in Phase 4" -- it gives the trigger a lifetime
and the Monitor none. Locate it by that opening phrase, not by line number:
three earlier beads in this chain edit SKILL.md before this one runs. Add the Monitor's: armed persistent, stopped when the wave
drains. Keep it to a clause; the mechanism stays in progress-streaming.md.

## 3. State no numeric cap

Do NOT write a cap figure into either file. The RFC reported 30 minutes; the
tool schema documents timeout_ms max 3600000 (60 minutes), and triage could not
reconcile them. A skill that asserts a false measurable constant is worse than
one that is silent, because an agent trusts it over its own observation. With
persistent: true the cap is not load-bearing anyway.

## Do NOT add a version property to progress-streaming.md

All six bead-bonanza references are unversioned; the skill versions as a bundle
and SKILL.md carries that version. See the same note on the batch-chaining bead.

## Version bump

This bead does NOT own the SKILL.md version bump. The dispatch-manifest effort
bead lands last of the five approved proposals editing this file and owns the
single 1.4 -> 1.5 bump.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] references/progress-streaming.md instructs arming the Monitor with persistent: true and stopping it with TaskStop when the wave drains
- [ ] It states that the default timeout_ms is five minutes, the same threshold at which the rule requires a Monitor
- [ ] It notes that the prescribed tail -F pattern never exits on its own, so a timeout kills it rather than the work ending it
- [ ] It keeps the fallback rule: when a Monitor expires while its subagent is still live, re-arm it, and expiry is not information about the bead
- [ ] SKILL.md's paragraph beginning 'Without being sent anywhere, the orchestrator arms a Monitor' gives the Monitor a lifetime (armed persistent, stopped when the wave drains) alongside the trigger's
- [ ] Neither file states a numeric cap for Monitor duration
- [ ] No version property was added to references/progress-streaming.md
- [ ] plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md frontmatter version is NOT bumped by this bead

metadata.tier_reason: Two short guidance edits with the wording drafted; the judgment (omit the cap figure, own the bundle version bump) is settled in Design.

title: groom-beads: reject a bare file:line anchor with no quoted content (RFC B-P2)
description:
groom-beads maintains a list of anti-patterns it actively rejects at grooming
time (plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md, "## Anti-patterns to actively reject") -- session-dependent language and similar defects that fail the
fresh-agent test. A bare file:line citation is not among them.

It should be. In sprint run 1786562615-17, fourteen of seventeen groomed beads
cited file:line positions and every one had moved by dispatch, because earlier
beads in the same run edited the same files. Six beads recorded it
independently; b13's is representative: "the bead's cited line numbers
(pre-flight-check.sh:269,:284,:455,:494-495; SKILL.md:1106-1113;
bb-close-bead.sh:159-165) had all moved -- four earlier-sprint beads (q1h, td1,
9p4, 8mv) touched pre-flight-check.sh. Located each effect by content..."

A bare line reference has two independent problems: the position is stale as
soon as any earlier order edits that file, and the reader is left with nothing
to relocate by. A citation that quotes its content survives the first problem
and eliminates the second.

The Definition of Ready defines what "ready" means; groom-beads is where a work
order is brought to it. This is the enforcement half.

Source: rfcs/inbox/groom-beads/rfc-self-line-anchors-rot-across-a-sprint.md, P2.
Approved adopt-now at triage on 2026-08-13.

Note: the grooming pass that produced those fourteen beads was performed by the
same model that authored the RFC and triaged it. The evidence is the
implementers' findings, not the groomer's self-assessment.
design:
Add one bullet to the "## Anti-patterns to actively reject" list in
plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md, alongside the existing session-dependent
language entry:

> A file:line citation with no quoted content -- the position is stale as soon
> as any earlier order edits that file, and the reader has nothing to relocate
> by. Inline the content the line held.

Match the surrounding bullets' form and length; this list is terse by
convention. Do not restate the Definition of Ready's rule here -- the DoR owns
the definition and this list owns the rejection. A one-line pointer is fine if
the surrounding bullets carry them; do not add one if they do not.

Ordering: the DoR change (the other approved proposal from this RFC) should land
first, so this bullet enforces a rule that already exists rather than one that
is still being written. That is why this bead depends on it.

## Version bump

This bead owns the plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md frontmatter version bump:
1.2 -> 1.3. It is the only approved proposal in this round editing that file.

Note that the other approved proposal regenerates
plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/*.md. Those are vendored reference
files, not SKILL.md, so there is no collision on the bumped file.

- [ ] groom-beads SKILL.md's 'Anti-patterns to actively reject' list contains an entry for a file:line citation with no quoted content
- [ ] The entry gives both reasons: the position goes stale when an earlier order edits the file, and the reader has nothing to relocate by
- [ ] The entry instructs inlining the content the line held
- [ ] The entry matches the surrounding bullets in form and length and does not restate the Definition of Ready's full rule
- [ ] plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md frontmatter version is bumped exactly once, 1.2 -> 1.3

title: bead-bonanza Phase 4: report the durable trigger's disposition (RFC A-P5)
description:
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md's Phase 4 step 6a instructs the
orchestrator to "Cancel the durable out-of-session trigger armed at first
dispatch", and references/progress-streaming.md gives the rationale in its
bullet beginning "**Cancel it in Phase 4**, when the run drains": a trigger left armed
after the run drains wakes an agent into a finished sprint, which trains the
reader to ignore it.

The rule exists, so an orchestrator skipping it is an execution miss, not a
skill defect. What IS a skill defect is that its omission is invisible at the
time. Every other Phase 4 step yields an artifact -- a report, a commit, a
closed bead. A live trigger yields nothing until it fires later, into a
different session.

Observed in sprint run 1786562615-17: the trigger for that run fired twice into
a fully drained sprint and was deleted by hand by a resuming session -- which is
precisely the outcome progress-streaming.md warns about.

The Phase 4 report is already the place where the run's steps produce checkable
output, so the fix is to make this step produce one line there.

Source: rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/rfc-self-report-citations-and-batch-base.md, P5.
Approved adopt-now at triage on 2026-08-13.

Related prior work: agent-plugins-92q.14 (closed) added the durable trigger and
its Phase 4 cancellation. This bead does not revisit that rule; it makes the
rule's outcome visible.
design:
Add the trigger's disposition to Phase 4's report contents in
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md, as a required line:

> Durable trigger: cancelled (<id>) / none armed.

Place it with the other Phase 4 report contents -- the numbered list whose
entries include "**Pushes** -- confirm all closed beads' commits are on the
remote", "6a. **Cancel the durable out-of-session trigger**" and "6b. **Delete
the run snapshot**" -- so the reporting requirement sits where a reader of the
report step finds it. Locate that list by those headings, not by line number:
two earlier beads in this chain edit SKILL.md before this one runs.

This adds no new rule and no new mechanism. It makes an existing rule's outcome
checkable by the same standard the report's other claims are already held to --
the citation requirement in specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md, which
requires a factual claim to name its source.

Both branches must be stateable: a run that never armed a trigger reports "none
armed" rather than omitting the line, because an omitted line is
indistinguishable from a forgotten cancellation -- which is the entire failure
being fixed.

## Version bump

This bead does NOT own the SKILL.md version bump. A later bead in this chain --
the Monitor lifetime bead -- lands last of the four approved proposals editing
this file and owns the single 1.4 -> 1.5 bump.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Phase 4's report contents in SKILL.md require a line giving the durable trigger's disposition
- [ ] Both branches are stateable: cancelled with its id, or 'none armed'
- [ ] The requirement is placed with the other Phase 4 report contents, near step 6a
- [ ] No new rule about arming or cancelling triggers is introduced; only the reporting of the outcome
- [ ] plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md frontmatter version is NOT bumped by this bead

title: Gate template drift: every template's property set must match its type's schema
description:
Templates are the most-copied and least-checked artifacts in the framework, and they ship to every adopting repository, so a drifted template distributes a defect at the source. Nothing checks them today: validate-corpus.py skips any filename containing "template" and templates sit outside the Spec CLI corpus root.

A template cannot be validated as an instance - its placeholder values (<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ>, adr-<nnn>) are deliberately invalid, and 12 of the 13 fail frontmatter parse for that reason. What can be validated is structural: the set of top-level properties a template declares must match the definition its declared type selects, because every document authored from it inherits that set.

This needs neither the corpus, nor the template concept as CLI vocabulary, nor any third-party dependency - only the generated schema bundle and the frontmatter key set, which is why it lands ahead of the ignore-patterns and first-class-templates work.

The type -> definition mapping is derived from the DocumentType enum by kebab-to-Pascal conversion rather than transcribed, so a type added to the vocabulary is covered without a second list to maintain, and a type with no definition is reported rather than skipped.
acceptance_criteria: A gate reports, for every *-template.md, any required property the template omits and any property the schema does not define, and any declared type with no definition; wired into checks.yml; it fails today on the two known defects.
close_reason: scripts/check-template-drift.py implemented and wired into checks.yml; found 2 real defects (agent-plugins-3xx, agent-plugins-j5n)

title: Standards: AC identifiers are append-only and are never renumbered
description:
ac-traceability-standards.md states that AC identifiers are never reused. Never reused and never renumbered are different rules, and only the first is written down.

Reuse means: do not assign a retired identifier to something new.
Renumbering means: do not shift existing identifiers when inserting one.

Inserting AC-SPEC-006.5 between an existing .4 and .5 must append rather than shift. If identifiers shift on edit, every identifier-keyed delta between FRD versions is garbage, and every test citation and work order source pointing at an AC silently retargets.

State the append-only rule explicitly before anything depends on it.
design:
Add the append-only rule to the SOURCE document, then re-vendor.

Source: plugin/skills/spec/references/ac-traceability-standards.md. It already states "AC identifiers are never reused" (line ~29, in the paragraph beginning "The durable traceability pair"). Add the second, distinct rule beside it.

The two rules and why both are needed:
  * never REUSED  — do not assign a retired identifier to new criteria (already stated)
  * never RENUMBERED — do not shift existing identifiers when inserting one. Inserting between AC-SPEC-006.4 and .5 appends a new number; it does not renumber .5 onward.

Write it in EARS form to match the surrounding document, and state the failure mode: if identifiers shift on edit, every test citation and work-order source silently retargets to different criteria, and any identifier-keyed diff between two versions of an FRD is meaningless.

MANDATORY second step — this document is VENDORED. scripts/sync-shared-references.sh line 59 maps it into groom-feature-blueprint/references/shared/. After editing the source, run `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` (no --check) to regenerate the copy and commit both. CI runs `--check` and fails on a stale copy. Never edit the vendored copy directly; its header says so.

Also bump the frontmatter: `version` (currently "0.2.0") and `updated_at`.

Independent of agent-plugins-lwu. That ADR relies on this guarantee, but the rule stands on its own and does not require the ADR to land first.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] ac-traceability-standards.md states that AC identifiers are append-only and are never renumbered on edit, distinct from the existing no-reuse rule
- [ ] The stated failure mode covers both consequences: retargeted test citations / work-order sources, and meaningless identifier-keyed FRD diffs
- [ ] The new rule is written in EARS form, consistent with the rest of the document
- [ ] Frontmatter `version` and `updated_at` are bumped
- [ ] plugin/skills/groom-feature-blueprint/references/shared/ac-traceability-standards.md is regenerated and committed alongside the source
- [ ] scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check exits 0
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0

title: ADR: how an FRD evolves — living document, with deltas keyed on AC identifiers
description:
The change process for an FRD is undecided, and the CLI report/guard changes are the first case that needs it.

Proposed decision:

An FRD is a living document; an ADR is an immutable record. An ADR is a decision at a moment, so it is superseded rather than edited. An FRD is the current answer to "what must this feature do", and that job is destroyed if a reader must replay a chain of amendments to learn the answer. The repository already encodes the split - ADRs are numbered with superseded_by, FRDs are slug-named per feature.

So: amendment-FRDs are rejected. The test is not "new or edit" but "is this the same feature", and feature identity is already carried by the slug. Same feature -> edit in place. New feature -> new FRD.

For targeting the change, diff AC identifiers rather than lines. ac-traceability-standards.md already states that AC identifiers are never reused, which is what makes an identifier-keyed delta sound:
  * in new, not in old -> new work
  * in both, text changed -> the blueprint sections and work orders citing it need revisiting
  * in old, not in new -> find what implemented it; that code may now be unspecified

A line diff fails in both directions: reordering or rewording produces noise that is not a requirements change, while SHALL -> SHOULD or 100ms -> 500ms is a one-word diff with large downstream impact.

The payoff is mostly already built: tests cite AC identifiers and work orders name their sources, so a changed AC traces forward to the tests verifying it and the work orders that produced it - a query over existing machinery, closer to a sibling of `spec refs` than a new document type.

Not an FRD itself: the decision is an ADR, and the process rule it implies belongs in a standards document. A `spec diff` CLI capability, if wanted, gets its own FRD later.
design:
Author ADR-020 from plugin/skills/spec/references/adr-template.md into specs/adrs/.

Number: ADR-020. ADR-019 is the current highest (specs/adrs/ADR-019-skill-composed-subagent-orchestration.md).

STATUS: `ready-for-review`, NOT `approved` or `active`. This records the decision for the owner to ratify; it does not enact it. Three ADRs in specs/adrs/ already sit at ready-for-review, so this is the established staging state. Moving it to approved is a human act and is explicitly out of scope for this bead.

The decision to record is stated in full in this bead Problem section — transcribe and structure it, do not re-derive it. It has three parts:
  1. An FRD is a living document; an ADR is an immutable record. Edit an FRD in place; supersede an ADR.
  2. The test for a change is "is this the same feature", and feature identity is carried by the slug. Same feature -> edit in place. New feature -> new FRD.
  3. Deltas between FRD versions are keyed on AC identifiers, not on lines.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES the ADR must record, with the reason each was rejected — this is what stops a later agent re-litigating them:
  * Amendment FRDs (a new FRD that modifies an old one). Rejected: a reader would have to replay a chain to learn current truth, which destroys the FRD one job as the single answer to what a feature must do.
  * Line-based diffs for targeting change. Rejected: fails in both directions — reordering or rewording produces noise that is not a requirements change, while SHALL -> SHOULD or 100ms -> 500ms is a one-word diff with large downstream impact.

CONSEQUENCES the ADR should draw out: tests already cite AC identifiers and work orders already name their `sources`, so a changed AC traces forward to the tests verifying it and the work orders that produced it. This is a query over existing machinery rather than new document types. It depends on AC identifiers being append-only, which agent-plugins-k9j adds to ac-traceability-standards.md.

Out of scope: any `spec diff` CLI capability. That would need its own FRD.

Frontmatter must satisfy the Adr schema definition — the corpus job runs `spec check --strict` over specs/, so a malformed document fails CI.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] specs/adrs/ADR-020-*.md exists, authored from adr-template.md

- [ ] It names the dependency on AC identifiers being append-only
- [ ] It does NOT specify a `spec diff` CLI capability
- [ ] `./spec check --strict` passes over specs/

title: Wire the two spec check --only CI steps and delete validate-corpus.py

  --only frontmatter/parse,frontmatter/schema,frontmatter/missing-property,slug/pattern-mismatch

SCOPE CHANGED 2026-08-12: agent-plugins-qz9.1 (ignore patterns) was deferred by the owner, so this bead can no longer delete the script outright.

    --only frontmatter/parse,frontmatter/schema,frontmatter/missing-property,slug/pattern-mismatch

title: spec check reports what it checked: document count, exclusions, and failures grouped by file
description:
`spec check` prints findings and a per-rule pass/fail summary. It never says how many documents it looked at, and it does not list exclusions - those reach only the index artifact. scripts/validate-corpus.py prints "checked 38 documents, 0 findings, 6 excluded".

Three changes:

1. Always print the document count. It is what makes the zero-document guard auditable by a human reading CI output.

2. Always list exclusions with their reasons. A file that "passed" because it was excluded did not pass. The report already keeps this discipline at rule level - passed and not-requested are distinct - and the same three states apply per file: checked and clean, checked and failed, excluded because X. Collapsing excluded into passed is how a document that should be a specification but is missing frontmatter goes invisible.

3. Group failures by file in the text rendering, keeping the per-rule tally in the summary. Rule grouping answers "is this systemic"; file grouping answers "what do I fix next", and the text report is read by whoever is fixing things. JSON stays flat for machines.

Do not list passing documents individually - for 130 documents that is a wall nobody reads, and the count plus the exclusion list answers the coverage question better.
design:
Three changes to the human-readable check report. JSON output is unchanged — machines already receive everything.

1. DOCUMENT COUNT, printed on success and failure alike. The count is what makes agent-plugins-qz9.2 auditable by someone reading CI output rather than an exit code.

2. EXCLUSIONS, with reasons. They already exist on the index (specmodel.IndexExclusion, with ExclusionReasonNoFrontmatter / ExclusionReasonUnknownType) and currently reach only the emitted index artifact. Surface them in the report. The distinction to preserve: a file that "passed" because it was excluded did not pass. Render three states per file — checked and clean, checked and failed, excluded with its reason — never collapsing excluded into passed.

3. GROUP FAILURES BY FILE in the text rendering, keeping the existing per-rule tally in the summary. Rule grouping answers "is this systemic"; file grouping answers "what do I fix next", and the text report is read by whoever is fixing things.

Do NOT list passing documents individually. Over 130 documents that is a wall nobody reads, and the count plus the exclusion list already answers the coverage question.

WHERE it lives: the rendering belongs to finding.Report.Text() in cli/core/finding, which cmd already selects between Text and JSON (renderReport in cli/cmd/root.go). Do not format findings in cmd — same Change Guidance as the sibling bead. Corpus will need to expose its exclusions to whatever builds the Report; Corpus.Index() already exists as the access point.

Snapshot tests will move. cli/cmd has snapshot_test.go and cli/testdata/cases/* golden files that capture current text output; regenerate with scripts/regenerate-cli-snapshots.sh and review the diff rather than hand-editing goldens.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `spec check` text output states how many documents were checked, on a clean run and on a failing run
- [ ] Exclusions are listed with their reasons in text output
- [ ] An excluded file is never reported as passed
- [ ] Findings in text output are grouped by file
- [ ] The per-rule pass/fail/not-requested summary is still present
- [ ] Individual passing documents are NOT listed
- [ ] `--json` output is unchanged
- [ ] Snapshots regenerated via scripts/regenerate-cli-snapshots.sh and the diff reviewed
- [ ] `cd cli && go test ./...` passes

title: specs.toml gains ignore patterns so a corpus root can exclude fixtures and templates
description:
A corpus root cannot currently exclude anything, which is what keeps `spec check` from covering the skills references/ directory: 13 *-template.md files fail frontmatter/parse on deliberate placeholders (updated_at: <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ>). frontmatter/parse cannot be dropped from the rule set to work around it - it is one of the checks that matters.

No directory arrangement separates them: templates sit alongside the guides that SKILL.md cites next to them.

The need is general, not a template workaround. Pointing a root at the repository root sweeps cli/testdata/, which alone produces 183 duplicate-slug errors - it is a corpus about broken corpora and must never be checked.

Rejected alternative: a `template: true` frontmatter flag. Its only semantic would be "skip me", which is an ignore pattern requiring every file to be edited, working only on markdown files under our control. Templates should become first-class eventually, but the payoff there is checking them harder, not skipping them - a flag built now under ignore-pressure would have to invert its meaning later.

Feasibility note for whoever builds the flag anyway: it would work. The frontmatter package parses to a generic property tree before typed decoding, and the template failures are in the typed-decode stage, so a top-level key is readable from a document whose envelope decode fails.
acceptance_criteria: specs.toml can declare ignore patterns; a root covering plugin/skills passes with templates excluded; cli/testdata/ can be excluded from a repository-root corpus.
