title: spec check must fail when it checked zero documents
description:
A spec root that no longer exists already errors loudly:

  Error: cmd: opening the corpus: corpus: opening the spec root: open .../nope-gone: no such file or directory

A root that exists but holds no documents does not:

  $ spec check --config <root="docs"> --strict
  no findings ... all checks passed          exit=0

That is the failure that let scripts/validate-corpus.py stale docs/**/*.md glob look healthy - it kept reporting a confident count over the wrong files. Directory-based scoping makes it rarer, not impossible: a typo in root, a moved directory, or an over-broad ignore rule all land here.

The script guards this with a MIN_CHECKED floor. That guard is the one thing it has that the CLI does not, and it is what gets lost the day the script is deleted.

A check run that indexed zero documents is a broken configuration, not a pass. Under a path or glob argument the same rule reads as "matched zero paths".
design:
Raise a finding when a check run indexed zero corpus members.

WHERE the rule lives: cli/core/corpus, not cli/cmd. container-spec-cli.md Change Guidance is binding here — "a check that lived here [the command surface] would be unavailable to a future API or MCP wrapper". cmd only renders and maps exit codes.

Steps:
  1. Add a rule identifier alongside the existing ones in cli/core/finding (RuleFrontmatterParse, RuleSchemaViolation, ... are the pattern). Suggested: corpus/empty.
  2. Raise it from Corpus.Check when the index has no entries. Severity ERROR, so it exits non-zero through the existing exitCodeFor mapping without needing --strict. AC-SPEC-006.6 already makes any error exit 1; do not add a special case in cmd.
  3. Register the new identifier in checkRules in cli/cmd/check.go, so --only can name it and so a run that does not raise it reports "passed" rather than being absent from the report accounting.
  4. The finding SHALL name the configured spec root in its message, since the whole point is telling the operator that the root they configured matched nothing.

Scope boundary: a root that does not EXIST already errors from corpus.Open ("opening the spec root: no such file or directory") and is out of scope. This bead is only the root that exists and contains no corpus members.

Do NOT raise it from CheckFor (the single-document path). A single-document check over a one-member corpus is not an empty corpus.

Add a testdata case under cli/testdata/cases/ following the shape of the existing check-* cases (see check-strict-warning-only for a case that exercises exit-code behavior). Note cli/testdata is a corpus of deliberately-broken fixtures; adding one is expected.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `spec check` against a root that exists and contains no corpus members exits non-zero
- [ ] It does so WITHOUT --strict, and also with --strict
- [ ] The finding message names the configured spec root
- [ ] The new rule identifier appears in the report accounting as "passed" on a normal run over a populated corpus
- [ ] `spec check --only <the new rule>` runs and reports it
- [ ] A single-document `spec check <path>` against a valid member is unaffected
- [ ] A testdata case covers the empty-root run and its exit code
- [ ] `cd cli && go test ./...` passes
- [ ] specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md is updated if the component boundary description changes

metadata.tier_reason: localized change following an established rule-registration pattern with clear acceptance; the only judgement is placing the rule in core rather than cmd, which the Design settles

Confirms the bead description exactly — a broken/empty configuration read as a clean pass.

Message: "spec root %q holds no corpus members: the run checked zero documents", with the configured root (relative to repo root, e.g. "docs") both quoted in the message and used as the finding's Path (no document exists to point at, so the spec root itself fills that field; Position is the zero Span).

comments.text: retro: Friction — FindingDetail is a closed union (schemas/finding.strata) whose variants are generated, unexported-method Go types cli/core/finding cannot extend, and the gate baseline forbids regen (stale strata binary) and forbids hand-editing generated code. No existing variant fits 'corpus-level, no document, freeform message' cleanly. Considered FindingUnverified{Reason} (tag "unverified") but rejected it: that tag is otherwise coupled 1:1 with SeverityUnverified everywhere else, and this finding is SeverityError by design mandate. Settled on reusing FindingFrontmatterParse{Message} (tag "frontmatter-parse") since it is the one existing variant already precedented at SeverityError with a bare message field — but a JSON consumer keying off detail.kind will see "frontmatter-parse" for a rule named corpus/empty, which is misleading. A future bead adding a real CorpusEmpty detail variant (via regen, once the strata binary situation is resolved) would remove this mismatch.

title: Retire scripts/validate-corpus.py in favour of the Spec CLI
description:
validate-corpus.py duplicates the Spec CLI everywhere the two overlap, and is weaker where they do.

Measured: the CLI validates the same generated schema bundle, plus per-type slug patterns the script does not check at all (it passes rfcs/ clean while `spec check` finds a real slug/pattern-mismatch in rfcs/outbox/retro-spec/rfc-agent-plugins-findings-capture-harvest.md), and validates raw property source text where the script sees only PyYAML-coerced values. The script also re-validates specs.toml, which cmd.Load already does on every CLI invocation, and delegates generated-copy detection to sync-shared-references.sh --check, which checks.yml already runs as its own step (0 files currently carry the header).

The scope difference is not a capability difference. rfcs/ and the skills references/ can be checked today with a second specs.toml and the existing --only flag, with no CLI change:

  spec check --config alt-rfcs.toml --strict --only frontmatter/parse,frontmatter/schema,frontmatter/missing-property,slug/pattern-mismatch

That run reports the corpus-global rules as not-requested rather than passed, which is more honest than the script, which silently does not check references and never says so.

Two things block deleting the script:
  * templates - 13 *-template.md files fail frontmatter/parse on deliberate placeholders under a root covering plugin/skills
  * the underpopulation guard - the script MIN_CHECKED floor has no CLI equivalent

Do not go per-document: `spec check <path>` requires corpus membership, and the 5 files it errors on are exactly the 5 the script reports as excluded/no-frontmatter, so a per-file loop cannot tell correctly-excluded from broken.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/validate-corpus.py is deleted; checks.yml gates rfcs/ and the skills references/ through `spec check --only`; no document loses coverage in the transition.
notes: BLOCKED IN PART 2026-08-12: agent-plugins-qz9.1 (ignore patterns) deferred by the owner. The skills references/ half of the deprecation has no route without it, so the script cannot be deleted. See the scope note on agent-plugins-qz9.4 for what remains available.

title: template-authoring-standards.md is checked by no gate
description:
plugin/skills/spec/references/template-authoring-standards.md is a real standards document (type: standards, with a slug) but no gate checks it.

scripts/validate-corpus.py excludes it: EXCLUDE_NAME_CONTAINS = ["template"] is a substring match, and the filename contains "template" although the document is not a template. It is also outside the Spec CLI corpus root, so `spec check` never sees it.

The substring match is the defect. Templates in this repository are identifiable precisely: every one ends in `-template.md`. A suffix match excludes the 13 templates and no genuine document.

scripts/check-template-drift.py already uses the suffix rule; whatever replaces validate-corpus.py should do the same.

## Steps to Reproduce

```
scripts/validate-corpus.py | grep template-authoring-standards
```

Expected: the document appears as checked.

Actual: no output — it appears neither as checked nor as excluded. It is
silently absent, because EXCLUDE_NAME_CONTAINS = ["template"] is applied as a
substring test and "template" occurs in "template-authoring-standards.md".

Confirm it is a genuine corpus-shaped document rather than a template:

```
head -12 plugin/skills/spec/references/template-authoring-standards.md
```

Expected/actual: it declares `type: standards` with a slug — a real standards
document, not a template.

It is not covered by the other gate either: `spec check` reads the corpus root
declared in specs.toml (`specs`), and this file is outside it.

Manifests in: scripts/validate-corpus.py (EXCLUDE_NAME_CONTAINS).
design:
Change the template-exclusion rule in scripts/validate-corpus.py from a substring match to a suffix match.

Current: EXCLUDE_NAME_CONTAINS = ["template"], applied as `any(s in path.name for s in ...)`. "template" is a substring of "template-authoring-standards.md", so a genuine standards document is skipped.

Chosen: match on the `-template.md` SUFFIX. Verified against the repository: every one of the 13 templates ends in `-template.md`, and no genuine document does. scripts/check-template-drift.py already uses this rule (its SEARCH constant) — this makes the two gates agree rather than inventing a third convention.

Rejected: keeping the substring and adding an allowlist entry for this one file. That leaves the trap armed for the next document whose name contains the word.

Expect the document to then be validated against the Standards definition by validate-corpus.py. If it fails, fix the document rather than re-excluding it; it is a real corpus-shaped document and the failure would be genuine.

Note the file is NOT vendored to another skill (only ac-traceability-standards.md and the work-order references are), so no sync-shared-references.sh re-run is needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] scripts/validate-corpus.py excludes templates by the `-template.md` suffix, not by the substring "template"
- [ ] template-authoring-standards.md appears in validate-corpus.py output as a checked document, not as excluded or absent
- [ ] The checked-document count reported by validate-corpus.py increases by exactly 1
- [ ] scripts/validate-corpus.py exits 0
- [ ] scripts/check-template-drift.py still reports 12 templates (the suffix rule is unchanged there)

metadata.tier_reason: one-line predicate change in a script, plus verifying one document validates; no ambiguity and no C4 component

title: bead-bonanza restates the findings-harvest pipeline instead of vendoring it, and the restatement has already drifted
description:
The repository already solves cross-skill sharing the way specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md:235-241 mandates: a single authored source, vendored into each consumer by scripts/sync-shared-references.sh, with --check diffing every copy and an orphan guard catching unregenerated files.

bead-bonanza is not wired into it for the findings-capture protocol, and restates the pipeline instead. The two have already diverged:

  canonical, plugin/skills/retro-spec/references/findings-capture-protocol.md:
    bd export | jq -r 'select((.labels//[]) | index("<feature-slug>")) | .comments[]? | select(.text|startswith("retro:")) | .text'

  restatement, plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/operating-principles.md:76-79:
    adds select(.status=="closed") and uses <slug> rather than <feature-slug>

Divergence in a hand-copied query is exactly the failure the vendoring generator exists to prevent, and it is invisible today because the file is not in the generator's MAP.

THE SPECIFIC CHANGE RECOMMENDED — three edits:
  1. Add one line to scripts/sync-shared-references.sh's MAP registering bead-bonanza as a consumer of retro-spec/references/findings-capture-protocol.md. This generates plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/shared/findings-capture-protocol.md with the GENERATED COPY header.
  2. Delete the restatement at operating-principles.md:76-79 (and the surrounding harvest prose that duplicates the protocol, ~1,800 chars) and replace it with a pointer to references/shared/findings-capture-protocol.md.
  3. Decide which query is correct — the canonical one, or the canonical one plus select(.status=="closed") — and fix it AT THE SOURCE in retro-spec, not in the generated copy. If the closed-status filter is right for a drained sprint, that belongs in the shared protocol with a note on when to apply it.

This also answers, and closes off, the 'shared retro skill' proposal: a skill-name dependency between skills has all three properties skill-best-practices.md:229-232 condemns — it silently depends on co-installation, dangles when a skill is copied alone, and is undiscoverable from the referencing skill's own tree — and is WORSE on the third, because a ../ path at least trips check-skills.sh while a skill name trips nothing. A private shared skill is not the way around vendoring; it is the alternative vendoring was chosen over.

## Steps to Reproduce

From the repository root, compare the two queries and confirm the file is unregistered:

    grep -n 'startswith' plugin/skills/retro-spec/references/findings-capture-protocol.md
    sed -n '76,79p' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/operating-principles.md
    grep -n 'bead-bonanza' scripts/sync-shared-references.sh

EXPECTED: one authored query, vendored into every consumer, verified by --check.
ACTUAL: two queries that differ by 'select(.status=="closed")' and by <slug> vs <feature-slug>, and bead-bonanza does not appear in the generator's MAP for this file — so nothing detects the divergence.
design:
SCOPE: the mechanical wiring only. Vendor the canonical protocol AS IT STANDS; do not alter its query.

Two edits:
  1. Add one line to scripts/sync-shared-references.sh's MAP registering bead-bonanza as a consumer of retro-spec/references/findings-capture-protocol.md. This generates plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/shared/findings-capture-protocol.md carrying the GENERATED COPY header, and brings the file under --check and under the orphan guard.
  2. Delete the hand-written harvest pipeline and its surrounding duplicate prose at plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/operating-principles.md:76-79 (and the ~1,800 characters of harvest prose around it that restates the protocol), replacing it with a pointer to references/shared/findings-capture-protocol.md.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE, and split to its own bead: deciding whether the harvest query should carry select(.status=="closed"). The vendored copy takes the canonical query verbatim. If the closed-status filter turns out to be correct, it is a change to the SOURCE in retro-spec and affects every consumer, which is why it is not bundled into this wiring change.

Rejected alternative, recorded so it is not re-litigated: a shared private skill holding the protocol, invoked by name from each consumer. Rejected because a skill-name dependency has all three properties specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md:229-232 condemns — it silently depends on co-installation, dangles when a skill is copied alone, and is undiscoverable from the referencing skill's own tree — and is worse on the third, since a ../ path at least trips scripts/check-skills.sh while a skill name trips nothing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check covers a vendored findings-capture-protocol.md under bead-bonanza and exits 0.
2. operating-principles.md states no jq pipeline of its own for harvesting findings.
3. Any correction to the query was made in retro-spec's source copy, not in a generated file.
4. CI fails if the two ever diverge again.

metadata.tier_reason: two mechanical edits — one MAP line and one deletion — with the generator and CI doing the rest; the hard part was split out to the decision bead

title: Extract dispatch planning into a private plan-sprint skill, dispatched to a subagent rather than run in the orchestrator
description:
Phase 2.5 is SKILL.md:559-818 = 14,805 bytes, plus references/dispatch-plan.md at 7,663.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES THIS. Phase 2.5 runs on every run: SKILL.md:790-793 'on every run — there is no queue-size or bucket-count exemption', and SKILL.md:1021-1023 'The dispatch plan has no lean path.' A private skill invoked in the ORCHESTRATOR'S OWN context therefore saves nothing at the moment of use, and costs more than a reference file: a hidden skill's description stays preloaded in the system prompt of every session forever (~500 chars), and the name dependency is invisible to scripts/check-skills.sh. references/*.md are already lazily loaded — that is the baseline any new skill must beat.

The saving is real only if planning is DISPATCHED TO A SUBAGENT. Planning is read-heavy analytic work: it consumes bd output for every queued bead, runs the C4 overlap query (dispatch-plan.md:106-115), and writes dispatch.md. The skill already establishes the pattern — SKILL.md:1039-1041 'Don't read source files in the orchestrator', and Phase 1.5 delegates grooming for exactly this reason. A subagent can do all of it and return a ~1.5KB wave table.

VERIFIED PREREQUISITE: user-invocable: false exists and does what is needed. Per Claude Code documentation, a skill marked user-invocable: false is hidden from the / menu, remains invokable by the model via the Skill tool including from a subagent, and keeps its description in context. NOT independently confirmed against this build's parser — confirm before relying on it.
design:
MOVE into plan-sprint: 'Classify each bead' (SKILL.md:570-642, 4,450), 'Choose a dispatch mode per bucket' (:643-686, 2,519), 'The dispatch plan' (:788-818, 1,772), and all of references/dispatch-plan.md (7,663). Total ~16,404 bytes out of the orchestrator's path.

KEEP in SKILL.md: 'Tier selection per bead' (:687-739, 2,972) and 'Push policy' (:777-787, 469). These are the orchestrator's own per-bead dispatch acts, not planning rules.

SEND TO A REFERENCE, not a skill: 'WHEN delegation is unavailable — the main-loop fallback' (:740-776, 2,055). It fires only where no Agent tool exists — a low-probability, read-once branch, which is the textbook reference case.

MERGE WITH THE GROOMING DISPATCH; do not add a second agent. Phase 1.5's grooming subagent already returns a wave preview (subagent-prompts.md:52-56) and has already read every bead. A separate planning agent means two partitions to reconcile. Have the grooming subagent invoke plan-sprint as its final act.

INTERFACE. In: run id, RUN_DIR, the ENUMERATED bead id list (never a filter — SKILL.md:799-803), gate profile and gate baseline, model lineup, standing authorization, and Phase 1.5's wave preview. Out: dispatch.md written to disk, and to the caller only the wave table plus one line per override of the preview.

RISK TO MITIGATE. dispatch.md is what recovery reads instead of re-deriving the run (recovery.md:84-91). Moving its authorship into a subagent puts the run's most load-bearing artifact one delegation hop further from the orchestrator. Keep dispatch.md's manifest — the pre-flight stdout block — written by the orchestrator itself.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A plan-sprint skill exists with user-invocable: false, and the flag is confirmed against the installed Claude Code build before merge.
2. SKILL.md no longer carries the classify/dispatch-mode/plan-authoring sections; tier selection and push policy remain.
3. The main-loop fallback lives in a reference file.
4. dispatch.md is still written on every run, still enumerates beads rather than naming a filter, and its manifest is still written by the orchestrator.
5. Recovery can still reconstruct a run from dispatch.md alone.

metadata.tier_reason: creates a new skill and moves a mandatory phase behind a delegation boundary; needs design judgment about the interface and about keeping recovery able to reconstruct a run

title: Factor the shared boilerplate out of the four dispatch prompt templates, and drop restatements of what bd prime already injects
description:

  • SKILL.md:1116-1117 (124) is a verbatim duplicate of :325-326

Also fix while here: references/project-setup.md:93-97 omits bb-backup-run.sh from the permission list, while SKILL.md:212 requires running it after every bead's acceptance check — so its omission costs a permission prompt per bead.
design:

Extend subagent-prompts.md:29-30 — the sentence that authorizes this factoring — to state explicitly that the orchestrator concatenates preamble plus template into the text it sends. title: pre-flight-check.sh writes user-global state (~/.claude/settings.json and dolt global config); warn and suggest instead of mutating
description:
pre-flight-check.sh silently mutates state outside the repository, on behalf of a skill the user invoked for a different purpose.

Measured at scripts/pre-flight-check.sh:
  • :284  DENY_ENTRY="$(add_deny_entry "$HOME/.claude/settings.json")" — adds 'WebFetch(domain:eventsapi.dolthub.com)' to permissions.deny in the USER-SCOPE settings file (helper at :182-184).
  • :269  dolt config --global --add metrics.disabled true — a global user-config write.

Both exist to suppress Dolt telemetry. Neither is disclosed in SKILL.md's 'Side effects — what each script leaves behind' section (SKILL.md:1111-1113 lists only three effects); grep -n 'deny' SKILL.md returns nothing.

Decision taken 2026-08-12: a pre-flight check should not perform a privileged configuration change on the user's global environment. It should detect the condition, warn that Dolt telemetry may emit, state that any telemetry-related permission prompt can be ignored, and print the exact command the user may run themselves if they want it suppressed.

This also removes an ordering hazard: the sandbox refuses the dolt write, and the script's own comment at :17-19 explains that a blind write 'fails in a way that looks like a dolt bug rather than a permission decision'. Not writing at all makes that whole branch unnecessary.
design:
Replace both writes with detection plus advice. Keep the measurement (is metrics.disabled already true; is the deny entry already present) because reporting the state is useful; drop the mutation. The self-test fixtures at :123-131 that exercise add_deny_entry's idempotency go with it.

Keep this bead's scope to the two user-global writes. The other undisclosed side effects (the probe push to the remote, and 'bash -c' on commands parsed out of AGENTS.md under --gate-baseline) are a separate disclosure bead.
acceptance_criteria:
1. pre-flight-check.sh makes no write to $HOME/.claude/settings.json.
2. pre-flight-check.sh makes no write to global dolt config.
3. Where telemetry suppression is absent, the script says so, states that telemetry permission prompts can be ignored, and prints the command the user may run.
4. The script's exit status does not depend on either condition.
notes:
SHARED SURFACE. This bead edits plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh, and so do agent-plugins-q1h, agent-plugins-9p4, agent-plugins-8mv and agent-plugins-b13. Dispatch these four as ONE shared-surface batch, or strictly sequentially. They must NOT go into a concurrent worktree wave: all four touch the same regions of one file and would produce conflicting edits.

They are deliberately left unchained by dependencies so a batch remains possible.

metadata.tier_reason: removes two writes and restructures the surrounding branch plus its self-test fixtures; the decision is already made, the execution needs care

title: SKILL.md's script side-effects list omits four effects, including a push to the remote and arbitrary command execution
description:
SKILL.md:1106-1109 justifies the side-effects section thus: 'the scripts are executed, not read, so an agent that obeys that rule cannot discover a side effect by opening the file.' The list at :1111-1113 then names three effects. Four more exist, verified in the script:

  • pre-flight-check.sh:284  — writes $HOME/.claude/settings.json (user-global permissions.deny).
  • pre-flight-check.sh:269  — writes global dolt config (metrics.disabled).
  • pre-flight-check.sh:494-495 — 'git push -q $REMOTE HEAD:refs/dolt/preflight-probe-$$' then --delete. This WRITES TO THE REMOTE.
  • pre-flight-check.sh:455  — under --gate-baseline, runs 'bash -c $cmd' on commands parsed out of AGENTS.md.

Also undisclosed: bb-close-bead.sh:161 writes msgfile=/tmp/bb-commit-msg.$$ using a hard-coded /tmp rather than ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} — a portability hazard the script's own self-test treats as worth testing elsewhere — and does not remove it on the git-commit failure path (:163-164 fails before :165's rm -f).

The remote push and the arbitrary-command execution are the two that matter: an agent cannot consent to what it is not told, and the section exists precisely to be that telling.

## Steps to Reproduce

From the repository root, list what the scripts actually write and compare against what SKILL.md discloses:

    sed -n '1111,1113p' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md
    sed -n '269p;284p;455p;494,495p' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh
    grep -n 'deny' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md
    sed -n '159,165p' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-close-bead.sh

EXPECTED: every write outside the run directory appears in the side-effects list.
ACTUAL: the list names three effects. The global settings.json write, the global dolt config write, the probe push to the REMOTE, and the --gate-baseline 'bash -c' are absent; the grep for 'deny' returns nothing. bb-close-bead.sh's temp file uses a hard-coded /tmp and is not removed on the commit-failure path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every write outside the run directory performed by any bundled script appears in SKILL.md's side-effects list.
2. The remote probe push and the --gate-baseline command execution are named explicitly.
3. bb-close-bead.sh uses ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} and removes its temp file on every exit path.
notes:
SHARED SURFACE. This bead edits plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh, and so do agent-plugins-q1h, agent-plugins-9p4, agent-plugins-8mv and agent-plugins-b13. Dispatch these four as ONE shared-surface batch, or strictly sequentially. They must NOT go into a concurrent worktree wave: all four touch the same regions of one file and would produce conflicting edits.

They are deliberately left unchained by dependencies so a batch remains possible.

metadata.tier_reason: the disclosure list is mechanical, but the bb-close-bead.sh temp-file fix must be correct on every exit path including the failure path

title: SKILL.md and subagent-prompts.md both claim pre-flight runs 'git worktree prune'; no script does
description:
Two documents assert a behaviour that is not implemented anywhere.

SKILL.md:90-91: 'Pre-flight and recovery both run git worktree prune before trusting the list.'
references/subagent-prompts.md:350-353: 'git worktree prune before git worktree list in pre-flight and in recovery.'

Measured 2026-08-12: grep -rn 'worktree prune' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/ returns zero matches. The only place it actually appears is references/recovery.md:99-108, which instructs the agent to run it by hand during recovery.

Consequence: an orchestrator trusting the documented behaviour reads 'git worktree list' output that may still carry stale registrations for worktrees whose directories are gone. Acceptance signal 4 (SKILL.md:181-185) treats worktree removal as state rather than testimony, so a stale registration reads as a bead still in flight.

## Steps to Reproduce

From the repository root:

    grep -rn 'worktree prune' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/
    grep -n 'worktree prune' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/subagent-prompts.md

EXPECTED: the first grep finds the prune the documents say pre-flight runs.
ACTUAL: the first grep returns nothing; the second returns the two claims that it happens.
design:
DECIDED: add the prune to the script. Do not treat this as a choice at implementation time.

scripts/pre-flight-check.sh runs 'git worktree prune' before it enumerates worktrees, making the two documents true rather than editing them to be weaker.

Rejected alternative, recorded so it is not re-litigated: correcting SKILL.md:90-91 and subagent-prompts.md:350-353 to say prune is a recovery-time step the agent runs by hand. Rejected because the operation is deterministic and cheap, and specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md:263-264 requires a script rather than prose instructions where an operation is deterministic. Weakening the documents would move a mechanical step back into prose, against the direction the standard sets.

references/recovery.md:99-108 keeps its by-hand prune instruction: recovery is entered by an orchestrator with no memory that may be unable to run the script at all.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Either pre-flight-check.sh runs 'git worktree prune' before enumerating, or no document claims it does.
2. grep across plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/ finds no claim about a script behaviour that the scripts do not implement.

metadata.tier_reason: mechanical: add one prune call before worktree enumeration; the design pins the choice and leaves nothing to decide

I placed the prune call at the very top of the script (right after cd to repo root, before any other check) rather than inventing an enumeration step to put it 'before' — this satisfies the docs' claim without adding scope the AC didn't ask for.

title: CI runs on every push to every branch and on draft PRs
description: Both checks.yml and cli.yml trigger on push to branches:["**"] and on the default pull_request types, so every push to a working branch burns a full run, every push to a branch with an open PR burns two (push + synchronize), and draft PRs are gated as if they were ready for review. cli.yml's matrix includes macos-latest (10x minute multiplier on private repos) and windows-latest (2x), so the spend is concentrated there. Restrict checks to pull requests that are ready for review, keeping a post-merge run on the default branch.

title: Five shipped skills changed across the 92q epic without a frontmatter version bump
description:
triage-rfc step 5 requires the `version` frontmatter of every changed shipped
skill to be bumped exactly once per triage, after its last change. The RFC
0016-0018 closeout (agent-plugins-92q.21) bumped the plugin (0.16.0 -> 0.17.0)
and the changed reference documents, but the SKILL.md frontmatter versions were
outside that bead's file scope and are still at their pre-sprint values.

MEASURED on the sprint-2 branch, against merge-base ae623c8:

| Shipped skill | SKILL.md diff | frontmatter version |
|---|---|---|
| plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md | 1102 lines changed | still "1.3" |
| plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md | 6 lines changed | still "1.1" |
| plugin/skills/groom-feature-blueprint/SKILL.md | 45 lines changed | still "1.2" |
| plugin/skills/retro-skill/SKILL.md | 3 lines changed | still "0.3" |
| plugin/skills/retro-spec/SKILL.md | 12 lines changed | still "1.3.0" |

plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md did NOT change (only its references did), so it
needs no bump.

Why it matters: triage-rfc step 1's provenance check compares an RFC's cited
`skill_version` against the skill's current version to decide whether a defect
has already been fixed. All three RFCs retired in this triage cite
`skill_version: "1.3"` for bead-bonanza, and bead-bonanza still reports 1.3
after a near-total rewrite - so that check silently returns "unchanged since
the run" for a skill that no longer contains most of the text those RFCs quote.

DESIGN

Bump each of the five, once, MINOR for normative changes:
bead-bonanza 1.3 -> 1.4, groom-beads 1.1 -> 1.2, groom-feature-blueprint
1.2 -> 1.3, retro-skill 0.3 -> 0.4, retro-spec 1.3.0 -> 1.4.0.

Edit the source under plugin/skills/; .claude/skills/<name> are committed
symlinks to it, so there is nothing to mirror. Do NOT bump plugin.json again -
0.17.0 already covers this whole set.

Then correct the "Version bumps" paragraph in each of
rfcs/retired/rfc-0016-close-ceremony-and-finding-harvest.md,
rfc-0017-run-dir-discoverability-and-orchestrator-recovery.md and
rfc-0018-silent-ceremony-loss-and-the-stale-twin.md, which currently records
these bumps as outstanding and names this bead.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [ ] Each of the five SKILL.md files carries a bumped frontmatter version
- [ ] plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json is unchanged at 0.17.0
- [ ] The three retired RFCs' Version bumps paragraphs name the landed values
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0; --strict shows no findings beyond the
      2-warning baseline; scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check exits 0;
      scripts/validate-corpus.py exits 0
design:
Bump the frontmatter version of each shipped skill whose SKILL.md changed, exactly once, AFTER its last change in this sprint.

The measured table in the description gives each file's pre-sprint value. Increment the minor component unless the skill's own history shows a different convention — retro-spec uses three-part (1.3.0) while the others use two-part (1.3), so follow each file's existing shape rather than normalizing them.

plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md did not change and gets no bump. Note that agent-plugins-d70 may change it; if that bead has landed by the time this runs, spec needs a bump too — check rather than assume.

SEQUENCING: this bead depends on agent-plugins-41z and must run after every other skill-changing bead in the sprint, or it will need doing twice.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every shipped skill whose SKILL.md changed in this sprint has had its frontmatter version incremented exactly once.
2. Each version keeps the two-part or three-part shape that file already used.
3. No skill whose SKILL.md did not change was bumped.
4. The bump is the last change to each of those files in this sprint.
notes:
STILL OPEN AND STILL ACCURATE as of 2026-08-12: plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md frontmatter reads version: "1.3". Confirmed by git log -S that 1.3 was set in commit 9affbca, and that commit 4443f24 ('Sprint 2') changed SKILL.md by 733 insertions / 454 deletions without touching the version line.

SEQUENCING NOTE: the bead-bonanza refinement round opened in this session (epic agent-plugins-41z plus the defect beads) will change all of these skills again. The rule this bead cites — bump exactly once, AFTER the last change — means this bead should be worked LAST among the skill-changing beads, not first, or it will need doing twice.

title: check-skills.sh skips five path prefixes, so a dangling docs/ or scripts/ reference in a skill is never caught
description:
check-skills.sh check 2 ("bundled paths resolve from the file that cites them") skips every backticked path beginning docs/, rfcs/, plans/, word/, ooxml/, scripts/ or .claude/, plus http.

The skip exists because those prefixes are written repo-root-relative while the check resolves from the citing file's directory — resolving them from the file would report every one as broken. Skipping them means a genuinely dangling repo-root path in a skill is invisible to the gate.

Measured 2026-08-12: plugin/skills/retro-skill/SKILL.md cited `docs/standards/skill-best-practices.md` while the document lives at specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md. The gate reported 0 errors throughout.

FIX: for the repo-root-shaped prefixes (docs/, rfcs/, plans/, scripts/, .claude/), resolve from the repo root instead of skipping. Keep the skip only for the prefixes that name a file in the USER's project rather than this one (word/, ooxml/, and the IGNORE set), and for http.

Watch for a second class the gate cannot see: unbackticked paths, and paths inside .sh and .py files under plugin/skills/**. Check 2 matches backticked paths in .md only. Widening that is optional and noisier — the shell scripts are full of $fixture/ and $dest/ expansions that look like paths.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] A backticked docs/, rfcs/, plans/, scripts/ or .claude/ path in a skill file that does not exist at the repo root is reported as an error
[ ] Existing repo-root paths that DO exist still pass; check-skills.sh reports no new errors on a clean tree
[ ] Paths naming a file in the consuming user's project (word/, ooxml/, the IGNORE set) are still skipped

title: Replace the vendored shared-reference copies with symlinks
description:
Reviewer, PR #19 on work-order-definition-of-ready.md: "Should we use symlinks instead of copying this file multiple times?"

VIABLE, and the packaging is why. marketplace.json ships ONE plugin containing all six skills (spec, groom-beads, groom-feature-blueprint, bead-bonanza, retro-spec, retro-skill). The source of truth is plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-definition-of-ready.md and `spec` therefore always installs alongside its consumers, so a relative symlink resolves wherever the plugin lands. The objection that would have killed this — per-skill installation leaving a dangling link — does not apply.

This repo already proves committed symlinks work in practice: .claude/skills/<name> are committed symlinks into plugin/skills/, and they load correctly from the working tree.

WHAT IT REPLACES: scripts/sync-shared-references.sh currently maintains 12 generated copies, each carrying a GENERATED COPY header, plus a --check mode, plus an orphan guard added recently to catch files claiming the header with no MAP entry. Symlinks make a whole class of drift impossible rather than detectable, which is the same single-sourcing argument that four fix-one-place-miss-the-other incidents made this sprint.

VERIFY BEFORE COMMITTING TO IT:
- Whether the install path preserves symlinks or dereferences them (a copying installer turns the link into a duplicate file and silently restores the problem).
- Windows checkouts without symlink support — core.symlinks=false yields a text file containing the path.
- What remains for sync-shared-references.sh afterwards: the strata docs are synced by a different script, and some vendored copies may not be intra-plugin. Do not delete the script without checking which MAP entries it still earns.
- check-skills.sh resolves backticked paths; confirm it follows links.

If the install path dereferences, keep the copies and this closes as rejected with that measurement recorded.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Symlink preservation through the actual install path is MEASURED, not assumed, and the result recorded
- [ ] Where viable: the intra-plugin vendored copies become relative symlinks, and sync-shared-references.sh keeps only the MAP entries it still earns
- [ ] check-skills.sh and the gates pass with symlinks in place
- [ ] Where not viable: closed as rejected, with the measurement that settled it
notes: rejected: a core.symlinks=false checkout turns the symlinked reference into a 58-byte text file holding the path while check-skills.sh still reports PASS (silent, undetectable by any gate; checks.yml is ubuntu-only), and scripts/install-spec-skill.sh's cp -RL dereferences the link back into a duplicate file (measured: 9780-byte regular file in the installed tree).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: MEASUREMENT 1 — install path DEREFERENCES. Two install paths exist. (a) README's plugin path is a marketplace git clone (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json ships one plugin, source ./plugin); no packaging script and no artifact-producing workflow exists in this repo for the plugin — release.yml builds only the Go CLI binaries — so the clone itself is outside this repo and NOT MEASURED here. (b) README also documents scripts/install-spec-skill.sh, which installs each skill separately into $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/skills/<skill> with 'cp -RL "$src" "$dest"'. -L dereferences by design; the script's own comment says '-L dereferences symlinks, in case one reappears in the source tree', and it carries a guard that fails on any broken symlink under plugin/skills. MEASURED: copied the worktree to a scratch dir, replaced plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md with a relative symlink ../../../spec/references/work-order-definition-of-ready.md, ran the script with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed at a temp dir. Installed result: '-rw-r--r-- 9780 work-order-definition-of-ready.md' — a regular file, not a link. The symlink is materialised back into a duplicate copy at install time.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: MEASUREMENT 2 — Windows checkout is fatal AND silent. This is the measurement that settles the bead on its own. MEASURED: built a git repo containing the relative symlink (git ls-files -s confirms mode 120000, so git stores it correctly), then 'git clone -c core.symlinks=false'. Result: '-rw-r--r-- 58 work-order-definition-of-ready.md' whose entire content is the single line '../../../spec/references/work-order-definition-of-ready.md'. An agent on such a checkout that reads references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md gets one line of path text instead of the readiness gate. Worse, check-skills.sh on that same clone reports '0 error(s), 2 warning(s) / RESULT: PASS' — the file exists and is non-empty, so the resolve check is satisfied. No gate in this repo detects it: checks.yml (skill invariants + vendored references) is ubuntu-latest only; cli.yml is the workflow that runs windows-latest and it works only in cli/, never touching plugin/skills. Windows is an explicitly supported consumer platform (release.yml cross-compiles windows/amd64 and windows/arm64; .gitattributes exists specifically because cli.yml runs on windows-latest). Vendored copies are byte-identical on every platform; symlinks trade that for a silent content loss on one.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: MEASUREMENT 3 — check-skills.sh DOES follow links (favourable, but not enough to carry the bead). Run empirically on the scratch copy, not reasoned about. With a valid relative symlink in place: '0 error(s), 2 warning(s) / RESULT: PASS', identical to baseline. With the symlink deliberately repointed at a nonexistent target: 'ERROR plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md: backticked path does not resolve from this file: references/shared/work-order-definition-of-ready.md', exit 1. So the resolver follows the link and a DANGLING link is caught. It cannot catch measurement 2's failure, because there the link is not dangling — it is not a link at all, it is a present, readable, wrong file.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: MEASUREMENT 4 — sync-shared-references.sh survives regardless; it could only have shrunk. Its MAP has 11 entries, all intra-plugin (plugin/skills/<consumer>/references/shared/ <- plugin/skills/<owner>/references/), so all 11 are the symlinkable set. Its PATH_MAP has 1 entry, rfcs/findings-capture.md, which is outside plugin/ and therefore not symlinkable within the shipped plugin; that entry is owned by another bead. The orphan guard (a GENERATED COPY header naming a generator nothing runs) is destination-agnostic and stays useful for any remaining copy. Net: even in the fully viable case the script keeps its --check mode, its PATH_MAP entry and its orphan guard — the win was never 'delete the script', only 'shrink the MAP from 11 to 0'. Also note --check would have needed those 11 entries removed in the same change: it diffs the destination against a render that prepends the GENERATED COPY header, and a symlink to the header-less source reads as STALE (differs).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: OUTCOME — NOT VIABLE, closed as rejected, zero file changes. Two independent fatal measurements, either sufficient: (1) a core.symlinks=false checkout silently replaces the reference content with a 58-byte path string while every gate reports PASS; (2) the documented scripts/install-spec-skill.sh path materialises the link back into a duplicate file via cp -RL. The premise that made the bead plausible held up — marketplace.json does ship one plugin, a relative link does resolve inside plugin/skills/, git does store mode 120000, and .claude/skills/<name> committed symlinks do work — but those establish only that the link resolves on a POSIX developer checkout, which was never the risk. The vendored copies plus --check stay: they are platform-invariant and the drift they permit is DETECTED, whereas the symlink failure mode is UNDETECTABLE by anything in this repo. Do not reopen without first changing the Windows story; a partial conversion is not available either, since the Windows failure applies to every one of the 11 MAP entries equally.

title: Bake findings-capture into the skills that need it, and stop writing rfcs/findings-capture.md
description:
User decision, 2026-08-12 (PR #19 review, then corrected in follow-up): "We need to bake findings-capture into the skill(s) that need it -- definitely not the bead. We want retros. We should also stop writing a copy to rfcs/findings-capture.md within the project -- I have no idea why we do that."

TODAY: bead-bonanza gates its retro wiring on a file existing in the consuming project — references/operating-principles.md says "If rfcs/findings-capture.md exists (retro-spec protocol) in the project, every batch prompt includes: record retro:-prefixed bd comments...". So a project that has not adopted the retro-spec protocol silently gets no findings capture, which is backwards: we always want retros.

TWO CHANGES:
1. Move the protocol INTO the skills that need it (bead-bonanza, and any other skill that harvests retro: comments). The instruction to record retro: comments becomes unconditional, not gated on a file in the consuming project. Note the correction: into the SKILL, not into the bead — a bead is per-issue and would carry it N times.
2. Stop generating rfcs/findings-capture.md in this project. Note that agent-plugins-92q.28 recently wired that file INTO the sync MAP as a managed generated copy, which entrenched the thing being removed — check what else references it before deleting, including scripts/sync-shared-references.sh and scripts/validate-corpus.py.

Check which other skills reference the protocol (retro-spec, retro-skill, groom-feature-blueprint, the work-order template all mention the shared channel) so the wiring moves rather than fragments.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The retro: comment protocol is stated in the skills that need it, unconditionally — no gate on a file existing in the consuming project
- [ ] rfcs/findings-capture.md is no longer generated, and nothing references it (sync MAP, validate-corpus, skill prose)
- [ ] Every skill that harvests retro: comments still describes the same channel — the protocol moved, it did not fragment
- [ ] A project with no retro-spec adoption still gets findings capture, verified by reading the dispatch prompt a run would send

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Consumer survey was one command, re-runnable: `grep -rn "findings-capture" . | grep -v '^./.git/'`. It found NINE live consumers, more than the four the bead named: (1) plugin/skills/retro-spec/references/findings-capture-protocol.md (source of truth, said work orders read the vendored project copy); (2) plugin/skills/retro-spec/SKILL.md; (3) plugin/skills/retro-skill/SKILL.md (points at its vendored shared copy — needed no change); (4) plugin/skills/groom-feature-blueprint/SKILL.md (FOUR sites: the reference list, the Phase 2 Retro-section rule, the Phase 3 'vendor the protocol' step that WRITES the file, and both verbatim Retro blocks); (5) plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md; (6) plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/operating-principles.md (the gate); (7) plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/SKILL.md ('Wire findings capture when the repo has it'); (8) scripts/sync-shared-references.sh (PATH_MAP entry + a stale orphan-guard comment naming the file); (9) cli/profile/profile_test.go (a realSlugs provenance string). Plus the two vendored work-order-template copies and two vendored protocol copies, which the sync script regenerates.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: The real generator of rfcs/findings-capture.md was groom-feature-blueprint Phase 3 ('vendor the findings capture protocol: copy references/shared/findings-capture-protocol.md to rfcs/findings-capture.md in the target project'), not the sync MAP. Removing only the PATH_MAP entry and the file would have left the next grooming run recreating it. Deleting that Phase 3 step is what actually satisfies 'stop writing a copy'; the sync MAP entry was downstream bookkeeping for a file another skill authored.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: validate-corpus.py delegated count, real output. BEFORE: 'delegated  rfcs/findings-capture.md: generated copy — checked by scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check' then 'checked 37 documents, 0 findings, 6 excluded, 1 delegated'. AFTER: 'checked 37 documents, 0 findings, 6 excluded, 0 delegated', exit 0, no delegated block printed. sync-shared-references.sh --check went from 'all 12 vendored references are current' to 'all 11', with '3 further generated file(s) name a generator this repo runs; 0 unmanaged' unchanged.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Dispatch-prompt evidence for the last acceptance criterion, read from plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/subagent-prompts.md as a subagent would receive it. Sequential per-bead template step 6, verbatim: '6. **Record findings as `retro:` comments on {ID}** — one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences each, friction only, no root-causing. That comment channel is what downstream retros and RFCs actually read.' Both batch templates inherit it by reference: 'Run the per-bead workflow (claim -> read -> implement -> write handoff file -> `retro:` comments -> atomic close -> stage -> single commit -> optional push) exactly as in the sequential template'. `grep -n 'findings-capture|rfcs/' subagent-prompts.md` returns nothing — no project file is named and no condition guards the step, so a project with zero retro-spec adoption still gets findings capture.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Tried and reverted — rewording bead-bonanza's operating-principles.md to end with 'stated once in `retro-spec`'s `findings-capture-protocol.md`'. check-skills.sh rejected it twice (once for the file, once for its .claude/skills symlink): 'backticked path does not resolve from this file: findings-capture-protocol.md'. The lint treats any backticked filename as a path that must resolve relative to the citing file, and bead-bonanza vendors no copy of that document. Reworded to prose ('the findings-capture protocol, stated once in the `retro-spec` skill's references') rather than adding a MAP entry to vendor it into bead-bonanza.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Decided silently, four. (1) Did NOT add 'bead-bonanza <tab> retro-spec/references/findings-capture-protocol.md' to the sync MAP — it would have given bead-bonanza a resolvable backticked path and a real one-authoritative-statement pointer, but the dispatch prompt already carries the whole operative rule and the bead's stated gate expectation was 12 -> 11, which an added entry would have kept at 12. (2) Kept PATH_MAP as an empty heredoc with a comment stating what it is for, rather than deleting the mechanism — the bead says remove one entry, not the mechanism; the loop's '[ -n "$dest_rel" ] || continue' guard already handles the empty case. (3) Left scripts/validate-corpus.py entirely unchanged: with 0 delegated files the 'if delegated:' branch is simply false, the summary honestly prints '0 delegated', and the docstring's claim stays conditionally true, so there is no misleading message to fix. (4) Left rfcs/inbox/** and rfcs/outbox/** RFCs citing 'rfcs/findings-capture.md' alone — those are provenance records of what a past run actually read, and rewriting them would falsify evidence.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Version bumps not asked for but required by the vendoring stamp, which records the source version in each generated header: findings-capture-protocol.md 0.3 -> 0.4 (updated_at to 2026-08-12) and work-order-template.md 1.3 -> 1.4. Without the bump the regenerated copies would carry a header claiming a version whose content no longer matches.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: The Go gate has a directory trap. 'go test ./cli/profile/...' from the repo root fails with 'directory prefix cli/profile does not contain main module or its selected dependencies' — the module root is cli/, so it must be run from there as 'go test ./profile/...' (passes). Only a one-string change in profile_test.go here, but the wrong invocation reads like a broken build rather than a wrong cwd.

title: validate-corpus.py skips GENERATED COPY files with no orphan check of its own
description:
Reported by agent-plugins-92q.28 while fixing the same class of bug in sync-shared-references.sh.

scripts/validate-corpus.py globs rfcs/**/*.md and SKIPS any file whose first line is a GENERATED COPY header. That header therefore confers "someone else checks this" status in a SECOND place, and validate-corpus.py does no orphan check — so a file can claim to be generated, be skipped by the corpus validator, and have nothing regenerate it. That is exactly the blind spot 92q.28 closed in sync-shared-references.sh, surviving in another gate.

92q.28 added an orphan guard to sync-shared-references.sh --check: every tracked *.md opening with the header must name a generator this repo can run. The same guard, or a delegation to it, is what validate-corpus.py needs.

NOTE a pre-existing container gap found while verifying: validate-corpus.py cannot run here at all (ImportError, needs pip install jsonschema pyyaml, fails before reading any repo content). Whoever takes this needs those deps to test.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A file claiming GENERATED COPY that nothing regenerates is reported by validate-corpus.py, or explicitly delegated to sync-shared-references.sh --check with that delegation stated
- [ ] Verified by breaking it: an orphan probe file makes the check fail, quoted from real output
- [ ] The jsonschema/pyyaml dependency gap is either resolved or recorded where a runner will see it

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro: PRE-FIX demonstration that an orphan slips through. Probe rfcs/zz-orphan-probe.md, git-added, first line '<!-- GENERATED COPY — DO NOT EDIT.' and 'Regenerate with: scripts/there-is-no-such-script.sh'. `python3 scripts/validate-corpus.py` output:

    excluded  rfcs/findings-capture.md: no-frontmatter
    excluded  rfcs/retro-log.md: no-frontmatter
    excluded  rfcs/zz-orphan-probe.md: no-frontmatter
    ...
    checked 37 documents, 0 findings, 8 excluded
    EXIT=0

Two defects in one line. The orphan exits 0, and the reason given is wrong: the file HAS frontmatter, six lines down. The same probe against the authority in the same working tree:

    scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check
      ORPHAN  rfcs/zz-orphan-probe.md
              carries a GENERATED COPY header naming no generator this
              repo can run ("scripts/there-is-no-such-script.sh"). Wire it to one, or drop the header.
    RESULT: 1 file(s) claim to be generated copies that nothing regenerates.
    EXIT=1

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro: POST-FIX failure output, same probe, same working tree. `python3 scripts/validate-corpus.py`:

    error  scripts/sync-shared-references.sh: generated-copy/delegated: 2 file(s) in this script's search scope (rfcs/findings-capture.md, rfcs/zz-orphan-probe.md) open with a GENERATED COPY header, so they are checked by `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` instead of here. That check failed (exit 1):
        | ORPHAN  rfcs/zz-orphan-probe.md
        |           carries a GENERATED COPY header naming no generator this
        |           repo can run ("scripts/there-is-no-such-script.sh"). Wire it to one, or drop the header.
        | RESULT: 1 file(s) claim to be generated copies that nothing regenerates.
    ...
    delegated  rfcs/findings-capture.md: generated copy — checked by scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check
    delegated  rfcs/zz-orphan-probe.md: generated copy — checked by scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check

    checked 37 documents, 1 findings, 6 excluded, 2 delegated
    EXIT=1

Probe removed (`git rm --cached` + `rm`), re-run: 'checked 37 documents, 0 findings, 6 excluded, 1 delegated', EXIT=0. `git status --porcelain` after removal showed only ' M scripts/validate-corpus.py'.

Second failure path also exercised, not just asserted: temporarily moved scripts/sync-shared-references.sh aside and re-ran, giving

    error  scripts/sync-shared-references.sh: generated-copy/no-authority: orphan detection for 1 generated-copy file(s) (rfcs/findings-capture.md) is delegated to `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh`, which is not present. Restore it, or check those files here.
    EXIT=1

The delegation may not fail open — a missing authority is the same blind spot as a missing check.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro: chose (b), invoke rather than restate — (a) was rejected because nothing enforces a comment.

scripts/validate-corpus.py now detects the GENERATED COPY header itself (constant GENERATED_COPY_HEADER), collects those paths into a `delegated` list instead of letting read_frontmatter mislabel them 'no-frontmatter', and after the loop runs ORPHAN_AUTHORITY = scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check as a subprocess, turning a non-zero exit into a finding with the delegate's full output quoted inline. A missing authority is its own finding. Zero lines of the orphan rule are restated here — the judgement stays in one place, so the two gates cannot disagree, which is what the script's docstring already demands of overlapping checks.

The delegation is visible to a reader of validate-corpus.py alone in three places: the module docstring ('DELEGATED, not skipped'), a comment at the skip site in the loop, and — on PASSING runs too — a 'delegated  <path>: generated copy — checked by scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check' line plus a delegated count in the summary. A pass that prints nothing about these files is how the blind spot read as health.

Accepted consequence, stated in the code: the authority answers one question for the whole repo, so when it fails validate-corpus.py reports its entire output, including staleness unrelated to any SEARCH match. Filtering its output for ORPHAN lines would be reimplementing its judgement here, which is exactly what (b) exists to avoid. In CI both steps then go red for one cause.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro: how CI resolves the Python deps, and what I did.

.github/workflows/checks.yml, `checks` job, has a step 'Install schema validation dependencies' running `python3 -m pip install --quiet jsonschema pyyaml` immediately before the validate-corpus.py step. There is no requirements file anywhere in the repo — that inline line is the whole dependency story.

Resolved rather than only noted: added a runnable block to AGENTS.md under '### Custom gates' with the same install command plus the script invocation, stating that a clean container has neither module and that the script exits before reading a document without them. Deliberately did NOT add a requirements.txt: a second declaration would drift from the workflow line, and the point was to make local and CI resolve identically. Noted `--break-system-packages` as the fallback for an externally-managed environment.

Confirmed the gap was real here first: `python3 -c 'import jsonschema, yaml'` -> ModuleNotFoundError. `python3 -m pip install --quiet jsonschema pyyaml` succeeded in this container without --break-system-packages (root, pip warns about it but proceeds), so the documented first line is the one CI runs verbatim. No venv created, nothing to gitignore.

Silent decision: aligned the ImportError message to the CI command — it said 'error: pip install jsonschema pyyaml', now 'error: python3 -m pip install jsonschema pyyaml', so the text a runner sees is copy-pasteable and matches both AGENTS.md and checks.yml. Docstring 'Requires:' line updated the same way.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro: what did not work, and what I decided silently.

Did not work / corrected mid-flight: the first no-authority message read '...hands orphan detection for 1 file(s) to this script, which is not present', where 'this script' was ambiguous because the finding is keyed on the authority's own path. Reworded to name scripts/sync-shared-references.sh explicitly. Caught only because I actually ran the missing-authority path instead of assuming its text.

Scope check on the delegation trigger: the subprocess runs only when a GENERATED COPY file actually falls in SEARCH. Today exactly one does (rfcs/findings-capture.md), so the delegated path executes on every real run and cannot rot unexercised. plugin/skills/*/references/shared/*.md are NOT matched by SEARCH — the glob `plugin/skills/*/references/*.md` does not descend into shared/ — so they never trigger it; the authority covers them on its own, over all tracked *.md.

Silent decisions:
- Invoked the authority as `bash <path> --check` rather than executing it directly, so the delegation does not break if the executable bit is lost on a checkout that does not preserve mode.
- Ran it with cwd=ROOT so it resolves the same repo whether validate-corpus.py is invoked from a worktree or by absolute path.
- Left the pre-existing historical paragraph in the SEARCH comment (the 'docs/**/*.md used to lead this list' narrative) alone — not mine, and rewriting it would widen the diff. I did rewrite the adjacent 'Not listed:' paragraph, which was the skip rationale and is in scope.
- Filed no new bead: the `&&`-chained test gate in AGENTS.md is already agent-plugins-txq, and 'enable --strict in CI' is agent-plugins-9ko.

Gates, run separately: check-skills.sh PASS (0 errors, 2 warnings); check-skills.sh --strict FAIL, 0 errors 2 warnings — the stated baseline, no new findings; sync-shared-references.sh --check 'all 12 vendored references are current, 3 further generated file(s) name a generator this repo runs; 0 unmanaged'; sync-strata-docs.sh --check 'all 3 vendored strata docs match'; validate-corpus.py 'checked 37 documents, 0 findings, 6 excluded, 1 delegated', exit 0.

title: references/final-report.md does not exist, but bead Designs reference it
description: agent-plugins-92q.12 found its own Design directing it to add content to plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/final-report.md. That file does not exist in the tree. The Phase 4 report specification is still inline in SKILL.md — the extraction was planned (agent-plugins-92q.7) but never landed, and at least one bead was groomed as though it had. Either create the file as part of 92q.7 or correct the Designs that assume it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Either references/final-report.md exists and holds the Phase 4 report spec, or every bead Design referencing it is corrected
- [ ] grep across beads and skill files shows no reference to a file that does not exist

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
retro: AUDIT METHOD — re-runnable, do not redo by eye.

Corpus (a) tracker: bd list --all --limit 0 --include-gates --include-infra --json (162 issues; the default limit of 50 hides two thirds of them). Scanned description, design, notes, acceptance_criteria.
Corpus (b) skill files: every .md/.sh/.py/.json under plugin/skills/**, skipping files whose first line is '<!-- GENERATED COPY'.

Extraction: regex for slash-bearing paths ending in a known extension, then existence-tested three ways — from the citing file's directory, from its skill root, and from the repo root — plus a suffix test against git ls-files, because beads write skill-relative paths like references/recovery.md that resolve under plugin/skills/<skill>/. Placeholders (RUN_DIR/, WORK/, .../, globs, $VARS) filtered out.

Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agent-plugins/f7294766-dd3c-454c-8922-b58eebf1fbbb/scratchpad/audit_paths.py (scratchpad, not committed — it is a one-shot, and check-skills.sh is where a standing gate belongs).

TWO TRAPS in writing this yourself:
1. Order the extension alternation jsonl|json, not json|jsonl, and anchor the tail with (?![A-Za-z0-9_-]). Leftmost-first alternation matches .jsonl as .json and manufactured 5 phantom findings across ~40 beads before I caught it.
2. Existence must be tested relative to the skill directory, not the repo root. Testing repo-root-only produced 71 candidates, of which 33 were false.

title: rfcs/findings-capture.md claims to be a generated copy, but no sync MAP covers it — and --check reports all references current
description:
`rfcs/findings-capture.md` opens with:

```
<!-- GENERATED COPY — DO NOT EDIT.
     Source of truth: plugin/skills/retro-spec/references/findings-capture-protocol.md (version 0.3)
     Regenerate with: scripts/sync-shared-references.sh
     Edit the source, then re-run that script. -->
```

**It is not generated by that script.** The MAP in
`scripts/sync-shared-references.sh` lists exactly two destinations for that
source — `groom-feature-blueprint` and `retro-skill` — and `rfcs/` is not among
them:

```
$ grep -n "findings-capture" scripts/sync-shared-references.sh
52:groom-feature-blueprint	retro-spec/references/findings-capture-protocol.md
53:retro-skill	retro-spec/references/findings-capture-protocol.md
$ scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check
RESULT: all 11 vendored references are current.
```

`--check` reports everything current while never looking at this file.

Discovered by the agent implementing `agent-plugins-92q.18`, which had to correct
the harvest command in the protocol. It edited the source, ran the sync, and
then had to hand-edit `rfcs/findings-capture.md` separately after noticing the
copy had not moved.

**The failure mode is drift that looks impossible.** The header instructs
readers not to edit the file and tells them the script maintains it. The script
doesn't. So the next person to change the protocol will edit the source, re-run
the sync, see `RESULT: all N vendored references are current`, and reasonably
believe every copy moved. This one won't have — and because the header forbids
hand-editing, nobody will think to check it. The two mechanisms that should
catch drift (the header's instruction and the `--check` gate) both actively
point away from the file that has drifted.

This is the same shape as the run's other findings: a claim of sufficiency that
runs clean and proves nothing.
design:
Decide which of two states the file should be in, then make it true. Do not
leave it in the current third state, which is neither.

**Option A — bring it under the script (preferred unless there is a reason not
to).** Add `rfcs/findings-capture.md` to `sync-shared-references.sh`'s MAP as a
third destination for `retro-spec/references/findings-capture-protocol.md`, then
run the sync and confirm `--check` covers 12 references rather than 11. The
header then becomes true as written, `--check` gains real coverage, and CI
catches future drift on every push.

Note the MAP's existing entries are `<skill> <source-path>` pairs resolving to
`plugin/skills/<skill>/references/shared/<basename>`. A destination outside
`plugin/skills/` does not fit that shape, so this needs either a per-entry
destination override or a second MAP for non-skill destinations. Keep whichever
you choose minimal and consistent with the script's existing style.

**Option B — if the file is deliberately a project-local variant** rather than a
copy, then the header is simply wrong. Replace it with one stating what the file
is, that it is maintained by hand, and which document it tracks — so a reader
knows to check the source when the protocol changes.

**Either way, add a guard against the general case.** A file carrying a
`GENERATED COPY` header that no sync MAP covers is undetectable today. Have
`sync-shared-references.sh --check` scan for that header across the repository
and fail when it finds one it does not manage:

```sh
grep -rl 'GENERATED COPY — DO NOT EDIT' --include='*.md' . \
  | while read -r f; do managed "$f" || echo "unmanaged generated file: $f"; done
```

That is the part with lasting value — the specific file is one instance, and the
gate currently cannot see any of them.

**Verify by breaking it.** Before closing, confirm the new check actually fires:
add the header to a scratch file, run `--check`, see it fail, remove the file.
Record the observed output. A guard that has only been seen to pass is the
failure this bead is about.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] rfcs/findings-capture.md is either covered by sync-shared-references.sh's MAP, or its header is corrected to say it is hand-maintained and which document it tracks
- [ ] IF brought under the script: --check reports 12 references and the file regenerates from the source
- [ ] sync-shared-references.sh --check fails when it finds a GENERATED COPY header on a file no MAP covers
- [ ] That new check was verified by making it fail on a scratch file, with the observed output recorded
- [ ] No other file in the repo carries an unmanaged GENERATED COPY header, or each one found is reported

metadata.tier_reason: Small script change, but it edits the gate that guards every vendored reference; a wrong MAP entry silently stops maintaining a real copy.

lasting value beyond this one file.

Carrying a GENERATED COPY header now obliges the file to name a generator this
repo can actually run. --check scans tracked *.md, and for each file whose
first line opens the header:

the guard, so the header this script stamps and the header the guard matches
cannot drift apart — the failure one level up from the one this bead fixed.

Scan is 'git ls-files' (with a find fallback outside a checkout) rather than a
raw filesystem walk: the gate speaks for what is committed, so an untracked
scratch copy in a working tree does not turn CI red.
