title: Stop .beads/issues.jsonl conflicting across branches: adopt a beads sync branch if upstream has one, else write a union-by-id merge driver
description:
`.beads/issues.jsonl` is committed by every agent that closes a bead, and it has
**no git merge driver**. `CLAUDE.md` states the consequence: *"There is no merge
driver configured for it, so beads created on two branches will conflict
textually on merge. Prefer creating beads on one branch until that is
resolved."*

That warning has been costing capability, and its cost is about to rise.

- It is why **worktree-parallel dispatch is currently unusable concurrently.**
  Every worktree agent must `bd export > .beads/issues.jsonl` in its own
  directory before committing (measured on `agent-plugins-t09`: auto-export
  always writes the MAIN checkout's copy, so a worktree's own file goes stale —
  DB 28 issues, main file 28 lines, worktree file 23, and `git status` read
  clean). N worktrees therefore commit N near-identical full exports of one
  shared database onto N branches. Merging them is an N-way textual conflict in
  a generated file.
- It is also why the project's standing advice is to confine bead creation to a
  single branch, which is a real constraint on ordinary parallel work, not just
  on this skill.

**The file is close to the ideal merge-driver case.** It is JSONL: one
self-describing record per line, each carrying a stable `id`, with no ordering
significance and no cross-line syntax. A union-by-id merge is well defined:
take every record from both sides, and where an `id` appears on both, resolve to
one. Nothing about that requires understanding the schema.

Investigated 2026-08-10 and ruled out as alternatives:

- **A `bd`-native sync branch does not exist.** `bd branch` branches the *Dolt
  database*, not the export. `bd config` exposes only
  `export.auto|path|git-add|interval`; there is no export-branch key.
- **`bd dolt push` to a Dolt remote** is the upstream sync model and is dead in
  this environment — the egress proxy returns 403 and `refs/dolt/data` does not
  exist on the GitHub remote.
- **`export.git-add: false` with the orchestrator owning the export** would work
  and needs no new code, but it breaks the "one commit carries code and closure"
  invariant and opens exactly the window that produced the silent close-export
  failure filed as `agent-plugins-92q.24`.

The merge driver is the one option that fixes the general problem rather than
routing around it.
design:
**1. Write the driver.** A small script — `scripts/merge-beads-jsonl.sh` — taking
git's three merge-driver arguments (`%O %A %B`, ancestor / ours / theirs) and
writing the merged result over `%A`.

Semantics, in order:

- Parse all three inputs as JSONL keyed by `.id`.
- A record present on one side only: **take it.** This is the common case —
  two branches each created or closed different beads — and it is why the
  conflict is spurious today.
- A record present on both sides and **byte-identical**: take it.
- A record present on both sides and **differing**: this is the only genuine
  conflict. Resolve by preferring the side whose record differs from the
  ancestor (one side changed it, the other did not). WHEN both differ from the
  ancestor and from each other, do not guess — leave the file with a conflict
  for that record and exit non-zero, so a human sees a real conflict rather than
  a silent overwrite.
- Sort output deterministically by `id`, so the file's line order stops
  depending on export timing and future diffs shrink.

Requires `jq`, which pre-flight already checks for. Must be bash-3.2/BSD-safe
like the other bundled scripts.

**2. Register it.** `.gitattributes` gains
`\.beads/issues\.jsonl merge=beads-jsonl`, and the driver is declared in git
config. **The declaration is the deployment problem, not the script:** merge
drivers live in `.git/config` or user config, neither of which is committed, so
a fresh clone silently falls back to the default driver and produces the
conflicts this bead is removing. Decide and document how it gets installed —
the session-start hook is the obvious candidate in this repo, and
`pre-flight-check.sh` can report whether the driver is registered as another
measured environment fact. Do not leave installation implicit.

**3. Prove it on real conflicts.** Do not close this on reasoning — the whole
epic exists because inferences were recorded without running the command. In a
scratch clone, construct and merge:

- two branches each creating a different bead (must merge clean, both present);
- two branches each closing a different bead (must merge clean, both closures);
- two branches closing the SAME bead (must resolve, one closure, no duplicate);
- two branches making genuinely different edits to the same bead's description
  (must conflict loudly and exit non-zero — verify this case fails, because a
  driver that silently picks a side is worse than the conflict);
- the N-worktree case: three worktrees each closing a bead and each re-exporting
  the full ledger, merged one at a time into the parent branch.

Record every observed outcome in the findings.

**4. Retire the warning it obsoletes.** `CLAUDE.md`'s "prefer creating beads on
one branch until that is resolved" is resolved by this bead — update it rather
than leaving stale advice that suppresses parallel work.

Out of scope: enabling concurrent worktree dispatch. That is a separate decision
resting on this plus the baseRef gate; this bead removes the blocker and says so
without flipping the mode on.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The current upstream beads release was checked for sync-branch support and the finding recorded with the command and version that established it
- [ ] IF upstream supports it: this bead is closed as superseded and an upgrade bead is filed naming the provisioning change and the worktree interaction
- [ ] IF not: scripts/merge-beads-jsonl.sh exists, takes git's %O %A %B arguments, runs clean under 'bash -n', and uses no bash-4 or GNU-only constructs
- [ ] Records present on one side only are taken; byte-identical records are taken; a record differing on one side from the ancestor takes that side
- [ ] A record differing on BOTH sides in different ways leaves a conflict and exits non-zero rather than picking a winner
- [ ] Output is deterministically sorted by id
- [ ] .gitattributes registers the driver and the installation path for the git-config declaration is implemented and documented, not left implicit
- [ ] pre-flight-check.sh reports whether the merge driver is registered
- [ ] All five listed merge scenarios were constructed and run, including the must-conflict case, with observed outcomes in the findings
- [ ] CLAUDE.md's 'prefer creating beads on one branch' advice is updated
- [ ] Concurrent worktree dispatch is NOT enabled by this bead
notes:
## Check upstream BEFORE writing the driver (2026-08-10)

A reviewer reported that beads supports a dedicated sync branch — `bd init
--branch <name>`, read back via `bd config get sync.branch` — letting issue
metadata live on its own git branch instead of in feature-branch commits. If
that exists, it is **strictly better than this bead**: it removes the export
from feature branches entirely rather than teaching git to merge it, and it
needs no code here at all.

**Measured against the installed binary, `bd version 1.1.2 (dev)`:**

- `bd init --help` lists no `--branch` flag. All 40+ flags enumerated; the
  only sync-related one is `--remote` — "Dolt remote URL to clone from and
  persist as sync.remote".
- `bd sync` -> `Error: unknown command "sync" for "bd"`.
- A `sync` config section exists, but its one documented member is
  `sync.remote`, a Dolt remote URL — the mechanism CLAUDE.md records as dead
  in this environment (egress proxy 403; no `refs/dolt/data` on the GitHub
  remote).

**And a trap worth recording, because it nearly produced a false confirmation.**
`bd config get sync.branch` prints `sync.branch (not set in config.yaml)`,
which reads like recognition of a known key. It is not. The wording keys off the
SECTION prefix only:

    sync.branch    -> (not set in config.yaml)
    sync.bogus     -> (not set in config.yaml)     # invented
    export.bogus   -> (not set in config.yaml)     # invented
    bogus.branch   -> (not set)

`sync.branch` and `sync.bogus` are indistinguishable to that command, so it
cannot be used as evidence a key exists.

### Required first step

The above scopes only to the installed build. The reviewer's sources cite
`steveyegge/beads` while this project's CLAUDE.md points at
`gastownhall/beads`, and this is a `(dev)` build — a version gap or a fork
difference is entirely plausible.

**Before writing any code:** check the current upstream release for sync-branch
support. WHEN it exists, close this bead as superseded and file the upgrade
instead — including what an upgrade costs here (the container provisions `bd`
via the session-start hook, so the pin moves with it) and whether a sync branch
interacts safely with worktrees sharing one database through git's common
directory. WHEN it does not exist, or the upgrade is not viable in this
environment, proceed with the merge driver as designed and record which it was
and on what evidence.
## Orphaned dispatch, recovered 2026-08-11

Dispatched and claimed at ~06:39Z; wrote `claimed` and `implementing` to its
progress ledger and nothing after. Discovered orphaned at 16:03Z — 9.4 hours
later — by the liveness rule from agent-plugins-92q.11: newest dirty-file mtime
33,872s old against a >30-minute orphaned threshold, while the ledger tail still
read `implementing`.

Resolution order applied (bd -> git -> ledger, per 'the ledger is a hint, never
the authority'): bd said `in_progress`; git showed no landing commit; the only
dirty files were `.beads/issues.jsonl` and `.beads/interactions.jsonl` — the
claim itself — with no source work and no handoff file. So the bead never got
past claiming.

Claim reset to `open` by the orchestrator, which owns claim reconciliation
across waves. No work lost; nothing to stash. Re-dispatch from the top.
## May be superseded by the re-scope (2026-08-11)

Do not implement before agent-plugins-92q.30 (worktrees) and agent-plugins-92q.31 (sync)
are decided: the merge driver exists because N branches each commit a copy of the tracker; if the tracker stops being a committed file there is nothing to merge.

Re-read this bead after those land. WHEN its premise is gone, close it as
superseded rather than implementing it; WHEN a reduced form survives, groom it
down before dispatch. This note exists so nobody implements doomed work.
close_reason: Superseded by agent-plugins-92q.31, which landed 2026-08-11 (commit 05fff9b). The union-by-id merge driver existed only because N branches each committed a full copy of one shared database. .beads/issues.jsonl is now untracked and the tracker is origin refs/dolt/data, so there is no file to conflict and nothing to merge. The supersession condition recorded on this bead at stage 0 — 'completes at 92q.31 step 5' — is now met.

metadata.tier_reason: A merge driver silently corrupts the tracker if its conflict semantics are wrong, and the must-conflict case is the one most likely to be skipped. Needs adversarial verification, not a happy-path test.

title: Worktrees must branch from the sprint branch: make the baseRef check blocking at worktree dispatch, not advisory at run start
description:
Two rules the reviewer set for worktree dispatch, one already half-enforced and
one not enforced at all.

**The rule (user, 2026-08-10):** *"Every worktree MUST branch from a dedicated
feature branch for the sprint, never from the default branch (main)."*

That is exactly two conditions, and the skill currently guarantees only the
first:

1. **The run's own HEAD must not be the default branch.** Already enforced —
   `scripts/pre-flight-check.sh` blocks the run when
   `HEAD == <remote>/HEAD`, exit 1.
2. **Worktrees must branch from that HEAD, not from the default branch.**
   `worktree.baseRef` must be `"head"`. `agent-plugins-jh6` measured the
   default: a worktree branched from `main` at `5390f1d` while session HEAD was
   `0ccc092`, eight commits ahead — so any bead building on an earlier bead in
   the same run silently loses that foundation. Pre-flight probes this and
   reports it as **advisory**, never blocking.

Advisory is the wrong severity once the rule is mandatory. The setting lives in
user-scope `~/.claude/settings.json`, which no repository owns, so a run can be
correctly configured on one machine and silently wrong on the next — and the
symptom is not an error, it is a worktree quietly missing the run's own commits.
design:
**1. Make the probe blocking, but only when it matters.** A run that dispatches
no worktree wave is unaffected by `baseRef`, and blocking those would be noise.
Two-stage:

- `pre-flight-check.sh` keeps reporting `BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF` and keeps its
  advisory line at run start. Do not make pre-flight itself exit 1 on this —
  most runs never dispatch a worktree.
- **Phase 2.5 gains a hard gate:** WHEN the dispatch plan assigns any bead to
  worktree-parallel, the orchestrator SHALL verify `BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF=head`
  before the first worktree dispatch, and SHALL NOT dispatch the wave otherwise.
  The remedy is one line — set `.worktree.baseRef = "head"` in
  `~/.claude/settings.json` — and `jh6` measured that it takes effect
  immediately, with no session restart, so this is a stop-and-fix, not a
  stop-and-abandon.

**2. State the branch rule where the mode is defined.** In `SKILL.md`'s
worktree-parallel description and in `references/subagent-prompts.md`'s worktree
notes:

> Every worktree branches from the sprint's own feature branch, never from the
> default branch. Two conditions produce that and both are checked: pre-flight
> blocks a run whose HEAD is the default branch, and `worktree.baseRef` must be
> `"head"` so the worktree takes session HEAD rather than the repository
> default.

**3. Verify per wave, not once per run.** `jh6`'s verification step already
belongs in the dispatch template; make it explicit that it runs before **each**
worktree wave, because the setting is global user state that anything could
change between waves:

```sh
git -C "<worktree>" merge-base --is-ancestor "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" HEAD \
  || { echo "worktree did not branch from session HEAD — abort the wave"; exit 1; }
```

Do NOT change `pre-flight-check.sh`'s exit-code contract (0 proceed / 1 blocking
/ 2 bad invocation) or add a new blocking condition to it. The gate belongs at
the point of use.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Phase 2.5 blocks a worktree wave unless BB_WORKTREE_BASEREF=head, and names the one-line remedy
- [ ] pre-flight-check.sh's exit-code contract is unchanged and it gains no new blocking condition
- [ ] SKILL.md and the worktree notes both state the two-condition branch rule (HEAD is not the default branch; baseRef is head)
- [ ] The per-worktree merge-base verification is stated to run before EACH worktree wave, with an abort on failure
- [ ] The retro records that the setting is user-scope global state no repository owns

metadata.tier_reason: Small edits with the wording supplied; the judgment is where the gate belongs, and the bead settles it.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Design item 3 proposed adding a new orchestrator-run 'git -C <worktree> merge-base --is-ancestor' verification and said to 'make it explicit that it runs before each worktree wave,' framing this as still needed. The dispatch template (references/subagent-prompts.md, 'Verify before every wave') already had a working per-wave verify-and-abort instruction, landed by the more recent sibling agent-plugins-92q.9. Left that mechanism as-is rather than duplicating it, and only broadened the surrounding rule text from 'safe only if beads build on each other' to the unconditional two-condition rule the user actually stated.

title: PR #18 review: tighten the run-time-loaded surfaces (run-id citations, find-the-run ordering, ledger numbering, script header, pre-flight paragraph)
description:
Five findings from the PR #18 review, all in files an agent loads at run time,
all small, none changing behaviour. Grouped because they are one theme —
**every byte in these files is paid on every run** — and because they touch
five different files, so there is no serialization benefit to splitting them.

1. **`references/recovery.md:33` and `:158` cite run `1786121603-ri`.** The
   reviewer: *"This type of commentary is superfluous unless the agent can look
   up run `1786121603-ri` and uncover useful information."* It cannot. That run
   directory lives under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` and is long reclaimed, and its
   `.bonanza/` copy was never committed to this branch. The finding is worth
   keeping; the unlookuppable provenance is not.

2. **`references/recovery.md:39` presumes the epic id it is supposed to help you
   find.** Step 1 of the orchestrator-recovery procedure opens with
   `bd show <epic-id>` — but that procedure runs precisely when the agent has no
   context, and nothing tells it which epic. Reviewer: *"How does the agent know
   which `epic-id` should be used?"* The ordering is backwards: the `current`
   symlink resolves with zero prior knowledge, and `dispatch.md`'s run manifest
   *contains* the epic id.

3. **`references/dispatch-plan.md:34` numbers the environmental-ledger
   template.** Reviewer asked whether it should be unordered. It should stay
   numbered — dispatch prompts cite entries by number, and this run's own
   prompts say "ledger entry 1" and "ledger entry 2" — but nothing in the file
   says so, so the next reader will reasonably "fix" it.

4. **`scripts/pre-flight-check.sh:4-12` opens with a nine-line history lesson.**
   Reviewer: *"Do we need the history lesson here!?"* The scripts are declared
   "executed, not read", so this header serves maintainers, not runtime — but it
   is still the first thing anyone opening the file reads, and it recounts a
   defect rather than stating a contract.

5. **`SKILL.md:72` narrates the pre-flight script's output contract.** Reviewer:
   *"What's the motivation behind describing what the script will output? Does
   the agent need to know these details before running the script?"* Partly yes
   — the caller must know to `eval` stdout and that exit 1 blocks — but the
   current paragraph goes well past that, inside the window that survives
   compaction.

Related but deliberately NOT in scope: the reviewer's proposal of a dedicated
git worktree per bead (`recovery.md:128`). That is a redesign of the isolation
model, not a tidy-up, and is tracked separately.
design:
Five edits. Keep every one tight; `SKILL.md` is far over the re-injection cap
and a sibling bead has to bring it under.

**1. Strip run-id citations from `references/recovery.md`.** Keep the fact,
drop the pointer: "a user interrupt that kills the orchestrator kills the
mechanism that would have announced its children's deaths — two kill
notifications were enqueued and never dequeued while the UI showed the task
running." No run id. Same at `:158`. Sweep for others:
`grep -n '17[0-9]\{8\}-' plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/`.

Leave `pre-flight-check.sh`'s usage examples alone if they use a run id as an
illustrative ARGUMENT — that is a shape, not a citation. Prefer `<run-id>` if
changing it costs nothing.

**2. Reorder `recovery.md` step 1** so nothing presumes prior knowledge:

> 1. **Find the run.** `ls -l "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/claude/bead-bonanza/current"` —
>    a symlink `pre-flight-check.sh` repoints at the start of every run, and the
>    only route that needs nothing you have to already know. Read
>    `$RUN_DIR/dispatch.md`; its run manifest names the epic, the branch and the
>    base sha. WHEN the symlink is gone (a reclaimed container, a run started
>    before it existed), the epic's tracker note carries the same `RUN_DIR`
>    pointer and every amendment — `bd show <epic-id>` once the manifest or the
>    user has named the epic, and that note is the copy that survives container
>    reclaim. Only if neither resolves, list the run root and take the newest
>    run-id directory, treating it as a guess: newest-by-mtime is wrong whenever
>    an older run's directory was touched after a newer one started. WHEN none
>    resolves, reconstruct from `git log` and `bd list --status all`, and **say
>    so in the report** — a reconstruction is not a plan.

Keep the existing point that the tracker note is what survives reclaim; it moves
position, it does not disappear.

**3. `references/dispatch-plan.md`** — one clause on the ledger template saying
entries are numbered because dispatch prompts cite them by number. A sentence,
not a paragraph.

**4. `scripts/pre-flight-check.sh` header** — replace the history with a
contract: what it measures, what it emits on stdout vs stderr, what the exit
codes mean, and the one-line reason it exists (Phase 0 was prose describing
shell commands, and one of its claims was environment-dependent and false).
Three or four lines. Keep the `Usage` block exactly as it is.

**5. `SKILL.md`'s pre-flight paragraph** — reduce to what the caller must act
on: `eval` the stdout, read the stderr report once, exit 0 proceed / 1 blocking
/ 2 bad invocation, and that a missing `AGENTS.md` block means read
`references/project-setup.md`. Everything about which `BB_*` facts exist belongs
with the script's published interface, not in the phase.

No behaviour changes. No new rules. If an edit tempts you into restating a rule,
stop — that is a different bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] No run-id citation remains in plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/ (grep for the timestamp-dash pattern returns nothing narrative)
- [ ] recovery.md step 1 leads with the current symlink, then dispatch.md's manifest, then the epic tracker note, then the newest-directory guess
- [ ] Step 1 no longer requires the reader to already know the epic id, and still states that the tracker note is the copy surviving container reclaim
- [ ] dispatch-plan.md states in one clause why ledger entries are numbered
- [ ] pre-flight-check.sh's header states the contract (measures / stdout / stderr / exit codes / why) in about four lines, with the Usage block unchanged
- [ ] SKILL.md's pre-flight paragraph covers only eval-the-stdout, read-stderr-once, and the three exit codes
- [ ] No behaviour changed and no rule was restated
- [ ] No new findings against the check-skills baseline

metadata.tier_reason: Five small edits with replacement wording supplied, but spread over five files with a standing instruction not to restate rules while trimming.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Design item 4 asked for a ~4-line contract covering measures/stdout/stderr/exit-codes/why but the file already had separate Output and Exit status sections stating stdout/stderr and exit codes in detail (incl. the four specific exit-1 causes). I folded those two sections into the new Contract block and dropped the enumerated exit-1 causes (now just 'named in the report') to hit the line count without restating — a diff reader wouldn't necessarily recognize that removal as deliberate rather than accidental.

title: recovery.md's find-the-run step misses the 'current' symlink pre-flight already creates, because script side effects are unpublished
description:
`references/recovery.md`'s orchestrator-recovery step 1 tells a recovering agent
to find the run by listing `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/claude/bead-bonanza/` and taking
"the newest run-id directory". That fallback is race-prone — newest-by-mtime
picks the wrong run whenever an older directory is touched after a newer one
started — and it is unnecessary, because a precise pointer already exists.

`scripts/pre-flight-check.sh:317` creates it on every run:

```sh
# -n is load-bearing: without it the second run's link is created INSIDE the
# first run's directory instead of replacing the pointer.
ln -sfn "$RUN_DIR" "$RUN_ROOT/current" 2>/dev/null && say "current -> $RUN_ID"
```

It is self-tested at `pre-flight-check.sh:131-133`, and it exists on disk in
this run: `/tmp/claude/bead-bonanza/current -> /tmp/claude/bead-bonanza/1786345424-bbh`.

**Why the agent that wrote step 1 believed otherwise is the more useful half of
this bead.** It recorded a finding that the `current` pointer "does not exist
anywhere in the skill" and substituted the weaker fallback in good faith. It was
reading `SKILL.md`, where the pointer is never mentioned — and it correctly did
NOT read `pre-flight-check.sh`, because `SKILL.md` declares the bundled scripts
"**executed, not read**" and publishes their interfaces precisely so no agent
has to open them.

That rule is right, and it has a hole: **the published interfaces are usage
lines only. They say nothing about what a script leaves behind.** Every
side effect a script produces — a symlink, a directory, an exported variable,
a file — is invisible to any agent that obeys the rule. `pre-flight-check.sh`
alone creates the run directory, the `current` symlink, and a set of `BB_*`
facts on stdout; a downstream agent can only know about the ones SKILL.md
happens to narrate.

Discovered mid-run by the orchestrator while verifying `agent-plugins-92q.11`'s
findings, and admitted under the mid-run scope test as a correction to a bead
already in this run: the recovery procedure `92q.11` shipped is wrong at its
first step.
design:
Two changes, small, one commit.

**1. Correct `recovery.md` step 1.** Name the symlink as the primary
machine-checkable route, keeping the tracker note first (it survives container
reclaim, which the symlink does not) and demoting newest-directory to a last
resort:

> 1. **Find the run.** `bd show <epic-id>` carries the `RUN_DIR` pointer in its
>    tracker note, and each amendment is mirrored there — that note is the
>    cheapest route in and the only one that survives container reclaim.
>    Failing that, `ls -l "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/claude/bead-bonanza/current"` — a
>    symlink `pre-flight-check.sh` repoints at the start of every run. Only if
>    neither resolves, list the run root and take the newest run-id directory,
>    treating it as a guess: newest-by-mtime is wrong whenever an older run's
>    directory was touched after a newer one started. WHEN none of the three
>    resolves, the run predates the pointer — reconstruct from `git log` and
>    `bd list --status all`, and **say so in the report**; a reconstruction is
>    not a plan.

**2. Publish script side effects, not just usage lines.** In `SKILL.md`'s
Reference-files section, where the three-plus script interfaces are published,
add a side-effects line per script — what it creates, writes or repoints —
and one sentence explaining why the list has to be there at all:

> These are the artifacts each script leaves behind. They are published for the
> same reason the usage lines are: the scripts are executed, not read, so an
> agent that obeys that rule cannot discover a side effect by opening the file.

At minimum `pre-flight-check.sh` (creates `$RUN_DIR`, repoints
`$RUN_ROOT/current`, emits `RUN_DIR`/`SCRIPTS`/`BB_*` on stdout) and
`bb-close-bead.sh` (rewrites `.beads/issues.jsonl`, stages, makes one commit).
Check `bb-progress.sh` and `bb-verify-skip.sh` and cover whatever they leave
behind. Where a sibling bead adds `bb-backup-run.sh`, that bead owns its own
row — do not pre-write it.

Keep both edits tight; `SKILL.md` is over the re-injection cap and a later bead
must bring it under. A side-effects line per script is a few hundred bytes and
earns them by preventing exactly this class of error.

Do NOT change `pre-flight-check.sh` itself — the pointer works and is
self-tested. This bead is about the two places that fail to mention it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] recovery.md step 1 names `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/claude/bead-bonanza/current` as a route, ordered after the tracker note and before the newest-directory guess
- [ ] The newest-directory route is explicitly labelled a guess, with the reason it can be wrong
- [ ] SKILL.md's script interface section publishes a side-effects line for each bundled script alongside its usage line
- [ ] It states why side effects must be published: the scripts are executed, not read
- [ ] pre-flight-check.sh's row names the run directory, the current symlink, and the stdout facts
- [ ] pre-flight-check.sh itself is unchanged
- [ ] No new findings against the two-warning check-skills baseline

metadata.tier_reason: Two small, fully specified edits with the replacement wording supplied; the judgment was done in the bead.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Clean bead — the Design supplied exact replacement wording for both edits; no friction points encountered.

title: plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md exceeds the 5,000-token re-injection cap (21,419 body bytes)
description:
Now that scripts/check-skills.sh thresholds skill bodies on bytes (agent-plugins-92q.2), plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md is a new warning: 21,419 body bytes (~5,354 tokens) against the 20,000-byte threshold. At 319 lines it never tripped the old line gate, so this over-cap condition has been invisible. Trim it under 20,000 bytes, the same way agent-plugins-8ef does for bead-bonanza.

Adjacent, NOT blocking agent-plugins-92q.2 — that bead's Design explicitly scopes to reporting newly-flagged skills, not fixing them.
design:
Same method as agent-plugins-8ef.2, applied to a file nobody has analysed yet — so the first half of this bead is finding the cuts, not making them.

Start by measuring: scripts/check-skills.sh reports the current body size. Then read the file and classify its content the way the bead-bonanza analysis did — content stated twice, rationale that fails CLAUDE.md's historical-prose test, and material whose need is conditional on a branch the run may not take (which extracts to references/ rather than being deleted).

specs/standards/skill-best-practices.md:151-155 governs: extract in preference to compressing, because compression loses the specificity that makes guidance followable.

The spec skill already has a references/ directory, so extraction has somewhere to go.
acceptance_criteria:
1. scripts/check-skills.sh reports plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md under the 20,000-byte threshold.
2. No rule present before the change was removed — content was relocated or deduplicated.
3. Any newly created reference file is reachable in one hop from SKILL.md.
4. Any reference file over 100 lines carries a table of contents.

That lands the body at ~19,700 bytes: under the 20,000 cap but with ~300 bytes of headroom, so the next sentence added to this SKILL.md re-trips the gate. title: Close out the RFC triage: write the three Resolutions, disclose self-authorship, retire and log, bump the plugin
description:
Three RFCs were triaged on 2026-08-10 and their approved proposals filed as the
beads in this epic. `triage-rfc`'s steps 5–7 are therefore **mid-flight, not
done**: the implementation was sequenced into beads (step 5's "Sequence before
you edit" branch, which applies here because more than five proposals were
approved and most of them change one file), but the Resolutions, the retro log
and the version bumps are all still outstanding.

The RFCs, all in `rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/`:

- `rfc-self-close-ceremony-and-finding-harvest.md` — P1 adopted, P2 adopted,
  **P3 rejected as written** (refuted by `agent-plugins-t09`'s measurement;
  replaced by a bead carrying the constraints measurement supports), P4 adopted.
- `rfc-self-run-dir-discoverability-and-orchestrator-recovery.md` — P1–P5 all
  adopted; P5 merged with the sibling RFC's P2.
- `rfc-self-silent-ceremony-loss-and-the-stale-twin.md` — P1–P6 all adopted;
  P3 adopted but **re-planned**, because as written it was a single restructure
  of a file whose contents were about to change.

Leaving them in the inbox with no Resolution is the failure mode `triage-rfc`
names directly: "Silent rejection (no Resolution entry) — the next retro
re-derives and re-proposes the same idea." Three self-authored RFCs re-derived
from the same runs would be indistinguishable from independent corroboration,
which is precisely the signal the accumulation model reads.

This bead is the closure. It runs last.
design:
Per `triage-rfc` steps 5–7, once the epic's beads have landed.

**1. Write each RFC's Resolution.** Per proposal, never per RFC: outcome
(adopted / adopted-with-refinement + the refinement / rejected + rationale), the
bead that carried it, date, files changed, version bumps. Specifically:

- Record **P3 of the close-ceremony RFC as rejected**, naming
  `agent-plugins-t09`'s measurement as the refutation and the replacement bead.
  A rejection is a first-class outcome and is recorded so the idea is not
  relitigated without new evidence.
- Record **P3 of the stale-twin RFC as adopted-with-refinement**, the refinement
  being that it was decomposed into the extraction beads plus a measurement
  gate, because the content-reducing work had to precede it.
- Record the **merge** of the run-dir RFC's P5 with the stale-twin RFC's P2 in
  both Resolutions, so neither reads as unaddressed.

**2. Disclose self-authorship.** All three carry `origin: self`. Each Resolution
SHALL state that the RFC was authored and triaged within this repository, and
name any proposal that ratifies a decision its own author made. Note that each
RFC's `model` field is withheld under the session policy tracked by
`rfcs/inbox/retro-skill/rfc-self-retro-skill-withheld-model.md`, so
same-agent authorship cannot be confirmed or excluded — say that rather than
implying independence. An approval recorded without the disclosure reads later
as independent corroboration when there was none.

**3. Record the triage-originated changes.** Several beads in this epic came
from the review session rather than from any RFC — the pre-flight script, the
DoR amendment and the Phase 2 deletion, C4-based bucketing, the sprint retro,
and the lost-deferral correction. Table each as a `T` row in the Resolution of
the RFC whose evidence prompted it (or of the RFC triaged alongside it where
none did), marked triage-originated, per step 4's convention. Do not number them
into any RFC's `P` sequence.

**4. Number and retire.** Rename each to
`rfcs/rfc-<nnnn>-<short-description>.md` using the next free numbers (0013
onward — 0010 and 0011 are referenced but absent from `rfcs/retired/`; confirm
before allocating), update each slug to match its filename, set status
`retired`, and move to `rfcs/retired/`.

**5. Log.** Append one row per RFC to `rfcs/retro-log.md` — date, origin
(`self`), the skill retroed (`bead-bonanza`), the item (`RFC <nnnn>`), and the
outcome as **per-proposal** counts. Commentary goes under `## Run notes`, never
inside a row.

**6. Publish.** `bead-bonanza` ships in the plugin, so bump
`plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (MINOR — these are normative changes). Note
that the `spec` skill's Definition of Ready also changed and also ships, so the
bump covers both; verify each changed shipped file was bumped exactly once for
the whole set, after its last change rather than before.

Do not edit any RFC's Evidence or Proposals sections. The RFC is the reporter's
testimony; triage writes only the Resolution.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each of the three RFCs carries a Resolution with a per-proposal outcome, the bead that carried it, files changed and version bumps
- [ ] P3 of the close-ceremony RFC is recorded as rejected, naming the refuting measurement and the replacement bead
- [ ] P3 of the stale-twin RFC is recorded as adopted-with-refinement, naming the decomposition
- [ ] The P5/P2 merge is recorded in both affected Resolutions
- [ ] Each Resolution discloses that the RFC is self-authored and that the withheld model field leaves same-agent authorship unconfirmable
- [ ] Triage-originated changes appear as T rows, distinct from any RFC's P sequence
- [ ] All three RFCs are renumbered, slugs updated, status set to retired, and moved to rfcs/retired/
- [ ] rfcs/retro-log.md has one row per RFC with per-proposal outcome counts
- [ ] plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json has a single MINOR bump covering the whole set, and every changed shipped file was bumped exactly once
- [ ] No RFC's Evidence or Proposals section was edited

metadata.tier_reason: Bookkeeping against a well-specified process, but the Resolutions must be accurate per proposal across three RFCs and one rejection — a wrong record misleads every future dedupe.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: [process] Writing Resolutions last was load-bearing, not bookkeeping. Between the 2026-08-10 classification and this closeout, 92q.30 (one worktree per bead) and 92q.31 (Dolt remote as tracker) deleted the premises three ADOPTED proposals rested on: RFC 0016 P1's tracker-write deferral, RFC 0018 P5's WIP-commit exception, and RFC 0017 P2's mtime liveness table all landed and were then retired inside the same epic. A Resolution written at approval time would today assert as current three rules the tree does not contain. triage-rfc's step 5 says 'implement, then write the Resolution' but nowhere warns that a long epic can invalidate an approved proposal mid-flight; the deferred-Resolution branch it already sanctions for large batches is what saved this, by accident rather than by rule.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: [skill-gap · triage-rfc] Nothing in step 5 or step 7 makes the version bump verifiable. The step says 'bump the version of every changed template, skill and standard ... verify the bump after the final change to that file', but supplies no way to enumerate 'every changed file' — the closeout agent has to derive it from a merge-base diff it must first guess (here: git diff --stat ae623c8..HEAD). Doing that found five shipped SKILL.md files changed across the epic with no frontmatter bump (bead-bonanza 1102 lines changed, still v1.3), while every changed REFERENCE document had been bumped correctly by the bead that touched it. The asymmetry is the tell: reference bumps live inside the bead that edits the file, skill bumps were left to a closeout that has no list. Proposal: give step 7 an enumeration command and make the bump list an output of it. Filed as agent-plugins-x8r.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: [record-defect] The bead's Design said to allocate 'the next free numbers (0013 onward — 0010 and 0011 are referenced but absent from rfcs/retired/; confirm before allocating)'. Confirmed and the premise is wrong: 0010–0015 are all allocated, to RFCs still sitting in rfcs/inbox/ (0010 feature-blueprint, 0011 standards, 0013 frd, 0014 and 0015 feature-blueprint). title: RFC-0004's deferral bead agent-plugins-1a9 was never persisted: correct the record and audit for other lost deferrals
description:
`rfcs/retired/rfc-0004-bead-bonanza-dispatch-and-script-contracts.md`'s
Resolution records a deferral:

> | P5 — record the gate profile's baseline verdict | **deferred** ->
> `agent-plugins-1a9`, `theme:gate-baseline`. Entangled with an unsettled
> question: the standard states the body budget in CHARACTERS while
> `check-skills.sh` measures LINES. Bead is `deferred` /
> `blocked-needs-info` pending that decision. | `agent-plugins-1a9` |

**That bead does not exist.** Measured 2026-08-10:

```
$ bd show agent-plugins-1a9
Error fetching agent-plugins-1a9: no issue found matching "agent-plugins-1a9"
$ grep -c '1a9' .beads/issues.jsonl
0
$ git log --all --oneline -S "agent-plugins-1a9" -- .beads/issues.jsonl
(no output)
$ bd label list-all | grep gate-baseline
(no output)
```

It never reached `.beads/issues.jsonl` on any branch, and the theme label was
never created. The deferral was lost with the container it was created in —
exactly the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` warns about ("A bead that is not in
`.beads/issues.jsonl` when the container dies is gone").

Two consequences, and the second is the one that matters.

**The record is false.** A retired RFC's Resolution names a bead a reader can
follow, and following it fails. Anyone auditing what happened to P5 concludes
the work is tracked when it is not.

**The accumulation model leaked.** `triage-rfc`'s deferral mechanism exists so
that recurrence across projects surfaces priority: a deferred bead is the
accumulation signal, and step 2's dedupe reads deferred beads to detect it. A
deferral that evaporates cannot accumulate. This one recurred twice —
`rfc-self-silent-ceremony-loss-and-the-stale-twin.md` P3 re-proposes gate
baselining, and a hardening bead re-proposed the units fix — and neither
recurrence was detected as one, because there was nothing to dedupe against.

The blocking question is now answerable: the binding constraint is the
5,000-token skill re-injection cap, so the threshold is a size, and the units
question resolves to bytes. Both halves of the original deferral are now live
beads. What is left is the record and the leak.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the Resolution table in
   `rfcs/retired/rfc-0004-bead-bonanza-dispatch-and-script-contracts.md` and
   note the bead cited for P5: `agent-plugins-1a9`.
2. Follow it:

```
$ bd show agent-plugins-1a9
Error fetching agent-plugins-1a9: no issue found matching "agent-plugins-1a9"
$ grep -c '1a9' .beads/issues.jsonl
0
$ git log --all --oneline -S "agent-plugins-1a9" -- .beads/issues.jsonl
(no output)
$ bd label list-all | grep gate-baseline
(no output)
```

**Expected:** a deferred bead a reader can follow, and a theme label carrying
the accumulation count.
**Actual:** neither exists, in any branch's database or history.
design:
**1. Correct RFC-0004's Resolution.** Do not rewrite the deferral row's history
— add a dated note beneath the table:

> **2026-08-10:** bead `agent-plugins-1a9` was never persisted to
> `.beads/issues.jsonl` and does not exist in any branch's database; the
> deferral was lost with its container. The blocking question (body budget in
> characters vs `check-skills.sh` measuring lines) is resolved: the binding
> constraint is the 5,000-token re-injection cap, so the threshold is a size in
> bytes. Both halves of P5 are now tracked by <the check-skills bead> and <the
> pre-flight bead, which captures the gate baseline>.

Editing a retired RFC's Resolution to record a later correction is within
`triage-rfc`'s conventions — triage writes the Resolution; it is the Evidence
and Proposals sections that are the reporter's testimony and must not be
touched.

**2. Create the `theme:gate-baseline` label** on the two beads that inherit the
deferral, so the accumulation signal exists going forward. This is the point of
theme labels — a bead without one is invisible to the model.

**3. Audit for other lost deferrals.** This one was found by accident while
deduping, not by looking. Enumerate every bead id cited in a Resolution across
`rfcs/retired/*.md` and check each resolves:

```bash
grep -ohE 'agent-plugins-[a-z0-9]+' rfcs/retired/*.md | sort -u \
  | while read id; do bd show "$id" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "MISSING: $id"; done
```

Report every miss. Recreate a lost bead only where its proposal is still live;
where the work has since landed by another route, note that in the Resolution
instead. Do not mass-recreate — an unread bead resurrected as an open work item
is worse than an honest note that it was lost.

**4. Note the systemic cause once, where it will be read.** `CLAUDE.md` already
documents that only `.beads/issues.jsonl` carries beads between containers, and
that `bd export` must be run and committed before a session ends. This incident
is evidence that the documented practice was not followed at least once. Add the
observation to the existing section — a dated line, not a rewrite — rather than
creating a new warning: the guidance was correct and present; what it lacked was
a verification step.

Deliberately out of scope: adding an automated check that every Resolution's
cited beads resolve. It is a reasonable idea and it is a different bead; propose
it if the audit in step 3 finds more than one miss.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] RFC-0004's Resolution carries a dated note recording that agent-plugins-1a9 was never persisted, that the units question is resolved to bytes, and which beads now carry both halves
- [ ] The RFC's Evidence and Proposals sections are unchanged
- [ ] theme:gate-baseline exists on the beads inheriting the deferral
- [ ] Every bead id cited in a Resolution across rfcs/retired/ was checked for existence and every miss is reported
- [ ] Any recreated bead corresponds to a proposal that is still live; work that landed by another route is noted in its Resolution instead
- [ ] CLAUDE.md's beads-persistence section carries a dated line recording this incident, without rewriting the existing guidance

title: bb-close-bead.sh writes no trailers, and the amend that adds them strands the sha the ledger recorded
description:
`bb-close-bead.sh` commits with the bare subject `{ID} P{PRIORITY} {TITLE}` and
no body. A repository whose convention requires commit trailers — this one
requires `Co-Authored-By` and `Claude-Session` — must therefore
`git commit --amend` after the script's step 6, which **rewrites the commit**.
The subagent template's step 7 then records the pre-amend sha.

Observed on `9kb.10` in run `1786121603-ri`:

```
$ tail -1 agent-plugins-9kb.10.progress.jsonl
{"phase":"committed","sha":"14f0be3"}
$ git log --oneline --grep=9kb.10        # landing commit on the branch
875593a ...
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 14f0be3 HEAD; echo $?
1                                        # dangling pre-amend object
```

Every bead in that run that pushed trailers has the same drift. The recorded sha
names an object that is not on the branch, which breaks the two things that
depend on it: the acceptance check being added in a sibling bead, and the
recovery procedure's `committed -> verify the sha` step.

Repro: run `bb-close-bead.sh`, `git commit --amend` to add any trailer, compare
the ledger's `sha` to `git rev-parse HEAD`.

Two independent fixes, both needed. The trailer support removes the amend; the
sha-source change makes the ledger correct even when something else rewrites the
commit.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a branch, run the close ceremony for any bead:
   `bb-close-bead.sh <id> <priority> "<title>" <retro-file> <paths>`
2. Note the short sha it prints.
3. Add any commit trailer the way a project convention requires:
   `git commit --amend` (append `Co-Authored-By:` or similar).
4. Follow the subagent template's step 7, which records the sha the script
   printed: `bb-progress.sh "$RUN_DIR" <id> committed sha=<printed sha>`
5. Compare: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <printed sha> HEAD; echo $?`

**Expected:** the recorded sha is the landing commit.
**Actual:** exit 1 — the recorded sha is a dangling pre-amend object.
Observed on `9kb.10`: ledger `14f0be3`, landing commit `875593a`.
design:
**1. `bb-close-bead.sh --trailers-file <path>`.** Contents are appended to the
commit message body, separated by a blank line. Optional: WHERE a project has no
trailer convention the flag is omitted and behaviour is unchanged. Update the
script's own header usage line and the interface published in SKILL.md — the
skill states the script is authoritative on disagreement, so both must move
together.

Phase 0 resolves the trailers file once per run, alongside the gate profile,
from the project's stated commit convention, and passes it into every dispatch
prompt. Where the convention lives in `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` prose rather than a
file, Phase 0 writes it to `$RUN_DIR/trailers.txt` and passes that. Note that
this repository's trailers include a session URL that varies per session, so the
file is per-run, not committed.

**2. Read the sha from the branch, not from the script's stdout.** Change step 7
of every affected template in `references/subagent-prompts.md`:

> 7. `bb-progress.sh "$RUN_DIR" {ID} committed sha=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)`
>    — read it from the branch, not from the script's printout, so any rewrite
>    between the two steps cannot desync it.

This is the fix that holds even when the amend comes from somewhere the skill
does not control — a hook, a signing step, a project convention added later. Do
it regardless of whether the trailers flag is used.

**3. Reorder so no amend is needed.** With trailers passed in, step 6 closes and
commits with trailers already in place and step 7's sha is final. Confirm the
per-bead, fast-lane and shared-surface templates all reflect the new ordering —
the fast-lane and shared-surface templates reference the per-bead workflow rather
than restating it, so check that the reference still resolves correctly.

**Do not** change `bb-progress.sh` or `bb-verify-skip.sh`. Do not change the
close ceremony's four ordering constraints — this adds a message body, not a
reordering.

Verify by running the repro: close a probe bead with `--trailers-file`, confirm
the trailers are on the commit, confirm no amend was needed, and confirm
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <ledger sha> HEAD` exits 0. Record the observed
output in the retro.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] bb-close-bead.sh accepts an optional --trailers-file whose contents are appended to the commit body after a blank line
- [ ] Omitting the flag leaves behaviour byte-identical to today
- [ ] The script header's usage line and the interface published in SKILL.md both show the new flag
- [ ] Phase 0 resolves the trailers file once per run and passes it into every dispatch prompt
- [ ] Every subagent template reads the committed sha from 'git rev-parse --short HEAD', not from the script's printout
- [ ] The per-bead, fast-lane and shared-surface templates all reflect the no-amend ordering
- [ ] bb-progress.sh and bb-verify-skip.sh are unchanged, and the close ceremony's four ordering constraints are unchanged
- [ ] The repro was run: trailers present, no amend needed, and 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <ledger sha> HEAD' exits 0, with the output recorded in the retro

metadata.tier_reason: Shell flag, template reordering across three prompts, and a repro to run. Touching the close ceremony means the ordering constraints must be preserved exactly.

title: Define the resume path for an interrupted bead: a WIP commit is the one sanctioned exception to one-commit-per-bead
description:
`SKILL.md:718-722` states the invariant absolutely:

> **One commit per bead, always.** Every closed bead = exactly one commit on the
> branch.

There is no interruption case, so an interrupted bead has no legal move. Bead
`9kb.5` in run `1786121603-ri` landed in two commits — `e3f2777` "WIP
agent-plugins-9kb.5 (PREG): profile registration, snapshots pending" at 20:52,
then `bb7ecc3` at 21:06. The agent improvised a commit the invariant forbids
rather than following a stated resume path, because there is none. The
alternative available to it was losing the work.

The invariant is right and should stay. What it needs is the one sanctioned
exception, plus the rule that restores the invariant at close time — so that
"one commit per bead" remains true of every *closed* bead, which is what the
invariant is actually protecting (bisectability, and a clean revert per bead).
design:
Append to the one-commit-per-bead principle (which moves to
`references/operating-principles.md` — put it there and leave the rule's
one-line summary above the cap):

> **WHEN a bead is interrupted mid-implementation** and its work must be
> persisted before the agent stops, commit it with a subject prefixed
> `WIP <bead-id>` and leave the bead `in_progress`. A WIP commit is the one
> sanctioned exception, and it is **not** a close: no `bd update --status
> closed`, no retro, no `committed` progress event. Emit
> `bb-progress.sh "$RUN_DIR" <id> blocked reason="interrupted; WIP <sha>"` so
> the ledger records where it stopped.
>
> The agent that resumes the bead finishes the work, then squashes its own
> commit together with every `WIP <bead-id>` commit on the branch into the
> single landing commit before running the close ceremony. Record the
> interruption and the squash in the bead's retro.

Two things the resuming agent needs and the rule must supply:

1. **How to find them.** `git log --oneline --grep="^WIP <bead-id>"` on the
   branch. State it, because the resuming agent may be a different agent with no
   knowledge that a WIP exists — which is the whole situation being handled.
2. **The safety boundary.** Squashing rewrites history, so it is permitted only
   while the WIP commits are unpushed. WHERE a WIP commit has already been
   pushed, do not rewrite it: land the completion as a normal second commit,
   note the two-commit landing in the retro, and report it in Phase 4. The
   existing prohibition on force-pushing a published branch
   (`references/subagent-prompts.md`, Constraints) is not weakened by this bead.

Also add the recovery counterpart in `references/recovery.md`: a bead whose
ledger tail is `blocked` with an `interrupted` reason is resumable, not failed —
distinct from the existing "last phase was `implementing` or earlier -> stash and
surface" path, which assumes nothing was committed.

Cross-check `bb-close-bead.sh` for anything that would reject a tree containing
prior WIP commits for the same bead. It refuses to run without a retro file and
with nothing staged; neither should fire here, but confirm rather than assume.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The one-commit-per-bead rule carries an interruption case permitting a 'WIP <bead-id>' commit with the bead left in_progress
- [ ] The exception explicitly excludes closing, writing a retro, and emitting a committed event, and requires a blocked event naming the WIP sha
- [ ] The resume rule requires squashing all WIP commits for the bead into the single landing commit before the close ceremony
- [ ] The rule states how a fresh agent finds prior WIP commits
- [ ] The rule forbids rewriting a pushed WIP commit and defines the two-commit fallback, without weakening the force-push prohibition
- [ ] references/recovery.md distinguishes an interrupted-with-WIP bead from the stash-and-surface path
- [ ] bb-close-bead.sh was checked against a tree containing a prior WIP commit for the same bead and the result recorded

metadata.tier_reason: One sanctioned exception plus its restore rule; the pushed-WIP boundary is the only judgment and it is stated.

title: Back the in-session Monitor with a durable out-of-session trigger, and cancel it in Phase 4
description:
The skill mandates a wake mechanism that cannot survive the failure it exists to
report.

`SKILL.md:612-615` and `references/recovery.md:62` require the orchestrator to
arm a `Monitor` on a subagent's progress JSONL for anything running past five
minutes. Run `1786121603-ri` complied: Monitor `btnrafelq` was armed and
relaying correctly — `gates-passed` at 18:27:46, `committed` at 18:29:20. At
18:33:08.850 a user interrupt landed. At 18:33:08.862 and .863 two notifications
were **enqueued**:

> `status: killed — Agent "Batch: RES + PREG (9kb.4, 9kb.5)" was stopped by user`
> `status: killed — Monitor "batch RES+PREG phase events" stopped`

Neither was ever dequeued — every prior notification in that transcript shows an
enqueue followed ~50ms later by a dequeue. The same interrupt stopped the
orchestrator, so the mechanism that would have reported the death died with it.
Result: 2h16m of silence while the UI showed the task running.

The underlying mechanics, which are easy to get wrong from the inside:

| Mechanism | Starts a turn | Carries state into it | Survives interrupt/clear |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task notification (child finishes or dies) | yes | no | **no** |
| `Monitor` on a file | yes | yes — the matched event | **no** — dies with the turn |
| Scheduled trigger (`send_later`, cron) | yes | yes — arbitrary text | **yes** — server-side |
| SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit hook | **no** | yes | n/a — enriches an existing turn |

A durable sprint needs one mechanism that wakes fast and one that survives. This
run had only the first kind, twice.

Verified in the same session: a `send_later` trigger armed at 21:13Z fired
correctly at 21:31Z and drove a full recovery check. Its binding is to the cloud
`persistent_session_id`, not to a local transcript, which is why it survives
clears and interrupts.
design:
Amend the Monitor rule (`SKILL.md:612-615`, and the matching text at
`references/recovery.md:62`) to require both mechanisms and to say why:

> **Monitor any subagent past 5 minutes, and back it with a durable trigger.**
> The `Monitor` is the fast path: it is in-session, and it dies with the turn
> that armed it, so it cannot report its own death. Before the first dispatch of
> a run, also arm a recurring out-of-session check-in — a cron/recurring trigger
> where the harness offers one, otherwise a re-armed `send_later` — at 15–30
> minute intervals, whose message states the RUN_DIR path and points at the
> orchestrator-recovery procedure. Cancel it in Phase 4 when the run drains. A
> run whose only wake mechanism is in-session cannot survive an interrupt that
> lands on the orchestrator.

Details that matter:

- **Prefer a recurring trigger over a one-shot** for a run of unknown length: it
  re-arms itself instead of depending on the agent to remember, and the agent
  forgetting is the failure mode being defended against.
- **The trigger's message must be self-contained.** It wakes a turn that may hold
  no run context. It carries the RUN_DIR path, the epic id, and one line
  instructing the woken agent to run the orchestrator-recovery procedure rather
  than to "check on the run".
- **Cancelling is part of Phase 4**, not optional tidy-up: a trigger left armed
  after the run drains wakes an agent into a finished sprint, which trains the
  reader to ignore it.
- **Do not have the check-in key liveness on `bd list --status in_progress`.**
  The improvised heartbeat in the observed run did exactly that and would have
  concluded "nothing in flight" while an agent edited twelve files. Point it at
  the recovery procedure's git-mtime rule instead.

Where the harness offers neither trigger mechanism, say so once at run start —
the run proceeds, but the user should know the only wake path is in-session.

Depends on the RUN_DIR pointer and the recovery procedure existing, since the
trigger's message points at both.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] SKILL.md and references/recovery.md both require a Monitor AND a durable trigger, and state that a Monitor cannot report its own death
- [ ] A recurring trigger is preferred over a one-shot, with the reason given
- [ ] The trigger message is required to be self-contained: RUN_DIR, epic id, and an instruction to run the orchestrator-recovery procedure
- [ ] Cancelling the trigger is a required Phase 4 step
- [ ] The guidance forbids keying the check-in's liveness test on bd claim status and points at the git-mtime rule
- [ ] The no-trigger-available case is handled with a one-line notice at run start

metadata.tier_reason: Guidance edit with the wording drafted; the mechanics table in the description settles the reasoning.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro: Implicit decision (assumed, not re-asked): kept the trigger-mechanism wording harness-agnostic — 'a cron/recurring trigger where the harness offers one, otherwise a re-armed send_later' — rather than naming a specific tool, since SKILL.md must work across harnesses and this session's own tool list (CronCreate/CronList and mcp__Claude_Code_Remote__create_trigger with cron_expression) confirms recurring triggers do exist in at least one harness, so the conditional phrasing is not hypothetical.

title: Make the mixed-tier batching rule decidable, and record deliberate over-routes in the Phase 4 report
description:
`SKILL.md:475-478` resolves a bucket whose beads carry different capability
tiers:

> prefer bucketing beads that share a tier. When a bucket mixes tiers, run the
> whole batch subagent at the **highest** tier among its members — never run a
> bead below its tier. If honoring that would drag several cheap beads up, split
> the bucket.

"Several" is the entire rule, and it is undefined. Worse, the rule omits the
quantity that actually decides the trade: what a full gate run costs. Batching
exists to avoid repeated full `<test>` runs — that is the stated reason in the
same phase ("Each 'plain sequential' bead burns a full `<test>` run (often 10+
min). Batching N beads in one subagent saves N-1 of those.") — so where the gate
suite finishes in seconds, batching buys nothing and the correct tier should
simply win.

Observed in the 23-bead run: the decision came up twice with opposite outcomes
and no principle to appeal to. `bge.9` (`light`) was batched with a `standard`
bead and ran a tier above its assignment; `bge.8` (`advanced`) and `bge.11`
(`standard`) were split rather than batched. Both calls were defensible, neither
was derivable from the skill. The deciding factor turned out to be gate-suite
cost — seconds in that repo — which the rule never mentions.

There is a reporting gap alongside it. Phase 4's escalation table captures
*under*-routing only: a bead escalated because its tier was too low shows up, a
bead deliberately run a tier high does not. `SKILL.md:670-679` already says
over-routing "succeeds silently and is paid for on every run" — and then
provides no place to record the instances the orchestrator knowingly created.
design:
Replace the final sentence of `SKILL.md:478` with a decidable rule:

> Split the bucket WHEN the number of beads dragged above their tier exceeds
> one, OR when any bead would be dragged more than one tier. Weigh that against
> what batching saves: batching exists to avoid repeated full `<test>` runs, so
> WHERE the gate suite completes in seconds the saving is negligible and the
> correct tier wins; WHERE it takes minutes, one bead one tier high is the
> cheaper error.

The gate-suite duration is knowable at this point — `pre-flight-check.sh`
captures the gate baseline, and its timing is the input this rule needs. Have
the rule name that source rather than asking the orchestrator to estimate.

**Add the over-routing record.** In the Phase 4 report specification (which
moves to `references/final-report.md` — sequence accordingly), add deliberate
over-routes alongside the escalation table:

> | Bead | Assigned | Ran at | Why raised |
> |------|----------|--------|------------|
> | demo-9h0 | light | standard | batched with a standard bead; gate suite ~11 min |
>
> State `none` explicitly when there were none. Together with the escalation
> table this is the run's complete routing evidence: escalations expose
> under-routing, this exposes over-routing, and `groom-beads`' retro loop needs
> both to recalibrate the rubric.

Keep the existing asymmetry note — a zero-escalation run is not a clean bill of
health — and cross-reference the new table from it, since the new table is now
the direct answer to the question that note raises.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The split rule is stated numerically: more than one bead dragged above tier, or any bead dragged more than one tier
- [ ] The rule weighs the split against gate-suite duration and names the pre-flight gate baseline as the source of that duration
- [ ] The Phase 4 report specification carries an over-routing table with bead, assigned tier, tier it ran at, and why
- [ ] 'none' is required explicitly when there were no over-routes
- [ ] The existing zero-escalation asymmetry note cross-references the new table
- [ ] The tier vocabulary and the escalation ladder are unchanged

title: Replace worktree-parallel's skip conditions with the measured git-side constraints (RFC P3 rejected as written)
description:
`SKILL.md:438-441` gives worktree-parallel exactly two skip conditions:

> Skip this mode if there are <3 isolated beads (parallelism savings don't pay)
> or if the beads aren't actually isolated (you'll just hit merge conflicts).

Neither covers the constraints that actually bite, so the mode has been skipped
for wrong reasons and would fail for unstated ones.

**The received proposal on this is wrong and is rejected.**
`rfcs/inbox/bead-bonanza/rfc-self-close-ceremony-and-finding-harvest.md` P3
proposes excluding worktree-parallel in the beads backend entirely, reasoning
that `.beads/embeddeddolt/` is gitignored so "a worktree cannot see the tracker
database at all". Bead `agent-plugins-t09` measured it and the inference does
not hold: `bd` 1.1.2 resolves the shared database through git's common
directory. From a worktree with `BEADS_DIR` unset, `bd where` prints the main
checkout's path, `bd worktree info` reports the main repo, `bd list` returns the
identical issue set, and no `embeddeddolt/` or redirect file is created in the
worktree. Concurrency was tested separately in an isolated repo: 8 concurrent
`bd create` -> 8 successes; 4 concurrent `bd label add` on one issue -> all four
present; 4 concurrent writes across main + 3 worktrees -> all landed, export
byte-valid. The premise (gitignored) is true; the conclusion drawn from it was
never run.

Triage decision, 2026-08-10: **P3 rejected as written**, replaced by the
constraints that measurement supports. This bead is that replacement. It is
sequenced after the two beads that establish the facts — the ledger correction
and the `worktree.baseRef` investigation — because writing skip conditions
before those land would repeat exactly the error being corrected.
design:
Replace `SKILL.md:438-441`'s skip conditions with the measured set. Final
wording depends on the `worktree.baseRef` bead's outcome, which is why this bead
waits on it; draft below.

**Keep:** <3 isolated beads; beads not actually isolated (now decided by C4
blast radius as well as file overlap — see the bucketing bead).

**Add — the git-side constraints, which are the real ones:**

> - **A worktree's own `.beads/issues.jsonl` goes stale while `git status` reads
>   clean.** Auto-export always writes the MAIN checkout's copy. Measured: DB 28
>   issues, main file 28 lines, worktree file 23 lines, worktree reporting no
>   changes. Any worktree subagent SHALL run `bd export > .beads/issues.jsonl`
>   in its own directory before committing. (`bb-close-bead.sh` does an export;
>   confirm it lands in the worktree's copy, not the main one, and fix it there
>   if not.)
> - **Auto-export is best-effort and was observed to miss** — three creates sat
>   unexported for 20+ seconds, flushing only on a later main-context write.
>   Never rely on it inside a worktree.
> - **`export.git-add: true` stages into the main index from writes issued
>   elsewhere.** This is the case the `git commit -- <pathspec>` guard exists
>   for; keep commits pathspec-scoped.
> - **The exported ledger has no merge driver in most projects**, so N worktrees
>   that each commit `.beads/issues.jsonl` produce an N-way textual conflict in
>   a generated file. Resolve by re-exporting on the merged tree, not by hand
>   merging — and say so, because the skill's existing fixture-conflict remedy
>   (`run <regen>`) does not name this case.
> - **`worktree.baseRef`** — carry whatever the investigation bead concludes.
>   WHEN worktrees branch from the default branch rather than session HEAD, any
>   bead building on an earlier bead's commit in the same run silently loses that
>   foundation, and the mode SHALL be skipped for any wave whose beads build on
>   in-run work.

**Also correct the RFC's premise inline**, briefly, so the next reader does not
re-derive it: `bd` resolves the shared database through git's common directory,
so tracker access is not the obstacle; the obstacles are the ledger file and the
base ref.

**Update `references/subagent-prompts.md`'s "Worktree parallel notes"** with the
same constraints — the orchestrator-facing merge notes there currently describe
only fixture conflicts.

Record the outcome in the RFC's Resolution as `rejected — refuted by
agent-plugins-t09's measurement; replaced by <this bead>`, and disclose that the
RFC is self-authored (`origin: self`, model field withheld) per the triage
convention.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] SKILL.md's worktree-parallel skip conditions name the stale worktree issues.jsonl, best-effort auto-export, export.git-add staging into the main index, the ledger's missing merge driver, and the worktree.baseRef outcome
- [ ] The text states that bd resolves the shared DB through git's common directory, so tracker access is not the obstacle
- [ ] references/subagent-prompts.md's worktree notes carry the same constraints
- [ ] Each constraint cites the command or measurement that established it
- [ ] The RFC's Resolution records P3 as rejected-as-written with the refuting measurement named, and discloses the RFC's self-authorship
- [ ] The mode is enabled or disabled per the baseRef bead's conclusion, and SKILL.md says which and why
notes: Dependency on agent-plugins-t09 removed 2026-08-10. t09 is bounced from run 1786345424-bbh because its entire scope lives in the strata repo, which is not attached to this session. The edge existed so the mode would not be enabled while the false 'worktree-parallel is unusable with bd' claim stood — and that claim was independently reproduced and refuted inside THIS repo by jh6's two probes (bd where resolved the main checkout's database from both worktrees, BEADS_DIR unset, no embeddeddolt and no redirect file created). The evidence this bead needed is therefore in hand; correcting strata's copy of the claim remains t09's job and no longer blocks this one.

title: No snapshot case exercises spec check <path>
description:
All 23 cases under cli/testdata/cases/ run either a corpus-wide `check`, an
`index`, or a query subcommand. Not one passes a path to `check`:

  grep -H '^args' */case.toml   # every check case is args = ["check", ...]

So the single-document form has no end-to-end coverage at all. It is covered
only by Go unit tests on corpus.CheckFor, which exercise the narrowing but not
the command surface — argument handling, path normalization, the rendered
report, or the exit code.

That is the form the spec skill instructs authors to run (SKILL.md step 7), and
it is the surface agent-plugins-fe1 changed and agent-plugins-ltd and the
retired-target bead both concern.

Cases worth adding, each cheap:
- check on a member with its own findings — the ordinary path
- check on a member whose slug rename broke references elsewhere: the referrers
  are reported at their own spans and the exit code is 1 (AC-SPECREF-002.9 end
  to end, currently only a Go test)
- check on a member that is clean while another document in the corpus is not:
  the other document's non-reference findings do NOT appear
- check on a path that names no member (pairs with agent-plugins-ltd; write it
  when that behaviour is decided)
- check <path> --only, to pin that the narrowing exception is still gated by
  requested rules

Note the second of these needs an edit between two builds, which a case's input
corpus cannot express — see the † footnote in reference-integrity-blueprint.md.
Either the harness grows a way to express a two-phase case, or that one stays a
Go test and the rest land as cases.
acceptance_criteria: cli/testdata/cases/ contains at least one case invoking check with a path, covering the ordinary single-document result and the narrowing exception; the harness-limited scenarios are explicitly recorded as Go tests rather than silently omitted.
