title: Persist per-file content digests in the index so a single-document check has real prior state
description:
Enhancement following agent-plugins-fe1, which delivered AC-SPECREF-002.9 by
letting unresolved-reference findings through the single-document narrowing
(option B). That reports the referrers a slug rename breaks, but cannot
distinguish 'broken by this edit' from 'already broken' — the rebuild has no
memory of the slug the referrers were resolved against. In a corpus kept green
the distinction is empty; in one already red, every single-document check
repeats the corpus's existing breakage.

**The fix (option A' from fe1's design notes).** Persist the per-file digest
list on the index, not only the single rolled-up InputHash. A check can then
tell exactly which files changed since the index was written. When the only
changed file is the one named, every other document's inbound edges are
trustworthy prior state, so the referrers this edit broke can be reported as
such and pre-existing breakage left to the corpus-wide check. When more than
one file changed, say so and fall back to fe1's corpus-wide behaviour rather
than guessing.

Note this is emphatically NOT option A from fe1 — reusing whatever index
happens to be on disk after a hash mismatch. That index's age is unbounded
(a different branch, fifty commits back), so referrers it names may themselves
have moved, and findings would be reported at spans that no longer exist. A'
differs precisely in proving the prior state is one edit old before trusting it.

**The digests already exist.** inputHasher.files (cli/core/corpus/hash.go)
holds {path, digest, unread} per candidate, sorted by path, and discards the
list once it is folded into the summary hash. This adds no computation — only
index size (~114 KB at 1,000 documents at full sha256 hex, ~70 KB truncated to
8 bytes) and a schema field.

**Uses beyond this one** (recorded in full as a comment on the parent ADR):
incremental rebuild — re-parse only changed files instead of the current
all-or-nothing cold rebuild, which is what keeps REQ-SPEC-009.1's warm-index
budget claimable as the corpus grows; actionable staleness diagnostics in place
of an opaque hash mismatch; and provenance tying a finding to the exact
document bytes it came from, relevant to the cross-repository merge semantics
of AC-SPEC-002.3.

**Sequencing.** This is an index schema change, so the parent ADR
(agent-plugins-h6c) decides the shape first; h6c in turn depends on
agent-plugins-47r, and if strata becomes the source of truth for the JSON
artifacts the digest list is a strata field. Migration is already provided for:
the input-hash-version tag folded into the summary invalidates every index
written under the old rules.
acceptance_criteria: A single-document check on a file whose slug changed reports the referrers that edit broke, and does NOT report unresolved references that were already broken before it — demonstrated by a test that edits a real file on disk rather than planting a row in the persisted index. When more than one file has changed since the index was written, the check reports that it cannot attribute the breakage and falls back to corpus-wide reporting.

title: Contract and .strata sources duplicate rationale prose near-verbatim; establish which is authoritative
description:
Raised by the repository owner in review of PR #16 against
`specs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md:8`: "How much of this contract
is already defined by `.strata` source files? Are we duplicating documentation
from those files rather than referencing it?"

**Measured: yes, in the rationale prose, near-verbatim.**

`schemas/config.strata` is 91 lines and **88% docstring by character count**
(2,490 of 2,844 chars). It is a prose document that happens to declare types.
The contract is 339 lines. The two carry the same argument in the same words.

`schemas/config.strata`:

> In particular there is no way to define a document type, register a block
> tag, or supply a schema from here. Those belong to the profile, and holding
> them back is what keeps the promise cheap: a key that was never public
> cannot be broken by changing it. Promotion runs one way and is additive, so
> a repository that never wrote a key it could not write is unaffected by a
> later version that lets it.

`specs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md:85-90`:

> There is deliberately no way to override a document type, add one, register
> a fenced block tag, or supply a schema. Those are the internal surface, and
> holding them back is what keeps v1's compatibility promise cheap: a key that
> was never public cannot be broken by changing it, and the framework's
> vocabulary is still moving. Promotion is one-way and additive — a repository
> that never wrote a key it could not write is unaffected by a later version
> that lets it.

Two copies of one argument, drifting independently. The risk is not the
duplication itself but that a future change updates one and not the other, and
neither reader can tell which is authoritative.

**Not all of the contract duplicates.** Sections that have no counterpart in
the `.strata` sources and are the contract's real content: Guarantees /
Resolution (`:206`), Checking the configuration (`:223`), Operational
Expectations (`:258`), Versioning and Change Policy (`:276`), Key Decisions
(`:299`), Open Questions (`:304`). The overlap is concentrated in Overview
(`:19`) and the two Specification subsections (`:62`, `:91`).
design:
This is a question about where prose lives across the whole spec corpus, not
just this one contract — treat the decision as setting a convention.

**Establish the rule first.** Which artifact is authoritative for what:

- The `.strata` source is authoritative for **shape** — what properties exist,
  their types and constraints. That is mechanically enforced and generated.
- The contract should be authoritative for **promise** — compatibility, the
  resolution order, what checking does, what a consumer may rely on across
  versions. None of that is expressible in a schema.
- **Rationale prose is the contested middle.** "Why the public surface is
  small" currently lives in both.

**Then check what the toolchain can actually do** before choosing:

1. Does the docs pipeline render `.strata` docstrings into a referencable
   page? If a contract can link to a generated page for the shape, the
   duplication is removable. If not, some restatement is unavoidable and the
   rule becomes "state the promise, summarise the shape in one line, link to
   the source".
2. Does `spec check` have any way to detect prose drift between a `.strata`
   docstring and a document that restates it? Probably not — note it if so,
   since that would make the convention enforceable rather than advisory.

**Then apply it to this contract**: keep Guarantees, Operational Expectations,
Versioning, Key Decisions and Open Questions; reduce Overview and the two
Specification subsections to the promise plus a pointer, with the worked
`specs.toml` example retained only if the generated docs do not carry an
equivalent.

**Do not simply delete the prose from one side.** The contract's version is
slightly richer ("and the framework's vocabulary is still moving"). Whichever
side loses the passage, the surviving copy should be the union of the two.

Check the other contracts and the `schemas/*.strata` sources for the same
pattern before closing — `finding.strata`, `frontmatter.strata`,
`index.strata`, `profile.strata` and `vocabulary.strata` are all candidates.

title: Ledger entries must cite the command that proved them, including claims of sufficiency
description:
Both repos keep an "environmental-failure ledger" in their agent instructions
(`/home/user/strata/AGENTS.md`, and per-run copies in `dispatch.md`) so agents
stop re-diagnosing the same failures. The mechanism is sound and worth keeping.
The problem is that entries are admitted on reasoning rather than on a run.

**Five ledger-shaped claims failed in one session (2026-08-07/08).** Four were
recorded as durable instructions; all five were plausible and none had been
executed:

| Claim | Reality | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| "worktree-parallel is unusable for any bead that runs `bd`" (`strata/AGENTS.md:493`) | False. `bd` resolves the shared DB via git's common directory; `bd where` from a worktree prints the main checkout's path. Concurrent writes lock-serialize cleanly. | Every bead of a 12-bead run dispatched sequentially |
| "release assets 404 through the proxy" (`strata/AGENTS.md:199-206`) | Half false. The browser URL 404s; `api.github.com/.../releases/assets/<id>` returns 200 with 3,141,712 bytes | A route dismissed without test |
| "`command -v bd strata`" verifies provisioning (`docs/session-bootstrap.md`) | Insufficient. Both binaries were present and `strata` was the build that silently destroys the schema | ~18 min plus three `cargo build --release` cycles |
| "`9kb.9.progress.jsonl` has never existed" (retro, since corrected) | False. Complete seven-event trail; the retro had read a stale snapshot | A published RFC with a refuted premise |
| "strata-lang/strata is public, so auth was never the bottleneck" (bead `bkf`, since corrected) | False. `private: True`. The reachability test ran with session credentials present | A viable PAT approach dismissed |

The common shape: **a true premise, a plausible inference, and no command.**
`.beads/embeddeddolt/` really is gitignored; the binaries really were on PATH;
the browser URL really does 404. Every inference drawn from those was wrong.

Note the third and fifth rows are not claims of impossibility — they are
claims of sufficiency and of access, which ran fine and proved nothing. A rule
that only gates "X is impossible" would miss them.
design:
Add a single admission rule to the ledger convention in both repos'
agent-instruction files, and to the `bead-bonanza` dispatch-plan template that
copies ledger entries into prompts.

**Proposed wording:**

> **Ledger entries are admitted on evidence, not on reasoning.** Every entry
> asserting what is impossible, unnecessary, unreachable, or already-verified
> SHALL cite the command that was run and the output observed. Run it first;
> record it after. A true premise plus a plausible inference is not evidence —
> five entries admitted that way in one session were wrong, and four of them
> had been copied into durable instructions where they kept costing capability.
>
> Applies equally to a claim of sufficiency ("this check verifies the install")
> as to a claim of impossibility — a check that runs clean and proves nothing
> is the harder case, because nothing about it looks like a failure.
>
> Where an entry cannot be tested cheaply, record it as **unverified** in the
> entry itself and say what would settle it. An entry marked unverified is
> useful; one that reads as settled and is not, is worse than absent.

**Also add the corollary about scope**, which is what made the two
credential-confounded claims wrong:

> State the conditions the command ran under when they could change the result
> — attached repositories, credentials present in the environment, warm versus
> cold caches, the toolchain version. A reachability or permission test run
> inside a session that already holds a grant measures the grant, not the
> capability.

**Where it goes:**
- `/home/user/strata/AGENTS.md` — at the head of the environmental-failure
  ledger section
- `/home/user/agent-plugins/CLAUDE.md` — wherever the equivalent guidance sits
- `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza` — the dispatch-plan ledger section, so per-run
  ledgers inherit the rule

**Then audit the existing entries** in both files against it. Any entry with no
cited command is either re-verified now or marked unverified. Expect several:
the two corrected this session were found by accident, not by audit.

Keep the existing trap-warning convention intact — this adds an admission bar,
it does not license deleting entries that carry forward-looking engineering
memory.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The admission rule is present at the head of the environmental-failure ledger section in strata's AGENTS.md and in this repo's equivalent guidance
- [ ] The rule covers claims of sufficiency and access, not only claims of impossibility
- [ ] The rule requires stating the conditions a command ran under when they could change the result (attached repos, credentials, cache warmth, toolchain version)
- [ ] The rule defines 'unverified' as a first-class entry state, with what would settle it
- [ ] The bead-bonanza dispatch-plan ledger section carries the same rule so per-run ledgers inherit it
- [ ] Every existing ledger entry in both files was audited; each is either re-verified with its command cited or marked unverified
- [ ] No entry was deleted to satisfy the rule — the trap-warning convention is intact

title: Move provisioning into the per-environment setup script, pinned by commit, with a verification that detects a wrong binary
description:
This session's SessionStart hook never ran, and the fallback that made it look
like it had was actively dangerous.

**Verified the hook did not fire.** `/root/.claude/session-env/<this-session>/`
is EMPTY, where a prior single-root session's directory contains
`sessionstart-hook-0.sh` with the hook's two exports verbatim. `env | grep
BD_` returns nothing (`session-start.sh:100-102,120-122` exports
`BD_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1`). Zero `[session-start]` log lines anywhere in the
transcript. Zero `bd prime` invocations.

**Root cause: two attached repos.** Claude Code registers hooks only from the
project root. Attaching `agent-plugins` and `strata` as siblings makes
`/home/user` the root, and `/home/user/.claude` does not exist — so
`agent-plugins/.claude/settings.json` is never read. Attaching ONE repo makes
that repo the root and the hook fires: verified against session `d49cdb0c`
(Aug 1, agent-plugins sole root), whose `session-env` directory contains the
hook's exports.

**Why nothing looked broken.** `bd` and `strata` were on PATH anyway, because
the container image was snapshotted on Aug 1 from that single-root session.
`/usr/local/bin/bd` mtime Jul 26; `~/.cache/strata-cli/build.log` ends Aug 1
with nothing appended since.

**And the snapshot carried `strata @ 44c1955`** — the build that per
`.bonanza/1786121603-ri/decisions.md` silently DESTROYS the schema (every
document type emits `"properties": {}`, 2202 lines -> 1326) while reporting
success. The session's first check at 16:53:34 read exactly that commit, then
spent ~18 minutes and three `cargo build --release` cycles isolating it.

**So the documented verification recipe is unsound.**
`docs/session-bootstrap.md` says the symptom is "no `bd` on PATH and no
`strata` binary" and verifies with `command -v bd strata`. This session had
both binaries present and one silently wrong. A presence check returns success
on a broken install — and note this is a claim of SUFFICIENCY that ran fine
and proved nothing, which is a harder case to catch than a claim of
impossibility.

## Correction — the PAT route is viable, and an earlier draft of this bead said otherwise

An earlier version of this description asserted that "strata-lang/strata is
public and already clones and fetches unauthenticated through the proxy, so
auth was never the bottleneck". **That is false.**

```
$ curl -sS https://api.github.com/repos/strata-lang/strata
  private: True
  visibility: private
$ env | grep -i token
  GH_TOKEN=<set>
  GITHUB_TOKEN=<set>
```

The reachability test that produced the claim ran inside a session where the
repo had already been attached by the user, with GitHub credentials in the
environment and the agent proxy brokering the request. It measured the
session's existing grant, not public access. Auth IS the bottleneck for an
unattached session, and a PAT is the mechanism that removes it.

Release GRANULARITY remains a separate, real objection to downloading a
prebuilt binary: the only published release is v0.7.0, fourteen commits behind
the only correct build (`840f9ba`), and `allowAdditionalProperties` — which
`schemas/strata.config.json:7` sets — does not exist at that tag. Releases are
tagged by version and `strata --version` reports `0.7.0` for all four relevant
builds, so no release artifact can express "I need v0.7.0-14". **Clone and
build at a pinned commit; do not download a release.**
design:
The durable fix is the per-environment setup script described in
`docs/session-bootstrap.md` — it runs before Claude Code launches and does not
depend on the project root. Combined with the correction above, the target
setup is:

**Attach ONE repo (`agent-plugins`) so the project root carries `.claude/` and
hooks fire. Obtain strata via a PAT-authenticated clone in the setup script.**

That gets the hook back AND drops the second root — the two problems have the
same cause and the same fix.

## Setup script requirements

1. **Clone strata with a PAT** stored as an environment secret. The repo is
   private; an unattached session has no credential for it. Use
   `git clone --filter=blob:none` — the blobless clone preserves per-file
   history, which `sync-strata-docs.sh` needs (it stamps each vendored file
   with `git -C "$STRATA_SRC" log -1 --format='%H' -- <path>`).
2. **Clone to `~/.cache/strata-src`, not `/opt/strata-src`.**
   `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh:62` searches `$STRATA_SRC_DIR`,
   `$REPO_ROOT/../strata`, `$HOME/strata`, `$HOME/.cache/strata-src` —
   `/opt/strata-src` is on none of them. With no match, `--check` prints
   `RESULT: SKIP (nothing to compare against).` and **exits 0**: a gate
   reporting green while comparing against nothing. The current draft in
   `docs/session-bootstrap.md` clones to `/opt/strata-src`.
3. **`git checkout <pin>` before `cargo build`.** The draft builds at whatever
   HEAD is; HEAD is currently `ce18d66`, which hard-errors with
   `/go/optionalStyle: unknown property`. Today's correct pin is `840f9ba`.
   Store it in a repo-owned file (e.g. `strata-pin`) that BOTH the setup script
   and `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh` read, so the two provisioning paths
   cannot drift.
4. **Write the pin to `~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit`** so the hook's warm
   path agrees instead of rebuilding.
5. **Replace the verification recipe** in `docs/session-bootstrap.md`. Instead
   of `command -v bd strata`, compare `cat ~/.cache/strata-cli/built-commit`
   against the pin. Note that a container image can carry provisioning from a
   prior single-root session, so presence proves nothing about correctness.
6. **Keep the shape assertion.** `scripts/generate-schemas.sh`'s `required`-list
   check is version-independent and catches the silent-destruction class a pin
   cannot (a pin only helps until it is bumped). Both halves are needed — this
   is `decisions.md`'s "2 + 3".

## Verify before recording

Per the ledger convention bead: run each command in a session with only
`agent-plugins` attached and confirm (a) the hook fires — check
`/root/.claude/session-env/<session>/` is non-empty — and (b)
`sync-strata-docs.sh --check` reports a real comparison rather than `SKIP`.
Record the observed output in the retro. Do not write the recipe into
`docs/session-bootstrap.md` before it has been run.

## Adjacent correction to fold in

`/home/user/strata/AGENTS.md:199-206` claims release assets are unreachable
through the proxy. Half wrong: the browser URL
(`github.com/.../releases/download/...`) returns 404, but the API endpoint
(`api.github.com/repos/.../releases/assets/<id>` with
`Accept: application/octet-stream`) returns 200 with 3,141,712 bytes of valid
gzip — verified twice. Correct the entry, while noting the release route stays
rejected for the granularity reason above. NOTE: that test also ran with
session credentials present, so re-verify it against a PAT-only session before
recording the correction.

## Separate hazard, same setup surface

`strata/.claude/skills/` carries sf-plugin skills vendored at **0.14.0** while
`agent-plugins/plugin` is **0.15.0**, and `spec/SKILL.md` differs (315 vs 333
lines). agent-plugins won the tie-break this session (verified from skill-load
base directories) but that ordering is not a guarantee. Moving to a single
attached repo makes this moot for co-attached sessions; if the vendored copies
stay, re-run `scripts/vendor-sf-skills.sh` in strata.

title: bd remember is write-only: bd export drops memories, and CLAUDE.md blames the import side
description:
`bd remember` is a write-only hole in this project: nothing written to it has
ever survived a container.

Measured today:

```
$ grep -c '"_type":"memory"' .beads/issues.jsonl
0                                  # of 95 records, all "_type":"issue"
$ bd export --help
  Memories (from 'bd remember') are excluded by default ...
  Use --include-memories or --all to include
$ bd import --help
  Memory records (lines with "_type":"memory") are automatically detected
  and imported ... 'bd export | bd import' a full round-trip
```

This is not inert plumbing. `plugin/skills/groom-beads/SKILL.md:334` instructs
agents to capture grooming-miss patterns as `bd remember "<insight>"`, and
`:103` tells a later agent to "skim existing `bd remember` insights". **A
shipped skill writes into a store guaranteed to be wiped, and another step
reads from the empty result.** The SessionStart hook's `bd prime --hook-json`
would inject those memories if any existed.

`CLAUDE.md:143-145` also misattributes the loss:

> - `bd remember` memories are **excluded** from `bd export` by default, and
>   the session-start hook imports without `--all`. Durable context belongs in
>   an issue description, not a memory.

The first clause is right; the second is wrong — `bd import` auto-detects
memory lines and has no `--all` flag at all. The loss is 100% on the export
side. Anyone debugging this from the current text goes to the wrong end.

Context: this was the only genuine persistence gap found when evaluating
third-party memory tooling. Every hosted option is proxy-403'd here
(`api.mem0.ai`, `api.getzep.com` both fail exactly as `bd dolt push` does) and
every local option must commit its store to git, reinventing
`.beads/issues.jsonl` with a weaker schema. Fixing this flag is the cheaper
and better win.
design:
Three edits, all small.

1. **Change the mandated export** wherever it appears — `CLAUDE.md`'s "Before
   ending a session" block, and any companion guidance in
   `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`:

   ```bash
   bd export --include-memories > .beads/issues.jsonl
   ```

   Note `bd config` exposes only `export.auto|path|interval|git-add` — there is
   no key that makes AUTO-export include memories. So the explicit end-of-session
   export is the only path, which the docs already mandate for the deletion
   reason. This adds a second reason to the same rule.

2. **Correct `CLAUDE.md:143-145`.** Replace the import clause with the measured
   behaviour: memories are excluded by `bd export` unless `--include-memories`
   or `--all` is passed; `bd import` auto-detects and imports them with no flag.
   Once the export carries them, drop or soften "durable context belongs in an
   issue description, not a memory" — that advice exists only to work around
   this bug.

3. **Verify the round trip end to end** before closing: `bd remember` a probe,
   run the corrected export, confirm the record appears in
   `.beads/issues.jsonl`, then confirm `bd import` of that file restores it.
   State the observed result in the retro.

Check whether the same stale advice appears in `/home/user/strata/CLAUDE.md`
or `AGENTS.md` and fix it there too if so.

title: Relational reference checks read documents off disk on the warm single-document path
description:
`cli/core/corpus/check.go` claims, in the comment immediately above the
`c.retiredTargetFindings()` / `c.pairingIncompleteFindings()` calls, that the
relational half of reference integrity is "a lookup over data already in
memory, not a second corpus walk". On a warm corpus that is not true of the
code path as written, and the comment is the kind of drift AGENTS.md says to
fix in the change that notices it.

## What the code actually does

`retiredTargetFindings` reaches `Corpus.document` through its helper
`successorOf` (`cli/core/corpus/check.go`); `pairingIncompleteFindings` calls
`c.document(resolved.TargetPath)` directly. `Corpus.document`
(`cli/core/corpus/corpus.go`) returns from the `c.docs` cache when present,
but on a warm corpus — where `c.docs` was never populated by a walk, because
there was no walk — it falls through to `readDocument`, which opens and
parses the file off disk.

Neither function is narrowed by `only`: both are called after the
`for _, entry := range c.index.Entries` loop that honours `only`, and each
iterates `c.index.References` corpus-wide. So a single-document check does
one disk read and parse per retired-target hit and per pairing reference in
the whole corpus, which makes AC-SPEC-009.2's single-document budget scale
with the corpus's relational-reference count rather than staying constant.

## Measured on this corpus — the defect is LATENT, not active

Taken during grooming against the committed tree, from `specs/specs.json`
built by `spec index`:

- `jq '.references | length'` -> **693** references, all 693 resolved.
- Documents with `status: retired`: **4**.
- References whose `resolution.target_path` is one of those retired
  documents: **0**. So `successorOf` — and therefore `Corpus.document` —
  is never reached from `retiredTargetFindings` on this corpus.
- `cli/profile/registration.go` declares
  `var pairings = map[string][]specmodel.PropertyPairing{}` — empty — and
  `TestTheProfileRegistersNoPairing` in `cli/profile/registration_test.go`
  asserts that emptiness. The `for _, pairing := range rules.Pairings` loop
  in `pairingIncompleteFindings` therefore never runs, so it performs no
  disk read either.
- Warm wall-clock, best of three each: whole-corpus `spec check` 177 ms;
  single-document `spec check specs/adrs/adr-002-ears-for-requirements.md`
  169 ms. The single-document path is not near the 100 ms target in
  AC-SPEC-009.2 for a different reason (this corpus is 58 documents, not the
  1,000 the criterion posits), and the relational checks contribute zero
  reads to either figure.

So the count the Design's first step asks for is **zero**, not "a handful".
The Design's own conditional therefore selects the cheap branch: this is a
comment fix plus a guard test, not a structural change.

## The coverage gap that makes it worth doing

`TestWarmQueriesAndChecksMeetTheirBudgets` in
`cli/core/corpus/cache_test.go` is the existing budget test — 1,000
documents, 20 samples, a 100 ms `checkTarget`. It builds its corpus with the
`document` helper in `cli/core/corpus/corpus_test.go`, which emits
`status: approved` and a body of nothing but the title heading. That corpus
has no retired documents and no references at all, so the budget test
exercises none of the relational path. The budget is green today because the
path is never taken, not because it is cheap — and nothing would report it if
a later change started taking it.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:`, 1-3 sentences.
Friction only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused
it (or the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs —
the plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro. A clean item
records none; say so rather than inventing filler.
design:
**Chosen approach: correct the comment, and add a guard test that exercises
the relational path against the budget.** The measurement in the Problem
selects this branch — zero references resolve to a retired target and the
profile registers no pairings, so the structural alternatives below buy
nothing measurable on this corpus and both were rejected.

Rejected, recorded so a later reader does not re-litigate them:

- *Carry the counterpart-declared fact and the target status on the index*,
  making the relational checks a genuine in-memory lookup and the comment
  true as written. This is the real structural fix, and it remains the right
  answer if the relational-reference count ever becomes non-trivial. Rejected
  now: it costs an index schema change and a rebuild, it would be a
  speculative optimization against a measured zero, and this sprint's other
  items are concurrently extending index resolution state — an index schema
  change here would collide with them for no measured gain.
- *Skip the relational checks for references whose findings the `only`
  narrowing would discard anyway.* Cheaper, keeps the index as-is, and makes
  the single-document cost proportional to one document's references.
  Rejected now for the same reason: it optimizes a path that currently costs
  nothing, and it adds a second narrowing rule to keep in step with the first.

## The work

1. **Fix the comment** above the `c.retiredTargetFindings()` /
   `c.pairingIncompleteFindings()` calls in `cli/core/corpus/check.go`. It
   must stop asserting that the relational half touches only memory. Say what
   is true: the relational checks walk the already-resolved reference
   collection rather than re-walking the corpus, but resolving a successor or
   a counterpart calls `Corpus.document`, which on a warm corpus reads and
   parses that one target off disk and caches it; and both run corpus-wide,
   unnarrowed by `only`. Keep the existing AC citations on the comment.

2. **Add the guard test.** Extend the corpus that
   `TestWarmQueriesAndChecksMeetTheirBudgets` (`cli/core/corpus/cache_test.go`)
   builds, or add a sibling test beside it, so that the warm single-document
   check runs against a corpus in which the relational path is actually taken:
   some documents `status: retired`, and live documents carrying references
   that resolve to them. Hold the same 100 ms `checkTarget` from
   AC-SPEC-009.2. Reuse the existing helpers (`document`, `write`, and the
   comparison helper the current test calls) rather than introducing a second
   fixture idiom; where `document` cannot express a status or a body
   reference, widen it or add a variant beside it rather than hand-rolling
   frontmatter inline.

The test is the durable part: it converts "green because the path is never
taken" into "green because the path is affordable", which is what the next
item to add per-reference work on this path needs in order to know whether it
regressed anything.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The comment above the `retiredTargetFindings` / `pairingIncompleteFindings` calls in `cli/core/corpus/check.go` no longer claims the relational checks are a memory-only lookup, and states that resolving a successor or counterpart reads the target document through `Corpus.document` and that both checks run corpus-wide regardless of `only`
- [ ] A warm single-document check is measured against a corpus in which at least one live document holds a reference resolving to a `status: retired` document, so the relational path is exercised rather than skipped
- [ ] That measurement holds the 100 millisecond target AC-SPEC-009.2 states for a single-document check against a warm index
- [ ] The new or extended test cites `AC: AC-SPEC-009.2`
- [ ] `TestWarmQueriesAndChecksMeetTheirBudgets` still passes
- [ ] `go test ./...` from `cli/` passes
- [ ] The project's declared checks pass: `format`, `vet`, `build`, `test-go`, `corpus`
- [ ] `module-document-core`'s Corpus component still describes the relational checks truthfully, updated if this change makes its text wrong

metadata.tier_reason: The decision is made and the measurement is inlined: correct one comment and extend an existing budget test with a fixture that exercises the relational path. Localized to two files in one package, with the approach and the rejected alternatives already recorded.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-08-09 at HEAD (5390f1d, spec built from cli/), which is step 1 of this bead's design note.

Corpus: 33 members. Relational references that reach c.document() on the warm path: 2 retired-target references (one each into feature-spec-reference-integrity and feature-spec-validation-cli) and 2 typed frd references from the two feature blueprints. Pairings: zero — the profile registers none (TestTheProfileRegistersNoPairings), so pairingIncompleteFindings does no disk work at all against this corpus.

Timing, warm index, 15 runs each:
  single document  median 49.1 ms | p95 57.8 ms
  corpus wide      median 48.6 ms | p95 64.5 ms
  slug-exists      median 42.4 ms | p95 44.8 ms

The two check paths are indistinguishable, and both sit ~42 ms above slug-exists — process start dominates, and 4 relational disk reads are not measurable inside it. AC-SPEC-009.2's 100 ms budget is for a 1,000-document corpus, so 58 ms p95 on 33 documents is not a margin reading either way.

CONCLUSION: this is option 1 from the design note — a comment fix plus a guard test, not urgent, and NOT a blocker for the reference-integrity feature. The real exposure is the scaling shape, not today's number: the relational checks are computed corpus-wide at check.go:136-138 before the --only narrowing at :143-150, so their cost tracks the corpus's retired-target and typed-reference count rather than the one document being checked. A corpus that retires documents routinely is where this bites. Worth a guard test that asserts the single-document path does no work proportional to corpus-wide relational references, so the regression is caught by the suite rather than by a slow hook.

Not implemented here.

title: sync-strata-docs.sh --check reports stale vendored copies after strata checkout advanced to HEAD
description:
# agent-plugins-ml9 Retro

## Bead Description

**sync-strata-docs.sh --check reports stale vendored copies after strata checkout advanced to HEAD**

The strata skill's vendored docs under `.claude/skills/strata/references/` (compiler-options.md, strata-llm-reference.md, language-reference.md) were stamped from older strata-lang/strata commits (8997153, 179d49029f4e, etc). Since `/home/user/strata` (the checkout scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh reads from) was advanced to HEAD ce18d66, `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` reported all 3 files STALE. This was masked in the combined 'test' gate because `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` exits 1 on a known pre-existing warning (bead-bonanza SKILL.md line count), short-circuiting the && chain before `sync-strata-docs.sh --check` ever runs.

## Retro

### Approach Taken
1. Ran `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh` (without --check) to re-vendor the docs from /home/user/strata HEAD (ce18d66)
2. Verified `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` exits 0 (confirming staleness is resolved)
3. Checked git diff to confirm against expected diffstat
4. Ran all gates independently (NOT chained with &&) to catch any issues
5. Staged and committed via `bb-close-bead.sh` script

### Actual Diffstat vs Expected
**Expected:** ~57 insertions and ~44 deletions across 3 files
**Actual:** 58 insertions, 44 deletions across 3 files (plus .beads/interactions.jsonl churn, which is expected audit trail)

Files changed:
- `.beads/interactions.jsonl` — +1 (audit trail, expected per CLAUDE.md)

title: Revise the specs-configuration contract's internal registration surface
description:
# agent-plugins-9kb.9 — Revise the specs-configuration contract's internal registration surface

**Blueprint:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-
blueprint.md — Contracts section.
**FRD:** specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 2); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-reference-integrity`.

[[contract-specs-configuration]]'s description of the **internal**
registration
surface enumerates what a profile supplies, and does not yet mention
reference-bearing properties, typed references, pairings, or the lifecycle
registration. This item brings the contract back in line with the surface
XPT
widened and PREG populated.

This is a Definition-of-Done entry rather than an element delta: the surface
it
documents is defined by XPT, populated by PREG, and modelled by MODEL, so it
belongs to no single delta.

**The revision is additive and to the internal half only**, which that
contract's own change policy exempts from versioning WHILE both
[[module-document-core]] and [[module-spec-profile]] are visibility:
internal. The public specs.toml surface is untouched, so **no **version**
bump
****is required** and no adopting repository's file changes meaning. Record
that
reason in the document rather than leaving the unchanged version
unexplained.

## Design

Anchor: specs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md (currently status:
approved, version: "1.0").

Revise **in place** — the blueprint calls this "drafted in place", meaning
the
contract is edited directly rather than superseded by a new document.

Enumerate, on the internal registration surface:

- reference-bearing frontmatter properties, per document type;
- typed reference properties, as a mapping from property name to the type
  its target must declare;
- property pairings, and that a profile MAY register none;
- the profile-level lifecycle registration: live statuses, retired statuses,
  and the successor property name.

Write these as statements of current behaviour, not as a change narrative —
no "newly added", no "as of this feature". Keep version: "1.0" and state why
the version is unchanged.

## Retro

### Approach

Read the delivered code first, as instructed, before touching the contract:
`cli/core/corpus/profile.go` (the `Profile` interface, `DocumentTypeRules`,
`LifecycleRules`) and `cli/profile/{profile.go,registration.go}` (what the
shipped `spec-driven-dev` profile actually registers — derived reference
properties from the embedded schema, one authored typed reference
(`FeatureBlueprint.frd` → `frd`), an empty pairing set by design, and the
lifecycle derived from the `Status` enum with `retired` as the sole retired
status).

Edited `specs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md` in place, inside the
existing "### The internal surface: profile registration" subsection:

- Added a bullet-list paragraph enumerating reference-bearing properties,
  typed reference properties, and pairings (explicitly noting a profile MAY
  register none), followed by a `DocumentTypeRules`/`PropertyPairing` Go
  snippet mirroring the real types — same convention the existing doc
  already used for the `Section` struct.
- Added a lifecycle paragraph (live statuses, retired statuses, successor
  property, and the MAY-register-none case) with a matching
  `LifecycleRules` Go snippet.
- Added one closing paragraph, right before `## Guarantees`, stating that
  `version` stays `"1.0"` for this whole addition and citing the specific
  exemption clause (both modules `visibility: internal`) plus the untouched
  public surface — the AC required this reason to be recorded in the
  document, not just true by cross-reference to the general policy already
  present further down.
- Bumped `updated_at` in the frontmatter to today's date, per
  `frontmatter-standards.md` convention (not explicitly required by the
  bead's AC, but consistent with how other spec docs are revised).
- Left `version: "1.0"` and everything else in the frontmatter untouched.

### Implicit decisions and why

1. **Did not touch the pre-existing "section hierarchy / named section sets
   / fenced block tags / record-XOR-blueprint-link invariant" paragraph**,
   even though it describes capabilities (`RequiredSections`, block-tag
   registration, custom invariant hooks) that do not exist anywhere in the
   live `corpus.Profile` interface today — confirmed by grepping for
   `RequiredSection`, `BlockTagRegistration`, and `type Section struct`
   across `cli/`, which only turn up in `cli/core/specmodel/specmodel.go`
   (the generated spec-index data model, not a consumed Go interface), and
   by `cli/profile/profile.go`'s own package comment: "Element records and
   required sections are later capabilities, and each will widen this
   interface further." This is a real, pre-existing inaccuracy, but the
   bead's Design section scopes the revision to four specific additive
   enumerations and its Acceptance Criteria don't ask for a fix here.
   Fixing it would have meant re-deciding whether to describe it as a
   stated future capability or remove the claim outright — a real editorial
   call outside this bead's remit. Filed `agent-plugins-x6c` (P3,
   `discovered-from` agent-plugins-9kb.9) instead of fixing it inline.
2. **Placement of the new content**: inserted between the existing
   `Section` struct paragraph and the "Because the public surface no longer
   overlaps..." bridging paragraph, rather than at the very top of the
   subsection. The bridging paragraph reads as a subsection-closer tying
   `[profile].name`/`[conventions]` back to `specs.toml`, so the new
   material needed to land before it to keep that closing role intact.
3. **Illustrated the new registrations with Go snippets** (`DocumentTypeRules`,
   `PropertyPairing`, `LifecycleRules`) mirroring the real struct shapes
   in `cli/core/corpus/profile.go`, rather than prose alone — matching the
   document's own established convention (the `Section` struct is already
   quoted that way) and reducing drift risk versus paraphrase.
4. **Version-unchanged rationale placed as its own paragraph at the end of
   the internal-surface subsection**, not folded into the Versioning and
   Change Policy section further down. The AC says the reason must be
   "recorded in the document" for *this revision specifically* — the
   existing general exemption clause in the Change Policy section states
   the *policy* but doesn't say this particular edit relied on it. Keeping
   both (general policy + this revision's explicit invocation of it)
   seemed the more literal reading of the AC.
5. **Did not touch the `## Specification` table row for the `Profile`
   interface** ("Shape of the internal registration surface") — it was
   already accurate and generic enough to cover the widened surface without
   naming `DocumentTypeRules` explicitly.

### What differed from the instructions

Nothing procedural differed. One thing worth flagging: the workflow step 3
says "Stay strictly in scope; file anything beyond it as a new bead ... and
do NOT implement it" — I used `bd dep add ... --type discovered-from`
(a real dependency type `bd` supports) rather than only a
`discovered-from:<id>` label, since the CLI has first-class support for it
and it produces a queryable `DISCOVERED FROM` relationship on `bd show`.
The instructions' example workflow elsewhere in this framework uses the
label form; I used the dependency type in addition to the label because it
is more correct and `bd dep add` accepted `discovered-from` as a listed
type — this is a strictly additive choice, not a deviation from what was
asked.

### Surprises / ideas for improving prompts or skills

- The single biggest time cost was distinguishing "the real, live
  `corpus.Profile` Go interface" from "the generated `specmodel.go` data
  model that happens to share vocabulary" (`DocumentTypeRegistration`,
  `Section`, `BlockTagRegistration` exist in both, but only one is actually
  wired to a consumer). A prompt or skill note that says "when grounding a
  contract revision in code, grep for callers of the type, not just its
  declaration — specmodel.go's generated types are a schema artifact, not
  necessarily a live extension point" would have saved a few minutes and
  is a genuinely reusable trap warning for this codebase.
- The bead's Design section was precise enough that no clarifying question
  was needed — the four enumeration items map cleanly onto
  `DocumentTypeRules.{ReferenceProperties,TypedReferenceProperties,Pairings}`
  and `Profile.Lifecycle()`/`LifecycleRules`. Grooming quality here was high.
- The gate list correctly flagged that
  `TestProfileSelfApplicationAgainstThisRepositorysCorpus` runs against this
  repo's own `specs/` corpus — worth double-checking the whole `cli` test
  suite (not just a targeted package) after any spec-doc edit, which I did
  (`go test -count=1 ./...`), and it was green with the new content in
  place.

title: RFC-0012 P7: derive children from parent_slug; drop the pairing
description:
Adopted at triage of rfcs/inbox/spec/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md (P7) on 2026-08-06.

## Problem
The framework's own worked example of a paired relationship — 'children'
paired with 'parent_slug' — requires both ends even though the index derives
either from the other, and a promoted child has exactly one parent. The
Document Relationship Standard reserves a pairing for a document that must be
read without the index, and forbids using one to enforce a mirror the index
already derives. The framework's shipped example now contradicts its standard.

## TRIAGE EXTENT FINDING — 'children' and 'parent_slug' are not in the vocabulary
Neither property exists in schemas/frontmatter.strata. Verified 2026-08-06 by
grepping parent_slug across the repo: every corpus-side hit is an EXAMPLE, not
a declaration. (The parent_slug in work-order-template.md and work-order-
definition-of-ready.md is a beads work-order field, a different namespace, and
is out of scope.) So this is not 'remove a pairing from the shipped
configuration' — there is no shipped configuration yet and no such properties.
It is: stop presenting that pairing as the framework's canonical example.

The pairing CAPABILITY stays. AC-SPECREF-004.1 and AC-SPECREF-004.3 are
unchanged — an adopting team may still need a pairing, and the standard
permits one when argued.

## Change
1. specs/features/reference-integrity/reference-integrity-frd.md, three sites:
   - the 'Paired relationship' glossary entry (~line 143): replace the
     '(for example children and parent_slug)' example with an adopter-side
     example, since this framework registers no pairing.
   - AC-SPECREF-002.5's Example (~line 276): same substitution.
   - AC-SPECREF-004.2 (~line 402-407): the shipped configuration marks
     'superseded_by' and (per P2) 'frd' as reference-bearing and registers NO
     pairing. State that absence deliberately, citing the standard.
2. schemas/profile.strata: the PropertyPairing struct doc-comment uses the
   same children/parent_slug example. Replace it, then run
   scripts/generate-schemas.sh.
3. plugin/skills/spec/references/frontmatter-standards.md: remove
   'parent_slug'/'children' from the relationship-property YAML block and the
   Contents summary. No version bump here — P8 owns it.
4. specs/adrs/ADR-009-nodes-and-edges-ownership.md: add the one-line
   companion note the RFC asks for — deriving a parent's membership roster
   from child back-pointers preserves this ADR's 'one authoritative home, no
   drift' intent, because the rule governs neighbour edges AMONG children,
   not the parent-child membership edge. Write it as a statement of current
   behaviour, not as an amendment note. Bump updated_at.

## Acceptance
- generate-schemas.sh --check clean; validate-corpus.py passes
- no children<->parent_slug pairing presented as this framework's own
close_reason: Landed in the RFC-0012 triage on 2026-08-06. See the Resolution in rfcs/retired/rfc-0012-document-relationship-vocabulary.md.
