title: Ship cross-compiled static binaries and CI
description:
# agent-plugins-bge.13 — Ship cross-compiled static binaries and CI

## DESCRIPTION

**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **BUILD**, section "Static binary and distribution in container-spec-cli (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 3 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Ship the CLI as a per-platform statically linked binary that installs without
a runtime or network fetch, satisfying the portability and supply-chain
requirements an adopting security review turns on.

**CI exists but does not cover Go.** `.github/workflows/checks.yml` runs on
push and pull_request, but only the docs-corpus gates (`check-skills.sh`,
`sync-shared-references.sh --check`, `validate-corpus.py`). There is no Go
build/test job and no release matrix. This item adds those; it does not
create CI from nothing. (Corrected 2026-08-04: the work order's original
premise that the repository had no CI at all was already stale when written.)

**Open obligation — the `(manual)` markers.** The blueprint's AC Coverage
table declares AC-SPEC-009.4, 009.5 and 009.6 verified at *manual* level, but
`specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md` does **not** append the
`(manual)` marker to those three criteria. Per the AC traceability standards,
a criterion is exempt from the citation obligation only once the FRD records
that designation — so as written these three are simultaneously
un-citable-by-test and non-exempt. Resolve it in this item by one of:
(a) appending `(manual)` to those criteria in the FRD, which is the mechanical
consequence of the level the blueprint already approved; or (b) recording an
automated verification for them. Do not close this item leaving the
contradiction in place. Flagged at grooming time — see also the final DoD
item, which audits citations.

`agent-plugins-55q` ("ADR: release and distribution of CLI binaries") is open
in the tracker and directly relevant to this item, though the blueprint's
Tracker Reconciliation does not list it. Check it before choosing a
distribution mechanism.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.


## DECISION (2026-08-04)

On the `(manual)` marker contradiction described above. Options considered:

- **Append `(manual)` to AC-SPEC-009.4/.5/.6 in the FRD — SELECTED.**
  Records in the FRD the verification level the blueprint already approved.
  A clerical fix, not a scope change: the three criteria become legitimately
  exempt from the citation obligation per
  `specs/standards/testing-standards.md` lines 266-268. This is RFC 0010 P3.
- Find automated verification for all three and move those rows off `manual`
  in the blueprint's AC Coverage table. Rejected for this run as materially
  more work than the bead was sized for.
- Leave unresolved and let the final DoD item flag it. Rejected: ships a
  known hole in AC traceability.

Implement the selected option as part of this bead: edit
`specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md` so each of AC-SPEC-009.4,
AC-SPEC-009.5 and AC-SPEC-009.6 carries the `(manual)` marker in the format
`frd-template.md` defines. Do not change what the criteria require.

## DESIGN

- The CLI runs on a machine with no language runtime, interpreter or package
  manager installed beyond the binary itself.
- Installation retrieves no executable content from the network, and the CLI
  is installable from at least one package registry that supports
  on-premises mirroring.
- The build produces the platform matrix by cross-compilation from a single
  source, and identical corpus content yields byte-identical output across
  Linux, macOS and Windows — in concert with the determinism the Corpus item
  implements.

Anchors: Go build/release configuration and CI under `.github/workflows`
(to be created).

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [ ] The binary runs in an image containing only a shell and the binary
      (**proves AC-SPEC-009.4**, manual).
- [ ] Installation retrieves no executable content from the network
      (**proves AC-SPEC-009.5**, manual).
- [ ] The CLI is installable from at least one registry supporting
      on-premises mirroring (**proves AC-SPEC-009.6**, manual).
- [ ] Identical corpus content yields byte-identical output on Linux, macOS
      and Windows, including a CRLF checkout on Windows (**proves
      AC-SPEC-009.7**, e2e).
- [ ] The platform matrix is produced by cross-compilation from a single
      source.
- [ ] CI exists under `.github/workflows` and runs the test suite.
- [ ] The `(manual)` marker contradiction described in Problem is resolved
      one way or the other, and the resolution is stated on this issue.
- [ ] Static binary and distribution are recorded in
      `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md`, delivered in this same
      change.

---

## Retro

### Approach taken

Five things shipped, in the order they became necessary rather than the
order the bead lists them.

**1. The `(manual)` markers (the baked-in DECISION).** Appended `(manual)`
to the criterion text of AC-SPEC-009.4, AC-SPEC-009.5 and AC-SPEC-009.6 in
`specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`, in the position
`plugin/skills/spec/references/frd-template.md` defines ("append the marker
`(manual)` to the end of the criterion text") — at the end of the SHALL
sentence, before each criterion's `*Example:*` sub-bullet, which is part of
the criterion's illustration rather than its text. What the three criteria
require is unchanged. They are now legitimately exempt from the citation
obligation per `specs/standards/testing-standards.md` lines 266-268, which
is what the blueprint's AC Coverage table (`manual` on all three rows)
already assumed.

**2. AC-SPEC-009.7 — and the two defects that stood in its way.** The bead
said the determinism was already implemented in `cli/core/corpus` and that
my job was the assertion. Half true. Probing before writing the test:

- `check --json` output *was* byte-identical between an LF and a CRLF
  working tree — the criterion's normative text ("the same findings in the
  same order") held.
- The **index** was not. Span offsets moved (`offset: 11` → `12`,
  `length: 158` → `163`) and `input_hash` changed entirely, because both are
  functions of the file's bytes and a CRLF checkout genuinely has different
  bytes. That is the criterion's own worked example ("a corpus checked out
  with CRLF line endings on Windows yields byte-identical JSON output")
  failing.

Fixed at the single choke point that makes it a small change:
`readUnder` in `cli/core/corpus/corpus.go` now normalizes CRLF to LF, and
`scanCandidates` is the only walk in the package — both `Build` and
`Fingerprint` read through it, so the index's spans and the warm-cache
hash can never disagree about what a file is made of. It is a no-op on an
LF checkout, so no committed golden moved (verified by diffing pre- and
post-fix output on the same corpus).

**3. The vacuous snapshot harness.** With the fix in, I ran a negative
control — reverted the normalization and expected the new portability test
to fail. **It passed.** `cli/cmd/snapshot_test.go` resolved each case's
directory as a path relative to the package (`../testdata/cases/<name>`)
and then `os.Chdir`'d into a fresh `t.TempDir()` before reading
`expected/checks.log` and `expected/manifest.json`. After the chdir that
relative path resolved against the temp dir, missed, and hit the
`os.IsNotExist(err) { return }` branch that exists so a case can carry only
one of the two artifacts. **Every artifact comparison in the entire
snapshot suite was silently skipping.** Only the exit-status assertion was
live. Confirmed directly: replacing `index-default`'s committed
`manifest.json` with `{"corrupt":true}` and running `TestSnapshotCases`
reported `ok`.

Fixed with `filepath.Abs(dir)` before the chdir. This was not in scope, but
AC-SPEC-009.7's entire evidence rested on those comparisons being live, so
the bead could not be delivered around it. After the fix every committed
golden still matches — the vacuum had not masked any drift.

Then the negative control behaves: with the normalization reverted, four
cases fail under CRLF (`check-only`, `index-default`, `index-out-custom`,
`index-out-stdout`); with it restored, all pass. Corrupting either kind of
golden now fails its case in both suites.

**4. The portability test** — `cli/cmd/portability_test.go`, citing
`// AC: AC-SPEC-009.7`. It replays *every* existing snapshot case a second
time from a working tree it has itself rewritten to CRLF, holding the
result to the same committed artifacts. Reusing the existing cases rather
than adding a fixture means zero new golden-maintenance surface and no
second regeneration path. `runSnapshotCaseWith` in `snapshot_test.go` is
the seam (a `materialize func(src, dst string) error` parameter); the check
logic is shared, not copied, so the two runners cannot drift apart. Also
carries two tests of the CRLF fixture machinery itself and a guard against
a zero-case run reporting success.

The file's own header states plainly which half of the claim it is: the
*cross-platform* half is the CI matrix comparing three operating systems to
one committed set of expected bytes, which no single test process can
observe; the *cross-checkout* half is what this file does.

**5. `.gitattributes`, CI, and the release pipeline.** Detailed below.

### Implicit decisions, and why

- **A separate `.github/workflows/cli.yml` rather than more jobs in
  `checks.yml`.** `checks.yml` is one Linux runner needing only bash and
  python3; this needs a Go toolchain and three operating systems, and its
  failures mean something different. Two workflows keep the two signals
  legible. `checks.yml` was not touched.
- **No `paths:` filter on `cli.yml`.** A path-filtered workflow that is
  required for merge simply never reports on a PR outside its paths, which
  blocks the merge rather than passing it. Running the matrix on a docs-only
  commit is the price of avoiding that. Stated in the workflow's header.
- **`.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`.** Forced by putting
  `windows-latest` in the matrix: Git's `core.autocrlf` default there would
  rewrite the committed `expected/*.json` goldens on checkout, and a
  repository whose expected artifacts arrive as CRLF cannot compare them to
  anything. This does not weaken AC-SPEC-009.7 — it is what makes it
  testable, since the CRLF checkout is reproduced synthetically on every
  platform by the portability test. Verified it causes no churn in this
  (already-LF) tree.
- **Platform matrix: six targets** — `linux`, `darwin`, `windows` × `amd64`,
  `arm64`. Covers `agent-plugins-55q`'s stated need (macOS, Linux, Windows)
  and adds arm64 because it is free with Go cross-compilation and is now the
  default Mac and a common CI runner.
- **`CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-trimpath`, `-ldflags="-s -w"`.** `CGO_ENABLED=0` is
  what makes each artifact one statically linked file with no libc to
  resolve, i.e. AC-SPEC-009.4. `-trimpath` keeps the builder's absolute
  paths out of the bytes. Archives are additionally built with
  `--sort=name --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime='UTC 2020-01-01'`
  so the container is reproducible too, not just its contents.
- **Distribution: two channels, `go install` first.** The Go module proxy is
  the registry AC-SPEC-009.6 is satisfied by — it is mirrorable on premises
  (GOPROXY, Athens, Artifactory), and it needs no release artifact at all,
  which is a much stronger answer to AC-SPEC-009.5 than "download a tarball"
  because no install-time code runs either way. GitHub Releases are the
  second channel, for a machine with no Go toolchain. No third-party
  actions anywhere in either workflow (`gh` CLI, not `softprops/…`), which
  is the same supply-chain argument applied to the pipeline itself.
- **The entry point moved: `cli/main.go` → `cli/spec/main.go`.** Go names an
  installed binary after the directory holding its main package, so at the
  module root `go install …/cli@latest` would install a binary called `cli`.
  From `cli/spec/` it installs one called `spec`, which is the tool's name
  and the name its own cobra `Use` field already claims. Since `go install`
  is the AC-SPEC-009.6 answer, that name is part of the deliverable rather
  than cosmetic. Nothing referenced `cli/main.go` — checked the specs, the
  scripts and the workflows.
- **Release tags are `cli/vX.Y.Z`, not `vX.Y.Z`.** Forced by the above: the
  Go module lives in the repository's `cli/` subdirectory, and the module
  proxy resolves a subdirectory module's versions only from tags carrying
  that prefix. Channel 1 does not work without it. Recorded in the workflow
  header and in the container blueprint.
- **`no-runtime` job proves AC-SPEC-009.4 by running rather than
  asserting** — the static `linux/amd64` binary is executed inside
  `busybox:latest` (a shell, coreutils, musl, no package manager, no Go)
  against a committed snapshot corpus. The criterion stays `(manual)` per
  the DECISION; this is evidence in addition, not a re-levelling. Also
  asserts static linkage via `file` rather than `ldd`, because `ldd`'s
  wording for a static binary varies by distribution ("not a dynamic
  executable" vs "statically linked") and its exit status is not a signal.
- **The release workflow re-runs the gates.** A tag can be pushed at a
  commit whose `cli.yml` run never completed; a released binary that was
  never tested is worse than a slower release.
- **Container blueprint over ADR.** Recorded build flags, the two
  distribution channels, the entry-point/tag-prefix reasoning, and the
  read-path basis of AC-SPEC-009.7 in
  `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md` — which is what the bead's own
  final AC asks for. See the `agent-plugins-55q` note below for what was
  deliberately *not* decided.

### How `agent-plugins-55q` was handled

Read it first, as instructed. It asks for "an approved ADR plus a release
workflow producing macOS, Linux and Windows artifacts on a tagged release."
The workflow half is now built. The ADR half is not, and **55q is left
open**.

My choices do pre-empt three of the five questions 55q lists — the
platform/arch matrix, GitHub Releases as the channel, and the fetch story
for an agent session (`go install`, or download-and-unpack). I have recorded
them in the container blueprint as decisions rather than leaving them
undocumented, but they are provisional: 55q can overturn any of them, and
the blueprint text says so.

Two of 55q's questions I deliberately did **not** answer, because answering
them would have been guessing at policy rather than implementing a bead:

- **How binaries are versioned against the plugin version.** The binaries
  currently carry no version string at all, and there is no `--version`
  flag. Filed as **`agent-plugins-8i2`** (`discovered-from` bge.13,
  `related` 55q). Does not block this bead.
- **Whether checksums and signing apply.** `SHA256SUMS` ships with every
  release; nothing is signed. Signing is a key-custody decision, which is
  ADR territory.

### What I could NOT verify

- **Neither workflow was executed.** There is no network path to GitHub
  Actions runners from this environment. Both were validated statically
  (`yaml.safe_load` parses each; every `run:` block passes `bash -n` with
  `${{ }}` expressions neutralized) and by rehearsal of the parts that do
  not need a runner:
  - the six-target cross-compile, the archive/zip packaging and the
    `sha256sum` step were **run end to end locally** and produced six
    correct artifacts plus `SHA256SUMS`;
  - the static-linkage assertion was run locally (`file` reports
    `statically linked`);
  - the CLI was confirmed to work against a **read-only** corpus, which is
    what the container step mounts.
- **The `busybox` container step could not be run** — a Docker client is
  present in this container but there is no daemon
  (`/var/run/docker.sock` absent). The step is reasoned-correct and its
  inputs were verified, but it has never executed.
- **`go test ./...` has never run on macOS or Windows.** That is precisely
  what the new matrix is for, and it is the one part of AC-SPEC-009.7's
  evidence I am handing to CI rather than to a local run. If a case fails
  on the Windows leg on first run, the likely suspects are `os.OpenRoot`
  behavior and path handling in `cli/core/corpus`, not the portability test
  itself.
- **`gh release create` was not exercised.** No token, no repository to
  release into.

### Surprises

- The bead's premise that "the determinism AC-SPEC-009.7 asserts is already
  implemented" was **half wrong**, and the half that was wrong was invisible
  from the findings output — `check --json` was already identical across
  line endings while the index was not. A findings-only assertion would have
  passed and certified nothing.
- The snapshot suite has been asserting nothing but exit codes since
  `agent-plugins-bge.12` landed. That is the second time in this bead that
  a negative control caught something a green test run reported as fine. I
  would not have found it if I had trusted the passing test.
- Both of these were found by the same habit — deliberately breaking the
  implementation to confirm the test notices. Worth institutionalizing.

### Beads filed

- **`agent-plugins-0i6`** (P2, bug, `discovered-from` bge.13) — the
  residual half of the harness defect: `checkChecksLog` and `checkManifest`
  still treat a *missing* golden identically to "this case carries only the
  other artifact", so a renamed or deleted expected file still passes
  silently. A case should declare which artifacts it carries. Does not
  block this bead; the path-resolution defect that made it universal is
  fixed here.
- **`agent-plugins-8i2`** (P2, `discovered-from` bge.13, `related` 55q) —
  `spec --version` and version stamping on released binaries.

### Files changed

- `cli/core/corpus/corpus.go` — CRLF normalization at the read choke point
- `cli/cmd/snapshot_test.go` — absolute case path (the vacuum fix) + the
  `runSnapshotCaseWith` seam
- `cli/cmd/portability_test.go` — **new**, AC-SPEC-009.7 evidence
- `cli/spec/main.go` — **moved** from `cli/main.go`
- `.gitattributes` — **new**
- `.github/workflows/cli.yml` — **new**
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — **new**
- `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md` — `(manual)` markers
- `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md` — build, distribution,
  entry-point and reproducibility record
- `AGENTS.md` — "What CI runs", and the `.gitattributes` rationale

### Gate results

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `cd cli && gofmt -l .` | clean (no output) |
| `scripts/check-skills.sh` | PASS — `0 error(s), 1 warning(s)` (the known-red baseline, unchanged) |
| `cd cli && go vet ./...` | pass |
| `cd cli && go build ./...` | pass |
| `scripts/check-skills.sh --strict` | exit 1 on the pre-existing 859-line warning — baseline, no new findings |
| `scripts/sync-shared-references.sh --check` | all 11 current |
| `scripts/sync-strata-docs.sh --check` | all 3 match |
| `cd cli && go test ./...` | all packages ok |
| `scripts/generate-schemas.sh --check` | up to date |
| `scripts/validate-corpus.py` (CI) | 24 documents, 0 findings |
| `spec check` (self-application) | the one expected `plan` finding on the blueprint (`agent-plugins-tff`), nothing new |
design:
- The CLI runs on a machine with no language runtime, interpreter or package
  manager installed beyond the binary itself.
- Installation retrieves no executable content from the network, and the CLI
  is installable from at least one package registry that supports
  on-premises mirroring.
- The build produces the platform matrix by cross-compilation from a single
  source, and identical corpus content yields byte-identical output across
  Linux, macOS and Windows — in concert with the determinism the Corpus item
  implements.

Anchors: Go build/release configuration and CI under `.github/workflows`
(to be created).

- [ ] The binary runs in an image containing only a shell and the binary

- [ ] Installation retrieves no executable content from the network
      (**proves AC-SPEC-009.5**, manual).
- [ ] The CLI is installable from at least one registry supporting
      on-premises mirroring (**proves AC-SPEC-009.6**, manual).
- [ ] Identical corpus content yields byte-identical output on Linux, macOS
      and Windows, including a CRLF checkout on Windows (**proves
      AC-SPEC-009.7**, e2e).
- [ ] The platform matrix is produced by cross-compilation from a single
      source.
- [ ] CI exists under `.github/workflows` and runs the test suite.

      one way or the other, and the resolution is stated on this issue.
- [ ] Static binary and distribution are recorded in
      `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md`, delivered in this same
      change.

title: triage-rfc: rule for versioning a changed file that has no version property (RFC P2)
description:
## Problem

`triage-rfc` step 5 instructs the agent to bump versions, and every
verb presupposes a predecessor. It gives no rule for a changed file
that carries no version property at all.

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:182-190`:

    - Bump the version of every changed template (instruction-block
      `Version:`), skill (frontmatter `version`), and standard
      (frontmatter `version`) per [[template-authoring-standards]].
      **Bump each file exactly once for the whole triage, no matter how
      many proposals changed it** — ...

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Observed in the triage run of 2026-08-01, model claude-opus-5.

`plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md` and
`plugin/skills/spec/references/ears-guide.md` had no `version` field —
the absence was itself one of the things that run was fixing. With no
rule available, the agent wrote `version: "0.2"` into `c4-guide.md`,
reasoning that the file was also receiving a content change and so
should land above its initial value, then reversed itself in a second
edit within the same run to `version: "0.1"`, on the ground that `0.2`
implies a `0.1` that a reader could diff against and none ever existed.
Both guides shipped `0.1`. The reversal is two consecutive edits to one
line in that session.

This is not cosmetic. Step 1's provenance check is version-keyed
(SKILL.md:66-67: "compare the cited skill/template/standard versions
against the current ones"), so a version implying a predecessor that
never existed makes the "already fixed?" question unanswerable for that
file.

Source: rfcs/inbox/triage-rfc/rfc-self-triage-rfc-evidence-completeness.md,
proposal P2 (severity snag, origin self, runs_observed 1).
design:
Append to the version-bump bullet in step 5, after the existing
sentence ending "verify the bump after the final change to that file,
never before.", continuing the same 5-space bullet-body indentation:

     WHEN a changed file carries no version property at all, do not
     bump — add one at `0.1`, and let this triage's change land inside
     that first version. A higher initial value implies a predecessor a
     reader could diff against; for a file that has never been
     versioned there is none, and step 1's provenance check would then
     be asking about a version that never existed. Place the property
     per [[frontmatter-standards]].

Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The step-5 version bullet states that a file with no version property gets 0.1 rather than a bump
- [ ] It gives the reason (a higher initial value implies a predecessor that never existed)
- [ ] It points at [[frontmatter-standards]] for placement
- [ ] Every line added is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead
notes: Tier: light. tier_reason: a single append to the end of one existing bullet with the wording supplied; no other step references it and no cross-file coordination is needed. No C4 component is affected.
close_reason: Step 5 version bullet now covers a changed file with no version property (add 0.1, do not bump).

title: triage-rfc: admit triage-originated changes to step 4 and the Resolution (RFC P3)
description:
## Problem

`triage-rfc` step 4 and the Resolution format both assume every change
originates as a proposal in a received RFC, so a change triage itself
originates has no id, no table row and no outcome slot.

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:127-128`:

    4. **Present the recommendation and STOP for approval.** One table:
       proposal, classification, one-line rationale, files touched.

`SKILL.md:225-228` (the Resolution bullet) is likewise per-proposal:
"per-proposal outcome (adopted / adopted-with-refinement + the
refinement / deferred + bead id / rejected + rationale)".

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Observed in the triage run of 2026-08-01, model claude-opus-5.

That run adopted one change no RFC proposed: adding a `version`
property to `plugin/skills/spec/references/c4-guide.md` and
`ears-guide.md`. It was not a proposal — both RFCs had recorded it
under *Considered and Not Proposed*, RFC 0007 explicitly asking for "a
sweep of all guides rather than two one-line fixes".

With no rule to follow, the agent invented a row id `X1` outside the
`P` numbering, annotated it "(your call — not a proposal)", and then at
Resolution time invented a section heading "**Also adopted, outside
this RFC's proposals**" because no per-proposal row could hold it. Two
inventions in one run for one change.

The same gap recurred immediately: the following triage run took a
change reported directly by the human (see the sibling bead on the
already-implemented wording), which likewise had no id or row until one
was improvised.

Source: rfcs/inbox/triage-rfc/rfc-self-triage-rfc-evidence-completeness.md,
proposal P3 (severity snag, origin self, runs_observed 1).
design:
Two edits.

1. In step 4, immediately after the sentence "One table: proposal,
   classification, one-line rationale, files touched." and before
   "Implement nothing before the human approves", insert at 3-space
   indent:

   A triage MAY originate a change no RFC proposed — one the evidence
   implies, or an item an RFC recorded under Considered and Not
   Proposed that this triage judges ready. Table it as its own row,
   numbered `T1..Tn` so it is never confused with an RFC's `P` ids,
   with its origin given as triage. It carries the same evidence bar
   and needs the same approval; what it lacks is a reporter, so the
   rationale column carries triage's own reasoning and says so.

2. Append to the Resolution bullet in step 5 (the bullet beginning
   "Write the RFC's Resolution section"), continuing its indentation:

     Record any `T` change in the Resolution of the RFC whose evidence
     prompted it, in its own row, marked as triage-originated rather
     than that RFC's testimony. WHERE no RFC prompted it — a change
     reported directly by the human — record it in the Resolution of
     the RFC triaged alongside it, marked the same way.

The second sentence of edit 2 goes beyond the RFC's proposed wording:
the RFC assumed a T change always traces to some RFC's evidence, and
the run that filed this bead produced one that did not. Flag this as an
adopted-with-refinement in the Resolution.

Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Step 4 describes triage-originated rows and the T1..Tn numbering
- [ ] Step 4 states they need the same approval and the same evidence bar
- [ ] The Resolution bullet says where a T change is recorded, including when no RFC prompted it
- [ ] Every line added is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead
notes: Tier: standard. tier_reason: two edits in different steps that must agree with each other, plus one clause that deliberately extends the RFC's proposed wording and must be reported as a refinement rather than applied silently. No C4 component is affected.
close_reason: Step 4 describes T1..Tn triage-originated rows; Resolution bullet says where a T change is recorded, including the no-RFC-prompted case (a refinement beyond the RFC's wording, to be reported as such).

title: triage-rfc: make already-implemented vs reject-already-addressed distinguishable (triage T1)
description:
## Problem

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:120-126` defines the
`already-implemented` classification and distinguishes it from
`reject — already addressed` with a single clause: "which is for a
proposal whose premise no longer holds". A human reader of the skill
reported that this does not convey the distinction, because in BOTH
cases the change is already present in the tree, so "the premise no
longer holds" appears to describe both.

Current text at SKILL.md:120-126:

    - **already-implemented** — the proposal is sound and its change is
      already present in the tree, landed by earlier work rather than by
      this triage. Distinct from `reject — already addressed`, which is
      for a proposal whose premise no longer holds: this one was right
      and nothing about it is being turned down. Record it in the
      Resolution as "adopted — already implemented", name where the
      change lives, and bump nothing.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Reported directly by the repository owner on 2026-08-01, quoting
SKILL.md:122 and stating: "This does not make it clear (to me) what the
distinction between `reject - already addressed` and `adopted - already
implemented`."

This is a triage-originated work order (id T1), not a proposal from a
received RFC. It has no reporting RFC; the reporter is the human gate.

The distinction that the text should convey, and currently does not:
both outcomes mean the change is already in the tree, but they differ
in whether triage is ruling on the proposal's MERITS at all.
`adopted — already implemented` affirms the proposal was correct;
`reject — already addressed` takes no position, because the thing the
proposal targeted no longer exists. The consequence is load-bearing at
step 2, which reads prior Resolutions during dedupe: "adopted" means
settled, do not relitigate; "rejected — already addressed" means only
that the evidence was stale, so the same idea with fresh evidence gets
a fresh hearing.
design:

     this triage. Record it in the Resolution as "adopted — already
     implemented", name where the change lives, and bump nothing.

     The test against `reject — already addressed` is whether triage is
     ruling on the proposal's merits at all. Use **already-implemented**
     WHEN you would have adopted it had the tree been untouched: the
     proposal was right, and this triage says so. Use **reject —
     already addressed** WHEN there is nothing to rule on — the text it
     quotes is gone or rewritten, so its premise fails and triage takes
     no position on whether the idea was ever good.

     Resolutions. "Adopted" tells a future triage the idea is settled
     and should not be relitigated; "rejected — already addressed"
     tells it only that the evidence was stale, so the same idea backed
     by fresh evidence gets a fresh hearing.

classifications. Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead.

title: No merge strategy for .beads/issues.jsonl — beads created on two branches will conflict
description:
`.beads/issues.jsonl` is the only carrier of issues between sessions and branches in this project (see the 'How beads persist in THIS project' section of CLAUDE.md). There is no `.gitattributes` in the repo, so git merges it as ordinary text.

Two branches that each create beads produce overlapping line-level edits in one file. Git will report a conflict, and the natural resolutions are both wrong: taking one side drops the other branch's issues, and a careless union can duplicate ids or interleave a partial record.

The failure is silent in the worst case — a conflict resolved by 'keep mine' loses issues that were correctly exported and committed, which is exactly the loss the export discipline exists to prevent.

## Options to evaluate
- A `.gitattributes` union merge driver for the file. Cheap, but union can produce two lines with the same id when both branches touched one issue, so it needs an id-dedupe pass afterwards.
- A custom merge driver that parses JSONL, keys by id, and prefers the higher `updated_at`. Correct, but needs a script every clone can run.
- Regenerate from the database after merge rather than merging the file: resolve by taking either side, then `bd import` both versions and `bd export` fresh. Uses beads' own conflict handling.
- Whether beads upstream ships a documented driver for this — check before building one.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, tested procedure for merging two branches that both added beads, with no issue lost and no duplicate id in the resulting .beads/issues.jsonl
close_reason: Premise dead, verified 2026-08-12. All three rest on .beads/*.jsonl being tracked in git and being the carrier of issues between sessions. It is not: 'git ls-files .beads/' lists only .gitignore, README.md, config.yaml, metadata.json and the hooks — no JSONL — and .beads/.gitignore:87-89 ignores issues.jsonl, issues-full.jsonl and interactions.jsonl. The Dolt remote (refs/dolt/data) is the source of truth and the SessionStart hook does no JSONL import. Two branches cannot conflict on a file git does not track; a deleted issue cannot return via an import that does not happen; and a stale issues-full.jsonl is not tracked so cannot be 'stale in git'.

title: Index: model references as a separate edge collection, not only object properties
description:
Architectural input for the index-schema ADR (not yet written). Raised in PR #4 review of the FRD, 2026-07-31, explicitly flagged as 'not a comment for the FRD, but an architectural one for later'.

## The proposal

The index should collect the domain's model objects — specs
('documents'), systems, containers, components, and eventually features
— AND separately build a collection of REFERENCES that behave like
edges in a graph rather than like members of the objects they connect.
Each reference carries the file and span where it occurs.

Rationale given: this makes references queryable independently of the
objects. 'What points at adr-007?' becomes an edge query rather than a
scan over every object's properties.

This does not mean relationships never live inside objects. Some
belong there — a 'component' object might carry an injected
'container' property naming its parent. The proposal is specifically
about references that occur INSIDE document bodies: those are better
modelled as edges.

## Why it is not in the FRD

The FRD (docs/frds/FRD-spec-validation-cli.md) states WHAT the index
must contain, and AC-SPEC-002.1 and AC-SPEC-002.5 already require
outbound and inbound references. HOW the index is shaped — one
collection of objects with embedded arrays, versus objects plus a
separate edge collection — is a schema design decision, and the FRD
deliberately defers index schema and versioning to an ADR.

## Why it matters more than it looks

AC-SPEC-002.2 makes the index schema a published API with a version
identifier, and AC-SPEC-002.3 requires a workspace identifier so
indexes from separate repositories merge into one graph. An edge
collection is materially easier to merge across repositories than
embedded arrays, because edges from repo A pointing at objects in repo
B are just rows — whereas embedded arrays require rewriting the source
object. Getting this wrong is expensive to change after publication.

## Related decisions already made

- Reference relationships are DERIVED from body wikilinks, not
  hand-maintained frontmatter (settled in review; see
  docs/plans/spec-validation-cli-brief.md section 3).
- A 'span' carries a byte offset and length plus line/column, so an
  edge can record exactly where in the source the reference occurs
  (FRD Terminology, revised 2026-07-31).
design:
Input to the index-schema ADR; not standalone work. The ADR must decide:

1. Objects-with-embedded-arrays vs objects-plus-edge-collection vs both.
2. IF both, which relationships live where, and how duplication between
   the two representations is prevented from drifting.
3. Whether edges are typed (references / parent / supersedes / composes)
   or uniform with a 'kind' discriminator.
4. How edges behave across a workspace boundary when the target object
   is not in this repository's index.

Do not implement ahead of that ADR — the index schema is a published
API under AC-SPEC-002.2 and changing it later is the expensive case.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The index-schema ADR records a decision on object-vs-edge representation, with this proposal weighed in Alternatives Considered.
- [ ] The decision addresses cross-repository merge, since that is the case that most distinguishes the options.
- [ ] IF edges are adopted, the FRD's AC-SPEC-002.1 and AC-SPEC-002.5 are re-examined for consistency with the chosen shape.
notes: Subsumed by the reference-integrity feature: ADR-018 takes exactly this decision (references as one top-level edge collection on SpecIndex, both directions derived) and work order agent-plugins-9kb.1 (delta MODEL) implements it. Close or re-scope when agent-plugins-9kb.1 lands; the feature's final DoD item agent-plugins-9kb.10 closes it against the ADR.
close_reason: Superseded by agent-plugins-9kb.1 (MODEL) and ADR-018. index.strata declares a top-level references list of Reference rows on SpecIndex — each carrying path, text, slug, anchor, origin, position and resolution — and both directions are derived from that one collection (corpus.Corpus.InboundReferences / OutboundReferences). This is exactly the separate edge collection dgn asked for; no reference is modelled as an object property on an entry.

title: Carry record-block content in the index once Strata has a JSON value type
description: Record blocks are YAML mappings the index locates but does not carry (commit 3e596be): Strata 0.8.0 has no open value type — declaring a property as Any, Json, JSON, Object, Value or Unknown fails with 'Unknown type', and unions are always tagged and struct-only — so an arbitrary mapping has no typed home in the generated model. Go itself has map[string]any and json.RawMessage; the blocker is generation, not the language. Proposal: add an open JSON value type to strata-lang/strata that emits {} in JSON Schema and json.RawMessage (or map[string]any) in Go, then add RecordBlock.content back to schemas/index.strata. Adding a property is additive under the index's schema_version 1.0.
acceptance_criteria: Strata ships a JSON value type; RecordBlock carries the decoded record as nested JSON; specs index on a corpus with a component block emits its title, slug and description as a JSON object.

title: Schema changes silently turn the warm-cache snapshot fixture cold
description: cli/testdata/cases/check-every-document-type/input/docs/specs.json is a persisted index whose input_hash must equal the current Fingerprint for the case to exercise the warm-cache path (corpus.openWarm). Fingerprint covers the embedded schema, so ANY change to schemas/*.strata makes the fixture stale: the case still passes (cold and warm outputs are identical by design), but the warm path goes unexercised. Measured while adding schemas/c4.strata: snapshot coverage fell 2,697 -> 2,645 of 3,405 statements with every test green; restoring the fixture hash to the new fingerprint restored 2,697. Only scripts/coverage.sh --check noticed, and its message says to regenerate the README, which would have locked in the lower figure. Fix: make the case assert it was served warm (or regenerate the fixture hash in scripts/generate-schemas.sh).

title: links/unresolved on an anchor-only citation reports the slug as [[]]
description:
An anchor-only citation whose anchor names no heading of the document
holding it settles no target and is reported as links/unresolved, which is
correct. The message names the empty slug rather than the reference, so it
reads as a citation of nothing at all.

Measured on a throwaway corpus (docs/adrs/adr-100-nowhere.md declaring
slug: adr-100, body 'See [[#Nowhere]] below.', no Nowhere heading), with a
binary built from cli/ both before and after agent-plugins-etyf:

  spec links docs/adrs/adr-100-nowhere.md
    links/unresolved  warning  12:7  [[]] matches no corpus document

The reference's text is '#Nowhere' and Reference.Text carries it;
finding.UnresolvedCitation is passed ref.Slug (cli/core/mdlinks/mdlinks.go,
resolveOne). A reader opening 12:7 finds [[#Nowhere]] and a message about
[[]].

Same shape as the check half: reference/unresolved on the same reference
reads '[[#Nowhere]] matches no document's slug', because
finding.UnresolvedReference is given ref.Text as well as ref.Slug. The
citation finding has no text argument.

Related but distinct from agent-plugins-oksv, which is about how MANY
findings that reference produces; this is about what one of them says.
Fixing it means widening finding.UnresolvedCitation, so it touches the
finding vocabulary and every snapshot asserting that message.

title: A refs answer carries resolution: unresolved on a self-anchor it now lists
description:
AC-SPECREF-001.8 puts an anchor-only reference into the inbound
references of the document holding it, so spec refs now answers with it.
The reference's own resolution is still unresolved — the slug half is
empty and reaches nothing — so the answer carries a row reading
resolution: {state: unresolved} beside rows reading resolved.

Measured on a throwaway corpus (docs/adrs/adr-098-good.md declaring
slug: adr-098, body 'See [[#Overview]] below.', its own ## Overview),
with a binary built from cli/ after agent-plugins-etyf landed:

  spec refs adr-098
    references:
      - path: docs/adrs/adr-098-good.md
        text: "#Overview"
        slug: ""
        resolution:
          state: unresolved
        anchor_resolution:
          state: resolved

A reader scanning the YAML sees a reference the tool calls unresolved in
the answer to 'what references this'. A consumer filtering --json on
resolution.state == "resolved" drops it again, which is the same wrong
answer AC-SPECREF-001.8 was added to remove, one layer out.

Three options, and the choice is the owner's:
  (a) leave it — the index records the same thing, and
      AC-SPECREF-002.12 already accepted that shape;
  (b) mark the row in the refs output, as AmbiguousAnchor is marked
      (refsMatch in cli/cmd/refs.go), so self-ness is legible without a
      reader comparing paths;
  (c) record such a reference's resolution as resolved against its own
      document, which would retire the exemption in
      unresolvedReferenceFinding and the branch in indexReferences —
      the largest change, and it contradicts the specmodel comment on
      Reference.AnchorResolution that distinguishes 'resolution reached
      a corpus member' from 'the reference names no slug at all'.

etyf implemented (a) deliberately: the dispatch said not to invent a new
top-level shape where an existing field already carries it, and
Reference.Path does carry the origin. Filing so the owner can revisit.

title: Ledger: the permission classifier blocks swarm dispatch accept's push step
description:
AGENTS.md's environmental-failure ledger has no entry for this, and the next
agent orchestrating a run in a session with the same permission classifier will
hit it with no warning.

## The fact

`swarm dispatch accept` without --no-push is blocked by this session's
permission classifier at its git push step. Recorded by the run's coordinator
as an `amend:` comment on run epic agent-plugins-59ic:

  "'swarm dispatch accept' without --no-push is blocked by this session's
  permission classifier (its git push step). Running with --no-push and pushing
  separately at post-flight."

Every accept on run agent-plugins-59ic therefore ran with --no-push, and the
sprint branch was pushed with plain git at post-flight. Confirmed on the
finished tree: `git log origin/sprint/agent-plugins-59ic..HEAD` was empty at
a852925, so nothing was stranded by the workaround.

## UNVERIFIED, and the entry must say so

What the classifier matches, and whether any invocation form other than
--no-push gets through, was NOT determined. No reachability or permission test
was run. The ledger's own rule applies: an entry that reads as settled and is
not is worse than absent.

Settle it by attempting one `swarm dispatch accept` WITHOUT --no-push in a
session carrying the same classifier, and recording the refusal verbatim —
the message, the exit status, and which step it fired on. Note also that a
reachability test run inside a session that already holds a grant measures the
grant, not the capability.

## Done is

AGENTS.md's "Environmental-failure ledger" carries an entry stating the fact,
the workaround (--no-push, then push with plain git), the evidence above, and
the unverified part with what would settle it. No figure that ages is recorded;
the command that would measure it is.

## Anchors

The "### Environmental-failure ledger" section of AGENTS.md; the amend: comment
quoted above on run epic agent-plugins-59ic; the "Pushes" and "What the run
could NOT verify" sections of
docs/retros/2026-09-05-59ic-spec-corpus-anchor-references.md.

Filed by the retro of run agent-plugins-59ic.

title: markdown.Identifier returns an empty, unaddressable identifier for a heading whose text renders to nothing
description:
## Problem

`markdown.Identifier` returns the empty string for a heading whose text
renders to nothing. The commonest cause is text goldmark reads as raw
inline HTML: a heading named `<Feature Name>` renders to no content at
all, so every character is gone before the character filter runs.

An empty identifier is not addressable — `spec headings '#'` cannot name
it, and a `[[slug#<Feature Name>]]` reference has no fragment to match.
The container document presents the identifier as how a heading is
addressed, with no stated exception for one that has none.

## Measured

At HEAD (`62e9e42`), over all 291 `.md` files in the repository:

    total headings:            2,434
    empty identifiers:            24
    leading-hyphen identifiers:    0

The same scan against `ec6b6fd` gives identical figures (2,434 / 24 / 0),
so this is pre-existing and d7w5.8 neither caused nor worsened it.

All 24 are `<Placeholder>` headings in template files, e.g.

    plugin/skills/spec/references/standards-template.md   "<Document Title>"
    plugin/skills/spec/references/frd-template.md          "<Feature Name>"
    plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/shared/work-order-template.md
                                        "<imperative summary of the unit of work>"

None is in `specs/**`, so no corpus member is affected today.

## Why it is worth recording

The exposure is not the templates — those placeholders are replaced before
a document becomes a corpus member. It is that ANY heading whose text is
entirely inline markup silently becomes unaddressable, with no finding, no
warning and no failing check. A heading like `## <T> parameters` in a real
document would hit it.

## Suggested shape

Decide what an identifier should be when the rendered text is empty —
falling back to the raw text, or emitting a finding at index time — and say
so where the derivation is documented in
`specs/modules/document-core/document-core-module.md`. Deciding it is
acceptable and documenting the exception is a legitimate outcome.

## Scope

Not introduced by run agent-plugins-d7w5. Filed for the record.

title: mdlinks.slugifyAnchor is a second, independent derivation of the heading-anchor rule markdown.Identifier owns
description:
## Problem

The heading-anchor rule is derived twice, in two packages, by two
different methods:

- `markdown.Identifier` (`cli/core/markdown/headings.go`) RENDERS the text
  as inline markdown, then filters characters.
- `slugifyAnchor` (`cli/core/mdlinks/mdlinks.go`) filters characters only,
  with no rendering:

      case r == '-' || r == '_' || unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.IsDigit(r):

`specs/modules/document-core/document-core-module.md` claims one:

  "which is what lets anchor resolution match against this one derivation
  rather than a second one"

There is a second one. A rewritten link `[[slug#Heading]]` can therefore
point at a fragment that `spec headings` never reports.

## Measured — and the good news

Both derivations run over every body heading in `specs/**` (frontmatter
excluded via the body offset, since `markdown.Headings` on a whole file
reads the envelope as a setext heading by design):

    before this run's d7w5.8 fix:  612 headings, 9 disagreements
    at HEAD (62e9e42):             612 headings, 0 disagreements

So d7w5.8 CONVERGED them — it did not cause this. The nine that diverged
were the ordinal family, e.g. in `work-order-definition-of-ready.md`:

    "3. `## Design` present (non-trivial, non-epic orders)"
      old Identifier =  -design-present-non-trivial-non-epic-orders
      slugifyAnchor  = 3--design-present-non-trivial-non-epic-orders
      new Identifier = 3--design-present-non-trivial-non-epic-orders

Note the old `Identifier` also produced a LEADING HYPHEN there; the fix
removed it.

## Why it is still worth closing

They agree today by coincidence of what the corpus contains, not by
construction. They still diverge wherever rendered text differs from raw
text — a link, raw inline HTML, an entity. `Identifier("See [the guide]
(http://example.com/guide)")` is `see-the-guide`; `slugifyAnchor` of the
same is `see-the-guidehttpexamplecomguide`. Nothing fails a test the day
a heading like that is written.

## Suggested shape

Have `mdlinks` call `markdown.Identifier` and delete `slugifyAnchor`, or —
if the two are deliberately different rules — say so in the module document
and drop the "one derivation" claim. A test asserting the two agree over
the corpus is the cheap guard if neither is possible now.

## Scope

Not introduced by run agent-plugins-d7w5; `slugifyAnchor` is untouched by
its diff. Filed for the record.

title: renderYAML ignores encoding/json's `,string` tag option, so the two renderings differ in value TYPE
description:
## Problem

agent-plugins-d7w5.11 made renderYAML resolve a struct's fields exactly as
`encoding/json` resolves them, so the two renderings now carry the same KEYS
in the same order. One divergence in VALUES remains: `encoding/json`'s
`,string` tag option renders a number, boolean or string as a quoted JSON
string, and renderYAML ignores the option entirely.

## Measured

Probe in package cmd on branch bb/dev-d7w5-3, after d7w5.11's fix:

    v := struct {
        N int `json:"n,string"`
    }{5}

    JSON: {"n":"5"}
    YAML: "n: 5\n"

The key agrees; the value's TYPE does not — a YAML reader gets the number 5
where a JSON reader gets the string "5".

## Why it is latent

No type on this command surface uses `,string`. `headingMatch` in
cli/cmd/headings.go, the only type renderYAML is called on, carries no such
tag. As with the promotion bug d7w5.11 fixed, the risk is the next command
migrated to [[cli-output-standards]].

## Suggested shape

`typeFields` in cli/cmd/yaml.go already parses the tag options into a map
(`parseJSONTag`); carrying `opts["string"]` onto `fieldSpec` and honouring it
in the scalar writers is the small version. Note `encoding/json` applies
`,string` only to a string, a floating-point, an integer or a boolean field
(and to a pointer to one), and silently ignores it elsewhere — the fidelity
this bead is about means reproducing that restriction too, not just quoting
whatever carries the option.

Decide also whether specs/standards/cli-output-standards.md should simply
FORBID `,string` on this surface, which would be cheaper than reproducing it
and is a legitimate outcome of this bead.

title: AC-SPECSTR-003.5 says --emit returns each match's section; the implementation returns their union, and only the container doc records that
description:
REVIEW FINDING (run agent-plugins-d7w5, pass 1). CLASSIFIED OUT OF SCOPE — see the verdict at the end.

THE TWO TEXTS. specs/features/structure/structure-frd.md:

    @AC-SPECSTR-003.5
    Scenario: The content beneath a match is returned on request
      When the CLI is asked to emit the content the headings a selection matches stand over
      Then the CLI returns the text of each match's section, read from its recorded span

    @AC-SPECSTR-003.4
    Scenario: A matched heading carries the headings nested beneath it
      ...
      Then the CLI returns every heading within that heading's section, each with its own level

Read literally and together: a match set of N headings, where some are nested inside others, yields N sections on `--emit`, and a child's text is written twice — once inside its parent's span and once as itself.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTATION DOES. cli/cmd/headings.go, `emitSections`, skips a section contained in one already written:

    for _, match := range matches {
        if match.Path == writtenPath && match.Section.Offset < writtenEnd {
            continue
        }

so `--emit` returns the UNION of the matched sections — every matched byte exactly once, outermost span only. The doc comment gives the reasoning ("this query exists to spend a reader's attention once on the text it selected. What is skipped is only ever a copy").

WHERE IT IS RECORDED. specs/containers/spec-cli/spec-cli-container.md, edited by this run, states it: "a section already contained in one just written is skipped, because the matches carry nested headings and a parent's span already covers its children's text." The FRD was NOT updated, so the acceptance criterion a future reader checks the behaviour against still reads as though N matches produce N sections.

ASSESSMENT: the behaviour is right and the reasoning is sound — writing a child's text twice would be a defect, not a feature. What is missing is that the criterion the behaviour is tested against does not say what the behaviour is. A container document is the wrong home for a refinement of an acceptance criterion; the FRD is.

VERDICT — OUT OF SCOPE. The behaviour is correct and no code changes. The only remedy is prose in a document that has not yet misled anybody, which the review criteria explicitly decline to admit into a run. File and let the next feature touching FEAT-SPECSTR-003 fold it in.

REMEDY WHEN TAKEN: amend AC-SPECSTR-003.5 to say the emitted text is the union of the matched sections, each byte once — or add a scenario covering the nested-match case — so the criterion and the implementation agree without a reader having to consult the container doc.
notes: Review pass 1 finding, filed but NOT admitted into run agent-plugins-d7w5: standing_auth.admit_review_findings=false, authorized by the human at gate agent-plugins-987r. Deferred to leave the run's ready set, not to hide the work — bd defer means postponed, and these stay visible in bd list for a later run to pick up.

title: Swarm work moved to brettcallaghan/swarm
description:
Children of the four swarm epics that migrated to brettcallaghan/swarm on 2026-09-03, kept here so bd did not rewrite their parent reference to [deleted:...].

HOW TO DECODE A [deleted:agent-plugins-...] REFERENCE.

The four migrated epics were y63n, offx, hg9t and ia3y. Deferred findings from

title: swarm ready --threshold accepts a non-positive value, which stops every run unconditionally
description:
`swarm ready`'s `--threshold` is registered with no validation, so a non-positive
value makes the circuit breaker stop every run — including one whose dispatch
just completed work, and whose count therefore RESET to zero.

In `func readyCmd` in `cli/swarm/cli/ready.go` (~line 130), the flag is bound
with no bound on its value:

    cmd.Flags().IntVar(&threshold, "threshold", breakerDefaultThreshold,
        "the circuit breaker's threshold: the number of consecutive dispatch returns
         that completed no bead which stops the run")

`func applyBreaker` in the same file then tests `next >= threshold` (and, on the
dry-run refusal path, `verdict >= threshold`) against a count that is never
negative, so any threshold <= 0 makes the comparison unconditionally true.

## Steps to Reproduce

Unit-level, through `breakerPass` in `cli/swarm/cli/ready_test.go`, which wraps
`applyBreaker` directly.

1. Record a `consecutive_dispatch_failures` of 3 in the manifest the fake serves.
2. Call `breakerPass` with `breakerReport{Given: true, Completed: 5}` — a
   dispatch that completed five beads, which resets the count to 0.
3. Pass `--threshold 0`, then `-1`, in `plan.ModeDryRun` and `plan.ModeExecute`.

Expected: a dispatch that completed five beads does not stop the run, in either
mode, at any threshold.

Actual: all four combinations report `stopped=true`. Re-measured on the current
tree (bec6637, so after agent-plugins-74xc landed):

    threshold=0  mode=dry-run  stopped=true
      summary="the run is stopped: 0 consecutive dispatch(es) returned with no bead completed (threshold 0)"
      reason="the write was refused: dry run: the step writes. The count stands at 3 and would have become 0 (threshold 0)"
    threshold=0  mode=execute  stopped=true
      summary="the run is stopped: 0 consecutive dispatch(es) returned with no bead completed (threshold 0)"
    threshold=-1 mode=dry-run  stopped=true   (same shape, threshold -1)
    threshold=-1 mode=execute  stopped=true   (same shape, threshold -1)

Two things are wrong and they are separable:

1. **The verdict itself.** `func stoppedSummary` writes "0 consecutive
   dispatch(es) returned with no bead completed" of a dispatch that completed
   five beads. The sentence is not merely unhelpful there, it is false.
2. **The dry-run result states a count RESET beside a stop summary** — "would
   have become 0 (threshold 0)" alongside "the run is stopped". That is the same
   self-contradiction agent-plugins-74xc removed for positive thresholds, and it
   survives here for non-positive ones.

The two modes AGREE throughout, so this is not the dry-run/execute divergence
74xc fixed. It is reachable only through an operator passing `--threshold 0` or a
negative value.

## The second numeric flag

`swarm ready` also binds `--completed` with `IntVar` and no validation (~line 132).
These two are the ONLY integer flags in the whole command surface — measured:
`grep -rn 'IntVar\|IntSliceVar\|Int64Var' cli/swarm/cli/` returns exactly those
two lines. A negative `--completed` is read by `report.Completed > 0` as false, so
it is silently treated as `--completed 0` and ADVANCES the failure count: an
operator reporting a malformed value gets a breaker advance rather than a
refusal.

## Discovered from

agent-plugins-74xc, while establishing that its AC "no result states a count
reset alongside a stop summary" holds. It holds for every threshold >= 1; this is
the residue. Adjacent, not blocking — 74xc's own criteria are met without it.
design:
Refuse both malformed values at the command surface, before any plan runs, using
the refusal machinery `readyCmd` already uses for its other argument checks.

`func RefuseArguments` in `cli/swarm/cli/exit.go` returns
`&Refusal{Outcome: OutcomeMalformed, ...}`, and `OutcomeMalformed` maps to
`StatusMalformed` (3) — the outcome whose documented meaning is "its own
invocation was malformed". That is the right one; do not invent a new outcome.

PLACEMENT, and it is settled here: put both guards in `readyCmd`'s `RunE`
immediately after the existing `--explain` / `--dry-run` mutual-exclusion check
and before the mode is resolved, matching the two refusals already there:

    return finish(streams, req, refusal(req, RefuseArguments(...)))

Two consequences that are the reason for this placement, not side effects:
- The refusal happens before `explainReady`, so a malformed invocation is
  malformed in EVERY mode, explain included. A malformed argument is not made
  well-formed by asking the command to only describe itself.
- It happens before `applyBreaker` is reached on either the `--agent` or the
  whole-run path, so nothing is read and nothing is written — the same guarantee
  the surface already states for its empty-`--run` refusal.

THE TWO GUARDS:
- `--threshold` < 1 is refused. Zero has no coherent reading: the breaker's own
  flag text is "the number of consecutive dispatch returns that completed no bead
  which stops the run", and zero such returns is the state every run starts in.
- `--completed` < 0 is refused. Its own flag text is "report that a dispatch just
  returned having completed this many beads", and a negative count of beads is
  not a report. Guard it only when the flag was actually given
  (`cmd.Flags().Changed("completed")`, which `readyCmd` already reads to build
  `breakerReport{Given: ...}`), so an omitted flag keeps its current meaning.

Each refusal names the flag and what a valid value is.

SCOPE, decided rather than left open — the earlier draft of this order asked
whether the same guard belongs on other numeric flags and left it to the
implementer. It does not need asking: `swarm ready`'s `--threshold` and
`--completed` are the only integer flags in `cli/swarm/cli` (measured above), and
both are covered here. There is no third.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- No spec or blueprint change. `specs/features/swarm-dispatch/swarm-dispatch-blueprint.md`
  states "The threshold SHALL arrive as an argument to the command, and WHERE it
  is absent the command SHALL use 3" and states no lower bound; adding one to the
  blueprint pulls in a new tagged Gherkin criterion in
  `specs/features/swarm-dispatch/swarm-dispatch-frd.md` (the AC-SWARM-DISP-002.N
  series), which is a separate order. The three sibling defect fixes on this
  branch (agent-plugins-4ca8, -74xc, -n3tn) were all code-only for the same
  reason.
- No C4 doc change. `specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md` already documents
  this convention generically for the Swarm Command Surface — "The scope is
  checked before the mode is resolved, so a command refusing an empty run scope
  has read and written nothing". A second argument refusal is an instance of what
  is already written, not a change to it.
- Do not change `applyBreaker`'s comparison, `func stoppedSummary`, or the
  dry-run refusal text. With a non-positive threshold refused at the surface, the
  false summary and the reset-beside-stop contradiction are both unreachable, and
  agent-plugins-74xc's behavior for positive thresholds must not move.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `swarm ready --threshold 0` and `swarm ready --threshold` with a negative value are refused with the malformed outcome and its exit status, before the breaker reads or writes anything.
- [ ] `swarm ready --completed` with a negative value is refused the same way; omitting `--completed` keeps its current meaning.
- [ ] Each refusal names the flag and what a valid value is.
- [ ] The refusals apply in explain, dry-run and execute modes alike.
- [ ] A positive `--threshold` is unaffected: the existing breaker tests in `cli/swarm/cli/ready_test.go` pass unchanged, and `applyBreaker`, `stoppedSummary` and the dry-run refusal text are not modified.
- [ ] A unit test covers `--threshold 0`, a negative `--threshold`, and a negative `--completed`.
- [ ] The project's declared checks pass: format, vet, build, test-go (judge on ubuntu and macOS; go test (windows-latest) is red on this branch for a diff-independent reason tracked separately).

metadata.tier_reason: two guard clauses in one function, using the refusal helper the same function already calls twice; placement and scope are both settled in the design, and the only decision left is where to put three lines

comments.author: dev-bguq-3
comments.text:
retro:proof The defect was reproduced and watched fail before the fix, in all three modes.

evidence: cli/swarm/cli/threshold_test.go written first, run against the unmodified tree:

    $ go test ./swarm/cli/ -run 'TestReadyRefusesANonPositiveThreshold|TestReadyRefusesANegativeCompleted|TestReadyAcceptsTheValidEdge'
    --- FAIL: TestReadyRefusesANonPositiveThreshold (0.00s)
        threshold_test.go:50: [ready --run run-1 --threshold 0] exited 2, want 3 (malformed)
        threshold_test.go:53: [ready --run run-1 --threshold 0] read or wrote something before refusing: [[bd ready --parent run-1 --exclude-type epic --exclude-label human --limit 0 --json]]
        threshold_test.go:57: [ready --run run-1 --threshold 0] does not name the flag it refused
        threshold_test.go:60: [ready --run run-1 --threshold 0] does not say what a valid value is
    EXIT=1

The second line is the sharper one: exit 2 was reached by RUNNING the ready query. So the pre-fix command did not merely mis-handle the value, it read the tracker before doing so — which is what the AC "before the breaker reads or writes anything" is about. The test asserts from the fake's own call record rather than from the exit status, so a refusal that had already read something would not pass a status-only check.

After the fix the same run exits 0, and `go test ./swarm/cli/` exits 0 whole — the existing breaker tests in ready_test.go pass unchanged, which is the AC that a positive --threshold is unaffected.

comments.author: dev-bguq-3
comments.text:
retro:decision Placement: both guards sit AFTER the mode-resolving switch, not inside it.

The Design says "immediately after the existing --explain / --dry-run mutual-exclusion check and before the mode is resolved". Those two are not separable in the code: cli/swarm/cli/ready.go resolves the mode in the same switch statement that carries the mutual-exclusion refusal —

    switch {
    case explain && dryRun:
        return finish(streams, req, refusal(req, RefuseArguments(
            "--explain and --dry-run select different interpreters; pass one")))
    case explain:
        req.Mode = plan.ModeExplain
    case dryRun:
        req.Mode = plan.ModeDryRun
    default:
        req.Mode = plan.ModeExecute
    }

so there is no point that is after the one and before the other. Placed immediately after the switch instead, which preserves both consequences the Design named as its reasons: the guards are still ahead of `if req.Mode == plan.ModeExplain { return finish(streams, req, explainReady(...)) }`, so a malformed invocation is malformed in explain mode too, and still ahead of applyBreaker on both the --agent and whole-run paths, so nothing is read or written. Both are asserted by the test across all three modes.

Rejected: placing them before the switch. It would make a threshold refusal preempt the --explain/--dry-run one when both are malformed, changing which of two correct refusals a caller sees, for no gain.

evidence: with the guards where they are, `go test ./swarm/cli/` exits 0, and TestReadyRefusesANonPositiveThreshold covers nil, --dry-run and --explain for each of 0, -1 and -3.

comments.author: dev-bguq-3
comments.text:
retro:proof No consumer in the tree passes a value either guard now refuses, so the refusals cannot break a caller.

evidence: `grep -rn -- "--threshold" .` over the working tree returns five non-test sites, and none of them supplies a literal value:

- specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md:299 — "`--threshold` defaults to 3 and is a flag"
- plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/dispatching.md:192 — the form `swarm ready --run <epic> --completed <n> [--threshold <n>]`, with the prose "the threshold is a run-level authorization row (`sf.toml`'s `[run] dispatch_failure_threshold`, else 3)"
- sf.toml:163-165 — the row itself, commented out at its default: `# dispatch_failure_threshold = 3`, described as "how many consecutive dispatch returns that completed no bead stop the RUN"
- cli/swarm/cli/ready.go:307 — `const breakerDefaultThreshold = 3`
- docs/retros/2026-09-02-e6xt-swarm-dispatch.md — a prior run's record, not a caller

So the only configured path resolves to 3 or to an operator-supplied row, and a row of 0 has no coherent reading under the documented semantics: it would stop every run before its first dispatch returned. `--completed 0` is untouched — the guard is `completed < 0`, and TestReadyAcceptsTheValidEdgeOfEachFlag pins `--completed 0`, `--threshold 1` and an omitted `--completed` as accepted.

comments.author: dev-bguq-3
comments.text:
retro:proof The gates pass with no finding beyond the run's baseline.

evidence: `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-checks.py` with no arguments, run in the dispatch worktree, exited 0 with all thirteen declared checks present — format, vet, build, test-go, skills, shared-refs, strata-docs, schemas, corpus, ref-links, template-drift, script-self-tests, skills-strict — and `grep -c FAIL` over the captured output returned 0. The run's checks_baseline records exit 0 with every check passing, so the bar was "no findings beyond that" and there are none.

The change is 29 inserted lines in one function, `git diff --stat` → `cli/swarm/cli/ready.go | 29 +++`, plus the new cli/swarm/cli/threshold_test.go. applyBreaker, stoppedSummary and the dry-run refusal text are untouched, which the AC requires and the diff shows.

title: branch.go's dry-run resolution tells a push caller to re-run a write
description:
In `landingVerdict` in `cli/swarm/cli/branch.go` (near line 406 today; anchor on
the symbols, the line moves), the verb-aware resolution on the "comparison did
not run" branch reuses the dry-run wording:

    Unestablished("landed",
        "the comparison against "+tracking+" did not run",
        invocationOf(divergeSteps[len(divergeSteps)-1], divergeRec)),
    ...
    resolution: fmt.Sprintf("run it again without --dry-run: swarm branch %s --branch %s --remote %s",
        verb, branch, remote),

That branch is only reachable once the fetch has ALREADY run — a dry run returns
earlier, from the `fetchRec` guard in the same function that reports "<remote>
was not fetched, so the comparison against <tracking> would rest on a possibly
stale local record". So a dry run never arrives here, and the advice cannot
apply.

Because `verb` is interpolated, for `push` the resolution now tells the caller to
re-run a WRITE as the fix for a READ that did not execute.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `swarm branch push` (not a dry run), so the fetch guard is passed.
2. Make the divergence comparison not run, taking the "comparison did not run"
   branch.
3. Read the resolution on the returned verdict.

Expected: a resolution naming the read that did not complete and how to obtain
it, with no instruction to re-run a write.
Actual: "run it again without --dry-run: swarm branch push --branch <b>
--remote <r>" — a write proposed as the remedy for an unexecuted read, on a
path no dry run can reach.

Found by the code-review pass on 2622f6c..37a9d83 that run e6xt never ran
(review_budget exhausted; retro candidate C13, accepted on PR #33).
design: Give the 'comparison did not run' branch its own resolution describing the read that did not complete — name the divergence comparison against the tracking ref and how to obtain it — instead of reusing the dry-run wording. Leave the dry-run resolution on the fetchRec branch, which a dry run does reach. Do not make the wording verb-conditional to paper over it: the defect is that the branch is unreachable by a dry run at all, so the dry-run advice does not belong on it for any verb.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The "comparison did not run" resolution does not tell the caller to re-run without --dry-run.
- [ ] That resolution names the read that failed — the divergence comparison against the tracking ref.
- [ ] For verb push, the resolution proposes no write as the remedy.
- [ ] The dry-run wording remains on the fetch branch, which a dry run does reach.
- [ ] A unit test in cli/swarm/cli pins the resolution on both branches.
- [ ] The project's declared checks pass: format, vet, build, test-go (judge on ubuntu and macOS; go test (windows-latest) is red on this branch for a diff-independent reason tracked separately).

metadata.tier_reason: one resolution string on one named branch plus a test pinning both branches; the analysis is already settled in the order and no design choice remains

comments.author: dev-bguq-1
comments.text:
retro:gap the "comparison did not run" branch is unreachable from OUTSIDE the function in either mode, not just in a dry run — so the test had to call landingVerdict directly, which the bead did not anticipate
evidence: the bead establishes that a DRY RUN cannot reach the branch. Tracing the execute path as
well, nothing else can either:

  - The divergence step is a plain read with literal arguments
    (cli/swarm/vcs/git/git.go, `func (v VersionControl) Divergence` -> `v.step(prefix, plan.Read,
    ...)` with "rev-list", "--count", "--left-right" and one built string), so it cannot be
    refused by dry run and cannot be skipped by an argument that will not resolve — the only two
    non-skipRest routes to a non-StepRan record (cli/swarm/plan/run.go).
  - That leaves skipRest, which needs an earlier step to stop the plan. The steps ahead of it in
    verifyLanded's plan are push, fetch and counterpart. Each has a branch in landingVerdict (or,
    for push, in verifyLanded) that RETURNS before the comparison is reached:
    the push through `rejected(result, remote, rec)`, the fetch through the guard above, and the
    counterpart through `if counterpartRec.Failed()`.

So the branch is a defence against a plan shape the current step set cannot produce. That is not
an argument for deleting it — the fragments are built by an interface, and a second
implementation of vcs.VersionControl could order things differently — but it does mean the branch
has no end-to-end test and cannot be given one through runBranch and the exec fake.

The test therefore calls landingVerdict directly with a hand-built plan.Report. That is possible
only because landingVerdict takes a report and three step fragments as plain values and returns a
verdict — no context, no runner, no I/O. Worth noting as a property to preserve: the same shape is
what let this branch be pinned at all, and a refactor that gave landingVerdict a runner would
remove the only way to test it.

Two helpers were added to cli/swarm/cli/branch_test.go for it — landingFragments (the three real
fragments) and ranRecord (a step that ran and answered) — and they are reusable for any other
landingVerdict branch that later needs the same treatment.

title: mergeCase.branchSHA is dead after merged_sha moved to the post-fold resolve
description:
## What

`cli/swarm/cli/accept.go`: `mergeCase.branchSHA` is now written and never
read. Measured at 2622f6c:

    $ grep -n "branchSHA" cli/swarm/cli/*.go
    swarm/cli/accept.go:368:	branchSHA  string
    swarm/cli/accept.go:426:	branchSHA, err := revision(report, branchStep, dispatchBranch)
    swarm/cli/accept.go:452:		branchSHA:  branchSHA,

Three lines: the declaration, the local, and the assignment. No read.
`0b8c2dd` moved `merged_sha` to the post-fold resolve and removed the only
consumer.

## Why it is worth removing rather than leaving

The `revision(report, branchStep, dispatchBranch)` call at 426 is still
worth keeping — it validates that the dispatch branch resolves at all and
refuses early if it does not. What should go is the FIELD: a populated
`mergeCase.branchSHA` sitting a few lines from the comment explaining
that the branch sha must never be used for `merged_sha` is exactly the
value the next reader reaches for. Keep the check, drop the carrier.

`m.branchInv` is still read (it cites the `dispatch_branch` fact), so
only `branchSHA` is dead.

## Acceptance

- `mergeCase` no longer carries `branchSHA`.
- The early validity check on the dispatch branch's resolution is
  retained.
- `go vet` and the full check set stay green.
design:
Remove the `branchSHA string` field from `mergeCase` in cli/swarm/cli/accept.go
and the `branchSHA:  branchSHA,` entry in `readCase`'s returned literal. Those
two lines plus the local assignment are the only occurrences — confirmed at
2622f6c by `grep -rn "branchSHA" cli/swarm/`, which returns exactly three lines
and no read.

KEEP the `revision(report, branchStep, dispatchBranch)` call. It is the early
validity check that refuses when the dispatch branch does not resolve, and its
refusal behaviour must not change. Since the value is no longer carried, either
discard it into `_` while still checking the error, or keep the local and drop
only the struct assignment — whichever leaves `go vet` and the project's linter
clean without an unused-variable error.

`m.branchInv` stays: it is still read, and it cites the `dispatch_branch` fact.

REJECTED: leaving the field and adding a comment. A populated `branchSHA` a few
lines from the comment explaining that the branch sha must never be used for
`merged_sha` is precisely the value the next reader reaches for; deleting the
carrier is the point.

REJECTED: removing the `revision` call along with the field. It refuses early on
an unresolvable dispatch branch; dropping it moves that failure later, into the
fold, where it is more expensive.

Acceptance evidence: re-run `grep -rn "branchSHA" cli/swarm/` after the change
and record that it returns nothing.

BATCH: SIXTH of batch b12, after e6xt.16 — which rewrites the post-fold
`merged_sha` handling in this same file. Run the deadness grep after e6xt.16 has
landed, not before, so the verdict is against the code that ships.

metadata.tier_reason: Delete one struct field and one assignment, keep a named check, re-run one grep as the evidence; rote and low-ambiguity with the retained call spelled out
