title: the unfetched-remote resolution tells a swarm branch push caller to run verify-landed instead
description:
## What

`cli/swarm/cli/branch.go`, `landingVerdict`'s new unfetched-remote
verdict names the wrong command when the caller ran `swarm branch push`:

    resolution: fmt.Sprintf(
        "run it again without --dry-run, or fetch first: swarm branch verify-landed --branch %s --remote %s",
        branch, remote),

`landingVerdict` takes no `pushFirst`, so both verbs get the same string.
`swarm branch push --branch X --dry-run` now exits 1 (attention) with a
resolution telling the caller to run `swarm branch verify-landed` — a
command that never pushes. A caller following the named command
rehearses a push and then performs only the check.

The two commands are deliberately "one implementation, not two commands
that resemble each other", so the resolution has to name the verb the
caller invoked.

## Test gap

`branch_test.go`'s `TestADryRunDoesNotReportLandedFromAnUnfetchedComparison`
loops over both verbs but asserts only

    if !strings.Contains(env.Resolution, "--dry-run")

which passes for both because the shared string happens to contain it.
The assertion cannot distinguish the two verbs, which is why the wrong
one shipped under a test that covers the case.

## Note

The pre-existing divergence-step verdict lower in the same function has
the same shape ("run it again without --dry-run: swarm branch
verify-landed ..."), so the pattern predates this run; the instance this
bead names is the one `a46658d` added, and it is the one a dry run of
`branch push` now actually reaches.

## Acceptance

- A dry run of `swarm branch push` names `swarm branch push` in its
  resolution.
- The both-verbs test asserts the resolution names the verb invoked,
  rather than a substring both share.
design:
Thread the verb into `landingVerdict` (cli/swarm/cli/branch.go). It takes
`(report, fetchSteps, counterpartSteps, divergeSteps, branch, remote)` and has
no way to know which command ran, so both verbs get the same resolution string.

Add a `pushFirst bool` parameter — the same flag `branchLandingCmd`,
`explainBranchLanding` and `verifyLanded` already carry — and derive the command
name once inside the function (`verb := "verify-landed"; if pushFirst { verb =
"push" }`).

Use it in TWO resolutions:

1. The unfetched-remote verdict, "run it again without --dry-run, or fetch
   first: swarm branch verify-landed --branch %s --remote %s". This is the
   instance the bead names and the one a dry run of `swarm branch push`
   actually reaches.
2. The divergence-step verdict lower in the same function, "run it again
   without --dry-run: swarm branch verify-landed --branch %s --remote %s",
   which has the identical defect. The parameter is in hand at that point;
   leaving one of the two naming the wrong verb re-creates the bug on the other
   path. This is a stated scope decision, not creep.

Leave the no-counterpart resolution alone: "push it: swarm branch push --branch
%s --remote %s" names push deliberately and is correct advice to a caller of
either verb.

Test, and it is the reason the wrong string shipped under coverage:
`TestADryRunDoesNotReportLandedFromAnUnfetchedComparison` in
cli/swarm/cli/branch_test.go loops over both verbs and asserts only
`strings.Contains(env.Resolution, "--dry-run")`, which both share. Strengthen it
to assert the resolution names the verb invoked (contains `"swarm branch "+verb`)
AND does not name the other. Both halves are needed — a contains-only check
passes on a string carrying both verbs.

REJECTED: building two resolution strings at the call site in `verifyLanded`.
`landingVerdict` is where a verdict and its resolution are constructed together;
splitting them puts the wording a function away from the condition it explains,
which is how these two drifted apart in the first place.

BATCH: seventh and last of batch b12. Only bead in the run touching
cli/swarm/cli/branch.go — it shares the `Swarm Command Surface` component with
the other six but no file, which is why it is in the chain at all.

metadata.tier_reason: Thread one parameter through an existing signature and strengthen a test assertion that currently cannot distinguish the two verbs; localized, with both call sites named

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b12
comments.text:
retro:proof the test was strengthened FIRST and watched fail on the exact
assertion the bead says was missing

The bead's point is that the case was already covered and the assertion could
not distinguish the two verbs, so the order matters: the assertion was
tightened against the unfixed code before the code was touched.

The old assertion, in TestADryRunDoesNotReportLandedFromAnUnfetchedComparison
(cli/swarm/cli/branch_test.go), inside a loop over both verbs:
    if !strings.Contains(env.Resolution, "--dry-run") {

The new one adds both halves the Design requires:
    other := "push"
    if verb == "push" {
        other = "verify-landed"
    }
    if !strings.Contains(env.Resolution, "swarm branch "+verb) { ... }
    if strings.Contains(env.Resolution, "swarm branch "+other) { ... }

command: cd cli && go test ./swarm/cli/ -run 'TestADryRunDoesNotReportLandedFromAnUnfetchedComparison' -v

output BEFORE the fix (test strengthened, code untouched):
  === RUN   TestADryRunDoesNotReportLandedFromAnUnfetchedComparison
      branch_test.go:327: push --dry-run's resolution does not name the command
        the caller ran: "run it again without --dry-run, or fetch first: swarm
        branch verify-landed --branch sprint/run-1 --remote origin"
      branch_test.go:331: push --dry-run's resolution sends the caller to
        `swarm branch verify-landed`, which is a different command: "run it
        again without --dry-run, or fetch first: swarm branch verify-landed
        --branch sprint/run-1 --remote origin"
  --- FAIL: TestADryRunDoesNotReportLandedFromAnUnfetchedComparison
  FAIL

The verify-landed iteration passed throughout, which is the control built into
the loop: the shared string happened to name that verb correctly, so only the
push iteration failed.

output AFTER the fix: exit 0.

Sweep for other hardcoded instances of the same string, after the change:
  command: grep -rn "swarm branch verify-landed" --include=*.go cli/ | grep -v _test.go
  output:
    cli/swarm/cli/branch.go:1:// The `swarm branch verify-landed` and `swarm branch push` commands: one
    cli/swarm/cli/branch.go:3:// of them. Per the "swarm branch verify-landed and swarm branch push"
  Both are the file header naming the two commands, which is correct prose. No
  resolution hardcodes the verb any more.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b12
comments.text:
retro:unverifiable the second resolution the Design required fixing is not
reachable by any test in this package, so it is corrected but unasserted

The Design named two resolutions and called fixing both a stated scope decision
rather than creep. Both are fixed, and they now derive the verb from one local:

  verb := "verify-landed"
  if pushFirst {
      verb = "push"
  }

1. The unfetched-remote verdict. Reachable and asserted -- it is what
   TestADryRunDoesNotReportLandedFromAnUnfetchedComparison drives, and the
   strengthened assertion covers both verbs.

2. The divergence-step verdict, guarded by
   `if !ok || divergeRec.Status != plan.StepRan` AFTER the fetch has run and
   the counterpart probe has succeeded. I could not construct that state
   against the exectest fake: the divergence step is in the same plan as the
   two reads before it, so a plan in which the fetch RAN and the comparison did
   not is a plan that stopped between them, and the fake replays declared argvs
   rather than truncating a plan. Its own comment says as much -- "The fetch
   ran, so this is a plan that stopped before the comparison".

So the second correction rests on the two resolutions sharing one `verb`
variable four lines apart, not on a test. What would settle it: a seam that
lets a test hand landingVerdict a plan.Report directly, with the fetch and
counterpart records present and the divergence record absent or non-StepRan.
landingVerdict already takes a plan.Report and vcs.Steps, so such a test is a
unit test on the function rather than through the command tree, and it would
cover both resolutions and the no-counterpart one in the same table.

Not filed as a bead: it is test infrastructure for a path this bead did not
introduce and no acceptance criterion asks for, and the bead's own acceptance
is satisfied by the strengthened both-verbs test. Recorded here so the gap is
visible rather than implied by a green check set.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b12
comments.text:
retro:tooling the `format` check is the one gate a narrowed run does not catch,
and it fired here after every targeted test had passed

Sequence, measured in this bead:
  cd cli && go test ./swarm/cli/ -run 'TestADryRun|TestAFailedFetch|Branch|Land'
  exit 0
  cd cli && go build -o /usr/local/bin/swarm ./swarm
  exit 0
  python3 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-checks.py
  exit 1
    === format
    unformatted:
    swarm/cli/branch.go
    === format FAILED (exit 1)
  (every other check passed in the same run)

The cause was a resolution string reflowed across two lines with an indentation
gofmt does not accept. Nothing in the compile, the vet or the tests can see it,
so the fast loop the skill recommends -- `bb-checks.py <id>...` while iterating
-- is silent on it by construction unless `format` is one of the ids picked.

Fixed by `gofmt -w ./swarm/cli/branch.go`; the full set then exited 0, matching
the run's baseline.

Worth noting because run-batch's guidance for the fast loop is "pick by what
you touched", and `format` reads as a check about formatting rather than about
a surface -- so a Go-only bead naturally picks `test-go` and `vet` and not
`format`. AGENTS.md already documents the neighbouring trap (gofmt -l exits 0
whether or not it found anything, which is why the check points at
scripts/format-check); this is the adjacent one, that `format` is the check
least likely to be selected and the one most likely to fire.

title: reportReady's doc comment still asserts the --agent arm carries no circuit-breaker semantics
description:
## What

`cli/swarm/cli/ready.go`, `reportReady`'s doc comment, verbatim at HEAD:

    // breaker and threshold are the CB delta's: whether this invocation is
    // reporting a dispatch return, and the count that stops the run. They
    // apply only here — --agent narrows to one dispatch's own queue and
    // carries no circuit-breaker semantics of its own.

That is the exact behaviour `4be01c8` removed. `reportAgentQueue` now
takes `breaker breakerReport, threshold int` and calls `applyBreaker`
itself; `swarm ready --run <r> --agent <a>` reads the count, writes it
back when `--completed` is given, and reports the run stopped at
threshold (measured at 2622f6c: exit 2).

`specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md` WAS updated in the same
commit ("`swarm ready` also carries the run's circuit breaker, **on both
arms**"). The comment three lines above the changed code was not, and it
is what the next editor of this function reads.

## Why it matters

The sentence does not merely lag — it asserts the opposite invariant, in
the file where the change lives. It reads as a licence to drop the
breaker from the `--agent` arm again, which is precisely the defect
`e6xt.11` was filed for.

## Acceptance

- `reportReady`'s doc no longer claims the `--agent` arm carries no
  breaker semantics.
- `reportAgentQueue`'s own doc already says it "carries the circuit
  breaker exactly as the whole-run arm does"; the two read consistently.
design:
Documentation only, one comment, no behaviour change.

In cli/swarm/cli/ready.go, `reportReady`'s doc comment ends:

    // breaker and threshold are the CB delta's: whether this invocation is
    // reporting a dispatch return, and the count that stops the run. They
    // apply only here — --agent narrows to one dispatch's own queue and
    // carries no circuit-breaker semantics of its own.

Keep the first sentence — it is what tells a reader what `breaker` and
`threshold` are — and replace the final clause with what is now true: both arms
carry the breaker through the same `applyBreaker`, and `--agent` narrows which
beads are reported without changing the dispatch return the same invocation
reports.

Do not restate `reportAgentQueue`'s own sentence ("It carries the circuit
breaker exactly as the whole-run arm does"); point at the shared function so the
two docs cannot drift into disagreeing.

REJECTED: deleting the paragraph outright. Only the final clause is wrong;
removing the whole thing loses the explanation of the two parameters.

Verify before assuming, do not re-edit: specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md
was corrected in the same commit that introduced this defect. Confirm with
`grep -n "both arms" specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md` and leave the
spec alone if it is already right.

No new test — the check set must simply stay green.

BATCH: FIFTH of batch b12, and deliberately the last of the four beads touching
cli/swarm/cli/ready.go. e6xt.13, e6xt.17 and e6xt.14 all rewrite code this
comment describes; a comment written before them describes a state about to
change again. Re-read `reportReady`, `reportAgentQueue` and `applyBreaker` as
they stand after those three, then write the sentence.

metadata.tier_reason: A doc comment and no behaviour change, but the sentence must state a correct invariant about code three sibling beads rewrite immediately before it; mechanical to type and not mechanical to get right

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b12
comments.text:
retro:proof a documentation-only bead carries no test, so the evidence is the
sweep and the verification the Design asked for

1. THE SPEC WAS VERIFIED, NOT RE-EDITED, as the Design directed.
  command: grep -n "both arms" specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md
  output:
    289:`swarm ready` also carries the run's circuit breaker, **on both arms**:
    352:**What landed is read from the target, after the fold, on both arms.**
  Already correct. The spec was left alone.

2. THE FALSE CLAIM IS GONE FROM THE TREE, swept after the edit for any other
copy of it:
  command: grep -rn "carries no circuit-breaker|apply only here|no circuit-breaker semantics" . --include=*.go --include=*.md
  output: no matches.

3. THE COMMENT WAS WRITTEN AGAINST THE CODE AS IT NOW STANDS, which is what
made this bead fifth in the batch rather than first. e6xt.13, e6xt.17 and
e6xt.14 all landed before it and all three changed what this comment describes,
so the sentence names the shared function and points at the one place the arms
genuinely differ instead of restating either arm's behaviour:

  // breaker and threshold are the CB delta's: whether this invocation is
  // reporting a dispatch return, and the count that stops the run. Both
  // arms carry them, through the one [applyBreaker] — --agent narrows
  // which beads are reported and changes nothing about the dispatch return
  // the same invocation reported. Where the two arms differ is in what a
  // stop supersedes, and that is stated on [reportAgentQueue], which is
  // the arm it is a property of.

The last sentence is new relative to the Design, which was written before
e6xt.14 established that the arms DO differ in one respect (reportAgentQueue
clears a superseded resolution; reportReady has none to clear). Saying "both
arms carry the breaker" and stopping there would have been true of the breaker
and misleading about the override three functions later. The Design's
instruction not to restate reportAgentQueue's own sentence is honoured: this
one points at it rather than copying it.

4. No behaviour change, so no test. The gate is the check set staying green:
  command: python3 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-checks.py
  exit: 0 — no findings beyond the run's baseline, which was also 0.

title: a breaker failure discards the queue answer swarm ready --agent already measured
description:
## What

`cli/swarm/cli/ready.go`, `reportAgentQueue`: adding the breaker to the
`--agent` arm gave a developer's own queue query two failure modes it did
not have before, and the way the error is returned throws away everything
the invocation had already measured.

    breaking, err := applyBreaker(ctx, deps, req, breaker, threshold)
    result.Records = append(result.Records, breaking.Records...)
    if err != nil {
        return Result{}, err
    }

`applyBreaker` refuses when `deps.Store == nil`, when the manifest read
fails, and when `consecutive_dispatch_failures` does not decode. On any of
those the `established`, `queue`, `queue_count` and `drained` facts — all
already established from queries that succeeded — and every record
collected are discarded, and the caller gets a bare unrepairable refusal
with no queue answer at all.

Before `4be01c8` the `--agent` arm never touched the manifest, so a
dispatched worker's queue query could not fail for a manifest reason.
`plugin/skills/run-batch/SKILL.md` has that worker run it as its first
act.

## Note on symmetry

`reportReady` (the whole-run arm) discards the same way, and always has —
so this is not an asymmetry between the arms. What is new is that the
`--agent` arm is now exposed to it, and that its consumer is a worker
rather than the coordinator.

The `breakerOutcome` doc added in this run says its `Records` field
exists "so a refused write is visible to a --full-result consumer rather
than only to this function". On the error path they are appended to a
result that is then thrown away, so that sentence is not true of the
failure case on either arm.

## Suggested shape (not prescriptive)

Return the result built so far with the breaker's own condition reported
as an unestablished fact, rather than discarding a queue answer that was
measured. Failing that, at minimum carry the records into the refusal.

## Acceptance

- A manifest read failure on either arm still reports the facts the
  invocation established before it, or states explicitly why it cannot.
- The invocations already run reach a `--full-result` consumer on the
  failure path.
design:
In `reportAgentQueue` (cli/swarm/cli/ready.go), replace the discard after
`applyBreaker`:

    breaking, err := applyBreaker(ctx, deps, req, breaker, threshold)
    result.Records = append(result.Records, breaking.Records...)
    if err != nil {
        return Result{}, err
    }

On error, return the result already built rather than an empty one: append
`Unestablished("consecutive_dispatch_failures", <the refusal's message>, <the
invocation where one exists>)`, set `result.Outcome = OutcomeAttention` and a
resolution naming what to fix (no manifest store configured / the manifest read
failed / the value does not decode), and return `result, nil`. The four facts
the invocation already established — `established`, `queue`, `queue_count`,
`drained` — and every record collected stay in the answer.

Apply the same shape to `reportReady`, which discards identically and always
has. Fixing one arm alone manufactures an asymmetry between them that nothing
asserts, which is the condition this run keeps filing beads about.

Outcome choice, pinned: `OutcomeAttention`. Not `OutcomeClear` — the breaker's
verdict is unknown and a clear answer would assert the run is dispatchable. Not
`OutcomeStop` — nothing established a stop. Attention is the outcome that says
"an answer, with something unmeasured in it".

Do NOT change `applyBreaker`'s own error returns. It is right to refuse; the
caller is what must not throw the measured answer away.

`breakerOutcome.Records`' doc says the records exist "so a refused write is
visible to a --full-result consumer rather than only to this function". That
sentence is false on the failure path today and true once this lands — assert
it, so it stays true.

REJECTED: carrying only the records into the refusal and still returning
`Result{}`. It is the bead's own stated minimum and it still loses the queue
answer, which is what a dispatched worker ran the command for — `run-batch` has
that worker run `swarm ready --agent` as its first act.

BATCH: third of batch b12, after e6xt.13 (which changes what `applyBreaker`
returns on the refused-write path) and before e6xt.14 (which rewrites the
`if breaking.Stopped` block three lines below this one).

title: swarm ready --agent: the breaker's stop override keeps the superseded case's resolution and drops its summary
description:
## What

In `cli/swarm/cli/ready.go`, `reportAgentQueue`'s breaker override sets

    result.Outcome = OutcomeStop
    result.Summary = breaking.Summary

and leaves `result.Resolution` alone. The `!established` case just above
it — the mistyped dispatch id — sets BOTH a summary and a resolution
("assign a bead in %s to %s, or dispatch a different agent id"). When the
breaker then stops the run, the summary is replaced and the resolution is
not, so the result reports a stop paired with a resolution for a
different condition, and the "not an established dispatch" signal
disappears from the answer entirely.

## Evidence (measured at 2622f6c, in-package probe against the fake runner)

`swarm ready --run run-1 --agent typo-1 --full-result --json`, with no
bead in the run naming `typo-1` and `consecutive_dispatch_failures` at 3,
threshold 3:

    "outcome": "stop",
    "status": 2,
    "summary": "the run is stopped: 3 consecutive dispatch(es) returned with no bead completed (threshold 3)",
    "resolution": "assign a bead in run-1 to typo-1, or dispatch a different agent id"

Two things wrong in one result: assigning a bead to `typo-1` will not
un-stop the run, and the mistyped id — which `run-batch` and
`dispatching.md` both say must never read as anything else — is now
reported only through the `established: false` fact, never in the
summary. `established` is still stated as a fact, so the information is
recoverable; the summary and resolution a caller reads first are not.

The whole-run arm (`reportReady`) has the same override and never sets a
resolution, so it is unaffected today — but the two arms now differ in a
way nothing asserts.

## Origin

Introduced by `4be01c8` (e6xt.11), which added the breaker to the
`--agent` arm. Before it, `reportAgentQueue` had no override at all.

## Suggested shape (not prescriptive)

Either clear the resolution when the breaker overrides the outcome, or
carry the superseded case forward in the summary ("...; dev-1 is not an
established dispatch in run-1"). Whichever is chosen, assert it, since a
stop that contradicts its own resolution is exactly the kind of result
`Result.Validate` exists to refuse and currently does not.

## Acceptance

- A stopped run reported through the `--agent` arm does not carry a
  resolution belonging to a condition the stop replaced.
- An unestablished dispatch id is still distinguishable from a drained
  one in the reported answer when the run is stopped.
- A test covers the combination (unestablished id + at threshold); none
  does today.
design:
In `reportAgentQueue` (cli/swarm/cli/ready.go), the breaker override

    result.Outcome = OutcomeStop
    result.Summary = breaking.Summary

replaces the summary and leaves `result.Resolution` holding the `!established`
case's text ("assign a bead in %s to %s, or dispatch a different agent id").

Chosen: do BOTH halves. When the outcome being overridden was the `!established`
attention, carry its distinguishing clause forward into the breaker summary
("...; %s is not an established dispatch in %s") and clear `result.Resolution`,
since no resolution un-stops a run. Both are required by the acceptance:
clearing alone satisfies the first criterion and drops the "not an established
dispatch" signal from the summary, which the second criterion forbids.

Assertion, with the choice pinned: prefer a direct test on the combination
(unestablished id + count at threshold), which is what the acceptance asks for
and which no test covers today. Adding the invariant to `Result.Validate` — a
stop paired with a resolution — is in scope ONLY if it does not newly refuse
results other commands legitimately produce; read cli/swarm/cli/result.go and
every `OutcomeStop` construction before touching it. Where it would, ship the
test and say so.

REJECTED: clearing the resolution only. It leaves the mistyped-id signal
recoverable only through the `established: false` fact, and both `run-batch` and
the dispatching reference require a mistyped dispatch id never to read as
anything else.

REJECTED: suppressing the breaker override when the id is unestablished. A
stopped run is stopped whoever asks, and hiding it from the arm a worker uses is
worse than the defect being fixed.

`reportReady` sets no resolution and is unaffected today, so the two arms differ
here with nothing asserting it. State that difference in `reportAgentQueue`'s
own doc comment rather than leaving it implicit.

BATCH: fourth of batch b12, after e6xt.17 — which rewrites the error path
immediately above this block, in the same function.

comments.author: dev-e6xt-b12
comments.text:
retro:decision the invariant was shipped as a TEST, not as a Result.Validate
rule, because a Validate rule would newly refuse results this package is
structurally written to produce

The bead left this bounded choice open and pinned the rule: prefer the test;
use Validate only if the rule would not newly refuse legitimate results. The
reading it asked for -- every OutcomeStop construction -- was done first.

command: grep -rn "OutcomeStop" --include=*.go . | grep -v _test.go
output (constructions only, from cli/):
  ./swarm/cli/branch.go:453   result.Outcome = OutcomeStop     (rejected())
  ./swarm/cli/branch.go:458   result.Outcome = OutcomeStop     (rejected())
  ./swarm/cli/ready.go:269    result.Outcome = OutcomeStop     (reportReady)
  ./swarm/cli/ready.go:618    result.Outcome = OutcomeStop     (reportAgentQueue)
  ./swarm/cli/manifest.go:218 result.Outcome = OutcomeStop
  ./swarm/cli/exit.go:102     &Refusal{Outcome: OutcomeStop}   (RefuseUnrepairable)

None of those pairs a stop with a resolution TODAY. But three call sites copy
an outcome and a resolution together with no stop check, so the shape is one
step away on paths that already exist:

  cli/swarm/cli/accept.go, acceptStopped (line 302 as a hint):
      result.Outcome    = stopped.refusal.Outcome
      result.Resolution = stopped.refusal.Resolution

  cli/swarm/cli/accept.go, settleDispatch fold (line 293 as a hint):
      if settled.outcome != OutcomeClear {
          result.Outcome    = settled.outcome
          result.Resolution = settled.resolution
      }

  cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go, the landing settlement (line 670 as a hint):
      outcome:    landed.Outcome,      // can be OutcomeStop, via rejected()
      resolution: landed.Resolution,

A resolution added to rejected() -- "pull --rebase and push again", which is
exactly what a refused push wants to say -- would travel through
that landing settlement into a stop-outcome result and the Validate rule would
then refuse a legitimate answer at render time.

The type's own documentation says the same. cli/swarm/cli/exit.go, Refusal:
  // Resolution names what would resolve the condition. Required when
  // the outcome is [OutcomeAttention]; the surface refuses to render an
  // attention result without one.
Required for attention; not forbidden elsewhere. Result.Resolution's doc is
worded identically. A Validate rule would contradict both.

So: the test ships and Validate is untouched, per the pinned rule. What the
bead observed is real but narrower than "no stop carries a resolution" -- it is
"no stop carries the resolution of the condition IT REPLACED", which is a
property of one override and not of the result type. It is enforced where it
holds, in reportAgentQueue, and asserted by
TestAStoppedRunDoesNotKeepTheSupersededCasesResolution.

title: the drain check's two halves apply different filters; dispatchBeads' claim of parity is false
description:
FOUND BY: sprint review of run agent-plugins-e6xt (reviewer: code-review, declared in sf.toml [review]).

WHAT. `dispatchBeads` in cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go carries this doc comment:

    "The same filters the drain check applies, because the set that had to
     drain is the set that is re-checked: an epic is not work, and a bead
     awaiting a human answer was never this agent's to finish."

That is false. The drain check applies those filters to ONE of its two halves. The two halves disagree about what a dispatch's set is.

MEASURED. Probe unit test in package `beads` (cli/swarm/tracker/beads), rendering both steps built from the SAME `tracker.ReadyFilter{Assignee: "dev-1", ExcludeKinds: ["epic"], ExcludeLabels: ["human"]}`:

    PROBE ready half: bd ready --parent run-1 --assignee dev-1 --exclude-type epic --exclude-label human --limit 0 --json
    PROBE held  half: bd list  --assignee dev-1 --status in_progress --limit 0 --json

The held half carries neither exclusion. The same asymmetry is visible from the shipped binary's own explain output:

    $ swarm ready --run agent-plugins-e6xt --agent dev-e6xt-b1 --explain
      "  bd ready --parent agent-plugins-e6xt --assignee dev-e6xt-b1 --exclude-type epic --exclude-label human --limit 0 --json  (this dispatch's ready half)"
      "  bd list --assignee dev-e6xt-b1 --status in_progress --limit 0 --json  (this dispatch's held half, narrowed to agent-plugins-e6xt)"

WHY THE FILTER NEVER REACHES THE HELD HALF. In cli/swarm/tracker/queue.go, `AgentQueue` builds:

    readyStep := t.Ready("ready", scope, filter)      // filter goes here
    heldStep  := t.Holding("held", scope, agent)      // and not here

`Tracker.Holding` (cli/swarm/tracker/beads/beads.go) takes no filter at all. The result is narrowed only by `Held.Within(beneath)` (cli/swarm/tracker/tracker.go), which intersects with `tracker.Descendants` - a full transitive walk that applies no kind or label filtering of its own.

CONSEQUENCE. An `epic`-kind or `human`-labelled bead assigned to a dispatch and left `in_progress` lands in `Queue.InProgress`, so `Queue.Drained()` is false forever and `swarm dispatch accept` refuses that dispatch permanently ("has not drained"), while `dispatchBeads` - the post-merge re-check - excludes the very same bead from the set it settles.

DURABLE ANCHOR. Two places, both by name:
 - cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go, function `dispatchBeads`, its doc comment beginning "The same filters the drain check applies". Grep handle: `grep -n "The same filters the drain check applies" cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go`
 - cli/swarm/tracker/queue.go, function `AgentQueue`, the two lines building `readyStep` and `heldStep`.

The caller that supplies the filter is cli/swarm/cli/accept.go's `tracker.AgentQueue(... tracker.ReadyFilter{ExcludeKinds: []string{epicKind}, ExcludeLabels: []string{humanLabel}})`.

REACHABILITY IS UNVERIFIED. No measurement here shows a human-labelled or epic-kind bead actually being assigned to a dispatch and claimed in a real run; `bd ready --exclude-label human` means such a bead is never handed out as ready. What IS measured is that the two halves disagree, and that the comment asserting they agree is false. Settle reachability by assigning a `human`-labelled bead to a dispatch, setting it `in_progress`, and running `swarm dispatch accept` against that dispatch.

FIX SHAPE (not attempted), either one: pass the filter through to `Tracker.Holding` (bd list accepts `--exclude-type`/`--exclude-label`), or apply the exclusions in `Held.Within`, so one definition of "this dispatch's set" serves both the drain verdict and the re-check. Whichever is chosen, the comment must end up true rather than merely edited.

SCOPE: row 1 - introduced by this run's own diff. `Tracker.Holding` was added by agent-plugins-o63s.1 (TRK) and `dispatchBeads` with its comment by agent-plugins-o63s.13 (RM); neither existed at base_sha 2490026ce2dc17d3813aeb5a1fed1a845c3da54e. Confirmed with `git log -S "func (t Tracker) Holding"` and `git log -S "func dispatchBeads"` over 2490026..HEAD.


## Steps to Reproduce

1. `swarm ready --run <epic> --agent <dispatch-id> --explain`

EXPECTED: the two halves of the dispatch's queue apply the same filters — that is what `dispatchBeads`' doc comment asserts.
ACTUAL: the ready half renders

    bd ready --parent <epic> --assignee <dispatch-id> --exclude-type epic --exclude-label human --limit 0 --json

while the held half renders

    bd list --assignee <dispatch-id> --status in_progress --limit 0 --json

carrying neither exclusion.

2. Unit-level, which is how it was measured: a probe in package `beads` (cli/swarm/tracker/beads) rendering both steps from ONE `tracker.ReadyFilter{Assignee: "dev-1", ExcludeKinds: ["epic"], ExcludeLabels: ["human"]}` reproduces the same asymmetry.

NOTE: this reproduces the disagreement between the halves, which is what this bead fixes. A live reproduction of the downstream consequence — a dispatch that can never drain — is UNVERIFIED; see the Design for why establishing it is not this bead's job.
design:
Give the drain check ONE definition of "this dispatch's set". `AgentQueue` in
cli/swarm/tracker/queue.go builds `readyStep := t.Ready("ready", scope, filter)`
and `heldStep := t.Holding("held", scope, agent)`; the filter reaches only the
ready half. `Tracker.Holding` (cli/swarm/tracker/beads/beads.go) takes no filter
at all, and the held result is narrowed only by `Held.Within(beneath)`
(cli/swarm/tracker/tracker.go), which intersects with the descendant walk and
applies no kind or label filtering of its own.

PREFERRED: thread the `tracker.ReadyFilter` through to `Holding`, which renders
`bd list --assignee ... --status in_progress` and can carry `--exclude-type` and
`--exclude-label` the same way the ready half does. ACCEPTABLE FALLBACK if that
interface change proves invasive: apply the exclusions in `Held.Within`. Both
produce the same observable outcome - the two halves agree - so this is an
internal placement choice, not a behavioural one; pick whichever leaves the
Tracker interface honest about what it filters.

Narrow the HELD half; do NOT widen the ready half. The blueprint fixes the ready
set: "The ready set SHALL exclude epics, closed beads, deferred beads, and beads
labelled for human attention."

The doc comment on `dispatchBeads` (cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go) - "The same
filters the drain check applies, because the set that had to drain is the set
that is re-checked" - must end up TRUE of the code, not merely edited to hedge.
The caller that supplies the filter is accept.go's
`tracker.AgentQueue(... tracker.ReadyFilter{ExcludeKinds: []string{epicKind},
ExcludeLabels: []string{humanLabel}})`.

REACHABILITY IS UNVERIFIED and establishing it is NOT this bead's job. No
measurement shows an epic-kind or human-labelled bead actually assigned to a
dispatch and left in_progress in a real run; `bd ready --exclude-label human`
means such a bead is never handed out as ready. What IS measured, and what this
bead fixes, is that the two halves disagree and the comment asserting they agree
is false. Do not spend the session hunting a live reproduction.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Both halves of the agent-queue derivation apply the same exclusions: an epic-kind bead and a `human`-labelled bead assigned to a dispatch and left `in_progress` appear in neither half.
- [ ] `swarm ready --run <epic> --agent <id> --explain` shows the held half's `bd list` carrying the same kind and label narrowing that the ready half's `bd ready` carries.
- [ ] `Queue.Drained()` is true for a dispatch whose only remaining `in_progress` bead is one the post-merge re-check excludes, so `swarm dispatch accept` no longer refuses that dispatch permanently.
- [ ] The ready half's exclusions are unchanged, and the held half is still narrowed to the run.
- [ ] `dispatchBeads`' doc comment in cli/swarm/cli/accept_settle.go is true of the code as it then stands.
- [ ] A Go test asserts both steps are rendered from the same filter, naming the exclusions each carries.
- [ ] `specs/architecture/container-swarm-cli.md` is consistent with the fixed behaviour for the Tracker and Beads Tracker components, or updated where it is not.
- [ ] All 13 checks pass: `python3 plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/bb-checks.py` exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: Crosses a Go interface and its beads implementation to make one filter serve both halves of the drain derivation without loosening the ready set or the drain verdict; three components changed

title: swarm status's --dry-run help says it performs no write; it runs git worktree prune
description:
## Problem

**Outside this review pass's assigned scope** (the pass was scoped to the
non-`cli/` half of the run's diff); found while verifying a `sprint-recovery`
claim and filed rather than dropped.

`swarm status`'s `--dry-run` flag help asserts the command writes nothing:

    cli/swarm/cli/status.go:99
      "measure live state; status performs no write, so this matches execute"
    cli/swarm/cli/status.go:19
      "…which for a command that performs no write at all is…"

It does write. `cli/swarm/vcs/git/git.go`'s `Worktrees` declares the prune a
`plan.Write` step —

    prune := v.step(prefix+"-prune", plan.Write, true, discard, "worktree", "prune")
    // The prune is a write, so a dry run refuses it

— and `swarm status` in execute mode runs `git worktree prune`, which mutates
`.git/worktrees`. That write is load-bearing downstream:
`plugin/skills/sprint-recovery/SKILL.md` dropped its own `git worktree prune`
step in this run on the strength of it ("It prunes stale worktree
registrations before it counts them, which is not optional").

The reported ANSWER is still right under `--dry-run`, because the list decoder
drops prunable entries — so this is a false statement in the help rather than a
wrong result.

## Evidence

- `cli/swarm/cli/status.go:19` and `:99`, the two strings quoted above.
- `cli/swarm/vcs/git/git.go:62-79`, `Worktrees`, and its comment "The prune is
  a write, so a dry run refuses it".
- `swarm status --run <epic> --dry-run` prints `git worktree prune` in the
  invocation list of the worktree facts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The `--dry-run` help says what is actually true: the command performs one
  write (the stale-registration prune) which a dry run skips, and the reported
  facts match execute anyway because prunable entries are dropped by the
  decoder.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -n "performs no write" cli/swarm/cli/status.go` -> lines 19 and 99.
2. `sed -n "62,79p" cli/swarm/vcs/git/git.go` -> the prune is declared `plan.Write` with the comment "The prune is a write, so a dry run refuses it".
3. `swarm status --run <epic>` (execute) lists `git worktree prune` among the invocations behind the worktree facts.

title: AGENTS.md's retraction procedure measures the replacement's truth but not what the false claim was justifying
description:
audience: project · target: `AGENTS.md`, "Retracting a claim found false" · recurrence: 0

## What is wrong, and what it costs

AGENTS.md's retraction procedure has five steps, and step 4 is "**Measure the
replacement.** Do not install a corrected universal you have not run." That
covers the replacement's TRUTH. It does not cover what the retracted claim was
DOING.

A false claim is often load-bearing: it is the stated justification for
defensive code. Swapping the value and leaving the sentence in place produces a
justification that no longer supports the code, and a reader with grounds to
delete the guard.

`agent-plugins-mpnf.18` hit this directly. The retracted claim ("`bd ready
--json` returns `null` when empty") appeared at seven sites in five files, and
at five of them it was justifying an `if type=="array"` guard. Simply writing
`[]` for `null` would have left every guard justified by a measurement that no
longer supports it — because `null` was never the hazard those guards face:

    $ printf 'null'                | jq -r 'length'  -> 0     exit 0
    $ printf '[]'                  | jq -r 'length'  -> 0     exit 0
    $ printf '"an error message"'  | jq -r 'length'  -> 16    exit 0
    $ printf '{"a":1,"b":2}'       | jq -r 'length'  -> 2     exit 0

A bare `jq length` already handles `null` correctly. The real hazard is a STRING
or OBJECT payload reporting a nonzero count. Each replacement was re-grounded on
that instead.

The same finding records a second, sharper instance: the agent's FIRST
replacement for `sprint-cleanup.sh` was itself inverted — it claimed the
destructive reading was "not empty", when `agent_drained` returns drained when
`json_empty` holds for both queries, so EMPTY is the destructive verdict. It was
caught mid-work and corrected. **A replacement is a new claim and gets a
replacement's worth of scrutiny; nothing in the procedure says so about the
claim's ROLE.**

Cost of not having this step: a retraction that is technically complete and
leaves five sites of correct defensive code looking unjustified. The next agent
to read them deletes a guard, correctly following the text.

## Evidence

- `agent-plugins-mpnf.18#3` — "the replacement sentences do not just swap null
  for []. Swapping alone would have left the defensive code justified by a
  measurement that no longer supports it — every site's guard is wider than
  'accept [] or null', and a reader who saw only '[] is what bd emits' would have
  grounds to delete the guard."
- `agent-plugins-mpnf.18#4` — the site inventory: seven sites in five files, two
  of the cited line numbers already moved.

## Proposed change

In AGENTS.md, "Retracting a claim found false", extend step 4:

> 4. **Measure the replacement, and re-ground what the claim was holding up.** Do
>    not install a corrected universal you have not run. At each site, ask what
>    the false claim was JUSTIFYING — a guard, a wider-than-necessary check, an
>    ordering — and whether the corrected fact still justifies it. Where it does
>    not, the replacement states the hazard that does, measured. A retraction
>    that leaves correct code with a justification that no longer supports it
>    invites the code's deletion, which is a worse outcome than the false claim.

---

title: An acceptance criterion may name a verification tool the environment lacks; grooming does not check
description:
audience: skill · target: `groom-beads` (Definition of Ready) · recurrence: 0

## What is wrong, and what it costs

An acceptance criterion may name a verification tool that the environment does
not have, and nothing between grooming and dispatch checks.

Two beads in this run carried the identical criterion, verbatim — "`sh -n` and
`shellcheck` (as `scripts/ci.sh` runs them) report nothing new". Every clause of
it is false in this repository:

    $ grep -n 'shellcheck' scripts/ci.sh sf.toml                    -> no output
    $ grep -n 'sh -n\|bash -n' scripts/ci.sh sf.toml bb-checks.py   -> no output
    $ command -v shellcheck                                         -> not found

`ci.sh` runs neither tool, and `shellcheck` is not installed. The 13 declared
check ids contain no shellcheck.

Two agents, working independently on different beads, each hit it, each measured
it, and each recorded the criterion UNVERIFIED rather than claiming a pass — the
correct handling, and the reason this cost nothing worse. But an AC that cannot
be satisfied is an AC that either blocks a bead or gets quietly downgraded, and
which of the two happens depends on the agent. The bar for "done" is set by
whoever is dispatched.

## Evidence

- `agent-plugins-mpnf.16#4` — "the acceptance criterion '`sh -n` and shellcheck
  (as `scripts/ci.sh` runs them) report nothing new' cannot be satisfied as
  written: ci.sh runs NEITHER, and shellcheck is not installed in this
  container. ... Same criterion appears verbatim on agent-plugins-mpnf.20."
- `agent-plugins-mpnf.20#5` — "this bead's '`sh -n` / shellcheck report nothing
  new beyond the recorded baseline' has the same defect as the identical
  criterion on agent-plugins-mpnf.16."
- `agent-plugins-mpnf.17#3` — "shellcheck is not installed in this container, so
  half of acceptance criterion 6 is UNVERIFIED."
- `agent-plugins-mpnf.24#6` — "shellcheck is not installed in this container ...
  so its half of the AC's '`sh -n` / shellcheck report nothing new' could not be
  exercised."

## Proposed change

Add one check to the Definition of Ready: **every executable named in an
acceptance criterion resolves on PATH, or is a declared check id in the project's
own check set.** Both halves are one command each —

    command -v <tool>
    <project check list> | grep -qx <id>

An AC naming a tool that satisfies neither is not Ready. The bead bounces with
the tool name quoted, and grooming either substitutes what the project actually
runs or files the tool's absence as its own work order.

---

title: Reconcile agent-plugins-qozp.22: superseded by qozp.20, not merely deferred
description:
Retro candidate C13 (P3) from the sprint retro of run epic agent-plugins-so39.
Findings: qozp.20#3; the coordinator's `amend:` comment 8 on agent-plugins-so39.
Report: rfcs/sprints/2026-08-24-run-2-coordination-corrections-findings.md (section 5, C13 — drafted verbatim there; the amend: comment is quoted in full in section 7).

WHAT IS WRONG, AND WHAT IT COSTS

agent-plugins-qozp.22 reports the same defect agent-plugins-qozp.20 fixed and proposes
the OPPOSITE derivation: `dev-<run-id>-<wave>-<batch>` against the run-wide numbering
that shipped (`<batch-id>` is the batch's position in the run, numbered once across
every wave). The two are mutually exclusive — only one of them can be the derivation.

It carries metadata.grooming_status=out-of-scope-this-run, which reads as "not yet"
rather than "no longer correct", so a future run picking it off the backlog would
re-break what this run shipped. Nobody touched it during the run, correctly, under the
do-not-undefer constraint — which is exactly why it needs a record somewhere that is
not the findings document.

MEASURED STATE AT FILING TIME, WHICH HAS MOVED

At the time C13 was drafted, qozp.22 was `deferred`. Measured at 2026-08-24T20:37Z by
`bd export`, it is now `closed`, closed_at 2026-08-24T20:35:50Z, still carrying
metadata.grooming_status=out-of-scope-this-run. It has NO comments, and no supersede
edge to qozp.20. Its sibling agent-plugins-qozp.21, excluded for the same reason, is
still `deferred`.

So one of the two dispositions below may already have been taken by hand, minutes before
this bead was filed. The record it needs still does not exist: a reader of qozp.22 today
sees a closed P1 bug with no statement of why it closed, and cannot tell "fixed" from
"superseded by the opposite fix" from "closed by accident". Confirm what happened before
acting.

PROPOSED CHANGE

Reconcile qozp.22 — either closed as superseded by qozp.20 with that stated on the bead,
or rewritten to whatever residual defect survives the run-wide numbering — carrying an
explicit statement that it must NOT be admitted as written.

Filing this bead is not undeferring qozp.22, and neither is closing it as superseded.
The decision stays with whoever grooms the next run.

ON "FILING SOMETHING AGAINST" A RECORD: THERE IS NO MECHANISM

Worth stating plainly, because the retro's phrasing can be read as naming machinery that
does not exist. There is no special channel for a finding that belongs to a record rather
than to the work that surfaced it. It is an ordinary bead — `bd create`, plus a
`discovered-from` edge to whatever tripped over it. agent-plugins-b9ft (type=bug, P1,
discovered-from -> agent-plugins-uva5) is the worked instance: uva5's agent hit a flaky
check, and the bead was filed against the CHECK, with an edge back to the bead that hit
it. "Filed against X" is a statement about ATTRIBUTION — the finding belongs to X, not to
whichever bead happened to trip it — and it buys the same thing here: this bead is
attributed to qozp.22's staleness, with a discovered-from edge to qozp.20, which is what
made it stale.
acceptance_criteria: agent-plugins-qozp.22 carries an explicit statement of its disposition relative to agent-plugins-qozp.20 — either closed as superseded, or rewritten to the residual defect — and in either case states that its `dev-<run-id>-<wave>-<batch>` derivation must not be admitted as written, since run-wide batch numbering shipped instead. A reader arriving at qozp.22 from the backlog can tell superseded from fixed without reading this bead.
close_reason: Motivating instance already resolved: agent-plugins-qozp.22 was superseded, commented and edge-linked to qozp.20 before this bead was filed. The filing agent observed a mid-write state.

title: capability-tier.md's nested-replace transcript does not reproduce: the shown output omits the four keys the same bead already carries
description:
`plugin/skills/groom-beads/references/capability-tier.md` presents this as measured on bd 1.2.2:

```
bd update <id> --metadata '{"alpha":1,"beta":"two","gamma":["x","y"]}'
bd update <id> --metadata '{"delta":9}'
bd show <id> --json | jq -c '.[0].metadata'
-> {"beta":"two","alpha":1,"delta":9,"gamma":["x","y"]}

bd update <id> --metadata '{"nest":{"a":1,"b":2}}'
bd update <id> --metadata '{"nest":{"c":3}}'
bd show <id> --json | jq -c '.[0].metadata'
-> {"nest":{"c":3}}
```

The second shown output is not what bd prints. `<id>` is the same bead throughout, with no `bd create` between, so the four keys from the first half are still there. Re-run on bd 1.2.2 in a throwaway scratch database, the second `bd show` returns:

`{"alpha":1,"beta":"two","delta":9,"gamma":["x","y"],"nest":{"c":3}}`

The conclusion the snippet draws is correct - `"a"` and `"b"` are gone, the nested object value was replaced whole. Only the transcript is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that makes the block look like a replace rather than a merge, which is the misreading the whole document exists to prevent.

A transcript offered as evidence has to reproduce, or the next reader who runs it concludes the document is stale. Either show the full output, or split the nested demonstration onto a fresh bead and say so.

title: Append three measured environment facts to the AGENTS.md ledger
description:

`environment` findings produce no issue by the retro's routing table, but landing them in
AGENTS.md's environmental-failure ledger is an edit that needs an owner, and without one
they die in the findings document. Three are ready:

   current, one command apart.

2. The Bash worktree-isolation guard refuses plainly in-worktree commands,
   non-deterministically. `bd update <id> --set-metadata dispatched_at="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"`
   — no git call in it at all — was refused with "this command is too complex to verify

   files with the Write tool, run them with a single bare command. Cost on that bead alone:

3. GitHub Actions is down at the account level. Jobs die in 2-4 seconds with no log
   content. This is a platform state, not a defect in any workflow in this repository, and
   CI results were unobtainable for this run's commits. Its evidence is the coordinator's
   observation reported at retro handoff, NOT a captured retro: finding.

Cost: entry 2 cost a bead five extra round trips this run; entry 1 produced a full bead's
worth of investigation that ended in a decline. The ledger's purpose is that the next agent

   $ bd ready --json        -> []     [exit 0]
   Same scratch database, same session. Eleven `bd ready` configurations (empty tracker; issues present with filters matching none; all issues closed; --assignee / --parent / --exclude-type combinations) returned [] and never null, with a positive control returning a populated array so that "[] everywhere" is not equally explained by a broken query. The `bd human list` -> null result is TRUE and must not be swept along with the retracted `bd ready` claim. (findings agent-plugins-mpnf.18#1, mpnf.18#2, mpnf#7)

2. bd distinguishes "nothing to report" from "cannot answer" by EXIT STATUS, not by payload.
   $ out="$(bd ready --assignee nobody-xyz --json 2>&1)"; echo "rc=$?"   -> rc=0, []
   $ cd <empty scratch dir>; out="$(bd ready --assignee nobody-xyz --json 2>&1)"; echo "rc=$?"   -> rc=1, "Error: no beads database found"
   An unanswerable query writes to stderr, so a command substitution captures the empty string — indistinguishable from an empty answer on content alone. The status is the only discriminator. This is what makes an ambiguity guard implementable at all, and discarding it is what made sprint-cleanup force-remove a live agent's worktree. (finding agent-plugins-mpnf.16#2)

3. bd dep add refuses to UPGRADE an edge type; `related` does not silently become `blocks`.
   $ bd dep add agent-plugins-0913 agent-plugins-qozp.8
   Error: dependency agent-plugins-0913 -> agent-plugins-qozp.8 already exists with type "related" (requested "blocks"); remove it first with bd dep remove then re-add
   [exit 1]
   Remove then re-add is the only path. (finding agent-plugins-mpnf#1)

4. shellcheck is NOT installed in this container and no declared check invokes one.
   $ command -v shellcheck   -> not found
   $ grep -n 'shellcheck' scripts/ci.sh sf.toml   -> no output
   The 13 declared ids are format vet build test-go skills shared-refs strata-docs schemas corpus ref-links template-drift script-self-tests skills-strict. Every shell change run 3 shipped therefore carries no lint verdict. Filed as its own work at agent-plugins-eejf; the LEDGER entry is the fact, independent of whether that bead is adopted. (findings agent-plugins-mpnf.16#4, .17#3, .20#5, .24#6, .18#6)

5. UNVERIFIABLE, and worth a ledger line as such: the harness's hook environment cannot be observed from a session. What CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR carries inside a real harness-fired hook invocation could not be settled from inside run 3 either. What would settle it: arm from a repo checked out under a multi-root parent and invoke the hook through the harness, comparing --status against what the hook reads. agent-plugins-mpnf.24 fixed the dependent behaviour by removing state_dir's dependence on the variable rather than by settling the claim, which is the right move when a claim cannot be measured. (finding agent-plugins-mpnf.24#3)

Report for all five: docs/research/sprint-findings/2026-08-25-agent-plugins-mpnf.md §5.

title: references/scripts.md's side-effect list for pre-flight-check.sh omits the concurrency_cap write
description:
plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/scripts.md:67-77 is the authoritative 'artifacts each script creates, writes, or repoints' list. Its pre-flight-check.sh entry still says it 'writes the checks baseline into the run epic's manifest' and enumerates worktree prune, the probe push, and the declared checks.

Since agent-plugins-h3j8 the script also writes `concurrency_cap` onto the epic, and deliberately does so on ANY epic-scoped pass rather than inside the checks-baseline branch (the script's own comment at pre-flight-check.sh:707-710 explains why). That is a second, unconditional manifest write and it is not listed.

The file's opening rule is 'The scripts are executed, not read ... read this file rather than opening one to learn how to call it' — which makes an incomplete side-effect list the only signal a reader gets.

Related: the same entry's phrase 'merging rather than replacing so grooming's and admission's keys survive' is not true on the concurrency_cap path's exception branch (see the P0 filed against h3j8); fixing both together is sensible.

FIX DIRECTION: add concurrency_cap to the side-effects entry, noting it is written on every epic-scoped pass.

Evidence: scripts.md:67-77 vs pre-flight-check.sh:687-737 at 9a88c6f.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read the `pre-flight-check.sh` bullet under `## Side effects — what each
   script leaves behind` in `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/scripts.md`.
2. `grep -n concurrency_cap plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh`
   — the script writes `concurrency_cap` onto the epic via `manifest_merge`,
   guarded only by `[ -n "$EPIC" ]`.
3. Expected: the side-effect list names every manifest key the script writes.
   Actual: it names only the checks baseline, so a reader who obeys the file's
   own rule ("the scripts are executed, not read") never learns that an
   epic-scoped pass writes `concurrency_cap` too.

## Grooming note — one premise in the description does not survive measurement

The description's "Related" paragraph says the entry's phrase *"merging rather
than replacing so grooming's and admission's keys survive"* is "not true on the
concurrency_cap path's exception branch". Measured: BOTH writes go through the
same `manifest_merge` helper — the checks-baseline write and the
`concurrency_cap` write — so the merging claim holds on both paths. The
"exception" the script's own comment describes is that the write sits OUTSIDE
the checks-baseline branch, not that it replaces rather than merges. Correcting
that phrase is therefore not part of this bead, and the acceptance criteria
below do not ask for it.
design:
Documentation only. Extend the `pre-flight-check.sh` bullet in
`plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/scripts.md`'s `## Side effects` list to
name the `concurrency_cap` write, and say that it happens on ANY epic-scoped
pass rather than only when the checks baseline is taken. That conditionality is
the part a reader gets wrong: a project declaring no checks still gets
`concurrency_cap`, which is precisely why the script places the write outside
the baseline branch.

IN SCOPE: the one bullet in `scripts.md`.

OUT OF SCOPE, and deliberately so:
- Editing `pre-flight-check.sh` itself. Its behaviour is correct; only the
  description of it is incomplete.
- Rewording "merging rather than replacing" — measurement says the phrase is
  accurate on both paths (see the grooming note in the description).
- Anything about the run manifest's schema. `agent-plugins-xpn8` owns that and
  is planned into a later wave; this bead must not anticipate it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The `pre-flight-check.sh` entry in `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/references/scripts.md`'s `## Side effects` list names the `concurrency_cap` write to the run epic's manifest.
- [ ] It states that the write happens on any epic-scoped pass, not only when the checks baseline is taken.
- [ ] No other side effect already listed for that script is removed or reworded.
- [ ] `plugin/skills/bead-bonanza/scripts/pre-flight-check.sh` is unchanged by this bead.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: One bullet in one reference file; the text to add is stated and the scope fence is explicit.

title: Stray closing code fence in sprint-plan/references/run-record.md environmental-ledger section
description:
plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md has an unmatched closing ``` in the '## Environmental ledger' section: the two ledger example lines are followed by a bare fence with no opener, so every renderer treats the rest of the document from that point as being inside a code block until the next fence.

Pre-existing, not introduced by the bead that found it — confirmed with:
  git show HEAD:plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md | sed -n '105,116p'
which shows the same bare fence after the two '1. `<claim>` — …' lines.

Fix: either open a fence before the two example lines or delete the closing one. No declared check catches it (skills, skills-strict, ref-links and shared-refs all pass with it present).
design:
DELETE the stray closing fence; do NOT add an opening one. The choice is
resolvable from the content: the two lines it follows are

    1. `<claim>` — proved by `<command>`, observed `<result>`
    1. `<claim>` — unverified; would be settled by `<command>`

a markdown numbered list carrying inline backticked placeholders. Opening a
fence before them would convert rendered prose into a code block and change
what the section says; deleting the bare closing fence restores the list and
un-swallows everything from that point to the next fence.

Measured: `grep -c '^```' plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md`
returns 11 — odd, i.e. unbalanced. The fence lines are at 50, 75, 127, 131,
148, 162, 174, 205, 214, 273, 280; 148 is the unmatched one and removing it
pairs the remaining ten (50/75, 127/131, 162/174, 205/214, 273/280).

Sequencing note for whoever holds this file: agent-plugins-xpn8 also edits
run-record.md (it replaces the `## Run manifest` key table with generated
markdown) and is planned into a LATER wave, so it branches from a tree that
already carries this fix and must preserve it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `grep -c '^```' plugin/skills/sprint-plan/references/run-record.md` returns an even number (10), i.e. every fence is paired.
- [ ] The two environmental-ledger example lines render as a numbered list, not as a code block.
- [ ] The `## Wave table` section that followed the stray fence is no longer swallowed into a code block.
- [ ] No content in the file changed other than the removal of the bare fence.
- [ ] `scripts/ci.sh` exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: One-line deletion in a markdown file; the fix is pinned in Design and the verification is a grep.

comments.author: retro-so39
comments.text: related: retro-so39 — the recovery trigger's INTERVAL now lives here. sprint-retro candidate C11 (run epic agent-plugins-so39) was split: its invariant half was filed to .sf/outbox/bead-bonanza/2026-08-24-naming-the-next-ceremony-is-not-dispatching-it.md, and its second half — choosing the durable recovery trigger's interval as an explicit liveness budget — was deliberately NOT filed, because this bead's background monitor on the bead event log subsumes it with a better mechanism: it reacts to the absence of events rather than polling on a timer. Evidence, for whoever implements this: so39#12 (the coordinator ended a turn announcing the next ceremony with nothing in flight; the run sat still until the human asked) and so39#10 (the trigger armed at first dispatch DID fire, at 17:57:32, with the right instruction — the design works; the gap was the 50-minute interval). This bead's status is untouched; it remains deferred/excluded per the run manifest.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text:
retro:proof what the bd event stream actually emits, measured in a throwaway Dolt database (zzscratch prefix, bd version 1.2.2 (dev)), never this tracker. Hooks written as .beads/hooks/on_create, on_update and on_close, each logging its own name plus $1 and $2:

  bd create                          -> on_create  <id>  create
  bd update <id> --status in_progress-> on_update  <id>  update
  bd update <id> --status closed     -> on_update  <id>  update
  bd close <id>                      -> on_close   <id>  close
  bd update <id> --claim             -> NOTHING          (no hook fired at all)

Three consequences, and none of them was in the file before:

1. `--claim` is silent. progress-streaming.md asserted 'a bead moving to in_progress or closed emits a line without the subagent writing one'. Half false: run-bead step 1 mandates `bd update {ID} --claim` as the claiming primitive, and that emits nothing. Measured directly -- probe C was claimed between two 3-second samples of the log and the log was byte-identical either side. Corrected in the file.

2. $2 never names a status. It is the hook's own name, so 'update' covers in_progress AND closed and a stream keyed on $2 cannot tell a claim from a close -- the one transition the orchestrator acts on. The OLD documented Monitor filter (grep -E 'close|update') matched only via the literal 'update' alternative; a filter on 'close' alone would have matched nothing the close ceremony produces, since the ceremony uses `bd update --status closed` and not `bd close`.

3. The issue JSON on stdin DOES carry the status. Measured:
   on_update args=[zzscratch-ck2|update] stdin=[{"id":"zzscratch-ck2","title":"probe D - stdin shape","status":"closed","priority":3,"issue_type":"task","owner":"...","created_at":"...","created_by":"dev-mpnf-4","updated_at":"...","closed_at":"..."}]
   So the hook snippet now extracts status from stdin and the log line has four fields. That is what makes the monitor's output actionable rather than just a heartbeat.

END TO END, nothing armed: monitor started against an EMPTY temp directory with no log file and no argument, then a bead created, moved to in_progress, and closed in the scratch database. Its stdout -- which is what the session receives as notifications:
   2026-08-24T21:44:12Z  zzscratch-bbg  create  open
   2026-08-24T21:44:16Z  zzscratch-bbg  update  in_progress
   2026-08-24T21:44:19Z  zzscratch-bbg  update  closed

comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text:
retro:unverifiable acceptance criterion 2 -- 'Demonstrated: closing a bead delivers a line to the SESSION with nothing having armed a watch' -- cannot be satisfied end to end from here, and I did not claim it was.

Why: monitors 'run only in interactive CLI sessions' and are 'skipped on hosts where the Monitor tool is unavailable' (code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference). This is a dispatched subagent session; no monitor declared in a file I just wrote is running in it, and re-reading monitors.json would not start one -- the docs say changes need /reload-plugins or a session restart.

What WAS demonstrated, which is every link in the chain except the harness's own delivery step: bd close -> .beads/hooks/on_update -> $BB_EVENT_LOG -> plugin/monitors/bb-events-monitor.sh stdout, with the monitor started against an empty directory and told nothing. Its three stdout lines are quoted in the proof comment above. Whether Claude Code turns those stdout lines into notifications is the documented contract ('Each stdout line from command is delivered to Claude as a notification during the session') and is the only unverified link.

What would settle it: enable the sf plugin in an interactive CLI session, /reload-plugins, invoke the bead-bonanza skill (the monitor is gated on-skill-invoke), install the .beads/hooks snippet with BB_EVENT_LOG exported, and close a bead. Expect one notification carrying the four-field line.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text:
retro:decision three choices a diff-reader would not recognise as choices.

1. The monitor GLOBS a directory instead of tailing $BB_EVENT_LOG. The bead's sketch is `tail -F $BB_EVENT_LOG`, and that variable is invisible to a monitor for the same reason it is invisible to a hook: the process is spawned by the harness, not by the orchestrator's shell that eval'd pre-flight's output. Unset, `tail -F "$BB_EVENT_LOG"` follows the empty path and `tail -F $BB_EVENT_LOG` unquoted reads stdin forever -- either way, silent and useless. It also cannot be handed a path at declaration time, because the monitor starts before any run is scoped. So it watches ${BB_EVENT_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}} for bb-events-*.log, which is exactly the name pre-flight-check.sh:529 constructs (${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bb-events-$EPIC.log). pre-flight-check.sh is unchanged.

2. The start offset differs by when a log appeared, and this was a REAL BUG caught by the self-test rather than a precaution. First attempt used `tail -n 0` for everything, and the assertion 'picks up a log created after it started' FAILED with empty output: the run's first events are written before the next reglob notices the file, so -n 0 attaches past them. Now a log already present at startup gets -n 0 (a backlog is not news, so a restart mid-run does not replay it) and a log appearing later gets -n +1 (all of it was written while this monitor was running). One tail per log, started once, rather than one tail restarted over a changing file list.

3. "when": "on-skill-invoke:bead-bonanza" rather than "always". D1's condition was that every adopter inherits these, so the monitor starts only in sessions that invoked the orchestrator. The cost is named in progress-streaming.md's fallback section: a solo run-bead session, and a sprint-recovery session resuming someone else's run, get no monitor. "when" takes one skill name, so covering sprint-recovery too is not expressible; "always" would have covered it at the price of a polling loop in every adopter session forever.

ALSO REJECTED: piping tail through `awk '{print; fflush()}'` for line buffering. Measured that it is unnecessary AND harmful here -- `tail -n 0 -q -F f > out` delivered a line appended 1s later within 2s, while the same tail piped through awk delivered nothing in the same window (mawk buffers its input read). Straight tail, no pipe.

NOT DONE, deliberately: pre-flight-check.sh is untouched, so BB_EVENT_LOG keeps its current meaning for the by-hand Monitor fallback; and plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json is untouched, because monitors/monitors.json is auto-discovered at the plugin root and needs no manifest key.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text:
retro:scope the bead's own comment from retro-so39 says this monitor subsumes the durable recovery trigger's interval question, 'because it reacts to the absence of events rather than polling on a timer'. It does not, and progress-streaming.md now says so explicitly instead of quietly dropping the section.

Two reasons, both structural:
1. A monitor is IN-SESSION, exactly as an armed Monitor is. It is started by Claude Code for the session and delivers into it, so it dies with the session -- and the case the durable trigger exists for is a user interrupt killing the orchestrator, which kills the monitor at the same instant.
2. It reports events, not their absence. Nothing in a stream of appended lines fires when no line is appended; noticing a gap requires something awake to notice, and after (1) there is nothing awake. 'Absence of an event is not an event' is already the reason SubagentStop cannot detect a stall; it applies here unchanged.

So the 'Back it with a durable trigger' section is kept verbatim, the interval choice so39 deferred is still open, and this bead did not settle it.

Also kept, against the bead's 'Deletes most of references/progress-streaming.md': the event-source section. The plan is explicit that the two things writing the log the monitor tails must survive, and it is right -- delete the .beads/hooks snippet and the monitor tails a file nothing writes.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text:
retro:tooling a --self-test that starts background processes and sleeps runs about 10 seconds, and the FIRST version of it hung past the 120s Bash tool timeout and had to be recovered from the background-task output file. Cause: it used `kill "$mon"; wait "$mon"` on a script whose `tail` children were still holding the redirected stdout open, so `wait` never returned. Fix that worked: `pkill -P "$mon"` before `kill "$mon"`, and no `wait` at all.

Worth a rule wherever this repo's scripts document their --self-test convention: a self-test that backgrounds anything must reap the CHILDREN, not just the job, and must never `wait` on a job whose descendants hold its stdout.

Second, smaller: sf.toml's script-self-tests check now runs a ~10s timing-sensitive test on every bead close in this repository. It is registered anyway, because an unbounded background tail that silently reports nothing is precisely the failure a one-off demonstration would not catch -- but the cost is real and is noted in the check's comment.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text:
retro:proof a defect found AFTER the first commit and folded into it by amend (unpushed, defer_push, sole agent on the branch). The monitor ignored SIGTERM and detached.

Observed: after several probe runs, ps showed ten orphaned monitors, all reparented to init --
   7658  1  S  bash .../plugin/monitors/bb-events-monitor.sh
   7912  1  S  bash .../plugin/monitors/bb-events-monitor.sh
   ... eight more ...
and `pkill -f bb-events-monitor` did not remove any of them; the count before and after was identical.

Cause: `trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM` where cleanup kills the child tails and RETURNS. A bash trap handler that returns normally resumes execution -- so the monitor cleaned up its tails, then went straight back round the watch loop and started new ones. The signal the harness stops a monitor with was, in effect, ignored.

Fix: split the traps.
   trap cleanup EXIT
   trap 'cleanup; exit 143' INT TERM

Regression test added to --self-test, and it FAILS on the pre-fix script (that is how the defect was isolated):
   ok   SIGTERM stops the monitor
   ok   and takes its tails with it
Verified no new orphan per run afterwards: process count identical before and after a full self-test, and the ten pre-fix orphans needed kill -9 because they still carried the old handler.

Worth generalising: this is not specific to monitors. Any long-running script in this repo that traps TERM to clean up must exit in the handler, or it becomes unstoppable by every ordinary means.

comments.author: dev-mpnf-4
comments.text: caveat: the bead's single commit was AMENDED after the close ceremony ran, to fold in the SIGTERM fix above. It was never pushed (defer_push, and no push ran in this dispatch), the branch qozp.15 had no other writer, and the subject and trailers are unchanged: 'agent-plugins-qozp.15 P3 Item 14: background monitor on the bead event log'. Sha moved 87fd2b2 -> f1784f6. Both the declared checks and scripts/ci.sh exit 0 on the amended tree.

title: Decide which pre-flight facts are durable, and offer a --json output
description:
## Question

PR #27 review, discussion_r3839735394: "Should this script emit these as JSON?
(Into a `.json` file?) Doesn't this get passed as JSON into the beads metadata?
Could structuring these properties mechanically simplify things for the agent?"

## What is actually true today

`pre-flight-check.sh` has TWO outputs, and they are not the same thing:

1. **An eval-able shell block on stdout** — `emit`/`emitq` produce
   `KEY='value'` because the caller runs
   `eval "$(pre-flight-check.sh)"`. This one **cannot** become JSON: a shell
   cannot eval JSON, and the whole point is that `$SCRIPTS` and the `BB_*`
   facts land in the environment.
2. **JSON written into the run epic's manifest** — it already does this, via
   `bd update <epic> --metadata <json>`, merging rather than replacing.

So the premise "doesn't this get passed as JSON into the beads metadata" is
half true: *some* of it does.

## The real gap the question exposes

Which facts belong in which output is implicit and nobody decided it. Today:

| fact | manifest | env |
|---|---|---|
| `checks_ids`, `checks_baseline` | yes | yes |
| `BB_MODEL_*` | yes (as `models`) | yes |
| `SCRIPTS`, `BB_NO_AGENT`, `BB_TREE_CLEAN`, `BB_PUSH_NEEDS_REFSPEC`, `BB_GIT_CONFIG_WRITABLE` | no | yes |

The second group describes THIS CONTAINER, not this run, which is a defensible
reason to keep them out of a durable manifest — but the reasoning is nowhere,
so the next person to add a fact has no rule to follow.

## Wanted

1. **State the rule**: a fact about the run is durable and goes to the
   manifest; a fact about the container is ephemeral and goes to the
   environment only. Put it in the script's header where a maintainer will
   see it.
2. **Add `--json`** as an additional output mode, emitting every fact as one
   object, for an agent that wants structure without eval. The eval block
   stays the default and stays shell.
3. Audit the current split against the rule and move anything misplaced.
design:
Three parts, and part 1 is the one that matters.

1. STATE THE RULE, in `pre-flight-check.sh`'s header where a maintainer adding
   a fact will read it:

     A fact about the RUN is durable and goes to the epic's manifest.
     A fact about the CONTAINER is ephemeral and goes to the environment only.

   Today the split is real but undocumented: `checks_ids`, `checks_baseline`
   and the model lineup reach the manifest; `SCRIPTS`, `BB_NO_AGENT`,
   `BB_TREE_CLEAN`, `BB_PUSH_NEEDS_REFSPEC` and `BB_GIT_CONFIG_WRITABLE` do
   not - correctly, since they describe this container.

2. ADD `--json`, emitting every fact as one object on stdout. The DEFAULT
   output stays the eval-able `KEY='value'` block: the caller runs
   `eval "$(pre-flight-check.sh)"` and a shell cannot eval JSON. This is an
   additional mode, not a replacement.

3. AUDIT the current split against the rule and move anything misplaced.

Extend `--self-test` to assert `--json` parses as JSON (`python3 -m json.tool`)
and carries the same keys as the eval block. Note that `--self-test` currently
falls through to the full environment probe, so it is excluded from `sf.toml`
and CI - the new assertion must not depend on the probe having run.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The durable/ephemeral rule is in the script header.
- [ ] `--json` emits every fact as one JSON object.
- [ ] The default output is byte-identical to today's for the same inputs.
- [ ] `--self-test` asserts `--json` is valid JSON and key-for-key consistent
      with the eval block.
- [ ] Any fact found on the wrong side of the rule is moved, or its exception
      stated.
- [ ] scripts/ci.sh exits 0.

metadata.tier_reason: shell script change with a self-test to extend; the audit needs judgement about which facts are run-scoped

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: retro:stale:sf.toml — the exclusion of pre-flight-check.sh from every self-test list rested on a false premise, which I propagated into three files. sf.toml, .github/workflows/checks.yml and scripts/ci.sh all claimed its --self-test 'falls through to the full environment probe, which pushes a probe ref to origin and runs git worktree prune on the live repo — measured'. Measured again: the arg loop runs 'self_test; exit $?' before any probe. It emits ZERO BB_* facts, leaves 'git worktree list' at the same count, and creates no refs/dolt/preflight-probe-* on the remote. pre-flight-check.sh is now in all three lists.
